TRIAGE ADDENDUM 2026-07-26 (WildIsland, pat-m81g6) — resolving the one unresolved entry in my close-candidate list.

title: 2D lights: wire the light/occluder pass into the runtime canvas with Godot node semantics
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/nodes2d-lights] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/light_2d.cpp (texture-shaped point lights, height for normal maps, blend modes, shadow filter/smooth/color, item cull masks; direction from node rotation), light_occluder_2d.cpp (occluder = OccluderPolygon2D sub-resource, cull modes), canvas_modulate.cpp

Godot applies 2D lights as a per-item shading pass: PointLight2D contributes its texture (scaled by texture_scale, tinted color x energy) with blend_mode add/sub/mix, occluded by LightOccluder2D polygons (from an OccluderPolygon2D sub-resource) with shadow filtering; DirectionalLight2D direction comes from node rotation; CanvasModulate tints the whole canvas; item_cull_mask gates receivers. comments.text:
STALE — resolved from the VERIFIER own build cache (HazyFinch 2026-07-27). Withdraws my earlier "needs a compiler, cannot settle this" note.

The failure was exit 101: "could not compile gdscene (lib test)" — an E0599, a compilation unit that a passing integration test genuinely does NOT cover, which is why I twice declined to call it stale.

I found the verifier keeps its own build tree, separate from engine-rs/target/:
  engine-rs/target-verifier/debug/.fingerprint/gdscene-*/output-test-lib-gdscene

Sorting those cached builds by mtime settles it outright:
  2026-07-26 11:10 -> 2 errors, E0599   (the recorded failure)
  2026-07-26 22:44 -> 0 errors          (NEWEST build of this unit)

The newest build of the exact failing unit is clean, so nothing newer disagrees. The E0599 in shapecast3d.rs was fixed between those two builds. Re-verify; expect green.

Reusable: the main engine-rs/target/ fingerprints are weeks stale and will make you think nothing has been built recently. Look in target-verifier/. Unit names are literal — output-lib-X is (lib), output-test-lib-X is (lib test), output-test-integration-test-NAME is (test "NAME"). Parse gotcha: level sits at the TOP level of each JSON line, not under a message key, so the obvious parser reports 0 errors for a failing build.

comments.author: FuchsiaStream
comments.text:
CAVEAT ON THE target-verifier TECHNIQUE (FuchsiaStream 2026-07-27) — adding to HazyFinch's writeup
above, because this is the comment people will copy the method from.

Their conclusion for this bead is untouched and correct: the newest recorded build of
`gdscene (lib test)` is clean (11:10 -> 2 errors, 22:44 -> 0 errors), so the recorded failure is
stale. I reproduced both numbers independently.

One thing the writeup does not say, and it bit me on pat-0q2kx.134:

  ⚠️ A CLEAN BUILD LEAVES NO `output-*` FILE AT ALL.

Cargo writes one only when rustc emitted diagnostics — errors *or warnings*. Proof from this repo:

  verifier.log:5235  dispatched and PASSED  -p gdscript-interop --test util_var_to_str_roundtrip_types

so that integration-test binary certainly compiled. Yet the crate has only two cached units:

  output-lib-gdscript_interop
  output-test-lib-gdscript_interop

No integration-test unit is recorded for gdscript-interop at all.

Two consequences for anyone using this method:

1. **"No cached build of unit X" is not evidence X was never built.** It means no build of X emitted
   diagnostics — which, for a warning-free unit, is exactly what success looks like. I wrote
   "nothing newer has built it at all" on pat-0q2kx.134 and had to retract that sentence.

2. **Every readable `errors=0` entry is a build that had warnings** — that is the only reason it
   left a record. This bead's own 22:44 clean build carried 22 warnings, which is why we can see it
   at all. A unit that gets cleaned up to zero warnings will go silent in the cache.

So: the cache is reliable POSITIVE evidence (a recorded failure really happened; a recorded clean
build really happened) and worthless as NEGATIVE evidence. When it is silent, fall back to dating
the source against the last recorded failure (file mtime + `git log -S`), which is what actually
settled .134.

Nothing here changes pat-0q2kx.104's verdict — the newest build of its unit IS recorded and IS
clean, which is the good case.

UPDATE 2026-07-27 (CalmCrane). The gdphysics2d outage cleared, so the re-verify finally reached the
real test — and clause (d) failed for a reason that is NOT the feature. A concurrent agent reached
the same diagnosis and has already fixed it; I verified their fix rather than duplicating it.

## The new failure decomposes exactly

  FAIL (100, panic) area2d_rotation_queries_and_angular_damp:284
  "moving the area must move its attraction centre — the body should now be pulled upward,
   got 360.00003"

  2000/60          =  33.33333   one step under the area's point gravity (clause d's first phase)
  20 * 980/60      = 326.66667   twenty steps under DEFAULT gravity
  sum              = 360.00000   vs observed 360.00003

So the ball received exactly ONE point-gravity step and then twenty default-gravity ones: the area
stopped affecting it the moment it moved. Not a frozen attractor — the body had left the area, and
an Area2D only overrides gravity for bodies overlapping it.

Root cause is the rect size semantics. `size` is the FULL rect size — physics_server.rs, the
"RectangleShape2D" arm, builds `half_extents: Vector2::new(size.x / 2.0, size.y / 2.0)`. At
size 400 the half-extent is 200, so a well moved to y=-400 spans y in [-600,-200] while the ball
sat near y=-50: outside.

(Aside for whoever reads the in-file comment: it explains this as "360, which is 980 * 21/60".
That evaluates to 343, not 360. The exact decomposition is the one above — one 2000-gravity step
plus twenty 980-gravity steps. The conclusion is unaffected.)

## The concurrent fix is correct — verified numerically

The area is now 800x800, so at y=-400 it spans y in [-800, 0] and encloses the ball throughout.
Simulating the post-move phase (start y=-50, v=+33.33, accel 2000 toward a centre at -400):

  final v_y = -633.33   -> assertion needs < 0            PASS
  final y   = -155.00   -> inside [-800, 0]               PASS

not testing the attractor.

sync_to_physics recomputes `area.gravity_point_center = position + point_offset` every physics tick
(physics_server.rs:1411, :1425). The bead description's claim that it is "frozen at registration"
is out of date.

assertion tests the attractor's position.

the 2000 px/s^2 attraction its max further descent is v^2/2a ~ 0.27 px, so it cannot cross y=0, and
over 20 steps it travels ~150 px up to y ~ -200 -- well inside [-800, 0].

1. gdphysics2d/src/area2d.rs — `AreaStore::overlapping_areas(area) -> Vec<AreaId>`
   The twin of `overlapping_bodies` (:551). Reads `previous_area_overlaps`, the same set the
   area_entered/area_exited events are derived from, so a script cannot get a different answer from
   the one the signals just reported. Sorted for stable script-visible order. The `monitorable` gate
   is already baked into that set by detect_area_overlaps (:588), so it needs no re-check.

   Mirrors publish_overlapping_bodies exactly, writing `_overlapping_areas`, mapping AreaId ->
   NodeId via the existing `area_to_node` map. Called from sync_from_physics immediately after the
   bodies publish, so both sets land on the same tick the enter/exit signals fire and both are
   visible before the script phase.

3. gdscene/src/scripting.rs — four arms in call_node_method
   get_overlapping_areas / has_overlapping_areas mirror the bodies arms. overlaps_body /
   overlaps_area share one arm: Godot answers these from the live set rather than recomputing, so
   they are membership tests over the published arrays, keyed by method name. A missing or

node.monitorable -> area.monitorable every sync_to_physics (and :1039 at registration).

rather than attaching scripts. Worth a follow-up if someone wants the script-call path pinned.

parse and are formatted, NOT compiled. Checked by hand: AreaId is `pub struct AreaId(pub u64)` with

## Evidence

  FAIL bead=pat-0q2kx.112 run_ms=149 reason=verification failed: failed (2, failure):
       cargo nextest run -p gdphysics2d --lib area2d &&

exit code 2 in 149 ms is a shell syntax error, not a test run. The START line shows why —
a DOUBLED `&&` between every pair of commands:

  commands=cargo nextest run -p gdphysics2d --lib area2d && && cargo nextest run -p gdscene
  --test area2d_rotation_queries_and_angular_damp && && cargo nextest run -p gdphysics2d
  --lib world_step_with_area_overrides && && cargo nextest run -p gdscene --lib physics_server

`cmd && && cmd` is a parse error, so the shell died before running anything. No test executed.

## What it is NOT

Not truncation. The full 261-char string is present in the log; the `&&`s are doubled, not cut.
(The "58-char cap" idea is a myth — long commands run fine, and this one arrived complete.)

## Likely cause, and the workaround I am applying

I have now sent FOUR completions for this bead (partial, partial, partial, complete). Comparing:

  pat-0q2kx.212, reported ONCE with the same single-string shape -> clean single `&&`, PASSED
  pat-0q2kx.112, reported FOUR times                             -> `&& &&`

pat-0q2kx.212's START also came back with its commands REORDERED relative to what I sent, which
says the coordinator merges/dedupes command lists across reports rather than replacing them. When
the stored value already contains `&&` and the merge joins with `&&` again, you get `&& &&`.

Workaround, and it is also the documented schema: send `test_commands` as SEPARATE ARRAY ELEMENTS
rather than one `&&`-joined string. mail-complete's contract is
`"test_commands": ["<cmd1>", "<cmd2>"]` — one command per element. Then nothing I send contains
`&&` and the joiner cannot double it.

My implementation of the areas-side query surface is intact in the tree:
  physics_server.rs  publish_overlapping_areas          2 hits (fn + call in sync_from_physics)
  scripting.rs       get_overlapping_areas + arms       2 hits

  141  // `MainLoop::step` does not register bodies for you — the scene has to be

Diagnosis 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch, no-cargo lane): the attractive hypothesis is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED -- do not chase it again.

Recorded failure (verifier.log:3499), physics2d_solver_stacking_conveyor_sleep.rs:103:

Summary: 4/7 run, 3 passed, 1 failed. So the conveyor and material-combine halves of this bead pass; only the stack-settling clause fails.

WHAT I ELIMINATED (all by reading):

1. "Sleeping is not implemented." It is. body.rs:218 update_sleep() runs a

3. "The fallback separate_bodies() wakes unconditionally." It does (collision.rs:710

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch) to my own earlier comment on this bead. My top-recommended experiment was WRONG and would waste a run. Read this instead.

I said: "Does the stack ever actually sleep? Print body.sleeping at tick 120 and 420 -- if they never sleep, something is calling wake()."

That experiment is already answered, and not the way I implied. The fixture DELIBERATELY DISABLES SLEEPING:

    physics2d_solver_stacking_conveyor_sleep.rs:69   body.can_sleep = false;

on every box in stack_world(). update_sleep() (body.rs:219) returns immediately when
!can_sleep, so these bodies can never sleep by construction. The stack integrates for all
420 ticks by design.

=> This clause is a pure SOLVER-CONVERGENCE test, not a sleeping test. The author switched
sleeping off precisely so that sleeping cannot mask solver drift. That is also why every
sleep-related hypothesis (mine included) was a dead end.

ALSO ELIMINATED since the earlier comment, so nobody re-checks:
- Gravity does not wake bodies. world.rs applies it via body.integrate_forces (body.rs:400),
  which early-returns on freeze/sleeping and never calls wake().
- The complete set of wake() callers in the crate is: apply_force / apply_impulse /
  apply_impulse_at_point (script-driven, correct), world.rs:610 (Entered contacts only,
  correct), and collision.rs:710 in separate_bodies (the FALLBACK path, not used by the
  world step for stacks). Nothing spuriously wakes anything.
- Solver iteration count is NOT the gap: DEFAULT_SOLVER_ITERATIONS = 16 (solver.rs:48),
  which is exactly Godot's `physics/2d/solver/solver_iterations` default of 16
  (physics_server_2d.cpp:914).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY LEFT: a 3-box stack creeps 1.4196601 px over 300 ticks (~0.28 px/s) with a
16-iteration Gauss-Seidel sweep. That is classic unconverged-stack behaviour, and the usual
remedies are things this solver may not have yet:
  (a) WARM STARTING -- persist each contact's accumulated normal/tangent impulse across
      frames and seed the next step with it. This is the single biggest stability win for
      stacks and the first thing to check for; grep solver.rs for whether manifold impulses
      survive between steps or are rebuilt from zero each step.
  (b) A penetration SLOP / bias tuning pass (Baumgarte), so depenetration does not fight the
      contact impulses and jitter the stack.
  (c) Contact-point caching keyed by feature id, so the manifold does not flip between
      points each frame -- a flipping manifold defeats (a).

Check (a) first: it is a yes/no code question that needs no test run.

Still needs a build-capable lane to land, because any of these changes the behaviour of every
2D stack and can only be judged by running the suite.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch) — answers question (a) from my previous comment, and it needed no test run.

THE SOLVER HAS NO WARM STARTING. Contact constraints are rebuilt from scratch every step with
their accumulated impulses zeroed:

    solver.rs:262   "Every contact between one pair of bodies for this step."
    solver.rs:356   acc_normal: 0.0,     <-- fresh every step

`acc_normal` / `acc_tangent` accumulate correctly ACROSS THE 16 ITERATIONS WITHIN one step
(solver.rs:510-519, clamping the accumulated value rather than the increment, which is right),
but nothing carries them INTO the next step. So every frame the solver starts cold and has 16
Gauss-Seidel sweeps to rediscover the support impulses for the whole stack.

That is a textbook cause of exactly this symptom. A cold 16-iteration sweep does not fully
cancel gravity through a 3-box chain, so each frame leaves a small residual velocity; the
residual integrates into position and the stack creeps. Measured: 1.4196601 px over 300 ticks
= ~0.28 px/s, small and steady — the signature of per-frame residual, not of a jitter or a
depenetration fight.

It also explains why the box count matters: impulse has to propagate box->box->floor, and each
extra link needs more iterations to converge from cold. A 1-box test would pass.

THE FIX is warm starting: persist each contact point's acc_normal/acc_tangent across steps and
apply them as the starting impulse next step. Two parts:
  1. Cache manifold points keyed by a stable contact FEATURE id (not by index/position, which
     flips as boxes shift and would defeat the cache).
  2. On rebuild, seed the new point's acc_* from the matching cached point, and apply that
     impulse to both bodies before the iteration loop.

ALREADY ELIMINATED (do not re-check — see my two earlier comments): sleeping (the fixture sets
can_sleep = false at test line 69, so this clause is a pure solver test), gravity waking bodies,
every wake() caller, and iteration count (16 already matches Godot's
physics/2d/solver/solver_iterations default of 16, physics_server_2d.cpp:914).

WHY I DID NOT IMPLEMENT IT: warm starting changes the impulse trajectory of every 2D contact in
the engine. It is the correct fix and it is also the kind that trades stack stability against
bounce/restitution behaviour elsewhere, so it must be judged by running the whole gdphysics2d
suite, not just this test. A no-cargo lane cannot tell a fix from a regression here.

Good news for whoever takes it: gdphysics2d is BELOW the gdscript-interop outage, so this bead
is verifiable right now even while most of the queue is not.

editor_server.rs:6130, inside api_set_resource_property:

comments.text:
Reported COMPLETE 2026-07-27 ~03:55 (msg 75213). Implemented Save As; deliberately did NOT implement
Make Unique.

## Added

POST /api/property/resource/save_as (editor_server.rs) — serializes the inline resource on
node.property to a .tres, writes it, and REPOINTS the property at the res:// path, undoably.

The repoint is the feature, not the file write. The route leaves the property in exactly the state an
assign-by-path produces (String value + __extres__<prop> companion, __resref__<prop> cleared), so the
EXISTING scene save emits an ext_resource and stops emitting a [sub_resource] — no writer changes.

Two type facts worth keeping:
  - Variant::Resource carries gdvariant::ResourceRef; TresSaver takes gdresource::Resource. DIFFERENT
    types.
  - gdresource::Resource.properties is PRIVATE, so the conversion goes through Resource::new() +
    set_property(), not a struct literal.

## Test

tests/res_picker_e2e.rs :: resource_save_as_writes_tres_and_repoints_the_property
Load-bearing assertion: the saved .tscn contains the .tres reference AND NO [sub_resource]. A route
that wrote the file but left the inline value would pass a file-exists check and still be broken —
the resource would duplicate on every save and edits to the .tres would be ignored.
Also asserts a second save_as on an already-external property returns 400 rather than silently
overwriting whatever the path points at.

## NOT built, on purpose

Make Unique would be INERT: resources live by value inside each node's property
(api_set_resource_property mutates a copy and stores it back, :6130). Nothing is shared, so there is
nothing to un-share. Needs node properties to hold a REFERENCE first — architectural, own bead.
Recommended filing it so the next reader of this bead's title does not assume it is menu wiring.

## Verified against definitions (no-cargo lane, nothing compiled by me)

TresSaver::save_to_string, Resource::new/set_property (private field), resolve_res_path,
get_property returning an OWNED Variant, EditorServerHandle::stop(mut self), and the
__extres__/__resref__ companion keys the saver actually reads. Confirmed both rustfmt anchors fell
inside my new block before formatting, since others have work in this file.

title: Rendering2D: wire scene 2D lights into the Play frame and implement texture/shadow_color/filter/cull-mask light features
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-lighting] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_render.h Light struct + shadow buffers; scene/2d/light_2d.cpp; extension_api.json Light2D properties (enabled, editor_only, color, energy, blend_mode, range_z_min/max, range_layer_min/max, range_item_cull_mask, shadow_enabled, shadow_color, shadow_filter, shadow_filter_smooth, shadow_item_cull_mask) and PointLight2D (texture, offset, texture_scale, height)

In Godot a PointLight2D in a scene lights canvas items every frame (renderer_canvas_render.h): its texture defines the light footprint (height for normal maps), blend_mode ADD/SUB/MIX composites per mode, shadows blend shadow_color with PCF5/PCF13 filters and shadow_item_cull_mask. Patina's whole 2D light stack is dead in production: gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs::apply_scene_lights (:119) has one test caller (tests/light2d_scene_shading_wiring.rs:58) and no render path invokes it; gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs::composite_light blend modes are never called by anything. Implementation: (1) in the Play raster path (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs::rasterize_render_list callers), after drawing items, run light2d_scene::collect_lights_2d/collect_occluders_2d + apply_scene_lights over the FrameBuffer honoring per-item light_mask (requires carrying item light_mask through Render2DItem and shading per-item regions, not whole-frame, so unshaded/light-only CanvasItemMaterial modes can work later); apply collect_canvas_modulate before/after per Godot order; (2) route blend_mode through composite_light instead of the current additive-accumulate-multiply; (3) extend Light2D with texture path + offset + texture_scale (sample the light texture for footprint, falling back to Godot's default gradient only if texture absent), shadow_color blending in is_occluded hits, shadow_filter NONE/PCF5/PCF13 + shadow_filter_smooth (sample N shadow rays), shadow_item_cull_mask distinct from range_item_cull_mask, and range_z_min/max + range_layer_min/max item filtering; (4) editor_only lights skipped in Play. Wiring requirement: .tscn with PointLight2D → MainLoop frame → shaded Play BMP.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. gdscene light2d_scene::apply_scene_lights/collect_lights_2d have a single caller: gdscene/tests/light2d_scene_shading_wiring.rs:58 (grep across examples/ + crates src). Neither viewport_2d_render.rs nor scene_renderer.rs references lights (the Play/design paths). apply_lights_to_framebuffer IS called at renderer.rs:669 but only inside SoftwareRenderer::render_frame, which reache

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a dark CanvasModulate, a white ColorRect, a red PointLight2D (texture set, energy 1) at its center, and a LightOccluder2D segment between the light and one rect corner: the Play-path frame shows brightened red-tinted pixels near the light, the occluded corner darker than the lit side and tinted toward shadow_color (not fully unlit black when shadow_color has alpha < 1), and setting blend_mode=SUB darkens instead of brightens; a light with range_item_cull_mask not matching the rect's light_mask leaves pixels unchanged (test: `light2d_shades_play_frame`).
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a dark CanvasModulate, a white ColorRect, a red PointLight2D (texture set, energy 1) at its center, and a LightOccluder2D segment between the light and one rect corner: the Play-path frame shows brightened red-tinted pixels near the light, the occluded corner darker than the lit side and tinted toward shadow_color (not fully unlit black when shadow_color has alpha < 1), and setting blend_mode=SUB darkens instead of brightens; a light with range_item_cull_mask not matching the rect's light_mask leaves pixels unchanged (test: `light2d_shades_play_frame`).

comments.text:
⚠️ CORRECTION to my own comment above (FuchsiaStream 2026-07-27) — one sentence of it was unjustified.

I wrote: "Nothing newer disagrees, because nothing newer has built it at all."

That inference is WRONG, and the technique needs a caveat before anyone else leans on it.

**A clean build leaves NO `output-*` file.** Cargo only writes one when rustc emitted diagnostics
(errors *or* warnings). Proof, from this same repo and log:

  verifier.log:5235  START/PASS  -p gdscript-interop --test util_var_to_str_roundtrip_types

That integration-test binary demonstrably compiled and ran. Yet the verifier's cache holds only
two units for the whole crate:

  target-verifier/debug/.fingerprint/gdscript-interop-*/output-lib-gdscript_interop
  target-verifier/debug/.fingerprint/gdscript-interop-*/output-test-lib-gdscript_interop

No `output-test-integration-test-util_var_to_str_roundtrip_types` exists, for a binary that
provably built. So absence of an `output-*` file is NOT evidence of absence of a build.

(This is also why the `errors=0` entries we have all carry warnings — e.g. gdscene's `(lib test)`
at 22:44 had 22 warnings, which is the only reason that clean build left a readable record.)

WHAT THIS DOES TO THE CONCLUSION: it does not weaken it, but it changes the reason.

  what I claimed:  no newer build exists  =>  the 13:09 failure is the latest word
  what is true:    no newer build EMITTED DIAGNOSTICS. That is consistent with either
                   "never rebuilt" or "rebuilt clean and silent" — and the second is
                   exactly what a repaired unit looks like.

The dating still stands on its own and is untouched by this: the only recorded failure ran 07-26
13:09, the test file was edited 13:12, and the fix committed in 2d5fa99 at 15:01. The fix postdates
the failure either way. But "nothing newer has built it" was me over-reading a silent cache, and I
would rather flag that than let it propagate — two of us are now using this technique.

Net: pat-0q2kx.134 is still STALE by the dating argument. Ignore my "no newer build" sentence.

title: ProjectSettings: seed script singleton from booted project + feature-tag overrides + missing methods
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/project-settings-runtime] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** core/config/project_settings.cpp (singleton holds every project.godot setting; get_setting_with_override applies active feature tags e.g. .web; save/save_custom; get_global_class_list from global_script_class_cache)

Godot's ProjectSettings singleton (core/config/project_settings.cpp) exposes every project.godot value to scripts, applies feature-tag overrides (setting.web on web builds), and supports save/get_global_class_list. Patina parses project.godot correctly at boot (patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:63 → gdcore::ProjectSettings, which already implements override resolution at gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:207) but the interpreter singleton is a disconnected empty thread-local (interpreter.rs:9454, self-documented TODO) so scripts read Nil for every real setting. Implement: (1) a pub seed API in gdscript-interop (e.g. seed_project_settings(iter of (String, Variant)) + set_active_feature_tags) called from boot_project and from the editor Play flow; (2) get_setting_with_override consults the active tag set via the gdcore logic; (3) add save (writes project.godot via ConfigFile-style serialization), get_global_class_list (from script class_name scan), set_order/get_order, set_initial_value, add_property_info, set_as_basic/set_as_internal, set_restart_if_changed, get_changed_settings/check_changed_settings_in_group (state-tracking); (4) globalize_path/localize_path use gdcore::project_root() not current_dir. Wiring: boot_project → seeded store → script visibility in the same run.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. PROJECT_SETTINGS is a thread-local HashMap seeded by nothing (interpreter.rs:9454-9462; doc self-documents 'Seeding the store from project.godot ... is still TODO'). Runner never seeds it — main.rs:342 only calls main_loop.configure_from_project_settings and InputMap; no seed_project_settings path into the interpreter. get_setting_with_override ignores features ('fall back to th

**Prove it:** Boot a temp project whose project.godot sets physics/2d/default_gravity=123 and display/window/size/viewport_width=111 plus viewport_width.web=222: a script run in the booted tree reads get_setting values 123/111, get_setting_with_override("display/window/size/viewport_width") returns 222 when the web feature tag is active, has_setting is true, and ProjectSettings.save() after set_setting persists a reloadable file. (test: `project_settings_script_visibility`)
acceptance_criteria: Boot a temp project whose project.godot sets physics/2d/default_gravity=123 and display/window/size/viewport_width=111 plus viewport_width.web=222: a script run in the booted tree reads get_setting values 123/111, get_setting_with_override("display/window/size/viewport_width") returns 222 when the web feature tag is active, has_setting is true, and ProjectSettings.save() after set_setting persists a reloadable file. (test: `project_settings_script_visibility`)

title: Resources: complete .tscn variant literal parser (Vector4/Rect2i/Projection/Object(), typed-array retention, int-vector
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-parse-fidelity] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp + core/variant/variant_parser.cpp (parses every builtin literal incl. Vector4(i), Rect2i, Projection, Object(Class,"prop":v,...), Array[Type]([...]) retaining the element type, Dictionary[K,V], &"sn", ^"np", inf/nan; unparseable values are a load ERROR, never dropped)

Godot's VariantParser (core/variant/variant_parser.cpp) accepts every builtin literal; unparseable values abort the load with a line-numbered error. Patina's parse_variant_value (gdresource/src/loader.rs:233) is missing Vector4/Vector4i/Rect2i/Projection/PackedVector4Array/Object(Class,"prop":value,...)/^"nodepath"/typed Dictionary/inf-nan, downgrades Vector2i/Vector3i to float vectors (loader.rs:420-441), and drops the Array[T] element type (loader.rs:530). gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:156,321 silently skips any value that fails to parse, so real Godot scenes lose properties invisibly and the editor round-trip persists the loss. Implement: (1) the missing literal arms in parse_variant_value (int-vector types depend on the core-variant bead adding Variant kinds; until merged, store them tagged so the saver can re-emit the exact literal — do NOT silently retype); (2) Object(...) constructor parsing into a typed sub-object (needed by theme overrides and embedded InputEvents); (3) retain Array[T]/Dictionary[K,V] annotations on the parsed value for save; (4) replace the silent skip in packed_scene.rs with a load error carrying file/line (Godot behavior), with MissingResource-style preservation (gdresource/src/missing.rs is currently dead code — wire it) reserved for unknown CLASS names only. Wiring: a .tscn using each literal loads through PackedScene::from_tscn into node properties the runtime reads.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. Spot-checks all hold: grep for Vector4/Rect2i/Projection/PackedVector4/Object( in loader.rs returns nothing (absent). Vector2i parses to Variant::Vector2 float (loader.rs:426), Vector3i to Variant::Vector3 float (loader.rs:438-439) — int type lost. Typed Array[T] annotation accepted then discarded, stored as plain Variant::Array (loader.rs:530-544, comment: 'accepted but not ret

**Prove it:** A fixture .tscn with properties of every builtin literal (incl. Vector4, Rect2i, Projection, Vector2i, Object(LabelSettings,"font_size":20), Array[int]([1,2]), inf) loads with zero skipped properties and each value retrievable with the correct type tag; a deliberately malformed value makes from_tscn return Err naming the line instead of loading a partial scene. (test: `tscn_value_parser_fidelity`)
acceptance_criteria: A fixture .tscn with properties of every builtin literal (incl. Vector4, Rect2i, Projection, Vector2i, Object(LabelSettings,"font_size":20), Array[int]([1,2]), inf) loads with zero skipped properties and each value retrievable with the correct type tag; a deliberately malformed value makes from_tscn return Err naming the line instead of loading a partial scene. (test: `tscn_value_parser_fidelity`)

title: Editor: lossless .tscn/.tres save — connection flags/binds, ext uid, single shared variant writer, .tres save route
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-save-lossless] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp ResourceFormatSaverText (writes flags=/binds= on [connection], uid= on [ext_resource], every variant via VariantWriter; editor saves must round-trip byte-stably)

Godot's text saver (scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp) writes [connection ... flags=N binds=[...]], uid= on ext_resources, and every variant through VariantWriter — an open+save in the editor is lossless. Patina: gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs:608 writes connections without flags/binds although the loader preserves them (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:190-216), scene_saver.rs:300 drops ext_resource uid, and both savers Display-fallback unknown variant kinds (scene_saver.rs:237, gdresource/src/saver.rs:146) producing unparseable lines; gdresource TresSaver additionally leaks the internal "ExtResource:id" string form and has no editor caller, so .tres edits can't persist. Implement: (1) extract ONE shared variant writer (inverse of parse_variant_value, covering every type the parser accepts incl. the new literals from the tscn_parse_fidelity bead) used by both scene_saver.rs and saver.rs; (2) emit flags= and binds= when nonzero/nonempty, matching Godot's omission-when-default; (3) preserve ext_resource uid= from load; (4) re-emit ExtResource("id")/SubResource("id") calls from the internal string tags; (5) an editor save-resource route (editor_interface.rs) that writes .tres via TresSaver. Wiring: editor open→save of a fixture must be semantically identical (re-parse equal), proven at the editor_interface level.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. write_connections emits only signal/from/to/method (scene_saver.rs:606-609) though the loader parses and stores flags+binds (packed_scene.rs:196-216 SceneConnection.flags/.binds) — dropped on save, so deferred/one-shot/bound connections are destroyed by an editor open+save (editor does save scenes via TscnSaver: editor_interface.rs:150 save_scene, editor_server.rs:5863 api_save_

**Prove it:** Open+save round-trip through gdeditor editor_interface on a fixture .tscn containing a deferred(flags=1) connection with binds, an ext_resource with uid, and math/packed-array properties: the re-parsed scene has identical connections (flags+binds), ext uid survives, and every property re-parses equal; saving a .tres through the new route re-loads with equal properties. (test: `tscn_save_lossless_roundtrip`)
acceptance_criteria: Open+save round-trip through gdeditor editor_interface on a fixture .tscn containing a deferred(flags=1) connection with binds, an ext_resource with uid, and math/packed-array properties: the re-parsed scene has identical connections (flags+binds), ext uid survives, and every property re-parses equal; saving a .tres through the new route re-loads with equal properties. (test: `tscn_save_lossless_roundtrip`)

title: Input routing: add GUI stage (Control._gui_input/focus/hover) and physics picking to push_input, with Godot dispatch ord
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-input] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp:3464-3580 (push_input: _input group -> _gui_input_event -> shortcut -> unhandled_key -> unhandled -> physics picking); scene_tree.cpp _call_input_pause iterates REVERSE (gr_node_count-1..0) and checks can_process/is_processing_input

Godot ground truth (viewport.cpp:3464-3580): a mouse/key event flows _input group (reverse order, can_process-gated) -> GUI stage (_gui_input_event: hit-test topmost Control under cursor honoring mouse_filter STOP/PASS/IGNORE, key events to the focus owner, hover enter/exit, pressed/focus signals) -> shortcut_input -> unhandled_key_input -> unhandled_input -> physics object picking (CollisionObject2D._input_event when input_pickable), stopping at set_input_as_handled. Patina current state: scene_tree.rs:1998-2023 push_input runs only the 4 script stages, forward order, ungated; control.rs:611 click_at_point (mouse_filter-aware hit test) and focus helpers (control.rs:1751) exist but have zero callers — buttons in a running game never receive clicks from the MainLoop input path; no physics picking. Implementation: insert a GUI stage into SceneTree::push_input between _input and _shortcut_input that (a) for mouse events resolves the target via the existing click_at_point/control-rect logic and dispatches _gui_input + BaseButton press/release/pressed signals + grab_focus on click, (b) for key events dispatches to the focus owner and handles ui_focus_next tab traversal, and consumes the event per mouse_filter; add a physics-picking stage after _unhandled_input querying the 2D physics world at the cursor for input_pickable colliders and calling _input_event; reverse the per-stage iteration order and gate each delivery on should_process_node + per-node set_process_input flags (new Node fields + SceneAccess setters). Wiring requirement: a browser event entering MainLoop::push_event must reach a Button's pressed signal and a Control script's _gui_input in editor Play and the runner.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. push_input (scene_tree.rs:1998-2023) runs only the 4 script stages (_input/_shortcut_input/_unhandled_key_input/_unhandled_input), iterating all_nodes_in_tree_order() FORWARD (top-down), with no can_process/should_process_node gating and no set_process_input toggles — Godot's _call_input_pause iterates the input group in REVERSE and gates on can_process. grep gui_input|_gui_inpu

**Prove it:** Feeding a mouse-click InputEvent at a Button's rect through MainLoop::push_event + step emits the button's pressed signal to a connected script and does NOT reach _unhandled_input (consumed by GUI stage per mouse_filter=STOP); clicking empty space reaches _unhandled_input then fires _input_event on an input_pickable Area2D under the point; two overlapping scripted nodes receive _input in Godot's reverse order; a node after set_process_input(false) receives nothing (test: `viewport_input_propagation_gui_stage`)
acceptance_criteria: Feeding a mouse-click InputEvent at a Button's rect through MainLoop::push_event + step emits the button's pressed signal to a connected script and does NOT reach _unhandled_input (consumed by GUI stage per mouse_filter=STOP); clicking empty space reaches _unhandled_input then fires _input_event on an input_pickable Area2D under the point; two overlapping scripted nodes receive _input in Godot's reverse order; a node after set_process_input(false) receives nothing (test: `viewport_input_propagation_gui_stage`)

title: PackedScene: apply instance-internal overrides, resolve inherited scenes, and implement InstancePlaceholder
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-packedscene] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp SceneState (instance diffs: [node] entries without type= override existing instanced nodes; inherited scenes via root instance=; editable_instances; InstancePlaceholder class with create_instance/get_stored_values)

Godot ground truth (scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp SceneState): when a .tscn instances a sub-scene, later [node] entries with parent paths inside that instance (and no type=) OVERRIDE the existing instanced nodes' properties (this is how every tweaked instance is saved); a scene whose root [node] has instance=ExtResource and no type is an INHERITED scene — the base scene instantiates first and the diff applies on top; [editable path] marks instances whose internal overrides persist; instance_placeholder creates an InstancePlaceholder node exposing get_stored_values()/create_instance(replace, custom_scene)/get_instance_path(). Patina current state (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:694-832 instance_with_subscenes): override entries targeting instance-internal paths create DUPLICATE new nodes (regular branch 795-830 never checks path_to_index for an existing node at name-under-parent), the root template's instance= is silently ignored (714-716) so inherited scenes lose their entire base tree, editable_instances is parse-only (115,657), and placeholder templates instantiate as plain empty-class nodes. Implementation: in the template loop, before creating a node, look up `parent_path + '/' + name` (and root '.') in path_to_index — if present, apply tmpl.properties/groups to nodes[idx] instead of pushing a new node; resolve a root-level instance= through resolve_scene and apply the root template as a diff on the instanced base (recursively supporting multi-level inheritance); instantiate instance_placeholder templates as class InstancePlaceholder storing the path + stored property bag, register the class in class_db.rs, and add SceneAccess/interpreter dispatch for create_instance. Wiring requirement: runner + editor load these files through the same add_packed_scene_to_tree_with_subscenes path; a saved-then-reloaded scene with instance overrides must round-trip identically (scene_saver.rs interplay).

**Merged findings (2):** classes InstancePlaceholder, PackedScene, SceneState
- also: Zero ClassDB reg (`ClassRegistration::new("InstancePlaceholder")` = 0) and no impl: `grep -rniE 'InstancePlaceholder' crates` (tests excluded) returns nothing. The taxonomy scene-tree stone explicitly lists InstancePlaceholder as part of PackedScene instancing (editable children / placeholders); the

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. (1) instance_with_subscenes regular branch (packed_scene.rs:795-830) unconditionally constructs a NEW Node::new and pushes it, inserting node_path into path_to_index — it never checks whether parent_path+'/'+name already exists, so a [node] override targeting an instance-internal child produces a duplicate sibling. (2) The root template's instance= is documented 'handled by the 

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn that instances enemy.tscn and overrides the instanced child Sprite's position yields ONE Sprite node carrying the override (not a duplicate sibling); loading an inherited scene (root instance=base.tscn plus a diff property and an extra child) produces the base tree with the diff applied; an instance_placeholder node loads as InstancePlaceholder whose create_instance() swaps in the real sub-scene at runtime (test: `packed_scene_instance_overrides`)
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn that instances enemy.tscn and overrides the instanced child Sprite's position yields ONE Sprite node carrying the override (not a duplicate sibling); loading an inherited scene (root instance=base.tscn plus a diff property and an extra child) produces the base tree with the diff applied; an instance_placeholder node loads as InstancePlaceholder whose create_instance() swaps in the real sub-scene at runtime (test: `packed_scene_instance_overrides`)

title: ScriptEditor: wire completion popup + Ctrl+Click goto-definition to the live endpoints
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/script-editor-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/script/script_text_editor.cpp (completion via CodeEdit, Ctrl+Click symbol lookup), editor/gui/code_editor.cpp find/replace bar

Godot's script editor completes members/locals as you type and Ctrl+Click jumps to a symbol. Patina's server half is done and green (POST /api/script/complete returns ranked candidates — editor_server.rs test editor_script_complete_endpoint_returns_candidates; goto_definition.rs exists but is orphan), while the served client has nothing: no popup, no keybinding, no fetch. Implement in EDITOR_HTML's script panel: (1) on identifier keystrokes (debounced) POST /api/script/complete with {current_class, prefix, locals} scraped from the buffer, render a popup list, Tab/Enter inserts; (2) Ctrl+Click on a symbol resolves via a new GET /api/script/goto?symbol=... backed by goto_definition.rs and jumps the editor (open file + line); (3) optionally route the existing local find/replace menu through /api/script/find//replace for whole-file counts. Wiring requirement: keystroke in the served editor -> fetch -> popup -> insertion mutates the buffer that /api/script/save persists.

**Verifier:** Server routes exist and are unit-tested: /api/script/find (editor_server.rs:2385), /replace (2386), /complete (2388, test at 15417-15429), /api/signal/goto_method (2468). Client wiring absent: `grep script/complete|script/find|script/replace|goto_method editor_ui.rs` = 0 hits; no completion popup element. goto_definition.rs is orphan (only lib.rs:80 mod decl + own tests). A local #script-find-bar 

**Prove it:** Served HTML contains the completion popup element and fetches /api/script/complete (assert EDITOR_HTML); endpoint round-trip: complete for a known local returns it and the goto route returns file+line for a method defined in a project script; an e2e that saves a script via /api/script/save after inserting a completed identifier sees it on disk. (test: `script_editor_completion_wiring_e2e`)
acceptance_criteria: Served HTML contains the completion popup element and fetches /api/script/complete (assert EDITOR_HTML); endpoint round-trip: complete for a known local returns it and the goto route returns file+line for a method defined in a project script; an e2e that saves a script via /api/script/save after inserting a completed identifier sees it on disk. (test: `script_editor_completion_wiring_e2e`)

title: SceneTree: gate physics/animation/tween/particle/timer/input phases on pause + process_mode
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scene-tree-pause] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1111-1140 (set_pause -> PhysicsServer2D/3D::set_active(!paused) + _propagate_pause_notification); node.cpp NOTIFICATION_DISABLED/ENABLED on process-mode transitions

Godot ground truth: SceneTree::set_pause (scene_tree.cpp:1111-1140) deactivates PhysicsServer2D/3D so nothing steps while paused; per-node process_mode gates every callback including input (_call_input_pause checks can_process); AnimationPlayer/Tween/GPUParticles honor pause via their process callbacks; Timer with default process_mode stops; nodes transitioning to/from Disabled receive NOTIFICATION_DISABLED/ENABLED. Patina current state: MainLoop::step (gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1364-1495) steps 2D+3D physics, character movement, animations (1427), tweens (1428), particles (1433), path follows (1438), navigation (1443) and Timer nodes (1456) unconditionally while tree.paused — a paused game keeps simulating everything except script callbacks; process_timer_nodes (scene_tree.rs:394-459) ignores tree pause; push_input (scene_tree.rs:1998) delivers to paused nodes; Tween has no pause-mode binding (tween.rs). Implementation: in MainLoop::step skip the physics-step block when paused (except bodies whose node's effective mode is Always/WhenPaused — Godot's server-inactive model simply skips the step entirely, so start with a whole-phase skip), filter process_timer_nodes/process_animations/process_tweens/process_particles/process_path_follows/process_navigation by should_process_node of the owning node, gate push_input per node with should_process_node, add TweenPauseMode (bound/process/idle) defaulting to bound, and fire new NOTIFICATION_DISABLED/ENABLED on effective-mode transitions. Wiring requirement: get_tree().paused = true (via the script bridge) or MainLoop::set_paused must freeze the whole world in runner and editor Play, while an Always-mode pause-menu script keeps processing.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:1310-1500) has NO pause guard around the physics block — I read from step's top; the physics while-loop (1368-1420) steps physics_server + 3D + character movement + navigation unconditionally, and process_animations(1427)/process_tweens(1428)/process_particles(1433)/process_path_follows/process_navigation/process_timer_nodes(1456) all run regardless 

**Prove it:** With a falling RigidBody2D, a repeating Timer, a playing AnimationPlayer, and a running tween in one scene: after set_paused(true) + 60 MainLoop::step frames, the body position, timer time_left, animation position and tweened property are all unchanged, no timeout fires, and a ProcessMode::Always script still receives _process and _input while a Pausable sibling receives neither; unpausing resumes all (test: `scene_tree_pause_gates_simulation`)
acceptance_criteria: With a falling RigidBody2D, a repeating Timer, a playing AnimationPlayer, and a running tween in one scene: after set_paused(true) + 60 MainLoop::step frames, the body position, timer time_left, animation position and tweened property are all unchanged, no timeout fires, and a ProcessMode::Always script still receives _process and _input while a Pausable sibling receives neither; unpausing resumes all (test: `scene_tree_pause_gates_simulation`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
PARTIAL DIAGNOSIS 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch) — eliminations only, no fix. Needs a build-capable lane.

FAILURE (verifier.log:3712) is the test's own CONTROL assertion, before pause is even exercised:
  scene_tree_pause_gates_simulation.rs:104 'control: gravity must move the body while unpaused, got y=0'
So the body never falls at all. The pause logic this bead is about is NOT implicated yet.

RULED OUT — do not re-test these:
  1. NOT the pat-0q2kx.16 move_and_slide gate. That gate (physics_server.rs:1725) applies only to
     SCRIPTED CharacterBody2D kinematic bodies. This fixture uses an UNSCRIPTED RigidBody2D, so the
     gate cannot reach it. I checked this first because 'body does not move' looks exactly like it.
  2. NOT shape resolution. shape_from_node (physics_server.rs:~231) explicitly accepts BOTH the
     .tscn SubResource form AND the hand-built form this test uses (class name in 'shape' plus bare
     dimension keys): 'Variant::String(s) => Some(s.clone())'. The CircleShape2D + radius=8 setup is
     valid.
  3. NOT the obvious fixture mistakes — the setup already sets mass=1.0, gravity_scale=1.0,
     can_sleep=false, calls physics_server_mut().set_gravity(0,980) and register_physics_bodies().
     Those comments record earlier rounds of exactly this debugging.
  4. sync_from_physics EXISTS and has its own passing unit test
     (physics_server.rs:2037 sync_from_physics_updates_node_position), so the body->node writeback
     is implemented in principle.

WHERE I WOULD LOOK NEXT (needs a compiler; I could not run anything):
  pos_y() reads the NODE's 'position' property, so the chain is
  register -> sync_to_physics -> world step -> sync_from_physics -> node.position.
  Instrument which link drops: is the body actually in node_to_body after
  register_physics_bodies, does the world body's position change during step, and does
  sync_from_physics run inside MainLoop::step (as opposed to only when called directly)?
  My suspicion is the last one, but I did NOT confirm it and it should not be treated as a finding.

Verify with: -p gdscene --test scene_tree_pause_gates_simulation

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS — real and current, exit 100, and it is NOT a pause bug (HazyFinch 2026-07-27).

Failure: "control: gravity must move the body while unpaused, got y=0" (scene_tree_pause_gates_simulation.rs:104).

Read that carefully — it is the CONTROL assertion. The body fails to move while UNPAUSED, so nothing about pause gating has been exercised yet. The pause logic this bead is about may well be fine; the fixture never gets off the ground.

Fixture: Root -> Faller (RigidBody2D + CollisionShape2D) + a repeating Timer. gravity_scale = 1.0, and the 2D space gravity is set explicitly to (0, 980) because MainLoop::new does not apply project settings.

The test file itself names two prerequisites, either of which would produce exactly y=0:
  - :39 "A body with no mass is not simulated" — check the fixture actually sets mass.
  - :68 the "call after loading a scene" sync step — "Without it the RigidBody2D is not in [the space]". If registration into the physics space does not happen, the body is inert and gravity never touches it.

So the first question is not "is pause gating right?" but "is the Faller registered and massed?". Start by asserting the body moves at all in isolation, then re-enable the pause assertions.

⚠️ NOT the same bug as pat-0q2kx.117, despite both reading as "a body will not fall". I checked: .117 is an unscripted CharacterBody2D whose velocity is zeroed on landing, a completely different mechanism from an unsimulated RigidBody2D. Do not assume one fix closes both.

comments.author: bone

My previous comment concluded: "the defect is that the encode_* mutation does not persist for this

wrote it.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

The FAIL I diagnosed (verifier.log:5335, `u8` got Int(0) want Int(200)) was a build of somebody's
MID-EDIT working tree. The verifier builds the working tree, not HEAD, so the failure tail described
an intermediate state that was already gone by the time I read the files.

  HEAD has                6 `#[test]` fns          -> matches the failing build
  the file I was reading  7 `#[test]` fns          -> a NEWER edit, +encoding_past_the_end_is_a_no_op

I was reading a file with `b.resize(19)` in it. HEAD's version has no `resize` at all — it encodes
into an EMPTY array and asserts the buffer grows to 19. Two different tests. I reasoned about the
new one and applied the conclusion to a failure produced by the old one.

THE TELL I MISSED, and it was free: **the failure tail prints the test count.** `1/6 tests run`
against a file containing 7 `#[test]`s is immediate proof the build predates the file. Compare those
two numbers BEFORE reasoning about a failure — it costs one `grep -c '^#\[test\]'`.

Everything I "ruled out" is still true of the current code (packed_resize, packed_byte_encode,
packed_byte_decode and the dispatch are all correct as read) — but it was never evidence about the
failure, because the failure came from different code. Ruling things out against the wrong snapshot

`ERR_FAIL_COND` semantics: an out-of-range encode must NOT grow the buffer and must not write.

since 12:18 today, still `if bytes.len() < end { bytes.resize(end, 0) }`), and the interpreter arm

`to_int(&args[0])?.max(0)`).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
## Diagnosis 2026-07-25 (MistyStone): the failure is isolated to inside process_character_movement, past its gates

The recent failure (verifier.log 2475/2476, run.log 19:30:45) is:

    cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test.rs:282
    link 3: the physics phase must honor the move_and_slide request,
    start Vector2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 } -> Vector2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }

The test is deliberately built as four separate links so a failure names the broken
one. Links 1 and 2 PASS, which rules out most of the chain:

- link 1 passes → `self.velocity = Vector2(0, 400)` reaches the NODE property.
- link 2 passes → a bare `move_and_slide()` reaches `SceneAccess::call_node_method`
  and sets `_move_and_slide_requested = true` on the node (scripting.rs:857).
- link 3 fails → after 29 further steps the position is still exactly (0, 0).

### What I verified is NOT the cause

- The consumer exists: `physics_server.rs:1067` reads `_move_and_slide_requested`,
  and consumes it one-shot at :1073.
- It is actually called: `PhysicsServer::process_character_movement` (:1031) is invoked
  from `main_loop.rs:1509` inside the physics step.
- The velocity source is the node property (`vec2_prop(tree, node_id, "velocity")`,
  :1053), which link 1 proves is (0, 400) — so the idle-skip at :1078
  (`velocity.length_squared() < 1e-8`) should not fire.
- Entry filter: the body must be `BodyType::Kinematic` AND the node class exactly
  `CharacterBody2D` (:1038-1044). The test uses CharacterBody2D.

### Where to look next (in order)

1. **Is the node actually in `char_entries`?** That filter needs the registered body to
   be `Kinematic`. If `sync_to_physics` registers a scripted CharacterBody2D as Static
   (or does not register it at all), the loop never sees it and every gate above is
   irrelevant. Print/assert `body_for_node(mover_id)` and its `body_type` first — this is
   the cheapest thing to falsify and the most likely culprit given links 1-2 both pass.
2. **Ordering of flag set vs consume.** Physics runs before scripts in a step, so the
   flag set during step N is consumed at step N+1. That works across 30 steps, but if
   anything clears the flag between the script and the next physics phase (a property
   sync writing the script instance's vars back over the node), the request never
   survives to be consumed. Check whether the script→node sync touches unknown keys.
3. Only after those: the movement math past :1082.

### Note on the reported command

The previous attempt reported
`nextest run -p gdscene --test cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test cross_node_script_and_native_method_dispatch`
which selects the binary and filters to the one function — that part is correct and
should be kept; the `4 skipped` in the summary is that filter working as intended.

Releasing the assignment: localizing this needs a real test run, which a no-cargo worker
cannot do. It should go to a build-capable lane, or to whoever can run the command above
and read the failure at step 1 of the list.

My earlier comment asked for a re-verify; the verifier ran it (verifier.log:5177-5178) and it FAILED
again at HEAD, same `(0,0) -> (0,0)`. So the bug is REAL and CURRENT, not stale. Retracting the
"just re-verify" recommendation — that run is what made the diagnosis possible.

## The bug (and why five agents missed it)

`process_character_movement` (physics_server.rs:1689-1706) builds `char_entries` by iterating
`self.node_to_body`. The ONLY writer of that map is `PhysicsServer::register_bodies`, and nothing
calls it from inside the engine — not `MainLoop::new` (verified, it constructs
`PhysicsServer::new()` and nothing else), not `step`, not `sync_to_physics` (which only syncs
bodies that are ALREADY registered). The host registers: `patina-runner/src/main.rs:369` calls
`main_loop.register_physics_bodies()` after loading the scene.

`character_scene` in the acceptance test returned `MainLoop::new(tree)` and never called it. So
`node_to_body` was EMPTY, `char_entries` was empty, and the loop body never executed for any node.
Every gate everyone traced — Kinematic body_type, the class_name check, the
`_move_and_slide_requested` one-shot, the idle-velocity skip — is downstream of a loop that had
nothing to iterate. That is why the body sat at exactly its spawn position and why link 1 and
link 2 both passed: dispatch was always fine; the body was simply not in the physics world.

MistyStone's very first hypothesis ("is the node actually in char_entries?") was RIGHT. It got
"falsified" because the follow-up checked that `body_type_for_class` maps CharacterBody2D =>
Kinematic and that registration has no script gate — i.e. it checked that registration would work
IF CALLED, and never checked whether anything called it.

## The tell that cracked it

The sibling test `characterbody2d_move_and_slide_script_dispatch.rs` covers the same mechanism and
has PASSED three times since (log:4210/4291/4402). Diffing the two fixtures: lines 108-114 of the
passing one call `ml.register_physics_bodies()` and carry a comment explaining exactly this trap.
The failing fixture does not. Same engine, same mechanism, one line apart.

## Fix (test-only; no engine change)

crates/gdscene/tests/cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test.rs
- `character_scene` now calls `ml.register_physics_bodies()`, with a comment naming the contract.
- Same one-line fix in `move_and_slide_is_callable_on_another_node` and
  `unscripted_character_body_still_auto_moves` — both had the identical omission and would have
  fail-fasted the binary right after link 3 was fixed.
- Idler moved from (0,0) to (200,0). It was spawned coincident with the Mover (both r=10), so once
  the bodies are actually registered, link 3 would have been exercising character-vs-character
  depenetration rather than the dispatch under test. No assertion weakened: the idler check is on
  `.y` only, and x=200 is well inside the 1000-wide floor.

No assertion was relaxed and no engine semantics changed. The gate this bead installed
(scripted bodies move only when the script asks) is untouched and still under test.

## Separate gap worth its own bead (NOT fixed here)

Godot adds a CollisionObject2D to the physics space on tree entry; Patina requires an explicit
host call. `patina-runner` makes it, but anything that builds or grows a tree at runtime
(`add_child` during play, instantiating a PackedScene, the editor play path) gets a body that is
silently inert — no error, just no physics. Worth checking whether the editor play path calls it.
I did not touch this: it is an engine-wide semantic change and out of scope for this bead.

Verify: -p gdscene --test cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test  (all 5 tests)

comments.text:
FRESH FAIL 2026-07-27 21:22 UTC (FuchsiaStream) — the "stale failure" hypothesis is REFUTED. This bug is LIVE.

The re-verify that MistyStone, WildIsland and HazyFinch all asked for HAS NOW RUN — twice, minutes ago —
and it FAILED both times with the SAME fingerprint as the July-25 report:

  verifier.log:5177-5178  FAIL pat-0q2kx.16  run_ms=8657   (--test cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test)
  verifier.log:5189-5190  FAIL pat-0q2kx.16  run_ms=10333  (+ function filter)

  cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test.rs:282
  link 3: the physics phase must honor the move_and_slide request,
  start Vector2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 } -> Vector2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }

Identical file:line, identical message, identical values. Nothing between 07-25 and now fixed it.
HazyFinch's "expect it to close with zero code change" is disproven — do NOT close this on inspection.

Note the shape of the failure: the body is at EXACTLY (0,0) after 30 steps. Not drifting, not
short — it never moved a single pixel. At 400 px/s and dt=1/60 one honored step is ~6.7 px, and
29 steps would be ~193 px against a floor at y=200. So the movement branch is not producing a
small/wrong delta; it is not executing, or its write-back is not landing.

## WildIsland's hypothesis 1 (ordering) is ALSO FALSIFIED

They suspected process_character_movement might run outside the accumulator loop and so execute zero
times at 60fps/60tps. It does not:

  main_loop.rs:2717  while self.physics_accumulator >= physics_dt && physics_steps < max
  main_loop.rs:2721      sync_to_physics
  main_loop.rs:2722      step_physics
  main_loop.rs:2723      sync_from_physics
  main_loop.rs:2740      process_character_movement   <-- INSIDE the loop, every tick

So both of WildIsland's ranked hypotheses and MistyStone's step-1 hypothesis are now eliminated.

## The one gap left in the existing refutations

WildIsland "falsified" the registration hypothesis by showing physics_server.rs:36 maps
"CharacterBody2D" => Kinematic and that the filter at :1696-:1699 matches on both body_type and
class_name. That proves the MAPPING is right — it does NOT prove the node is in `node_to_body` at
all. char_entries is built by iterating `self.node_to_body` (:1691-1706); a node absent from that map
is invisible to every gate below it, and the symptom would be exactly this: flag set (link 2 passes),
zero motion, position untouched at (0,0).

Worth noting the flag would also never be consumed in that case, since the consume at :1731 sits
inside the same loop body. That is a cheap discriminator: assert
`_move_and_slide_requested` is FALSE after a step in which physics should have honored it. If it is
still TRUE, the loop never reached this node and the bug is registration, not movement math.

The other live candidate is the write-back at :1812 (`node2d::set_global_position`) silently not
landing in the `position` property.

I am NOT taking this bead — it is assigned to CalmCrane and I have written no code for it. Posting
because three agents in a row concluded "stale, just re-verify", and the re-verify has now happened
and says otherwise.

comments.author: CalmCrane
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-27 (CalmCrane). The failure is NOT stale — I was wrong earlier today,
and so was the 07-26 memo predicting it "likely no longer reproduces". The re-verify I requested
came back FAIL, live, at the same link 3 with the same `(0,0) -> (0,0)`:

  verifier.log:5189  START bead=pat-0q2kx.16 stale=false
  verifier.log:5190  FAIL  run_ms=10333  (100, panic)
  verifier.log:5192  cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test.rs:282
                     link 3: start Vector2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 } -> Vector2 { x: 0.0, y: 0.0 }

## The bug was never in the engine — it is the TEST FIXTURE

`MainLoop::step` does not register physics bodies, and neither does `MainLoop::new`.
`PhysicsServer::register_bodies` (physics_server.rs:906) is the ONLY writer of `node_to_body`,
exposed as `MainLoop::register_physics_bodies` (main_loop.rs:2088), and NOTHING calls it
internally — grep shows ~50 call sites and every one of them is a test or a host doing it by hand.

`process_character_movement` builds `char_entries` by iterating `node_to_body`
(physics_server.rs:1691). Empty map => empty entries => the loop body never runs for any body.

So the mover never moved because the physics phase had no body to act on. Every gate the four
previous passes traced — Kinematic registration, the `has_script` gate, the one-shot flag, the
idle skip, `move_and_slide_delta`, the node write-back — was correct AND unreachable.

## Why this is the signature we all misread

Position stayed at EXACTLY (0,0), never a fraction, never a drift. That is not a movement bug;
that is code that did not execute. Four static passes (MistyStone, WildIsland, HazyFinch, and my
own earlier one today) each traced deeper INTO `process_character_movement` and confirmed the
chain — which was true and irrelevant. Nobody checked whether the loop had anything to iterate.

## The differential that gives it away

`characterbody2d_move_and_slide_script_dispatch` (pat-0q2kx.33) exercises this same physics chain
and PASSES — verifier.log:4209/4290 PASS under .200 and .213. Its fixture, at test :108-114, calls
`ml.register_physics_bodies()` and carries a comment saying exactly why it must. This file's
fixtures never did. Same subsystem, same scene shape, one call apart.

## Status

Already fixed in the working tree by a concurrent agent, in all three fixtures that build bodies:
`character_scene`, `move_and_slide_is_callable_on_another_node`,
`unscripted_character_body_still_auto_moves`. Their change also separates the Mover/Idler
coincident spawn (Idler to x=200), which removes the depenetration-vs-dispatch confound that the
07-26 memo flagged as a test-design smell. No assertion was weakened. I made no edit — I confirmed
theirs is complete and am routing it to the verifier.

## Deliberately NOT done

Making `MainLoop::step` auto-register bodies. It is arguably the real parity gap (Godot registers
on tree entry), but it would change behavior under ~50 existing call sites and belongs to the
physics-lifecycle surface, not to this bead's method-dispatch scope. Worth its own bead.

comments.text:
WildIsland analysis 2026-07-27 ~03:40 — claimed pat-0q2kx.16 from the ready queue. NOT reporting
complete. This narrows MistyStone's list by inspection alone (I am also a no-cargo lane, but their
step-1 hypothesis turned out to be statically checkable).

## FIRST: MistyStone's line numbers are STALE

They cite process_character_movement at :1031 and the flag consumer at :1067. Those are now :1689 and
:1725. physics_server.rs has changed materially since that diagnosis, so their conclusions should be
re-derived, not trusted.

## Hypothesis 1 (their "most likely culprit") is FALSIFIED

"Is the node actually in char_entries? ... If sync_to_physics registers a scripted CharacterBody2D as
Static (or not at all), the loop never sees it."

  physics_server.rs:36   "CharacterBody2D" => Some(BodyType::Kinematic)
  physics_server.rs:1696 filter requires body_type == Kinematic
  physics_server.rs:1699 AND node.class_name() == "CharacterBody2D"

The registration maps to Kinematic and the filter matches on both conditions. No need to spend a
build run on this one.

## The rest of the chain is present and correct

  - flag SET:       scripting.rs:1300  n.set_property("_move_and_slide_requested", true) on the NODE
  - flag READ:      physics_server.rs:1725
  - flag CLEARED:   physics_server.rs:1731 (one-shot, as designed)
  - motion:         character.move_and_slide_delta(velocity, dt, &obstacles)  (~:1794)
  - NODE write-back EXISTS: crate::node2d::set_global_position(tree, node_id, new_position) (~:1812)
    plus velocity / platform_velocity / is_on_floor / is_on_wall / is_on_ceiling
  - the test's script calls move_and_slide() EVERY _physics_process, so the one-shot flag is re-armed
    each tick

So: gate satisfied, motion computed, write-back present. Position staying exactly (0,0) after 29
steps is therefore NOT explained by anything on MistyStone's list.

## Where I would look next (updated, in order)

1. ORDERING INSIDE ONE TICK. The test comments assert "the physics phase runs before scripts". If
   process_character_movement runs BEFORE the script phase in the same tick, tick 1 skips (flag
   false), the script arms it, and tick 2 should move. Confirm process_character_movement is actually
   called on every tick of the loop in main_loop.rs, not once per step() or outside the accumulator
   loop — if it is called before the accumulator loop it may run zero times at 60fps/60tps.
2. THE VELOCITY WRITE-BACK. The same block writes `velocity` back from `result_velocity`. If
   move_and_slide_delta returns ~zero (e.g. no obstacles => a degenerate slide result), the node's
   velocity is overwritten with 0 on the first move and every later tick reads 0 — which would look
   exactly like "never moved" while every gate passes. Check what move_and_slide_delta returns with
   an EMPTY obstacle set.
3. Only then the movement math itself.

Suspicion ranking: (2) fits the evidence best — it explains a body that passes every gate, moves
zero distance, and stays at exactly the start position rather than drifting.

## Honest limit

I cannot run the suite. What is above is static tracing only. The decisive experiment is still
MistyStone's: run the target and print body_type + velocity + the flag at the top of each tick.
Verify command (as they noted, the binary + function filter is correct):
  -p gdscene --test cross_node_and_native_method_dispatch_test cross_node_script_and_native_method_dispatch

Environment (interpreter.rs:245) is a Vec<HashMap<String, Variant>> with clean define/set/pop_scope hooks, so binding-based refcounting looks like a tidy three-site change. That breaks one of two ways: decrements are MISSED (nothing frees, so the acceptance's "reports gone" never fires), or the clone pops its scopes and PREMATURELY FREES an object the original still holds. Give Environment a hand-written Clone that increments every refcounted ObjectId it copies and a Drop that decrements what it holds — real RAII, correct by construction rather than by remembering a hook; pop_scope then only decrements the HashMap it discards. If a simpler route is wanted, note that Clone for Interpreter is ALREADY hand-written, so an increment pass can be added there, and with no Drop on Environment a dropped clone LEAKS rather than double-frees — imprecise but never corrupting. Erring toward a leak is the right bias here.

  + is_instance_valid fixed for non-scene objects (it returned `true` unconditionally with no
    SceneAccess, so a released RefCounted still read as valid)
  + 14 tests: gdobject --lib refcounted_handle, gdscript-interop --test refcounted_script_lifecycle
  + the acceptance test refcounted_weakref_lifecycle now EXISTS (was absent from the tree entirely),
    #[ignore]d pending auto-free. ⚠️ Never report it as a passing command while ignored — a skipped
    test exits 0.

REMAINING, ALL OF IT COMPILER-GATED:
  - Auto-free on scope exit. Four sites: define/define_const take a reference; set must RELEASE THE
    OLD VALUE before taking the new (else `var a = r; a = other` leaks r permanently — this one was
    in no prior analysis); pop_scope releases the discarded scope; Clone for Environment increments
    what it copies. Environment::get returns v.clone() (interpreter.rs:342), so ownership must key
    off binding sites, not Variant copies.
    Safe shape: hand-written Clone that increments, NO Drop — a dropped clone then leaks rather than
    double-frees. refcounted_handle::unreference already no-ops on unknown handles, so the only
    sharp edge left is decrementing a still-LIVE handle, which the set and Clone cases guard.
  - `extends RefCounted` instances (acceptance clause 4) — entangled with the above; the
    script-instance construction path differs from the builtin .new() gate.
  - Remove the #[ignore] once those land.

Three agents have now independently reached the same conclusion about the auto-free core (WildIsland,
FuchsiaEagle, me). I read the code myself rather than deferring, and found the design MORE delicate
than the earlier notes, not less. A blind edit here frees live objects out from under unrelated
scripts, intermittently, in the crate everything depends on.

Ready for a build-capable lane. Everything it needs is in this bead's comments.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
BLOCKED 2026-07-26 (WildIsland) — the routing this bead describes is NOT wiring; it needs a new injected trait seam. Set to blocked only to stop the reassign livelock (the automated coordinator does not act on bead-blocked mail). Status change only; done/close remains the coordinator's.

THE ARCHITECTURAL FINDING, which is not visible from the bead text:
The bead says "route EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem()/get_file_system_dock()/get_editor_paths() to the existing implementations", which reads like a lookup. It cannot be done that way:
- gdeditor DEPENDS ON gdscript-interop (gdeditor/Cargo.toml:27).
- gdscript-interop therefore CANNOT depend on gdeditor — that is a dependency cycle.
- EditorInterface is not bound in the interpreter at all today (0 hits for "EditorInterface" in gdscript-interop/src), so there is nothing to extend either.

So a @tool script cannot reach gdeditor's EditorFileSystem by any direct call. The interpreter reaches downstream capability exactly one way: an injected trait. See `pub trait SceneAccess` (gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:301) with the `scene_access` field on Interpreter — the scene is reached through that seam, not by depending on gdscene.

WHAT THE FIX ACTUALLY IS: define an `EditorAccess` trait in gdscript-interop mirroring SceneAccess (get_filesystem_root, dir_subdir/dir_file_count/dir_file_path/dir_file_type, editor paths getters), add an `editor_access: Option<Box<dyn EditorAccess>>` field on Interpreter, implement it in gdeditor over the existing filesystem.rs, and bind `EditorInterface` in the interpreter to dispatch through it. That is a genuine architectural addition across two crates plus a new injection point — not a registration change.

VERIFIED STATE, so nobody redoes it:
- Acceptance test editor_filesystem_service_reachable_via_editorinterface does not exist.
- NONE of the six classes are registered: EditorFileSystem, EditorFileSystemDirectory, FileSystemDock, EditorResourcePreview, EditorPaths, EditorFileDialog all have 0 hits in class_db.rs.
- gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs DOES have a real EditorFileSystem (scan, files, files_by_extension, resolve_res_path, to_res_path, file_exists, get_modified_time, UID map, list_dir -> Vec<DirChild>). The bead is right that the implementation exists; it is only unreachable from script.
- NOTE list_dir is `list_dir(&self, _res_path: &str)` — the parameter is UNUSED (leading underscore), so directory walking is not actually implemented per-path yet. Whoever wires EditorFileSystemDirectory.get_subdir() should check that before assuming it can enumerate a subtree.

SAFE NO-CARGO SPLIT: registering the six classes in ClassDB (with their documented method/signal surfaces) is mechanical, contained, and carries no architectural risk — it is also explicitly part of the acceptance ("the classes are ClassDB-registered"). It cannot satisfy the bead alone, since the acceptance also requires a @tool script to walk the tree through EditorInterface, so it wants to be its own bead rather than a partial here. I am happy to take that slice immediately if it is split out.
