comments.text:
PARTIAL 2026-07-27 (CalmCrane). Claimed cleanly from the BLOCKED pool — no blocking dependency, no
assignee (`br update` reported `(none) -> CalmCrane`).

## Delivered: 4 of the 6 classes, registered against the DOC XML

`EditorFileSystem` + `FileSystemDock` are implemented natively (gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs:19 and
:332) but ClassDB knew nothing about them, so a @tool script had no class to reach them through and
`EditorFileSystemDirectory` — the type a script WALKS to enumerate the project — did not exist.

New `register_editor_filesystem_classes()` in class_db.rs, called from `register_editor_classes`:

  EditorFileSystem           -> Node    9 methods, 6 signals
  EditorFileSystemDirectory  -> Object  14 methods
  EditorPaths                -> Object  6 methods
  EditorResourcePreview      -> Node    5 methods, 1 signal

Every signature is from `upstream/godot/doc/classes/*.xml`, not from Patina's implementation. The
two do NOT line up — Patina's `EditorFileSystem::scan()` returns a count where Godot's returns void,
and Patina has no `EditorFileSystemDirectory` type at all. ClassDB describes GODOT's surface, which
is what a ported script looks for.

## The bead description is WRONG about two parents — do not copy them

  bead says: EditorFileSystem <- Object      4.6.1 doc XML: <- Node
  bead says: FileSystemDock  <- VBoxContainer 4.6.1 doc XML: <- EditorDock

I used the doc XML. Parents are load-bearing: `Node::is_class` resolves through ClassDB, so a
mis-parented class silently drops out of every walk that consults it. The test pins both.

Also corrected by the oracle: `queue_resource_preview` takes 4 args, not the 1-2 a reader would
guess.

## NOT registered, and why — 2 of 6 have UNREGISTERED PARENTS

  FileSystemDock    needs EditorDock  -> `ClassRegistration::new("EditorDock")` count = 0
  EditorFileDialog  needs FileDialog  -> `ClassRegistration::new("FileDialog")` count = 0

Registering a class against a base that is not itself registered truncates the inheritance chain,
which is the exact silent breakage this bead exists to fix. Registering EditorDock/FileDialog to
unblock them pulls in two unrelated class families (docks, dialogs) with their own doc surfaces —
wider than this bead. Left undone deliberately rather than shipped broken.

(The bead's `EditorFileDialog <- ConfirmationDialog` would "work" — ConfirmationDialog IS registered
— but it is wrong for 4.6.1, and a wrong parent is worse than an absent class.)

## Tests

`crates/gdobject/tests/editor_filesystem_classes_registered.rs`, 4 tests: documented parents;
documented methods (incl. the `get_filesystem` entry point this bead's acceptance names, and the
full EditorFileSystemDirectory walk surface); documented signals; and idempotent re-registration,
since `register_editor_classes` is reachable from several entry points and each block guards on
`class_exists`.

## Remaining scope

The acceptance test `editor_filesystem_service_reachable_via_editorinterface` does not exist and I
did not add it: it requires routing `EditorInterface.get_resource_filesystem()` /
`get_file_system_dock()` / `get_editor_paths()` through the interpreter to the native impls, plus a
script-visible EditorFileSystemDirectory handle. That is interpreter work, and
gdscript-interop/src/{interpreter,parser}.rs are BOTH dirty with foreign WIP right now — that crate
has broken the shared lane repeatedly today. A blind edit there from a no-cargo lane risks a
crate-wide outage. Registration is the prerequisite and is what I delivered.

Note `EditorInterface` is already registered WITH `get_file_system_dock` (class_db.rs:12832) — the
method was declared while the class it returns did not exist. That half is now closed.

## Verification limit

No-cargo lane (AGENTS.md:88). rustfmt --check clean on both files. Name-resolution checked by hand:
`ClassRegistration`/`MethodInfo`/`SignalInfo` are `pub struct`s in class_db.rs itself (no import
needed), `class_exists`/`register_class` are file-local `pub fn`s, `register_editor_filesystem_classes`
occurs exactly once (no E0428), and every test import is re-exported at the crate root
(gdobject/src/lib.rs:31-35) with `pub mod class_db` at :20.

title: Navigation: runtime bake pipeline — 2D outline triangulation with carving, 3D source parsing + param-honoring bake, regi
description:
[audit-key: navigation/navigation-baking] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/navigation_2d/2d/nav_mesh_generator_2d.cpp (parse+carve+triangulate via clipper/poly-partition), modules/navigation_3d/3d/nav_mesh_generator_3d.cpp (Recast voxel bake), doc/classes/NavigationRegion3D.xml bake_navigation_mesh/is_baking/bake_finished

Godot ground truth: (2D) nav_mesh_generator_2d.cpp parses traversable/obstruction outlines from scene geometry per parsed_geometry_type/source_geometry_mode, carves obstructions and NavigationObstacle2D carve vertices (clipper), offsets by agent_radius, then convex-partitions/triangulates per sample_partition_type — NavigationPolygon.make_polygons_from_outlines is the manual entry; (3D) nav_mesh_generator_3d.cpp parses MeshInstance3D/colliders into NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D then runs a Recast bake honoring cell_size/cell_height/agent params/region sizes/edge params/filters; NavigationRegion2D.bake_navigation_polygon(on_thread) / NavigationRegion3D.bake_navigation_mesh emit bake_finished with is_baking during. Patina current state: 3D bake is a per-triangle slope+inradius filter ignoring nearly every param it copies (gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309-385) with no non-test callers; 2D has nothing (make_polygons_from_outlines grep = 0); no source parsing from nodes; no region bake methods/signals. Implementation (stage 1, 2D): implement outline->polygon pipeline in a new gdscene (or gdserver2d) module — ear-clip triangulation + convex partition of traversable outlines minus obstruction outlines and NavigationObstacle2D carve polygons, agent_radius offset; expose as NavigationPolygon methods (add_outline/make_polygons_from_outlines/clear...) and NavigationServer2D.bake_from_source_geometry_data + parse_source_geometry_data reading StaticBody2D/Polygon2D/TileMap children per source_geometry_mode; add NavigationRegion2D.bake_navigation_polygon dispatch + bake_finished emission. Stage 2 (3D) may follow as its own bead: source parsing from MeshInstance3D/collision shapes + a real voxel bake honoring cell/agent/region/edge/filter params. Wiring requirement: script or editor calls region.bake_* on a live scene and the resulting polygons immediately feed the runtime map (path query succeeds post-bake).

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. bake_navigation_mesh (gdserver3d/src/navigation.rs:309-368) only filters triangles by agent_max_slope and inradius-vs-agent_radius; cell_size/cell_height/agent_height/agent_max_climb/region_min_size/edge_max_length/filter_* are copied into the output struct (370-379) but never used in the bake - no voxelization/merge. It is not wired to the game runtime: bake_navigation_mesh / g

**Prove it:** In a loaded scene, calling bake_navigation_polygon on a NavigationRegion2D whose NavigationPolygon has one traversable outline and one obstruction outline produces polygons that exclude the hole, fires bake_finished, and an agent immediately paths around the carved hole; NavigationPolygon.make_polygons_from_outlines standalone matches. (test: `navigation_polygon_bake_from_outlines_carves`) runnable via cargo nextest --test navigation_polygon_bake_from_outlines_carves
acceptance_criteria: In a loaded scene, calling bake_navigation_polygon on a NavigationRegion2D whose NavigationPolygon has one traversable outline and one obstruction outline produces polygons that exclude the hole, fires bake_finished, and an agent immediately paths around the carved hole; NavigationPolygon.make_polygons_from_outlines standalone matches. (test: `navigation_polygon_bake_from_outlines_carves`) runnable via cargo nextest --test navigation_polygon_bake_from_outlines_carves

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
## Diagnosis 2026-07-25 (MistyStone): most of this is wired; what remains needs a test run to localize

Handing back with findings rather than a speculative fix. A no-cargo worker cannot
localize a failing pixel assertion, and guessing at a render path is the likeliest way
to make it worse. This should go to a build-capable lane, or to a worker who can run:

    nextest run -p gdeditor --test play_view_renders_controls_e2e

### What is ALREADY wired (contrary to the bead description)

The description says the Play path draws only Sprite2D/Polygon2D/Line2D/ColorRect/Label
and that render_control_tree has no callers. That is now out of date:

- `gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:459` has `build_control_render_items(tree, root, size)`,
  which is the whole wiring the bead asks for:
  - (1) walks the subtree and calls `control::sort_container_tree` at every container
    that is not nested inside another container — the correct entry rule, since entering
    only at the subtree root would skip a container under a plain Control (Panel > VBox).
  - (2) calls `gdscene::control_render::control_draw_items(tree, root, &theme, size)` and
    translates each primitive into a `Render2DItem`: filled rects become
    `Render2DKind::ColorRect`, stroked rects become a closed `Line` polyline, and each
    item carries the draw item's `z`.
- The acceptance test already calls that function directly and compiles against it, so
  the "unwired" half of the bead is done. Note it uses `control_draw_items`, not
  `render_control_tree` — the description's alternative ("port draw_control's per-class
  arms") is effectively the route taken, so `render_control_tree` having no callers is
  NOT evidence of the gap.

### What is still MISSING

- `gdeditor/src/control_binding.rs::invalidate_layout` still has **zero callers** in
  `editor_server.rs` (`rg -c invalidate_layout editor_server.rs` = 0). The bead asks for
  it to be called from the inspector property-set route so anchor/margin edits reflow in
  the edit viewport. This is small, self-contained, and verifiable without pixels —
  a good first move for whoever picks this up.

### The failure

Last recorded run: `failed (100, panic)` at run_ms 6414 (verifier.log 1730/1731) — it
compiled and ran, so one of the five assertions in `play_view_renders_controls_e2e`
tripped. The exact message has rotated out of run.log. The five, in order, are:

1. items non-empty
2. no item falls through to `Render2DKind::Marker`
3. every item's `z_index >= CONTROL_Z_BASE`
4. the VBox produced >= 2 distinct ColorRect y-origins (children stacked, not overlapped)
5. >200 painted pixels, and some ColorRect spans 30–70% of width (the 50% ProgressBar fill)

Assertion 3 is worth checking first: `build_control_render_items` propagates the draw
item's own `z` verbatim, so unless `control_draw_items` already offsets by
`CONTROL_Z_BASE`, item `z_index` values will be small and that assertion fails while
everything visually renders fine. That is a one-line fix if it is the cause — but it
needs the actual failure text to confirm rather than a guess.

title: 2D behavioral nodes: RemoteTransform2D sync + VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D signals + TouchScreenButton input
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/nodes2d-behavioral] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/remote_transform_2d.cpp (_update_remote pushes global or local pos/rot/scale to remote_path each transform change); visible_on_screen_notifier_2d.cpp (rect vs viewport visible rect -> screen_entered/screen_exited, is_on_screen; Enabler toggles process/physics/visibility of target); TouchScreenButton (scene/2d, InputEventScreenTouch/mouse synthesis, shape hit-test, passby_press, pressed/released signals, action injection)

Three registered-or-absent nodes have zero runtime behavior. Godot: RemoteTransform2D pushes its (global|local) position/rotation/scale each frame to the node at remote_path (update_position/rotation/scale toggles); VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D tests its rect against the camera-visible rect emitting screen_entered/screen_exited and serving is_on_screen, with Enabler2D auto-toggling the target's processing; TouchScreenButton hit-tests touches/clicks against its texture/shape, emits pressed/released, and injects its action. Implement in gdscene/src/main_loop.rs as per-frame phases mirroring process_path_follows: (1) process_remote_transforms — resolve remote_path via get_node semantics, copy transform components per flags using node2d helpers; (2) process_visibility_notifiers — compute visible world rect (viewport size + Camera2D from the camera bead; fallback: viewport rect at origin), intersect with node rect (register the classes + rect default (-10,-10,20,20)), publish is_on_screen and emit the signals on state change; Enabler2D sets the target's process mode; (3) route pointer/touch events in the MainLoop input phase (main_loop.rs:1621 area) to TouchScreenButton nodes (point-in-texture/shape at global transform), set is_pressed, emit pressed/released, inject the named action into the input state. Wiring requirement: signals observable from script connections in a loaded .tscn while frames step.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. RemoteTransform2D registered bare (class_db.rs:3136 parent Node2D only) — grep remote_path/RemoteTransform in gdscene/src = 0, zero sync behavior. VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D unregistered and grep screen_entered/screen_exited/is_on_screen/VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D in gdscene/src = 0. TouchScreenButton registered WITH properties, VisibilityMode enum, and pressed/released signals (c

**Prove it:** (a) A RemoteTransform2D with remote_path to a sibling moves the sibling to its global position after one frame; (b) a VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D whose rect leaves the view rect emits screen_exited once and is_on_screen flips false; (c) a synthetic touch inside a TouchScreenButton's texture bounds emits pressed and sets its action pressed, release emits released. (test: `behavioral_2d_nodes_runtime_wiring`) runnable via cargo nextest --test behavioral_2d_nodes_runtime_wiring
acceptance_criteria: (a) A RemoteTransform2D with remote_path to a sibling moves the sibling to its global position after one frame; (b) a VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D whose rect leaves the view rect emits screen_exited once and is_on_screen flips false; (c) a synthetic touch inside a TouchScreenButton's texture bounds emits pressed and sets its action pressed, release emits released. comments.author: bone
comments.text:
CORRECTION to my 08:08 comment + the real fix (HazyFinch 2026-07-27).

My earlier comment blamed the verify command. Wrong conclusion: the coordinator ran the correct binary form (-p gdscene --test behavioral_2d) twice. The first FAIL was a foreign gdobject break (E0433 Vector2 at gdobject:2822, since cleared). The SECOND FAIL was real and in my code:

  tests/behavioral_2d.rs:629 passby_press_gates_drag_activation
  left: Nil, right: Bool(false) -- "a drag over a normal button does not press it"

Root cause: route_touch_screen_buttons wrote is_pressed ONLY on the frames the state flipped, and bailed early (continue) for a non-passby button receiving a drag. So a button that had never been pressed had NO is_pressed property at all -- a script reading it got Nil, not false. Godot's TouchScreenButton::is_pressed() returns false from construction. Three test cases hit this same hole: the plain-drag case above, touch_outside_the_bounds_does_not_press, and right_click_does_not_press_the_button (the latter two never even reach the router).

Fix (src/behavioral_2d.rs, src/main_loop.rs):
1. route_touch_screen_buttons: the non-passby drag case now holds was_pressed instead of dropping out of the pass, and EVERY button the event reaches republishes its state whether or not it moved. Published before any signal fires, so a handler reading is_pressed sees the state it is being notified about.
2. New per-frame phase process_touch_screen_buttons (main_loop.rs:2913, beside process_remote_transforms) materializes the default on buttons no event ever reaches -- MouseMotion and right-click both return early from the router. It re-publishes the value it just read, so it is idempotent and cannot clobber a press routed earlier in the same frame regardless of phase order.
3. New test untouched_button_reports_not_pressed pushes NO input event at all, which is what separates it from the 3 cases above -- they all reach the button through the router. 14 tests now.

Note fail-fast: only 5/13 ran before cancelling, so the other two Nil sites were never reported. Fixed all three, not just the one the log named.

NOT COMPILED BY ME (AGENTS.md:88 no-cargo). Checked: rustfmt --check clean on all 3 files; gdscene lib cached diagnostics 0 errors; the earlier FAIL exited 100 (panic) not 101, so the crate builds; the set_local_transform E0428 that broke .195/.197 is gone (one definition, node3d.rs:248); all_nodes_in_tree_order/set_property already used 5x in this file.

The writeback primitive the bead requires did NOT exist - only the getter. get_bone_global_pose accumulates parent_global*rest*pose down the chain, so the local pose landing a bone at G is (parent_global*rest).inverse()*G. rustfmt clean.

- gdphysics3d joints are real AND solved: joint.rs PinJoint3D::new(id,body_a,body_b).with_pivots(a,b), Joint3D::Pin(..), world.add_joint -> JointId3D, world.solve_joints.

- PhysicsBody3D fields: position: Vector3, rotation: Quaternion, body_type, mass. Global xform = Transform3D{basis: Basis::from_quaternion(rot), origin: position}.
- skeleton3d: get_bone_count/get_bone_parent(->i64)/get_bone_rest/get_bone_pose/set_bone_pose.

DESIGN: register PhysicalBone3D as Kinematic by default; physical_bones_start_simulation flips those bodies to Rigid via get_body_mut and auto-creates a pin joint to the parent bone's body; per-tick writeback maps body transform -> set_bone_global_pose; stop_simulation flips back to Kinematic so animation drives again.

comments.author: RedGorge
comments.text:
RedGorge 2026-07-27 (no-cargo lane) — the stale-failure call is right, but "close with zero changes"
would have shipped a feature that is DEAD IN THE EDITOR. Found and fixed a real production bug.

CORRECTION TO THE 07:22 COMMENT (third bead I have seen carry this same wrong attribution): it says
the failure was "a compile error in the gdeditor LIB (E0599)". Both FAILs here (verifier.log:4317,
:4348) end with `could not compile 'gdscript-interop' (lib) due to 2 previous errors`, E0599 around
`CallableRef::Bound { inner, bound_args }`. Different crate. The remedy happens to be the same, but
the attribution is wrong and it is being copied across beads.

That break IS gone — pat-0q2kx.69 and pat-0q2kx.153 have both since passed commands that build
gdscript-interop.

THE REAL BUG: a registered ClassDB default silently killed the feature.

  canvas_layer.rs:150  layer_transform()
      if let Variant::Transform2D(t) = node.get_property("transform") { return t; }
      ...otherwise compose from offset/rotation/scale

`transform` is a REGISTERED CanvasLayer property (class_db.rs:8113, default
`Transform2D::IDENTITY`), added by the earlier work on this very bead. And every node built from a
scene is pre-seeded with its class's entire registered default set — packed_scene.rs
`node_with_class_defaults` (:1105/:1141/:1305/:1457), same for scene_tree.rs `create_node`. So in
any process that has called `register_2d_classes()`, EVERY CanvasLayer carries an identity
`transform`, the "explicit transform wins" branch fires for all of them, and offset/rotation/scale
never reach the render list.

The production chain, each link checked:
  editor_server.rs:836  register_editor_classes()
    -> class_db.rs:12208  register_2d_classes()
      -> class_db.rs:8113  CanvasLayer.transform = Transform2D::IDENTITY
  packed_scene.rs:1547  node_with_class_defaults -> set_property("transform", IDENTITY)
  canvas_layer.rs:152   early-return fires -> IDENTITY
  => a HUD authored with offset=(50,20) rotation=0.5 renders at the origin, unrotated.

WHY THE ACCEPTANCE TEST DID NOT CATCH IT: canvas_layer_xform.rs never calls register_2d_classes(),
so ClassDB is empty in that binary, nothing is seeded, `get_property("transform")` is Nil, and the
composition path runs. The test passes for the one reason the editor fails. This is the
classdb-not-populated-in-unit-tests trap in its most expensive form: the test and production differ
in exactly the variable the feature depends on.

THE FIX (canvas_layer.rs): treat an IDENTITY transform as "not authored" and fall through to the
decomposed trio. Costs nothing — composing rotation 0 / scale 1 / offset 0 also yields identity, so
an author who genuinely wrote `Transform2D(1,0,0,1,0,0)` gets the same matrix by the other path —
and when a scene sets BOTH spellings, Godot's set_transform/set_offset are last-writer-wins on one
underlying matrix, so preferring the decomposed trio over a default-valued one is the better guess.

TESTS ADDED (crates/gdeditor/tests/canvas_layer_xform.rs):
  - layer_offset_survives_the_seeded_classdb_transform_default — registers ClassDB, then asserts the
    SAME expectation as the acceptance. The two tests now differ in exactly one variable: whether
    the class defaults are present. It also asserts the precondition that `transform` is registered,
    so if seeding ever stops the test says so instead of silently losing its teeth. FAILS before the
    fix (child lands at (10,0) instead of (60.6, 24.8)).
  - an_authored_transform_still_overrides_offset_and_rotation — the other half of the rule: a .tscn
    authoring `transform = Transform2D(1, 0, 0, 1, 7, 3)` alongside offset/rotation must still win
    (child at (17,3), no rotation). Without this, "skip identity" could silently degrade into
    "ignore the property".
  Safe to register ClassDB in this binary because nextest runs each test in its own process, so the
  global registry cannot leak into the three pre-existing tests.

TWO THINGS IN THIS FILE'S HEADER WORTH CORRECTING (not fixed by me, they are only comments):
  - It says the binary is named `canvas_layer_xform` "so the command stays under the verifier's
    58-character truncation". There is no 58-char cap — that belief has been checked and disproven
    (hundreds of longer commands have run fine). The name is fine; the reason given is not.
  - Its claim that only `transform`, `follow_viewport_scale` and `custom_viewport` were missing from
    ClassDB is now moot: all 9 doc/classes/CanvasLayer.xml members are registered at class_db.rs:8093.
    I verified that against the doc XML rather than trusting the note — my own first grep found only
    6 because the multi-line `PropertyInfo::new` calls do not match a single-line pattern. Anyone
    auditing registration counts by grep should watch for that.

comments.text:
RedGorge 2026-07-27, follow-up after my own FAIL (verifier.log:5457) — second, deeper defect found.
My previous fix was correct but incomplete; the tests could never have passed either way.

WHAT THE FAIL SAID: exit 100 (panic), so it compiled and ran — my canvas_layer.rs change is sound.
The panic was `a_following_layer_tracks_the_camera_scaled` at canvas_layer_xform.rs:69,
"Hud is not in the render list". That is a PRE-EXISTING test, not one I added, and nextest's

I first suspected my own change (a degenerate scale from the composition path could plausibly cull

/`get_offset` likewise default to zero, so for that scene the composition yields exactly IDENTITY —
the same matrix the early return produced. My change is a no-op there. Not the cause.

THE ACTUAL CAUSE — the whole file could never have passed:
  viewport_2d_render.rs:347   if !node.is_class("CanvasItem") { return None; }
  node.rs:319                 is_class() falls through to gdobject::is_parent_class()
No test in this file called register_2d_classes(), so ClassDB was EMPTY, there was no
ColorRect -> CanvasItem chain, `collect_canvas_items` filtered out every node, and the render list
came back empty. All three pre-existing tests fail this way; fail-fast only reported the first. It
went unnoticed because both earlier verifies of this bead (log:4317, :4348) died compiling
gdscript-interop, so these tests had NEVER actually executed — the bead's whole test surface was
unproven, not passing.

Note the symptom hides the cause completely: "Hud is not in the render list" says nothing about
ClassDB. This is the classdb-empty-makes-collectors-return-empty trap.

load-bearing rather than bookkeeping. That fixes all three pre-existing tests AND makes every test
in the file run the editor's actual configuration (editor_server.rs:836), which is what makes the
seeded-class-default interaction reachable from a test at all.

`layer_offset_survives_the_seeded_classdb_transform_default` became a duplicate of the acceptance —
same scene, same assertions, no contrasting variable left. I removed it rather than keep a test

CanvasLayer property. The second matters because registration is what seeds identity onto every

comments.text:
RedGorge 2026-07-27, third defect on this bead (verifier.log:5487). Each fix uncovered the next —
this bead's tests had NEVER executed, so nothing in it was proven.

PROGRESS: the ClassDB fix worked. "Hud is not in the render list" is gone; the render list now
populates. The same test now fails on a real assertion instead:
    canvas_layer_xform.rs:194  "a 0.5-scaled following layer must move half as far as the camera:
                                expected -50, got -100"
Note -100 is the FULL camera distance: `follow_viewport_scale` was completely inert.

NOT MY REGRESSION, and I checked before saying so: the first assertion in that same test
(`canvas_follow == CanvasFollow::Follows(0.5)`) passes, so 0.5 does reach the render item — the loss
happens downstream in `apply_camera2d_view`, which I had not touched. It was unreachable before
because the test died earlier on the empty render list.

THE DEFECT (viewport_2d_render.rs, CanvasFollow::Follows arm):
    let scaled = Transform2D::scaled(Vector2::new(scale, scale));
    item.global_transform = view * scaled * item.global_transform;
Post-multiplying by a scale rescales the basis it is applied to; it does NOT touch `view`'s own
origin. So the layer translated by the full view offset regardless of the scale factor — the
property did nothing at all. For an item at the origin under a -100 camera: -100, not -50.

FIX: scale the view's TRANSLATION instead.
    let followed = Transform2D { x: view.x, y: view.y, origin: view.origin * scale };
    item.global_transform = followed * item.global_transform;

KNOWN DIVERGENCE, deliberate and documented in the code: Godot applies this as a scale about the
VIEWPORT CENTRE over the whole composed transform —
`xfpivot * xfscale * xfpivot.affine_inverse() * xf` in
upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_viewport.cpp `_canvas_get_transform` — so it also resizes
the layer's contents, which is the "pseudo-3D effect" CanvasLayer.xml describes. That needs the
viewport size, which `apply_camera2d_view` is not given, and threading `p_vp_size` through changes
the signature and every call site. Scaling the translation alone reproduces the parallax idiom the
property is overwhelmingly used for, leaves contents at their authored size, and matches what the
pre-existing test asserts. A faithful pivot-based port deserves its own bead.

⚠️ Worth noting the old comment justified the broken form as "matching Godot's parent-with-scale
rather than scaling the finished item — which would also resize the contents." The premise is
wrong: Godot DOES resize the contents. The comment defended a composition that was inert on the
strength of a behaviour Godot does not have.

I checked the other consumer of `apply_camera2d_view` in this file before changing it:
`follow_viewport_decides_whether_the_camera_moves_a_layer` exercises only the `Fixed` and
`DefaultCanvas` arms, both untouched.

RUNNING TALLY for this bead, all three genuine and each only reachable after the previous was fixed:
  1. A registered ClassDB `transform` default (seeded onto every node) made layer_transform's
     "explicit transform wins" branch fire for every CanvasLayer, killing offset/rotation/scale in
     the editor.
  2. No test in the file registered ClassDB, so `is_class("CanvasItem")` was false for everything
     and `collect_canvas_items` returned an empty list — all three pre-existing tests failed.
  3. `follow_viewport_scale` was inert in `apply_camera2d_view`.
The bead was marked PARTIAL by the audit and carried a "re-verify, expect zero changes" note. Three
defects later, the note's advice would have closed every one of them unnoticed.

RedGorge 2026-07-27, FOURTH defect (verifier.log:5508). The follow_viewport fix worked — 2/5 tests
now run and the previously-failing follow test passes. The new failure is MY OWN test, and it is
correct: it caught a real double-application.

  an_authored_transform_still_overrides_offset_and_rotation
  expected (17, 3), got (15.7758255, 7.7942553)

I reproduced that number exactly rather than guessing at it:

  then translate by the AUTHORED transform's origin (7,3) -> (15.7758, 7.7943)   <-- matches to 7 s.f.

comments.author: CalmCrane
comments.text:
CORRECTION + UPDATE 2026-07-27 (CalmCrane).

## First: my earlier "implementation is complete" call on this bead was WRONG

I reported COMPLETE on source reading, evidencing that `layer_transform`, `follow_viewport_*` and
the class registration were all WIRED (viewport_2d_render.rs:605-607, class_db.rs:8091). Every one
of those facts was true. The conclusion was not: the composition those wired calls performed was
double-counting the layer.

Checking that a helper is CALLED is not checking that what it computes is CORRECT. I had the call
sites and stopped there. Recording it because the same shortcut would misjudge any "unwired helper"
bead the same way.

## The real defect, decoded from the failure

  FAIL an_authored_transform_still_overrides_offset_and_rotation
  "an authored non-identity transform must win over offset/rotation,
   got Vector2 { x: 15.7758255, y: 7.7942553 }"

Scene: Layer{offset(50,20), rotation 0.5, transform=Transform2D(1,0,0,1,7,3)}, Hud at (10,0).
Expected (17,3) — the authored matrix is a pure translation, so no rotation at all.

  child (10,0) rotated by 0.5   -> (8.775826, 4.794255)
  plus authored translation(7,3)-> (15.775826, 7.794255)
  observed                         (15.7758255, 7.7942553)

Exact to 7 significant figures. So the authored translation WAS winning, and a rotation of 0.5 was
being applied on top of it — from somewhere else.

Source: viewport_2d_render.rs:362 composes
  global_transform: layer_xform * node2d::get_global_transform(tree, id)
and `get_global_transform` (node2d.rs:102-119) walks EVERY ancestor multiplying
`get_local_transform`, which reads `position`/`rotation`/`scale` by NAME off whatever node it
passes. A CanvasLayer really does carry `rotation` and `scale`, so the layer was contributing a
second time through the walk — and when an authored `transform` was present, it mixed in a rotation
that the authored matrix was supposed to replace outright.

Note this also falsifies the doc comment at viewport_2d_render.rs:595-598, which claims the walk
"passes straight through it and the layer silently reads as identity". It did not read as identity;
it read the layer's rotation/scale as if they were a Node2D's.

## A concurrent agent has already fixed it — verified, not duplicated

Uncommitted in node2d.rs: `get_local_transform` now returns `Transform2D::IDENTITY` for a
`CanvasLayer`, with two unit tests (`canvas_layer_contributes_identity_to_the_walk`,
`a_child_of_a_rotated_canvas_layer_is_not_pre_rotated`). Their write-up reaches the same conclusion
independently, including the authored-transform interaction.

Checked it satisfies BOTH assertions of the failing test:
  get_global_transform(Hud) = T(10,0)      (layer contributes identity)
  layer_xform               = T(7,3)       (authored, non-identity, wins)
  product origin            = (17.0, 3.0)  -> test wants (17,3)          PASS
  product rotation          = 0.0          -> test wants |rot| < 1e-3    PASS

And it does not break the non-authored path: a layer with offset(50,20)+rotation 0.5 and no
authored transform now rotates its child exactly ONCE, via layer_transform, landing at
(58.776, 24.794) instead of double-rotating.

I made no edit. node2d.rs is the file carrying their WIP; I deliberately did not touch it, and did
not reach for the wider change of altering `get_global_transform` itself — that function is used by
physics (`get_global_position`) and the narrower fix at `get_local_transform` is both correct and
smaller.

title: Shaders: screen-reading shaders (hint_screen_texture + SCREEN_UV) in 2D and 3D

Godot: a uniform `sampler2D screen : hint_screen_texture;` samples the partially-rendered screen at SCREEN_UV (canvas: what's behind the item; spatial: opaque pass color), enabling distortion/blur/refraction — one of the most common custom-shader patterns; hint_depth_texture/hint_normal_roughness_texture read the depth/normal prepass (3D). Patina has zero support; the 2D compiler only lists it as an unsupported feature (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1090-1095). Implementation: 2D software path — before rasterizing an item whose shader declares a screen texture, snapshot the framebuffer (gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs render_frame around rasterize_item at 326) and bind it as that sampler with SCREEN_UV = fragment position / viewport size (add SCREEN_UV to the fragment context); 3D software path — bind the color buffer after the opaque pass (renderer.rs draw ordering) and depth from depth_buffer.rs for hint_depth_texture; wgpu paths — copy target texture to a bindable screen texture between passes. Wiring requirement: a .tscn shader sampling the screen texture visibly composites what was drawn behind it.

**Verifier:** Feature genuinely absent: hint_screen_texture / screen_texture appear only as an unsupported-feature string (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1090-1092); no screen/depth/normal-roughness buffer binding in either renderer; hint_depth_texture / hint_normal_roughness grep = zero. **Prove it:** A scene with a red background rect and, above it, a ColorRect whose shader outputs `texture(screen, SCREEN_UV).rgb * 0.5` renders half-intensity red inside the rect (proving live screen sampling), and a 3D mesh with hint_depth_texture renders values correlated with scene depth. (test: `shader_screen_texture_sampling`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Diagnosis 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch, no-cargo lane): the evaluator is arguably CORRECT and the test's expectation is the thing in question. This reduces to one binary decision -- do not "fix" it without deciding which.

Recorded failure (verifier.log:4498), sky_parity_tests.rs:310:
  "down should be COLOR=(0,0,1), got Color { r: -1.0, g: 0.0, b: 2.0, a: 1.0 }"
2 tests run, 1 passed, 1 failed -- the "up" half passes.

THE ARITHMETIC. The shader is
    COLOR = vec3(EYEDIR.y, 0.0, 1.0 - EYEDIR.y)
and the test samples down as EYEDIR = (0, -1, 0), so EYEDIR.y = -1 and
    COLOR = (-1, 0, 1 - (-1)) = (-1, 0, 2)
which is EXACTLY what the renderer produced. The evaluator computed the expression faithfully;
EYEDIR reached it correctly (that is what the passing "up" case proves: y=1 -> (1,0,0)).

The expected (0, 0, 1) is precisely saturate((-1, 0, 2)). So the test is asserting a CLAMPED
result while sample_shader_sky (renderer.rs:1396) returns the raw value scaled by
background_energy, with no clamp.

THE BINARY DECISION -- one of these, not both:

(A) The renderer should saturate sky COLOR to [0,1]. Then the fix is a clamp in
    sample_shader_sky and the test is right as written.
    Against: Godot's sky is HDR. Values above 1.0 are legitimate and are what
    background_energy, bloom and tonemapping consume. Clamping at sample time would crush a
    bright sun and is a real rendering-semantics change the bead never asks for.

(B) The test's expectation is wrong and should assert the mathematically correct
    (-1, 0, 2) -- or the shader should be written so "down" lands in range, e.g.
    COLOR = vec3(max(EYEDIR.y, 0.0), 0.0, 1.0 - max(EYEDIR.y, 0.0)).
    For: the test comment says "red rising with EYEDIR.y", which at y=-1 IS -1. The
    assertion assumes down gives r=0, which only holds under clamping. The test appears
    internally inconsistent with its own shader.

WHAT THE BEAD ACTUALLY REQUIRES (it does not mention clamping at all -- grep for
clamp/saturate/hdr in the bead returns 0): a vertical gradient distinct from the default
procedural sky, verified through the scene->render path, and sky uniforms altering the output.
All three can hold under either (A) or (B).

I did not choose. Picking (B) blind risks masking a genuine missing-saturation gap; picking
(A) blind changes HDR semantics across the whole sky path to satisfy one assertion. Deciding
needs someone who can run the render and compare against Godot's actual sky output for an
out-of-range COLOR -- specifically whether Godot clamps sky COLOR before it reaches the
tonemapper.

Cheapest decisive experiment: render the bead's own .tscn scene with a sky shader whose COLOR
exceeds 1.0 in a visible region and see whether Godot's output saturates or blooms. That
settles (A) vs (B) in one observation.

Note this bead is one of only three in the ready queue whose acceptance is BELOW the
gdscript-interop outage (gdrender3d --lib), so it is verifiable right now. Its second command
(-p gdeditor --lib shader_sky_scene) is NOT -- gdeditor is above the break.

title: Variant: make global hash() match Godot's Variant::hash (djb2/hash_one_uint64), consistent with String.hash()

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
WildIsland — foundation slice done. Bead stays in_progress. NOT complete.

DONE: exported the XR types from gdplatform (crates/gdplatform/src/lib.rs).
lib.rs re-exported ONLY {XrPose, XrServer}, so WebXrInterface — a complete, natively-tested state machine since pat-nzgdu.150 — was unreachable from every other crate. That is why the workspace grep shows zero consumers: not disuse, unreachability. Now exports WebXrInterface, WebXrSessionMode, WebXrSessionState, WebXrSignal, WebXrStub alongside the existing two. All 7 verified as real pub items in xr.rs.

⚠️ DESIGN BLOCKER for the acceptance — please read before continuing this bead.
The acceptance requires: connect to session_started/session_failed on the object returned by XRServer.find_interface("WebXR"), call initialize(), and observe the signal fire with correct args.

That object must be a tagged HANDLE (it is not a scene node), and **no handle family in the interpreter has signals today**. I checked both connect dispatch paths in interpreter.rs:
  - :8387 — connect on a node, resolved through scene access by node path
  - :7242 — Signal.connect, which calls access.connect_signal_flags(source, ...)
Both require SceneAccess and a node identity. A ConfigFile/RegEx/Expression/Thread handle has neither. So  has nothing to bind to.

This is new infrastructure, not wiring. The cheapest shape I can see:
  (1) a per-handle callback registry in the interpreter — HashMap<(raw_handle, signal_name), Vec<CallableRef>> in a thread_local beside the handle tables;
  (2) a  arm in the WebXR handle dispatch that appends to it;
  (3) a drain step that calls WebXrInterface::take_signals() and invokes the registered Callables with Godot's argument shapes — session_supported(mode, supported) and session_failed(message) carry args, the other four are bare.
Note (3) needs &mut Interpreter to invoke Callables, so the dispatch must be an inherent method (as I did for Expression and Thread in .207/.209), not a free function.

Where the drain runs matters and is worth a decision rather than a guess: WebXrInterface::initialize() enqueues its signals synchronously, so draining immediately after each handle method call is enough for the acceptance and avoids inventing a pump. A general 'each interpreter pump' drain (as the bead text suggests) would need a hook that does not currently exist.

REMAINING: (a) grow XrServer to Godot's surface (world_scale/world_origin/reference_frame on Transform3D, interface + tracker registries) — xr.rs XrServer is presently a defaults-only mock with session_active + a fixed head pose; (b) the XRServer interpreter singleton arm, following the CameraServer pattern (ident match ~:1854 + call_cameraserver_static ~:10635) with a handle tag like CAMERA_FEED_HANDLE_TAG (~:9697); (c) register XRInterface (abstract) + WebXRInterface (not instantiable, parent XRInterface) in class_db.rs; (d) the handle method routing + the signal work above; (e) xr/* project settings.

Test target when it lands: -p gdscript-interop --test xr_server  (54 chars with runner prefix; the acceptance's own name xr_server_script_singleton would make it 70 and silently truncate to a missing target).

NOTE: gdscene is currently broken again (pat-0q2kx.233/.235 failing with 'could not compile gdscene'), but this bead touches gdplatform/gdscript-interop/gdobject only, so its verify should not be affected.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Reported complete 2026-07-27. Acceptance satisfied end to end via `-p gdscript-interop --test xr_server` (7 tests).

Root cause was reachability, not absence: `gdplatform/src/xr.rs` has had a complete WebXR session state machine since pat-nzgdu.150 with ZERO consumers, because `lib.rs` re-exported only `{XrPose, XrServer}`. It now also exports `WebXrInterface`, `WebXrSessionMode`, `WebXrSessionState`, `WebXrSignal`, `WebXrStub`.

NEW INFRASTRUCTURE, relevant well beyond this bead: **handle objects can now carry signals.** No handle family (ConfigFile / RegEx / Expression / Thread / Mutex / Semaphore / XR) had them before, because both `connect` paths in `interpreter.rs` (:8387 by node path, :7242 via `access.connect_signal_flags`) resolve through `SceneAccess` and a node identity, which a handle does not have. The shape added here:
  - an `XR_SIGNAL_CALLBACKS` map keyed by `(handle, signal name)`
  - a `connect` arm on the handle dispatch
  - a drain that runs immediately after each handle method, so a signal is observable in the same frame the script triggered it (no interpreter "pump" hook exists to hang it on)
  - the dispatch is an INHERENT method, because the drain needs `&mut Interpreter` to reach `invoke_callable`
  - callbacks are taken OUT of the table before invoking: a callback may re-enter the interface, and holding the `RefCell` borrow across script execution would panic
Copy this shape for any other handle type that needs signals.

`find_interface` is name-keyed, not fresh-per-call. Godot's XRServer owns its interfaces, so a second lookup handing back a new handle would silently give each caller its own session state. Covered by `find_interface_is_stable_across_calls`.

`_set_test_stub` is deliberately NOT a Godot method, and the leading underscore says so. There is no real `navigator.xr` here, and the acceptance explicitly requires "initialize() with a stubbed navigator answer", so the seam has to exist somewhere; a visibly non-Godot name beats smuggling it into `initialize()` as a fake argument.

Verified the bare-method-reference idiom the tests depend on: `interpreter.rs:2565` resolves a bareword naming a script method to `CallableRef::Method`, i.e. Godot 4's `sig.connect(_on_pressed)` form really is supported.

NOT DONE — each independent, each a clean follow-up bead:
  (a) `XrServer` is still the defaults-only mock. `world_scale` / `world_origin` / `reference_frame` math and the interface + tracker registries are unimplemented. `get_hmd_transform` returns a yaw-only basis, carrying no pitch or roll.
  (c) `XRInterface` (abstract) and `WebXRInterface` (not instantiable, parent `XRInterface`) are still unregistered in `class_db.rs`.
  (e) No `xr/*` project settings are parsed.

Binary is named `xr_server` rather than after the acceptance function: `xr_server_script_singleton` would make the verify command 70 chars, past the 58-char truncation where the target silently resolves to nothing. This one is 54.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — verify FAIL in msg 74877, resent as 74896.

The failing assertion was WRONG; the implementation was RIGHT. One test changed, no source changes.

`session_failed_delivers_its_message` asserted `initialize() == false` when a required feature is
unavailable. It returns **true**, deliberately: `initialize()` reports that the *request was accepted
for processing*, not that the session started. WebXR's `requestSession` is async, so the outcome can
only arrive by signal, and Godot's return value mirrors that. The contract is stated at
`gdplatform/src/xr.rs:246` and was ALREADY covered by that crate's own passing native test
`a_missing_required_feature_fails_the_session` (`xr.rs:441`), which asserts
`assert!(xr.initialize(), "the request itself is accepted")`.

I wrote the expectation from intuition about what "failed" ought to return, ~200 lines from a test
that spelled out the real answer. Recorded as a durable lesson: for async-shaped APIs (initialize /
request* / connect / start), assert on observable STATE, never on the returned bool.

The rewritten test is strictly stronger than the original — it now asserts:
  - the request is accepted (true)
  - `session_failed` fired with a message that NAMES the missing feature ("hand-tracking")
  - `is_initialized()` is false — no live session left behind

That last assertion is the one with real regression value: a bug letting a session through despite a
missing required feature now fails here, whereas the old `== false` check would have passed for the
wrong reason. The acceptance test's comment was corrected too — it called the same return value
"must succeed", when it is `is_initialized()` at v[2] that proves the session started.

Because fail-fast cancelled 3 of 7 tests, I re-checked every surviving assertion against the
implementation instead of resubmitting on hope: session_supported drains as [String(mode),
Bool(supported)] matching the 2-arg callback; get_required_features returns PackedStringArray;
find_interface returns ObjectId or Nil so both the `!= null` and Nil assertions hold;
get_hmd_transform returns Transform3D; thread_local isolation holds because nextest gives each test
its own process.

**Wiring requirement:** adding a CopyTransformModifier3D under a Skeleton3D and configuring a setting (apply bone ← reference bone) rewrites the apply bone's pose each frame the skeleton updates.
**Prove it:** build a 2-bone Skeleton3D with a CopyTransformModifier3D copying bone A onto bone B, advance one modifier pass, assert bone B's global pose equals bone A's (scaled by amount).

**Prove it:** class_exists true for CopyTransformModifier3D and ConvertTransformModifier3D (parent BoneConstraint3D); a Skeleton3D with a configured CopyTransformModifier3D writes the reference bone's transform onto the apply bone during the modifier pass, and ConvertTransformModifier3D maps a source axis component onto the configured target (test: `bone_constraint_modifiers_apply`).

**Prove it:** A scene script calls Input.action_press("jump"), Input.set_mouse_mode(MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED), and Input.start_joy_vibration(0,0.5,0.9,1.0); after MainLoop.step: is_action_just_pressed("jump") observed true from a second node's script, MainLoop.input_state().mouse_mode()==Captured, and joy_vibration(0) reports (0.5,0.9,1.0). title: Editor: expose EditorPlugin scripting surface (dock/context-menu/debugger/command-palette classes)
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-plugin-scripting-api] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/: EditorCommandPalette (ConfirmationDialog), EditorContextMenuPlugin (RefCounted), EditorDebuggerPlugin/EditorDebuggerSession (RefCounted), EditorDock (MarginContainer). The @EditorPlugin scripting ecosystem.

[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-plugin-scripting-api] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** EditorDock (MarginContainer) is a dockable editor container; EditorContextMenuPlugin adds custom context menus; EditorDebuggerPlugin + EditorDebuggerSession implement custom debugger panels; EditorCommandPalette (ConfirmationDialog) is the command-palette accessor. These are the @tool/EditorPlugin scripting surface (upstream/godot/editor/plugins/).
**Patina today:** none exist (`rg 'EditorDock|EditorContextMenuPlugin|EditorDebuggerPlugin|EditorDebuggerSession|EditorCommandPalette' engine-rs/crates` → 0). Patina's editor is served HTML/JS (gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs) and exposes no Godot editor-plugin scripting API.
**Implement:** register the five classes in class_db.rs with their parents and the methods editor plugins call (EditorContextMenuPlugin.add_context_menu_item, EditorDebuggerPlugin.setup_session/_has_capture, EditorCommandPalette.add_command, EditorDock as a dockable container), and bridge them to the served editor's dock/context-menu/debugger/command-palette machinery so a @tool script can register into the real editor UI.
**Wiring requirement:** a @tool EditorPlugin script that adds a command via EditorCommandPalette.add_command makes that command appear+invokable in the served editor's command palette.
**Prove it:** load a @tool script that registers a custom command and a custom dock, assert the editor server reports the command in the palette list and the dock in the layout.

**Prove it:** class_exists true for EditorCommandPalette/EditorContextMenuPlugin/EditorDebuggerPlugin/EditorDebuggerSession/EditorDock with correct parents; a @tool plugin script that calls EditorCommandPalette.add_command results in that command being listed by the editor server's command endpoint (proving the class is wired to the served editor, not just registered) (test: `editor_plugin_scripting_api_registered`).
acceptance_criteria: class_exists true for EditorCommandPalette/EditorContextMenuPlugin/EditorDebuggerPlugin/EditorDebuggerSession/EditorDock with correct parents; a @tool plugin script that calls EditorCommandPalette.add_command results in that command being listed by the editor server's command endpoint (proving the class is wired to the served editor, not just registered) (test: `editor_plugin_scripting_api_registered`).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
WildIsland progress 2026-07-27 — the WIRING half is implemented; the ClassDB half is blocked on a
file lease. NOT reporting complete.

## The finding that shaped the design

The bead reads like "register 5 classes", but registration alone would have been inert:
`GET /api/commands` (editor_server.rs) enumerated a `const EDITOR_COMMANDS` array, so a command added
by a script had NO path to the palette however the class was declared. That gap is the real bead.

Also important: `gdeditor/src/editor_plugin.rs` contains a large `EditorPluginRegistry` (docks,
custom types, autoloads) with **zero consumers outside its own file** — it is a dormant module.
Bridging the new classes into it would have produced exactly the inert wiring this bead's acceptance
is written to catch. The LIVE path is `EditorState.active_plugins: HashMap<String,
GDScriptNodeInstance>`, populated by `start_editor_plugin` (editor_server.rs ~15232), which really
does run a @tool script's `_enter_tree`. Everything here targets that path.

## Implemented (5 files, all rustfmt-clean)

1. `gdscript-interop/src/editor_commands.rs` (NEW) — the script-command store.
   PROCESS-GLOBAL (OnceLock<Mutex<Vec<..>>>), deliberately not thread_local: the plugin is enabled on
   one HTTP connection thread and `GET /api/commands` is served on another, so the interpreter's
   usual thread_local handle-table idiom would strand the command on the enabling thread and leave
   the endpoint reading empty. Placed in gdscript-interop because the writer is the interpreter and
   the reader is gdeditor, which depends on it (the reverse placement is not visible). Same
   constraint that put shader_globals in gdvariant on .225. Re-adding a key replaces in place, since
   a disabled+re-enabled plugin re-runs _enter_tree and Godot shows one entry per key. Godot's
   literal "None" shortcut is normalised to absent. 6 unit tests.
2. `gdscript-interop/src/lib.rs` — module declaration.
3. `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` — `EditorCommandPalette` singleton arm +
   `call_editor_command_palette_static` (add_command / remove_command / has_command /
   get_command_count). Only a `CallableRef::Method` yields a callback name; a lambda has no name so
   it is stored absent rather than as a misleading placeholder.
4. `gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs` — `api_get_commands` now MERGES the store with the built-ins
   (script entries carry "source":"plugin"); a plugin cannot shadow a built-in id, because
   /api/command/execute dispatches built-ins by id and a collision would show one command and run
   another. Plus `invoke_plugin_command`: executing a plugin command finds the owning enabled plugin
   by asking which instance `has_method(callback)` and calls it — so the command is genuinely
   invokable, not merely listed.
5. `gdeditor/tests/editor_plugin_api.rs` (NEW) — 5 tests driving the REAL server and the REAL plugin
   path: temp project with addons/palette_demo/plugin.cfg + @tool script → /api/project/open →
   /api/plugins/toggle → assert on /api/commands and /api/command/execute.

## BLOCKED — the ClassDB half

`gdobject/src/class_db.rs` is held exclusively by GrayBeaver (lease extended twice, now to 03:51), so
I have NOT edited it. Still to append inside `register_editor_classes()`:
  EditorCommandPalette -> ConfirmationDialog
  EditorContextMenuPlugin / EditorDebuggerPlugin / EditorDebuggerSession -> RefCounted
  EditorDock -> MarginContainer
  AcceptDialog -> Window, ConfirmationDialog -> AcceptDialog   (BOTH currently unregistered)

The two dialog ancestors are not optional: `inheritance_chain` stops walking at the first
unregistered name, so without them the chain for EditorCommandPalette would be just
[EditorCommandPalette] and the "correct parent" assertion could never pass.

## Two traps verified rather than assumed

- ClassDB is NOT populated for free in a test process. The test explicitly calls
  register_2d_classes() (MarginContainer, RefCounted), register_root_window_chain() (Window) and
  register_editor_classes(); without that the class assertions fail whether or not the registrations
  exist.
- `call_method` is a `ScriptInstance` TRAIT method, not inherent. editor_server.rs already imports
  the trait at line 39 with a comment citing pat-0q2kx.76, where someone hit this before.

Verify target when it lands: -p gdeditor --test editor_plugin_api (54 chars with the runner prefix;
the acceptance's own name editor_plugin_scripting_api_registered would make it 75 and silently
truncate to a missing target).

comments.text:
Cycle 3 (2026-07-27 ~02:28) — still blocked on the class_db.rs lease, but the remaining work SHRANK.

The collision I warned about in 74911 actually happened, and checking for it paid off: GrayBeaver has
landed AcceptDialog (class_db.rs:7835) and ConfirmationDialog (:7869) inside
register_root_window_chain(), with exactly Godot's parents (AcceptDialog -> Window,

So I DELETED my staged copies of those two rather than leaving them guarded. The

more complete than what I had staged.

EditorCommandPalette -> ConfirmationDialog -> AcceptDialog -> Window chain will resolve.

  EditorContextMenuPlugin -> RefCounted
  EditorDebuggerPlugin    -> RefCounted
  EditorDebuggerSession   -> RefCounted
  EditorDock              -> MarginContainer

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Cycle 4 (2026-07-27 ~02:31) — class_db.rs still leased (GrayBeaver, now three overlapping leases).
Still not reporting complete.

Added a SECOND test target that does not depend on ClassDB at all:
  engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests/editor_cmds.rs   (6 tests)
  verify: -p gdscript-interop --test editor_cmds   (56 chars, under the 58 truncation)

Why it exists: the bead's acceptance test must live in gdeditor, because it asserts on the served
editor's /api/commands endpoint AND on ClassDB. That makes it unrunnable until the class registrations
land. This second binary isolates the other half of the seam — that a GDScript can actually CALL
EditorCommandPalette — so it is verifiable right now, and a failure in it points at the interpreter
rather than at the editor or at ClassDB.

Covers: add_command reaching the store with label/shortcut/callback/category intact; has_command +
remove_command round trip (including that a second remove reports false rather than success);
Godot's literal "None" shortcut normalised to absent; re-registering a key replacing rather than
duplicating (the disable/re-enable case); a bare key falling back to the "plugin" category; and an
unknown method raising instead of silently succeeding, so a typo in a plugin script cannot look like
a working registration.

Assumptions checked rather than assumed before writing it:
  - `null` is a real literal here (tokenizer.rs:587) with precedent in
    engine_debugger_singleton_script_reachable.rs passing null to a singleton static.
  - A leading `@tool` is tolerated by run_class: the parser emits Stmt::AnnotationStmt (asserted by
    parser.rs:3218) and the interpreter treats it as a no-op (interpreter.rs:1037). This is the only
    gdscript-interop test using @tool, so it was worth confirming both ends rather than copying a
    pattern that did not exist.
  - Every method the script calls (add_command / remove_command / has_command / get_command_count)
    resolves to an arm in call_editor_command_palette_static.

Remaining blocked work is unchanged: 5 Editor* registrations in register_editor_classes().

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Reported COMPLETE 2026-07-27 (msg 74982), after 4 cycles blocked on the class_db.rs lease.

## How the block was resolved WITHOUT taking the leased file

class_db.rs was held exclusively by GrayBeaver for the whole bead (3 overlapping leases, latest
03:51). Waiting would have burned ~80 loop cycles. Instead:

  - the 5 classes went into a NEW module, gdobject/src/editor_plugin_classes.rs
  - EditorState::new() (editor_server.rs:836 — the editor's real startup path, a file I held) calls
    register_editor_plugin_classes() right next to class_db::register_editor_classes()

That makes them live in the running editor rather than test-only, which is the difference between
this and a workaround. It also fits the codebase: registration here is PULL-BASED (register_2d_classes,
register_root_window_chain, ...) with no central startup call, and class_db.rs is already ~11k lines.

Recommended 1-line follow-up when the lease frees: add
  crate::editor_plugin_classes::register_editor_plugin_classes();
to the end of class_db::register_editor_classes(), so existing callers of THAT function pick these up
and the split stops being something a reader must know about.

## The oracle caught my inventions

Every parent / method arity / property default was read from upstream/godot/doc/classes/<Class>.xml.
My first staged draft had invented set_dock_title, set_dock_icon and set_default_dock_slot for
EditorDock — none exist. Real surface: open/close/make_visible + _load_layout_from_config/2,
_save_layout_to_config/2, _update_layout/1, and properties title / default_slot(-1) / global(true) /
closable / transient / layout_key / icon_name / title_color / available_layouts(5) / force_show_icon.
A WRONG registration is worse than a missing one, because class_exists still answers true.

Also learned from the XML: EditorCommandPalette's real API is only add_command/4 and remove_command/1.
Patina's interpreter also answers has_command and get_command_count — deliberately NOT registered in
ClassDB, so ClassDB keeps describing Godot rather than Patina (same call as _set_test_stub on .236).

## Bugs caught by inspection (no-cargo worker, nothing compiled by me)

1. E0382 in api_get_commands: moved cmd.key_name into the json! literal, then called cmd.category()
   on the partially-moved value. rustfmt reported CLEAN throughout.
2. get_property_list returns INHERITED properties, base-first, WITHOUT dedupe. A forward .find() would
   have read an ancestor's declaration whenever a name is shadowed, so the EditorDock defaults test
   searches .rev() to take the most-derived one.

## Coordination

GrayBeaver landed AcceptDialog + ConfirmationDialog mid-bead — exactly the pair EditorCommandPalette
needed, and in a better home (register_root_window_chain) than I had planned. I deleted my staged
duplicates: the `if !class_exists(..)` guard makes a duplicate a SILENT no-op, so the loser's
properties vanish with no error anywhere. Checking for that collision before pasting is what kept it
from happening.

Verify targets: -p gdeditor --test editor_plugin_api (54) and -p gdscript-interop --test editor_cmds
(56). Plus 4 unit tests inside editor_plugin_classes.rs on gdobject's lib target.

title: GDScript: enforce global-enum membership on qualified access (reject cross-enum EnumName.MEMBER)
description:
[audit-key: globalscope-enum-constant-value-fidelity/globalscope-enum-value-fidelity] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/@GlobalScope.xml (each <constant> is tagged enum="..."; Godot's GDScript analyzer rejects members not belonging to the named enum). extension_api.json .global_enums[].values[] defines each enum's fixed member set.

Godot ground truth: every @GlobalScope enum (Key, Error, PropertyHint, MouseButton, ...) has a fixed member set (extension_api.json .global_enums[].values[]; @GlobalScope.xml constants carry enum="..."). `Key.KEY_SPACE` is valid; `Key.OK` and `Error.KEY_ESCAPE` are compile errors in Godot 4.6 ('Cannot find member ... in enum ...').

Patina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs:600 global_enum_member() delegates ANY member of a recognized enum prefix straight to the flat global_constant() table (via is_global_enum at line 571). Wired at engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:8870 as the fallback of the ClassName.MEMBER resolver. So `Error.KEY_ESCAPE` silently resolves to 4194305. The flat value table itself is 100% correct (all 512 @GlobalScope values verified exact) — only the membership check is missing.

Implementation approach: replace the single flat is_global_enum delegation with a per-enum membership table generated 1:1 from extension_api.json .global_enums[] — e.g. a `fn enum_members(enum_name: &str) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]>` or a match keyed enum->member set — and have global_enum_member() return the value only when `member` is in the named enum's set (still delegating value lookup to global_constant for the shared flat namespace). Keep barewords unchanged.

Wiring requirement: interpreter.rs:8870 must return None for out-of-enum members so the interpreter surfaces its normal undefined-member resolution error instead of an integer.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed on every axis. Patina side verified: global_constants.rs:600-606 global_enum_member() delegates ANY member to the flat global_constant() table when is_global_enum(enum_name) (the 20-enum list at 571-595, count confirmed); flat values KEY_ESCAPE=>4194305 (line 73), KEY_SPACE=>32 (193), OK=>0 (357) are all Godot-exact per @GlobalScope.xml. Wiring is a REAL runtime path, not test-on

**Prove it:** Through the real interpreter dispatch (run_class -> instantiate_class -> call_instance_method -> eval_expr): a script returning `Key.KEY_SPACE` still yields 32 and `Error.OK` still yields 0, while `Error.KEY_ESCAPE` and `Key.OK` raise a resolution error (do NOT return 4194305 / 0). (test: `enum_qualified_membership_enforced`)
acceptance_criteria: Through the real interpreter dispatch (run_class -> instantiate_class -> call_instance_method -> eval_expr): a script returning `Key.KEY_SPACE` still yields 32 and `Error.OK` still yields 0, while `Error.KEY_ESCAPE` and `Key.OK` raise a resolution error (do NOT return 4194305 / 0). (test: `enum_qualified_membership_enforced`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Reported COMPLETE 2026-07-27 (msg 75006). 3D counterpart of pat-0q2kx.219.

## Shared vs separate — the design call

REUSED directly from the 2D module: PhysicsInterpolationMode, INTERP_MODE_PROP,
effective_interpolation. physics_interpolation_mode is a Node property with no dimensionality, so a
second inherit-walk would just be a second place to drift.

SEPARATE state, because the maths differs: 2D blends a scalar angle along its shortest arc; 3D blends
a Quaternion with slerp. Mirroring the 2D shape by storing Euler triples and lerping per axis would
have been the easy copy and is WRONG — Euler angles wrap independently and gimbal-lock, so a body
tumbling through a pole snaps visibly. Quaternion::slerp already existed in gdcore::math3d
(math3d.rs:107).

Already done by .219 and needing no change: the physics/common/physics_interpolation project-setting
gate, and the accumulator fraction. reset_physics_interpolation() now resets BOTH buffers — Godot's is
one call on Node, not one per dimension, and resetting only the matching one would make callers know
which server owns the node and would silently smear a 3D teleport.

## Deliberate deviation from the bead text, flagged not hidden

Bead says "write interpolated transforms to nodes". The blend instead publishes to
__interp_position_3d / __interp_rotation_3d and the raw node transform stays authoritative — the same
choice the ALREADY-CLOSED 2D path made. Writing the blend onto the node would feed interpolated values
into the next tick's sync_to_physics and corrupt the simulation.

## Test robustness: ticks are DETECTED, not counted

1.0/60.0 has no exact binary representation, so 6 frames can accumulate to a hair under physics_dt and
the tick fires on the 7th. A frame-counting test would then sample across a tick boundary and fail
intermittently — a flake, not an honest red. step_frame() observes the `current` snapshot changing
instead, and run_until_ticks() drives to a real tick count. The interpolation-OFF path has no
snapshots to observe, so it counts how many of 12 frames moved the node and asserts it is a small
minority.

Two vacuity guards worth keeping in mind for any 3D physics test:
  - A CollisionShape3D child is REQUIRED; sync_to_physics looks for one when registering the body.
    Without it the ball never enters the simulation and every assertion passes against a motionless
    node.
  - 3D bodies self-register inside sync_to_physics, so there is NO 3D equivalent of
    register_physics_bodies() (that one is 2D-only, main_loop.rs:2088).

Teleport moves the NODE, not the body — sync_to_physics pushes node->body each tick, so a body-side
write is reverted before the step. Cost a wasted cycle on .219; now a comment in the test.

Verify: -p gdscene --test physics3d_interp (52 chars). Acceptance fn: physics3d_interpolation.
5 tests, all rustfmt-clean. Types checked against definitions (Quaternion derives Copy/PartialEq,
Vector3: Mul<f32>, slerp(self, to, t: f32), set_physics_ticks_per_second(u32)) since I compile nothing.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-27 — verify FAIL in msg 75008, resent as 75017. TEST-ONLY change; the
interpolation implementation is unchanged.

## The 2D rule is INVERTED in 3D, and I copied it across without re-deriving it

The teleport section published y = 9.412, the PRE-teleport position. I teleported by writing the
node's position, carrying the rule learned on .219 where 2D's sync_to_physics pushes node -> body for
Rigid bodies too.

In 3D:
  - sync_to_physics sends Rigid bodies to sync_rigid_body (physics_server_3d.rs:1049), which reads
    velocities, forces, damping and flags but NEVER position or rotation.
  - Only Static/Kinematic get their node transform pushed into the world (~:598).
  => The BODY is authoritative for a RigidBody3D. A node-side write is silently overwritten by the
     next sync_from_physics — which is exactly the 9.412 in the tail.

The 2D comment was reproduced verbatim into this test, so the test asserted the opposite of what the
file under test actually does. Nothing errors; the write just vanishes. Recorded as a durable memory.

## Fix

Teleport now uses a CharacterBody3D — the only 3D body whose node transform reaches the world, and
the honest subject anyway since a teleport is a manual move, not a simulated one. Two ticks at
distinct positions (y=10 then y=9) establish a real previous->current blend, then the teleport to
y=-500 plus reset.

ALSO ADDED a control that performs the identical teleport WITHOUT the reset and asserts the blend is
still streaking (> -400). Without it, the reset assertion could pass merely because a teleport moved
something. The original teleport case had no such guard — the failure exposed that too.

## Parity gap found on the way (reported, not fixed — out of scope for this bead)

A RigidBody3D cannot be repositioned from its scene node AT ALL. Godot moves the body when a script
assigns global_position/global_transform; Patina drops the write because sync_rigid_body never reads
position. Any script doing `body.global_position = spawn_point` is a silent no-op. Flagged to the
coordinator as deserving its own bead.

Tick detection (rather than frame counting) was unchanged and is what kept the other three tests
honest through this failure — the one that broke did so for a real reason, not a timing artefact.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch) — needs a BUILD-CAPABLE lane. Diagnosis is complete; I did not implement it and explain why.

THE BUG: self.current_line IS NEVER WRITTEN.
  declared   interpreter.rs:445
  initialised interpreter.rs:710  -> 0
  READ at    :746, :752 (make_location), :5725, :5734
  ASSIGNED   nowhere. There is no 'self.current_line =' anywhere in the file.

So make_location() always returns line 0. Every StackFrame gets source_location = Some(line 0)
(pushed at :6183 with Some(self.make_location()), so the Option is NOT the problem — the VALUE is).
That makes bt.get_frame_line(0) return 0, and the test asserts > 0. 3 of the 4 cases pass; only
frame_metadata_and_out_of_range_indices fails.

BLAST RADIUS — this silently degrades more than this bead:
  - ScriptBacktrace.get_frame_line   (this bead)
  - get_stack()      :4713 — every frame reports line 0
  - print_stack()    :4736 — prints 'line 0'
  - runtime error reporting, which uses the same SourceLocation

WHY I DID NOT FIX IT: the fix needs the AST to carry positions, and IT DOES NOT. I checked:
no Stmt variant and no Expr variant has a line/span/pos field (the only 'line' hits in parser.rs
are ParseError, plus a false positive on the word 'inline'). So a correct fix means threading
line info from the tokenizer through the parser into every Stmt, then setting current_line as
each statement executes. That is a large change to parser.rs AND interpreter.rs — two of the
hottest shared files — and I can neither compile nor test it (worker lane; and the verifier
daemon is currently dead, see mail 75417).

DO NOT 'fix' it by having capture_script_backtraces substitute the function-declaration line.
That would turn the assertion green while get_frame_line still does not mean what Godot means
(the CURRENT line within the frame), and it would leave get_stack/print_stack wrong.

SUGGESTED SHAPE for whoever has a compiler:
  1. add a line (and ideally column) to Stmt — either a field per variant or a Spanned<Stmt> wrapper
  2. populate it in parser.rs from the token position already available there
  3. in the statement-execution loop, set self.current_line before executing each statement
  4. then this test, get_stack and print_stack all become truthful together
Verify with: -p gdscript-interop --test backtrace

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
SCOPE REFINED — smaller than I first said, and the type layer is ALREADY DONE (HazyFinch 2026-07-27). Supersedes my earlier "needs AST position threading, too large" note.

WHAT EXISTS: crates/gdscript-interop/src/script_backtrace.rs is 351 lines and already provides BacktraceFrame, ScriptBacktrace, and a handle registry (insert/get/count/clear). None of that needs writing.

THE ENTIRE GAP is one field never being assigned. interpreter.rs:
  :445  current_line: usize          declared
  :710  current_line: 0              initialised, and this is the ONLY write
  :488  copied into a frame
  :746 :747 :752                     read to build the frame line + source text
  :5731 :5740 :5752                  read for get_stack / print_stack / error text
There is no assignment anywhere else, so every frame reports line 0 and the source-line
lookup at :746 always fails its `> 0` guard.

GOOD NEWS I HAD WRONG: position info already exists at parse time. The tokenizer yields
token-with-span — parser.rs:460-461 reads `ts.line, ts.col` — so nothing new needs computing.
Stmt simply does not retain it.

FOUR DESIGNS, with the blast radius I measured for each:

 (a) add `line` to every Stmt variant
     — `Stmt::` appears 130x in parser.rs alone. Every construction AND match site. Worst.

 (b) change the body type from Vec<Stmt> to a spanned collection
     — `body: Vec<Stmt>` at parser.rs:74,248,259,268,281,341,356 and interpreter.rs:517,
       plus every consumer. Wide.

 (c) inject a `Stmt::Line(n)` marker variant
     — looks cheap but is the WORST for lane safety: Stmt:: is matched 130x parser,
       37x interpreter, 20x type_checker, and 1x in gdscene/src/scripting.rs. A new variant
       on a shared enum is a downstream lane outage (E0004 at every exhaustive match) —
       the exact failure I caused earlier this session with WebXrSignal.

 (d) RECOMMENDED — a parallel `body_lines: Vec<usize>` field beside the existing
     `body: Vec<Stmt>` on the function-def struct (parser.rs:356 / interpreter.rs:517).
     Indices align with body indices; the statement-exec loop sets self.current_line =
     body_lines[i] before dispatching each statement. Additive: touches ONE struct pair,
     their construction sites, and one loop. No enum change, no match sites, nothing
     downstream.
     Limitation: top-level statements per function body only, not nested block statements.
     That is still strictly better than a constant 0 and matches how Godot reports a frame
     (function + line).

⚠️ Even (d) needs a compiler: adding a field means sweeping EVERY construction site of those
structs, and a manual Clone impl can hide a struct literal from the error list. That is why
I did not implement it under the no-cargo rule rather than because the bead is large.

Suggested acceptance beyond the stored test: assert a frame reports a NON-ZERO line matching
the statement actually executing, so the fix cannot pass by coincidence on a 1-line script.

comments.author: FuchsiaStream
comments.text:
READY-TO-EXECUTE PLAN, line numbers verified against the tree TODAY (FuchsiaStream 2026-07-27).
NOT claiming this bead — it needs a build-capable lane. Reasoning at the bottom.

## The whole gap is one field that is never assigned

`interpreter.rs` `current_line: usize` — declared :445, initialised to `0` at :710, and **that is
the only write in the file**. Read at :488, :746, :747, :752, :5731, :5740, :5752. So every
backtrace frame reports line 0, and the source-line lookup at :746 always fails its `> 0` guard.
`get_stack` / `print_stack` degrade the same way.

The types are already built: `gdscript-interop/src/script_backtrace.rs` (351 lines) has
`BacktraceFrame`, `ScriptBacktrace`, and the handle registry. Nothing there needs writing.

Line info already exists at parse time — the tokenizer yields token-with-span and the parser reads
`ts.line, ts.col`. Nothing new needs computing; the AST just does not retain it.

## ⚠️ An earlier scoping note of mine cited `parser.rs:356` for the function-def struct. That has DRIFTED

`parser.rs:351` is now `MatchArm`. The real target is the struct **`FuncDef` at
`interpreter.rs:511`**, not anything in parser.rs. Verify before editing.

## The measured edit list (this is the useful part)

Adding a parallel `body_lines: Vec<usize>` beside `body: Vec<Stmt>`:

  1. `interpreter.rs:511`   struct `FuncDef` — add the field
  2. `interpreter.rs:538`   `FuncDef::from_params_annotated` — the only place that builds `Self { .. }`
                            for the struct (`from_params` at :530 delegates to it)
  3. `interpreter.rs:11307` and `:11323` — the two bare `FuncDef {` struct literals
  4. `Stmt::FuncDef` **variant** construction sites: `parser.rs:1088`, `interpreter.rs:946`,
     `:11255`, `:11390`
  5. the exec loop — set `self.current_line = body_lines[i]` before dispatching statement `i`

Roughly 8 sites. The ~56 `FuncDef` hits in parser.rs are overwhelmingly test destructuring of the
form `if let Stmt::FuncDef { params, .. }` — `..` absorbs a new field, so they do not break. That is
also the hazard: `..` silences the new field at every consumer, so nothing will *tell* you which
consumers still need wiring. Grep the `..` sites deliberately rather than trusting the error list.

## Design note the earlier scoping missed: `exec_block` is a single funnel

`exec_block(stmts: &[Stmt])` at `interpreter.rs:1041` (plus `exec_block_no_scope` at :1065) is where
**every** statement list runs — function bodies, `if`/`while` bodies (:850, :855, :859, :870, :914),
match arms (:988). If a line lived on `Stmt` itself, one assignment inside `exec_block` would cover
nested blocks too.

It still does not justify changing `Stmt`: a `line` field on every variant is ~130 construction and
match sites in parser.rs alone, and a new `Stmt::Line(n)` marker variant is worse — E0004 at every
exhaustive match, including `gdscene/src/scripting.rs`, which makes it a downstream lane outage.

So the parallel-vec design stands, with its limitation stated honestly: **function-body granularity
only, not nested blocks**, because `exec_block` receives bare `&[Stmt]` slices with no companion
line vector. Still strictly better than a constant 0, and it matches Godot's frame granularity
(function + line).

## Acceptance worth strengthening

Assert a frame reports a **non-zero line that matches the statement actually executing** — on a
script of several lines. A one-line script would let a broken fix pass by coincidence.

## Why I am not landing it

Adding a field means every construction site must be swept, and `#[derive(Clone)]`/`..` patterns
hide struct literals from the error list. I cannot compile (no-cargo lane), and `gdscript-interop`
is depended on by gdscene, gdeditor, patina-runner and gdscript-interop's own consumers — I have
watched two `gdscript-interop (lib)` breaks take every lane down today (verifier.log:2598, :5249).
Staking a fleet-wide outage on an unverifiable P3 edit is not a good trade. Handing over a measured
edit list instead.
