comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-27 22:23 UTC (TealIsland). Mail 75840. Supersedes my earlier block (75742),
which was wrong -- see the correction in 75795.

## Design: parallel `body_lines: Vec<usize>`

Carried beside `body: Vec<Stmt>` on BOTH `Stmt::FuncDef` and `FuncDef`, index-aligned. The
function-body exec loops set `current_line` before dispatching statement i.

Rejected alternatives (measured): a `line` field on every Stmt variant = ~130 sites in parser.rs
alone; `body: Vec<Stmt>` -> spanned collection = 8 type sites + every consumer; a `Stmt::Line(n)`
marker variant = E0004 at every exhaustive match in the workspace INCLUDING gdscene/src/scripting.rs.
The parallel vector is additive and stays inside gdscript-interop.

## SECOND DEFECT found while implementing (the plan predicted only the first)

A frame's `source_location` is snapshotted in `call_user_func_impl` when the frame is PUSHED and is
never updated -- so it holds the line of the CALL SITE in that function's caller. For every OUTER
frame that is correct (a caller's current line IS the call it sits on). For the INNERMOST frame it
is wrong, and that is the frame a capture is about.

`capture_script_backtraces` now reports `current_line` for the innermost frame and keeps the
push-time location for the rest. Note `from_call_stack` REVERSES, so Godot frame 0 == innermost ==
`call_stack_frames.last()`.

Without this second fix the whole change would have compiled, looked done, and still reported the
caller's line. Assigning current_line alone is NOT sufficient.

## Sites (all in gdscript-interop; enumerated by workspace rg, then re-counted after editing)

  Stmt::FuncDef variant + its 1 construction site (parser.rs)
  parse_block_with_lines() + current_line(); parse_block delegates (one implementation)
  FuncDef struct; from_params_annotated gained a body_lines param; from_params passes &[]
  4 builder call sites
  3 `..` destructures -- these would have absorbed the field SILENTLY and shipped a no-op
  2 bare accessor literals (body_lines: Vec::new() -- accessors have no line table)
  2 function-body exec loops
  capture_script_backtraces

Checked every Stmt::FuncDef pattern workspace-wide for one lacking `..` (would now fail to compile):
ZERO, including both type_checker.rs sites.

## Test

Added `frame_line_is_the_line_of_the_executing_statement`. The pre-existing assertion is only
`get_frame_line(0) > 0`, which ANY constant satisfies. The new test pins two capture sites five
lines apart in one script against their exact lines (4 and 9) and asserts they differ -- so a frame
reporting its function's first line, the call site, or a constant fails.

## Caveat

Inspection only (no-cargo lane). rustfmt --check clean on all three files; sites enumerated by rg and
re-counted. Nothing compiled -- the verify is the first real check.

comments.text:
Progress 2026-07-27 ~02:55 — NOT reporting complete. Blocked on the interpreter.rs lease.

## The good news: nothing new has to be tracked at call time

The interpreter ALREADY maintains `call_stack_frames: Vec<StackFrame>` for error messages, and
`get_stack()` already exposes it (pat-0q2kx.174, interpreter.rs:4560). So this bead is a SNAPSHOT +
handle surface over state that exists, not new call-stack instrumentation.

Key shapes confirmed by reading, not assuming:
  - StackFrame { function_name: String, source_location: Option<SourceLocation> }  (:188)
  - SourceLocation { line, column, source_line } — NOTE: no `file` field, so get_frame_file() can
    only be non-empty once a script path is threaded in. Empty for string-run scripts.
  - Pushed ONLY in call_user_func_impl (:6030), popped at :6084 / :6096.
  - call_instance_method_impl pushes NOTHING, so a script's ENTRY method never appears in a
    backtrace — only functions it calls. A bare `inner()` inside a method does route through
    call_self_func_or_native -> call_user_func -> call_user_func_impl (:10848), so nested calls DO
    produce frames. The acceptance test must therefore nest at least two levels deep BELOW the entry
    method.
  - I am deliberately NOT adding a push to call_instance_method_impl: it would change every existing
    error message's stack and likely break foreign tests.

## Landed this cycle (no conflict, rustfmt-clean)

engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/script_backtrace.rs  (+ `pub mod` in lib.rs)
  ScriptBacktrace snapshot + BacktraceFrame + a process-global handle registry, with the full Godot
  getter surface taken from upstream/godot/doc/classes/ScriptBacktrace.xml:
    format(int,int), get_frame_count, get_frame_file/function/line,
    get_global_variable_count/name/value, get_language_name,
    get_local_variable_count/name/value, get_member_variable_count/name/value, is_empty
  Engine.capture_script_backtraces(include_variables=false) -> ScriptBacktrace[]  (also from the XML)

  ORDER IS THE SUBTLE PART: call_stack_frames is push-order (outermost first) and get_stack() returns
  it that way, but Godot's ScriptBacktrace indexes from the INNERMOST frame. from_call_stack()
  reverses on the way in, and a test pins frame 0 == innermost. A copy of get_stack()'s ordering

`script_backtrace_captures_gdscript_stack`. rustfmt-clean.

The acceptance reads the backtrace AFTER the stack has unwound (check receives it back through two
returns). That is deliberate: a ScriptBacktrace is a SNAPSHOT, not a live view, and an implementation
that lazily read the interpreter's current stack would report empty/wrong here while sailing through
a naive same-frame test.

Scripts nest check -> level_two -> level_three because call_stack_frames is pushed ONLY in
call_user_func_impl; call_instance_method_impl pushes nothing, so the entry method never appears.
Two frames is the minimum that makes "in order" observable.

## Bug 1 caught: the verify command would have silently truncated

`-p gdscript-interop --test script_backtrace` is 61 chars, past the 58-char cut where the target
resolves to NOTHING and the verifier reports a pass over zero tests. Binary renamed to `backtrace`
=> 54 chars. The acceptance function keeps its full name inside the file.

## Bug 2 caught: handle-tag collision

My staged patch had SCRIPT_BACKTRACE_HANDLE_TAG = 0xE7. That is ALREADY SEMAPHORE_HANDLE_TAG
(interpreter.rs:16542). Two families sharing a tag byte means is_semaphore_handle and
is_script_backtrace_handle both claim the same handles and method calls misroute — with no error
anywhere, because each dispatcher just sees a handle it believes is its own. Corrected to 0xE9.
Tags taken as of today: CA 5B B9 ED E1 C1 C2 C3 E8 E5 E6 E7 E4 E2 E3.

## Design constraint discovered (drives the pending patch)

`call_engine_static` (interpreter.rs:18026) is a FREE FUNCTION and cannot see self.call_stack_frames,
so capture_script_backtraces CANNOT be just another arm inside it. It has to be intercepted at the
dispatch site (:2746) and routed to an INHERENT method — the same shape the XRServer handle needed on
.236.

Full staged patch (dispatch hook, inherent capture fn, instance dispatch, ClassDB block with every
arity taken from the doc XML) is written out at:

`include_variables=true` will be accepted but produce EMPTY locals/members: populating them honestly
needs the per-frame environment scope chain, which call_stack_frames does not record. Empty is
truthful; fabricated values would not be. Will be stated in the completion, and it deserves its own
bead rather than a silent half-implementation.

Reported COMPLETE 2026-07-27 ~03:09 (msg 75077). The interpreter.rs lease lapsed this cycle and the
staged patch went in immediately — the routing request in 75058 is moot.

## Shape of the bead

Not new instrumentation: the interpreter already kept call_stack_frames for error messages
(get_stack() has exposed it since pat-0q2kx.174). This was a SNAPSHOT + script surface over existing
state. No push/pop site touched.

Landed:
  gdscript-interop/src/script_backtrace.rs   snapshot type + process-global registry, 7 unit tests
  gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs        3 additive arms:
     - Engine dispatch hook at the METHOD-call site (:2746, not the assignment site at :1677)
     - inherent capture_script_backtraces (must be inherent: call_engine_static is a FREE fn and
       cannot see self.call_stack_frames)
     - is_script_backtrace_handle + call_script_backtrace_instance (FREE fn — the getters read only
       the snapshot, so unlike XR/Thread it needs no interpreter access)
  gdobject/src/class_db.rs                   ScriptBacktrace registered, arities from the doc XML
  tests/backtrace.rs (5) + tests/backtrace_class.rs (3)

## Frame order

call_stack_frames is push-ordered (outermost first) and get_stack() returns it that way; Godot's
ScriptBacktrace indexes from the INNERMOST. from_call_stack() reverses. Copying the neighbouring
builtin would have been silently backwards. Both orders pinned by tests.

## Four bugs caught before shipping (I compile nothing — each would have cost a verify cycle)

1. 0xE7 tag collided with SEMAPHORE_HANDLE_TAG -> both is_*_handle predicates would claim the same
   handles and misroute every call, no error anywhere. Moved to 0xE9, re-checked free just before
   applying.
2. `--test script_backtrace` = 61 chars, past the 58 truncation where the target resolves to NOTHING
   and a verify passes over zero tests. Binary renamed to `backtrace` (54).
3. Cell/RefCell are NOT imported in interpreter.rs; existing counters use fully-qualified
   std::cell::Cell. A bare RefCell would have been E0433.
4. ClassDB is EMPTY in a bare interpreter — nothing seeds it in production, callers do. Without
   register_3d_classes() in the test helper, ClassDB.class_exists("ScriptBacktrace") answers false no
   matter how well the class is registered. (The one seeding call inside interpreter.rs is in its own
   #[cfg(test)] module — a test helper, not production.)

## Deliberately NOT done, flagged in the report

- call_instance_method_impl pushes no frame, so a script's ENTRY method never appears in a backtrace.
  Changing it would alter every existing error message's stack and likely break foreign tests.
- include_variables=true is accepted but yields EMPTY locals/members: honest population needs the
  per-frame environment scope chain, which call_stack_frames does not record. Empty is truthful.
- get_frame_file returns "" — SourceLocation has line+column but no file.
Each named as deserving its own bead rather than implied as covered.

title: Rendering2D: implement snap-2D-to-pixel, visibility_layer/canvas_cull_mask filtering, and msaa_2d in the software raster
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-quality] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: MISSING]

Godot Viewports offer snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel / snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel (rounds canvas item transforms/vertices for crisp pixel art), per-item visibility_layer ANDed against the viewport's canvas_cull_mask to cull items, msaa_2d antialiasing, and a canvas SDF (sdf_oversize/scale) consumed by GPUParticles2D collision. **Prove it:** With snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel=true a ColorRect at position (10.6, 10.4) rasterizes with its edge exactly at pixel column 11 (no half-covered blend column), and false reproduces the blended edge; an item with visibility_layer=2 disappears when the viewport canvas_cull_mask=1 and appears when mask=3; msaa_2d=4x renders a diagonal Line2D edge with intermediate-alpha pixels absent in the off case (test: `canvas_pixel_snap_and_msaa`).
acceptance_criteria: With snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel=true a ColorRect at position (10.6, 10.4) rasterizes with its edge exactly at pixel column 11 (no half-covered blend column), and false reproduces the blended edge; an item with visibility_layer=2 disappears when the viewport canvas_cull_mask=1 and appears when mask=3; msaa_2d=4x renders a diagonal Line2D edge with intermediate-alpha pixels absent in the off case (test: `canvas_pixel_snap_and_msaa`).

comments.text:
Progress 2026-07-27 ~03:27 — ClassDB half LANDED and tested. Interpreter half NOT done. Not
reporting complete.

## Landed

gdobject/src/class_db.rs — 12 classes registered in register_3d_classes():
  the 9 targets + 3 ancestors that did not exist (XRTracker, XRPositionalTracker, XRInterface).
  Without the ancestors the chains have no base — inheritance_chain stops at the first unregistered
  name, so "correct parent" would have been unsatisfiable. Same situation as AcceptDialog/
  ConfirmationDialog on .241.

gdobject/tests/xr_trackers.rs — 4 tests. Verify: -p gdobject --test xr_trackers (48 chars).
  Acceptance fn xr_tracker_class_surface covers the ClassDB clauses only.

## The doc XML CONTRADICTS the bead text in three places — all now asserted so they cannot regress

  * bead: "XRHandTracker/XRBodyTracker/XRFaceTracker extend XRTracker"
    truth: XRHandTracker and XRBodyTracker extend XRPositionalTracker; only XRFaceTracker extends
           XRTracker directly
  * bead: "modifiers extend SkeletonModifier3D"
    truth: XRFaceModifier3D extends Node3D, NOT SkeletonModifier3D
  * XRVRS extends Object, not RefCounted
Following the bead text would have produced registrations that pass class_exists while sitting at the
wrong depth — invisible to any existence check.

## Method

GENERATED the registration code from doc/classes/*.xml rather than transcribing: 183 enum constants
(XRFaceTracker's blend shapes alone ~60) and a single wrong value is invisible to class_exists.
Verified HAND_JOINT_PALM=0 (named in the acceptance) and HAND_JOINT_WRIST=1 — the non-zero one
matters, since a zero-initialised table would satisfy PALM alone.

MobileVRInterface has NO doc XML (module class); parent and lens properties taken from
modules/mobile_vr/mobile_vr_interface.h/.cpp (class MobileVRInterface : public XRInterface).

3 properties deliberately omitted for want of an honest scalar default: XRFaceTracker.blend_shapes
(PackedFloat32Array), XRFaceModifier3D.target (NodePath), XRVRS.vrs_render_region (Rect2i).
Variant::NodePath takes a NodePath, not a String — the first generator pass emitted a type error
there and was regenerated.

Before running rustfmt I checked that EVERY diff anchor (5204-5597) fell inside my inserted block
(5181-~5600); other agents have WIP in this file and a stray whole-file reformat would pull their
formatting into my diff.

## REMAINING (the other half of the acceptance)

Interpreter reachability: a script must instantiate XRHandTracker, set a joint transform, call
XRServer.add_tracker, and get_tracker must return it with the joint intact. Needs a tracker handle
family + an XRServer tracker registry in interpreter.rs (grep: no add_tracker/get_tracker arms
exist). Comparable in size to the XR handle work on .236. Doing it next cycle.

comments.text:
Reported COMPLETE 2026-07-27 ~03:31 (msg 75160). Both halves in.

## Interpreter half (this cycle)

interpreter.rs:
  - XR_TRACKER_HANDLE_TAG = 0xEA (chosen after enumerating the 16 tags in use; a shared byte makes
    two is_*_handle predicates claim the same handles and misroute every call with NO error — I hit
    exactly that with 0xE7 on .253)
  - ScriptXrTracker + XR_TRACKERS + XR_TRACKER_REGISTRY (name -> handle)
  - XRHandTracker/XRBodyTracker/XRFaceTracker/XRTracker/XRPositionalTracker `.new()`
  - instance dispatch: tracker name/type/hand, hand joint transform/flags/radius, blend shapes
  - XRServer.add_tracker / get_tracker / remove_tracker / get_trackers

KEY DESIGN: the registry stores the HANDLE, not a copy. A snapshotting registry would pass a naive
same-object test and silently drop every joint written after add_tracker. The test therefore writes a
joint AFTER registering and reads it back through get_tracker — that is the assertion with real
regression value.

Joint data is a SPARSE map, not a dense 26-entry array: a dense array would report zeroed transforms
for joints nobody wrote as though they had been tracked. Unset joint reads back as
Transform3D::IDENTITY — that type has NO Default impl, so my first `unwrap_or_default()` was a
compile error, caught by reading the derive list.

## Caught by reading (no-cargo worker, nothing compiled by me)

  1. Transform3D has no Default -> unwrap_or_default() E0277; used ::IDENTITY (the constant other
     code uses).
  2. Variant::NodePath takes a NodePath, not a String — generator's first pass emitted a type error.
  3. get_method_list / get_property_list include INHERITED entries base-first without dedupe, so the
     .rev() search is required to read the most-derived declaration.

## Flagged as NOT done rather than implied

The three modifier nodes are registered but INERT — nothing drives a skeleton from a tracker yet
(needs the SkeletonModifier3D frame loop). XRVRS.make_vrs_texture and the XRInterfaceExtension
GDExtension seam are registration-only too. Each deserves its own bead.

03:35:13 and the failure 03:35:23 — ten seconds apart. The verifier's build almost certainly started

ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-07-27 ~04:08 (msg 75244). The E0004 that failed 5 verifies across 3 beads is
NOT in main. It is in a stale agent worktree.

  main  /Users/bone/dev/games/patina        2d233eb   variant has Bound: yes   interpreter arms: 11  OK
  .claude/worktrees/agent-a464e33c          448c26e   variant has Bound: YES   interpreter arms: 0   <-- E0004
  .claude/worktrees/agent-ac4202b6          68be5e0   variant has Bound: yes(6) interpreter arms: 4  partial
  .claude/worktrees/agent-afb60017          448c26e   variant has Bound: no    interpreter arms: 0   consistent

agent-a464e33c has the new CallableRef::Bound/Unbound variants in gdvariant but ZERO matching arms in
interpreter.rs — exactly the reported error. Note afb60017 sits at the SAME commit and is fine, so the
difference is UNCOMMITTED work inside a464e33c, not the commit.

## Why every diagnosis in this thread failed, mine included

We all assumed the verifier builds the tree we can read. It does not. That is why:
  - brace-matching every CallableRef match in main's interpreter.rs found ZERO candidates (75223)
  - HEAD and worktree both showed 11 arms
  - the error survived ~35 minutes and 5 verify runs while main never changed
No fix applied to main would EVER have cleared it.

## Impact

Parked on this: .13, .263 (both mine, complete and unchanged).
Awaiting re-verify: .16, .34, .36, .39, .69 (all already implemented — 75233).
Seven beads freed by one fix in the right tree.

## Did NOT do

I have not touched any worktree. They are other agents' uncommitted working copies; editing someone's
working state from outside is exactly the kind of collision the file-lease system exists to prevent.

Saved as a durable memory: feedback_unfindable_compile_error_check_agent_worktrees — the tell is an
error that (a) cannot be found by careful search, (b) survives many minutes with no relevant commits,
and (c) hits crates you never touched. That combination means WRONG TREE, not wrong reading. Run
`git worktree list` FIRST next time.

## BLOCKED pending orchestrator redeploy — do not retry yet (MistyStone, 2026-07-25)

This bead cannot pass verification no matter what a worker reports, and the cause is
in the bead text rather than the code.

**The mechanism.** The deployed coordinator harvests commands out of the bead body and
prepends them to the verify set. This description contains

    cargo nextest --test collision_shape2d_subresource_scene_wiring

which is missing the `run` subcommand, so cargo exits **2** at argument-parse time. The
verifier stops at the first failing command, so the worker's own correct command never
executes. Signature in verifier.log: `failed (2, failure)` with run_ms ~1485 and a
command list whose FIRST entry is not one the worker reported (lines 2511/2512).

51 beads in issues.jsonl carry the same malformed string, so this is not specific to
this bead.

**The fix is already written** in apps/orchestrator/crate/src/verifier.rs (parse_acceptance
now reads only `Acceptance:` lines, plus an is_runnable_command guard) and is waiting on
a rebuild + redeploy. Escalated to the coordinator as msg 72626.

**The code for this bead looks complete.** I traced every acceptance clause through the
current implementation before hitting the wall (full detail in completion msg 72624):

- sub-resource geometry: packed_scene.rs stores sub_resource_props and flattens them to
  `__shape__*`; physics_server.rs `v2()` prefers `__shape__size`; RectangleShape2D halves
  it, giving half_extents (32, 8) from `size = Vector2(64, 16)`.
- disabled: find_collision_shape `continue`s past a disabled child, contributing nothing.
- one_way: one_way_collision_for reads the flag off the shape child and copies it to the
  body; the direction assertion holds off the Body default of (0, -1).

**When the redeploy lands,** re-report with exactly:

    nextest run -p gdscene --test collision_shape2d_subresource_scene_wiring

**Known gap, out of the acceptance criteria:** find_collision_shape returns on the first
enabled shape child, so a body with several CollisionShape2D children collides as only
one of them. The description mentions multi-shape; the acceptance does not test it.
Worth a separate bead.

title: Node3D: unify position/rotation/scale/transform into one canonical local-transform state
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/node3d-core] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp — set_position/set_rotation/set_scale and set_transform mutate ONE local-transform state (dirty-flag conversion between euler and matrix forms); reading transform after writing position always reflects the write

Godot (scene/3d/node_3d.cpp) stores one local transform; position/rotation/scale/transform/basis/quaternion are views over it with dirty-flag conversion. Patina stores two competing representations: the .tscn parser writes 'transform' (Transform3D) while set_position/set_rotation/set_scale (gdscene/src/node3d.rs:19-57) write separate keys, and get_local_transform (node3d.rs:75-96) prefers 'transform' when present — so script writes to position/rotation/scale on any node loaded with a transform= line are silently ignored by rendering and physics. Fix in node3d.rs: on any position/rotation/scale write, decompose-and-update the 'transform' key (or delete it and recompose), and route scripting.rs:391 set_node_property through node3d setters for Node3D-derived classes so 'position'/'rotation'/'scale'/'transform' writes stay coherent in both directions. Wiring requirement: .tscn load → script _process sets position → get_global_transform/editor viewport/Play frame reflect the move.

**Merged findings (2):** classes Node3D
- also: gdscene/src/node3d.rs:227-317 implements look_at/to_global/to_local/rotate/translate but the GDScript interpreter dispatch has NO case for any of them (grep '"look_at"|"to_global"|"to_local"|"rotate|"global_position"|"global_transform"|"basis"|"quaternion"' in gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs → z

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. Verified the two-representation incoherence directly: node3d.rs:78 get_local_transform returns node.get_property("transform") first and only composes from position/rotation/scale when "transform" is absent (node3d.rs:82-97). set_position/set_rotation/set_scale write separate keys (node3d.rs:20,37,54) via Node::set_property, a plain HashMap insert (node.rs:260-263) with no decomp

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a MeshInstance3D carrying transform = Transform3D(rotated basis, origin) plus an attached script that sets `position` in _process moves the node: after MainLoop::step, get_global_transform().origin equals the scripted position while the rotation from the .tscn basis is preserved; same for `rotation` and `scale` writes. (test: `node3d_transform_state_coherence`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a MeshInstance3D carrying transform = Transform3D(rotated basis, origin) plus an attached script that sets `position` in _process moves the node: after MainLoop::step, get_global_transform().origin equals the scripted position while the rotation from the .tscn basis is preserved; same for `rotation` and `scale` writes. (test: `node3d_transform_state_coherence`)

title: GDScript: dispatch CharacterBody2D move_and_slide/move_and_collide + floor-state query methods to the physics bridge

title: Physics2D: resolve .tscn CollisionShape2D/CollisionPolygon2D sub-resources into real world shapes (offset, disabled, one
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-shape-load] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

- also: All 3D shape resources registered but zero Shape2D resources (no Shape2D base). Physics builds colliders by name (physics_server.rs:134,144) so .tscn colliders work but CircleShape2D.new()/introspection impossible.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Diagnosis 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch, no-cargo lane): the failing sub-test is a MISSING LAYOUT PASS, and the fix location is exact.

Recorded failure (verifier.log:2047): play_view_renders_controls_e2e.rs:131 -- "VBoxContainer did not stack its children -- all filled rects share y [0]".

ROOT CAUSE: arrange_container (gdscene/src/control.rs:1703) is fully implemented and unit-tested, but has ZERO production callers. A grep across crates/ and examples/ finds it only in gdscene/tests/container_size_flags_parity.rs. So no container is ever arranged at render time and every child keeps its default (0,0) -- which is exactly "all filled rects share y [0]".

This is the same class as this bead's own third merged finding, which says render_control_tree "bridges control layout previously exercised only from tests" and has callers only in tests. That finding is now HALF-STALE and worth correcting: control_draw_items IS live -- viewport_2d_render.rs:962 calls it -- so the render walk does run. What is missing is not the walk, it is the layout step before it.

The live chain:
  viewport_2d_render.rs:962 -> control_render::control_draw_items
    -> render_control_tree_with_fonts -> render_node        <-- no layout step anywhere

EXACT FIX: arrange containers before the walk, inside control_draw_items (or at the top of render_control_tree_with_fonts) -- for each descendant whose class is a container, call control::arrange_container(tree, id, <its resolved size>) top-down, so a nested VBox inside an arranged parent receives its parent's allotted size first.

WHY I DID NOT SHIP IT: this shifts the position of every Control in the Play path, and I cannot run a single test to tell a fix from a regression. container_size_flags_parity calls arrange_container directly so it is unaffected, but play_view_renders_controls_e2e, control_render_test and the other gdeditor render tests all assert current positions. A layout pass added blind is exactly the change that satisfies one assertion and silently moves everything else.

For a build-capable lane this should be short: add the pass, run the controls test first, then this bead's other three reported commands, then scan the gdeditor render suite for position drift.

SCOPE NOTE: the other three reported commands were NOT the failure on this run. play_canvas_inheritance_semantics and camera2d_scroll_drives_runtime_canvas cover separate concerns (modulate/z/y-sort accumulation, camera transform); only the controls test failed. Whoever picks this up should not assume the whole bead is broken.

title: Tween: expose create_tween()+tweeners to GDScript and dispatch callbacks/methods/finished from the frame tick
description:
[audit-key: animation/tween-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/tween.cpp, extension_api.json Tween (26 methods) + PropertyTweener/CallbackTweener/MethodTweener/IntervalTweener/SubtweenTweener, Node.create_tween

Godot: node.create_tween() returns a Tween; tween_property/tween_callback/tween_method/tween_interval/tween_subtween chain fluently; callbacks fire when reached, tween_method delivers interpolated values to a Callable each frame, and 'finished' emits once (upstream/godot/scene/animation/tween.cpp). Patina: the Tween engine with all five tweener kinds exists (gdscene/src/tween.rs TweenerKind) and process_tweens runs per frame (main_loop.rs:1428), but (a) scripts cannot create tweens — 'tween' never appears in gdscript-interop, and SceneTree::create_tween (scene_tree.rs:1676) has only test callers; (b) scene_tree.rs:1702 process_tweens only applies property values and never calls Tween::method_values/poll_callbacks/take_just_finished, so tween_callback/tween_method/finished silently never fire even from Rust. Implement: (1) interpreter support for create_tween() returning a tween handle Variant, with tween_property/tween_callback(Callable)/tween_method/tween_interval/set_loops/set_trans/set_ease/parallel/chain/kill/pause/play methods routed through the SceneAccess trait to the SceneTree tween store; (2) in process_tweens, invoke poll_callbacks + method_values against the owning node's script via call_script_with_access, and emit 'finished' when take_just_finished returns true; (3) register Tween + Tweener classes in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Wiring: a plain GDScript in a .tscn must animate a node and receive its callback with no Rust scaffolding.

**Merged findings (5):** classes CallbackTweener, IntervalTweener, MethodTweener, PropertyTweener, SubtweenTweener, Tween
- also: tween.rs:199 TweenerKind::Callback fires a script method but no Tween/Tweener classes registered (rg=0); the returned CallbackTweener with set_delay() is not introspectable.
- also: The tween_interval FEATURE exists as an internal step: `gdscene/src/tween.rs:295 pub fn interval(duration)` + tween_interval delay (tween.rs:208, test :1092). But IntervalTweener is NOT a registered class (`ClassRegistration::new("IntervalTweener")` = 0) — nor is the Tweener base or siblings Propert
- also: Tween is implemented in gdscene/src/tween.rs with a TweenerKind enum (Property/Method/Callback/Interval/Subtween @199) and TweenBuilder.tween_property (@653) -- interpolation runs -- but there is no discrete PropertyTweener object: grep of quoted name in class_db.rs and in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. gdscript-interop has no 'tween' support (grep hits are the word 'between' in comments only). SceneTree::create_tween/add_tween (scene_tree.rs:1676/1683) have ONLY test callers (scene_tree.rs:4379-4622, all in #[cfg(test)]). process_tweens (scene_tree.rs:1702-1723) calls only tween.advance()+get_current_values()+set_property; it never calls Tween::method_values(563)/poll_callback

**Prove it:** A runner-loaded scene whose script runs create_tween().tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 100.0, 0.5) followed by tween_callback moves the sprite over frames and then invokes the callback method exactly once; awaiting/connecting 'finished' also fires (test: `gdscript_create_tween_property_and_callback`)
acceptance_criteria: A runner-loaded scene whose script runs create_tween().tween_property($Sprite, "position:x", 100.0, 0.5) followed by tween_callback moves the sprite over frames and then invokes the callback method exactly once; awaiting/connecting 'finished' also fires (test: `gdscript_create_tween_property_and_callback`)

title: Rendering2D: implement Viewport canvas_transform and feed it from the active Camera2D each Play frame
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-transform-stretch] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/viewport.h canvas_transform + global_canvas_transform properties; scene/2d/camera_2d.cpp sets the viewport canvas transform each frame; RenderingServer.viewport_set_canvas_transform

Godot Viewports carry canvas_transform (camera view) and global_canvas_transform (stretch); Camera2D updates the canvas transform every process/physics frame (camera_2d.cpp::_update_scroll → viewport_set_canvas_transform), and CanvasLayers with follow_viewport use it too. Patina has NO canvas_transform anywhere (grep zero hits); render_runtime_frame throws away zoom/pan with 'Camera2D handling is a later sub-task' (gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:148-160) so a scrolling game is impossible. The math already exists unused: gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs::compute_camera_transform (:548) implements the exact Godot convention over gdserver2d Viewport camera fields that nothing sets. Implementation: add canvas_transform to the runtime render path — find the enabled Camera2D in the running SceneTree each frame (honoring `enabled`/make_current; anchor mode + offset + zoom + ignore_rotation minimum; full smoothing/limits belong to the nodes-2d Camera2D bead), build the view Transform2D per compute_camera_transform, and pre-multiply it into every world-canvas Render2DItem's global_transform in viewport_2d_render::rasterize_render_list — while items under a CanvasLayer without follow_viewport stay screen-fixed (HUD). Plumb through render_runtime_frame and the Play loop in examples/editor.rs. Wiring requirement: MainLoop step moves the Camera2D → next rasterized Play frame shifts world pixels but not CanvasLayer HUD pixels.

**Merged findings (2):** classes Camera2D, CanvasLayer, Viewport, Window
- also: grep 'content_scale|stretch_mode|window/stretch' across gdscene/gdplatform: only TextureRect.stretch_mode helpers (gdscene/src/control.rs:1587-1600). No stretch-mode concept exists in any render path; the Play frame renders 1:1 at panel pixel size (examples/editor.rs:225 renders at state.render_widt

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. grep 'canvas_transform' across crates/*/src + examples = ZERO hits. render_runtime_frame (scene_renderer.rs:148) discards camera: `let _ = (zoom, pan);` (:159) with comment 'Camera2D handling is a later sub-task' (:157). The Play rasterizer (rasterize_render_list) applies no view transform; build_runtime_render_list computes per-item global_transform but never a camera view. gdr

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a Camera2D at (200,0) (anchor DRAG_CENTER), a world Sprite2D/ColorRect at (200,0), and a CanvasLayer ColorRect at screen (10,10): the Play-path frame draws the world rect at the viewport center (camera view applied) and the HUD rect still at (10,10); moving the camera +50px via the main loop shifts world pixels by −50px on the next frame while HUD pixels do not move; zoom 2× scales world but not HUD (test: `camera2d_drives_runtime_canvas_transform`).
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a Camera2D at (200,0) (anchor DRAG_CENTER), a world Sprite2D/ColorRect at (200,0), and a CanvasLayer ColorRect at screen (10,10): the Play-path frame draws the world rect at the viewport center (camera view applied) and the HUD rect still at (10,10); moving the camera +50px via the main loop shifts world pixels by −50px on the next frame while HUD pixels do not move; zoom 2× scales world but not HUD (test: `camera2d_drives_runtime_canvas_transform`).

title: Render3D: sync Omni/Spot lights and shadow_enabled from the scene into editor+play rendering
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/r3d-lights-shadows] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/light_3d.cpp (OmniLight3D/SpotLight3D params, shadow_enabled), servers/rendering/renderer_scene_cull.cpp light culling

In Godot every Light3D in the tree illuminates the scene — omni with range/attenuation, spot with angle/angle_attenuation — and shadow_enabled turns on shadow mapping per light (upstream/godot/scene/3d/light_3d.cpp). Patina's renderer supports Point/Spot lights, spot cones, omni cubemap shadows and directional cascades (gdrender3d/src/shadow_map.rs, wgpu_pipeline.rs pack_lights_with_shadows/upload_omni_shadow_array), and gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs sync_light_properties:1499 parses all node props — but that adapter is dead code; the wired path (gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs scene_directional_lights:227) syncs ONLY DirectionalLight3D with 6 properties and never enables shadows, so OmniLight3D/SpotLight3D emit no light and no shadow ever renders in the product. Implement: generalize scene_directional_lights into a scene_lights collector handling OmniLight3D (position from global transform, omni_range, omni_attenuation) and SpotLight3D (spot_angle, spot_angle_attenuation, range), reusing/moving sync_light_properties so color/energy/shadow_enabled/shadow params/cull-mask flow; have setup_editor_lighting_3d add them via renderer.update_light; keep the preview sun fallback. Wiring requirement: .tscn -> editor_3d_render_inputs -> both SoftwareRenderer3D and GpuRenderer3D shade with the scene's omni/spot lights and render shadows when shadow_enabled=true.

**Merged findings (2):** classes DirectionalLight3D, Light3D, OmniLight3D, SpotLight3D
- also: ShadowMap::sample is a single-tap binary compare against a fixed SHADOW_BIAS constant (gdrender3d/src/shadow_map.rs:49-88). Light3D carries shadow_blur and shadow_filter_quality with taps()/is_soft() (gdserver3d/src/light.rs:82-115,382-386) but grep 'shadow_filter_quality|.taps()|shadow_blur' outsid

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. scene_directional_lights (viewport_3d_render.rs:227-258) filters is_class("DirectionalLight3D") and caps at 4; omni/spot nodes only become Light gizmos (node_gizmos push at populate_editor_scene_3d:864-871) with zero illumination. setup_editor_lighting_3d (viewport_3d_render.rs:896-937) sets direction/color/energy/angular_distance/sky/affects_scene but never shadow_enabled. sync

**Prove it:** A scene with only an OmniLight3D near a cube renders lit pixels (dark when the light is removed); enabling shadow_enabled on a DirectionalLight3D makes an occluded plane region measurably darker than the unoccluded region in the editor frame (test: `scene_lights_and_shadows_render`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene with only an OmniLight3D near a cube renders lit pixels (dark when the light is removed); enabling shadow_enabled on a DirectionalLight3D makes an occluded plane region measurably darker than the unoccluded region in the editor frame (test: `scene_lights_and_shadows_render`)

title: Render3D: wire StandardMaterial3D resources (params + textures) from .tscn into the editor/play render path
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/r3d-materials] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/material.cpp (BaseMaterial3D::_update_shader), scene/3d/mesh_instance_3d.cpp (surface material chain); extension_api BaseMaterial3D ~130 properties

Godot resolves MeshInstance3D materials via material_override > surface_material_override/N > mesh surface material, loading full StandardMaterial3D property bags and textures (upstream/godot/scene/3d/mesh_instance_3d.cpp, scene/resources/material.cpp). Patina's wired path (gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs populate_editor_scene_3d:835-888) renders every mesh with solid_material_3d(item.albedo) — a flat color; gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:379-405 flattens only albedo_color from the material sub-resource, dropping metallic/roughness/emission/textures; no code anywhere loads an image into gdserver3d::material::TextureImage (renderer sampling exists at gdrender3d/src/shader.rs:203-237 but is dead in production). The full resolve chain in gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:880-1073 is unwired (zero external callers) and its material_from_path uses filename color heuristics. Implement: (1) in packed_scene.rs keep the material sub/ext-resource reference queryable (like __resref__), (2) in viewport_3d_render.rs (or a shared resolver in gdscene) resolve the referenced material's full property bag via PackedScene::sub_resource_props / gdresource .tres loading into Material3D including metallic/roughness/emission/shading_mode, (3) load albedo/normal/roughness/metallic/emission textures through gdresource::importers into Arc<TextureImage> with a cache keyed by res:// path, (4) extend Render3DItem to carry the resolved Material3D instead of Option<Color> and pass it to renderer.set_material in populate_editor_scene_3d, and mirror uniforms/texture bind groups in the GPU path (gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs fs_main currently has no texture sampling). Wiring requirement: scene load (editor_server.rs api_load_scene) -> render list -> both SoftwareRenderer3D and GpuRenderer3D show the textured, correctly-parameterized surface in the served editor viewport and in Play.

**Merged findings (4):** classes BaseMaterial3D, Material, ORMMaterial3D, Shader, ShaderMaterial, StandardMaterial3D, Texture2D
- also: gdrender3d/src/render_modes.rs defines Transparency/alpha_scissor_discard/depth-draw policy but has ZERO users outside its own file (grep 'render_modes::|Transparency::' excluding the module: 0 hits). Material3D (gdserver3d/src/material.rs:128-166) has no transparency/blend/cull/depth fields at all 
- also: grep 'rim_enabled|clearcoat|anisotropy|heightmap_scale|subsurf_scatter|backlight|refraction_scale|detail_blend_mode|proximity_fade' across crates/: zero material hits (only Light3D distance-fade fields). grep 'billboard|triplanar|uv1_scale|uv2_scale' — material-level: none (Sprite3D has its own bill
- also: Both backends support instance shader materials: Instance3D.shader_material (gdserver3d/src/instance.rs:23-24), software eval + GPU custom_spatial_module_wgsl/resolve_shader_albedo (gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs:1012-1060,1848), and packed_scene.rs:407-463 flattens ShaderMaterial sub-resources ont

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. The only wired 3D render paths are render_editor_3d_frame (gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1063) and render_runtime_frame->render_editor_3d_frame (Play, scene_renderer.rs:164) — patina-runner has NO 3D render wiring at all (grep set_material/SoftwareRenderer3D/TextureImage in patina-runner/src: 0). Both wired paths call populate_editor_scene_3d, which assigns solid_material_3

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a MeshInstance3D whose StandardMaterial3D sets albedo_texture (a real PNG ext-resource), metallic=1, roughness=0.1, emission renders visibly differently per-pixel (texture pattern present, specular highlight) from a flat-albedo material in the editor viewport frame, via the real scene-load path; overrides win in Godot priority order (test: `material_resource_to_pixels`)

comments.author: SunnyHill
comments.text:
SunnyHill 2026-07-25: Handing back UNSTARTED. No code written. Scoping below so the next taker does not repeat the assessment.

WHY NOT DELIVERABLE BY THIS LANE:
1. Primary file is contested. gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs is held exclusively by EmeraldBeaver until 08:44Z with substantial uncommitted work. This beads core edits all live there: the Render3DItem struct (:72), its construction in render_item_for (:98-109), and populate_editor_scene_3d (:966). Workers cannot build (rust_task.sh refuses by agent name), so a cross-crate struct swap of this size is unverifiable here. Three of my beads today parked on defects only a compiler or a run reveals.

Worth stating explicitly because it makes this bead materially more tractable than pat-nzgdu.76, which does require rendered pixels.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (each piece independently verifiable):
(a) Data only, uncontested files: extend gdserver3d Material3D with the missing fields and have packed_scene.rs keep the material sub/ext-resource reference queryable (like __resref__). Assert the resolved property bag directly - no renderer involved.
(b) Texture load + cache: gdresource::importers -> Arc<TextureImage> keyed by res:// path. Assert the decoded image, not pixels on screen.
(c) Render wiring: swap Render3DItem::albedo for the resolved Material3D and pass it to set_material. Needs viewport_3d_render.rs uncontested; this is where material_resource_to_pixels belongs.
(d) GPU parity: wgpu_pipeline.rs texture sampling. Needs a build-capable lane with a GPU.

(a) and (b) are good worker beads right now. (c) needs the file free. (d) needs a different lane.

title: Render3D: honor primitive mesh size/subdivision properties and render real ArrayMesh/glTF/OBJ geometry
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/r3d-mesh] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/primitive_meshes.cpp (BoxMesh.size, SphereMesh.radius/height, etc.), scene/resources/mesh.cpp (ArrayMesh), editor renders real mesh geometry

In Godot the edited scene's meshes render at their authored dimensions (BoxMesh.size, SphereMesh.radius/height/segments, CylinderMesh top/bottom radius, PlaneMesh.size/orientation, PrismMesh left_to_right — upstream/godot/scene/resources/primitive_meshes.cpp) and ArrayMesh/imported meshes render their actual surfaces. Patina drops every mesh property at parse: packed_scene.rs:466-482 stores only 'primitive:<TypeName>' (unlike collision shapes, which encode dims at :489-499), then build_mesh_for_primitive (gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:175-186) returns fixed-size primitives — a 20x1x20 floor renders as a 0.8 cube, PrismMesh as a cone — and ArrayMesh/.glb/.obj fall to a default cube (gdserver3d has generators taking real params: primitive_mesh.rs BoxMesh/SphereMesh/CapsuleMesh/CylinderMesh/PlaneMesh generate(), extra_meshes.rs PrismMesh, and Mesh3D::from_obj + gdresource::import_gltf exist unused). Implement: (1) extend the packed_scene mesh marker to carry the sub-resource property bag (mirror encode_shape_marker) or keep the sub-resource id resolvable; (2) in viewport_3d_render.rs build the mesh through gdserver3d::primitive_mesh generators with real properties (add a true prism generator); (3) for mesh ext-resources pointing at .obj/.glb, load geometry via Mesh3D::from_obj/gdresource::import_gltf with a path-keyed cache; (4) support ArrayMesh sub-resources (surface arrays from the .tscn) through primitive_mesh.rs ArrayMesh. Wiring: scene load -> render list -> both render backends draw the authored geometry in editor and Play.

**Merged findings (9):** classes ArrayMesh, BoxMesh, CapsuleMesh, CylinderMesh, ImmediateMesh, MeshDataTool, MeshInstance3D, MultiMesh, MultiMeshInstance3D, PlaneMesh, PointMesh, PrismMesh, QuadMesh, RibbonTrailMesh, Skeleton3D, Skin, SkinReference, SphereMesh, SurfaceTool, TextMesh …
- also: class_db.rs registration counts: TorusMesh 0, TextMesh 0, TubeTrailMesh 0, RibbonTrailMesh 0, PointMesh 0, QuadMesh 0, ImmediateMesh 0, MeshDataTool 0, SurfaceTool 0, MultiMesh 0 (grep '"<Class>"' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs). gdserver3d/src/text_mesh.rs (523 lines) exists with ZERO users outsid

title: Play mode: render 3D game frames from the scene's active Camera3D without editor overlays; honor camera_override

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
## Partial delivery 2026-07-25 (MistyStone): 3 of the 4 acceptance clauses are wired; the Area bus override is NOT

Delivered and covered by `gdscene/tests/audio_spatial_players_wiring.rs`:

1. AudioStreamPlayer3D 30 units right of the current camera mixes right-loud and
   below 0.5 of unity (inverse-distance, unit_size 10 gives 0.25).
2. Moving that source to -X flips the pan, proving the recompute is per-frame off the
   live global transform.
3. AudioStreamPlayer2D right of the 2D listener pans right and goes silent past
   max_distance.
   Plus two extra guards: a current AudioListener3D overrides the camera, and
   attenuation_model is genuinely mirrored (DISABLED is louder than INVERSE at the
   same distance).

NOT delivered — the fourth clause:

4. "a player inside an Area with audio_bus_override routes to that bus (verified via a
   -60 dB override bus silencing it)."

Why it was left out: it needs the physics area-overlap state (which Area2D/3D contains
the player this frame) joined to the audio bridge, then a call to
AudioServer::redirect_stream_bus (gdaudio/src/server.rs:167, which today has zero
non-test callers). That is a separate integration — physics query plumbing, not audio
math — and it is the only part of this bead that touches PhysicsServer. Everything it
needs on the audio side already exists.

Suggested split for whoever picks it up:

- Home crate: gdscene (audio_server_bridge.rs), reading overlap state from
  PhysicsServer/Area nodes.
- Godot semantic: scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp — when the player is inside an
  Area whose `audio_bus_override` is true, its voice is rerouted to that Area's
  `audio_bus_name` for as long as the overlap lasts, and returns to the player's own
  `bus` when it leaves. Innermost/last-entered Area wins in Godot.
- Concrete test: put an autoplaying AudioStreamPlayer3D inside an Area3D with
  audio_bus_override = true and audio_bus_name pointing at a bus set to -60 dB; step
  MainLoop and assert the mix is silent; move the player out of the Area and assert it
  is audible again.

Also intentionally not done (out of the acceptance criteria, named in the description
as follow-up): Doppler tracking and the attenuation lowpass filter.

Known limitation of what WAS delivered: 2D panning uses a fixed screen half-width
(576.0 = half of Godot's default 1152 viewport), settable via
AudioServerBridge::set_screen_half_width. Nothing in the tree currently reports the
real viewport width to the bridge; wiring that is a small follow-up.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
Diagnosis 2026-07-27 (HazyFinch, no-cargo lane): the Transform2D failure is a one-function bug and the fix is ready to apply. NOT applied -- see the hold at the end.

Recorded failure (verifier.log:2445), var_to_str_emits_constructor_text_not_display_text:
  left:  "Transform2D(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 5.0, 6.0)"
  right: "Transform2D(1, 0, 0, 1, 5, 6)"

The test is CORRECT. Verified against the vendored Godot source rather than assumed -- Godot uses two different float formats in var_to_str and Patina uses one for both:

  * standalone FLOAT: core/variant/variant_parser.cpp:2022-2025 calls rtos_fix() and then
    explicitly appends ".0" ("Append .0 to floats to ensure they are float literals").
    So var_to_str(1.0) really is "1.0".
  * math-type COMPONENTS: variant_parser.cpp:2090 (Transform2D) calls rtos_fix() BARE, with
    no ".0" appended. rtos_fix -> String::num_scientific -> grisu2 to_chars, which emits the
    shortest round-trip form: "1", not "1.0".

So a whole component prints WITHOUT a decimal, while a standalone float prints WITH one. That
distinction is the whole bug.

ROOT CAUSE: gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:13060 format_gd_float() unconditionally appends
".0" when the rendered number has no '.', 'e', 'E', inf or nan. It is correct for the standalone
FLOAT case and wrong everywhere it is used for components. Component call sites that inherit the
bug: Rect2 (:13163), Transform2D (:13170), Basis (:13179), and any other math type routed through
the same helper -- worth grepping format_gd_float and splitting them all, not just Transform2D,
or the same failure reappears one type over.

FIX: add a sibling that does not append, e.g.

    /// Godot's `rtos_fix` for math-type COMPONENTS (variant_parser.cpp:2090): the
    /// shortest round-trip form with no trailing ".0". Distinct from
    /// `format_gd_float`, which is the standalone-FLOAT case and DOES append ".0"
    /// (variant_parser.cpp:2025). Using one for both is what produced
    /// "Transform2D(1.0, ...)" where Godot writes "Transform2D(1, ...)".
    fn format_gd_component(f: f64) -> String { format!("{f}") }

and use it at the component sites, leaving format_gd_float for Variant::Float.

Also check the -0.0 case while there: rtos_fix returns "0" for 0.0 explicitly, to avoid writing
"-0" (variant_parser.cpp:1986-1987). Rust's format! prints "-0" for negative zero, so a
component of -0.0 would serialize as "-0" where Godot writes "0".

HOLD -- why I did not apply it:
interpreter.rs is currently (a) in a crate that does not compile, and (b) carrying ~670 lines of
orphaned uncommitted WIP from pat-0q2kx.263/.32 (both unassigned, no lease). Editing it now would
entangle this fix with that WIP -- and the recommended remedy for the outage is to stash those
files, which would silently take this fix with it. Apply this AFTER the gdscript-interop outage is
cleared. See my blocker reports 75224 / 75231 / 75241.

Note the acceptance test var_to_str_roundtrip_all_types lives in gdscript-interop, so this bead
cannot verify at all until that crate builds -- but two of its three reported commands are
-p gdvariant and are unaffected.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
## Diagnosis 2026-07-25 (MistyStone): 6 of 7 tests are unproven; exactly one assertion fails, and it is narrow

### The failure (recovered from run.log before it rotates)

    spriteframes_editor_e2e.rs:478
    test: an_unstarted_sprite_does_not_advance_but_autoplay_does
    "autoplay must start the named animation, as Godot's AnimatedSprite2D does"

    Summary: 1/7 tests run: 0 passed, 1 failed, 6 SKIPPED

nextest cancels the run on first failure, so **six of the seven tests never executed**.
Do not read this as "the feature is broken" — the routes/UI/persistence half may well be
green. Only this one runtime behavior is known-bad. Re-running after a fix will reveal
whether the other six pass; expect to iterate.

### Where the gap is NOT

`SceneTree::process_animated_sprites` (scene_tree.rs ~1900) is wired into the idle phase
(`main_loop.rs:1573`) and the autoplay branch exists and looks right:

- :1917 — if `playing` is not true, read `autoplay` (a String animation name).
- :1919-1921 — empty/absent → `continue` (correct: no autoplay means no animation).
- :1922-1924 — `__sf_autoplayed` guard so autoplay fires once and a stopped
  non-looping clip is not restarted next frame.
- :1925 — sets `autostart = Some(auto)`.
- :1930-1936 — `anim` resolves to the autostart name when present, else the node's
  `animation` property, else Godot's `"default"`.

So detection and name resolution are implemented.

### Where to look

The remaining suspect is the **write-back** after the playback is built (scene_tree.rs
past ~1938). The test asserts that autoplay *started the named animation*, which means
the node must end the frame with `animation` set to the autoplay name and `playing`
true (and `__sf_autoplayed` recorded). Check that the autostart path persists all three
onto the node rather than only driving the local `AnimatedSpritePlayback`. A playback
that advances correctly but never writes `animation`/`playing` back would produce
exactly this failure while every other frame-advance test still passes.

Read scene_tree.rs from ~1938 to the end of the loop body and confirm each of:
`node.set_property("animation", ...)`, `("playing", true)`, `("__sf_autoplayed", true)`.

### Command

    nextest run -p gdeditor --test spriteframes_editor_e2e

Releasing the assignment — localizing the rest needs a real run, which a no-cargo worker
cannot do.

ALL FIVE IMPLEMENTATION ITEMS FROM THE DESCRIPTION ARE PRESENT (checked at the call site, not by
tag-grep):
  (1) clip capability in the pipeline — CanvasItem::clip_rect (gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs:208-215,
      set_clip_rect :261) -> FrameBuffer::scissor (gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:41), applied per item
      at renderer.rs:401 and restored on the way out.
  (2) control_render emits it for ScrollContainer and any clip_contents=true control —
      clips_contents (control_render.rs:334), which also forces it on for ScrollContainer because
      Godot's constructor sets clip_contents and a .tscn never serializes it.
  (3) clamping — arrange_scroll (control.rs:2327) clamps to max_scroll and WRITES THE CLAMPED VALUE
      BACK, so a script that assigns 999 reads 200.
  (4) wheel -> scroll — scene_tree.rs:3386, returning whether anything scrolled so a non-scrolling
      container does not consume the event.
  (5) scrollbars from the Range model — control_render.rs:472/505, with page = view/content.

WHAT I ADDED. The gdrender2d half of item (1) had NO direct test: `grep -rn clip_rect|scissor` over
crates/gdrender2d finds only src/ (renderer.rs, test_adapter.rs, draw.rs) and the crate's three
integration binaries (canvas_item_shader, line_shading, render_pipeline) do not touch it. The
rasterizer was covered only transitively, through gdscene's control_render_test — which proves the
whole chain works but cannot say WHERE a regression is. Added 6 unit tests to
gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs's tests module:
  - scissor_discards_writes_outside_the_rect — both primitive write paths (set_pixel AND
    blend_pixel; skipping the blend path would let translucent overflow through).
  - scissor_edges_are_half_open — position+size is OUTSIDE. Get this wrong and every clipped
    control bleeds exactly one pixel, which no end-to-end colour assertion would catch.
  - no_scissor_writes_everywhere — unclipped is the default.
  - canvas_item_clip_rect_cuts_off_an_oversized_command — end-to-end through render_frame.
  - clip_rect_follows_the_items_transform — the rect is in LOCAL space, so it rides the transform.
    This is the one that matters for this bead: scrolling IS a translation, so a clip applied in

Neither existing file covers it. `crates/gdplatform/tests/input_map_action_semantics_parity.rs` says so
in its own header and defers it (gdplatform cannot see the interpreter).
`tests/input_suite/input_map_action_semantics_parity.rs::script_api_rebinds_actions_at_runtime`
exercises the **Rust** API, not GDScript.

That path is strictly longer than the Rust API and can break on its own: the script phase only QUEUES
an InputCommand on the tree (scripting.rs:2337 / :2362) and `MainLoop::apply_script_input_commands`
(main_loop.rs:2997) drains it into the engine InputState at the end of the frame. Break anything in

test stays green.

NEW: crates/gdscene/tests/input_map_script_rebinding_takes_effect.rs

  nothing) and the script binds it; frame 2 presses Q again and the action fires.
- a second test asserts the binding landed on the ENGINE map, not just the tree's read mirror.

  and the snapshot build at :2601 preceding the input phase at :2657.

That is what failed at log:2775: a foreign module in the grouped suite fail-fasted and cancelled 124
of 147 tests, which makes this bead unverifiable. Use the positional filter, which runs all 7 tests of
the acceptance module:

  -p gdplatform --test input_map_action_semantics_parity

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
CORRECTION 2026-07-27 ~04:21 — verify FAIL 75255 (18 compile errors) was ENTIRELY MY FAULT. Rewritten
and resent as 75256.

## The mistake

I wrote `ActionBinding::new(Key::Tab)`. There is no such constructor. The `pub fn new(key: Key)` I
grepped at input.rs:759 belongs to **KeyCombo**, a different type in the same file.

I verified the NAMES existed and never checked which TYPE owned them. One file holds many impl
blocks, so `rg "pub fn <name>"` tells you the file has that method, never who owns it.

Real shape:
  InputMap      new / add_action / action_add_event / action_match / event_matches_action
  InputState    process_event / is_action_pressed / get_action_strength
  ActionBinding axis_negative / axis_positive / shift_key / ctrl_key   (NO `new`)

## The rewrite

Asserts through InputMap::action_match, which returns Godot's action_match out-parameters
(pressed / strength) directly — the function the bead's clauses are actually about, with no
InputState event plumbing between the test and the behaviour.

4 tests: negative-direction binding ignores positive deflection; strength remap (0.75 under deadzone
0.5 => 0.5); deadzone gates pressing and centre releases rather than latching; Shift-qualified
binding refuses the bare key.

## The check I should have run first, now recorded as a memory

  L=$(rg -n "pub fn <name>" <file> | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  awk -v l=$L 'NR<=l && /^impl /{o=$0} END{print o}' <file>    # the OWNING type

Note the sibling trap it exposed: that one-liner returns the FIRST `pub fn new` in the file, so a
checker looping over method names silently mis-attributes every constructor — which is exactly how my
own verification script reported "InputMap::new MISMATCH -> KeyCombo" when InputMap::new does exist at
:912. Confirm per-call, not by loop.

Added to feedback_verify_scope_at_the_call_site_not_just_existence.

PARKED 2026-07-27 ~04:22 after 2 failed verifies. BOTH FAILURES WERE MINE — not a foreign break, not
the environment. Not retrying (instructed). This note exists so the next person fixes it in a minute.

## The implementation is DONE; only this test is broken

Everything the bead asks for already exists in gdplatform/src/input.rs — signed axis directions,
inverse_lerp deadzone strength, modifier bindings, 72 builtin ui_* actions, joypad parsing, InputMap
singleton. The bead's verifier note describes none of it. Only the named acceptance test was missing,
and my attempt at it does not compile.

## What is wrong with my test file, exactly

  tests/input_map_action_semantics_parity.rs

Failure 1 (75255, 18 errors): I wrote `ActionBinding::new(Key::Tab)`. No such constructor — the
`pub fn new(key: Key)` I grepped belongs to KeyCombo, a different type in the same file.

Failure 2 (75257, 4 errors): I wrote `GamepadAxis::LeftX`. No such variant.

## THE CORRECT NAMES (read from the definitions, not guessed)

GamepadAxis variants (input.rs:416):
    LeftStickX, LeftStickY, RightStickX, RightStickY, LeftTriggerAnalog, RightTriggerAnalog
  -> every `GamepadAxis::LeftX` in my file must become `GamepadAxis::LeftStickX`

ActionBinding is an ENUM, constructed either by variant or by helper:
    variants: KeyBinding(Key), KeyWithModifiers(KeyCombo), MouseBinding(MouseButton),
              GamepadButtonBinding(GamepadButton), GamepadAxisBinding(GamepadAxis), + a directional one
    helpers:  ActionBinding::axis_negative(axis), axis_positive(axis), shift_key(key), ctrl_key(key)
  -> `ActionBinding::new(Key::Tab)` must become `ActionBinding::shift_key(Key::Tab)` (already fixed)
     or `ActionBinding::KeyBinding(Key::Tab)` for the unmodified case

With those two substitutions the file should compile; the four assertions themselves were never in
question.

## My root failure, three times in one bead

I asserted names I had not read the definition of: a method's owning type, then an enum's variants.
Each time a grep "confirmed" something adjacent and I treated it as confirmation. The fix I recorded
in feedback_verify_scope_at_the_call_site_not_just_existence is to map a `pub fn` hit back to its
enclosing `impl`, and the same discipline applies to enum variants: read the `pub enum` block, never
infer a variant from the domain.

For a no-cargo lane this is the expensive class of mistake — each instance costs a whole verify, and
two of them park the bead. Cheap prevention: before submitting a test, list every `Type::Name` it
mentions and confirm each against its declaration block.

title: Variant/GDScript: first-class Signal type with connect/emit/disconnect + Godot 4 connect(Callable) signature
description:
[audit-key: core-object/signal-value-api] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json builtin_classes Signal (10 methods: connect/disconnect/is_connected/emit/get_connections/has_connections/get_object/get_object_id/get_name/is_null); upstream/godot/core/object/object.cpp:1607 Error Object::connect(StringName, Callable, uint32_t)

Patina has no Variant::Signal arm (variant.rs:200-292); only the removed-in-4.0 3-arg connect(signal, object, method_string) works (interpreter.rs connect arm), and bareword signals resolve to an await-dict hack whose resumption matches by NAME globally across all objects (coroutine.rs:238-241) — two different buttons' `pressed` awaits cross-resume. Implement staged: (1) add Variant::Signal{object_id, name} to gdvariant + variant_type/to_string/equality; (2) MemberAccess on an ObjectId/self whose name is a declared class-or-script signal yields Variant::Signal (replacing the dict hack, keeping `await sig` working via AwaitTarget carrying object_id+name and notify keyed on both); (3) method arms connect/disconnect/is_connected/emit/get_name/get_object/get_object_id/is_null/get_connections/has_connections on Variant::Signal routing through SceneAccess to the tree's SignalStore; (4) extend the object-level connect arm to accept (String, Callable[, flags]) storing the callable's target+method (needs cross-object-call bead's target routing). **Verifier:** Repo-wide rg for Variant::Signal|SignalRef|VariantType::Signal = 0 hits; the gdvariant Variant enum (variant.rs ~200-292) has no Signal arm. The single 'connect' arm (interpreter.rs:5710) demands (String, ObjectId, String) — a Callable second arg hits TypeError 'connect() target must be ObjectId', so the Godot-4 idiom is impossible. Bareword signal resolves to the await-dict {__await_kind:"signal"

**Prove it:** In a loaded scene: `$B.my_signal.connect(_on_sig)` + `$B.my_signal.emit(7)` invokes the handler with 7; `connect("my_signal", Callable($C, "m"))` dispatches to C; `sig.is_connected(cb)`/`disconnect` round-trip; `await $B.my_signal` resumes only when B emits (a same-named signal on another node does NOT resume it) (test: `signal_value_connect_emit`).

title: Input: pointer-lock mouse capture + cursor shape pipeline to the browser game view
description:
[audit-key: input/input-mouse-mode] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** core/input/input.cpp mouse modes; platform/web/display_server_web.cpp (MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED -> requestPointerLock, relative motion via movementX/Y, CSS cursor mapping, custom cursor images); Control.mouse_default_cursor_shape

Godot ground truth: MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED hides the cursor and locks it (web: canvas.requestPointerLock), after which mouse motion reports relative movement (movementX/Y) and position freezes; MOUSE_MODE_HIDDEN maps to CSS cursor:none; Input.set_default_cursor_shape/set_custom_mouse_cursor and Control.mouse_default_cursor_shape drive the CSS cursor (platform/web/display_server_web.cpp). Patina current state: mouse mode is a stored enum reachable only in tests (gdplatform/src/input.rs:630-667; accessor no-op per the input-singleton-wiring bead); the editor client never requests pointer lock (0 hits) and always sends absolute coords (editor_ui.rs:9549); CursorManager (gdplatform/src/cursor.rs) is dead code; no cursor script API. Implementation (depends on input-singleton-wiring): (1) include mouse_mode in the periodic /api/runtime/input/state (or frame status) response; client watches it and calls viewport.requestPointerLock()/exitPointerLock() + CSS cursor:none accordingly, listening for pointerlockchange to POST the actual state back; (2) while locked, post movementX/movementY as relative motion; server synthesizes MouseMotion with relative and keeps position stationary (Godot captured semantics); (3) wire CursorManager into MainLoop/editor state, add Input.set_default_cursor_shape/get_current_cursor_shape/set_custom_mouse_cursor to the interpreter + accessor, and map CursorShape to CSS cursor names (custom cursors to data-URI cursor images) in the game view. Wiring requirement: a script calling Input.set_mouse_mode(MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED) in Play must cause the served client to request pointer lock and scripts to receive relative-only motion.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. The real runtime accessor SceneTreeAccessor (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:325) does NOT override set_mouse_mode, so it inherits the no-op default (bindings.rs:473) — the only overrides are a test mock (interpreter.rs:14732, InputCmdAccess) and InputState's own method (input.rs:961). mouse_mode never appears in editor_server.rs or editor_ui.rs (0 hits); requestPointerLock/pointerlock

**Prove it:** After a scene script sets MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED, the input/state response reports mouse_mode 2 (client contract), subsequent posted relative motion {dx,dy} reaches _input as MouseMotion.relative with unchanged position, and Input.get_mouse_mode() returns CAPTURED from a second script; set_default_cursor_shape(CURSOR_POINTING_HAND) is reflected in the state payload the client applies as CSS cursor. (test: `mouse_mode_pointer_lock_pipeline`)
acceptance_criteria: After a scene script sets MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED, the input/state response reports mouse_mode 2 (client contract), subsequent posted relative motion {dx,dy} reaches _input as MouseMotion.relative with unchanged position, and Input.get_mouse_mode() returns CAPTURED from a second script; set_default_cursor_shape(CURSOR_POINTING_HAND) is reflected in the state payload the client applies as CSS cursor. (test: `mouse_mode_pointer_lock_pipeline`)

comments.text:
FIXED 2026-07-27 (CalmCrane). HazyFinch's "stale, expect zero changes" call was HALF right: the
recorded failure is indeed dead, but the test could not have passed anyway. There was a second,
independent fixture bug underneath it. Re-running without this change would have burned another
verify slot.

## The recorded failure IS dead (proved from source, not inferred)

Recorded:  assertion failed: http_post(port, "/api/runtime/step", "").contains("200 OK")

That is the BARE `assert!` form — no message. The only `""`-bodied step assertion in the suite is
now mouse_mode_pointer_lock_pipeline_test.rs:145, and it carries a message
("stepping a paused runtime must succeed"), so it cannot produce that panic text. The file was
rewritten in a9ab6a5 (07-26) and gained the ⚠️ doc comment at :131 explaining that
`/api/runtime/step` 400s with "not paused" — written by someone who had diagnosed exactly this.
(The one remaining bare step assert in editor_suite_b, editor_game_toolbar_runtime_test.rs:161,
posts body "{}" not "", so it is not the one either.)

The later 101 was the gdeditor-lib break, since fixed — gdeditor compiles as of verifier.log:5252,
`-p gdeditor --test res_picker_e2e` PASS.

## The REAL blocker: the fixture never set the root the Play path actually reads

    editor_server.rs:13057   let project_root = state.texture_cache.project_root().to_string();
    editor_server.rs:13058   attach_scripts_to_tree(&mut cloned, &project_root, state);

Play resolves `_script_path` through **texture_cache.project_root()**. `boot_with_script` set only
`state.project_root` (:109) — the field that serves the filesystem routes. So the texture cache's
root stayed empty, `attach_scripts_to_tree` could not find main.gd, it logged "Failed to read
script", NO script was attached, and `_ready` never ran.

With `_ready` never running, `Input.set_mouse_mode(MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED)` never executes, so
mouse_mode is never 2 and `seen_mode` stays -1. The test would have failed at the mouse_mode
assertion and read as a mouse-mode wiring bug — while the wiring is fine.

Fix: set BOTH roots in `boot_with_script`. Precedent: editor_play_lifecycle_order.rs:131-133 and
:204-206 both call `state.texture_cache.set_project_root(...)`. One fixture change covers all three
booting tests (`mouse_mode_pointer_lock_pipeline`, `uncaptured_motion_still_moves_the_pointer`,
`client_can_report_the_actual_pointer_lock_state`); the fourth only string-matches EDITOR_HTML.

## The bead's implementation is DONE — every gap its Verifier note cited is closed

The note said: the real accessor does not override set_mouse_mode and inherits the no-op default;
mouse_mode appears 0 times in editor_server.rs/editor_ui.rs; requestPointerLock 0 hits. Today:

  scripting.rs:2189/2195/2274/2280   SceneTreeAccessor DOES override set_mouse_mode /
                                     get_mouse_mode / set_default_cursor_shape /
                                     get_current_cursor_shape
  editor_server.rs                   16 mouse_mode/cursor_shape hits; the state payload carries
                                     mouse_mode, cursor_shape, cursor_css, custom_cursor
  editor_ui.rs                       5 requestPointerLock / pointerlockchange hits

So this was never an implementation gap — only the fixture.

## Verification limit

No-cargo lane (AGENTS.md:88). `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` on the edited file exits 0 with no
diff, which proves it parses and is formatted — NOT that it compiles. `texture_cache` is a public
field (editor_server.rs:392) and `set_project_root` a `pub fn` taking `impl Into<String>`
(texture_cache.rs:90), so no new import is needed.

## Worth its own bead (NOT done here)

Play reads `texture_cache.project_root()` while the filesystem routes read `state.project_root`.
Two sources of truth for one concept is a standing trap — this is at least the second fixture to
fall into it. Unifying them is a real cleanup but out of scope for an input bead.

comments.author: CalmCrane
comments.text:
SECOND FIX 2026-07-27 (CalmCrane). The fixture fix worked; a THIRD bug was behind it. This test
had three independent defects stacked, none of them in the feature under test.

## The fixture fix is confirmed working by the verifier itself

  before: 1/4 tests run, 0 passed   (script never attached)
  after:  2/4 tests run, 1 passed   (script attaches, _ready runs)

and the failure payload now contains  "value":{"type":"Int","value":2}  — mouse_mode 2 = CAPTURED.
So `Input.set_mouse_mode(MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED)` executes and reaches the state. The first three
assertions (mouse_mode, cursor_shape, cursor_css) all pass now.

## Bug 3: find_script_var could never match anything

New failure:  left: None  right: Some(7.0)   at the rel_x assertion.

`/api/runtime/node` returns property entries shaped like

    {"name":"rel_x","type":"Float","type_name":"","value":{"type":"Float","value":7.0}}

The variable name is a **value under the "name" key**, never a key itself, and `value` is
DOUBLED — an outer typed wrapper around the actual number. The helper searched for a KEY equal to
the variable name and then called `as_f64()` on it, so:

  - no key is ever named `rel_x` -> no match, at any depth
  - even on a match, the outer `value` is an object, so `as_f64()` would return None anyway

It returned None for every variable regardless of how well the pipeline worked. All four of its
call sites (rel_x, rel_y, seen_mode, seen_shape) were therefore unpassable. Nothing depended on the
old behavior — every caller asserts a real number — so fixing it cannot break another assertion.

Fix: match `map["name"] == name`, then read `value.value`, falling back to a bare `value`. Kept the
recursive search (the doc comment explains why this test does not pin the schema).

## The feature itself is implemented — verified before blaming it

`/api/runtime/input/mouse_move` handles `{dx,dy}` with Godot captured semantics, written for THIS
bead: editor_server.rs:14294 `relative_only`, :14296-14302 — when captured it returns the previous
position unchanged and carries (dx,dy) as relative; :14304-14306 — outside capture a relative post
still moves the pointer. So the remaining assertions are testing real code.

Prediction for the next run, stated so it can be checked: if anything still fails at rel_x it will
now report `Some(0.0)` (the script's initial value — handler ran, feature broken) rather than
`None` (never observable). That distinction is the whole point of the fix.

## Verification limit

No-cargo lane (AGENTS.md:88). `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check` exits 0 on the edited file — parses
and is formatted, NOT compiled. Only the test helper changed; no engine code touched.

## Running tally for this bead — all three defects were in the test, none in the feature

  1. `/api/runtime/step` 400 "not paused"   fixed earlier by a9ab6a5 (play -> pause -> step)
  2. fixture set only state.project_root    fixed by me last pass (texture_cache root)
  3. find_script_var matched keys not names fixed by me this pass

Every recorded "failure" of pat-0q2kx.90 has been test scaffolding. The mouse-mode/cursor/pointer-
lock implementation has been complete the whole time.

title: Input: propagation-order parity — reverse iteration, can_process gating, shortcut stage filtering
description:
[audit-key: input/input-routing] [port-audit 2026-07-17] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** scene/main/scene_tree.cpp:1404-1450 (_call_input_pause iterates group REVERSED, skips !can_process()); scene/main/viewport.cpp:3558-3576 (_shortcut_input only for Key/Shortcut/JoypadButton; _unhandled_key_input only for Key)

Godot ground truth: each input stage iterates its node group in REVERSE order and skips nodes failing can_process() (upstream scene_tree.cpp:1404-1450); _shortcut_input runs only for Key/Shortcut/JoypadButton events and _unhandled_key_input only for Key events (viewport.cpp:3558-3576). Patina current state: SceneTree::push_input (gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:1998-2023) iterates forward tree order, ignores pause/process_mode, and runs _shortcut_input for every event type (mouse motion included). Implementation: in push_input, (1) iterate self.all_nodes_in_tree_order().rev() (or maintain per-stage groups matching Godot's group semantics) per stage; (2) filter each candidate with the existing should_process_node/can_process logic before dispatch; (3) gate the _shortcut_input stage to Key (and future Shortcut/JoypadButton) events alongside the existing _unhandled_key_input key gate; (4) expose Viewport.push_input/is_input_handled to scripts via the interpreter so tests and user code can inject events (matching Godot's API). Wiring requirement: the ordering must hold for events pushed through MainLoop.push_event during Play, verified across two scripted sibling nodes.

**Verifier:** Refutation failed. push_input iterates self.all_nodes_in_tree_order() FORWARD with no .rev() (scene_tree.rs:2016) — Godot iterates the group reversed (scene_tree.cpp:1435). _shortcut_input is included for BOTH key and non-key events (2004-2013), so mouse motion triggers it; Godot gates it to Key/Shortcut/JoypadButton (viewport.cpp:3560). No can_process gating in the input path: call_script_with_ac

**Prove it:** In a scene with parent P and later-sibling child C both implementing _input: C's _input runs before P's, and C calling set_input_as_handled() prevents P's _input and all later stages; a paused (process_mode=disabled) node receives no _input; a MouseMotion event never triggers _shortcut_input. (test: `input_propagation_order_parity`)
acceptance_criteria: In a scene with parent P and later-sibling child C both implementing _input: C's _input runs before P's, and C calling set_input_as_handled() prevents P's _input and all later stages; a paused (process_mode=disabled) node receives no _input; a MouseMotion event never triggers _shortcut_input.
