title: Rendering2D: wire SceneTree -> canvas pipeline with global transforms and z/y-sort draw order
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-pipeline-core] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot draws every CanvasItem-derived node each frame through RenderingServer canvas commands, honoring the node's GLOBAL Transform2D (position*rotation*scale composed up the parent chain), z_index+z_as_relative global ordering, y_sort_enabled cross-parent ordering, and modulate/self_modulate propagation (scene/main/canvas_item.cpp). Patina has none of this in any runtime: the canvas pipeline (gdserver2d::canvas + gdrender2d::renderer::SoftwareRenderer) has zero scene-node producers (grep 'DrawCommand::' hits only tests), patina-runner is headless (main.rs:273-397, no gdrender2d dep), and the only wired 2D surface — the editor viewport via examples/editor.rs:372 -> scene_renderer.rs:213-277 — draws icons at LOCAL position (extract_position, scene_renderer.rs:220) with no rotation/scale/parent composition and no z-order draw sort, despite gdscene::node2d::get_global_transform (node2d.rs:83) already existing. Implement a scene->canvas render bridge (new module, e.g. gdrender2d::scene_bridge with a gdscene dep, or promote the editor's renderer): walk tree in order, compute each node's global Transform2D via node2d::get_global_transform, build CanvasItems ordered by accumulated z_index (respect z_as_relative) then y_sort within a subtree then tree order, propagate modulate*self_modulate and visible/visible_in_tree, feed gdserver2d::Viewport + SoftwareRenderer::render_frame to a FrameData, and replace the schematic path in examples/editor.rs so the live editor viewport shows the real transformed/ordered scene. Expose the same entry as the public 2D render for the web runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose root Node2D is rotated 45deg and translated, containing a Sprite2D child plus two overlapping ColorRects with z_index 0 and 1, renders (a) the sprite pixels at the globally-rotated+translated location (not the local position) and (b) the z_index=1 rect fully on top of the z_index=0 rect. The editor /api/viewport frame reflects parent rotation. Prove wiring end-to-end from PackedScene::from_tscn to FrameData pixels. (test: `scene_canvas_render_bridge`)

comments.text:

All 10 classes registered in register_viewport_classes -> register_rendering_device_classes():

  1. NO GLSL->SPIRV compiler anywhere in the workspace (no shaderc/naga/spirv-* in any Cargo.toml).

title: Add MissingNode/MissingResource to preserve unknown classes losslessly on scene round-trip
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/resources-io/missing-placeholders] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-7/resources-io/missing-placeholders] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** When a .tscn/.tres references a class/script the engine doesn't recognize, Godot instantiates a MissingNode/MissingResource that stores the original_class name + all raw properties, so re-saving the file preserves the data byte-for-byte instead of dropping it. doc/classes/MissingNode.xml, MissingResource.xml.

**Patina today:** neither class exists (grep matches are unrelated test names in compare3d.rs/export.rs/property_undo.rs). An unknown class today has no preservation path, risking silent data loss on load→save — exactly the failure the resources-io stones forbid ("NO silent skips of unparseable values").

**Implement:** Add MissingNode (Node) and MissingResource (Resource) holding original_class + a property bag; make the .tscn/.tres loader (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs, gdresource/src/loader.rs) emit them for unrecognized types and the saver re-emit the stored class + properties verbatim.

**Wiring requirement:** Load a .tscn referencing an unknown class into a MissingNode and save it back with the original type string + properties intact.

**Prove it:** Round-trip a .tscn containing an unregistered node type; assert the re-saved text preserves the original class name and every property (no drops).
acceptance_criteria: Loading a scene/resource that references an unknown class produces a MissingNode/MissingResource retaining original_class + all properties, and re-saving reproduces the original type and properties losslessly (test: `unknown_class_preserved_via_missing_node_roundtrip`).

even the import-options class models no options as properties. Registered with its 14 virtuals,
exact vs the dump. Options are DESCRIBED by virtuals, never STORED as a schema.

+ the 16 concrete importers + EditorImportPlugin. Ground-truth verified: parents, is_instantiable,
property counts (0 across the board), and ImportOrder = IMPORT_ORDER_DEFAULT 0 / IMPORT_ORDER_SCENE
100 (NOT 1 — scenes import last so their dependencies are ready first). Tests assert every class
REACHES Object, not merely exists.

register_editor_classes, and hence absent from a game-runtime ClassDB.

EditorImportPlugin::append_import_external_resource — real Godot methods, but nothing dispatches them

identity — none of this is a cheap extension of the registration. Suggested split:

  (c) the Import dock UI
  (d) the app-level reimport test

title: Resources/Boot: boot patina-runner from project.godot (main scene, autoloads, input map, ProjectSettings, res:// root)
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/project-boot] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot boots a project by parsing project.godot: it resolves application/run/main_scene, registers [autoload] scene/script singletons, installs the [input] InputMap actions, applies config/features (incl. .web overrides), and populates the ProjectSettings singleton the runtime honors (physics/rendering/audio). Patina's runner (patina-runner/src/main.rs) instead takes a raw .tscn path and ignores project.godot entirely; the parsers that exist (gdresource/src/project.rs ProjectLoader, gdcore/src/project_settings.rs ProjectSettings::load_godot_project) are library-only with no runtime caller, and gdcore::file_access::set_path_roots is never invoked so res:///user:// cannot resolve. Implement a boot path that: (1) if given a project dir/project.godot, calls ProjectLoader::load + ProjectSettings::load_godot_project, (2) calls gdcore::set_path_roots(project_root, user_root) so FileAccess res:// works, (3) resolves main_scene and loads it via the scene loader, (4) instantiates autoloads before the main scene, (5) installs the input map into gdplatform input. Wire this into patina-runner/src/main.rs and patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs init_resources()/init_main_scene().
acceptance_criteria: Running the runner against a fixtures project dir containing project.godot (with run/main_scene, an [autoload], and an [input] action) boots the declared main scene, the autoload node exists in the tree, res:// FileAccess resolves under the project root, and ProjectSettings.get_setting reflects a project.godot value. (test: `runner_boots_project_godot`)

title: Physics3D: implement PhysicalBone3D + PhysicalBoneSimulator3D ragdoll driven by MainLoop
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/physics3d-ragdoll] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ragdolls use PhysicalBoneSimulator3D (a SkeletonModifier3D) plus PhysicalBone3D bodies joint-connected per skeleton bone; physical_bones_start_simulation() hands skeleton pose control to the physics bodies, which are stepped and write their transforms back to the Skeleton3D bone poses. Patina has neither class (unregistered.txt; no struct in gdphysics3d). Implementation: register PhysicalBone3D (parent PhysicsBody3D) and PhysicalBoneSimulator3D (SkeletonModifier3D); create rigid bodies per PhysicalBone3D connected by joints (depends on the joints bead), and on start_simulation drive the parent Skeleton3D bone global poses from the simulated body transforms each physics frame; on stop, return control to the animation pose. Wiring: stepped by MainLoop's physics sub-step and applied to Skeleton3D poses the renderer consumes.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn Skeleton3D with PhysicalBone3D bodies under a PhysicalBoneSimulator3D, with simulation started, run through MainLoop::step under gravity, moves the skeleton bone global poses (a bone's global position falls) instead of staying at the rest pose. (test: `physical_bone_3d_ragdoll_via_mainloop`)

title: EngineDebugger: expose script singleton and wire runner→editor remote debug/profiler over WebSocket
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/engine-debugger] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: EngineDebugger is script-callable (is_active, register_profiler, profiler_add_frame_data, register_message_capture, send_message, insert_breakpoint) and, more importantly, the running game speaks a remote-debug protocol to the editor so breakpoints/stack/locals, error trees, and profiler frames appear live in the editor debugger panel (upstream core/debugger/, editor/debugger/). Patina current state: EngineDebugger is not script-reachable (0 interpreter dispatch); gdcore/src/debugger.rs and debug_protocol.rs implement the pieces but are only referenced by gdcore/src/lib.rs — nothing connects a running game to the editor, and gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs (419-443) holds its own disconnected debug/profiler state. Approach: add an EngineDebugger singleton dispatch arm in interpreter.rs over gdcore debugger; establish the debug_protocol channel (WebSocket in the browser-native model) between the runner and the editor server so breakpoints hit in the runner surface in the editor and profiler frames stream into editor_server profiler_frames. Wiring requirement: a breakpoint set in the editor pauses the running scene and its stack is reported back over the protocol. (Note: this overlaps editor-ux for the panel UI; this bead owns the EngineDebugger singleton + protocol transport.)
acceptance_criteria: A headless test starts the debug protocol between a runner instance and a mock editor endpoint, sets a breakpoint on a script line, runs a .tscn whose script reaches that line, and asserts the editor side receives a break message with the correct script/line and a stack frame — plus `EngineDebugger.is_active()` returns true from a script under the debug session. (test: `engine_debugger_remote_protocol_e2e`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 58277): EngineDebugger is SCRIPT-REACHABLE. KEEP OPEN.
Does NOT meet acceptance: no break message crosses the protocol, no .tscn run.

THE BEADS PREMISE IS ACCURATE (rare — I checked rather than assumed):
EngineDebugger appeared NOWHERE in the workspace (zero hits). gdcore/src/debugger.rs (536 lines) +
debug_protocol.rs (869 lines) COMPILE but were referenced only by gdcores own lib.rs. Two healthy
islands, no bridge.

DONE: 21 of Godots 23 EngineDebugger methods dispatched to the REAL gdcore::debugger::Debugger — not a
private mock. Breakpoints a script sets are visible to the runner via should_break(), which is what
lets them actually stop execution. Diffed vs 4.6.1: nothing invented. (debug/script_debug not
implemented — they need the break machinery; they fall to UndefinedFunction.)

*** ARG-ORDER TRAP (tested BOTH ways) ***
Godot: insert_breakpoint(line: int, source: StringName) — LINE FIRST.
gdcore: BreakpointLocation::new(script, line) — SCRIPT FIRST.
Both args come out of &[Variant], so swapping them is NOT a compile error — it silently registers a
breakpoint on a script named "12". A test asserts the breakpoint lands on line 12 of res://player.gd
AND that no script named "12" exists.

OTHER TRAPS PINNED:
- is_active() is FALSE on a normal run (Godot only activates under --remote-debug); true only under a

- detach() KEEPS breakpoints while clearing runtime state. An editor dropping its session must not
  lose the users breakpoints. Easy to "tidy" into a full reset.
- Godots `depth` is the STEPPING counter, NOT the call-stack depth stack_depth() reports. A test
  asserts they differ (call stack empty while depth==4).

  or the miss passes vacuously.

REVIEWER CAUGHT 3 REAL BUGS PRE-FLIGHT (I cannot compile in this lane):
1. ORDER-DEPENDENT TEST: two tests shared profiler name "servers"; entry().or_default() does NOT reset
   an existing entry, so under a SINGLE-THREADED test-harness run (one shared thread = shared
   thread_local) the second saw enabled=true and failed. Namespaced the name.
2. VACUOUS ASSERT: is_skipping_breakpoints was hardwired false with no setter — the test asserted a
   constant. Added engine_debugger_set_skipping_breakpoints seam; now asserts BOTH states.

documents that re-entering the interpreter inside the closure panics with BorrowMutError.

Verify: -p gdscript-interop --test engine_debugger_singleton_script_reachable
NEVER --lib for this crate: pre-existing fuzz_deeply_nested_parens stack overflow cancels the run at
77/665. That is why these are integration tests.

REMAINING (the acceptance): THE TRANSPORT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS COMPLETE — DebugServer::bind/accept,

+ CallStack{frames} are EXACTLY what the acceptance asks the editor to receive. Missing is the wiring:
(1) interpreter calls should_break() per line and emits Paused + CallStack over a session; (2) runner

editor_server.rs:419-443 disconnected debug state consumes it; (4) the .tscn run.

title: Editor/Resources: lossless .tscn save — regenerate ext_resource/sub_resource tables, uid+load_steps header, and full Variant serialization
description:
[audit-key: resources-io/tscn-save] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot's text saver round-trips a scene exactly: it collects external resource references (scripts, textures, sub-scenes) into an [ext_resource] table with ids, inline sub-resources into [sub_resource] sections, writes a header with load_steps and uid=, and serializes every Variant type in canonical .tscn syntax. Patina's TscnSaver (gdscene/scene_saver.rs:134) drops ext/sub-resource sections entirely and Debug-formats unsupported Variants, so any real scene (one with a script, texture, material, shape, or instanced child) is corrupted on save. Fix: reconstruct the ext_resource/sub_resource tables from node references and __resref__ companions during save, emit the load_steps/uid header, write script/instance as unquoted ExtResource("id"), and extend format_variant_value to cover Vector2i/Vector3i/Vector4(i)/Transform3D/Basis/Quaternion/Plane/AABB/Projection/Packed* arrays.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a complex .tscn (root with a script ext_resource, a child instancing a sub-scene, a node with an inline sub_resource and a Transform3D property), saving it via TscnSaver, and re-parsing yields the same ext_resources, sub_resources, script path, instance ref, and Transform3D value as the original (round-trip diff is empty for those). (test: `tscn_save_roundtrip_ext_and_sub_resources`)

title: MovieWriter: register abstract MovieWriter class + add_writer surface
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/movie-writer] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: MovieWriter (servers/movie_writer/movie_writer.cpp) is the abstract base used for deterministic offline video capture, activated via the `--write-movie <path>` CLI. Scripts can subclass it and register via the static add_writer(), overriding _handles_file/_get_audio_mix_rate/_get_audio_speaker_mode/_write_begin/_write_frame/_write_end. Built-in writers produce MJPEG(+WAV) and PNG(+WAV). On a browser target the headless CLI + real filesystem output are not available, so full frame capture is out of practical scope, but the class should exist so script/tool references resolve.

Patina current state: entirely absent (grep MovieWriter empty; unregistered).

Implementation approach: register an abstract MovieWriter class + static add_writer() in gdobject class_db.rs with the virtual method surface, so it is script-extendable and instantiable-as-subclass without error. Actual frame/audio writing to a container is explicitly deferred as beyond web scope (document it); the goal is class-surface presence and a functioning add_writer registry.

Wiring requirement: MovieWriter resolves as a registered class from ClassDB; a GDScript subclass can be defined and add_writer() accepts it into the writer registry queried at movie-mode start.
acceptance_criteria: MovieWriter is a registered ClassDB class; a script subclass of MovieWriter can be created and passed to MovieWriter.add_writer() and is retrievable from the writer registry; no error is raised referencing the class (test: `movie_writer_class_registered`).

title: Implement SkeletonModifier3D base + AimModifier3D bone aim constraint
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/skeleton-modifier-family] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

The SkeletonModifier3D/BoneConstraint3D family is entirely absent. Introduce a SkeletonModifier3D base node that hooks the Skeleton3D pose-update pass, a BoneConstraint3D intermediate, and AimModifier3D which rotates a target bone about a forward axis to point at a reference node/bone each skeleton update. Register the classes in ClassDB with correct parents (AimModifier3D<-BoneConstraint3D<-SkeletonModifier3D<-Node3D).
acceptance_criteria: An AimModifier3D child of a Skeleton3D rotates its configured bone so its forward axis points at a moving target node after the skeleton pose update; ClassDB reports AimModifier3D<-BoneConstraint3D. (test: `aim_modifier_3d_aims_bone_at_target`)

title: SkeletonModifier3D base + BoneConstraint3D / BoneTwistDisperser3D
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/skeleton-modifier-3d-constraints] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Introduce the SkeletonModifier3D base (Node3D that post-processes its parent Skeleton3D's pose each frame with an influence weight) and the constraint modifiers: BoneConstraint3D (per-bone constraint set: apply reference/target bones, copy position/rotation/scale, look-at/aim) and BoneTwistDisperser3D (distributes a bone's roll/twist across a chain to avoid candy-wrapper deformation). Register all three in ClassDB and run them in the Skeleton3D pose-update step.
acceptance_criteria: SkeletonModifier3D + BoneConstraint3D + BoneTwistDisperser3D registered with correct parents; a BoneConstraint3D copying a target bone's rotation drives the constrained bone's global pose to match (within influence); BoneTwistDisperser3D spreads a set twist across the chain's intermediate bones; modifiers run from the SceneTree tick, not just unit tests. (test: `boneconstraint3d_copies_target_and_twist_disperses`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 58069): CLASS SURFACE ONLY. KEEP OPEN.
Does NOT meet acceptance: no constraint drives a pose, no twist disperses, nothing runs from the tick.

PREMISE 1/3 STALE: SkeletonModifier3D was ALREADY registered (pat-nzgdu.151). BoneConstraint3D +
BoneTwistDisperser3D were genuinely absent (zero hits workspace-wide) — both now registered, diffed
TWO WAYS vs Godot 4.6.1.stable: zero invented, zero missing, every arity + constant exact.

*** BUG FIXED (pre-existing behaviour change) ***
SkeletonModifier3D was marked .abstract_class() with a comment claiming "The base is abstract".
Godot reports is_instantiable=TRUE. The flag is meaningful, not noise: PhysicsBody3D /
CollisionObject3D / BaseMaterial3D all report false. A test asserts PhysicsBody3D IS abstract so the
check is not vacuously true. Regression-checked: nothing in the workspace assumes it abstract;
create_dialog.rs consumers use a hand-rolled hierarchy after clear_for_testing().

*** TRAPS PINNED BY TESTS ***
1. BoneConstraint3D declares NO static properties. Surface = INDEXED methods: set_amount(index,value),
   get_amount(index). Godot synthesises settings/N/... at runtime from setting_count. Registering
   amount/apply_bone as plain properties invents a schema Godot does not have.
2. BoneTwistDisperser3D declares exactly TWO (mutable_bone_axes, setting_count). setting_count is a
   property THERE but NOT on BoneConstraint3D, though both have set/get_setting_count methods.
3. SecondaryDirection is OFF BY ONE vs BoneAxis: it reserves 0 for NONE, so PLUS_X=1 not 0. Copying
   BoneAxis numbering silently means "no secondary direction".
4. clear_setting (SINGULAR) on BoneConstraint3D vs clear_settings (PLURAL) on BoneTwistDisperser3D.
   Godots own inconsistency — normalising either name breaks parity.
5. Joint accessors take (setting_index, joint_index) — one arg deeper than per-setting accessors.
Reviewer caught a real omission: the 4 virtuals (_process_modification,
_process_modification_with_delta, _skeleton_changed, _validate_bone_names). Added + tested.
_process_modification is the seam the solvers must run from.

*** DEFAULTS ARE NOW MACHINE-CHECKED, NOT RECALLED ***
Godot --doctool dumps the class reference WITH default="..." (extension_api.json has NO defaults).
It caught one immediately: mutable_bone_axes defaults TRUE, not the false I was about to ship.
Re-checked all 10 defaults shipped from memory in pat-nzgdu.175 — every one correct.

Verify: -p gdobject --test bone_constraint_twist_disperser_registration
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING (the acceptance): BoneConstraint3D settings list + apply/reference resolution driving the
constrained bones global pose within influence; BoneTwistDisperser3D spreading twist across
intermediate joints (EVEN/WEIGHTED/CUSTOM + damping curve); both running from the Skeleton3D pose
step via the SceneTree tick. Acceptance test boneconstraint3d_copies_target_and_twist_disperses DOES
NOT EXIST — do not trust a stale-recovery close (0-match filters exit 0). Pose math would live in
gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs.

UNRELATED PRE-EXISTING RED TEST (not mine, please bead separately):
engine-rs/tests/misc_suite_d/node3d_runtime_slice_test.rs:121-126 register_3d_classes_total_count
asserts class_count()==12 ("Object + Node + 10 3D classes"). At COMMITTED HEAD register_3d_classes
registers 141 -> setup() yields 143. Already RED by 131 independent of any WIP; a fossil from when the
3D surface had 10 classes. Mine takes it to 162. Live (mod in misc_suite_d/main.rs:24), package
patina-engine, so -p gdobject does NOT run it. Right fix = assert a floor, not a magic number, once
the ~17 foreign uncommitted classes settle.

title: Implement IterateIK3D base + FABRIK3D solver as a SkeletonModifier3D
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/skeleton-ik-fabrik] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Add the SkeletonModifier3D/IterateIK3D base and FABRIK3D (forward-and-backward reaching IK) that solves a configured bone chain toward a target_node with optional pole/magnet, iteration count and tolerance, writing the result into the parent Skeleton3D pose during the modifier pass. Register in ClassDB.
acceptance_criteria: A FABRIK3D on a 3-bone chain drives the end effector to a moving target within tolerance across frames (pose-verified); ClassDB reports FABRIK3D : IterateIK3D; disabling the modifier restores the rest pose. (test: `fabrik3d_chain_reaches_target`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 58504): FABRIK3D SOLVES, pose-verified. 2 of 3 acceptance clauses. KEEP OPEN.

*** FIRST gdscene BUILD SINCE MY E0119 FIX — the verify run is load-bearing beyond this bead. ***
Nobody has compiled gdscene since .116/.114 died on the conflicting-Debug bug I fixed in main_loop.rs.
GREEN proves the fix and unblocks pat-u3l8c.12 (parked at 2 strikes PURELY on this), .145, .171, .173.
RED gives the real error. I included .151s existing IK test in the same run as a regression check.

THE BEADS PREMISE IS STALE IN TWO LOAD-BEARING WAYS:
1. [status: MISSING] is WRONG — the FABRIK MATH CORE ALREADY EXISTED: ik_solver::solve_fabrik with its
   own passing tests incl. a 3-bone convergence test. NOTHING ROUTED TO IT: process_modifiers only knew
   IKModifier3D -> CCD. Two healthy islands, no bridge (same shape as .176, .114).
2. The title says "IterateIK3D base ... as a SkeletonModifier3D". Godots REAL chain is:
   SkeletonModifier3D <- IKModifier3D <- ChainIK3D <- IterateIK3D <- FABRIK3D
   TWO intermediate classes the bead never mentions, BOTH ABSTRACT.

DONE: ChainIK3D + IterateIK3D (abstract) + FABRIK3D registered, two-way diffed vs 4.6.1 —
17/17 and 22/22 methods, 5/5 props, zero invented, zero missing, every arity exact.
Plus the MISSING HALF of the wiring: solve_fabrik works in WORLD POSITIONS, a skeleton stores POSES.
solve_fabrik_chain converts solved positions back to per-bone rotations (root->tip, re-reading
positions each step because rotating a joint carries its whole subtree).

TRAPS PINNED:
- FABRIK3D declares NOTHING of its own — no props, no methods. It is purely the CHOICE OF ALGORITHM;
  every knob is inherited. CCDIK3D/JacobianIK3D are siblings differing only in the solve. Giving it a
  target/iterations property would invent schema.
- angular_delta_limit default = 0.034906585 = EXACTLY 2 degrees in radians. max_iterations = 4, NOT a
  big number — these run every frame and converge ACROSS frames. Machine-checked vs doc XML.
- Only the leaf is instantiable; ChainIK3D/IterateIK3D are abstract (is_instantiable=false).
- bone0 is the FIXED PIVOT: reach is 2, not 3 (same trap .151 documents).

REVIEWER SIMULATED THE MATH IN PYTHON against the engines Basis/Transform conventions:
tip lands on target err=1.3e-7 after ONE frame (I assert 0.05 after 4); moved target 1.7e-7;
unreachable target parks at exactly 2.0 from the pivot, STABLE across all 6 frames; partial influence
0.25 gives 2.5 -> 1.846 (both bounds real, non-vacuous). .151 untouched: IKModifier3D routes to CCD
argument-for-argument as before, CCD still converges 2.0 -> 1.3e-6.

Verify: -p gdobject --test iterate_ik3d_fabrik3d_registration
        -p gdscene --test fabrik3d_chain_reaches_target
        -p gdscene --test ik_modifier3d_drives_bone_chain_tip_toward_target   (regression, .151)
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

*** THIRD ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE NOT MET — needs a design decision ***
"disabling the modifier restores the rest pose" is NOT achievable as the pipeline stands. Patina has NO
per-frame pose reset: process_modifiers mutates poses CUMULATIVELY, which is exactly how "converge
across frames" works today and what .151s tests rely on. Godot resets to the animation/rest pose each
frame BEFORE modifiers run, so disabling naturally restores. Adding that reset changes .151s CCD too —
a deliberate follow-up, not a quiet edit. My tests assert what IS true: inactive modifier and
influence=0 contribute NOTHING (pose exactly untouched).

REMAINING / follow-up beads (all PRE-EXISTING, none introduced here):
1. REGISTERED KNOBS ARE INERT: max_iterations/angular_delta_limit/deterministic/setting_count have ZERO
   consumers in gdscene/src. solve_fabrik_chain reads .151s flat `iterations` prop + a fixed tolerance.
   angular_delta_limit (2deg/frame cap) UNIMPLEMENTED: real Godot eases a 48.6deg swing over ~25 frames
   where this arrives in 1. Code comment now says so rather than implying the knob is honoured.
2. BUG — IKModifier3Ds registration is INVENTED (from .151): Patina gives it
   target_position/root_bone/tip_bone/iterations — NONE of which exist in Godot — MISSES the real
   mutable_bone_axes, registers ZERO methods, and is NOT marked abstract though Godot says
   is_instantiable=false. Godot drives chains via set_target_node(index,node) + indexed settings. NOT
   fixed here: the whole .151 solver + its green tests read those invented props. Own bead.
   Consequence today: class_has_method("IterateIK3D","get_setting_count") is false; Godot says true.
3. COLLINEAR IK TARGETS FREEZE THE CHAIN (pre-existing in solve_ccd, inherited by the FABRIK path): a
   target straight down (0,-1,0) leaves the tip at (0,3,0) forever — from x to is zero so the joint is
   skipped. (0.001,-1,0) solves perfectly. Measure-zero, but "straight down" is not exotic. Fix mirrors
   ik_solver::aim_rotation, which already handles it: fall back to any_perpendicular(from), angle pi.

title: Implement RootMotionView editor root-motion grid node
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/root-motion-view] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Register RootMotionView (parent VisualInstance3D) with animation_path/cell_size/radius/zero_y/use_custom_color/color properties. In the editor viewport, draw a grid that scrolls according to the accumulated root-motion delta of the referenced AnimationMixer. Editor-only visualization; no runtime behavior needed.
acceptance_criteria: ClassDB::class_exists('RootMotionView') true with VisualInstance3D parent and the documented properties; instantiating from a .tscn and pointing animation_path at an AnimationMixer produces a grid whose offset advances with root-motion accumulation in an editor-viewport test. (test: `root_motion_view_grid_test`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 58698): class surface + the grids ACCUMULATION. KEEP OPEN.
Editor-viewport DRAWING and .tscn/animation_path resolution are follow-up.

*** BIG FIND FOR EVERY WORKER: GODOTS FULL C++ SOURCE IS VENDORED IN-TREE AT upstream/godot/ ***
2189 .cpp files. extension_api.json gives SCHEMA, doc_classes XML gives DEFAULTS — NEITHER can tell you
what the code DOES. This can, exactly. For ANY bead whose acceptance is BEHAVIOURAL ("drives",
"scrolls", "converges", "restores"), read the upstream .cpp rather than inferring from property names.
Cite file:line so the next agent can check you.

BUG IT CAUGHT IN MY OWN CODE: I wrapped the grid offset on ALL THREE AXES by reasoning. Godots
RootMotionView::_notification (root_motion_view.cpp:124-128) wraps X and Z ONLY and NEVER Y — Y is the
height of a flat grid, there are no cells along it. My doc comment claimed "mirrors Godot" — BACKWARDS.
The test that should have caught it was itself broken: y=0.5 against a 1.0 cell, where rem_euclid is
the IDENTITY — blind to the very bug it existed for. Now y=1.5, load-bearing.

*** THE BEADS DESCRIPTION INVENTS use_custom_color ***
Godot 4.6.1 has NO such property. RootMotionView declares EXACTLY five: animation_path, cell_size,
color, radius, zero_y. A test asserts the surface is EXACTLY those five — that is what refuses it.
Registering it would mean a .tscn that will not round-trip in Godot.

DEFAULTS (machine-checked vs doc XML, not recalled): cell_size=1.0, radius=10.0, zero_y=true,
animation_path empty, color=Color(0.5,0.5,1,1) — a PALE BLUE, not white: the grid must read as a gizmo
rather than as geometry. Getter is get_zero_y NOT is_zero_y — Godot breaks its own bool-getter idiom
here (confirmed root_motion_view.cpp:187).
Wrapping with rem_euclid is VERIFIED PARITY: Math::fposmod (math_funcs.h:287) is byte-for-byte
rem_euclid for a positive divisor.

The grid test drives the REAL AnimationPlayer::consume_root_motion — the same call the runtime makes —
not hand-made deltas. A grid scrolling on invented numbers would look identical and prove nothing. It
also pins the inverse: an animation with NO root-motion track leaves the grid STILL.

REVIEWER CAUGHT 2 MORE THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED THE RUN:
1. My headline test would have PANICKED: with cell_size=4, accumulated z of exactly 4.0 wraps to 0.0,
   landing precisely ON the cell boundary. Deterministic (exact binary floats), not tolerance. Now 8.
2. E0451 — the file would NOT COMPILE: RootMotionView{cell_size: 4.0, ..RootMotionView::new()} needs
   EVERY field visible and `accumulated` is private, so struct-update syntax is illegal from another
   crate. The in-file unit tests use the identical pattern LEGALLY (mod tests is a descendant of the
   defining module) — which is exactly why it slipped past me. Now a plain field assignment.

Verify: -p gdobject --test root_motion_view_registration
        -p gdscene --test root_motion_view_grid_test
        -p gdscene --lib root_motion_view
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING:
1. Editor-viewport DRAWING (gdeditor) — this delivers the offset that drives it.
2. .tscn + animation_path resolution: follow the NodePath to an AnimationMixer and pull its root motion
   each frame. The acceptances full clause needs this.
3. rotation_y IS DISCARDED (documented in code, not hidden): Godot rotates each position delta by the
   accumulated basis before adding (root_motion_view.cpp:120-122), so a TURNING walk accumulates along
   a curve. Straight-line motion unaffected; every test here uses a linear track so nothing catches it.
4. DELIBERATE DEVIATION (stated as such, never "mirrors"): Godot keeps NO unwrapped travel — it wraps
   and zeroes IN PLACE, destroying the value each frame. I keep the full delta and apply
   zero_y/wrapping at READ time so accumulated() reports the real distance walked. The DRAWN output
   matches Godot exactly; only the retained extra differs.
5. Parity increment available: Godot declares PROPERTY_HINT_RANGE "0.1,16,0.01,or_greater" on
   cell_size/radius and PROPERTY_HINT_NODE_PATH_VALID_TYPES "AnimationMixer" on animation_path. Not
   registered here (no test claims hints, so nothing is false).

title: Add SubtweenTweener (Tween.tween_subtween) nested-tween stepping
description:
[audit-key: animation/animation/subtween-tweener] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

[audit-key: sweep-13/animation/subtween-tweener] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** Tween.tween_subtween(subtween) appends a SubtweenTweener (<-Tweener) that runs an entire nested Tween as one step of the parent sequence, blocking the parent's chain until the sub-tween finishes (respecting parallel/chain semantics).

**Patina today:** Tween is wired into the frame loop (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:425 -> process_tweens at scene_tree.rs:1307) but the builder only supports property tweens (crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs:442 tween_property); there is no tween_subtween and no Tweener hierarchy, so a nested tween cannot be sequenced.

**Implement:** Extend the TweenStep model in tween.rs with a Subtween step holding a nested Tween, and have Tween::advance drive the nested tween to completion before advancing the parent chain; expose tween_subtween on the builder and wire it through the existing process_tweens advance.

**Wiring requirement:** From a script in a runner scene, `create_tween().tween_subtween(inner)` must run `inner` to completion at the correct point in the parent sequence, with the parent chain waiting on it.

**Prove it:** App-level test builds a parent tween that tween_subtweens an inner property tween, advances process_tweens across the combined duration, and asserts the inner property animates and the parent step after it only starts once the sub-tween finished.
acceptance_criteria: A Tween using tween_subtween runs the nested Tween to completion before its next chained step begins, and the nested property animates to its end value when process_tweens is advanced across the total duration (test: `subtween_tweener_nested_test`)

title: AudioSample + AudioSamplePlayback sample-pool API (4.3+)
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio/sample-playback-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Add Godot's low-level sample-playback surface used by the sample-based AudioServer playback path: AudioSample (<-RefCounted, wraps an AudioStream + LoopMode for one-shot register-and-play) and AudioSamplePlayback (<-RefCounted, the handle for a playing registered sample). Register both in ClassDB. Back them with the existing AudioSampleBuffer (sample.rs:22).
acceptance_criteria: AudioSample and AudioSamplePlayback registered in ClassDB (parent RefCounted); a registered AudioSample can be triggered and its AudioSamplePlayback reports playing state; is honestly documented as the sample-playback fast path (vs stream mixing). (test: `audiosample_register_and_playback_handle`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 58880): all 3 acceptance clauses met, BUT the pool has NO CALLER yet.

*** THE HEADLINE: AudioSample + AudioSamplePlayback register with NOTHING but a parent, and that is
EXACT, not laziness. ***
Both are plain data structs with GDCLASS(..., RefCounted) and NO _bind_methods()
(upstream/godot/servers/audio/audio_stream.h:43-74). They ARE GDREGISTER_CLASS-d
(servers/register_server_types.cpp:171-172), so ClassDB knows name+parent — but every field is a public
C++ MEMBER, not a bound property. Their doc XMLs have NO <members>, <methods> or <constants> at all.
The bead says AudioSample "wraps an AudioStream + LoopMode": TRUE of the struct, INVISIBLE to
ClassDB/GDScript. Registering stream/loop_mode/pitch_scale would have INVENTED SCHEMA.

AudioSample::LoopMode is a C++-ONLY enum — no BIND_ENUM_CONSTANT, no VARIANT_ENUM_CAST — absent from
extension_api.json, unreachable from GDScript. A test asserts it is NOT a ClassDB enum, checked
GENERALLY (constants/enums vs the RefCounted baseline) so a wrongly-NAMED registration cannot slip past.

THIS BEAD IS ONLY ANSWERABLE FROM THE VENDORED C++ AT upstream/godot/. The API dump shows these classes
with zero members, which LOOKS like a dump gap; only the source proves the emptiness is intentional.

SAMPLE PLAYBACK IS A DRIVER FEATURE AND GODOTS BASE RETURNS A CONSTANT false:
  virtual bool is_sample_playback_active(...) { return false; }   (audio_server.h:143)
Every sample virtual is an empty/false default. The ONLY real impl in the engine is
platform/web/audio_driver_web.cpp, which asks the BROWSER. AudioServer binds exactly TWO sample methods
to GDScript: register_stream_as_sample / is_stream_registered_as_sample (audio_server.cpp:2097-2098).
Everything else is engine-internal. This delivers the engine-side registry a driver sits behind,
answering is_playing from REAL STATE rather than a constant.

*** REVIEWER CAUGHT ME ABOUT TO LOCK IN A PARITY BUG WITH A PARITY TEST ***
My test asserted is_abstract("AudioStreamPlayback"). That is FALSE about Godot:
register_server_types.cpp:167 is GDREGISTER_CLASS, NOT the abstract macro (the same file uses
GDREGISTER_ABSTRACT_CLASS at :180 for a SUBCLASS — the contrast is deliberate). It passed only because
PATINA WRONGLY MARKS IT ABSTRACT (class_db.rs:3594, from pat-nzgdu.153). Assertion removed, deviation
documented instead of cemented. FOLLOW-UP BEAD: AudioStreamPlayback should NOT be .abstract_class().
Also: my registration_is_idempotent was 100% VACUOUS — it compared ([], []) to ([], []), and since
get_property_list also returns empty for an UNREGISTERED class it would have passed even if the second
call had DELETED both classes. Now asserts class_count() stability + survival.

HONEST DEVIATIONS (documented in code, never claimed as parity):
- PingPong/Backward are Godots declared VOCABULARY, not its BEHAVIOUR. Its JS driver routes
  forward/backward to the same restart() and drops pingpong into `default: // do nothing`
  (library_godot_audio.js:783-793). This pool loops all three forward: matches Godot for
  Forward/Backward, DEVIATES for PingPong (where Godot does nothing).
- loop_begin/loop_end are STORED BUT NEVER APPLIED by Godot — the web driver keeps them and never sets
  loopStart/loopEnd on the AudioBufferSourceNode; forward just restart()s from 0. My loop-region wrap
  is a deliberate modelling choice. Now tested (the loop_end != 0 branch + loop_begin clamp — the most
  error-prone lines, on pub fields — were previously NEVER EXECUTED).
- register()/is_registered() map to the UNBOUND driver virtual register_sample, NOT the scriptable
  register_stream_as_sample (which takes Ref<AudioStream> and calls generate_sample() first).

Verify: -p gdobject --test audiosample_register_and_playback_handle
        -p gdaudio  --test sample_pool_playback_handle
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

REMAINING — THE POOL HAS NO CALLER ("wired but inert", the same shape I keep flagging on others work):
1. NOTHING calls SamplePool. No AudioServer dispatch, no driver, no interpreter reachability.
2. Patina registers NO AudioServer and NO AudioStream class at all — so the two scriptable methods have
   nowhere to live, and register_stream_as_sample (stream -> generate_sample() -> pool) cannot be wired
   until they exist.
3. The web driver path (the only place samples actually play in Godot) is unimplemented.

title: Register OggPacketSequence / OggPacketSequencePlayback so imported OggVorbis resources load losslessly
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio/ogg-packet-sequence] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

OggPacketSequence (inherits Resource) and OggPacketSequencePlayback (inherits RefCounted) are absent (grep 'OggPacketSequence' across engine-rs/crates → 0 hits). Patina decodes .ogg straight to PCM via lewton (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs:133 decode_ogg), so it has no representation for Godot's imported form, whose AudioStreamOggVorbis references an embedded OggPacketSequence holding the demuxed Ogg pages (packet_data arrays, sampling_rate, granule positions, loop offsets). Loading such a .oggvorbisstr/.tres currently drops the packet sequence. Register both classes in ClassDB (OggPacketSequence : Resource, OggPacketSequencePlayback : RefCounted), parse OggPacketSequence sub-resources during resource loading, and feed the reconstructed Ogg stream into the existing gdaudio decode path so imported OggVorbis streams play.
acceptance_criteria: A .tres/.oggvorbisstr containing an OggPacketSequence sub-resource loads without dropping data: ClassDB reports is_parent_class("OggPacketSequence","Resource")==true and is_parent_class("OggPacketSequencePlayback","RefCounted")==true, the loaded OggPacketSequence exposes its packet_data and sampling_rate, and an AudioStreamOggVorbis referencing it decodes to non-empty PCM via the existing gdaudio path. (test: `ogg_packet_sequence_resource_load`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — delivered. Registration + a real OggPacketSequence type with demux/decode, plus the repo's first Ogg Vorbis test fixture.

*** THE BEAD'S PREMISE CITES DEAD CODE ***
The bead says "Patina decodes .ogg straight to PCM via lewton (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs:133 decode_ogg)". THAT FUNCTION HAS NEVER BEEN COMPILED. audio_import.rs is committed (df37e87) but is NOT declared in gdresource/src/lib.rs, and nothing anywhere references it. It is doubly unwirable: it opens with `use gdaudio::import::AudioFormat` while gdaudio IS NOT A DEPENDENCY of gdresource at all. So `mod audio_import;` alone would not fix it — that needs a new crate dependency edge. Its ~10 #[cfg(test)] tests have never run.
=> The LIVE ogg path is gdaudio::decode::decode_ogg. That is why I put the new type in gdaudio, next to it.
=> RECOMMEND a separate bead: "wire or delete gdresource/src/audio_import.rs" (it also invents properties Godot doesn't have — sample_rate/channels/length_seconds/frame_count/has_samples — where Godot's AudioStreamWAV uses mix_rate/stereo and AudioStreamOggVorbis has neither).

*** THE BEAD ASKS FOR 2 CLASSES; THE GAP WAS 4 ***
Patina had registered EVERY AudioStream*Playback* class — the runtime instances — but NOT ONE of the streams they play. AudioStream and AudioStreamOggVorbis were both absent, so a stream could be played but never named. The bead's own acceptance names AudioStreamOggVorbis, so both are registered here. register_audio_classes() also guarded Object/Node/RefCounted but NEVER Resource, and every class here descends from it — the acceptance's is_parent_class("OggPacketSequence","Resource") would have failed standalone without that guard.

Registered, all diffed EXACT against extension_api.json (methods+arities, properties, parent, abstractness):
  AudioStream               6 methods, 0 props  <- Resource     (GDREGISTER_CLASS = concrete, not abstract)
  OggPacketSequence         7 methods, 3 props  <- Resource
  OggPacketSequencePlayback 0 methods, 0 props  <- RefCounted   (binds nothing; opaque handle)
  AudioStreamOggVorbis     16 methods, 7 props  <- AudioStream

*** ORACLE FINDINGS ***
- THE DUMP LIES ABOUT packet_data'S TYPE. It says `typedarray::PackedByteArray` (a flat array of byte arrays). ADD_PROPERTY at modules/ogg/ogg_packet_sequence.cpp:131 says Variant::ARRAY, and the setter takes TypedArray<Array> over `Vector<Vector<PackedByteArray>>` — an array of PAGES, each holding packets. The dump's shape would collapse the page grouping the granule positions index against. Doc XML agrees with the C++ (`Array[]`). Registered as Variant::Array.
- NAME QUIRK: the property is `granule_positions` but its accessors are `{set,get}_packet_granule_positions`, and the values are one per PAGE, not per packet (`page_granule_positions` in the header). Pinned in a test.
- bar_beats defaults to 4, NOT 0 (doc XML). A zero-default would silently mean a 0-beat bar.
- `loop` is a GDScript keyword so Godot binds has_loop/set_loop, not get_loop.
- instantiate_playback() EXISTS on the C++ OggPacketSequence but is deliberately NOT in _bind_methods — so it must NOT be registered. Pinned with a negative assertion (safe: verified `instantiate_playback` is not an Object method and OggPacketSequence's chain is Resource->Object, which excludes AudioStream).

*** IMPLEMENTATION (gdaudio/src/ogg_packet_sequence.rs, the LIVE crate) ***
Mirrors AudioStreamOggVorbis::load_from_buffer: group packets by the page they arrived in, tag each page with that page's granule, drop zero-byte packets, error when no pages are found.
- demux(&[u8]) -> OggPacketSequence   (via the `ogg` crate — ALREADY in Cargo.lock as a lewton dep, so no new version resolves; I added the lock's dependency edge by hand so a --locked build stays consistent)
- decode(&self) -> AudioBuffer        (lewton's packet-level API, not its container reader)

*** THE BUG I NEARLY SHIPPED — caught by reading lewton's source ***
I was about to assert "demux+decode == decode_ogg byte-for-byte". IT IS NOT. lewton's OggStreamReader (inside_ogg.rs:189-195) truncates the last packet against a running absgp and primes/discards the first audio packet; a raw packet decode does neither. More importantly this was a REAL CORRECTNESS BUG, not just a bad test: Vorbis decodes in fixed 2048 blocks, so the fixture's 17 audio packets yield 16x1024 = 16384 frames while the stream is only 15488 long — 896 frames (~20ms) of padding that is not audio. ffmpeg's raw decode gives exactly 16384, confirming the overshoot from a second direction; ffprobe reports duration_ts=15488 as the true length. decode() now trims to the final granule position, which is the Ogg spec's definition of stream length and where Godot's playback stops. The test asserts frame_count()==15488 and deliberately does NOT assert cross-path sample equality (documented why).

*** FIXTURE: THE REPO'S FIRST .ogg ***
There was not a single .ogg file in the tree, so gdaudio::decode::decode_ogg had ONLY ever been exercised by its error path — the happy path was untested. Added tests/fixtures/test_tone.ogg (5.1KB, 0.35s 440Hz stereo, ffmpeg native vorbis encoder; libvorbis isn't available and the native one is stereo-only). Generated ONCE and committed — no test-time ffmpeg dependency, no flake. Structure verified independently by parsing the Ogg pages in Python, so the test constants are facts about the file rather than values copied from a first run: 3 pages, granules [0,0,15488], 20 packets (1 ident + 1 comment + 1 setup + 17 audio), ident says channels=2 rate=44100.

*** BLAST RADIUS — swept with NO exclusions (the .227 lesson) ***
Last bead I filtered class_db.rs out of its own blast-radius grep and missed an in-file test. This time: every hit for OggPacketSequence/AudioStreamOggVorbis/"AudioStream" across the workspace, unfiltered. All hits are mine (4731-4830), all before the #[cfg(test)] mod at 6814. Checked class_count() assertions specifically since I add 4 classes — the exact ones (classdb_parity_test 17, node3d_runtime_slice 12) run register_core_classes/register_3d_classes, which never call register_audio_classes; nothing reachable from register_audio_classes asserts a count. The in-file tests that DO call register_audio_classes (line 6984, 6958) are positive-existence/parent checks only, which adding classes cannot break — but I am listing `--lib class_db` as a test command anyway, because that is exactly the command I failed to run last time.

*** NOT DONE — honest gap ***
The bead's "parse OggPacketSequence sub-resources during resource loading" is NOT wired end-to-end. The .tres loader ALREADY parses [sub_resource] sections and PackedByteArray()/PackedInt64Array() values generically, so such a .tres already loads into a Resource carrying the right Variants. The missing bridge (Resource's Variants -> typed OggPacketSequence) must live in gdresource, which does not depend on gdaudio — the same missing dep edge that orphans audio_import.rs, and the only consumer of that bridge would be the orphan. Adding a cross-crate dep for dead code is not a P3 call I should make unilaterally; it belongs with the audio_import bead above.

I cannot compile (worker cargo policy), so every lewton/ogg signature was verified against the vendored crate sources before use, and all 3 new/changed files are rustfmt-clean (my class_db.rs block too; the file has 111 PRE-EXISTING fmt diffs that are not mine and I did not touch).

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — SECOND submission. First one failed verification: `failed (100, panic)` on `gdaudio --test ogg_packet_sequence_demux_decode`. Root cause found and fixed WITHOUT guessing — two independent bugs, both in the fixture/decode path (the ClassDB registration and the demux structural tests were and are correct).

The verifier reported only the terse "panic" with no assertion text, and worker cargo policy means I can't run the test myself. So I diagnosed from measured facts, not hypotheses:

*** BUG 1: THE FIXTURE WAS ENCODED WITH FFMPEG'S EXPERIMENTAL NATIVE VORBIS ENCODER, WHICH LEWTON CANNOT DECODE ***
My first test_tone.ogg came from `ffmpeg -c:a vorbis -strict -2` (libvorbis is NOT installed here; the native encoder is all ffmpeg has). It emits NON-STANDARD blocksizes: bs0 == bs1 == 2048 (no short blocks). Every real libVorbis file uses 256/2048 block switching. lewton is a strict pure-Rust decoder and errors on the 2048/2048 stream -> decode().expect(...) panics.

Diagnosed by parsing the ident-header blocksize byte of my fixture vs the only real .ogg files on the box (livekit pip resources): mine = 2048/2048, all real ones = 256/2048. Confirmed by the vorbis-comment vendor string: mine said "Lavf..." (ffmpeg), real ones (and the new fixture) say "Xiph.Org libVorbis...".

FIX: I compiled a ~90-line C encoder from godot's OWN vendored libvorbis+libogg (upstream/godot/thirdparty; cc is not blocked by the no-cargo hook), generated a 0.35s 440Hz sine (OUR content -> clean license; I did NOT commit the third-party livekit audio), and encoded it with reference Xiph libVorbis at VBR q=0.4. New fixture: vendor "Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20200704", blocksizes 256/2048, 5517 bytes, 3 pages, granule 15434 = exactly 0.35s. Structure re-verified by parsing the pages (no cross-page packets, so the ogg crate groups exactly [1,2,17]).

*** BUG 2: assert_eq!(frame_count(), granule) WAS WRONG EVEN WITH A GOOD FILE ***
A Vorbis decode does NOT land on the granule. The stream opens with a short block whose leading half is decoder ramp-up, so ffmpeg decodes the NEW fixture to 15306 frames -- 128 BELOW the granule 15434 -- and a raw packet decode that keeps the priming packet lands elsewhere again. You cannot predict the exact decoded count without running the decoder. So I no longer assert an exact count: the decode tests now assert a BAND (granule - 2048 <= frames <= granule) plus non-empty / correct rate+channels / finite / audible. That proves "full-length stream" without encoding a decoder-internal number. (The decode() granule cap is unchanged and still correct -- it is an upper bound only, `if target < len`, never an extend, which is right precisely because raw decode often lands below the granule.)

Ground truth used to set the bands (not predictions): `ffprobe -show_entries stream=duration_ts` = 15434 (the granule); `ffmpeg -i test_tone.ogg out.wav` -> 15306 decoded frames.

*** WHAT DID NOT CHANGE ***
- All 4 ClassDB registrations still diff EXACT vs extension_api.json. The registration test file is untouched.
- The demux structural assertions (page_count 3, granules [0,0,15434], page_data [1,2,17], packet_count 20) are provably correct: I re-verified the ogg crate's read_packet reliably sets last_in_page/absgp_page (reading/reading.rs), and the new fixture has no cross-page continuations, so the crate's grouping equals my byte-parse.
- decode()/demux() LOGIC is unchanged; I only edited doc comments (the old ones cited the old fixture's 15488/16384/896-overshoot numbers, now false) and swapped the fixture + the test assertions.

Files (same set as before; fixture bytes replaced):
- engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/ogg_packet_sequence_resource_load.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/ogg_packet_sequence.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/lib.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/Cargo.toml
- engine-rs/Cargo.lock
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/tests/ogg_packet_sequence_demux_decode.rs
- engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/tests/fixtures/test_tone.ogg  (now Xiph libVorbis)

Residual risk I can't eliminate without running lewton: that lewton errors on a STANDARD Xiph file (a lewton bug — lewton is the ecosystem's pure-Rust Vorbis decoder, built for exactly this), or that its raw count falls >2048 off the granule. Both very low. This is grounded in measured facts (ffmpeg decode of the exact fixture, page byte-parse, vendor strings), not a guess-and-hope.

Generator preserved in scratchpad (make_tone.c + build_tone.sh) for reproducibility; the test module doc records provenance and why the fixture is Xiph-encoded.

title: Implement EncodedObjectAsID and emit it from the Variant byte decoder
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant/encoded-object-as-id] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Add EncodedObjectAsID (RefCounted) with an object_id property, and make bytes_to_var / the RPC-wire decoder produce it when an OBJECT is encoded as an ID and full-object decoding is disabled. Register in ClassDB.
acceptance_criteria: var_to_bytes of an object with object-as-id encoding, decoded via bytes_to_var, yields an EncodedObjectAsID whose object_id matches; ClassDB.class_exists('EncodedObjectAsID') is true. (test: `encoded_object_as_id_roundtrip`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59116). READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING bytes_to_var: my first cut opened a REAL SECURITY HOLE.

*** THE TRAP THIS BEAD SETS ***
The bead says "make bytes_to_var produce EncodedObjectAsID". The obvious implementation — decode
OBJECT|AS_ID to Variant::ObjectId and return it — is EXPLOITABLE IN THIS PORT.
Variant::ObjectId here is NOT an inert id: it is the SAME LIVE NODE REFERENCE get_node() returns, and
get_children() on one walks the scene tree (interpreter.rs, the Variant::ObjectId method arm). So
  bytes_to_var(untrusted_bytes).get_children()
would reach into the RUNNING SCENE — with ids that START AT 1 (gdcore/src/id.rs:20), i.e. trivially
guessable. In Godot you get an EncodedObjectAsID whose ONLY surface is object_id; turning it into a
usable object needs an EXPLICIT instance_from_id(). THAT EXTRA STEP IS EXACTLY WHAT p_allow_objects=false
BUYS. A reviewer caught this; I would have shipped it.

FIX: decoded ids are re-wrapped in a tagged INERT handle (0xE1 — the family pattern used by
ConfigFile 0xCF / FileAccess 0xFA / DirAccess 0xDA / CameraFeed 0xCA / UndoRedo 0xED) that reports its
id and resolves to NOTHING. Applied RECURSIVELY (an RPC payload is normally an ARRAY of arguments; a
nested id is just as dangerous). BOTH decode doors covered: bytes_to_var AND
Marshalls.base64_to_variant (same decode, different transport).
The intercept MUST precede the Variant::ObjectId arm or the wrapper is pointless.
TEST DESIGN THAT MATTERS: a test asserts a LIVE node CAN reach the scene (mock returns 1 child), so
"inert" cannot pass merely because the scene was empty; and the wrapper must ERROR on get_children(),
not return an empty list — an empty list would mean the call reached the scene layer at all.

*** TWO BEAD-DESCRIPTION ERRORS (both settled by the vendored C++ at upstream/godot/) ***
1. It says EncodedObjectAsID appears "when full-object decoding is DISABLED". FALSE. The as-id branch is
   taken REGARDLESS of p_allow_objects — Godots own comment reads "This _is_ allowed."
   (core/io/marshalls.cpp:699-700). Only the FULL-OBJECT branch is gated (:717). Decoding an id can
   never construct anything, so it is always safe. Refusing ids would be STRICTER than Godot and would
   reject RPC payloads it accepts.
2. A NULL id decodes to NIL, not to an object with id 0 (:707-708). So object_id==0 is UNREACHABLE
   through the wire, even though the property defaults to 0.

HEADER_DATA_FLAG_OBJECT_AS_ID is the SAME BIT as HEADER_DATA_FLAG_64 (both 1<<16). Not a clash —
Godots design: bit 16 is read against the variants TYPE.

CONTRACT CHANGE, HANDLED: Variant::ObjectId previously encoded as Unsupported. Checked the whole
workspace for dependents — gdplatform/src/network.rs has its OWN PRIVATE encode_variant with a
different format and never touches this codec; the fuzz suite round-trips via JSON. One existing test
asserted the old contract; updated, keeping the property it actually guarded (errors propagate out of
containers) via a still-unsupported type.

REVIEWER ALSO CAUGHT (all fixed):
1. NULL-ENCODE DIVERGENCE: Godot writes a bare 4-BYTE NIL for a null object and never emits an OBJECT
   header (marshalls.cpp:1385-1393 — an early return ABOVE the flag logic I had verified). I was
   emitting 12 bytes Godot never writes, in a module whose first line claims "a faithful port".
2. MISSING IDEMPOTENCY GUARD: mine was the ONLY unguarded register_class in register_io_classes()
   (called ~20x per suite). register_class does NOT dedupe — it mints a fresh ClassId and leaves a
   stale by_id alias.
3. MY IDEMPOTENCY TEST COULD NOT CATCH #2: class_count() is NAME-keyed, so a duplicate registration
   overwrites and the count never moves. Now asserts CLASSID STABILITY — the thing that actually changes.
4. Deleted a vacuous test (it asserted independence from an allow-objects policy this API does not
   have, so the property was unfalsifiable).

Verify: -p gdvariant --test encoded_object_as_id_roundtrip
        -p gdvariant --lib binary
        -p gdobject --test encoded_object_as_id_registration
        -p gdscript-interop --test encoded_object_as_id_script_wrapper
        (NEVER -p gdscript-interop --lib: pre-existing fuzz_deeply_nested_parens stack overflow.)

REMAINING: var_to_bytes_with_objects / bytes_to_var_with_objects (the full-object form) are NOT
implemented; the codec always refuses full objects. That is the safe default and matches
p_allow_objects=false. instance_from_id() already exists in the interpreter, so the Godot idiom
instance_from_id(decoded.get_object_id()) is the intended way back to a live object — the explicit step
this bead restores.

title: Runtime: drive the MainLoop continuously during editor Play
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/runtime-drive] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot advances the SceneTree every rendered frame while a game runs (Main::iteration → SceneTree::process/physics_process). Patina's editor Play (api_runtime_play, editor_server.rs:9435) constructs a MainLoop and flips is_running=true but never advances it — the sole main_loop.step() call is api_runtime_step (editor_server.rs:9562), reachable only from the manual 'next frame' button (editor_ui.rs:8293). The browser's runtime polling (editor_ui.rs:9845 schedulePoll) refreshes status/viewport but never posts /api/runtime/step, so a played scene's _process/_physics_process, tweens, Timer nodes and physics never tick. Implement a continuous driver: either a server-side stepping thread that calls run_main_loop.step(delta) while is_running && !is_paused (honoring time_scale and max_fps and pushing frame_count + rendered viewport to the game view), or an /api/runtime/tick that the served game view drives via requestAnimationFrame at delta_time. Wire the EDITOR_HTML game view to advance frames automatically when Play is active and stop on Stop/Pause.
acceptance_criteria: After POST /api/runtime/play on a scene whose root script increments a counter in _process, both runtime_frame_count (GET /api/runtime/status) and the script counter climb over ~0.5s WITHOUT any /api/runtime/step call; POST /api/runtime/stop halts advancement. (test: runtime_play_auto_advances_frames) driving the gdeditor server end-to-end.

title: Implement SyntaxHighlighter base + EditorSyntaxHighlighter + GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-ux/script-editor-syntax-highlighter] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Register SyntaxHighlighter (Resource), EditorSyntaxHighlighter (with _get_name/_get_supported_languages/_get_supported_extensions/_get_line_syntax_highlighting virtuals) and GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter, and produce token color ranges for GDScript source that the served script editor consumes for coloring (instead of ad-hoc client JS). Allow plugins to register custom highlighters.
acceptance_criteria: GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter.get_line_syntax_highlighting returns keyword/string/comment/number color spans for a sample .gd line matching Godot's categories; ClassDB reports the three-class chain; the script editor renders those colors. (test: `gdscript_syntax_highlighter_line_colors`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59168): the CLASS CHAIN ONLY, 1 of 3 acceptance clauses. KEEP OPEN.
Colour spans and editor rendering are NOT done. Deliberately scoped small; the recon below should save
the next agent most of the discovery.

DONE (acceptance clause 2, "ClassDB reports the three-class chain"), diffed vs 4.6.1 + the vendored C++:
  Resource <- SyntaxHighlighter <- EditorSyntaxHighlighter <- GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter
ALL THREE ARE CONCRETE — unusually, none is abstract. A bare SyntaxHighlighter instantiates and simply
colours nothing. GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter declares NOTHING of its own: it is the GDScript
IMPLEMENTATION, everything inherited.

*** THE BEADS DESCRIPTION INVENTS A VIRTUAL ***
It lists _get_supported_extensions on EditorSyntaxHighlighter. GODOT HAS NO SUCH VIRTUAL.
editor/script/script_editor_plugin.h:62-64 declares EXACTLY three GDVIRTUALs:
  _get_name, _get_supported_languages, _create
Registering it would invent a hook a plugin could override that Godot would NEVER CALL. A test asserts
the surface is exactly those three AND that _get_supported_extensions is absent.
(_get_line_syntax_highlighting is INHERITED from SyntaxHighlighter, not declared here — another way the
description misleads.)

*** get_line_syntax_highlighting(line) TAKES A LINE NUMBER, NOT TEXT ***
The highlighter reads the line from the TextEdit it is BOUND TO, and returns an EMPTY dictionary when
it has none (scene/resources/syntax_highlighter.cpp:41-43). Any design that passes the text in is
inventing an API.

RECON FOR THE REMAINING 2 CLAUSES (all verified against source, not guessed):
1. RETURN SHAPE is { start_column: { "color": Color } } — a Dictionary keyed by the column where a
   colour STARTS, value a Dictionary with a "color" key (syntax_highlighter.cpp:212-213). NOT a list of
   spans; NOT {col: Color}.
2. gdscript-interops tokenizer is most of the work already done: tokenize(source) -> Vec<TokenSpan>,
   TokenSpan { token, line, col } with 1-BASED line/col (tokenizer.rs:289-337). Keywords, strings and
   numbers are distinct Token variants -> those three categories map straight across.
3. *** BUT COMMENTS ARE STRIPPED BY THE TOKENIZER *** (tokenizer.rs:336: "Comments (starting with #)
   are stripped"). The acceptances COMMENT category CANNOT come from tokens. It needs a separate scan
   of the raw line, and that scan MUST BE STRING-AWARE: `var s = "# not a comment"` has a # that must
   not start a comment. The token spans give you the string extents to exclude, so the two passes
   compose.
4. Godot caches PER LINE (highlighting_cache) — that is what update_cache/clear_highlighting_cache are
   for. Any implementation must invalidate on edit or colours go stale.
5. Current editor highlighting is ad-hoc CLIENT CSS (.sh-keyword et al., editor_ui.rs:1466), so clause 3
   means replacing that with server-produced spans.
6. _create is WHY EditorSyntaxHighlighter exists: the script editor CLONES a registered highlighter per
   open file rather than sharing one instance. Plugin registration depends on it.

Verify: -p gdobject --test syntax_highlighter_family_registration
        -p gdobject --lib class_db

WHY I STOPPED HERE: the rest is a real GDScript highlighter (two-pass, string-aware comment scanning,
per-line cache) plus an editor-server change to feed spans to the client — substantially bigger than the
registration. Better to hand over accurate recon than a half-built highlighter in a shared file. The
chain is registered correctly and the invented virtual is refused; both are permanent wins.

title: Expose the editor plugin scripting API classes over existing editor backends
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-ux/plugin-scripting-classes] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED] [unverified]
[verify-note: triage (sweep, unverified)]

Register and script-bind the editor plugin API: EditorSettings (get/set/has_setting, get_setting_list, property_get_revert, persistence via editor_settings_store), EditorSelection (get_selected_nodes/get_transformable_selected_nodes, add/remove/clear, selection_changed signal, over the editor selection state), EditorUndoRedoManager (create_action/add_do_*/add_undo_*/commit_action/get_history_undo_redo over the Editor undo stack), EditorScript (_run for @tool one-shot scripts), EditorScriptPicker, EditorSpinSlider (inspector numeric widget), EditorToaster (push_toast), EditorVCSInterface, EditorResourcePreviewGenerator, EditorResourceTooltipPlugin, EditorTranslationParserPlugin, and FileSystemDock (get_current_path, navigate_to_path, files-selected signals) — reusing filesystem.rs/editor_settings_store.rs/editor_compat.rs rather than reimplementing. Make EditorInterface.get_editor_settings/get_selection/get_file_system_dock return these.
acceptance_criteria: A @tool EditorPlugin script can read/write EditorSettings, query EditorSelection.get_selected_nodes() reflecting the real selection, commit an action through EditorUndoRedoManager that undoes in the editor, run an EditorScript._run(), and get FileSystemDock via EditorInterface; ClassDB.class_exists is true for each. (test: `editor_plugin_scripting_api_surface`)

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — DELIVERED (mail 59243): 9 of 12 classes registered (ClassDB layer only). SCRIPT BINDING NOT DONE. KEEP OPEN.
This bead is far bigger than one iteration: 12 classes + script binding + EditorInterface wiring + a
@tool plugin acceptance test.

REGISTERED 9 (schemas diffed vs 4.6.1): EditorSettings, EditorSelection, EditorUndoRedoManager,
EditorScript, EditorVCSInterface, EditorResourcePreviewGenerator, EditorResourceTooltipPlugin,
EditorTranslationParserPlugin, EditorToaster.
The beads "reuse the existing backends" premise is ACCURATE — editor_settings_store.rs, filesystem.rs
and editor_compat.rs all exist.

*** THE BEADS DESCRIPTION INVENTS FOUR APIs (all refused, all pinned by tests) ***
1. EditorSettings.get_setting_list — DOES NOT EXIST. Real readers: get_setting / has_setting.
2. EditorSettings.property_get_revert — DOES NOT EXIST on EditorSettings (it is an Object method).
3. FileSystemDock.get_current_path — DOES NOT EXIST. Its WHOLE surface is:
     navigate_to_path/1, add_resource_tooltip_plugin/1, remove_resource_tooltip_plugin/1
4. "FileSystemDock files-selected signals" — there is NO files_selected. Real signals:
     inherit, instantiate, resource_removed, file_removed, folder_removed, files_moved, folder_moved,
     folder_color_changed, selection_changed, display_mode_changed
Registering any of them would promise a plugin an API that ERRORS ON CALL.

*** TWO CLASSES ARE ABSTRACT AND THE BEAD SAYS SO OF NEITHER ***
EditorUndoRedoManager is_instantiable=FALSE — a script NEVER constructs one; it gets the editors via
EditorPlugin.get_undo_redo(). EditorToaster is_instantiable=FALSE — the editor owns the one toaster; a
plugin only pushes to it. FileSystemDock is also abstract.
Smaller corrections: it is add_node/remove_node, NOT add/remove. And get_top_selected_nodes is a THIRD

**Implement:** Add a Node3DGizmo base (RefCounted) + the editor gizmo-plugin registration path, register in class_db.rs, and route the 3D viewport's per-node gizmo drawing/handle editing through it.

**Wiring requirement:** A registered gizmo for a node type draws its handles in the served 3D viewport and dragging a handle mutates the node.

comments.text:

The beads "register in class_db.rs" clause is done. Its WIRING REQUIREMENT — a registered gizmo drawing

gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs.

EditorNode3DGizmo concrete; viewport_3d.rs really exists; "zero matches" was accurate; it cites the doc
XML. A marked contrast with .184/.190/.191/.193.

*** ONE CORRECTION: Node3DGizmo DECLARES NOTHING ***
No properties, no methods, no virtuals — and it is ABSTRACT. The bead attributes
add_lines/add_handles/redraw/"handle drag callbacks" to it. ALL OF THAT LIVES ON EditorNode3DGizmo,
its concrete subclass. Node3DGizmo exists ONLY so Node3D can hold a gizmo reference without the scene
tree depending on the editor. Registering that surface on the base would let a script call methods
Godots Node3DGizmo does not have.

*** THE ARITY TRAP — verified for ALL 12 HOOKS by computing it from the API dump, not transcription ***
EVERY EditorNode3DGizmoPlugin hook takes the GIZMO as its FIRST argument, so each is EXACTLY ONE ARITY
HIGHER than EditorNode3DGizmos same-named virtual:
  _redraw                      gizmo=0 plugin=1
  _get_handle_name             gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _is_handle_highlighted       gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _get_handle_value            gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _begin_handle_action         gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _set_handle                  gizmo=4 plugin=5
  _commit_handle               gizmo=4 plugin=5

  _set_subgizmo_transform      gizmo=2 plugin=3
  _get_subgizmo_transform      gizmo=1 plugin=2
  _commit_subgizmos            gizmo=3 plugin=4
A PLUGIN SERVES MANY GIZMOS; A GIZMO SERVES ONE NODE. Copying the arities across would COMPILE and then
be handed the WRONG ARGUMENT at runtime. The test asserts both the literal pairs AND the +1 relation.
NOTE the get/set pair looks lopsided (get 1/2, set 2/3) — that is Godot; do NOT "correct" one to match.

  add_collision_segments/add_collision_triangles. A gizmo you can SEE is not automatically one you can

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — delivered. CodeHighlighter registered + a real runtime highlighter wired into the TextEdit draw path. 3 integration tests + 7 unit tests.

*** STALE BEAD PREMISE (partially) ***
"Not registered" is only half true. SyntaxHighlighter (the base) plus EditorSyntaxHighlighter and GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter were ALREADY registered (class_db.rs register_editor_classes). Only CodeHighlighter — the bead's actual subject — was missing. The other half held: the runtime TextEdit had NO draw case in control_render.rs at all (it drew nothing), so there was nothing for a highlighter to color.

*** WHAT I DID ***
1. Registered CodeHighlighter (class_db.rs, next to SyntaxHighlighter in register_editor_classes). Diffed EXACT vs extension_api.json: parent SyntaxHighlighter, concrete (GDREGISTER_CLASS at scene/register_scene_types.cpp:533), 28 methods, 7 properties. The 4 scalar colors default Color(0,0,0,1) (opaque black, per doc XML) and the 3 maps default empty.

2. New module gdscene/src/syntax_highlighter.rs — the RUNTIME highlighter, not the ClassDB schema and not the editor's. `CodeHighlighter { keyword_colors, default_color }` with `line_spans(line) -> Vec<HlSpan>`: tokenizes a line into identifier words vs separators, colors words that are configured keywords, merges adjacent same-color runs. Whole-word matching, so keyword `func` does NOT color the identifier `function`. 7 unit tests. `from_keyword_dict` builds it from a `{String: Color}` Variant::Dictionary, skipping mistyped entries.

3. Wired into control_render.rs draw_control: added a "TextEdit" | "CodeEdit" arm that reads `text`, builds the highlighter, and emits one DrawString per colored span at advancing x (mirroring how RichTextLabel already emits bbcode color spans). Without a highlighter it draws the whole line in the font color — TextEdit now draws its text at all.

4. Integration test gdscene/tests/syntax_highlighter_resource_test.rs (the acceptance test name): a CodeHighlighter with keyword `func`->blue on a TextEdit holding `func foo()` produces a BLUE DrawString for `func` and nothing else blue; class_exists true for both classes; plus a whole-word-matching case (`function` stays uncolored).

*** DESIGN NOTE — property representation ***
The bead says "assign a CodeHighlighter to a TextEdit". control_render reads ALL control config as flat node properties (theme_override_colors/font_color, texture-as-path, fx_elapsed_time), keeping "the renderer a pure function of the tree". So I carry the highlighter's keyword_colors as a node Dictionary property `syntax_highlighter/keyword_colors` — the exact shape of Godot's CodeHighlighter.keyword_colors ({String: Color}). A full live-resource-reference system for TextEdit.syntax_highlighter (a SyntaxHighlighter Resource pointer read at draw) would be a larger cross-cutting change to the resource/property model; the flat-dict representation is faithful to the existing renderer and fully exercises the acceptance.

*** SCOPE HONESTY ***
I implemented keyword_colors coloring — the path the acceptance exercises (`func`->blue). The schema also registers number_color/symbol_color/function_color/member_variable_color/member_keyword_colors/color_regions; coloring THOSE at draw time (number literals, symbols, member access, multi-line color regions) is a documented follow-up, not done here. I did not ship untested coloring logic for them.

*** BLAST RADIUS (swept, nothing excluded) ***
- The existing gdobject/tests/syntax_highlighter_family_registration.rs asserts only on SyntaxHighlighter/EditorSyntaxHighlighter/GDScriptSyntaxHighlighter (class_exists, is_parent_class, arities, own_methods subtraction) — it never mentions CodeHighlighter and asserts no total count, so adding CodeHighlighter cannot break it. Included it as a test command anyway.
- The only class_count() assertions (class_db.rs 7729/7732/7743 = 0/2/1) use register_class directly with clear_for_testing, NOT register_editor_classes — unreachable from my change.
- No test couples TextEdit/CodeEdit to an empty draw list, so adding the draw case breaks nothing.
- is_control recognizes "TextEdit" via CONTROL_CLASSES, so draw_control runs my arm (the richtextlabel test proves this exact render setup).

Cannot compile (worker cargo policy). All APIs (Dictionary iter/insert, Variant match ergonomics, Color Copy, get_property, text_width/GLYPH_*, Viewport/render_control_tree) verified against source. My regions in class_db.rs / control_render.rs / lib.rs are rustfmt-clean (those files carry pre-existing fmt diffs elsewhere that are not mine); the two new files are fully clean.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
GentleBadger — SECOND submission. First failed verification with a COMPILE error (101), fixed. Diagnosed from the real error, not guessed.

THE ERROR: the gdscene lib-test build failed with E0277, "1 previous error". The verifier's output tail happened to end on an unrelated `unused_assignments` WARNING in shapecast3d.rs:539 (a sibling file's test helper, not mine), which briefly looked like a foreign break — but that is a warning, and the crate had exactly 1 error, which was MINE:
