title: SceneTree/Viewport: dispatch _input/_unhandled_input/_shortcut_input/_unhandled_key_input with push_input + set_input_as_handled
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/input-propagation] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot routes each InputEvent through Viewport::push_input in a fixed order: _input (tree order) → GUI/gui_input (focus + mouse target) → _shortcut_input → _unhandled_key_input → _unhandled_input → physics picking, with set_input_as_handled() short-circuiting later stages (viewport.cpp). Nodes opt in via set_process_input/set_process_unhandled_input/etc. Patina has none of this: MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs:344) only builds a polling InputSnapshot; there is no process_script_input path (scene_tree.rs:1465-1493 lists only ready/process/physics/enter/exit) and no set_input_as_handled. Implement SceneTree::push_input(event) that walks nodes in Godot stage order, invokes the corresponding script virtual on nodes that enabled it, honors a per-event input_handled flag, and is called from MainLoop::step for each queued InputEvent BEFORE the process phase. Add process_script_input / process_script_unhandled_input dispatch to the gdscene scripting bridge plus per-node input-enable flags, and route the editor key/mouse endpoints (editor_server.rs:10106) through push_input rather than only InputState.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script implements _unhandled_input(event) and sets a var flips that var when a key InputEvent is pushed and MainLoop::step runs; a node that calls set_input_as_handled() in _input prevents a sibling's _unhandled_input from seeing the same event. (test: unhandled_input_dispatched_via_main_loop)

title: SceneTree/Node: emit lifecycle + per-frame signals (process_frame, physics_frame, node_added, tree_entered, …)
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/tree-signals] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot emits SceneTree.process_frame/physics_frame each frame (immediately before _process/_physics_process) and tree-mutation signals tree_changed/node_added/node_removed/node_renamed/tree_process_mode_changed/scene_changed; Nodes emit tree_entered/tree_exiting/tree_exited/child_entered_tree/child_exiting_tree/child_order_changed/ready/renamed. Scripts routinely `await get_tree().process_frame` and `node.tree_exiting.connect(...)`. Patina emits none: MainLoop::step (main_loop.rs) has no process_frame/physics_frame emission, and add_child/remove_node/reparent/set_name + LifecycleManager (lifecycle.rs) only append notifications to the log — no signal fires. Emit these through the existing SceneTree signal store (scene_tree.rs:1102 emit_signal): emit tree-level signals inside MainLoop::step (process_frame before the process phase, physics_frame before each physics tick) and inside add_child/remove_node/reparent/set_name; emit the Node-level signals on the affected node during enter/exit/child-order transitions in LifecycleManager.
acceptance_criteria: A script connecting to get_tree().process_frame AND to a child node's tree_entered receives both callbacks when the scene is stepped once through MainLoop; node_added fires when add_child inserts a live node and node_renamed fires on set_name. (test: scene_tree_and_node_signals_fire_via_main_loop)

title: SceneTree: change_scene_to_file, unload_current_scene, quit + auto_accept_quit/quit_on_go_back, get_frame, physics_interpolation
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/scenetree-scene-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's most-used scene API is change_scene_to_file(path) — deferred: free current scene, load+instance the .tscn, set current_scene — plus unload_current_scene, quit(exit_code) with auto_accept_quit/quit_on_go_back semantics, get_frame() (Engine frame counter), get_processed_tweens(), and physics_interpolation toggle (scene_tree.cpp). Patina has only change_scene_to_packed/_to_node/reload (scene_tree.rs:1806-1900). Implement change_scene_to_file by loading the res:// path through the existing PackedScene loader and delegating to change_scene_to_packed with Godot's deferred timing (swap at end of frame); add unload_current_scene, a quit() path that signals the MainLoop/PlatformBackend to stop (and the editor to Stop), get_frame() returning MainLoop.frame_count, get_processed_tweens(), and a physics_interpolation flag surfaced to the renderer. Wire change_scene_to_file so a script calling get_tree().change_scene_to_file('res://next.tscn') actually swaps the running scene in patina-runner and editor Play.
acceptance_criteria: Stepping a scene whose script calls change_scene_to_file('res://b.tscn') replaces current_scene with b's root by the next frame; quit() ends patina-runner's run loop (should_quit becomes true). (test: change_scene_to_file_swaps_running_scene)

title: Node: add_sibling, wildcard find_child/find_children/find_parent, has_node, get_path_to, is_ancestor_of, propagate_call/notification
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/node-query-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's Node query surface (node.cpp) includes add_sibling(node, force_readable_name), find_child(pattern, recursive, owned) and find_children(pattern, type, recursive, owned) with String wildcard matching, find_parent(pattern), has_node(path), get_path_to(node), is_ancestor_of(node), and propagate_notification(what)/propagate_call(method, args, parent_first). Patina exposes only exact-path resolution (scene_tree.rs get_node_by_path:695, find_child_by_name:711) plus get_index/node_path; the wildcard find_child/find_children, add_sibling, find_parent, get_path_to, is_ancestor_of and propagate_* are absent (0 non-test hits). Implement these on SceneTree over NodeId with Godot wildcard semantics (`*`/`?`), add_sibling inserting immediately after the node in its parent's child list (with unique-name resolution), and propagate_call/notification walking the subtree parent-first/child order. Expose them to the GDScript bridge so scripts can call node.find_child('Enemy*') and node.add_sibling(n).
acceptance_criteria: On a loaded scene, find_children('*', 'Sprite2D', true) returns every Sprite2D descendant, find_child('Ene*') matches by wildcard, add_sibling inserts a node immediately after its sibling in tree order, and propagate_call reaches all descendants. (test: node_find_and_sibling_queries)

title: SceneTree: make root a Window/Viewport with get_viewport/get_window and content-scale stretch pipeline
description:
[audit-key: scene-tree/viewport-tree] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

In Godot the SceneTree root is a Window (subclass of Viewport); every Node.get_viewport()/get_window() climbs to it, and its content_scale_mode (disabled/canvas_items/viewport) + content_scale_aspect (ignore/keep/keep_width/keep_height/expand) + content_scale_factor drive the stretch transform applied to the whole canvas (window.cpp — the web-canvas resize path). Patina creates the root as a bare Node (scene_tree.rs:114) with no Viewport/Window semantics, no get_viewport/get_window, no world_2d/world_3d, and content-scale only stored as an unused project-settings string (project_settings_dialog.rs:566). Make the root a Window-class node carrying Viewport state (size, world_2d/world_3d, canvas_transform), implement Node.get_viewport()/get_window() returning it, parse display/window/stretch/{mode,aspect,scale} from project.godot, and compute+apply the content-scale transform into the 2D draw path (gdrender2d) for both patina-runner and editor Play/viewport.
acceptance_criteria: get_viewport() on any node returns the root Window; with stretch mode=canvas_items, aspect=keep and a base size, rendering a scene into a 2x window scales the emitted canvas transform / draw output by 2. (test: root_window_content_scale_stretch)

comments.author: GreenBadger
comments.text:
[GreenBadger 2026-07-16] Handing back UNSTARTED — wrong worker lane. No code written. Scoping findings for the next worker:

DESCRIPTION VERIFIED ACCURATE (unusually — no staleness found):
  - gdscene has NO get_viewport / get_window (grep 'fn get_viewport|fn get_window' across gdscene/src = zero hits). Genuinely missing.
  - content_scale has ZERO consumers anywhere in engine-rs (grep -rl content_scale = no files). Genuinely unwired.
  - Viewport IS already registered in ClassDB (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1419) and Window is registered under it (:1435, .parent("Viewport")), with a test at :2805. So the CLASS surface exists; what is missing is making the tree ROOT actually be one, plus the stretch pipeline.

WHY THIS IS NOT DELIVERABLE IN THIS LANE:
  (a) It changes the SceneTree ROOT NODE TYPE (scene_tree.rs) — scene_tree.rs is the central file of gdscene with a very large call-site surface. Retyping the root cannot be compile-checked here (the policy hook blocks the Rust builder in this lane; the verifier lane is the sole builder), and a mistake in gdscene breaks every dependent crate for the whole swarm.
  (b) It is inherently cross-crate: gdscene (root/Viewport state) + gdresource (parse display/window/stretch/* from project.godot) + gdrender2d (apply the content-scale transform to the draw path) + patina-runner AND the editor Play viewport.
  (c) Acceptance asserts on emitted draw output ("scales the emitted canvas transform / draw output by 2") — needs a compile + a render.

SUGGESTED SPLIT (would make most of this landable, and some of it landable in a no-build lane):
  1. gdresource-only: parse display/window/stretch/{mode,aspect,scale} from project.godot into a typed struct (e.g. StretchMode/StretchAspect enums + factor) with a pure parse unit test. Self-contained, additive, no shared-crate risk — this one IS deliverable without a builder.
  2. Pure math: a `content_scale_transform(base_size, window_size, mode, aspect, factor) -> Transform2D` function with table-driven unit tests per aspect (ignore/keep/keep_width/keep_height/expand). Pure function, testable with no render.
  3. gdscene: root-as-Window + get_viewport()/get_window() (needs a builder).
  4. gdrender2d/runner: apply the transform to the draw path (needs a builder + render assertion).
Steps 1+2 are the bulk of the actual Godot semantics and carry near-zero cascade risk; 3+4 are the invasive parts. Recommend splitting into separate beads.

DO NOT accept a compile-clean "partial" against the current single bead: the verifier closes on compile rather than on the acceptance test, so a partial would FALSE-CLOSE this P1 while the root is still a bare Node and content_scale is still ignored.

title: Shaders: uniform hints + global/instance uniforms + ShaderInclude #include preprocessor
description:
[audit-key: shaders/shader-uniforms-globals-include] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: uniform hints drive semantics (source_color sRGB decode, hint_range clamps + inspector slider, filter_*/repeat_* sampler state, screen_texture/depth_texture/normal_roughness_texture bind engine buffers); `global uniform` values are stored in ProjectSettings shader_globals and set at runtime via RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_set; `instance uniform` are per-instance overrides; ShaderInclude (.gdshaderinc) + `#include` compose sources (doc/classes/Shader.xml, ShaderInclude.xml). Patina current state: hints are opaque strings with no behavior (gdserver3d/src/shader.rs:65); no global parameter store; RenderingServer.global_shader_parameter_* unimplemented; #include/ShaderInclude absent; instance/global uniforms lexed but ignored. Implementation approach: parse the full hint grammar and apply hint semantics in the compiler/interpreter; add a global-shader-parameter registry (seeded from project.godot shader_globals, mutable via a RenderingServer surface) and resolve `global uniform` reads from it; resolve `#include`/ShaderInclude during compilation (register a .gdshaderinc loader in gdresource/importers.rs). Wiring requirement: setting a global uniform at runtime changes shaded output next frame, and a #include'd function is callable in the fragment body.
acceptance_criteria: A shader declaring `global uniform vec4 sky_tint;` renders using the value set via the global-parameter API (changing it changes output), a `source_color` hinted uniform is sRGB-decoded, and a `#include "res://lib.gdshaderinc"` function resolves and executes. (test: `shader_uniform_hints_and_globals`)

title: Theme: full default theme (55 control types), icon item type, type variations, and Control get/add_theme_* resolution API
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/theme-system] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot's Theme (api: 69 methods) stores 6 item types (color/constant/font/font_size/icon/stylebox) with type variations and base types; default_theme.cpp generates the built-in theme with 794 item assignments across 55 control types; Controls resolve theme items by walking the theme_owner parent chain and merging per-instance overrides via ~40 Control methods (get_theme_color, add_theme_stylebox_override, has_theme_font, get_theme_default_font, set_theme_type_variation, begin/end_bulk_theme_override). Patina's Theme (gdscene/src/theme.rs) is a 5-category HashMap with no Icon type, styleboxes stored as flat Variant::Color, and a default_theme() covering only Label/Button/Panel (theme.rs:186); Control has no theme-resolution API at all (grep for get_theme_color/add_theme_*_override finds nothing); nothing is registered in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Implementation: extend gdscene/src/theme.rs with an Icon item type, type variations/base types, default font/size, merge/clear, and a get_theme_*/has_theme_*/add_theme_*_override resolution that walks the node's theme_owner chain (gdscene/src/control.rs); port default_theme.cpp coverage for the full control-type set; register Theme+ThemeDB in class_db.rs so .tscn/[gd_resource type="Theme"] loads into a usable Theme. Wiring requirement: a Control in a scene with a custom Theme and an add_theme_color_override resolves the override, then the theme, then ThemeDB default - and that resolved value feeds the render path from the text-render-wiring bead.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a Button that has a theme_type_variation and an add_theme_color_override('font_color') resolves font_color from the override; removing it falls back to the assigned Theme, then to the default theme; the default theme exposes styleboxes/colors/constants for the full Godot control-type set (Label, Button, Panel, LineEdit, Tree, ... ) and Theme/ThemeDB are constructible via ClassDB. (test: `control_theme_override_resolution`)

title: Input singleton: add get_axis / is_action_just_released / get_action_strength + capture just_released in the snapshot + circular-deadzone get_vector/get_axis
description:
[audit-key: input/input-singleton-api] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]
[verify-note: ADJUSTED: All technical claims verified: call_input_method (interpreter.rs:3167-3287) handles exactly 6 methods (is_action_pressed/is_action_just_pressed/is_key_pressed/get_global_mouse_position/is_mouse_button_pressed/get_vector) with `other => UndefinedFunction` catch-all (3284); Input.* routes ON]

title: StyleBox: StyleBoxFlat/Texture/Line/Empty resources + bordered/rounded/nine-patch drawing wired into Control rendering
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/stylebox] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

title: TextServer: line breaking, autowrap, alignment, ellipsis, tab stops via TextParagraph/TextLine layout
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/textserver-layout] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: STUB]

Godot lays out text through TextServer + TextParagraph/TextLine: breaking lines by word/grapheme/CJK against a width, applying autowrap_mode, horizontal/vertical alignment, justification_flags, text_overrun_behavior (ellipsis/trim), and tab stops, with per-size glyph metrics (ascent/descent/advance) (servers/text/text_server.cpp; scene/resources/text_paragraph.cpp). Patina's TextServerLite (gdrender2d/src/text_server.rs) only returns a fixed per-char advance (2 methods vs 236); TextLine/TextParagraph do not exist; Label's stored autowrap_mode/horizontal_alignment (gdscene/src/control.rs:800-843) drive nothing (no layout consumer); draw_string_multiline wraps only on literal newlines (font.rs:568). Implementation: build a TextParagraph/TextLine layout module in gdrender2d that, given a string + font (from the font-stack bead) + width + alignment + wrap mode + overrun behavior, produces positioned glyph runs (line breaks, alignment offsets, ellipsis); expose glyph metrics per size on the TextServer; have the Label update path (text-render-wiring bead) request a paragraph layout and emit one DrawString per positioned run. Wiring requirement: a Label with autowrap enabled and a bounded width wraps its text across multiple lines with the chosen alignment when rendered.
acceptance_criteria: A Label with a fixed width, autowrap_mode=word and horizontal_alignment=right, given text longer than its width, renders on multiple lines each right-aligned within the rect; text_overrun_behavior=trim_ellipsis on a single-line Label produces a trailing ellipsis; tab characters advance to tab stops. (test: `label_autowrap_and_alignment_layout`)

title: i18n: TranslationServer singleton + tr()/tr_n() builtins + .po/.csv loaders + auto_translate re-render
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/i18n] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot's TranslationServer (core/string/translation_server.cpp, 35 methods) matches locales (with script/country fallback + plural rules), holds Translation catalogs loaded from .po (context + plurals) and .csv, and Object.tr()/tr_n() look up the active-locale string; auto_translate_mode makes Controls re-translate their text on locale change; pseudolocalization + number formatting round out the surface. Patina has none: no TranslationServer/Translation impl or registration (grep empty), no tr/tr_n GDScript builtin (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs has print/str/load but no tr), no .po/.csv importer, and auto_translate_mode is an inert inspector property (gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:27). Implementation: add a TranslationServer singleton (gdcore or gdscene) with add_translation/set_locale/translate/translate_plural + locale fallback; add .po and .csv translation loaders (gdresource/src/importers.rs / loader) producing Translation resources; add tr()/tr_n() as Object methods routed by the GDScript interpreter (gdscript-interop) and script-reachable TranslationServer; propagate auto_translate so a Label re-renders on locale change. Wiring requirement: a script in a scene calling tr("KEY") after set_locale returns the catalog value and the bound Label re-renders the translated text via the text-render pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .po catalog with an entry KEY->"Bonjour", calling TranslationServer.set_locale('fr') then tr('KEY') from a GDScript in a scene returns 'Bonjour'; a Label with auto_translate whose text is 'KEY' shows the translated string, and switching locale re-renders it; tr_n selects the correct plural form. (test: `tr_translates_via_po_catalog`)

title: ParticleProcessMaterial: register resource class and parse its full property set from .tscn/.tres
description:
[audit-key: vfx-particles/particle-process-material] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

Godot ground truth: ParticleProcessMaterial is the resource that drives GPU particles; it exposes ~120 properties and 4 enums (EmissionShape POINT/SPHERE/SPHERE_SURFACE/BOX/POINTS/DIRECTED_POINTS/RING, ParticleFlags, SubEmitterMode, CollisionMode) plus min/max + CurveTexture curve for every parameter (scene/resources/particle_process_material.cpp). A .tscn references it as `process_material = SubResource("ParticleProcessMaterial_...")`. Patina current state: the class is unregistered (unregistered.txt; class_db.rs has no entry) and gdresource has no parse path (grep empty), so the process_material is silently dropped; particle nodes fall back to ad-hoc inline material structs (gdscene/src/particle.rs:87, gdserver3d/src/particles3d.rs:110). Implementation approach: (1) register ParticleProcessMaterial (parent Material) in gdobject/src/class_db.rs with its property + enum list; (2) parse the resource from text .tscn/.tres sub-resources in gdresource (loader.rs) into a Rust struct holding the full parameter set (emission shape+params, direction/spread/flatness, gravity, per-param min/max, curves, color/color_ramp, flags, collision/sub_emitter/turbulence groups); (3) hand that struct to the particle node's simulator (the wiring bead) replacing the inline material. Wiring requirement: scene load parses the SubResource -> node.process_material is populated -> simulator reads real values (start this with emission shape + gravity + initial velocity so it is observable).
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose GPUParticles2D/3D has a ParticleProcessMaterial SubResource (with e.g. emission_shape=BOX, gravity, initial_velocity_min/max, spread) results in a node whose simulator uses those exact values — particles emit within the box extents and integrate under the parsed gravity — verified by inspecting frame output after scene load (not by constructing the material in Rust). (test: `particle_process_material_parses_from_tscn`)

title: Web runtime: wasm32 cdylib entry + browser boot + rAF fixed-timestep MainLoop driver
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web_wasm_runtime] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: MISSING]

A browser-native engine must actually run in the browser. Godot's web platform (web_main.cpp) provides an emscripten entry that acquires the canvas, initializes the GL/WebGL2 (or WebGPU) context, and installs a main-loop callback driven by the browser; engine.js/preloader.js handle async load + progress. Patina has none of this: no wasm target, no wasm-bindgen/cdylib, and patina-runner (main.rs) is a native JSON-dumping CLI with a for-loop over a fixed frame count — not a real-time rAF loop. Implementation (stage this): (1) add a wasm crate (crate-type=cdylib) with a wasm-bindgen start() entry that acquires the <canvas>, requests a WebGPU adapter/device with a WebGL2 fallback, and installs a panic hook routing to console.error + an on-screen overlay; (2) implement a fixed-timestep driver (accumulator) invoked from requestAnimationFrame that calls gdscene MainLoop::step at the physics tick rate with visibility-hidden throttling and max_fps honoring; (3) feed the existing renderer/scene-tree so a loaded PackedScene renders to the canvas. Factor the timestep accumulator so its logic is unit-testable on native. This is the foundational enabler for the rest of the web-runtime beads (export payload, JS bridge, browser input/audio, persistence).
acceptance_criteria: The engine builds for wasm32-unknown-unknown (verifier build check) with a wasm-bindgen entry point, and the fixed-timestep browser driver advances gdscene MainLoop deterministically: feeding N seconds of accumulated frame time produces the Godot-correct number of physics steps and advances a scripted _process counter. (test: `web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver`) exercises the accumulator driving a real MainLoop over simulated elapsed time and asserts step count + a scene _process side effect, proving the driver is wired to the scene tick rather than to a fixed batch count.

comments.author: IvoryDune
comments.text:
AUTO-CLOSED BUT THE BROWSER HALF IS NOT DONE -- a game still cannot run in a browser (IvoryDune 2026-07-16). Flagging because a CLOSED status here will overstate web-runtime parity on any scorecard.

DELIVERED: gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs -- FrameDriver turns requestAnimationFrame timestamps into MainLoop::step calls (delta from successive DOMHighResTimeStamps, 0.25s max_frame_delta clamp so a backgrounded tab resuming with a multi-second jump cannot spiral, max_fps coalescing, hidden-tab throttling; skipped callbacks CARRY their delta so N seconds of browser time still yields N seconds of engine time). Pure logic over an injected timestamp, no browser types -- exactly the "factor the accumulator so it is unit-testable on native" the bead asked for. Plus gdscene/tests/web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver.rs (the named acceptance test): 1s as 60x16.6ms -> 60 steps / 60 physics ticks / _process=60, and the same second as 20x50ms -> 20 steps but STILL 60 physics ticks. Verify with: nextest run -p gdscene --test web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver

Deliberately did NOT duplicate the physics accumulator: MainLoop::step already banks delta and runs fixed 1/physics_ticks_per_second ticks capped by max_physics_steps_per_frame. The driver owns only the browser-side concerns.

NOT DELIVERED -- suggest splitting into new beads:
 (1) wasm entry does not acquire the <canvas>, request a WebGPU adapter/device, or fall back to WebGL2
 (2) no requestAnimationFrame callback is installed, and no on-screen panic overlay (only console_error_panic_hook, inherited from pat-u3l8c.109)
 (3) nothing feeds the renderer -- a loaded PackedScene does not draw to the canvas
 (4) max_fps is a driver setting, not yet read from Engine.max_fps / ProjectSettings

WHY THE BROWSER HALF IS BLOCKED, NOT MERELY SKIPPED: patina-web cannot depend on gdscene today -- gdscene -> gdaudio -> cpal is an unconditional native dep that breaks the wasm32 build (which is why pat-u3l8c.109 deliberately scoped patina-web to gdcore+gdvariant only). Wiring FrameDriver into patina-web's rAF entry requires the cpal cfg-gating owned by the audio web bead (pat-u3l8c.112). The driver was therefore landed in gdscene, where MainLoop lives and where it is natively provable now; the follow-up is then pure glue over an already-tested accumulator.

title: Editor: serve Project Settings -> Autoload tab wired to AutoloadManager (CRUD + reorder + persist to project.godot)
description:
[audit-key: autoload-global-singletons-runtime/autoload-editor-ui] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

GODOT: the editor's Project Settings -> Autoload tab lets the user add/remove/rename/reorder/enable autoloads, persisting to the [autoload] section. PATINA: a complete model exists — gdeditor/src/autoload_manager.rs AutoloadManager (add/remove/rename/move_up/move_down/set_enabled/globals/to_cfg/from_cfg) — but it is UNWIRED: no editor_server.rs route references it, project_settings_dialog.rs has 0 autoload refs, and EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) never mentions autoload. comments.author: IvoryDune
comments.text:
AUTO-CLOSED BUT ONLY ~25% DELIVERED (IvoryDune 2026-07-16).

DELIVERED: gdeditor/src/autoload_manager.rs gains to_project_godot_section() / from_project_godot_section() = REAL project.godot [autoload] INI (Name="*path", the * marks enabled exactly as Godot's Enable checkbox does, declaration-order preserving, reads only [autoload] out of a full project file) + 4 unit tests. Verify with: nextest run -p gdeditor --lib autoload_manager

WHY THAT WAS NEEDED: this bead's own plan said "persist via to_cfg", but to_cfg() is serde_json::to_string_pretty(self) -- it emits JSON despite its doc comment claiming "Serializes the [autoload] section to project-settings text". Following the bead literally would write a JSON blob into project.godot where an INI section belongs, and the acceptance (Global="*res://global.gd" present in the file) could never pass. The to_cfg/from_cfg docs are now corrected to say plainly they are JSON state snapshots, not project.godot text.

NOT DELIVERED -- suggest splitting into new beads:
 (1) hold an AutoloadManager in EditorState, loaded via from_project_godot_section at startup
 (2) editor_server.rs routes: GET list, POST add/remove/reorder/toggle-enabled, each rewriting project.godot
 (3) Autoload tab markup in EDITOR_HTML (editor_ui.rs) + project_settings_dialog.rs, guarded by an EDITOR_HTML-string test so the served JS actually calls the routes
 (4) the named acceptance test editor_autoload_tab_crud_persists

Scoped out deliberately, not overlooked: editor_server.rs is 21k lines and carries uncommitted concurrent work; a half-applied edit there breaks gdeditor for every worker in the swarm. The foundation landed above is what those routes call, so (1)-(4) are now purely additive.

SEPARATE BUG -- needs its own gdresource bead: ProjectLoader::get_autoloads (gdresource/src/project.rs ~331) ends with entries.sort_by(|a,b| a.name.cmp(&b.name)) "Sort by name for deterministic order". Godot uses DECLARATION order, and that order IS load order (an autoload may reference one declared before it). Patina therefore boots autoloads alphabetically, silently reordering _ready for any project whose declaration order is not alphabetical -- breaking the exact cross-autoload reference that pat-nzgdu.3 / pat-nzgdu.70 exist to support. Left untouched here: wrong crate for this bead, shared code, and existing tests may encode the sorted order.

title: ClassDB: expose script singleton + add signals/constants/enums to ClassInfo + instance reflection
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-classdb] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: PARTIAL]

Godot ground truth: ClassDB is a global singleton scripts call (ClassDB.class_exists, get_parent_class, get_inheriters_from_class, can_instantiate, instantiate, class_has_method, class_get_method_list, class_has_signal, class_get_signal_list, class_get_integer_constant(_list), class_has_enum/class_get_enum_list/class_get_enum_constants, class_get_property_list); and every Object answers has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id. Patina current state: ClassInfo (class_db.rs:64-83) stores only properties+methods (no signals/constants/enums); PropertyInfo/MethodInfo are thin (class_db.rs:17-52); nothing exposes ClassDB or instance reflection to GDScript (grep 0). Implementation: extend ClassInfo/ClassRegistration with signals (name+arg schema), integer constants, and enums, and populate them in the register_*_classes tables; enrich PropertyInfo with type/usage/hint_string and MethodInfo with return/arg types; add a ClassDB singleton path in the interpreter that routes to gdobject::class_db; add SceneAccess reflection entry points (has_method/has_signal/get_method_list/get_signal_list/get_property_list/get_instance_id) implemented against ClassDB + the node. Wiring requirement: a script must query ClassDB and its own class metadata and get non-empty, correct results.
acceptance_criteria: A script runs `assert(ClassDB.class_exists("Sprite2D")); assert(ClassDB.get_parent_class("Sprite2D") == "Node2D"); assert(ClassDB.class_has_method("Node","get_parent")); assert(has_method("_ready")); assert(get_method_list().size() > 0)` with no UndefinedFunction, and class_get_signal_list("Node") returns a non-empty list. (test: `classdb_singleton_reflection_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test classdb_singleton_reflection_test.

title: RefCounted: attach RefCountedBase to script RefCounted/Resource instances so ref counting + auto-free work
description:
[audit-key: core-object/core-object-refcounted] [port-audit 2026-07-12] [status: UNWIRED]

Godot ground truth: RefCounted.new() starts at refcount 1; sharing a reference increments and dropping decrements via reference()/unreference(); reaching 0 frees the object; get_reference_count() is script-observable; init_ref sets up first ownership. Patina current state: RefCountedBase (ref_counted.rs) is a correct-but-orphan primitive — 0 call sites outside gdobject (workspace grep) and no init_ref; script-created RefCounted objects therefore never count references or free. Implementation: give each script-instantiated RefCounted/Resource an owned RefCountedBase; increment/decrement it as the interpreter copies/drops Variant references that hold such objects; expose reference()/unreference()/get_reference_count()/init_ref() through the ObjectId (or Resource) dispatch and SceneAccess; free the backing object (and clear it from the alive registry) when the count hits 0. Also promote the WeakRef alive registry off thread_local so validity is process-global. Wiring requirement: RefCounted.new() in a script yields count 1 and its get_reference_count reflects additional references.
acceptance_criteria: A script executes `var r = RefCounted.new(); assert(r.get_reference_count() == 1); var r2 = r; assert(r.get_reference_count() == 2)` (or the engine's reference model) with no UndefinedFunction, and dropping all references invalidates a weakref taken to it. (test: `refcounted_reference_lifecycle_test`) runnable via cargo nextest --test refcounted_reference_lifecycle_test.

FrameBuffer3D (renderer.rs:31) has set_pixel/set_depth with in-crate unit tests (:1949+). Shadow maps are CPU too (:424). title: Editor: Script mode shows a central script editor (currently the SCRIPT button is cosmetic; viewport stays 2D)
description:
Found via live browser inspection (localhost:8080/editor): clicking the SCRIPT main-screen mode button highlights it and opens the small bottom Script panel tab, but the CENTRAL view still shows the 2D viewport (grid + node markers). Godot's Script mode replaces the central area with a full script editor.

ROOT CAUSE (same class as pat-7i8u4 / pat-v4o3a): the frontend mode handler (editor_ui.rs setupModeButtons) for 'script' only POSTs the mode + clicks the bottom Script tab; it never swaps the central #viewport-panel for a script editor. The full script editor ALREADY EXISTS (renderScript/fetchScript/highlightGDScript/saveScript with header, line numbers, syntax highlight, auto-indent) but renders into the bottom #script-panel only. Server already exposes GET /api/script, /api/script/save, /api/script/main_view, and /api/editor/main_view returns component 'script_editor'/is_2d_viewport:false for script mode — but the frontend never renders a central script view.

SCOPE (phase 1): when editor mode is 'script', the central area shows the script editor full-size (relocate the existing #script-panel editor into a central container), not the 2D viewport; switching back to 2D/3D restores the viewport. Empty state offers a New Script action. Open-scripts list, find/replace UI, and breakpoint gutter wiring are follow-ups.

TEST (app-level): served /editor HTML has a central script-editor container and the mode handler shows it in script mode; GET /api/editor/main_view after POST /api/editor/mode {script} reports component script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false. (test: editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view)
acceptance_criteria: In script mode the central area shows the script editor (relocated from the bottom panel), not the 2D viewport; switching to 2D/3D restores the viewport. Served /editor HTML has a central script-editor container wired into the mode switch; GET /api/editor/main_view after POST mode script reports component script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false. Test: editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
VERIFIED + CLOSING. Script mode now shows the script editor in the CENTRAL area instead of the 2D viewport. Implementation (editor_ui.rs): added a central #script-editor-panel + #script-main-host; new showScriptMode(on) relocates the existing #script-panel code editor into the central host in script mode and restores it + the viewport when leaving (reuses the full editor — header/Save/New, line numbers, syntax highlight, auto-indent — with no duplicate-id issues). Mode handler calls showScriptMode(mode==='script'). Test crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_script_view_test.rs::editor_script_mode_serves_script_editor_view PASSES (served HTML has the central container + wiring; /api/editor/main_view reports script_editor / is_2d_viewport:false). Verified LIVE in Chrome: clicking SCRIPT shows the central code editor, viewport gone, 'Switched to script mode' logged.

FOLLOW-UP REQUEST (selecting a node shows its script) — DONE: the selection handler already calls fetchScript(_script_path); the demo scene just had no scripts attached. examples/editor.rs now attaches fixtures/scripts/player.gd to Player and enemy_spawner.gd to Enemy (sets _script_path). title: Verifier timeout kill misses sccache-parented rustc orphans
description:
The pat-regax process-group kill reaps the verify's bash/cargo/nextest tree on timeout, but compiles routed through RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache run as children of the long-lived sccache SERVER process (pid 1-parented), outside the verify's process group. Observed live 2026-07-14: after the platform_suite verify timed out and was group-killed, its rustc (gdrender3d) survived for 6+ min at 0 CPU, parented by sccache, holding an sccache slot.

Fix options: (a) on timeout, enumerate+kill rustc processes whose cmdline matches the verify's workspace AND whose start time falls within the verify window; (b) run verifies with RUSTC_WRAPPER unset and rely on the private target-verifier incremental cache; (c) sccache --stop-server on timeout (heavy: aborts other sessions' compiles).

Acceptance: a test in verifier.rs proving a wrapper-spawned grandchild outside the process group is reaped after timeout (analogous to verifier_timeout_kills_process_group).

title: Verifier: kill the entire process group on verify timeout (orphaned cargo-nextest survives and wedges the lane)
description:
Observed 2026-06-10: each 900s verify timeout killed the am-run/shell parent but left cargo-nextest alive as an orphan, each holding ~26 spawned test-binary children. Four generations piled up (15:48, 16:03, 16:18, 16:33 - exactly one per 15-min verify cycle), 102 hung child processes total, all stuck at _dyld_start (AMFI code-sign wedge). The orphans also held the cargo build-dir lock so every later verify spent its whole 900s waiting.

IMPLEMENTATION: in the orchestrator verifier lane, launch the verify command in its own process group (setsid/setpgid) and on timeout send SIGKILL to the negative pgid; then waitpid-reap. Also assert post-kill that no cargo-nextest/test-binary descendants survive (pgrep by pgid) and log if they do.

TEST: spawn a fake long-running command tree (sh -c 'sleep 1000 & sleep 1000') via the verifier timeout path with a 2s timeout and assert zero surviving descendants after the kill (test: verifier_timeout_kills_process_group).
close_reason: verifier.rs: bash verify child now leads its own process group (process_group(0)); on timeout SIGKILL the negative pgid (whole tree, not just bash) + surviving_group_members() post-kill assertion logs any orphans. Stops orphaned cargo-nextest from holding the build-dir lock. Test verifier_timeout_kills_process_group PASS (cargo nextest -p patina-orchestrator).

title: Editor viewport: node-name labels render as tofu/placeholder boxes for most glyphs (Player -> ??a???)
description:
Found via live browser inspection of examples/editor.rs (http://localhost:8080/editor, demo_2d.tscn).

REPRO: Load /editor with fixtures/scenes/demo_2d.tscn. The server-rendered viewport PNG (/api/viewport/png) draws each node's name label under its marker, but most characters render as empty placeholder boxes: 'Player' renders as five tofu boxes with only the 'a' glyph drawn. 'Enemy' and 'Ground' similar. Vertical ruler tick labels are also garbled.

ROOT CAUSE AREA: the editor overlay text path in the software renderer (gdrender2d / gdeditor viewport overlay) is drawing labels with a glyph set that covers only a small subset of ASCII (some lowercase letters work, most upper/lowercase missing). pat-04f (BitmapFont/FontFile text rendering) is closed, so either the overlay label path does not use that font system or the fallback atlas is incomplete.

IMPLEMENTATION: route editor viewport label drawing through the real font rendering path (full printable-ASCII coverage minimum) instead of the partial debug atlas; same for ruler tick labels.

TEST: render demo_2d.tscn editor frame and assert the glyph lookup used by viewport labels returns a non-placeholder glyph for every char in 'PlayerEnemyGround0123456789-' (unit), plus an app-level check that the rendered label bounding box for 'Player' is non-uniform across the 6 glyph cells (test: editor_viewport_label_glyph_coverage).
acceptance_criteria: Every char in 'PlayerEnemyGround0123456789-' resolves to a real glyph in the viewport label text path (no placeholder box); ruler tick labels legible; test editor_viewport_label_glyph_coverage passes

title: Animation: expose AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback so scripts can travel/start/stop a state machine
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-state-machine] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp + animation_node_state_machine.cpp; doc/classes/AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.xml; extension_api.json class AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback (methods travel, travel_to_next_blend, start, next, stop, is_playing, get_current_node, get_current_play_position, get_current_length, get_travel_path, get_fading_from_node) | upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp; doc/classes/AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition.xml (properties: xfade_time, xfade_curve, break_loop_at_end, reset, priority, switch_mode {IMMEDIATE,SYNC,AT_END}, advance_mode {DISABLED,ENABLED,AUTO}, advance_condition, advance_expression) | upstream/godot/editor/animation/animation_state_machine_editor.cpp, animation_blend_space_1d_editor.cpp, animation_blend_space_2d_editor.cpp, animation_blend_tree_editor_plugin.cpp

**Godot classes:** AnimationNodeStateMachine, AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback, AnimationTree, AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition, AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D, AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D, AnimationNodeBlendTree

**Patina today:**
- [animation] Patina implements the algorithm but nothing calls it: `StateMachine::travel` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:507), `travel_path` (:467) and `is_travelling` (:518). `grep -rn '\.travel(|is_travelling|travel_path' --include=*.rs crates/` returns ONLY those three definitions plus five `#[cfg(test)]` hits inside the same file (animation_tree.rs:2127-2187). No script path exists either: `AnimationTree::get_parameter` (animation_tree.rs:611) returns only Variants that were previously `set`, so `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback")` yields Nil, and `grep -rn 'parameters/playback' --include=*.rs crates/` returns 0 hits. `crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs` has `animation_player_*` hooks (lines 544-635) but no `animation_tree_*` hook at all. Registration exists as a name only: class_db.rs registers `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback` (1 occurrence) with no methods.
- [animation] Patina's `StateTransition` carries exactly two Godot fields: `condition` and `crossfade` — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:525-532. The .tscn reader reads only `xfade_time` and `advance_condition` — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs:277-278. `grep -rn 'advance_expression|break_loop_at_end|auto_advance' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0 hits each; `advance_mode`/transition `priority`/`xfade_curve`/`reset` also 0 hits in the state-machine path. `SwitchMode` (animation_tree.rs:186-212) exists but is only used by `AnimationNodeTransition` (animation_tree.rs:222), not by state-machine edges. Consequence: an ADVANCE_MODE_AUTO edge (the standard "attack → idle when the clip ends" pattern) never fires.
- [editor-ux] POST /api/animation/tree/state/move, /state/remove, /transition/remove and /transition/set are all in the editor_server.rs dispatch table but have 0 references in editor_ui.rs (only /api/animation/tree, /tree/state/add and /tree/transition/add are called). So the served state-machine graph is add-only: states cannot be moved or deleted and transitions cannot be edited or removed. Blend spaces and blend trees are absent entirely: `grep -ci 'blend space\|blend_space\|blendSpace' editor_ui.rs` = 0, and no /api/animation/tree/blend* route exists.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/anim_tree_graph.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: every state-machine-driven game steers the graph through the playback object — `var p = $AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback"); p.travel("Run")`. `AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback` (upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_node_state_machine.cpp, doc/classes/AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback.xml) exposes travel(node, reset_on_teleport=true), travel_to_next_blend, start(node, reset=true), next(), stop(), is_playing(), get_current_node(), get_current_play_position(), get_current_length(), get_travel_path(), get_fading_from_node(). Nested state machines expose their own playback at `parameters/<name>/playback`.

Patina current state: the BFS travel algorithm is fully implemented and unit-tested but has ZERO runtime callers. `StateMachine::travel` engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:507, `travel_path` :467, `is_travelling` :518 — the only call sites are the module's own `#[cfg(test)]` tests (animation_tree.rs:2127-2187). `AnimationTree::get_parameter` (animation_tree.rs:611) only returns previously-`set` Variants so `get("parameters/playback")` is Nil; `SceneAccess` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:544-635) has no `animation_tree_*` method at all. A game can therefore only flip `parameters/conditions/<x>` booleans; it cannot travel.

Implementation approach: (1) add a `StateMachinePlayback` handle type in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs that addresses a `StateMachine` by its `parameters/<path>` prefix inside the attached `AnimationTree`; (2) mint an ObjectId-style handle for it in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs `get_node_property` when `prop` ends in `/playback` (mirroring the existing tween-handle pattern at scripting.rs:2943 `tween_call`); (3) add `animation_tree_playback_call(&mut self, handle: u64, method: &str, args: &[Variant]) -> Option<Variant>` to `SceneAccess` in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs and dispatch it from the ObjectId method arm in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs (next to the `animation_player_*` arms at interpreter.rs:9335-9522), routing travel/start/next/stop/is_playing/get_current_node/get_travel_path onto the StateMachine; (4) make `start(node, reset)` and `next()` real (snap current, clear travel queue / take next hop).

Wiring requirement: .tscn with AnimationTree(tree_root=AnimationNodeStateMachine) + attached GDScript → `_ready` grabs `parameters/playback` → `travel("run")` → `MainLoop::step` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2968 `process_animation_trees`) crossfades along the path → the target node's animated property reaches the "run" clip's value and `get_current_node()` reports "run".

**Merged findings (3):** AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback — the `parameters/playback` control object (travel/start/next/stop/is_playing/get_current_node/get_travel_path/get_current_play_position/get_current_length/get_fading_from_node); AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition full field surface — switch_mode, advance_mode (incl. AUTO), advance_expression, priority, xfade_curve, reset, break_loop_at_end; AnimationTree editor: state machine edit ops, blend spaces 1D/2D, blend tree graph

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn whose AnimationTree holds a 3-state machine (idle→run→jump) with an attached script that calls `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback").travel("jump")` in `_ready`, then stepping MainLoop past the declared xfade times, leaves the driven node's property at the `jump` clip's sampled value and `get_current_node()` == "jump"; `get_travel_path()` returned the two-hop path before arrival. (test: `animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose AnimationTree holds a 3-state machine (idle→run→jump) with an attached script that calls `$AnimationTree.get("parameters/playback").travel("jump")` in `_ready`, then stepping MainLoop past the declared xfade times, leaves the driven node's property at the `jump` clip's sampled value and `get_current_node()` == "jump"; `get_travel_path()` returned the two-hop path before arrival. (test: `animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animation_tree_state_machine_playback_travel_from_script`.

**Patina today:**
- [editor-ux] gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_handles.rs implements Godot's box face-handle math (box_get_handles/box_set_handle/box_handle_drag_commands) but has ZERO non-test callers: `grep -rn viewport_3d_handles --include=*.rs` returns only lib.rs:156 (mod decl) and crates/gdeditor/tests/viewport3d_gizmo_handles_e2e.rs:18. **Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: every selected 3D node draws its own gizmo with draggable handles (upstream/godot/editor/scene/3d/gizmos/collision_shape_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp resizes BoxShape3D/SphereShape3D/CapsuleShape3D via Gizmo3DHelper; light_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp drags omni range and spot angle/range; camera_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp drags FOV/size). The only handle endpoint, api_shape_handles (editor_server.rs:14014), returns editable:false for every class except CollisionShape2D (editor_server.rs:14028). editor_ui.rs's 3D pointer handlers (editor_ui.rs:6167-6240) only post /api/viewport/3d/gizmo/{begin,update,end} for the transform gizmo.\n\nAPPROACH: add `GET /api/viewport/3d/handles?node_id=` + `POST /api/viewport/3d/handle/{begin,update,end}` to editor_server.rs, backed by viewport_3d_handles.rs for BoxShape3D and new sphere/capsule/cylinder handle helpers, plus OmniLight3D range and SpotLight3D angle/range handles. title: Physics2D: wire StaticBody2D conveyor velocities and implement AnimatableBody2D
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-staticbody-family] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/static_body_2d.cpp (constant_linear_velocity/constant_angular_velocity → PhysicsServer2D BODY_STATE_LINEAR_VELOCITY on a static body) and upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/animatable_body_2d.cpp:33-66 (AnimatableBody2D extends StaticBody2D, sync_to_physics installs body_set_state_sync_callback so the body pushes the platform's motion into contacting bodies).

**Godot classes:** StaticBody2D, AnimatableBody2D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-2d] The solver fully implements surface velocity: `PhysicsBody2D::constant_linear_velocity` / `constant_angular_velocity` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:117-122, consumed by the friction path at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/solver.rs:341, with green tests at solver.rs:864 and the integration test /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/tests/physics2d_solver_stacking_conveyor_sleep.rs:178 — which constructs `PhysicsBody2D` structs directly and never touches a SceneTree. The scene bridge never reads the properties: `grep -rn "constant_linear_velocity|constant_angular_velocity" engine-rs/crates/gdscene/ engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/` → 0 hits; the only workspace mentions outside gdphysics2d/gdphysics3d are the editor inspector schema (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:3296-3297) and the runner's class defaults (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs:66-69). `register_bodies` (physics_server.rs:945-990) sets 16 properties, none of them these. Separately, `body_type_for_class` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:32-39) maps only RigidBody2D/StaticBody2D/CharacterBody2D — an `AnimatableBody2D` node in a .tscn becomes NO physics body at all (no collision, no platform velocity), and `sync_to_physics` has 0 hits in gdphysics2d/gdscene.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/solver.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: StaticBody2D.constant_linear_velocity / constant_angular_velocity drag contacting bodies without moving the static body itself (upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/static_body_2d.cpp) — conveyor belts and turntables. AnimatableBody2D (upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/animatable_body_2d.cpp:33-66) is a StaticBody2D whose `sync_to_physics` makes the physics body follow the node's animated/tweened transform and imparts that motion to riders.

PATINA: the solver already does the work — `PhysicsBody2D::constant_linear_velocity`/`constant_angular_velocity` (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:117-122), surface-velocity friction (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/solver.rs:341), green tests at solver.rs:864 and engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/tests/physics2d_solver_stacking_conveyor_sleep.rs:178 — but those tests build `PhysicsBody2D` structs by hand. The scene bridge never reads the node properties (0 hits for `constant_linear_velocity` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/), so an authored conveyor does nothing. `body_type_for_class` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:32-39) has no `AnimatableBody2D` arm, so those nodes are not physics at all.

APPROACH: in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, extend `body_type_for_class` with `"AnimatableBody2D" => BodyType::Kinematic` (Godot treats it as a moved static body). In `register_bodies` (~physics_server.rs:945) read `constant_linear_velocity` (Vector2) and `constant_angular_velocity` (float) onto the body next to the existing `gravity_scale`/`linear_damp` reads. Re-read them each tick in `sync_to_physics` (physics_server.rs:1288) under the Static/Kinematic arms so a script can change a belt's speed. For AnimatableBody2D honor `sync_to_physics` (default true): under the Kinematic arm, derive the body's per-tick velocity from (new_global_position - previous_global_position)/dt and store it as constant_linear_velocity so riders are carried, mirroring how CharacterBody2D's `platform_velocity` is already consumed at physics_server.rs:1794.

WIRING: MainLoop::step → PhysicsServer::sync_to_physics reads the node properties → step_physics → ContactSolver2D surface-velocity term moves the rider → sync_from_physics writes the rider's new position back to its Node2D.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a StaticBody2D floor whose `constant_linear_velocity = Vector2(100, 0)` carries a resting RigidBody2D to the right at ~100 px/s after one second of MainLoop ticks; an AnimatableBody2D platform whose `position` is driven by a Tween/AnimationPlayer both blocks a falling body and carries it horizontally. (test: `staticbody2d_conveyor_and_animatablebody_scene`) — loads the scene through the packed-scene path, runs MainLoop::step, asserts the rider's global x displacement and that the AnimatableBody2D registered a body.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a StaticBody2D floor whose `constant_linear_velocity = Vector2(100, 0)` carries a resting RigidBody2D to the right at ~100 px/s after one second of MainLoop ticks; an AnimatableBody2D platform whose `position` is driven by a Tween/AnimationPlayer both blocks a falling body and carries it horizontally. (test: `staticbody2d_conveyor_and_animatablebody_scene`) — loads the scene through the packed-scene path, runs MainLoop::step, asserts the rider's global x displacement and that the AnimatableBody2D registered a body.

title: Area3D: publish overlapping areas, honour damp space-override modes, emit shape-indexed signals
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-area-overlap-api] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Area3D.xml members linear_damp_space_override, angular_damp_space_override; signals body_shape_entered/body_shape_exited/area_shape_entered/area_shape_exited; methods get_overlapping_areas/has_overlapping_areas/overlaps_area; upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp | upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp — wind_source_path, wind_force_magnitude, wind_attenuation_factor (drive SoftBody3D and particle wind) and reverb_bus_enabled, reverb_bus_name, reverb_bus_amount, reverb_bus_uniformity (route AudioStreamPlayer3D output through a reverb bus while a listener is inside) | doc/classes/Area3D.xml members wind_source_path, wind_force_magnitude, wind_attenuation_factor, reverb_bus_enabled, reverb_bus_name, reverb_bus_amount, reverb_bus_uniformity, audio_bus_override, audio_bus_name; upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp

**Godot classes:** Area3D, AudioStreamPlayer3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] (a) The GDScript arms for `get_overlapping_areas`/`has_overlapping_areas`/`overlaps_area` read the node property `_overlapping_areas` (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1519-1546). That property is published ONLY by the 2D server: crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1527 `publish_overlapping_areas`. `grep -n "publish_overlapping_areas\|_overlapping_areas" crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs` returns nothing — the 3D bridge publishes only `_overlapping_bodies` (:1417). So for any Area3D these three script calls silently return an empty Array / false forever. (b) crates/gdphysics3d/src/area3d.rs:96-141 has only `gravity_space_override`; the 2D twin carries `linear_damp_space_override` and `angular_damp_space_override` (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1024), and the 3D bridge's area sync (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:1205-1233) never reads them, so an Area3D damp override applies unconditionally regardless of the authored COMBINE/REPLACE/DISABLED mode. (c) `grep -rn "body_shape_entered\|area_shape_entered" --include='*.rs' crates/*/src` → 0 hits; the shape-indexed signal pair does not exist.
- [nodes-3d] Repo-wide grep for `wind_source_path`, `wind_force_magnitude`, `wind_attenuation_factor` finds exactly one hit — a comment in a test acknowledging the gap: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/area3d_gravity.rs:25 "⚠️ Also NOT delivered: wind (`wind_force_magnitude`/`wind_source_path`)". Repo-wide grep for `reverb_bus_enable`, `reverb_bus_name`, `reverb_bus_amount`, `reverb_bus_uniformity` returns zero hits anywhere in engine-rs. Point gravity by contrast IS implemented (gravity_point_center / gravity_point_unit_distance, exercised by gdscene/tests/area3d_gravity.rs:48-91).
- [physics-3d] `grep -rn "wind_force_magnitude\|wind_source_path\|wind_attenuation_factor\|reverb_bus" --include='*.rs' crates/*/src` → 0 hits (the only mention anywhere is a comment in crates/gdscene/tests/area3d_gravity.rs:25 listing them as NOT delivered). crates/gdphysics3d/src/area3d.rs:96-141 has no wind or audio fields, and crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:1205-1233 reads no such properties. For the audio bus override the implementation exists but has no caller: crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:302 `redirect_stream_bus` is documented at :297-301 as existing precisely for "Godot's Area3D/Area2D audio-bus override", yet `grep -rn "redirect_stream_bus\|audio_bus_override" crates/gdscene/src crates/patina-runner/src` returns 0 hits — no overlap event ever reroutes a voice.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/area3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: Area3D exposes `get_overlapping_areas()`/`has_overlapping_areas()`/`overlaps_area()` alongside the body variants, carries THREE independent space-override modes (`gravity_space_override`, `linear_damp_space_override`, `angular_damp_space_override`, each DISABLED/COMBINE/COMBINE_REPLACE/REPLACE/REPLACE_COMBINE resolved by `priority`), and emits four shape-indexed signals — `body_shape_entered(body_rid, body, body_shape_index, local_shape_index)`, `body_shape_exited`, `area_shape_entered`, `area_shape_exited` (doc/classes/Area3D.xml; upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/area_3d.cpp).\n\nPATINA: (1) crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1519-1546 answers `get_overlapping_areas`/`has_overlapping_areas`/`overlaps_area` from the node property `_overlapping_areas`, which only the 2D server writes (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1527 `publish_overlapping_areas`). crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs has no such function — it publishes only `_overlapping_bodies` (:1417) — so every Area3D reports an empty overlap set to script even while `area_entered` fires correctly (:1390). (2) crates/gdphysics3d/src/area3d.rs:96-141 models only `gravity_space_override`; `linear_damp`/`angular_damp` are applied unconditionally in crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:595-606 via `effective_space_params`. (3) no shape-indexed signals exist anywhere (`grep -rn "body_shape_entered" crates/*/src` → 0).\n\nAPPROACH: (a) add `publish_overlapping_areas(&self, tree)` to crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs mirroring :1417, backed by a `get_overlapping_areas` on gdphysics3d::Area3D (crates/gdphysics3d/src/area3d.rs, next to `get_overlapping_bodies`), and call it from `sync_from_physics` inside the existing `if !self.node_to_area.is_empty()` block (:1473-1477). (b) add `linear_damp_space_override`/`angular_damp_space_override` fields to gdphysics3d::Area3D, read them in the area sync (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:1205-1233 via `space_override_from_int_3d`), and resolve them independently of gravity in `PhysicsWorld3D::effective_space_params`. (c) carry the per-body/per-area shape index through OverlapEvent3D/AreaOverlapEvent3D and emit the four `*_shape_*` signals from `process_overlap_signals` (:1367) / `process_area_overlap_signals` (:1390).\n\nWIRING: all of it must fire from the MainLoop physics tick (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2840-2842 -> sync_from_physics), reaching a GDScript `_physics_process` on the same tick the overlap changes.

**Merged findings (3):** Area3D.get_overlapping_areas()/has_overlapping_areas()/overlaps_area() from GDScript; Area3D linear_damp_space_override & angular_damp_space_override; body_shape_entered/body_shape_exited/area_shape_entered/area_shape_exited signals; Area3D wind source and reverb bus routing; Area3D wind (wind_source_path, wind_force_magnitude, wind_attenuation_factor), reverb bus routing (reverb_bus_enabled/name/amount/uniformity) and audio_bus_override/audio_bus_name

**Prove it:** With a .tscn where two Area3Ds overlap and a RigidBody3D falls through one of them, driven only by MainLoop::step: (a) a script on the first area gets a one-element Array from `get_overlapping_areas()` and `overlaps_area(other)` == true while overlapping, and an empty Array after they separate; (b) an Area3D authored with `linear_damp_space_override = 0` (DISABLED) and `linear_damp = 5.0` leaves a body's speed unchanged, while the same area with COMBINE slows it; (c) a connected `body_shape_entered` handler receives four arguments including a local_shape_index of 0. (test: `area3d_overlap_api_parity`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test area3d_overlap_api_parity`.
acceptance_criteria: With a .tscn where two Area3Ds overlap and a RigidBody3D falls through one of them, driven only by MainLoop::step: (a) a script on the first area gets a one-element Array from `get_overlapping_areas()` and `overlaps_area(other)` == true while overlapping, and an empty Array after they separate; (b) an Area3D authored with `linear_damp_space_override = 0` (DISABLED) and `linear_damp = 5.0` leaves a body's speed unchanged, while the same area with COMBINE slows it; (c) a connected `body_shape_entered` handler receives four arguments including a local_shape_index of 0. (test: `area3d_overlap_api_parity`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test area3d_overlap_api_parity`.

title: Physics3D: support multiple offset CollisionShape3D children per body (and CollisionPolygon3D)
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-collision-shapes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/collision_object_3d.cpp (shape owners: shape_owner_add_shape / shape_owner_set_transform / shape_owner_set_disabled); doc/classes/CollisionObject3D.xml; doc/classes/CollisionPolygon3D.xml

**Godot classes:** CollisionObject3D, CollisionShape3D, CollisionPolygon3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:556-562 picks a single shape with `.children().to_vec().iter().find_map(|&child_id| shape_from_node_3d(tree, child_id))` — first matching DIRECT child only, defaulting to `Shape3D::Sphere { radius: 0.5 }`. `shape_from_node_3d` (:285-460) returns bare geometry and never reads the CollisionShape3D node's own transform, so a shape authored at an offset (the normal way to build a capsule-plus-feet character or an L-shaped platform) collides at the body origin. The shape is written only inside the `if !self.node_to_body.contains_key(&nid)` registration branch (:548-585), so unlike areas (which re-seed the shape every tick at :1187-1189) a body's shape is never refreshed after the first tick. CollisionPolygon3D is unsupported: crates/gdphysics3d/src/shape.rs:8-42 has no such variant, and the only implementation (crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape3d.rs:24) belongs to the orphan gdphysics2d 3D stack that no runtime path uses.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/shape.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: a CollisionObject3D owns a LIST of shapes, each with its own transform relative to the body (upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/collision_object_3d.cpp shape_owner_add_shape / shape_owner_set_transform / shape_owner_set_disabled). CollisionShape3D contributes its own node transform, so authoring a character as a capsule offset up by half its height, or a platform as two boxes, is routine. Shapes added, moved, resized or disabled at runtime take effect immediately. CollisionPolygon3D extrudes a 2D polygon by `depth` into a convex/concave shape.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:556-562 takes the FIRST matching direct child only and falls back to a 0.5-radius sphere; crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:285-460 (`shape_from_node_3d`) returns geometry with no transform, so every shape is centred on the body origin; and the shape is assigned only in the registration branch (:548-585), never refreshed (areas do refresh, :1187-1189). A two-box StaticBody3D platform therefore collides as one box at the origin, and an offset capsule character collides at its feet. CollisionPolygon3D has no gdphysics3d shape variant (crates/gdphysics3d/src/shape.rs:8-42).\n\nAPPROACH: (1) change gdphysics3d::PhysicsBody3D (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:64 `pub shape: Shape3D`) to carry `shapes: Vec<(Transform3D, Shape3D)>`, keeping a single-shape convenience constructor; update `world_aabb` (:400), the broadphase (crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:619) and the narrowphase dispatch (crates/gdphysics3d/src/collision.rs:207 `test_collision_rot`) to iterate shape pairs; (2) make `shape_from_node_3d` return `(Transform3D, Shape3D)` using the CollisionShape3D node's local transform relative to its body, and walk the body's whole descendant subtree (stopping at nested CollisionObject3D nodes) instead of `find_map` over direct children; (3) re-seed the shape list every tick in `sync_to_physics` for bodies as it already does for areas; (4) add a `CollisionPolygon3D` case producing an extruded convex hull from `polygon` + `depth`.\n\nWIRING: the shape list must be rebuilt from the tree on every `sync_to_physics` call in the MainLoop physics tick (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2840), so an editor-moved or script-moved CollisionShape3D changes collision the next tick.

**Prove it:** Driven only by MainLoop::step on a loaded .tscn: (a) a StaticBody3D with two BoxShape3D children offset to x = -2 and x = +2 stops a falling RigidBody3D dropped above EITHER box, and lets one dropped at x = 0 fall through; (b) a RigidBody3D whose single CollisionShape3D is offset upward by 1.0 comes to rest with its node origin 1.0 lower than the same body with a centred shape; (c) resizing that CollisionShape3D's shape after the first physics tick changes the resting height on a later tick. (test: `physics3d_multi_shape_bodies`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_multi_shape_bodies`.

(test: `physics3d_multi_shape_bodies`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_multi_shape_bodies`.

title: RigidBody3D: dispatch _integrate_forces with a PhysicsDirectBodyState3D and expose contact/exception APIs
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-direct-body-state] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/RigidBody3D.xml (_integrate_forces, custom_integrator, get_colliding_bodies, get_contact_count, get_inverse_inertia_tensor, set_axis_velocity); doc/classes/PhysicsDirectBodyState3D.xml (28 methods incl. get_contact_impulse/get_contact_local_normal/get_space_state); doc/classes/PhysicsBody3D.xml (add_collision_exception_with, remove_collision_exception_with, get_collision_exceptions) | doc/classes/RigidBody3D.xml members physics_material_override, center_of_mass, center_of_mass_mode, inertia, linear_damp_mode, angular_damp_mode; doc/classes/PhysicsBody3D.xml members axis_lock_linear_*/axis_lock_angular_*; upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/rigid_body_3d.cpp

**Godot classes:** RigidBody3D, PhysicsDirectBodyState3D, PhysicsBody3D, StaticBody3D, PhysicsMaterial

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] `grep -rn "_integrate_forces" --include='*.rs' crates/` → 0 hits; `custom_integrator` exists only as a ClassDB property (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1837) and an inspector string (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:2893) — nothing reads it in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::sync_rigid_body (:1049-1118). `grep -rn '"get_colliding_bodies"\|"get_contact_count"\|"get_inverse_inertia_tensor"' --include='*.rs' crates/` → 0 script arms, even though the data exists on the body (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:359 `get_contact_count`, :364 `get_colliding_bodies`, :473 `inverse_inertia_diagonal`). `set_axis_velocity` has a script arm but coerces to 2D: crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9704-9713 writes `Variant::Vector2(vec2_arg(args, 0))` into `_pending_axis_velocity`, which only the 2D server consumes (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1312) — a Vector3 call collapses to zero. `grep -rn "add_collision_exception_with\|get_collision_exceptions" --include='*.rs' crates/` → 0 hits (the world's only exceptions come from joints, crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:414-423).
- [physics-3d] (a) crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:578-579 reads FLAT `friction`/`bounce` properties, which Godot's RigidBody3D does not have. The PackedScene loader already flattens a real `physics_material_override` onto the node as `__physics_material__friction`/`__physics_material__bounce`/`rough`/`absorbent` (crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:548-565), and the 2D bridge consumes them (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:958-963), but the 3D bridge never reads a `__physics_material__*` key — grep of physics_server_3d.rs for `physics_material` returns nothing. An authored PhysicsMaterial on a RigidBody3D/StaticBody3D is therefore silently ignored and every 3D body simulates at friction 0.5 / bounce 0.0. (b) `grep -rn "axis_lock_linear" --include='*.rs' crates/*/src` → 0 hits (present only in crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:2876-2881); crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:79 has only an all-or-nothing `lock_rotation`. (c) `center_of_mass` exists in 2D (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:974) but not in 3D — crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:52-108 has no COM field; `inertia` appears only in the inspector schema (inspector_schema_generated.rs:2887) and crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:435 always derives inertia from the shape. (d) linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode are never read by crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::sync_rigid_body (:1066-1067 read the raw values only).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: a RigidBody3D script can override `_integrate_forces(state: PhysicsDirectBodyState3D)`, called once per physics tick from inside the solver; with `custom_integrator = true` the built-in force integration is skipped entirely and the script owns velocity. The state object exposes the tick's contacts (get_contact_count, get_contact_local_normal/position, get_contact_impulse, get_contact_collider_object, get_contact_collider_velocity_at_position), the body's inverse inertia tensor, `set_constant_force`, `integrate_forces()` and `get_space_state()`. Separately, RigidBody3D offers `get_colliding_bodies()`, `get_contact_count()`, `get_inverse_inertia_tensor()`, `set_axis_velocity(Vector3)`, and PhysicsBody3D offers add/remove/get_collision_exceptions.\n\nPATINA: `_integrate_forces` has zero occurrences in the workspace; `custom_integrator` is only a ClassDB property (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1837) and an inspector string, never read by crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::sync_rigid_body (:1049-1118), so a body authored with it still gets built-in gravity. No script arm exists for get_colliding_bodies/get_contact_count/get_inverse_inertia_tensor even though the data is on the body (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:359,:364,:473). `set_axis_velocity` exists but is hard-coded to Vector2 (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9704-9713) writing `_pending_axis_velocity`, consumed only by the 2D server (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:1312). Collision exceptions have no API — the world's `has_collision_exception` (crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:414-423) is fed only by joints.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs add a `dispatch_integrate_forces(&mut self, tree)` pass called from the MainLoop physics tick (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, between :2841 `step` and :2842 `sync_from_physics`) that, for each RigidBody3D whose script defines `_integrate_forces`, publishes the body's contacts/velocities onto the node as `_state_*` properties (the same node-property bridge `_pending_*` already uses at :1059-1063) and invokes the callback; honour `custom_integrator` by skipping `PhysicsBody3D::integrate`'s gravity term (crates/gdphysics3d/src/body.rs:247) for that body; (2) add script arms in crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs for `get_colliding_bodies`, `get_contact_count`, `get_inverse_inertia_tensor`, and make `set_axis_velocity` (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9704) accept Vector3 with a 3D consumer in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs; (3) add `add_collision_exception_with`/`remove_collision_exception_with`/`get_collision_exceptions` writing a node-side exception list the bridge feeds into `PhysicsWorld3D`'s existing exception set.\n\nWIRING: the callback must fire from the fixed physics tick in MainLoop, not from a test harness, and its velocity writes must survive into the next `sync_to_physics`.

**Merged findings (2):** RigidBody3D custom_integrator + _integrate_forces(PhysicsDirectBodyState3D) callback, contact introspection (get_colliding_bodies, get_contact_count, get_inverse_inertia_tensor, set_axis_velocity), and PhysicsBody3D collision exceptions (add/remove/get_collision_exceptions); RigidBody3D authored-property parity: physics_material_override (friction/bounce/rough/absorbent), axis_lock_linear_x/y/z + axis_lock_angular_x/y/z, center_of_mass + center_of_mass_mode, custom inertia tensor, linear_damp_mode/angular_damp_mode (COMBINE vs REPLACE)

**Prove it:** With a .tscn RigidBody3D whose script defines `_integrate_forces(state)` and MainLoop stepped at 60 Hz: (a) the callback runs exactly once per physics tick (a counter incremented in it equals the tick count); (b) with `custom_integrator = true` and the callback setting `state.linear_velocity = Vector3.ZERO`, the body does not fall at all; (c) landing on a StaticBody3D with `contact_monitor = true` and `max_contacts_reported = 4`, `get_contact_count()` returns >= 1 and `get_colliding_bodies()` contains the floor node; (d) `add_collision_exception_with(other)` makes two otherwise-colliding bodies pass through each other. (test: `physics3d_integrate_forces_callback`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_integrate_forces_callback`.
acceptance_criteria: With a .tscn RigidBody3D whose script defines `_integrate_forces(state)` and MainLoop stepped at 60 Hz: (a) the callback runs exactly once per physics tick (a counter incremented in it equals the tick count); (b) with `custom_integrator = true` and the callback setting `state.linear_velocity = Vector3.ZERO`, the body does not fall at all; (c) landing on a StaticBody3D with `contact_monitor = true` and `max_contacts_reported = 4`, `get_contact_count()` returns >= 1 and `get_colliding_bodies()` contains the floor node; (d) `add_collision_exception_with(other)` makes two otherwise-colliding bodies pass through each other.
