## Audit of the remaining scope (MagentaBrook, 2026-08-19 13:00 UTC) — 4 of 5 items are DONE, and there is a new bug

I claimed this to work item (e)'s follow-on finding and found that stale too, so I checked every item on the list before writing any code. Posting the corrected record so the next assignee does not repeat the audit.

| item | recorded as | verified at HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| (a) `xformed_by` | "NOT implemented" | **DONE** — `interpreter.rs:3911`, with the local-vs-screen-space distinction handled |
| (a) `accumulate` | "NOT implemented" | **still absent** (0 hits) — and genuinely blocked, see below |
| (b) `unicode` / `location` / `meta_pressed` | always 0/0/false | **still true** — `scene_tree.rs:6753`, `:6813-6814` |
| (c) `InputMap.load_from_project_settings()` | "still a no-op returning Nil" | **DONE** — `scripting.rs:3912`, and `input_map_load_from_project_settings_resets.rs` covers it |
| (d) ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag/gesture/MIDI delivery "untested" | untested | **DONE** — `touch_and_midi_events_reach_script_input.rs` and `gesture_events_reach_script_input.rs` |
| 🔴 the follow-on finding: "nothing OVERRIDES get_action_strength/get_action_raw_strength" | not done | **DONE** — both overridden at `scripting.rs:3569` and `:3585`, reading the analog/deadzoned pair from the input snapshot with a digital fallback |

### Why `accumulate` is not merely undone but blocked here

`input_event_method` takes `&ResourceRef` and returns a `Variant`; there is no write-back to the caller's place. Godot's `accumulate` **mutates the receiver** and returns whether it merged, so a copy-returning implementation cannot express it. The `xformed_by` arm's own doc comment states the constraint exactly: *"Godot returns a COPY, which is why this one is implementable at all: Patina's events are value Resources, so a method that mutated the receiver could not be seen by the caller."*

So this needs a mutating-method path (the shape the compound member-assignment path uses for `Color`), not just another arm. Recording the semantics here so whoever builds that path does not have to re-derive them from `input_event.cpp:1019-1064`:

- Returns **false** unless both are `InputEventMouseMotion` **and** window_id, canceled, pressed, button_mask, shift, ctrl, alt and meta all match.
- On merge, `position`, `global_position`, `velocity` and `screen_velocity` are **REPLACED** by the incoming event's, while `relative` and `screen_relative` are **SUMMED** (`+=`).
- ⚠️ That asymmetry is the whole correctness question. Summing position, or replacing relative, produces a plausible-looking result and is wrong.

### 🔴 NEW: mouse and gesture events report every modifier as false

`InputEventMouseButton` inherits `InputEventMouse` inherits **`InputEventWithModifiers`** (doc/classes/InputEventMouseButton.xml:2, InputEventMouse.xml:2), so `event.shift_pressed` on a click is real state in Godot. In Patina it is always `false`: `scene_tree.rs:6840` (MouseButton), `:6860` (MouseMotion), `:6950` and `:6959` (the two gestures) all call `modifier_props(false, false, false)`. Only the Key arm at `:6818` passes the real `*shift, *ctrl, *alt`.

**Shift-click and Ctrl-click cannot be implemented by any script** — multi-select, add-to-selection, and the whole class of modifier-qualified clicks. This is a wider gap than item (b)'s `meta_pressed`, which is at least a single missing bit on one class.

It is also fixable without touching the `InputEvent::Key` enum: `InputState::is_key_pressed` already answers Shift/Ctrl/Alt (`gdplatform/src/input.rs:1886`), and `input_event_to_variant` already takes side-channel arguments for exactly this reason — `double_click` and `pen` are both passed in by the frame owner rather than carried on the event (the pattern pat-s3rrv.76 established). A modifier triple is the same shape.

I have **not** made that change: `scene_tree.rs` and `main_loop.rs` are both leased (BronzeLake, to 13:23Z) and they are the two files it needs. Picking it up when the lease lapses unless someone else takes it first.

[audit-key: audio/effect-record-capture] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** `AudioEffectCapture : AudioEffect` taps a bus into a ring buffer a script drains: `can_get_buffer(frames)`, `get_buffer(frames) -> PackedVector2Array`, `clear_buffer()`, `get_frames_available()`, `get_discarded_frames()`, `get_pushed_frames()`, `get_buffer_length_frames()`, property `buffer_length` (default 0.1 s). `AudioEffectRecord : AudioEffect` records a bus to memory: `set_recording_active(bool)`, `is_recording_active()`, `get_recording() -> AudioStreamWAV`, property `format` (AudioStreamWAV.Format enum, default 1 = FORMAT_16_BITS). Sources: `upstream/godot/servers/audio/effects/audio_effect_capture.cpp` and `audio_effect_record.cpp`. Both are in scope on web: Godot's own web export supports them (capture is a pure mixer tap; record encodes in memory).

**Patina today:** neither exists. `rg -n '^pub struct ' engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/effects.rs` lists Amplify/Reverb/EQ/Delay/Distortion/Filter/Compressor/Limiter/HardLimiter/SpectrumAnalyzer only. ClassDB has no entry (`engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7359-7460`) and the bus-layout loader has no arm (`engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/mixer.rs:369-386`).

**Implement:** add both effects to `engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/effects.rs` on the existing `AudioEffect` trait — Capture pushing processed frames into a bounded ring (reuse the SPSC ring already in `engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/web_output.rs` if it fits) and reporting pushed/discarded counts; Record accumulating frames and, on `get_recording()`, encoding via the existing WAV path (`engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs`) into an `AudioStreamWAV` resource. Register both classes with Godot's properties/methods in `engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` and add `effect_from_sub_resource` arms in `mixer.rs`. Expose their instances to script through `AudioServer.get_bus_effect_instance` (see the audio/audioserver-singleton bead) so a script can drive them.

**Wiring requirement:** a script in a running scene must be able to fetch the capture effect instance from the bus, call `get_buffer()` each frame while audio is playing, and receive the frames the mixer actually produced that tick; a Record effect toggled on/off must yield an `AudioStreamWAV` whose sample count matches the recorded duration.

**Prove it:** boot a scene with an AudioStreamPlayer on a bus carrying an AudioEffectCapture, step N frames, and assert the script-drained buffer's frame count and non-silence match the mixed output; then activate an AudioEffectRecord for a known duration, stop it, and assert `get_recording()` returns an AudioStreamWAV with the expected sample count and format.

**Prove it:** AudioEffectCapture and AudioEffectRecord are registered, constructible from a bus layout, and a script can drain captured frames matching the mixer output and retrieve an AudioStreamWAV from a completed recording with the expected sample count (test: `audio_effect_capture_and_record_tap_bus`)
acceptance_criteria: AudioEffectCapture and AudioEffectRecord are registered, constructible from a bus layout, and a script can drain captured frames matching the mixer output and retrieve an AudioStreamWAV from a completed recording with the expected sample count (test: `audio_effect_capture_and_record_tap_bus`)

**Godot classes:** AudioStreamMicrophone, AudioEffectCapture, AudioEffectRecord, AudioServer

**Patina today:**
- [audio] No implementation anywhere: `grep -rn "getUserMedia\|Microphone\|capture_get_device\|input_device" crates/ --include="*.rs"` returns only an Android permission enum (crates/gdplatform/src/android.rs:270,283), an editor settings tooltip string (crates/gdeditor/src/project_settings_dialog.rs:689), and a generated inspector-schema row (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4308). AudioStreamMicrophone, AudioEffectCapture and AudioEffectRecord are all in the sweep's unregistered.txt (lines 11, 28, 33). AudioServer's input half (get_input_device_list/set_input_device/set_input_device_active/get_input_frames_available/get_input_buffer_length_frames/get_input_mix_rate) has no counterpart in crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/effects.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/web_audio.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `AudioStreamMicrophone` plays the capture device through the bus graph; `AudioEffectCapture` lets a script pull raw frames off a bus (`get_buffer`, `get_frames_available`, `can_get_buffer`, `clear_buffer`) and `AudioEffectRecord` records a bus to an `AudioStreamWAV`. `AudioServer` exposes `get_input_device_list`, `get_input_device`, `set_input_device`, `set_input_device_active`, `get_input_frames_available`, `get_input_buffer_length_frames`, `get_input_mix_rate`. Godot's OWN web export implements capture with `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` (platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_audio.js:1303-1320), so this is in scope for a browser port, not a native-only feature.\n\nPATINA: nothing exists. `grep -rn "getUserMedia|Microphone|input_device|capture" crates/ --include="*.rs"` finds only an Android permission enum (crates/gdplatform/src/android.rs:270), an editor settings label (crates/gdeditor/src/project_settings_dialog.rs:689) and a generated inspector-schema row (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4308). All three classes are unregistered in ClassDB, and crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs has no input-side API.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) add an `AudioInputStream` trait mirroring `AudioOutputStream` (crates/gdaudio/src/sample.rs:43) plus a ring-buffered capture source in gdaudio; (2) implement `AudioEffectCapture` and `AudioEffectRecord` as `AudioEffect` impls in crates/gdaudio/src/effects.rs, with Record encoding to a WAV buffer via crates/gdaudio/src/wav.rs `build_wav_bytes`; (3) add the input half of the AudioServer API in crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs and expose it through the AudioServer singleton bead's dispatch; (4) implement the web backend in crates/patina-web/src/web_audio.rs using `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` + a MediaStreamAudioSourceNode feeding an AudioWorklet capture ring, with the permission prompt happening on the same user gesture that unlocks the context; native uses cpal's input stream; (5) make `AudioStreamMicrophone` a stream type the scene bridge can assign to a player (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs).\n\nWIRING: a scene with an `AudioStreamPlayer` whose stream is an `AudioStreamMicrophone`, plus an `AudioEffectCapture` on its bus, lets a script read live input frames each frame.

**Prove it:** With a synthetic input device injected, a scene whose `AudioStreamPlayer.stream` is an `AudioStreamMicrophone` mixes the injected samples into the output, an `AudioEffectCapture` on that bus reports `get_frames_available() > 0` and `get_buffer()` returns those samples, and `AudioEffectRecord` start/stop produces a decodable `AudioStreamWAV`; `AudioServer.get_input_device_list()` returns at least the default device. (test: `audio_microphone_capture_record`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio_microphone_capture_record`.
acceptance_criteria: With a synthetic input device injected, a scene whose `AudioStreamPlayer.stream` is an `AudioStreamMicrophone` mixes the injected samples into the output, an `AudioEffectCapture` on that bus reports `get_frames_available() > 0` and `get_buffer()` returns those samples, and `AudioEffectRecord` start/stop produces a decodable `AudioStreamWAV`; `AudioServer.get_input_device_list()` returns at least the default device. - [audio] `AudioStreamGenerator` (crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs:359-470: push_frame/push_buffer/can_push_buffer/frames_available/clear_buffer/mix) and `PolyphonicPlayer` (decode.rs:472-540) are implemented and unit-tested, but nothing outside gdaudio references them: `grep -rn "AudioStreamGenerator\|PolyphonicPlayer\|get_stream_playback\|push_frame" crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdscene/src` returns ZERO hits — there is no `get_stream_playback()` on a player and no script path to `push_frame`. crates/gdaudio/src/sample_pool.rs is likewise a dead module (its only workspace reference is `pub mod sample_pool;` at crates/gdaudio/src/lib.rs:17). AudioStreamRandomizer/Playlist/Interactive/Synchronized/Polyphonic exist ONLY as rows in a generated inspector table (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4306,4323-4326) and are in unregistered.txt (lines 31-38) — no runtime type, no ClassDB entry.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/sample_pool.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `AudioStreamGenerator` + `get_stream_playback()` is the procedural-audio path (`playback.push_frame(Vector2)` / `push_buffer` / `can_push_buffer` / `get_frames_available`, buffer_length and mix_rate_mode properties). `AudioStreamPolyphonic` + `AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic` (`play_stream`, `stop_stream`, `set_stream_volume/pitch_scale`) is the standard many-one-shots-from-one-node pattern. `AudioStreamRandomizer` (playback_mode, random_pitch, random_volume_offset_db, add_stream/set_stream_probability_weight), `AudioStreamPlaylist` (shuffle/loop/fade_time + up to 64 stream slots), `AudioStreamInteractive` (clips + transitions) and `AudioStreamSynchronized` are the composite stream types.\n\nPATINA: the Generator and a polyphonic voice pool already exist and are tested (crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs:359-470 and :472-540; crates/gdaudio/src/sample_pool.rs) but are UNWIRED — `get_stream_playback` does not exist in the interpreter, `push_frame` has no script binding, and crates/gdaudio/src/sample_pool.rs has exactly one workspace reference (`pub mod sample_pool;` at lib.rs:17). The composite streams do not exist at all: they appear only as rows in crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4306,4323-4326 and are unregistered in ClassDB.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) add `has_stream_playback`/`get_stream_playback` to the interpreter's player-method arms (near crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:9458-9530) returning a handle object whose `push_frame`/`push_buffer`/`get_frames_available`/`can_push_buffer` route into the bridge's `AudioStreamGenerator` for that node; (2) let the bridge treat a `stream` whose class is AudioStreamGenerator/AudioStreamPolyphonic as a live source instead of a file import (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:439-481); (3) implement Randomizer (weighted/sequential pick + random pitch/volume at play time), Playlist (ordered/shuffled with fade_time crossfade) and Synchronized (parallel mix of sub-streams) as stream kinds in gdaudio, resolving their sub-stream lists from the .tscn/.tres sub-resource properties; stage AudioStreamInteractive (clip transition matrix) last; (4) register all of them plus their properties in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.\n\nWIRING: a .tscn with these stream resources plays through the same bridge -> AudioServer -> mix path as a plain file stream, and a script can push generated frames that appear in the very next mix.

**Prove it:** A scene script obtains `$Player.get_stream_playback()` from an `AudioStreamGenerator` stream, pushes a sine block, and the next `MainLoop::step` mixes those exact samples; an `AudioStreamRandomizer` with two sub-streams plays one of them per `play()` with the configured pitch jitter; an `AudioStreamPlaylist` advances to its second entry after the first ends. (test: `audio_meta_streams_playback`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio_meta_streams_playback`.
acceptance_criteria: A scene script obtains `$Player.get_stream_playback()` from an `AudioStreamGenerator` stream, pushes a sine block, and the next `MainLoop::step` mixes those exact samples; an `AudioStreamRandomizer` with two sub-streams plays one of them per `play()` with the configured pitch jitter; an `AudioStreamPlaylist` advances to its second entry after the first ends. [audit-key: audio/stream-container-classes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Wiring requirement:** a `.tscn` whose AudioStreamPlayer stream is an `AudioStreamRandomizer` (or Playlist/Interactive/Synchronized) must play through the normal SceneTree tick, honouring shuffle/weights/transitions; the microphone stream must feed real captured frames into the mixer when the browser grants permission.

**Prove it:** load a scene with an AudioStreamRandomizer wrapping two distinguishable buffers, play it repeatedly with a fixed RNG seed and assert the selection sequence matches the configured playback_mode and weights; do the same for a Playlist (assert clip order + fade_time crossfade) and a Synchronized stream (assert both sub-streams contribute at their configured volumes in one mixed block).

title: Make weakref() return a real WeakRef object and register WeakRef in ClassDB
description:
[audit-key: core/core-object-weakref-object-class] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/register_core_types.cpp:140 `GDREGISTER_CLASS(WeakRef);`; doc/classes/WeakRef.xml — class WeakRef inherits RefCounted with a single method get_ref() -> Variant returning null once the referent is gone; @GlobalScope.weakref() (core/variant/variant_utility.cpp:816, bound at :1748) returns a WeakRef, and holding one must NOT contribute to the referent's reference count

**Godot classes:** WeakRef

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-7] Not in ClassDB: `grep -x WeakRef` against the 4186 string literals extracted from engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs = 0 hits (RefCounted IS registered). Behaviour is implemented — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs defines `WeakRef` over a process-global alive-objects registry — but the GDScript builtin does not construct one: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:6079-6084 implements `weakref` as `Ok(args[0].clone())`, i.e. it returns the referent's ObjectId UNCHANGED, with the comment "A WeakRef is a non-owning handle: return the object id unchanged". `get_ref` is then serviced on the RefCounted handle dispatcher at interpreter.rs:18750. So in Patina `weakref(o) == o` is true and `weakref(o).get_class()` reports the referent's class, where Godot returns a separate WeakRef object; `w is WeakRef` and `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` (interpreter.rs:14922) both fail. WeakRef appears in gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs only as an inspector table row (that file has 0 register_class calls).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** WeakRef is a registered core class (upstream/godot/core/register_core_types.cpp:140 `GDREGISTER_CLASS(WeakRef)`) inheriting RefCounted with exactly one method, `get_ref() -> Variant`, returning null once the referent is freed (doc/classes/WeakRef.xml). `@GlobalScope.weakref(obj)` (core/variant/variant_utility.cpp:816) returns a NEW WeakRef instance that is a different object from its referent and does not bump the referent's reference count. Therefore in Godot: `weakref(o) != o`, `weakref(o) is WeakRef` is true, `weakref(o).get_class() == "WeakRef"`, and `weakref(o).get_ref() == o` while alive.

**Patina today:** the referent is handed back unchanged. engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:6079-6084 implements the `weakref` builtin as `Ok(args[0].clone())`; `get_ref` is answered by the RefCounted handle dispatcher at interpreter.rs:18750 by re-querying gdobject::weak_ref::is_object_alive. The liveness half is right, the identity half is wrong: `weakref(o) == o`, `get_class()` reports the referent's class, and `x is WeakRef` cannot work. WeakRef is also absent from ClassDB (0 hits for the literal in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs), so `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` is false.

**Implement:** (1) register WeakRef in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs with parent RefCounted and the single method `get_ref` (arity 0). (2) mint a distinct tagged handle for weakrefs — follow the existing tagged-handle convention in interpreter.rs (see the XR interface / ScriptBacktrace handle tags around interpreter.rs:17339-17365) so `is_weakref_handle` can route `get_ref`, `get_class`, `is_class` and `free`/validity queries without colliding with another family's tag byte. Store the referent ObjectId beside the handle in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs. (3) change interpreter.rs:6079 to return that handle instead of the referent, and route `get_ref` on it back through gdobject::weak_ref::is_object_alive.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a loaded scene can do `var w = weakref(node)`, get a value that is not the node, ask `w.get_class()` and `w is WeakRef`, read `w.get_ref()` as the node, free the node, and read `w.get_ref()` as null — all from the runner, and `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` answers true.

**Prove it:** a GDScript-level lifecycle test asserting identity, class, liveness and post-free null.

**Prove it:** A GDScript running in a loaded scene where `var w = weakref(obj)` observes: `w != obj`, `w.get_class() == "WeakRef"`, `w is WeakRef` is true, `w.get_ref() == obj` while the object lives, and `w.get_ref() == null` after the object is freed; and `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` is true with `ClassDB.get_parent_class("WeakRef") == "RefCounted"` (test: `weakref_is_its_own_object_class`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript running in a loaded scene where `var w = weakref(obj)` observes: `w != obj`, `w.get_class() == "WeakRef"`, `w is WeakRef` is true, `w.get_ref() == obj` while the object lives, and `w.get_ref() == null` after the object is freed; and `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` is true with `ClassDB.get_parent_class("WeakRef") == "RefCounted"` (test: `weakref_is_its_own_object_class`)

title: RefCounted: release on scope exit in the interpreter and register RefCounted/WeakRef metadata in ClassDB
description:
[audit-key: core-object/refcounted-lifecycle] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/object/ref_counted.h — Ref<T> drops a reference when the binding dies and the object is deleted at zero; extension_api.json .classes[RefCounted].methods (init_ref/reference/unreference/get_reference_count) and .classes[WeakRef]

**Godot classes:** RefCounted, WeakRef, Object

**Patina today:**
- [core-object] /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/refcounted_handle.rs:18-25 states the limitation in its own doc comment: 'It does not free anything on scope exit. Godot drops a reference when a binding goes out of scope; here only an explicit `unreference()` decrements. Automatic release needs ownership tracking inside the interpreter's Environment.' The registry (refcounted_handle.rs:47-127) is correct for explicit calls and correctly unregisters from the alive-objects set on release. Consequence: `func f(): var r = RefCounted.new()` leaks the handle forever and `is_instance_valid` keeps answering true (interpreter.rs:5413-5440 routes refcounted handles to `weak_ref::is_object_alive`). Also `WeakRef` is not a ClassDB class at all — `grep -rn 'ClassRegistration::new("WeakRef")' crates/` returns nothing (the only "WeakRef" string in engine-rs is /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5393) — so `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` is false, and `RefCounted` is registered with no methods (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3354 plus 8 guarded duplicates), so `ClassDB.class_has_method("RefCounted","get_reference_count")` is false. The `weakref()` builtin (interpreter.rs:6079-6085) returns the raw object id rather than a WeakRef object, so `w.get_ref()` only works because the ObjectId method table has a `get_ref` arm (interpreter.rs:9093-9107).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/refcounted_handle.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a `Ref<T>` binding takes a reference on assignment and drops it when the binding dies; at zero the object is deleted and any WeakRef over it reports null (upstream/godot/core/object/ref_counted.h, core/variant/variant.cpp). RefCounted exposes init_ref/reference/unreference/get_reference_count; WeakRef exposes get_ref (extension_api.json).\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/refcounted_handle.rs implements the registry and the explicit half correctly, and its own doc comment at lines 18-25 records the missing half — nothing decrements on scope exit, so `var r = RefCounted.new()` inside a function leaks and `is_instance_valid(r)` (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:5413-5440) stays true for the life of the process. `WeakRef` is absent from ClassDB entirely (`grep -rn 'ClassRegistration::new("WeakRef")' crates/` → 0 hits), and `RefCounted` is registered with zero methods at gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3354, so `ClassDB.class_has_method("RefCounted","get_reference_count")` answers false. `weakref()` (interpreter.rs:6079-6085) hands back the bare object id instead of a WeakRef object.\n\nApproach: in the interpreter's `Environment`, track which locals hold `Variant::ObjectId` values whose tag is REFCOUNTED_HANDLE_TAG (gdobject/src/refcounted_handle.rs:42); on scope pop, call `refcounted_handle::unreference` once per binding that took a reference, and take a reference when a handle is assigned to a new binding or stored in a container. Register `RefCounted` with its four methods and `WeakRef : RefCounted` with `get_ref` in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. Wiring requirement: observable from a script in a .tscn run by the MainLoop — no direct pokes at the registry.\n\nCareful with the shared `weak_ref` alive registry (gdobject/src/weak_ref.rs:34) — release must unregister exactly once.

**Prove it:** A script does `func make(): var r = RefCounted.new(); return weakref(r)` and, after the function returns and the frame completes, `w.get_ref() == null` and `is_instance_valid(w.get_ref()) == false`; assigning the same handle to a second variable that outlives the function keeps it alive until that variable goes out of scope; `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` and `ClassDB.class_has_method("RefCounted","get_reference_count")` are both true. (test: `refcounted_scope_release_and_weakref_class`)
acceptance_criteria: A script does `func make(): var r = RefCounted.new(); return weakref(r)` and, after the function returns and the frame completes, `w.get_ref() == null` and `is_instance_valid(w.get_ref()) == false`; assigning the same handle to a second variable that outlives the function keeps it alive until that variable goes out of scope; `ClassDB.class_exists("WeakRef")` and `ClassDB.class_has_method("RefCounted","get_reference_count")` are both true. (test: `refcounted_scope_release_and_weakref_class`)

title: Math builtins: close the AABB/Basis/Quaternion/Plane/Rect2/Transform2D method gaps and honour euler order
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant-affine-methods] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json AABB 25 methods, Basis 20, Quaternion 19, Plane 11, Rect2 16, Transform2D 21; upstream/godot/core/math/{aabb,basis,quaternion,plane,rect2,transform_2d}.cpp. `Basis::get_euler(EulerOrder order = EULER_ORDER_YXZ)` supports all six orders.

**Godot classes:** AABB, Basis, Quaternion, Plane, Rect2, Transform2D

**Patina today:**
- [core-variant] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs:657-1015 holds the whole affine dispatch. Diffed against extension_api.json: AABB missing get_longest_axis(_index/_size), get_shortest_axis(_index/_size), get_support, has_surface, intersects_plane, intersects_ray, intersects_segment, is_equal_approx, is_finite (13 of 25 absent); Basis missing from_euler, from_scale, looking_at, scaled_local, is_conformal, is_finite, tdotx/tdoty/tdotz; Quaternion missing from_euler, slerpni, spherical_cubic_interpolate(_in_time), exp, log, is_finite; Plane missing intersect_3, is_equal_approx, is_finite; Rect2 missing get_support, is_equal_approx, is_finite; Transform2D missing is_conformal, is_finite, looking_at. `get_euler` at variant_math.rs:834 (`"get_euler" => Ok(Variant::Vector3(b.to_euler()))`) and :889 for Quaternion ignore the `order` argument entirely, so any script using a non-YXZ order gets wrong angles silently.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: extension_api.json binds 25 AABB / 20 Basis / 19 Quaternion / 11 Plane / 16 Rect2 / 21 Transform2D methods; upstream/godot/core/math/{aabb,basis,quaternion,plane,rect2,transform_2d}.cpp are the oracles. `Basis::get_euler` and `Quaternion::get_euler` take an `EulerOrder` (default EULER_ORDER_YXZ) and support all six orders; `Basis::from_euler(euler, order)` is the static inverse.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs:657-1015 implements the affine dispatch and is missing, per class: AABB — get_longest_axis/_index/_size, get_shortest_axis/_index/_size, get_support, has_surface, intersects_plane, intersects_ray, intersects_segment, is_equal_approx, is_finite; Basis — from_euler, from_scale, looking_at, scaled_local, is_conformal, is_finite, tdotx/tdoty/tdotz; Quaternion — from_euler, slerpni, spherical_cubic_interpolate, spherical_cubic_interpolate_in_time, exp, log, is_finite; Plane — intersect_3, is_equal_approx, is_finite; Rect2 — get_support, is_equal_approx, is_finite; Transform2D — is_conformal, is_finite, looking_at. AABB's missing `intersects_ray`/`intersects_segment` block script-side 3D picking. Separately, variant_math.rs:834 (`"get_euler" => Ok(Variant::Vector3(b.to_euler()))`) and :889 discard the order argument, so a script asking for XYZ order silently receives YXZ angles.

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: extend the per-type helpers already in variant_math.rs (`rect2_method` 657, `transform2d_method` 693, `basis_method` 826, `quaternion_method` 872, `aabb_method` 921, `plane_method` 954), adding the underlying math to engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/math3d.rs where it is missing. Add an `EulerOrder` enum (global enum in extension_api.json) and thread the optional argument through get_euler/from_euler/Basis construction, matching basis.cpp's per-order extraction exactly. Add the static constructors (Basis.from_euler/from_scale, Quaternion.from_euler) to `static_member`/the constructor table so `Basis.from_euler(v)` resolves.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: a script on a Node3D in a .tscn must be able to build a rotation with `Basis.from_euler(Vector3(...), EULER_ORDER_XYZ)`, assign it to `transform.basis`, read `basis.get_euler(EULER_ORDER_XYZ)` back, and raycast an AABB — with the node's transform reflecting the result after a frame.

**Prove it:** A scene script that calls Basis.from_euler with a non-default order and reads get_euler back with the same order recovers the input angles; AABB.intersects_ray/intersects_segment/get_longest_axis, Quaternion.from_euler/slerpni/spherical_cubic_interpolate, Plane.intersect_3 and the is_finite/is_equal_approx family all execute and match Godot. (test: `affine_builtin_methods_and_euler_order_from_scene`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene script that calls Basis.from_euler with a non-default order and reads get_euler back with the same order recovers the input angles; AABB.intersects_ray/intersects_segment/get_longest_axis, Quaternion.from_euler/slerpni/spherical_cubic_interpolate, Plane.intersect_3 and the is_finite/is_equal_approx family all execute and match Godot. (test: `affine_builtin_methods_and_euler_order_from_scene`)

title: Viewport2D: wire ruler-drag guides and Frame Selection into the served 2D viewport
description:
[audit-key: editor-ux/editor-2d-guides] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/scene/canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp (drag from ruler creates a guide stored in scene meta `_edit_horizontal_guides_`/`_edit_vertical_guides_`; VIEW_FRAME_SELECTION 'Frame Selection' shortcut F)

**Godot classes:** CanvasItemEditor

**Patina today:**
- [editor-ux] GET and POST /api/viewport/guides are dispatched at editor_server.rs:2265-2266 and the stored guides feed apply_snap (used at editor_server.rs:15302). POST /api/viewport/frame_selection is dispatched at editor_server.rs:2398 and has server-side tests (editor_server.rs:23220, 23265, 23278, 23284). Neither appears in the client: `grep -c 'viewport/guides' editor_ui.rs` = 0 and `grep -c 'frame_selection' editor_ui.rs` = 0. The client only fetches /api/viewport/snap_guides (editor_ui.rs:14150), which returns transient snap feedback lines, not user guides.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/guides.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: dragging from the 2D rulers drops a horizontal/vertical guide that snapping honours and that persists in the scene's editor meta (upstream/godot/editor/scene/canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp, `_edit_horizontal_guides_`/`_edit_vertical_guides_`); guides can be dragged and removed. 'Frame Selection' (F) recentres and zooms the view onto the selection.\n\nPATINA: both are implemented server-side and unreachable. GET/POST /api/viewport/guides are dispatched at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:2265-2266 and the guide list is already consumed by apply_snap (editor_server.rs:15302), and POST /api/viewport/frame_selection is dispatched at editor_server.rs:2398 with four passing server tests (editor_server.rs:23220-23284). Neither string occurs anywhere in EDITOR_HTML — the client draws rulers and origin (editor_ui.rs:14016) and fetches only transient snap feedback from /api/viewport/snap_guides (editor_ui.rs:14150).\n\nAPPROACH: in editor_ui.rs, make the ruler strips drag sources — pointerdown on a ruler creates a provisional guide that follows the cursor and POSTs /api/viewport/guides on release; render guides from GET /api/viewport/guides in the existing overlay canvas draw pass; allow drag-to-move and drag-off-canvas-to-delete. Bind F (and a toolbar/View menu entry) to POST /api/viewport/frame_selection and apply the returned pan/zoom. Persist guides into the scene's editor meta so they survive a save/reload.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a created guide must both draw and change the snap result of a subsequent node drag, and must survive /api/scene/save + /api/scene/load.

**Prove it:** Dragging from the horizontal ruler in the served 2D viewport creates a guide line; dragging a Sprite2D near it snaps to the guide; saving and reloading the scene keeps the guide; pressing F frames the selection. (test: `editor_viewport2d_guides_served`) POSTs a guide, asserts a subsequent /api/viewport/drag snaps to it, asserts the guide round-trips through save/load, and asserts EDITOR_HTML contains "/api/viewport/guides" and "/api/viewport/frame_selection".
acceptance_criteria: Dragging from the horizontal ruler in the served 2D viewport creates a guide line; dragging a Sprite2D near it snaps to the guide; saving and reloading the scene keeps the guide; pressing F frames the selection. (test: `editor_viewport2d_guides_served`) POSTs a guide, asserts a subsequent /api/viewport/drag snaps to it, asserts the guide round-trips through save/load, and asserts EDITOR_HTML contains "/api/viewport/guides" and "/api/viewport/frame_selection".

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Findings for the remaining scope (EmeraldIsland, after delivering View Frame Time)

'View Frame Time' is done and wired to `GET /api/viewport/3d/perf` (its first client consumer). Recording what I verified about the rest so the next attempt does not start from the bead's assumptions.

### The perf payload is only 2/7 real

Counted `.store()` / `.fetch_add()` sites across `crates/`:

| field | producer | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `frames` | `PERF_FRAME_COUNT.fetch_add` x2 (editor_server.rs:1754, :1773) | LIVE |
| `encode_ms` | `PERF_LAST_ENCODE_US.store` (editor_server.rs:1750, around the PNG/BMP encode) | LIVE |
| `raster_ms` | **no `.store()` anywhere in the workspace** | ALWAYS 0.000 |
| `scale` | `PERF_SCALE_X1000.store` only in `api_viewport_3d_perf_set`; loaded only in `api_viewport_3d_perf_get` | INERT KNOB |
| `grid_in_motion`, `tick_ms`, `stream` | not audited | unknown |

The overlay I added deliberately renders only `frames` and `encode_ms`, with a test asserting `raster_ms` and `scale` do NOT appear in the overlay body. Do not "complete" it by adding them — that puts a number on screen that looks measured and never changes.

### Half Resolution cannot be built on `scale` as the bead's approach suggests

`PERF_SCALE_X1000` (default 400 = 0.4) has **no consumer outside its own getter/setter pair**. Setting it changes nothing. So Half Resolution needs a real render-size consumer first; the knob is itself an unwired feature and worth its own bead if you want the perf benchmark honest.

Where I stopped looking: `EditorState::render_width/height` (editor_server.rs:353) has only three readers — :8249/:8254 (the resize endpoint) and :15283 (the RUNTIME/play-mode loop, not the editor 3D render). `idle_render.rs:86` uses `render_width` only inside a change-detection SIGNATURE, not to size a framebuffer. `ViewportCache::update_frame_ex` (editor_server.rs:1738) receives an already-built `FrameBuffer`, so the sizing decision is upstream of it and I did not locate it. That search is the first step for whoever takes Half Resolution.

### Display modes are the real bulk

The wiring requirement — "switching to Wireframe must change the pixels returned by GET /api/viewport" — means a `display_mode` threaded into the raster call in `viewport_3d_render.rs`, not just a flag in state. `api_viewport_3d_view_flag` (editor_server.rs:9175 — note the bead says :8329, stale) 400s on anything outside sun/environment/grid/origin/local_space/snap, so the server needs extending too. Needs a compiler and a pixel test.

### Do not add Gizmos / Audio Listener / cinematic as flags alone

This file's standing rule is that the editor must not advertise what it cannot do. A `gizmos` flag that toggles nothing is the same failure mode as the `scale` knob above.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Investigation + implementation shape (EmeraldIsland — blocked on file leases, nothing landed)

Could not implement: both `editor_ui.rs` and `editor_server.rs` are under BronzeBridge's live exclusive leases (reservations 3915/3916, expiring 02:43:04Z). Recording what I verified so the next attempt does not repeat it.

### Bead claims — all four verified accurate

- `/api/resource/property/set`: 3 hits in `editor_server.rs`, **0** in `editor_ui.rs`
- `/api/property/resource/save_as`: 2 in the server, **0** in the client
- `make_unique` / `quick-load` / `quickLoad`: **0** anywhere in the client
- `subresource_inline.rs`: referenced only by `pub mod subresource_inline;` (lib.rs:144) and its own `#[cfg(test)]` test — a dead module

### Two things the bead does not say, and they change the plan

**1. There is no READ endpoint, so the expander has nothing to render.**
The server can WRITE a sub-property — `api_set_resource_property`, `editor_server.rs:6809`, dispatched at :2373 — but nothing serves the sub-resource's property LIST. The bead's approach offers "extend GET /api/node/<id> **or** add /api/resource/properties" as an either/or; it is actually mandatory, and it is the reason the existing 'Edit' button can call `fetchSelected()` and show nothing new. Wiring only the client would produce an expander with no data source.

**2. The read logic already exists — in the dead module.**
`subresource_inline::expand_subresource(tree, node, property) -> Option<Vec<(String, Variant)>>` returns exactly what an expander needs, sorted by name, `None` when the property is not a Resource. Meanwhile `api_set_resource_property` re-implements the write inline (match on `Variant::Resource`, insert, `EditorCommand::SetProperty`) instead of calling `commit_subresource_property` sitting beside it. So there are two implementations of the same operation, one of them unreachable — which is what "PARTIAL" really means here.

### Suggested shape

1. `POST /api/resource/property/list` in `editor_server.rs`, body `{node_id, resource_property}`. Parse exactly like `api_set_resource_property` does (`parse_json_body` -> `node_id` u64 -> `find_node_by_raw_id`), then call `subresource_inline::expand_subresource`.
2. Map each `(name, value)` through the EXISTING `property_entry(name, "", value, 0, "", false)` helper (`editor_server.rs:3579`). This matters: it emits the same row shape as `GET /api/node/<id>`, so the client can render sub-resource rows through the same `buildPropertyRow` path instead of a parallel renderer — which is what the wiring requirement is really asking for.
3. Client: replace the text-only Resource branch (`editor_ui.rs:5783-5806`) with a slot button + dropdown (New / Load / Quick Load / Make Unique / Save As / Clear) and an expander that fetches the list above and renders rows, each POSTing the existing `/api/resource/property/set`.
4. While in there, consider deleting the duplicate inline write in `api_set_resource_property` in favour of `commit_subresource_property`, so the module stops being dead in both directions.

### Verification notes for a no-cargo lane

`editor_ui.rs` holds ~636KB of JavaScript inside `EDITOR_HTML`; `rustfmt --check` proves only that the RUST parses. Extract the `<script>` block and run `node --check` on it, and run the same check against HEAD to confirm the check discriminates rather than passing vacuously.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Correction to my own suggestion #4 (EmeraldIsland) — do NOT de-duplicate the write

Still blocked on the leases; used the cycle to check whether the dead module and the live server code actually agree. **They do not**, and my earlier step 4 ("consider deleting the duplicate inline write in `api_set_resource_property` in favour of `commit_subresource_property`") would be a regression. Ignore it.

### The two write paths are not equivalent

`subresource_inline::commit_subresource_property` (dead):
- `get_node_mut` -> mutate -> `set_property`, returns bool
- **no undo command, no redo clear, no `scene_modified`, no log entry**

`api_set_resource_property` (live, `editor_server.rs:6809`):
- builds `EditorCommand::SetProperty`, `cmd.execute(&mut state.scene_tree)`
- `undo_stack.push(cmd)`, `redo_stack.clear()`, `scene_modified = true`, `add_log(...)`

Swapping the live path for the module's would silently drop undo/redo and the unsaved-changes indicator for every sub-resource edit — a loss with no error anywhere. The duplication is real, but the live copy is the one carrying the editor semantics; the dead one is a bare mutator.

If de-duplication is wanted, it has to go the other way: `commit_subresource_property` would need to take the command/undo path, and at that point it is no longer a `SceneTree`-only helper.

### One thing I checked and it is NOT a bug

`api_set_resource_property` constructs `EditorCommand::SetProperty { .., old_value: Variant::Nil }`, which looks like it would make undo restore Nil. It does not: `execute()` overwrites the field with the real previous value (`*old_value = node.set_property(...)`, `lib.rs:757`) before the command is pushed, and `undo()` reads that. Undo of a sub-resource edit is correct. Flagging it because the construction site reads alarmingly and is worth not re-investigating.

### Net effect on the plan

Steps 1-3 of my earlier comment stand (add the read endpoint using `expand_subresource`, map through `property_entry`, then the client expander). Step 4 is withdrawn — `expand_subresource` is still the right thing to reuse for the READ side, but the WRITE side should stay exactly as it is.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## ⚠️ CORRECTION 2 (EmeraldIsland) — do NOT build the read endpoint on `expand_subresource`

Still blocked on the leases, so still no code. But I found something that invalidates steps 1-2 of my own earlier plan. Read this before implementing.

### An inline resource has TWO representations, and the dead module handles the rare one

`editor_server.rs:7524-7532` documents it directly, in `api_save_resource_property_as`:

> (a) `Variant::Resource(ResourceRef)` — a resource loaded from a file and then edited in place by `api_set_resource_property`.
> (b) `SubResource("id")` on the property, `__resref__<prop>` = `Class::id`, and the body flattened into `<prefix><key>` companions — which is exactly what `api_new_resource_property` ("New <Type>") writes and what `.tscn` loading produces. **This is the COMMON case: every resource the picker creates lands here, never in (a).**

`subresource_inline::expand_subresource` matches **only** `Variant::Resource` and returns `None` for everything else. So on the common case — a resource created by the picker, or any resource loaded from a `.tscn` — it returns `None`, i.e. "not expandable".

That is almost certainly why the module has been dead: it was written against representation (a) alone. Building the new read endpoint on it would ship an expander that reports "not a Resource" for exactly the sub-resources the inspector exists to edit, and it would pass a unit test written the same way (its own test constructs a `ResourceRef` directly — representation (a)).

Corroborating detail on the client side: the existing 'Edit' affordance is gated on `v.indexOf('SubResource') >= 0` (`editor_ui.rs:5995`) — a **string** check — and parses the id out with `/SubResource\(\s*"?(\d+)"?\s*\)/` at :6004. The client already knows it is looking at representation (b).

### What to use instead

`api_save_resource_property_as` (`editor_server.rs:7471`) already resolves BOTH representations into a single `(class_name, res_props)` pair — matching `Variant::Resource` first, then falling back to `__resref__<prop>` plus `inline_resource_companion_prefix(&property)` to gather the flattened `<prefix><key>` companions. That resolution is the piece the read endpoint needs; lifting it into a shared helper and calling it from both places is the right shape.

### Revised plan

1. Extract the dual-representation resolver out of `api_save_resource_property_as` into a helper (both files are leased, so this has to wait).
2. `POST /api/resource/property/list` calls that helper, maps each pair through `property_entry(name, "", value, 0, "", false)` (`editor_server.rs:3579`) so rows match `GET /api/node/<id>`.
3. Client expander renders those rows; each row POSTs the existing `/api/resource/property/set`.
4. WITHDRAWN (see my previous comment): do not replace the live write with `commit_subresource_property` — it has no undo/redo/`scene_modified`/logging.
5. `subresource_inline.rs` should probably be deleted rather than revived, unless it is first taught representation (b). As written it is not a shortcut; it is a trap.

### Test warning

Any test for this MUST build its fixture the way `.tscn` loading and the picker do — `SubResource("id")` + `__resref__<prop>` + flattened companions — not by constructing a `ResourceRef`. A fixture built the second way passes against code that cannot handle real scenes, which is exactly how the dead module got a green test.

The matching live-property endpoint exists server-side, GET /api/runtime/node (editor_server.rs:2481 -> api_runtime_node, editor_server.rs:13364-13396, reading state.run_main_loop.tree()), but EDITOR_HTML never calls it: selecting a node while the game runs shows the EDIT tree's stored values from /api/selected, which is wrong for anything a script changed at runtime. There is also no write path — no route sets a property on run_main_loop, so Godot's live edit is absent.\n\nAPPROACH: in editor_ui.rs, when runtimeRunning is true, have fetchSelected() call GET /api/runtime/node?path=<remote node path> and render those properties (marked live/read-through). Add POST /api/runtime/property/set in editor_server.rs that resolves the path in run_main_loop.tree() and applies the Variant on the running tree (no undo entry, matching Godot), and route inspector edits there while running. (3) In the SubViewportContainer input path in gdscene, gate forwarding on `_propagate_input_event(event)` when defined. (4) Declare all of them in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.\n\nWIRING: .tscn -> scripted TextEdit/CodeEdit/GraphEdit/SubViewportContainer -> MainLoop GUI input / draw pass -> the virtuals -> observable text buffer, connection polyline or forwarded-event state.

(test: `advanced_control_virtual_hooks`)

comments.text:
## Scope audit (EmeraldIsland) — merged finding 3 is ALREADY DONE; 1 and 2 remain

Verified every claim in this bead before implementing. **One of the three merged findings is complete** and should not be re-done. The other two are real and both need a compiling lane.

### Merged finding 3 — "shallow tables" — RESOLVED

The bead's per-class counts are stale. Actual registration depth right now:

| class | bead claim | actual |
|---|---|---|
| TextEdit | 3/47 props, 1/7 signals | **48 props, 7 signals, 5 methods** |
| CodeEdit | "registers nothing" | **24 props, 5 signals** |
| RichTextLabel | "registers nothing" | **32 props, 4 signals, 5 methods** |
| GraphEdit | 4/25 props, 0/19 signals | **25 props, 19 signals** |
| ItemList | 3/18 | **21 props, 5 signals** |
| TabBar | 3/14 | **16 props, 8 signals** |
| TabContainer | 2/12 | **12 props, 7 signals** |
| PopupMenu | 3/10 | **12 props, 4 signals** |
| ColorPicker | 4/12 | **12 props, 3 signals** |
| Label3D | 15/33 | **33 props** |
| VideoStreamPlayer | 4/12 | 8 props, 1 signal (still partial) |

LineEdit likewise: the bead says 7 of 36, it now registers all 36.

That also retires the bead's load-bearing consequence — CodeEdit carries 5 signals, so `class_has_signal("CodeEdit", "breakpoint_toggled")` and `code_completion_requested` no longer answer false, and `script_completion.rs` enumerates a real table.

Only `VideoStreamPlayer` (8 of 12) is arguably still shallow.

### Merged finding 1 — the 16 virtuals — REAL, 15 of 16 still absent

Grepped each as an exact quoted literal over `crates/`:

- 15 of 16 return **0 hits tree-wide**, exactly as the bead says.
- `_structured_text_parser` is the exception: it is now DECLARED (`class_db.rs:16448`, arity 2) and pinned by `gdobject/tests/node_and_control_declare_their_virtuals.rs:205`. Declared only — no dispatch.

### Merged finding 2 — the editing surface — REAL

Over `crates/gdscene/src/`: `add_caret` 0, `get_caret_count` 0, `code_completion` 0, `breakpoint` 0, `bookmark` 0, `fold_line` 0. `gutter` and `minimap` have 3 hits each, which are GraphEdit's `minimap_*`, not TextEdit gutters. `line_edit.rs` still drives LineEdit/TextEdit/CodeEdit through one single-caret state machine.

### Why I did not do the ClassDB half of finding 1

Declaring the remaining 15 virtuals without dispatching them would break this file's standing rule that ClassDB must not advertise what the engine cannot run. A virtual is an override POINT: registering `_handle_unicode_input` tells a script "override this and we will call it", and nothing would. That is the same failure I documented on pat-s3rrv.150 for the inert `scale` knob, and `_structured_text_parser` above is already an instance of it — declared, never dispatched.

**Dispatch first, declaration second.** The declaration is a two-line change once the seam exists; doing it first produces a silent lie.

### Why the dispatch is not a no-cargo slice

The three acceptance clauses all need a script call inside code that currently holds an immutable borrow:

- `_propagate_input_event`: the SubViewportContainer forwarding lives in `control.rs:799`, inside `hit_test_control(tree: &SceneTree, ...)`. Calling a script virtual needs `&mut SceneTree`, which ripples through the whole hit-testing chain.
- `_get_connection_line` / hotzones / `_draw_port`: `graph_edit.rs` is a pure data model — `GraphElement`/`GraphNode`/slots, no signal emission, no scene-tree integration. There is no draw pass in it to intercept.
- The TextEdit virtuals: `line_edit.rs`'s editing loop would need a script check before each default operation.

All three want a compiler and a scripted-scene test.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Blocked on a lease — but the hard part is already built (EmeraldIsland)

`editor_server.rs` is under BronzeBridge's exclusive lease, and it is the only viable dispatch site. Nothing landed. Recording two findings that should make this much smaller than it looks.

### 1. The generic plugin-virtual dispatcher ALREADY EXISTS

`editor_server.rs:5071-5090` takes `state.active_plugins`, and for each `(folder, instance)`:

- skips it unless `instance.has_method(method)`,
- calls `instance.call_method(method, args)`,
- treats a truthy return as a "claim" (with `stop_at_first_claim`),
- routes errors into the editor log as `Plugin '<folder>' <method> failed`.

That is exactly the shape `_can_handle` / `_handles` / `_has_gizmo` need. `editor_server.rs` already drives `_handles` (:5005), `_edit` (:5017), `_make_visible` (:5026), `_build` (:5143) and `_get_state` (:5190) through this machinery.

So the remaining work for the editor virtuals is **not** building dispatch — it is calling the existing dispatcher from the right points. That is a much smaller job than the bead implies.

`state.active_plugins: HashMap<String, GDScriptNodeInstance>` is a `pub` field (`editor_server.rs:547`), so the loop is reachable from other modules if the helper is ever made `pub(crate)`.

### 2. The other listed files cannot host the dispatch

- `inspector.rs` (4544 lines) contains **zero** references to `EditorState`. It is a standalone data model — `PropertyEntry`, `InspectorPanel`, `CustomPropertyEditor` — not the live serving path. The rows the editor actually serves are built by `property_entry` in `editor_server.rs:3579`.
- `viewport_3d.rs` (4307 lines) likewise has zero `EditorState` references; it holds `Viewport3D` camera/gizmo-drag state, and is owned by `editor_server.rs` as `state.editor_viewport_3d`.

Both are free of leases, and neither can reach `active_plugins`. The dispatch has to go in `editor_server.rs`.

### 3. ⚠️ Do NOT register the 30 absent extension classes as the other half

`TextServerExtension` (241 virtuals), `PhysicsServer3DExtension` (194), `PhysicsServer2DExtension` (138) and the rest carry 900+ virtual pairs between them. A virtual is an override POINT: declaring one tells a script "override this and we will call it". Registering 900 of them, with nothing dispatching any, is this codebase's documented failure mode at 30x scale — the same reason I declined the 15 TextEdit/GraphEdit virtuals on pat-s3rrv.155 and only declared `_propagate_input_event` after landing its dispatch.

Dispatch first, declaration second. For these extension classes that means: do not touch them until something actually calls into them.

### Verified

Sampled 7 of the bead's virtuals (`_has_gizmo`, `_create_gizmo`, `_redraw`, `_import`, `_generate`, `_can_handle`, `_parse_property`) as quoted literals across `crates/`, excluding `class_db.rs`, `editor_plugin_classes.rs` and tests: **0 hits each**. The bead's core claim is accurate — they are registration rows only.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Addendum: on EditorPlugin, declaration already EXCEEDS dispatch by 8

Checked whether there was any honest declaration work available in the unleased files (the reverse of the bead's ask: virtuals that ARE dispatched but not declared). There is none — the gap runs the other way.

`editor_server.rs` dispatches 14 EditorPlugin virtuals:
`_apply_changes`, `_build`, `_clear`, `_edit`, `_forward_canvas_gui_input`, `_get_plugin_name`, `_get_state`, `_handles`, `_has_main_screen`, `_make_visible`, `_process`, `_ready`, `_save_external_data`, `_set_state`.

`class_db.rs` declares 22, i.e. all of the above plus **8 that nothing calls**:
`_disable_plugin`, `_enable_plugin`, `_forward_canvas_draw_over_viewport`, `_forward_canvas_force_draw_over_viewport`, `_get_breakpoints`, `_get_plugin_icon`, `_get_unsaved_status`, `_get_window_layout`, `_run_scene`, `_set_window_layout`.

(That list is 10 names for 8 slots because `_process`/`_ready` are dispatched but inherited from Node rather than declared on EditorPlugin — the arithmetic is 22 declared vs 12 declared-and-dispatched.)

So on the one class where both halves exist, ClassDB is already ahead of the engine. Adding the 900+ virtuals of the 30 absent extension classes would widen an inversion that is already there, and `class_has_method` would keep getting further from the truth.

Concrete suggestion for whoever unblocks this: before adding any declaration, close some of those 8 — each is a call to the existing dispatcher (`editor_server.rs:5071`) from the right point, and each turns an existing lie into a working override.

title: Resources: honour `resource_local_to_scene` and call `_setup_local_to_scene` at instantiation
description:
[audit-key: engine-virtual-method-table/virtual-resource-core] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json Resource._setup_local_to_scene(), _get_rid()->RID, _reset_state(), _set_path_cache(String); upstream/godot/core/io/resource.cpp Resource::setup_local_to_scene, scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp which calls it for every resource with resource_local_to_scene set during instantiation.

**Godot classes:** Resource, PackedScene, ViewportTexture, ShaderMaterial

**Patina today:**
- [engine-virtual-method-table] `rg -F '"_setup_local_to_scene"' / '"_get_rid"' / '"_reset_state"' / '"_set_path_cache"' engine-rs/crates/` each return 0 hits tree-wide. The enabling flag has no implementation either: `rg -F 'local_to_scene' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**' -g '!**/inspector_schema_generated.rs'` returns only occurrences inside serialized .tscn INPUT strings (patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:474, gdplatform/src/input.rs:2355/4304-4429, gdresource/src/project.rs:584) — the parser sees `resource_local_to_scene` as a key inside an InputEventKey literal and nothing acts on it. PackedScene instancing (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs) never duplicates a resource per instance.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: a Resource with `resource_local_to_scene = true` is DUPLICATED for every scene instance rather than shared, and immediately after the copy the engine calls its `_setup_local_to_scene()` virtual so the copy can bind to its owning scene (scene/resources/packed_scene.cpp calls it during instantiation; core/io/resource.cpp Resource::setup_local_to_scene). This is how a ViewportTexture finds its SubViewport and how per-instance ShaderMaterials get unique parameter state. Resource also exposes `_get_rid()` and `_reset_state()`.\n\nPATINA: none of the four virtuals exists — `rg -F '\"_setup_local_to_scene\"'`, `'\"_get_rid\"'`, `'\"_reset_state\"'`, `'\"_set_path_cache\"'` over engine-rs/crates/ each return 0 hits tree-wide. Worse, the flag itself is unimplemented: `rg -F 'local_to_scene' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**' -g '!**/inspector_schema_generated.rs'` returns only matches inside serialized .tscn text used as test INPUT (patina-runner/src/project_boot.rs:474, gdplatform/src/input.rs:2355, gdresource/src/project.rs:584). engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs shares one resource across all instances of a scene.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) Parse and retain `resource_local_to_scene` on sub- and ext-resources in engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs so the flag survives to instancing. (2) In engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs, when instantiating a PackedScene, deep-copy every resource whose flag is set (per instance, not per scene) before assigning it to node properties. (3) Immediately after the copy, if the resource carries a script defining `_setup_local_to_scene`, dispatch it through the script instance with the owning node reachable. (4) Register the four virtuals on Resource in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.\n\nWIRING: .tscn with two instances of a sub-scene carrying a local-to-scene resource -> loader -> PackedScene instancing -> two DISTINCT resource copies, each having had `_setup_local_to_scene` called once.

**Prove it:** A .tscn instancing the same sub-scene twice, where the sub-scene holds a scripted Resource with `resource_local_to_scene = true` and `func _setup_local_to_scene(): stamp = get_instance_id()`, ends with the two instances holding resources with DIFFERENT stamps (proving both the duplicate and the callback), while the same setup with the flag false leaves both instances sharing one resource with a single stamp. (test: `resource_local_to_scene_setup_virtual`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn instancing the same sub-scene twice, where the sub-scene holds a scripted Resource with `resource_local_to_scene = true` and `func _setup_local_to_scene(): stamp = get_instance_id()`, ends with the two instances holding resources with DIFFERENT stamps (proving both the duplicate and the callback), while the same setup with the flag false leaves both instances sharing one resource with a single stamp. (test: `resource_local_to_scene_setup_virtual`)

title: Animation: dispatch custom AnimationNode, SkeletonModifier3D and RichTextEffect virtuals from the scene tick

- [engine-virtual-method-table] SkeletonModifier3D's four virtuals are declared at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1742-1745 with an in-source comment at :1739-1741 conceding `_process_modification` "is the pose-update hook itself — the seam the constraint/twist solvers will run from once they exist"; grepping each name over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) returns class_db.rs ONLY. `_process_animation_node` likewise hits only class_db.rs:2617; `_process_custom_fx` only class_db.rs:7086. AnimationNode's 8 virtuals and AnimationMixer._post_process_key_value and CompositorEffect._render_callback have zero declarations and zero references (`rg -F '\"_get_child_nodes\"'`, `'\"_get_parameter_list\"'`, `'\"_get_caption\"'`, `'\"_has_filter\"'` = 0 files each).\n\nAPPROACH: (1) In engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs, when resolving a blend-graph node whose resource carries a script, call `_get_parameter_list` at graph build time to publish its `parameters/...` properties and `_process(time, seek, is_external_seek, test_only)` / `_process_animation_node` each tick, feeding the returned remaining-time back into the graph. (2) In engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs, run the SkeletonModifier3D stack after pose evaluation and before skinning: for each scripted modifier call `_process_modification_with_delta(delta)` (falling back to `_process_modification`) with the skeleton reachable, and `_skeleton_changed`/`_validate_bone_names` on rebinding. (3) In engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/char_fx.rs, resolve `[custom]` BBCode spans to a scripted RichTextEffect and call `_process_custom_fx(char_fx)` per glyph per frame, applying the mutated offset/color/visible. (4) Call `AnimationMixer._post_process_key_value` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs before each track value is written.\n\nWIRING: .tscn -> AnimationTree / Skeleton3D / RichTextLabel -> MainLoop tick -> the virtuals -> node property, bone pose or glyph transform that differs from the unmodified value.

**Prove it:** A .tscn Skeleton3D with a scripted SkeletonModifier3D child whose `_process_modification_with_delta(delta)` rotates bone 0 by delta leaves bone 0's global pose rotated by exactly one frame's delta after one MainLoop step, and by zero when `active = false`; a RichTextLabel with `[custom]text[/custom]` and a scripted RichTextEffect setting `char_fx.offset.y = 5` renders those glyphs offset by 5px; an AnimationTree containing a scripted AnimationNode has that node's `_process` called once per tick and its declared parameters visible as `parameters/...` properties.
