title: Audio: script-defined AudioStream/AudioStreamPlayback — dispatch `_instantiate_playback` and pull frames through `_mix`
description:
[audit-key: engine-virtual-method-table/virtual-resource-ext-audio] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json AudioStream (10: _instantiate_playback, _get_stream_name, _get_length, _is_monophonic, _get_bpm, _get_beat_count, _get_tags, _get_parameter_list, _has_loop, _get_bar_beats), AudioStreamPlayback (10: _start, _stop, _is_playing, _get_loop_count, _get_playback_position, _seek, _mix, _tag_used_streams, _set_parameter, _get_parameter), AudioStreamPlaybackResampled (2), AudioEffect._instantiate, AudioEffectInstance (_process, _process_silence); upstream/godot/servers/audio/audio_stream.h.

**Godot classes:** AudioStream, AudioStreamPlayback, AudioStreamPlaybackResampled, AudioEffect, AudioEffectInstance

**Patina today:**
- [engine-virtual-method-table] AudioStream IS registered (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10191) but only with the NON-virtual getters `get_length`/`is_monophonic`/`instantiate_playback` — the underscore-prefixed virtuals are absent from the registration and from the codebase: `rg -F '"_instantiate_playback"' / '"_mix"' / '"_get_stream_name"' / '"_get_playback_position"' / '"_start"' / '"_stop"' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**'` returns 0 files for every one. Per-class tally from the api dump vs Patina's ClassDB: AudioStream 0/10 declared, AudioStreamPlayback 0/10, AudioEffect 0/1, AudioEffectInstance 0/2, AudioStreamPlaybackResampled 0/2. There is no mixer callback anywhere in engine-rs/crates/gdaudio that would pull PCM frames from a script.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `extends AudioStream` + `_instantiate_playback()` returning an `extends AudioStreamPlayback` whose `_mix(dst, rate_scale, frames)` fills the buffer is the supported way to synthesize or procedurally stream audio; the mixer also calls `_start(from_pos)`, `_stop()`, `_is_playing()`, `_seek(pos)`, `_get_playback_position()`, `_get_loop_count()`. `AudioEffect._instantiate()` returning an `AudioEffectInstance` whose `_process(src, dst, count)` runs per bus block is the custom-DSP twin. Ref: upstream/godot/servers/audio/audio_stream.h.\n\nPATINA: AudioStream is registered at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10191 with only the non-virtual getters (`get_length`, `is_monophonic`, `instantiate_playback`); none of the 10 AudioStream virtuals, 10 AudioStreamPlayback virtuals, 2 AudioStreamPlaybackResampled, 1 AudioEffect or 2 AudioEffectInstance virtuals is declared, and none appears in source: `rg -F '\"_instantiate_playback\"'`, `'\"_mix\"'`, `'\"_start\"'`, `'\"_stop\"'`, `'\"_get_playback_position\"'` over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) return 0 files each. The mixer in engine-rs/crates/gdaudio has no script-callback path, so a scripted stream is completely silent.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) Register the AudioStream / AudioStreamPlayback / AudioEffect / AudioEffectInstance virtual sets in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs. (2) Add a script-backed stream source in engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs: when an AudioStreamPlayer's `stream` is a script-carrying object, call `_instantiate_playback()` once at play time and hold the returned playback object. (3) On each mixer block, call `_mix` on it with the frame count and copy the returned PackedVector2Array into the bus buffer; route `_start`/`_stop`/`_seek`/`_is_playing`/`_get_playback_position` from the player's play/stop/seek/position API. (4) Do the same for `AudioEffect._instantiate` -> `AudioEffectInstance._process` in the per-bus effect chain. (5) Bridge through engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs so the calls happen with scene access installed.\n\nWIRING: .tscn AudioStreamPlayer whose stream is a scripted AudioStream -> MainLoop audio tick -> `_instantiate_playback` -> per-block `_mix` -> non-silent samples in the bus output buffer the runner's sink receives.

**Prove it:** A .tscn AudioStreamPlayer whose stream is a scripted AudioStream returning a playback that fills `_mix` with a constant 0.5 amplitude produces a bus output buffer whose frames are all 0.5 after stepping MainLoop, with `_instantiate_playback` called exactly once and `_mix` called once per block; calling stop() makes `_stop` fire and subsequent blocks silent. (test: `script_audio_stream_playback_mix_virtuals`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn AudioStreamPlayer whose stream is a scripted AudioStream returning a playback that fills `_mix` with a constant 0.5 amplitude produces a bus output buffer whose frames are all 0.5 after stepping MainLoop, with `_instantiate_playback` called exactly once and `_mix` called once per block; calling stop() makes `_stop` fire and subsequent blocks silent. (test: `script_audio_stream_playback_mix_virtuals`)

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## ⚠️ The central approach is not achievable from GDScript (EmeraldIsland)

The bead's title asks to "pull frames through `_mix`". **`_mix` cannot be implemented by a GDScript**, in Godot or here, and matching Godot means never exposing it to one.

### Three of these virtuals take raw pointers

From the doc XML:

| virtual | pointer parameters |
|---|---|
| `AudioStreamPlayback._mix` | `buffer: AudioFrame*` |
| `AudioEffectInstance._process` | `src_buffer: const void*`, `dst_buffer: AudioFrame*` |
| `AudioStreamPlaybackResampled._mix_resampled` | `dst_buffer: AudioFrame*` |

GDScript has no pointer type, so these are **GDExtension-only** virtuals. A `.gd` script cannot override them, and Godot does not let it. Building a GDScript `_mix` bridge would be inventing an API Godot does not have — and it would then need a signature of our own devising, which is exactly the kind of divergence this audit exists to find.

The remaining virtuals ARE plain-typed and script-implementable: all 10 on `AudioStream` (`_instantiate_playback`, `_get_stream_name`, `_get_length`, `_is_monophonic`, `_get_bpm`, `_get_beat_count`, `_get_tags`, `_get_parameter_list`, `_has_loop`, `_get_bar_beats`), `AudioEffect._instantiate`, `AudioEffectInstance._process_silence`, `AudioStreamPlaybackResampled._get_stream_sampling_rate`, and on `AudioStreamPlayback` everything except `_mix` (`_start`, `_stop`, `_is_playing`, `_get_playback_position`, `_seek`, `_get_loop_count`, `_tag_used_streams`, `_set_parameter`, `_get_parameter`).

### Why `_instantiate_playback` alone would be dormant

It returns an `AudioStreamPlayback` that the mixer then pulls frames from. With no frame-pull path, dispatching it hands a script a callback that produces an object nothing ever asks for — the "declared but nothing calls it" failure this bead's family is about, one level down.

So the useful ordering is: build the frame path FIRST (see below), then `_instantiate_playback` has somewhere to deliver to.

### Where the frame path has to live

`gdaudio`'s dependencies are `gdcore` and `gdobject` only — it has no access to scripts, so the mixer cannot call into one. The pull must happen in the script-aware bridge:

`AudioServerBridge::process(&mut self, tree: &mut SceneTree, delta)` — `gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:307` — already holds `&mut SceneTree` and does the per-frame mix at `:349-353` (`mix_and_write(...)` or `self.server.mix(frames)`), with `player_ids` in scope and `publish_playback_position` running right after at `:359`.

That is the seam. A script-backed stream would need the bridge to gather its frames before/alongside `server.mix` and feed them in as that player's source, which needs an "externally supplied frames" entry on the server.

Since `_mix` is off the table for GDScript, the honest shape is a Patina-side pull the bridge performs itself, NOT a Godot virtual — and it should be named so nobody mistakes it for one.

### Verified

`AudioStream` is registered (`class_db.rs:10191`) with the non-virtual getters only; the underscore virtuals are absent from ClassDB and from the codebase, as the bead says. Declaring any of them before the frame path exists would repeat the pattern — see my notes on pat-s3rrv.155/.156, and pat-s3rrv.158 where dispatch landed first and no new declaration was needed.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## The capability this bead wants is reachable — by PUSH, not by `_mix` (EmeraldIsland)

Follow-up to my previous comment. The bead conflates two different Godot features, and the one a GDScript can actually use is already 90% built here.

### Godot has TWO script-audio paths, and only one is open to GDScript

**Pull (`_mix`) — GDExtension only.** Implementing a custom `AudioStream`/`AudioStreamPlayback` and having the mixer pull frames from it. `_mix(buffer: AudioFrame*, ...)` is pointer-typed, so no `.gd` script can do this. That is what this bead's acceptance asks for.

**Push (`AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback`) — the GDScript path.** Every method is plain-typed:

| method | params | pointers |
|---|---|---|
| `push_frame` | `Vector2` | none |
| `push_buffer` | `PackedVector2Array` | none |
| `can_push_buffer` | `int` | none |
| `get_frames_available` | — | none |
| `clear_buffer` | — | none |
| `get_skips` | — | none |

This is how a GDScript actually generates audio in Godot: `AudioStreamGenerator` on the player, `get_stream_playback()` for the playback object, then `push_buffer()` each frame.

### Patina already implements the push side

`gdaudio/src/decode.rs` has `push_frame` (:381), `frames_available` (:404), `can_push_buffer` (:409) and `push_buffer` (:418) — the matching set, unit-tested. What is missing is the wiring: `get_stream_playback()` has no interpreter arm and the bridge does not treat an `AudioStreamGenerator` stream as a live source. That is pat-s3rrv.143's remaining scope, and I registered the ClassDB half of it earlier.

### Suggested re-scope

1. **Drop `_mix` / `_process` / `_mix_resampled` from this bead** — they are GDExtension-only and cannot be dispatched to a script at all. If Patina ever wants custom stream types from Rust, that is a different feature with a different name.
2. **Keep the 22 plain-typed virtuals**, but note that `_instantiate_playback` and friends only become non-dormant once something pulls from the playback they return — so they follow the frame path, not precede it.
3. **Point the "script-defined audio" capability at pat-s3rrv.143 instead**, where the mechanism is Godot-correct, GDScript-reachable, and the DSP already exists.

The seam for (3) is the same one I identified for the pull: `AudioServerBridge::process` (`gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:307`), which holds `&mut SceneTree` and mixes at `:349-353`. `gdaudio` depends only on `gdcore`/`gdobject`, so the script side must live in the bridge either way.

comments.author: EmeraldIsland
comments.text:
## Correction: pat-s3rrv.143 is CLOSED — the push wiring is now homeless

My previous comment said to "point the script-defined audio capability at pat-s3rrv.143 instead". **That bead is closed.** I checked after writing it. Following that advice would send the work nowhere, so ignore that line — the rest of the analysis stands.

### What this changes

`AudioStreamGenerator` + `AudioStreamGeneratorPlayback.push_buffer()` is Godot's only GDScript-reachable path for script-supplied audio (all plain-typed; `_mix` is pointer-typed and GDExtension-only). Patina implements the DSP already — `gdaudio/src/decode.rs`: `push_frame` :381, `frames_available` :404, `can_push_buffer` :409, `push_buffer` :418, unit-tested — and none of it is reachable from a script.

With .143 closed, **this bead is the only open home for that capability**, and its own `Files:` list already names the two places the wiring belongs: `gdaudio/src/server.rs` and `gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs`.

### Why I still did not implement it

Two things, both concrete:

1. **The script-facing half is lease-blocked.** `get_stream_playback()` needs an interpreter arm, and `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` is under another agent's exclusive lease. Without it, a bridge-side generator source has no way to be filled from a script — the frames would only ever come from Rust.

2. **The stream-representation question is unresolved.** A `[sub_resource type="AudioStreamGenerator"]` stream does not arrive as a path string. The bridge currently resolves `stream` via `__extres__stream` then a plain path (`audio_server_bridge.rs:656-663`), and an inline sub-resource takes the `SubResource("id")` + `__resref__stream` form instead — the same two-representation split that made `subresource_inline` dead code on pat-s3rrv.152. Guessing which form to match, with no compiler, is how that module ended up handling the rare one.

### Recommended scope for this bead

Replace the `_mix` acceptance with the push path:

- interpreter: `get_stream_playback()` on an `AudioStreamPlayer` whose stream is an `AudioStreamGenerator`, returning a handle whose `push_buffer` / `push_frame` / `can_push_buffer` / `get_frames_available` route into the existing `gdaudio::decode` generator;
- bridge: own a generator per such player and mix its buffered frames in `AudioServerBridge::process` (`:307`, mixes at `:349-353`);
- drop `_mix`, `_process`, `_mix_resampled` entirely — no script can implement them.

That is a real, Godot-correct, GDScript-reachable feature built on code that already exists and is tested. It needs the interpreter lease and one decision about which stream representation to match.

title: Multiplayer: make MultiplayerPeer script-constructible and assignable via multiplayer.multiplayer_peer
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-peer-script-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json MultiplayerAPI.set_multiplayer_peer + property `multiplayer_peer`; upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp; doc/classes/MultiplayerAPI.xml. Canonical Godot line: `var peer = WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new(); peer.create_client(url); multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = peer`. | upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_rpc_interface.cpp:471-500 (`rpcp`: p_peer_id==0 → all peers, p_peer_id<0 → all except -p_peer_id), :303-345 (`_send_rpc` builds the target set and relays), :248-261 (`_process_rpc` can_call check: RPC_MODE_AUTHORITY requires p_from == node->get_multiplayer_authority(), RPC_MODE_DISABLED always rejects), :90 (rpc_mode from per-node config dict); SceneMultiplayer server_relay property in extension_api.json. | upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_cache_interface.cpp (send_object_cache / path confirmation), scene_rpc_interface.cpp:320-345 (`has_all_peers` gate choosing 8/16/32-bit node ids), scene_multiplayer.h:69-76 (NETWORK_COMMAND_SIMPLIFY_PATH / CONFIRM_PATH); MultiplayerAPI::decode_and_decompress_variants(..., is_object_decoding_allowed()) at scene_rpc_interface.cpp:288.

**Godot classes:** MultiplayerAPI, SceneMultiplayer, MultiplayerPeer, WebSocketMultiplayerPeer, OfflineMultiplayerPeer, ENetMultiplayerPeer

**Patina today:**
- [multiplayer] NO MultiplayerPeer subclass is script-constructible and there is no peer setter. (1) The interpreter's `.new()` dispatch chain at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3060-3130 knows only WebSocketPeer (line 3082) and StreamPeerBuffer (line 3100) among network types. `grep -c '"WebSocketMultiplayerPeer"' interpreter.rs` = 0; same for ENetMultiplayerPeer, TcpMultiplayerPeer, OfflineMultiplayerPeer, MultiplayerSpawner, MultiplayerSynchronizer, SceneReplicationConfig, StreamPeerTCP, PacketPeerUDP, TCPServer, UDPServer, PacketPeerStream (all 0). (2) `call_multiplayer_method` (interpreter.rs:7266-7370) implements exactly 10 methods — is_server, get_unique_id, has_multiplayer_peer, get_peers, get_remote_sender_id, get_authenticating_peers, send_bytes, complete_auth, set_refuse_new_connections, is_refusing_new_connections — and falls through to `UndefinedFunction("multiplayer.{other}")` at 7369. There is NO `set_multiplayer_peer`, and `multiplayer` is only reachable as a method-call receiver (`matches!(object, Expr::Ident(n) if n == "multiplayer")`, interpreter.rs:2894), never as a property target, so `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = peer` cannot parse to anything. (3) The SceneAccess trait (gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:1077-1127) has no peer-assign hook at all. (4) Every green multiplayer test injects the peer from RUST: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/rpc_annotation_end_to_end_dispatch.rs:59-61 does `MockNetwork::create_pair` + `tree_a.get_multiplayer_mut().set_multiplayer_peer(Box::new(server))`. No GDScript path exists.
- [multiplayer] (1) NO BROADCAST. `MultiplayerAPI::rpc` at crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:347-379 resolves a single target: line 358 `let target_id = self.authority_map.get(&node_path).copied().unwrap_or(PeerId::SERVER);` then one `peer.send_packet(target_id, packet)`. Godot's `rpc()` is `rpcp(obj, 0, ...)` = broadcast to every connected peer. (2) `rpc_id` at network.rs:391-421 does `peer_handle.send_packet(PeerId(peer as u32), packet)` (line 415) — a negative peer id (Godot's 'all except N') becomes a garbage u32, and 0 is not treated as broadcast. (3) The transport cannot broadcast either: crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs:437-441 server-side does `self.conns.get(&to).ok_or(NetworkError::PeerUnreachable(to))` — a single connection lookup; PeerId(0) is unreachable. There is no server relay: `grep -n 'server_relay' crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs` = 0 hits, and the server's `pump_server_reads` only pushes into its own inbox, never forwarding a client packet addressed to another client. (4) NO RECEIVE-SIDE AUTHORITY CHECK: crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:489-500 dispatches every decoded inbound RPC straight into `call_script_with_access` with no `can_call` gate — any peer can invoke an `@rpc("authority")` method. (5) RPCMode (network.rs:126-133) has only Authority and Any; RPC_MODE_DISABLED is absent. (6) RPC configs are keyed by bare method NAME on the whole tree (`rpc_configs: HashMap<String, RPCConfig>`, network.rs:169; `register_script_rpcs` at scene_tree.rs:513-546 inserts by name), and `call_local` is a separate tree-global `HashSet<String>` (scene_tree.rs:234) — two different scripts declaring the same method name with different modes collide. Godot's config is per-node (`_get_node_config(p_node)`, scene_rpc_interface.cpp:243).
- [multiplayer] The whole path-cache machinery is dead code behind a green test named after the feature. `crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:875-975` defines RpcPathCache, encode_simplify_path, decode_simplify_path, encode_confirm_path, decode_confirm_path, encode_rpc_call, encode_rpc_packet_with_id, decode_rpc_packet_cached, and the ObjectDecoding enum (network.rs:291-299). `grep -rn 'encode_rpc_call|RpcPathCache|encode_simplify_path|encode_confirm_path|decode_rpc_packet_cached|ObjectDecoding' crates/ --include='*.rs'` outside network.rs matches ONLY crates/gdplatform/tests/multiplayer_godot_wire_protocol.rs (lines 11-136) and the re-export list in crates/gdplatform/src/lib.rs:67-72. The `MultiplayerAPI` struct (network.rs:167-195) has no RpcPathCache field at all; `MultiplayerAPI::rpc` (network.rs:347-379) and `rpc_id` (network.rs:391-421) both call `encode_rpc_packet(node_path, ...)` — the unconditional full-8-byte-path form (network.rs:1029-1041) — and `MultiplayerAPI::poll` (network.rs:435) calls the cache-less `decode_rpc_packet`, which hardcodes `ObjectDecoding::Deny` (network.rs:1043-1045). Consequence: `SceneMultiplayer.allow_object_decoding` can never be enabled even though ClassDB advertises the property (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11631-11634), and every RPC pays 8 bytes of path forever.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/tests/multiplayer_godot_wire_protocol.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: every Godot multiplayer project starts with three lines of GDScript — construct a peer, call create_server/create_client on it, assign it to `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer`. `MultiplayerAPI` exposes `set_multiplayer_peer`/`get_multiplayer_peer`/`has_multiplayer_peer` plus the `multiplayer_peer` property (extension_api.json MultiplayerAPI; upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/scene_multiplayer.cpp). `MultiplayerPeer.create_*` lives on each transport subclass. On web the transports are WebSocketMultiplayerPeer and WebRTCMultiplayerPeer; OfflineMultiplayerPeer is the default single-player peer.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: the whole stack is Rust-only. `crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:3060-3130` is the `.new()` dispatch chain; the only network handles it mints are WebSocketPeer (line 3082) and StreamPeerBuffer (line 3100). grep for the string literals "WebSocketMultiplayerPeer", "ENetMultiplayerPeer", "OfflineMultiplayerPeer", "TcpMultiplayerPeer" in interpreter.rs returns 0 hits each. `call_multiplayer_method` (interpreter.rs:7266-7370) handles 10 methods and errors `UndefinedFunction` on everything else, including `set_multiplayer_peer`. `interpreter.rs:2894` routes `multiplayer` only as a method-call receiver, so property assignment has no path. The `SceneAccess` trait (crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs:1077-1127) declares multiplayer_is_server / multiplayer_unique_id / … but no peer-assign hook. The transports themselves are real: `crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs:205-240` has create_server/create_client, `crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:778-836` has OfflineMultiplayerPeer implementing NetworkPeer. Nothing in a script can reach them — the only callers are Rust tests (crates/gdscene/tests/rpc_annotation_end_to_end_dispatch.rs:59-61).\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (a) mint handle types for the peer transports in interpreter.rs alongside the existing WebSocketPeer handle table (websocket_peer.rs:995-1022 is the pattern: is_*_handle / new_*_handle / with_* / release_*). Add `new_ws_multiplayer_peer_handle()` in gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs and `new_offline_multiplayer_peer_handle()` in gdplatform/src/network.rs, and register "WebSocketMultiplayerPeer"/"OfflineMultiplayerPeer" in the `.new()` chain. (b) add a `call_multiplayer_peer_instance` dispatcher covering create_server/create_client/poll/close/get_unique_id/get_connection_status/set_target_peer/get_peers/disconnect_peer. (c) add `multiplayer_set_peer(&mut self, handle: u64) -> bool` to `SceneAccess` in bindings.rs, implement it in crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs (near the existing multiplayer_* impls at 2251-2318) by taking the handle out of the peer table and calling `tree.get_multiplayer_mut().set_multiplayer_peer(Box::new(peer))`. (d) teach the interpreter's member-assignment path to route `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = <ObjectId>` into that hook, and add `set_multiplayer_peer(peer)` to `call_multiplayer_method`.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: the end-to-end path must be scene-load → script `_ready()` constructs a peer and assigns it → SceneTree's MultiplayerAPI holds it → the existing per-frame `poll_multiplayer_with_delta` (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3051) drives it. No Rust-side `set_multiplayer_peer` may appear in the acceptance test.

**Merged findings (3):** MultiplayerPeer assignment from GDScript (multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = peer; ENetMultiplayerPeer/WebSocketMultiplayerPeer/OfflineMultiplayerPeer .new()); rpc() broadcast semantics, rpc_id(0)/rpc_id(-N), receive-side authority validation, RPC_MODE_DISABLED, per-node rpc_config, server relay; RPC node-path id negotiation (SIMPLIFY_PATH / CONFIRM_PATH) and allow_object_decoding policy

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn whose script does `var p = OfflineMultiplayerPeer.new(); multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = p` in `_ready()` and then reads `multiplayer.is_server()` and `multiplayer.get_unique_id()` in `_process()` yields true/1 after one MainLoop frame, with the peer assigned purely from GDScript. A second scene doing the same with `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new()` + `create_server(0)` reports CONNECTION_CONNECTED from `get_connection_status()`. (test: `multiplayer_peer_assigned_from_gdscript`) — the test must drive `MainLoop::step`/scene load and must contain no Rust call to `get_multiplayer_mut().set_multiplayer_peer`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose script does `var p = OfflineMultiplayerPeer.new(); multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = p` in `_ready()` and then reads `multiplayer.is_server()` and `multiplayer.get_unique_id()` in `_process()` yields true/1 after one MainLoop frame, with the peer assigned purely from GDScript. A second scene doing the same with `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new()` + `create_server(0)` reports CONNECTION_CONNECTED from `get_connection_status()`. (test: `multiplayer_peer_assigned_from_gdscript`) — the test must drive `MainLoop::step`/scene load and must contain no Rust call to `get_multiplayer_mut().set_multiplayer_peer`.

title: Rendering: dispatch script-defined Texture2D, Mesh/PrimitiveMesh and StyleBox virtuals from the render paths
description:

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json Texture2D._get_width/_get_height/_is_pixel_opaque/_has_alpha/_draw/_draw_rect/_draw_rect_region; TextureLayered._get_format/_get_layered_type/_get_width/_get_height/_get_layers/_has_mipmaps/_get_layer_data; Texture3D (6); Mesh._get_surface_count/_surface_get_arrays/... **Patina today:**
- [engine-virtual-method-table] TextureLayered (7/7) and Texture3D (6/6) ARE fully declared in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (see the comments at class_db.rs:8837 "The seven `_`-prefixed virtuals a script/GDExtension overrides" and :8904 "The six virtuals a script overrides to supply the volume data") yet nothing dispatches them: `rg -F '"_get_layer_data"' / '"_get_format"' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**'` hits only class_db.rs. Texture2D 0/7, Mesh 0/14, PrimitiveMesh 0/1, VisualInstance3D 0/1, StyleBox 0/4, Material 0/4 declared: `rg -F '"_draw_rect"' / '"_draw_rect_region"' / '"_get_draw_rect"' / '"_test_mask"' / '"_get_surface_count"' / '"_create_mesh_array"' / '"_get_aabb"' / '"_get_shader_rid"' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**'` returns 0 files for each. `_get_width`/`_get_height` hit class_db.rs only.

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `extends Texture2D` with `_get_width`/`_get_height`/`_draw`/`_draw_rect`/`_draw_rect_region`/`_has_alpha`/`_is_pixel_opaque` gives a fully procedural texture usable anywhere a Texture2D is; `extends PrimitiveMesh` + `_create_mesh_array()` builds procedural geometry; `extends Mesh` supplies surfaces directly (14 virtuals); `extends StyleBox` + `_draw(canvas_item, rect)` / `_get_draw_rect` / `_get_minimum_size` / `_test_mask` gives a fully custom control background; `VisualInstance3D._get_aabb` supplies custom culling bounds; `Material._get_shader_rid` / `_get_shader_mode` back custom materials.\n\nPATINA: TextureLayered (7/7) and Texture3D (6/6) are fully DECLARED in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (comments at :8837 and :8904 say so explicitly) but nothing calls them — grepping `\"_get_layer_data\"` / `\"_get_format\"` over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) hits class_db.rs only. Texture2D, Mesh, PrimitiveMesh, VisualInstance3D, StyleBox and Material have ZERO of their virtuals declared and zero references: `rg -F '\"_draw_rect\"'`, `'\"_draw_rect_region\"'`, `'\"_get_draw_rect\"'`, `'\"_test_mask\"'`, `'\"_get_surface_count\"'`, `'\"_create_mesh_array\"'`, `'\"_get_aabb\"'`, `'\"_get_shader_rid\"'` each return 0 files. A script-defined texture, mesh or stylebox is inert.\n\nAPPROACH, staged: STAGE 1 (Texture2D) — in engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs, where a texture handle is resolved for a draw item, detect a script-carrying Texture2D and call `_get_width`/`_get_height` for sizing and `_draw`/`_draw_rect`/`_draw_rect_region` to let the script emit its own draw commands; `_has_alpha`/`_is_pixel_opaque` feed blending and hit-testing. STAGE 2 (StyleBox) — in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, when a theme stylebox carries a script, call `_get_minimum_size` for content margins and `_draw(canvas_item, rect)` instead of the built-in stylebox painter; `_test_mask` gates hit testing. STAGE 3 (PrimitiveMesh/Mesh) — in engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, call `_create_mesh_array()` once per scripted PrimitiveMesh to build the ArrayMesh, and the Mesh surface virtuals for a full custom Mesh; call `VisualInstance3D._get_aabb` for culling. Declare every virtual in this bead in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.\n\nWIRING: .tscn -> a node whose texture/mesh/stylebox resource carries a script -> the renderer's per-frame resolve -> the virtuals -> draw items / vertex data that differ from the built-in default.

**Prove it:** A .tscn Sprite2D whose texture is a scripted Texture2D returning 64/32 from `_get_width`/`_get_height` and emitting one rect from `_draw_rect` produces exactly that rect in the frame's 2D draw-item list at 64x32; a Panel whose theme stylebox is a scripted StyleBox emitting a circle from `_draw` produces that circle rather than the default flat box; a MeshInstance3D whose mesh is a scripted PrimitiveMesh returning a 3-vertex `_create_mesh_array` renders one triangle. (test: `script_defined_texture_mesh_stylebox_virtuals`)

## EmeraldIsland — behaviour half landed; registration + .tscn flatten waiting on two leases

### The bead's "Patina today" is stale

It says nothing enforces exclusivity and cites `class_db.rs:7192`. Both are wrong now:

- `crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:2711-2788` already had `button_group_of`, `button_group_siblings` and sibling un-pressing in `set_button_pressed`, plus a hardcoded refusal to un-press the active grouped button in `fire_button_action`.
- `crates/gdscene/tests/base_button_toggle_group_and_capture_semantics.rs` case (e) already covered two grouped CheckBoxes via real click routing.
- The `button_group` property registration is at `class_db.rs:14190`, not `:7192` — the file has shifted.

The bead's `extension_api.json` citation is also unusable: that file is not in this repo. Ground truth used instead: `upstream/godot/doc/classes/ButtonGroup.xml` and `upstream/godot/scene/gui/base_button.cpp`.

### Real remaining gap, and what I landed

Verified missing: `ClassRegistration::new("ButtonGroup")` = 0 hits; `allow_unpress` / `get_pressed_button` / `get_buttons` = 0 hits anywhere.

Landed in `control.rs` (free file), with `button_group_enforces_radio_exclusivity` + 3 supporting tests driven entirely through `push_input`:

- `button_group_allows_unpress()` and the `fire_button_action` fix — the refusal was hardcoded, so `allow_unpress = true` did nothing. Godot spells this as forcing `status.pressed = true` back on inside `_unpress_group` (`base_button.cpp:43-46`); refusing the flip up front reaches the same state without emitting a `toggled(false)` that is immediately contradicted.
- `button_group_buttons()` = `ButtonGroup.get_buttons()`. ⚠️ **Includes the receiver**, unlike the existing `button_group_siblings`: Godot's `_get_buttons()` walks the whole list with no `continue` while `_unpress_group` skips `this`. The two differ by exactly one element and the wrong one un-presses the button just clicked. `button_group_siblings` is now expressed on top of it rather than duplicating the filter.
- `button_group_pressed_button()` = `get_pressed_button()`, first pressed member in tree order.

### Blocked, not skipped

- **`class_db.rs`** (BronzeBridge, to 03:12Z) — the `ButtonGroup` Resource registration.
- **`packed_scene.rs`** (BronzeBridge, to 03:36Z) — flattening the `ButtonGroup` sub-resource body onto member nodes as `__button_group__allow_unpress`, mirroring the existing `__material__*` / `__shape__*` / `__replication__*` passes. **Until this lands, `allow_unpress` cannot be set from a `.tscn` at all** — the node carries only `__resref__button_group` naming `class::id`, and the body is unreachable at runtime. My tests set the flattened companion directly, which is exactly what that pass will produce.

I checked whether the flatten could route around the lease as a post-instantiation pass like `setup_local_to_scene` (which reads bodies via the public `PackedScene::sub_resource_props`). It cannot usefully: `setup_local_to_scene` has **no production caller** — its only caller is its own test — so a second module in that shape would be dead code.

### One acceptance clause is not deliverable as written

`ButtonGroup.pressed(button)` is a signal on the **resource**. Patina resources are values with no object identity, and `BaseButton.button_group` reads as `Nil`, so there is nothing to emit from and nothing a script could connect to. The same applies to calling `get_pressed_button()` / `get_buttons()` *on a group* from GDScript — the behaviour is implemented and tested, but the receiver does not exist. Emitting into the void would be unreachable and untestable.

That is a real architecture gap (resources-as-values), not a defect in this bead, and it wants its own bead rather than a fake signal here. Registering the two methods and the signal in ClassDB would advertise what the engine cannot dispatch, which this project's convention forbids — so when I take the `class_db.rs` half I intend to register `ButtonGroup` with `allow_unpress` only, and say so.

### The bead is partly stale

It says `rg -in foldable crates/` matches only the script editor and that `ClassRegistration::new("FoldableContainer")` returns 0 hits. **`FoldableContainer` is already registered** at `class_db.rs:19232` (parent `Container`, with `folded` / `title` / `title_alignment`). `FoldableGroup` really is absent, and `control.rs` really had zero Foldable anything — that half was accurate.

The `extension_api.json` citation is unusable again: not in this repo. Ground truth used: `upstream/godot/scene/gui/foldable_container.cpp` and `doc/classes/FoldableContainer.xml`.

### Landed in `control.rs`

Title band (`FOLDABLE_TITLE_HEIGHT` + a `theme_override_constants/title_height` reader, mirroring `TAB_BAR_HEIGHT`), `title_position` top/bottom, fold collapse, group exclusivity, and the click seam. Five tests including the named acceptance.

**Three traps, each marked at the code:**

1. **FoldableContainer must NOT join the `PASS` mouse-filter list** beside its container siblings. `container.cpp:233` sets `MOUSE_FILTER_PASS`, but `foldable_container.cpp:600` sets it straight back to `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` — the title bar is a click target, so the container has to win the hit test. Adding it to `PASS` is the obvious-looking move that makes the title silently unclickable. It IS in `CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES` and `is_container_class`.
2. **`folding_changed` is emitted by the CLICK path, never by `set_folded`** (`:57-63`, `:235-236`). So the sibling that `_update_group` folds stays silent — one click fires exactly one signal, not one per group member.
3. **A refused fold still emits.** Godot reads `folded` back out on the line *after* `set_folded`, so a refused toggle emits `folding_changed` carrying the unchanged value rather than staying quiet.

I also **removed a `_folding_changed` script virtual I had added by analogy with `BaseButton._toggled`**. `foldable_container.h` declares no `GDVIRTUAL` at all and the doc XML lists `folding_changed` under `<signals>`, so that pairing would have been inventing a Godot API. Signal only.

A folded container shrinks *itself* to the title band. Godot reaches that through `update_minimum_size` and a parent re-sort; `arrange_container` takes an explicit size instead, so the collapse has to be applied in the arrange arm or a folded container keeps occupying its full expanded height with nothing in it.

### Blocked, not skipped

- **`scene_tree.rs`** (BronzeBridge, to 03:35Z) — the routed-click hop. `gui_input_stage` needs to call `point_in_foldable_title` then `toggle_foldable_from_click`. Everything from that seam inward is tested; the hop from a raw `push_input` is the one thing the acceptance still wants.
- **`class_db.rs`** (released to BronzeBridge at 02:59Z at their request, for pat-s3rrv.162) — `FoldableGroup` registration, plus `FoldableContainer`'s missing `title_position` / `foldable_group` / `title_text_overrun_behavior` / `title_text_direction` / `language` properties and the `folding_changed` signal.

I will take both as they free up rather than racing anyone for them.

### Note for whoever writes the `FoldableGroup` half

`allow_folding_all` lives in the sub-resource BODY, so it needs the same flatten `__button_group__allow_unpress` got in `packed_scene.rs` (pat-s3rrv.161) — a node carries only the reference. `control.rs` already reads `__foldable_group__allow_folding_all` and the test sets that companion directly, so the flatten is the only missing link.

title: LinkButton: unregistered, invisible (no draw arm), and its uri/underline properties do not exist
description:
[audit-key: gui/gui-controls-linkbutton] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/link_button.cpp; doc/classes/LinkButton.xml (text, underline {ALWAYS/ON_HOVER/NEVER}, uri, language, structured_text_bidi_override, text_direction; inherits BaseButton)

**Godot classes:** LinkButton

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] Not registered: 'LinkButton' is absent from class_db.rs's complete string-literal dump. Never drawn: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:42-87 `const CONTROL_CLASSES` (the draw-pass membership gate) lists Button, Label, CheckBox, CheckButton, OptionButton, TextureRect, ItemList, TabBar ... and no LinkButton; `rg -n '"LinkButton"' crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs` returns nothing. No LinkButton-specific behavior exists: `rg -n 'uri|underline' crates/gdscene/src/control*.rs` returns only unrelated hits (control_render.rs:124 a generic Line draw item comment, control.rs:166/809/1282/3087 unrelated). It IS present in three class-name fallback lists — control.rs:828 and :868 (BUTTON_CLASSES, so a click emits `pressed`), control.rs:837-area CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES (hit-testable) and control.rs:2758 FOCUSABLE_BY_DEFAULT — so a LinkButton in a scene is clickable and tab-focusable but paints nothing and never opens its uri.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

LinkButton is Godot's hyperlink-styled button: text drawn with an underline (ALWAYS / ON_HOVER / NEVER) that opens `uri` via OS.shell_open when pressed with no `pressed` handler attached.

Patina registers it nowhere — 'LinkButton' is absent from the full string-literal set of engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs — and never draws it: control_render.rs:42-87 CONTROL_CLASSES, the membership list that gates the draw arm, has no LinkButton entry, and there is no `"LinkButton" =>` arm in draw_control.

It IS in three class-name fallback lists: control.rs:868 BUTTON_CLASSES (so node_is_base_button returns true and a click emits `pressed`), the CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES list at control.rs:828-838 (hit-testable), and control.rs:2758 FOCUSABLE_BY_DEFAULT (tab-reachable). The result is the worst combination: an invisible rectangle that is clickable and focusable. Neither `uri` nor `underline` exists anywhere — `rg 'uri|underline' crates/gdscene/src/control*.rs` finds nothing related.

Work: register LinkButton (parent BaseButton) with text, uri, underline (enum), language, text_direction and structured_text_bidi_override; add a draw arm in control_render.rs that emits the text plus an underline Line item per the underline mode and hover state; open `uri` on press when it is set.

**Prove it:** 1. ClassDB registers LinkButton with parent BaseButton -> Control and Godot's properties, with `underline` defaulting to UNDERLINE_MODE_ALWAYS (per doc/classes/LinkButton.xml).
2. control_draw_items() for a scene with a LinkButton whose text is "Docs" returns a Text item carrying "Docs" and a Line item underneath it.
3. With underline = ON_HOVER, the Line item is absent when the pointer is elsewhere and present after a mouse-motion event lands inside the button rect.
4. With underline = NEVER, no Line item is ever emitted.
5. Pressing a LinkButton with uri = "https://example.com" and no connected `pressed` handler invokes the shell_open path (assert via the recorded platform call, not a real browser).
6. Its `pressed` signal still fires for scripts that connect one (test: `link_button_draws_text_with_underline_and_opens_uri`)
acceptance_criteria:
1. ClassDB registers LinkButton with parent BaseButton -> Control and Godot's properties, with `underline` defaulting to UNDERLINE_MODE_ALWAYS (per doc/classes/LinkButton.xml).
2. control_draw_items() for a scene with a LinkButton whose text is "Docs" returns a Text item carrying "Docs" and a Line item underneath it.
3. With underline = ON_HOVER, the Line item is absent when the pointer is elsewhere and present after a mouse-motion event lands inside the button rect.
4. With underline = NEVER, no Line item is ever emitted.
5. Pressing a LinkButton with uri = "https://example.com" and no connected `pressed` handler invokes the shell_open path (assert via the recorded platform call, not a real browser).
6. Its `pressed` signal still fires for scripts that connect one (test: `link_button_draws_text_with_underline_and_opens_uri`)

title: Register NinePatchRect in ClassDB and finish region_rect + texture_changed
description:
[audit-key: gui/gui-controls-ninepatchrect-classdb-and-region] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/NinePatchRect.xml — inherits Control, instantiable, members: axis_stretch_horizontal, axis_stretch_vertical, draw_center, mouse_filter (override, default 1/PASS), patch_margin_bottom/left/right/top, region_rect, texture; signal `texture_changed`. extension_api.json: 12 methods / 9 properties.

**Godot classes:** NinePatchRect

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-3] IMPLEMENTED AND DRAWN, BUT NOT REGISTERED. Draw producer: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1196 `"NinePatchRect" => { … out.push(DrawCommand::DrawNinePatch { texture_path, rect, margin_left/top/right/bottom, draw_center (defaults true), axis_h, axis_v, modulate }) }` reusing `stylebox::AxisStretchMode::to_nine_patch_axis()`. Mouse hit-testing: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:821 lists "NinePatchRect" in CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES. Property setters: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:352 (texture) and :359 (nine-patch margins), with tests at node2d.rs:1186/1197/1206 and engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/nine_patch_rect_draw.rs:29,157.
ABSENCE 1 — ClassDB: `rg -n '"NinePatchRect"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` → 0 hits, while its direct siblings ARE registered: class_db.rs:7245 `register_class(ClassRegistration::new("TextureRect").parent("Control"))` and class_db.rs:7783 `ColorRect`.parent("Control"). Consequence: the editor's Create Node dialog is built from `class_db::get_class_list()` (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:934, also :1050/:1176/:1188), so NinePatchRect can never be created from the editor, and `ClassDB.instantiate("NinePatchRect")` / `ClassDB.class_get_property_list` fail. Script completion has the same source (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/script_completion.rs:300).
ABSENCE 2 — region_rect: `rg -n 'region_rect' engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs` → 0 hits, so a NinePatchRect that sources its patch from a sub-rect of an atlas draws the whole texture instead.
ABSENCE 3 — `texture_changed` signal: `rg -n 'texture_changed' engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/` → no NinePatchRect declaration.
The only other repo hit is engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4714 `("NinePatchRect", "Control")`, a name→parent string row in `generated_parent_of` with no property schema arm (the file seeds 70 classes; NinePatchRect is not one of them).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

NinePatchRect already rasterizes correctly — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1196 emits DrawCommand::DrawNinePatch with per-axis stretch modes and a draw_center default of true, it is hit-tested (control.rs:821), it has property setters (node2d.rs:352/359) and a passing draw test (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/nine_patch_rect_draw.rs). What is missing is the registration and two members:

1. ClassDB. `rg -n '"NinePatchRect"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` is empty, while sibling Controls are registered right there (TextureRect at class_db.rs:7245, ColorRect at :7783). Because the editor's Create Node dialog and script completion both enumerate `class_db::get_class_list()` (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:934, script_completion.rs:300), a user cannot add a NinePatchRect in Patina's editor at all, and `ClassDB.instantiate("NinePatchRect")` fails from script.
2. `region_rect` is never read by the renderer (`rg -n region_rect engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs` → 0 hits), so an atlas-sourced nine-patch draws the entire texture.
3. The `texture_changed` signal is not declared.

**Prove it:** 1) `class_exists("NinePatchRect")` is true and `is_parent_class("NinePatchRect", "Control")` and `is_parent_class("NinePatchRect", "CanvasItem")` hold.
2) The class registers all 10 documented members with Godot's defaults from upstream/godot/doc/classes/NinePatchRect.xml: texture=null, draw_center=true, patch_margin_left/top/right/bottom=0, region_rect=Rect2(0,0,0,0), axis_stretch_horizontal=0, axis_stretch_vertical=0, mouse_filter=1 (PASS, overriding Control's default of 0).
3) `class_db::get_class_list()` contains "NinePatchRect", and the editor create-dialog listing (create_dialog.rs `filtered_classes()` with base_class "Control") includes it — this is the check that proves the editor can actually add the node.
4) A NinePatchRect with `region_rect = Rect2(16, 16, 32, 32)` over a 64x64 texture emits a DrawNinePatch whose source sampling is confined to that sub-rect: the drawn corner patches come from the region's corners, not the texture's. A default (zero-size) region_rect keeps the current whole-texture behavior byte-for-byte (existing nine_patch_rect_draw.rs assertions unchanged).
5) Assigning a new `texture` emits the `texture_changed` signal exactly once, and the signal is listed by `ClassDB.class_get_signal_list("NinePatchRect")` (test: `ninepatchrect_registered_and_region_rect_drawn`)
acceptance_criteria:
1) `class_exists("NinePatchRect")` is true and `is_parent_class("NinePatchRect", "Control")` and `is_parent_class("NinePatchRect", "CanvasItem")` hold.
2) The class registers all 10 documented members with Godot's defaults from upstream/godot/doc/classes/NinePatchRect.xml: texture=null, draw_center=true, patch_margin_left/top/right/bottom=0, region_rect=Rect2(0,0,0,0), axis_stretch_horizontal=0, axis_stretch_vertical=0, mouse_filter=1 (PASS, overriding Control's default of 0).
3) `class_db::get_class_list()` contains "NinePatchRect", and the editor create-dialog listing (create_dialog.rs `filtered_classes()` with base_class "Control") includes it — this is the check that proves the editor can actually add the node.
4) A NinePatchRect with `region_rect = Rect2(16, 16, 32, 32)` over a 64x64 texture emits a DrawNinePatch whose source sampling is confined to that sub-rect: the drawn corner patches come from the region's corners, not the texture's. A default (zero-size) region_rect keeps the current whole-texture behavior byte-for-byte (existing nine_patch_rect_draw.rs assertions unchanged).
5) Assigning a new `texture` emits the `texture_changed` signal exactly once, and the signal is listed by `ClassDB.class_get_signal_list("NinePatchRect")` (test: `ninepatchrect_registered_and_region_rect_drawn`)

title: Register PopupPanel and the ScrollBar/Slider/SpinBox Range chain in ClassDB
description:
[audit-key: gui/gui-controls-popup-panel-and-scrollbar-classes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/popup.h (PopupPanel : Popup), upstream/godot/scene/gui/scroll_bar.h (ScrollBar : Range, abstract; HScrollBar/VScrollBar concrete). extension_api.json: PopupPanel inherits=Popup inst=true; ScrollBar inherits=Range inst=false with a `custom_step` property.

**Godot classes:** PopupPanel, ScrollBar

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-5] Neither is in ClassDB: `rg -c '"PopupPanel"' /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` -> 0; `rg -n 'ScrollBar' class_db.rs` -> a single hit at :12225 which is only a comment mentioning ScrollBar. The Popup chain that IS registered stops one class short: class_db.rs:7814-7821 registers `Popup` (parent Window) and `PopupMenu` (parent Popup); `rg -n 'parent("Popup")' class_db.rs` returns only PopupMenu. The Range chain is likewise truncated: `rg -n 'parent("Range")' class_db.rs` returns ONLY ProgressBar (:7228) — no Slider/HSlider/VSlider/SpinBox/ScrollBar/HScrollBar/VScrollBar. Both classes are nonetheless referenced by working subsystems, which is what makes the ClassDB hole visible: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:579 registers a `("PopupPanel", "panel")` default-theme stylebox, and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:836-838 lists "ScrollBar"/"HScrollBar"/"VScrollBar" in CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES — a fallback list that exists precisely because "the ClassDB inheritance table has not been populated" (control.rs:812-814). Consequence: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/create_node_catalog.rs:50-52 gates `can_instantiate` on `class_db::instantiate`, so neither node can be created from a ClassDB-driven picker, and `is_class("Range")` on a scrollbar is false.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Two Control chains stop one level short of Godot's. Popup and PopupMenu are registered (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7814-7821) but PopupPanel — the plain themed popup that every custom dropdown, tooltip panel and floating inspector uses — is not: `rg -c '"PopupPanel"' class_db.rs` returns 0, even though gdscene/src/theme.rs:579 already ships its `panel` stylebox in the default theme.

The Range chain is worse: `rg -n 'parent("Range")' class_db.rs` returns ONLY ProgressBar (:7228). ScrollBar, HScrollBar, VScrollBar, Slider, HSlider, VSlider and SpinBox are all absent, so `is_class("Range")` is false for every one of them and none can be instantiated through ClassDB (create_node_catalog.rs:50 `can_instantiate`). gdscene/src/control.rs:836-838 already carries them in a hardcoded CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES fallback list whose own doc comment (control.rs:812-814) explains it exists because ClassDB may not be populated — that workaround is the symptom.

Scope: register PopupPanel (parent Popup) and the abstract ScrollBar (parent Range, `custom_step` float default -1.0) with concrete HScrollBar/VScrollBar, plus the abstract Slider (parent Range: editable, scrollable, tick_count, ticks_on_borders) with HSlider/VSlider, and SpinBox (parent Range: alignment, editable, prefix, suffix, step, update_on_text_changed, select_all_on_focus, custom_arrow_step). Take every default from upstream/godot/doc/classes/*.xml; register only properties the doc XML gives a default for, per the convention noted at class_db.rs:12225.

**Prove it:** A test asserts `class_exists("PopupPanel")` with `is_parent_class("PopupPanel", "Popup")` and `is_parent_class("PopupPanel", "Window")`; that ScrollBar/HScrollBar/VScrollBar/Slider/HSlider/VSlider/SpinBox all report `is_parent_class(name, "Range")` and `is_parent_class(name, "Control")`, with ScrollBar and Slider abstract and the H/V leaves instantiable; that `instantiate("HScrollBar")` reports `custom_step == -1.0` and `instantiate("SpinBox")` reports `step == 1.0`; and that every name in gdscene::control's CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES resolves through ClassDB as a Control descendant (assert the fallback list is now redundant) (test: `popup_panel_and_range_chain_registered_in_classdb`)
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts `class_exists("PopupPanel")` with `is_parent_class("PopupPanel", "Popup")` and `is_parent_class("PopupPanel", "Window")`; that ScrollBar/HScrollBar/VScrollBar/Slider/HSlider/VSlider/SpinBox all report `is_parent_class(name, "Range")` and `is_parent_class(name, "Control")`, with ScrollBar and Slider abstract and the H/V leaves instantiable; that `instantiate("HScrollBar")` reports `custom_step == -1.0` and `instantiate("SpinBox")` reports `step == 1.0`; and that every name in gdscene::control's CONTROL_HIT_CLASSES resolves through ClassDB as a Control descendant (assert the fallback list is now redundant) (test: `popup_panel_and_range_chain_registered_in_classdb`)

title: Register the Range subtree Controls (Slider/HSlider/VSlider, ScrollBar/HScrollBar/VScrollBar, SpinBox) in ClassDB
description:
[audit-key: gui/gui-controls-range-slider-scrollbar-classdb] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/gui/slider.h + scroll_bar.h + spin_box.h; doc/classes/VSlider.xml (inherits Slider), VScrollBar.xml (inherits ScrollBar), Slider.xml/ScrollBar.xml (inherit Range), Range.xml (inherits Control). Godot registers all of them in scene/register_scene_types.cpp

**Godot classes:** VScrollBar, VSlider

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-7] Behaviour exists but the classes are not in ClassDB. Registered: `Range` (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7199) and `ProgressBar` (class_db.rs:7228). NOT registered — `grep -x <name>` against the 4186 literals extracted from class_db.rs = 0 hits for each of: Slider, HSlider, VSlider, ScrollBar, HScrollBar, VScrollBar, SpinBox. Meanwhile the runtime does implement them: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:833/838 lists "VSlider"/"VScrollBar" among recognised Control classes, control.rs:2762 lists VSlider in the focusable set, gdscene/src/theme.rs:586/588 map ("VScrollBar","scroll") and ("VSlider","slider") stylebox types, and gdscene/src/control_render.rs:507 documents ScrollContainer creating internal HScrollBar/VScrollBar children. Consequence is user-visible, not cosmetic: gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs:1-10 states it "lists registered classes from ClassDB", so a VSlider/VScrollBar cannot be created from the editor's Create-Node dialog, and GDScript `ClassDB.class_exists("VSlider")` answers false (interpreter.rs:14922). gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5190-5192 carries ("VScrollBar","ScrollBar")/("VSlider","Slider") rows, but that file contains no register_class call (`rg -n 'register_class|ClassRegistration'` = 0 hits) — it is an inspector table, not registration.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** Godot 4.6.1's Range subtree is Range -> Slider -> {HSlider, VSlider}, Range -> ScrollBar -> {HScrollBar, VScrollBar}, Range -> SpinBox. Slider and ScrollBar are abstract bases; the H/V leaves are concrete and placeable in a scene. Slider carries editable/scrollable/tick_count/ticks_on_borders; ScrollBar carries custom_step; SpinBox carries prefix/suffix/step/update_on_text_changed/custom_arrow_step/alignment/editable/select_all_on_focus. Members and defaults: upstream/godot/doc/classes/{Slider,HSlider,VSlider,ScrollBar,HScrollBar,VScrollBar,SpinBox}.xml.

**Patina today:** only Range (class_db.rs:7199) and ProgressBar (class_db.rs:7228) are registered; Slider, HSlider, VSlider, ScrollBar, HScrollBar, VScrollBar and SpinBox are all absent from ClassDB (0 hits each against class_db.rs's string literals). The behaviour is implemented and themed — gdscene/src/control.rs:833,838 and :2762 (focus ring), gdscene/src/theme.rs:586,588 stylebox types, control_render.rs:507 (ScrollContainer's internal scrollbars) — so this is rung (a) of the ladder missing under working rungs (b)-(c). Because gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs enumerates ClassDB, none of these can be created from the editor's Create-Node dialog, and `ClassDB.class_exists("VSlider")` is false from GDScript. gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5190-5192 has the parent rows but performs no registration.

**Implement:** add the subtree to engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs next to Range/ProgressBar, following the Separator pattern at class_db.rs:12225-12238 (abstract base + a loop over the H/V leaves). Mark Slider and ScrollBar `.abstract_class()`; leave the H/V leaves and SpinBox concrete. Take every property default from the doc XML. Keep the leaves free of re-declared inherited members (the property-list walk does not dedupe — class_db.rs:5016).

title: Multiplayer: drive MultiplayerSpawner/MultiplayerSynchronizer as real scene nodes from the SceneTree tick
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-replication-nodes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/multiplayer_spawner.cpp, multiplayer_synchronizer.cpp, scene_replication_config.{h,cpp} (REPLICATION_MODE_NEVER/ALWAYS/ON_CHANGE at scene_replication_config.h:43-45), scene_replication_interface.cpp; extension_api.json MultiplayerSpawner (spawn_path/spawn_limit/spawn_function, signals spawned/despawned), MultiplayerSynchronizer (root_path/replication_interval/delta_interval/replication_config/visibility_update_mode/public_visibility, add_visibility_filter, update_visibility, signals synchronized/delta_synchronized/visibility_changed), SceneReplicationConfig (property_get/set_watch).

**Godot classes:** MultiplayerSpawner, MultiplayerSynchronizer, SceneReplicationConfig

**Patina today:**
- [multiplayer] The replication layer has ZERO runtime call sites. (1) `crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:461` — `let _other = self.multiplayer.poll();` — the non-RPC packets (SPAWN/SYNC, `REPLICATION_KIND_SPAWN`/`REPLICATION_KIND_SYNC` at network.rs:1284/1287) are bound to `_other` and dropped on the floor every frame. (2) `MultiplayerReplicator` (crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs, the only bridge to a real SceneTree) has no callers: `grep -rn 'MultiplayerReplicator' crates/ --include='*.rs' | grep -v 'src/multiplayer.rs'` returns nothing. (3) `grep -rn 'poll_outbound|spawn_and_notify|observe_spawn_packet|apply_sync_packet|REPLICATION_KIND' crates/ --include='*.rs'` outside gdplatform/src/network.rs matches only the re-export lines gdplatform/src/lib.rs:73-74. (4) MultiplayerSpawner/MultiplayerSynchronizer are registered in ClassDB as plain `Node` subclasses with a property bag (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11731-11768) — no gdscene node implementation exists (grep for those names in crates/gdscene/src returns only doc comments in multiplayer.rs:3, 171-194). A .tscn containing them instantiates an inert Node. (5) `SceneReplicationConfig` is not registered anywhere: `grep -rn '"SceneReplicationConfig"' crates/gdobject/src crates/gdscript-interop/src` = 0 hits, so a `.tres` replication config cannot load; `property_get_watch`/`property_set_watch` are absent from the gdplatform struct (network.rs:1820-1934). (6) Synchronized values are strings, not Variants: `crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs:83-90` `decode_property_value` parses "x,y" into a Vector2 and leaves everything else a `Variant::String`; `MultiplayerSynchronizer::set_property_value` takes `impl Into<String>` (network.rs:1696).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: MultiplayerSpawner and MultiplayerSynchronizer are Nodes registered with the MultiplayerAPI via `object_configuration_add` when they enter the tree (upstream/godot/modules/multiplayer/multiplayer_spawner.cpp `_notification(NOTIFICATION_POST_ENTER_TREE)`, multiplayer_synchronizer.cpp). SceneReplicationInterface (scene_replication_interface.cpp) then, on every `MultiplayerAPI::poll`, emits SPAWN packets for scenes added under `spawn_path`, emits SYNC packets at `replication_interval` carrying the Variant values of the properties flagged `sync` in the node's SceneReplicationConfig, and applies inbound SPAWN/SYNC on the receiving peer — instantiating the PackedScene and writing the properties onto the live node. Property values travel as binary Variants, not strings. SceneReplicationConfig is a Resource saved in `.tres` with per-property spawn/sync/watch flags and a ReplicationMode (NEVER=0/ALWAYS=1/ON_CHANGE=2, scene_replication_config.h:43-45).\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: every piece exists as a library and nothing connects them. `crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:461` discards the non-RPC packets: `let _other = self.multiplayer.poll();`. `MultiplayerReplicator` in crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs is the only tree-aware bridge and has zero callers outside its own `#[cfg(test)]` module. `MultiplayerSpawner::spawn_and_notify`/`observe_spawn_packet` and `MultiplayerSynchronizer::poll_outbound`/`apply_sync_packet` (crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs:1540-1781) have zero callers. crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11731-11768 registers both classes as bare Nodes with a partial property list (spawn_path/spawn_limit; root_path/replication_interval) — no spawn_function, no delta_interval, no replication_config, no visibility_update_mode, no signals. SceneReplicationConfig is registered nowhere (0 grep hits in gdobject/gdscript-interop), so a `.tres` config cannot load. Synchronized values are strings: crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs:83-90 special-cases "x,y" into a Vector2 and stringifies everything else.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (a) add node behaviour in crates/gdscene: on `_enter_tree`, register a MultiplayerSpawner/MultiplayerSynchronizer node's config with the tree's MultiplayerAPI keyed by NodeId (mirroring `object_configuration_add`). (b) In `SceneTree::poll_multiplayer_with_delta` (scene_tree.rs:454-501), replace `let _other = ...` with a dispatch that routes `NetworkCommand::Spawn`/`Sync` packets into `MultiplayerReplicator::apply_spawn`/`apply_sync`, resolving `scene_path` through the real resource loader instead of the `resolve` closure. (c) Add an outbound pass in the same function: for each MultiplayerSynchronizer node whose `replication_interval` has elapsed and whose node is locally authoritative, snapshot the config's sync properties from the live node and send an encoded SYNC packet; for each MultiplayerSpawner, emit SPAWN for children added under `spawn_path` since last poll and DESPAWN for removals. (d) Change the property payload from `Vec<(String,String)>` to `Vec<(String, Variant)>` encoded with `gdvariant::binary::encode_variant` (already used for RPC args at network.rs:1021), deleting `decode_property_value`. (e) Register `SceneReplicationConfig` in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs with the full method set including `property_get_watch`/`property_set_watch`, add those two to the gdplatform struct (network.rs:1820-1934), and make it loadable from `.tres` in gdresource. (f) Complete the ClassDB registrations for both nodes (spawn_function, delta_interval, replication_config, visibility_update_mode, public_visibility, and the spawned/despawned/synchronized/visibility_changed signals).\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: SceneTree poll → spawner/synchronizer node state → packets over the peer → receiving SceneTree instantiates the PackedScene and writes real Variant properties onto the live node, all from a .tscn with no Rust orchestration.

**Prove it:** Two SceneTrees loaded from .tscn files, connected by a peer pair and stepped through MainLoop frames: the host tree adds a child under the MultiplayerSpawner's `spawn_path`, and after N frames the client tree contains an instantiated node of the spawned scene at the mirrored path. Moving the host node then updating its `position` results in the client node's `position` matching as a `Variant::Vector2` after the replication_interval elapses, with the value having travelled as a binary Variant (assert a Vector3 or Color property also survives, which the string codec cannot represent). (test: `multiplayer_spawner_and_synchronizer_replicate_from_scene`) — the test must call only MainLoop::step and scene loading; no direct call to MultiplayerReplicator, poll_outbound, or encode_sync_packet.

Moving the host node then updating its `position` results in the client node's `position` matching as a `Variant::Vector2` after the replication_interval elapses, with the value having travelled as a binary Variant (assert a Vector3 or Color property also survives, which the string codec cannot represent). ## Diagnosis pass (EmeraldIsland): THREE of the prior hypotheses ELIMINATED by inspection — no code changed

The previous worker left three hypotheses for why the acceptance test fails and wrote "NEXT STEP: needs someone who can RUN it." I cannot run either (same no-compiler lane), but three of them are statically decidable, and all three are **wrong**. Recording that so nobody re-walks them.

### (b) "MultiplayerAPI::poll() may not surface REPLICATION_KIND_SPAWN frames (it filters RPC/raw first)" — **DISPROVEN**
`poll()` (network.rs:422) classifies each packet as RPC → raw → `other`, and returns `other`. The two filters are strict:
- `decode_rpc_packet` matches only the RPC command byte.
- `decode_raw_packet` (network.rs:756) returns `None` unless the first byte is exactly `NetworkCommand::Raw`.

`REPLICATION_KIND_SPAWN`/`SYNC` are `NetworkCommand::Spawn`/`Sync` bytes, so neither filter can swallow them. Replication frames DO reach `other`.

### (a) "check `replication.spawners.len()` / `tracked_paths` right after `register_replication_nodes()`" — the registration IS reached
`MainLoop::step` → `poll_multiplayer_with_delta` (main_loop.rs:3287) → `register_replication_nodes()` → `poll_replication_spawns()` → `poll_replication_outbound()`. Registration runs on **every** poll and is idempotent via `replication.registered`. It matches `node.class_name()` against the exact strings `"MultiplayerSpawner"` / `"MultiplayerSynchronizer"`, which is what a `.tscn` `[node type="…"]` produces.

### The NodePath theory I formed and then killed — also wrong
The test writes `spawn_path = NodePath("../Players")` and `root_path = NodePath("..")`, which arrive as `Variant::NodePath`, not `Variant::String`. A String-only read would yield an empty path and register a spawner that tracks nothing — exactly the reported symptom. But `variant_as_path_string` (scene_tree.rs:62) handles `NodePath`, `String` **and** `StringName`. Not the bug.

### (c) "MockNetworkPeer cross-delivery timing" — structurally fine
`MockNetwork::create_pair` (network.rs:1246) cross-wires `inbox`/`remote_inbox` as shared queues, so a host send is visible to the client immediately. The test steps `host_loop` then `client_loop` in that order, which is correct, and gives 4 frames for the spawn and 6 more for the sync.

### What this leaves
The failure is below what inspection reaches at this depth — most likely inside the outbound passes (`poll_replication_spawns` / `poll_replication_outbound`) or the encode/decode round trip, where only actual values will tell you. **This bead genuinely needs a build lane**, which is now the independent conclusion of two workers.

⚠️ Worth checking first when someone can run it, since they are cheap and I could not settle them statically:
- `replication_interval` is read ONLY as `Variant::Float`/`Variant::Int` (scene_tree.rs ~600). If the `.tscn` value lands as anything else the interval is `0`, and a zero interval may mean "never elapses" rather than "every frame" — check which.
- `_sync_properties` accepts only `Variant::String`/`StringName` inside a `Variant::Array`. If the `.tscn` array parses to a packed string array instead, the list is empty and `poll_outbound` returns early — the synchronizer would be inert with no error.

Both are the same shape as the NodePath trap above: a narrow type match silently yielding a default.

### Status
I changed **no code** this pass. Implementation was already reported complete and compiling by the earlier worker; ClassDB registrations were delivered by SageCastle. The only thing missing is a diagnostic run.

comments.text:
EmeraldIsland — I briefly took this bead by mistake and have returned it to BronzeBridge. Leaving
one verified finding so the research is not wasted; I have changed no code here.

WHY I BACKED OFF: `br ready --unassigned` listed this bead, but `br update` reported
`assignee: BronzeBridge -> EmeraldIsland`, i.e. it was already owned. Checking before doing
anything: crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs was modified 11:39:02Z and scene_tree.rs 11:36:25Z —
minutes ago — and the verifier had just logged
`PASS pat-s3rrv.17 ... replication_config_child_paths_sync`, which is remaining-scope item (2).
BronzeBridge is plainly mid-flight. Reassigned straight back.

THE FINDING — remaining-scope item (4) is CONFIRMED, and it does broadcast:

Your note says "Despawn fires only when a child leaves its spawner's spawn_path; Godot also
despawns when the spawner itself leaves the tree." I went to check whether Godot really sends a
packet there or merely stops tracking locally, because implementing the wrong one would emit
despawns Godot never sends. It really does send them. The chain:

  1. multiplayer_spawner.cpp:211-219 — `case NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE:` iterates every
     `tracked_nodes` entry, disconnects its `tree_exiting` handler and calls
     `get_multiplayer()->object_configuration_remove(node, this)` with the SPAWNER as the config.
  2. That routes to `SceneReplicationInterface::on_despawn`
     (scene_replication_interface.cpp:195-221), whose own comment is
     "Forcibly despawn to all peers that knows me".
  3. It builds one despawn packet via `_make_despawn_packet(node, len)` and `_send_raw`s it to
     every peer whose `spawn_nodes` contains that node's ObjectID — then clears the spawner
     link, erases the node from `spawned_nodes`, and drops it from every peer's `spawn_nodes`.

So the correct behaviour is: on spawner exit, for EACH node the spawner tracks, send a despawn to
each peer that knows that node, and clear the tracking. Not a single packet, and not silence.

⚠️ The ordering in step 3 matters — the packet goes out BEFORE the peer bookkeeping is cleared,
because the send is gated on `E.value.spawn_nodes.has(oid)`. Clearing first would send nothing
while looking correct.

A test worth having asserts the peer actually received one despawn per tracked node, not just
that the local tracking emptied — the local half passes even if nothing is sent.

comments.text:
EmeraldIsland — no code this pass; every remaining item is behind a lease. Recording three findings so
the next worker does not re-derive them, one of which changes what item (2) should DO.

## ⚠️ ITEM (2) IS A DOCS-vs-CODE CONFLICT IN GODOT. Do not "fix" it without deciding which side wins.

The remaining-scope note says Patina should adopt Godot's formula. I read the upstream source to
implement it and stopped, because the change would flip two existing tests and the correct answer is
genuinely contested:

  modules/multiplayer/multiplayer_synchronizer.cpp
    :207  is_visible_to()      -> `return peer_visibility.has(0) || peer_visibility.has(p_peer);`
    :220  set_visibility_for() -> insert if visible, ERASE if not (:225/:227)
    :186  is_public_visibility -> `peer_visibility.has(0)`     (peer 0 IS the public flag)
    :456  constructor          -> `peer_visibility.insert(0)`  (public by default)

`peer_visibility` is a **HashSet<int>**, not a map to bool. The consequence is unintuitive:

  **while public visibility is ON, `set_visibility_for(peer, false)` does NOT hide from that peer** —
  `has(0)` is already true, and erasing an absent entry changes nothing.

Patina resolves `visibility.get(peer).unwrap_or(public_visibility)` (gdplatform/src/network.rs:1697),
so an explicit `false` DOES win. That is the deviation.

But the doc XML argues the other way — modules/multiplayer/doc_classes/MultiplayerSynchronizer.xml:58
calls `public_visibility` "visible to all peers **by default**. See set_visibility_for ... for ways of
configuring **fine-grained** visibility". A per-peer override that cannot override is not fine-grained.
So Godot's own docs describe Patina's behaviour and Godot's code implements the other one.

**Blast radius if you adopt the C++ semantics — both of these currently assert the opposite and are
live gates:**
  - gdscene/tests/synchronizer_visibility_from_script.rs:92-113 — `set_visibility_for(2, false)` then
    asserts `is_visible_to(2) == false`. Under the C++ rule this is `true`.
  - gdscene/tests/visibility_filter_callables_run.rs:205-228
    (`a_passing_filter_does_not_overwrite_an_explicit_set_visibility_for`) — same shape, same flip.
    ⚠️ The property that test actually cares about (a filter must not clobber the stored map) is
    INDEPENDENT and survives either way, because Godot AND-s filters with the stored set at query time
    (:194-206). Do not delete that test; only its expected value moves.

My recommendation: leave the behaviour, and if parity is wanted, change it as its own bead with those
two tests updated in the same commit — not as a side effect of another item.

## ITEM (1): the spawn-state gap is REAL, and it is not a one-file change

`SceneReplicationConfig::spawn_properties()` (network.rs:1980) has exactly ONE caller repo-wide and it
is a test assertion (:2066) — so the config records which properties are spawn-flagged and nothing ever
sends them. Confirmed inert.

⚠️ But the wire half alone cannot fix it. `SpawnRequest` is built in `MultiplayerSpawner::spawn`
(:1594), which has no access to property VALUES — those live on the synchronizer struct. Godot gathers
the spawn state at send time in `SceneReplicationInterface::_make_spawn_packet`. So the population half
belongs in the scene layer; adding `properties` to `SpawnRequest`/`SpawnPacket` on its own just ships an
always-empty list — the same registered-but-inert shape this audit keeps finding.

Sizing when someone takes it: `SpawnRequest` has 5 construction sites (network.rs :1594 :1629 :2389
:2579, plus gdscene/tests/multiplayer_replication_link_probes.rs:198), and `encode_sync_packet` (:1414)
already has exactly the framing to copy — `u16 name_len | name | u16 value_len | binary Variant`, with
the entry count written AFTER the body so a value that fails to encode cannot desync the reader.

## ITEM (3): `remove_visibility_filter` is genuinely missing at BOTH layers

No script arm (only `add_visibility_filter` at scripting.rs:1797) and no tree API (only
`synchronizer_add_visibility_filter` at scene_tree.rs:2873). It is a small additive change and
`Variant` derives `PartialEq`, so `retain(|f| f != &filter)` compares Callables correctly.

⚠️ While you are there: Godot's `visibility_filters` is a **HashSet**, so `add_visibility_filter` with
the same Callable twice is a no-op upstream. Ours `push`es to a `Vec` (:2881), so a filter added twice
runs twice per outbound pass. Worth deduping in the same edit.

`update_visibility` is the one item I would NOT add a route for yet: our outbound pass already recomputes
every tick, so a script route would be a call that does nothing — inert by construction.

## Why no code: leases

scripting.rs held by MagentaBrook to 13:44:32Z. scene_tree.rs was free, but I had just told BronzeLake
(msg 80006) it was theirs for a two-file atomic gesture change on pat-s3rrv.14 that cannot be split, so
taking it back 90 seconds later would have blocked the peer I had just unblocked. Items (1), (3) and (6)
all route through one or the other.

comments.text:
## ⚠️ Item (4) is BLOCKED ON ITEM (5), not leftover cruft (MagentaBrook, 2026-08-19 14:11 UTC)

Item (4) reads as a cleanup — "receiver still marks inbound spawns announced-at-birth" — and the code says so itself: the authority gate's comment at `scene_tree.rs:1189` states it "REPLACES a workaround: the receiver marks inbound spawns announced-at-birth purely to stop an echo cascade, which suppressed the symptom without expressing the rule."

I went to delete the workaround and stopped. **It is still load-bearing in one direction.**

### The gate covers server→client, and only that

`is_multiplayer_authority` (`:2996`) compares the local peer id against `get_multiplayer_authority`, which walks up for an explicit `multiplayer_authority` property and otherwise returns **`PeerId::SERVER`** (`:2968`, and `SERVER = PeerId(1)`).

- **Server → client.** On the client (`unique_id` 2 in the standard `create_pair(PeerId(2))` fixture), `2 == 1` is false, so the outbound diff skips the spawner and the client cannot echo. ✅ The gate expresses the rule; the workaround is redundant here.
- **Client → server.** The server IS the default authority for every node, so the gate does **not** fire. With the workaround removed, a spawn arriving from a client would be re-announced by the server — and the receiving client would apply it, diff it, and announce again. That is the unbounded echo the workaround exists to stop: one node per frame on both trees, for as long as the peers stay connected.

The reason the gate cannot cover that direction is **item (5)**: authority is not replicated between peers, so a client-authoritative spawner is authority-SERVER as far as the server is concerned. Until authority travels, "only the authority announces" cannot be evaluated correctly on the receiving side.

### So the ordering is fixed

**(5) before (4).** Deleting the workaround first trades a suppressed symptom for a live echo in a direction that has no test — and an echo that adds a node per frame is the kind of failure that looks like a memory leak or a desync rather than a replication bug.

Recording rather than doing: item (5) is a protocol addition (authority has to be carried on the spawn packet or a dedicated frame, and applied on arrival), and it deserves its own careful pass rather than being started as a prerequisite at the end of someone else's.

No code changed this pass. The workaround stays exactly where it is, and the comment at `:1189` is the one thing I would adjust when (5) lands — it currently reads as though the replacement is already complete.

title: Containers: wire SplitContainer divider drag and add ScrollContainer/TabContainer/AspectRatioContainer options
