comments.text:
## EmeraldIsland — step 1 (registration) landed; steps 2-6 still blocked on navigation.rs

### Landed

The four classes are registered in `class_db.rs` with their complete documented property sets, plus five tests in `gdobject/tests/nav_path_query_classes_registered.rs`.

Every name, default and accessor pair was **transcribed** from `doc/classes/NavigationPathQuery{Parameters,Result}{2D,3D}.xml`, not derived. That mattered immediately:

⚠️ **The getter is `get_simplify_path`, NOT `is_simplify_path`.** Godot uses the `is_` prefix for a great many bool getters — `is_editable`, `is_allow_unpress`, `is_showing_hidden_files` — and does not use it here. Deriving from the convention gives a plausible, wrong string. There is a test pinning it with that reasoning.

Two defaults that would fail *silently* if copied wrong, both now asserted:

- **`navigation_layers = 1`**, not 0. A zero mask matches no region, so every query through a default-constructed parameters object returns an empty path — which reads as a pathfinding bug, not a default.
- **`path_search_max_polygons = 4096`**, not 0. Zero means "no limit" for the three neighbouring caps (`path_return_max_length/radius`, `path_search_max_distance`), but this one is a real budget and 0 would refuse every search.

There is also a control test: the 2D/3D assertions run in a shared loop, which would pass if 3D had been registered as a copy of 2D, so one test asserts they differ exactly where Godot says — `Vector2`/`Vector3` and `PackedVector2Array`/`PackedVector3Array`.

### ⚠️ Finding for whoever does the rest of step 1

**ClassDB registration alone does NOT make these constructible from a script.** `Interpreter::classdb_instantiate` (`gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:8635`) branches:

- `is_parent_class(class, "Node")` → `scene_access.create_node`;
- **every non-Node class → it delegates to the expression `ClassName.new()`**, i.e. to the interpreter's ~30 bespoke handle arms, deliberately (pat-s3rrv.57 comment: "a bare refcounted handle would be worse than the Nil this used to return: an object that exists and answers nothing").

So `NavigationPathQueryParameters2D.new()` needs a real arm in `interpreter.rs`; the registration is the introspection half only. The Rust-side `class_db::instantiate` *does* build a `GenericObject` from the property table, which is what my test exercises — the two paths are different and it is easy to conclude from the Rust one that the script one works.

### Still blocked

Steps 2-6 all live in `navigation.rs`, held by MagentaBrook since 04:31 and unreleased. I asked for a ping when they drop it and explicitly told them not to release on my account — they are mid-edit, which is when a file should be left alone. I have released every duplicate row I took rather than leave a second HELD row.

The two pieces I would take first, in order: wiring `nav_simplify` (dead tested code, two fields plus two call sites), then the 3D corridor funnel (a port of the working 2D funnel at `:429-498`, replacing the centroid pushes at `:1812-1817` and `:1840-1845`).

title: AnimatedSprite2D: backwards playback, pause/set_frame_and_progress, and the animation_looped/animation_changed signals
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/animated-sprite-2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/animated_sprite_2d.cpp; extension_api.json AnimatedSprite2D methods play(name, custom_scale, from_end)/play_backwards/pause/stop/set_frame_and_progress/get_playing_speed and signals animation_changed/animation_looped/animation_finished/frame_changed/sprite_frames_changed

**Godot classes:** AnimatedSprite2D, SpriteFrames

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2360-2450 process_animated_sprites` covers autoplay, `speed_scale`, `frame`, `frame_progress`, `frame_changed` and `animation_finished`. It does not cover: backwards playback — `AnimatedSpritePlayback::advance` at `crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs:256-290` only ever increments (`self.frame + 1`) and multiplies `dt * self.speed_scale` without handling a negative scale, so `play_backwards()` / `from_end` cannot work; `animation_looped` and `animation_changed` are declared in ClassDB (`crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1248-1250`, `:6206-6208`) but never emitted (`grep -rn 'animation_looped' crates/gdscene/src` = 0); `set_frame_and_progress` and `get_playing_speed` have no binding (`grep -rn 'set_frame_and_progress' crates/` = 0); `pause()` (which freezes without resetting, unlike `stop()`) has no script binding.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `AnimatedSprite2D.play(name, custom_scale, from_end)` and `play_backwards(name)` run a clip in reverse (negative effective speed, wrapping from frame 0 to the last frame). `pause()` freezes on the current frame and progress without resetting; `stop()` resets. `set_frame_and_progress(frame, progress)` sets both atomically. `get_playing_speed()` returns the signed effective speed. The node emits `animation_looped` each time a looping clip wraps and `animation_changed` when the selected animation switches (upstream/godot/scene/2d/animated_sprite_2d.cpp).

PATINA: `crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2360-2450` already handles autoplay, `speed_scale`, `frame`, `frame_progress`, `frame_changed` and `animation_finished`. Missing: `crates/gdscene/src/sprite_frames.rs:256-290 AnimatedSpritePlayback::advance` only ever does `self.frame + 1` and accumulates `dt * speed_scale` with no negative-direction branch, so reverse playback is impossible; `animation_looped` and `animation_changed` are declared at `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1248-1250` and `:6206-6208` but never emitted (`grep -rn 'animation_looped' crates/gdscene/src` = 0); `set_frame_and_progress`, `get_playing_speed` and `pause` have no script bindings anywhere (`grep -rn 'set_frame_and_progress' crates/` = 0).

APPROACH: give `AnimatedSpritePlayback` a signed direction: let `speed_scale` be negative and, in `advance`, step `frame - 1` when negative, wrapping to `count - 1` on a looping clip and stopping at frame 0 otherwise; return an enum/flag distinguishing 'wrapped' from 'finished'. In `scene_tree.rs::process_animated_sprites`, emit `animation_looped` on the wrap flag and `animation_changed` when the resolved `animation` differs from the previous frame's. Add `play`/`play_backwards`/`pause`/`stop`/`set_frame_and_progress`/`get_playing_speed` bindings to `crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` alongside the AnimationPlayer bindings at `scripting.rs:2740`.

WIRING: `.tscn` with an AnimatedSprite2D and a script -> `MainLoop::step` -> `process_animated_sprites` -> `frame` and `texture` published -> `build_runtime_render_list` draws the reversed frame; signals reach connected script methods.

**Prove it:** A .tscn AnimatedSprite2D whose script calls `play_backwards("walk")` in `_ready()` shows a strictly DECREASING `frame` across successive `MainLoop::step` calls and wraps from 0 to the last frame on a looping clip, with the node's published `texture` matching the reversed frame each tick. A looping clip emits `animation_looped` exactly once per wrap to a connected script method. `pause()` freezes `frame` and `frame_progress` across further steps while `stop()` resets them. `set_frame_and_progress(2, 0.5)` is reflected in both properties on the next tick. (test: `animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn AnimatedSprite2D whose script calls `play_backwards("walk")` in `_ready()` shows a strictly DECREASING `frame` across successive `MainLoop::step` calls and wraps from 0 to the last frame on a looping clip, with the node's published `texture` matching the reversed frame each tick. A looping clip emits `animation_looped` exactly once per wrap to a connected script method. `pause()` freezes `frame` and `frame_progress` across further steps while `stop()` resets them. `set_frame_and_progress(2, 0.5)` is reflected in both properties on the next tick. (test: `animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test animated_sprite_2d_backwards_and_signals`.

title: Canvas2D: implement CanvasGroup compositing, BackBufferCopy screen texture, and MultiMeshInstance2D
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/canvas-compositing-2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/canvas_group.cpp, back_buffer_copy.cpp, multimesh_instance_2d.cpp; extension_api.json CanvasGroup{fit_margin, clear_margin, use_mipmaps}, BackBufferCopy{copy_mode, rect}, MultiMeshInstance2D{multimesh, texture}

**Godot classes:** CanvasGroup, BackBufferCopy, MultiMeshInstance2D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] All three are registered in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` but have zero behavior: `rg -n 'CanvasGroup|BackBufferCopy|MultiMeshInstance2D' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src crates/gdrender2d/src crates/patina-runner/src` (excluding the generated inspector schema) returns NOTHING. They are absent from the render-kind dispatch at `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:677-798`, so each one falls through to `Render2DKind::Marker` and draws an editor placeholder glyph at runtime. Godot uses CanvasGroup for grouped alpha/outline compositing and BackBufferCopy to feed `SCREEN_TEXTURE` to canvas_item shaders — with no BackBufferCopy, no 2D shader can read the screen behind it.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `CanvasGroup` renders its whole CanvasItem subtree into an offscreen buffer (grown by `fit_margin`, cleared by `clear_margin`, optionally mipmapped) and composites that buffer once, so `modulate`/alpha applies to the group rather than per child and shaders can operate on the flattened result. `BackBufferCopy` copies the current framebuffer region (`rect`, or the whole screen when `copy_mode = VIEWPORT`) into the back buffer that a canvas_item shader samples as `SCREEN_TEXTURE`. `MultiMeshInstance2D` draws a `MultiMesh` (per-instance transform/colour/custom data) with one `texture`, in a single batch.

PATINA: all three classes are registered in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` and have NO implementation anywhere — `rg -n 'CanvasGroup|BackBufferCopy|MultiMeshInstance2D' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src crates/gdrender2d/src crates/patina-runner/src` returns nothing outside the generated inspector schema. The render-kind dispatch at `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:677-798` has no arm for them, so each falls into the `Render2DKind::Marker` catch-all at `:796` and shows an editor placeholder in the running game. Without BackBufferCopy no 2D shader can read `SCREEN_TEXTURE` even though the canvas shader stack is otherwise wired (`crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:126` / `crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs`).

APPROACH: (1) In `build_runtime_render_list`, tag items whose ancestor is a CanvasGroup with a group id; in `rasterize_render_list`, rasterize each group into its own `FrameBuffer` sized by the group's item bounds grown by `fit_margin`, then blit that buffer once with the group node's `modulate`. (2) Add a `Render2DKind::BackBufferCopy { rect, copy_mode }` that, at its position in the sorted draw list, snapshots the framebuffer into a screen-texture slot the canvas shader path samples. (3) Add a `Render2DKind::MultiMesh { texture, instances: Vec<(Transform2D, Color)> }` fed from the `multimesh` sub-resource (flatten it in `crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs` alongside the existing `__viewport_mesh__` pass) and rasterize each instance through `gdrender2d::polygon_raster::fill_polygon_textured`.

WIRING: `.tscn` -> `build_runtime_render_list` -> `rasterize_render_list` -> a CanvasGroup with `modulate.a = 0.5` shows uniform half-alpha over overlapping children (not doubled alpha at overlaps), a BackBufferCopy makes SCREEN_TEXTURE non-black for a shader below it, and a MultiMeshInstance2D draws N quads.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a `CanvasGroup` (modulate alpha 0.5) over two overlapping opaque children renders the overlap region at the SAME alpha as the non-overlap region (proving one composite, not two blends). A .tscn with a `BackBufferCopy` above a red ColorRect and a canvas_item ShaderMaterial sampling SCREEN_TEXTURE renders a non-black sampled colour. A `MultiMeshInstance2D` with 3 instance transforms produces 3 drawn quads at the expected positions instead of a marker glyph. (test: `canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a `CanvasGroup` (modulate alpha 0.5) over two overlapping opaque children renders the overlap region at the SAME alpha as the non-overlap region (proving one composite, not two blends). A .tscn with a `BackBufferCopy` above a red ColorRect and a canvas_item ShaderMaterial sampling SCREEN_TEXTURE renders a non-black sampled colour. A `MultiMeshInstance2D` with 3 instance transforms produces 3 drawn quads at the expected positions instead of a marker glyph. (test: `canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test canvas_group_backbuffer_multimesh_2d_render`.

title: Node2D: compose skew into the local transform and honor CanvasItem.top_level in the global walk
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/node2d-transform-parity] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp `CanvasItem::get_global_transform` (top_level breaks the parent chain), scene/2d/node_2d.cpp `Node2D::_update_transform` (skew shears the Y basis: `Transform2D(angle, scale, skew, pos)`)

**Godot classes:** Node2D, CanvasItem

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:86-98 get_local_transform` composes only `translate * rotate * scale` — `skew` is never read, even though it is registered as a Node2D property at `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5947` and `gdcore::math::Transform2D::from_rotation_scale_skew_origin` already exists (`crates/gdcore/src/math.rs:674`) and is used by `crates/gdscene/src/canvas_layer.rs:179`. `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:102-120 get_global_transform` walks EVERY ancestor unconditionally; it never checks `top_level`, which is registered as a CanvasItem property at `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:6094` and asserted by `crates/gdobject/tests/canvas_item_classdb_properties.rs:30`. The 3D side does honor it (`crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:279 get_global_transform_top_level`), so this is a 2D-only omission: `grep -rn 'top_level' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs` yields hits only in `node3d.rs`. A `top_level = true` sprite (the standard 'detach from the parent's transform' idiom, e.g. for projectiles) still inherits its parent's transform, and a skewed Node2D draws unskewed.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `Node2D::_update_transform` builds the local matrix as `Transform2D(rotation, scale, skew, position)` — `skew` shears the Y basis relative to X (upstream/godot/scene/2d/node_2d.cpp). `CanvasItem::get_global_transform` stops climbing at any node whose `top_level` is set: that node's local transform IS its global transform, which is how detached projectiles, screen-space effects and parented-but-world-space nodes work (upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp).

PATINA: `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:86-98 get_local_transform` composes only `translated * rotated * scaled` and never reads `skew`, although the property is registered (`crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5947`) and `gdcore::math::Transform2D::from_rotation_scale_skew_origin` already exists at `crates/gdcore/src/math.rs:674` (used by `crates/gdscene/src/canvas_layer.rs:179`). `crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:102-120 get_global_transform` multiplies through the entire ancestor chain with no `top_level` check, while the 3D sibling `crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:279 get_global_transform_top_level` does implement it. So both properties round-trip through .tscn and the inspector but change nothing on screen.

APPROACH: read `skew` in `get_local_transform` and build the matrix via `Transform2D::from_rotation_scale_skew_origin(rotation, scale, skew, position)`, preserving the existing CanvasLayer-identity short-circuit at `node2d.rs:87-92`. Add `is_top_level_2d(tree, id)` and make `get_global_transform` break the ancestor walk at the first `top_level` node exactly as `node3d.rs:279-297` does. Sweep the derived helpers in the same file so they stay consistent: `get_global_rotation` (`:148`), `get_global_scale` (`:159`), `set_global_position` (`:126`), `set_global_rotation` (`:172`), plus `crates/gdscene/src/behavioral_2d.rs:78 global_scale_of`.

WIRING: `.tscn` -> `PackedScene` -> `build_runtime_render_list` (which calls `node2d::get_global_transform` at `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:362`) -> rasterized item transform.

**Prove it:** A .tscn where a Sprite2D with `top_level = true` sits under a Node2D at `position = Vector2(500, 500)` renders at world (0,0), while its `top_level = false` sibling renders at (500,500); the same sprite's `get_global_position()` read from a GDScript returns (0,0). A Node2D with `skew = 0.5` produces a rendered item transform whose basis is sheared (the y-column x-component is non-zero) and whose corner positions differ from an unskewed node. (test: `node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn where a Sprite2D with `top_level = true` sits under a Node2D at `position = Vector2(500, 500)` renders at world (0,0), while its `top_level = false` sibling renders at (500,500); the same sprite's `get_global_position()` read from a GDScript returns (0,0). A Node2D with `skew = 0.5` produces a rendered item transform whose basis is sheared (the y-column x-component is non-zero) and whose corner positions differ from an unskewed node. (test: `node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test node2d_skew_and_top_level_affect_scene_transform`.

title: Skeleton2D: add a 2D bone phase that poses Bone2D chains and skins Polygon2D
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/skeleton2d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp, polygon_2d.cpp (bone weights); extension_api.json Skeleton2D{get_bone/get_bone_count/get_skeleton/set_modification_stack/execute_modifications}, Bone2D{rest, get_index_in_skeleton, apply_rest, get_skeleton_rest, set_autocalculate_length_and_angle, ...}, SkeletonModification2D + CCDIK/FABRIK/Jiggle/LookAt/PhysicalBones/StackHolder/TwoBoneIK, SkeletonModificationStack2D | upstream/godot/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp, scene/2d/polygon_2d.cpp (`bones`, `skeleton`, `add_bone`, `internal_vertex_count`), scene/resources/skeleton_modification_2d*.cpp; doc/classes/Skeleton2D.xml, Bone2D.xml, Polygon2D.xml

**Godot classes:** Skeleton2D, Bone2D, SkeletonModificationStack2D, SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK, SkeletonModification2DLookAt, SkeletonModification2DCCDIK, SkeletonModification2DFABRIK, SkeletonModification2DJiggle, Polygon2D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] No runtime pose system exists. `crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs` (solve_two_bone_ik_2d) is referenced only by its `pub mod` at `crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:46` — `rg --type rust -l -F 'ik_solver_2d::' crates examples` is empty. `crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs:290-360` defines `Bone2D`, `Skeleton2D::skinning_transforms` and `deform_polygon_vertices`, none of which has a caller outside `crates/gdrender2d/tests/line_shading.rs` (verified with `rg --type rust -l -F deform_polygon_vertices crates examples`). The MainLoop skeleton phase is 3D-only: `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2986 crate::skeleton3d::process_skeletons` — there is no 2D equivalent. `Polygon2D`'s `bones`/`skeleton` properties are never read (`grep -rn '"bones"' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src` = 0). `SkeletonModification2D`, `SkeletonModification2DCCDIK/FABRIK/Jiggle/LookAt/PhysicalBones/StackHolder/TwoBoneIK` and `SkeletonModificationStack2D` are not registered at all (`grep -c 'ClassRegistration::new("SkeletonModification2D")' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` = 0), so a .tscn referencing them loses the nodes.
- [animation] The deformation math exists as a library-only module: `Bone2D`, `Skeleton2D`, `skinning_transform`, `skinning_transforms`, `deform_polygon_vertices` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs:290-370. Its `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` begins at polygon_raster.rs:373 and every `deform_polygon_vertices` call site is inside it (lines 541, 560, 585, 604, 625); `grep -rn 'deform_polygon_vertices|skinning_transforms|polygon_raster::Skeleton2D' --include=*.rs crates/` finds no caller outside that file. `engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs` (135 lines, the SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK core) has exactly one workspace reference — its own `pub mod ik_solver_2d;` at gdscene/src/lib.rs:46. There is no `Polygon2D` node implementation in gdscene at all (`grep -rn 'Polygon2D' crates/gdscene/src` matches only CollisionPolygon2D in physics_server.rs). Skeleton2D/Bone2D are registered in class_db.rs but the nine `SkeletonModification2D*` classes plus `SkeletonModificationStack2D` are unregistered (verified: `grep -c '"SkeletonModification2D"' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` → 0).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `Skeleton2D` collects its `Bone2D` descendants, holds their `rest` transforms, and each frame produces skinning transforms (`bone_pose * rest.affine_inverse()`) that a `Polygon2D` with a `skeleton` NodePath and per-vertex `bones` weights uses to deform its vertices (upstream/godot/scene/2d/skeleton_2d.cpp, polygon_2d.cpp). A `SkeletonModificationStack2D` assigned to the skeleton runs `SkeletonModification2D*` entries (TwoBoneIK, LookAt, CCDIK, FABRIK, Jiggle, PhysicalBones, StackHolder) after animation, in stack order, via `execute_modifications`.

PATINA: nothing runs. `crates/gdscene/src/ik_solver_2d.rs` (`solve_two_bone_ik_2d`) is only `pub mod`-declared at `crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:46` and never called. `crates/gdrender2d/src/polygon_raster.rs:290-360` already has `Bone2D`, `Skeleton2D::skinning_transforms()` and `deform_polygon_vertices()` — all dead outside `crates/gdrender2d/tests/line_shading.rs`. The MainLoop's skeleton phase at `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2986` calls only `skeleton3d::process_skeletons`. `Polygon2D.bones`/`skeleton` are read nowhere. The whole `SkeletonModification2D*` family and `SkeletonModificationStack2D` are unregistered in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, so those nodes vanish on scene load.

APPROACH: add `crates/gdscene/src/skeleton2d.rs` with `process_skeletons_2d(tree)`, modelled on `crates/gdscene/src/skeleton3d.rs`: walk each `Skeleton2D`, gather its `Bone2D` children with their `rest` and current `position/rotation/scale`, run the node's modification stack (call `ik_solver_2d::solve_two_bone_ik_2d` for TwoBoneIK; add LookAt and CCDIK inline), write the resulting poses back to the Bone2D nodes, and publish the skinning transforms on the Skeleton2D as an internal property. Call it from the skeleton phase in `main_loop.rs:2986`, right after `skeleton3d::process_skeletons`. In `crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs`, when a Polygon2D names a `skeleton`, run `polygon_raster::deform_polygon_vertices` over the published transforms before emitting `Render2DKind::Polygon`. Register `SkeletonModificationStack2D` and the seven `SkeletonModification2D*` classes in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`.

WIRING: `.tscn` with Skeleton2D > Bone2D chain + a skinned Polygon2D + a TwoBoneIK modification -> `MainLoop::step` skeleton phase -> bone poses written -> `build_runtime_render_list` emits deformed polygon vertices -> the drawn shape moves with the bones.

**Merged findings (2):** Skeleton2D / Bone2D / SkeletonModification2D stack and Polygon2D skinning; 2D skeletal animation — Skeleton2D/Bone2D pose propagation, Polygon2D bone weights/deformation, SkeletonModification2D stack

**Prove it:** A .tscn with `Skeleton2D > Bone2D > Bone2D` and a `Polygon2D` bound to that skeleton with per-vertex weights renders polygon vertices at their rest positions on frame 0; after a script rotates the root Bone2D by 45 degrees and one `MainLoop::step` runs, the emitted `Render2DKind::Polygon` points have moved by the corresponding skinning transform. A `SkeletonModificationStack2D` with a TwoBoneIK entry pointed at a target Marker2D bends the chain so the tip lands within 1px of the target. `SkeletonModificationStack2D` and `SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK` survive scene load as registered classes. (test: `skeleton2d_poses_bones_and_skins_polygon`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test skeleton2d_poses_bones_and_skins_polygon`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with `Skeleton2D > Bone2D > Bone2D` and a `Polygon2D` bound to that skeleton with per-vertex weights renders polygon vertices at their rest positions on frame 0; after a script rotates the root Bone2D by 45 degrees and one `MainLoop::step` runs, the emitted `Render2DKind::Polygon` points have moved by the corresponding skinning transform. A `SkeletonModificationStack2D` with a TwoBoneIK entry pointed at a target Marker2D bends the chain so the tip lands within 1px of the target. `SkeletonModificationStack2D` and `SkeletonModification2DTwoBoneIK` survive scene load as registered classes. (test: `skeleton2d_poses_bones_and_skins_polygon`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test skeleton2d_poses_bones_and_skins_polygon`.

title: Nodes3D: apply Camera3D near/far, keep_aspect, frustum_offset and h/v_offset in the Play viewport
description:
[audit-key: nodes-3d/nodes3d-camera] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp Camera3D::get_camera_projection / _update_camera_mode (near, far, keep_aspect KEEP_WIDTH/KEEP_HEIGHT, frustum_offset, h_offset, v_offset, environment, attributes, compositor)

**Godot classes:** Camera3D

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-3d] The wired camera builder /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:2091 `viewport_for_scene_camera` copies only the global transform, projection type and `fov`/`size`. Grep for `near`/`far` fields on the editor camera (gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs:69-106) shows the struct has `fov_degrees`, `ortho_size`, `override_transform` and no near/far plane at all — so Camera3D `near`/`far` never clip. `keep_aspect`, `frustum_offset`, `h_offset`, `v_offset`, `environment`, `attributes` and `compositor` are never read there. Correct implementations exist but are unused by this path: gdscene/src/camera3d.rs:518 get_frustum_offset, :535 get_keep_aspect, :569/:586 get_h/v_offset, :716 get_camera_projection.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/camera3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: Camera3D builds its projection from fov/size, near, far, keep_aspect (KEEP_WIDTH vs KEEP_HEIGHT decides which axis fov applies to), frustum_offset (FRUSTUM projection), and shifts the view by h_offset/v_offset; it can also override the world Environment/CameraAttributes/Compositor per camera (upstream/godot/scene/3d/camera_3d.cpp `get_camera_projection`, `_update_camera_mode`).\n\nPATINA: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:2091 `viewport_for_scene_camera` — the function that turns the scene's Camera3D into the Play view — copies only `override_transform`, the projection type, `fov` and `size`. The editor camera struct itself (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs:69-106) has no near/far fields at all, so `near`/`far` never clip anything: a mesh 5000 units away still draws with the Godot default `far = 4000`. `keep_aspect`, `frustum_offset`, `h_offset`, `v_offset`, `environment`, `attributes` and `compositor` are never read. The correct accessors already exist and are unit-tested in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/camera3d.rs (:518 frustum_offset, :535 keep_aspect, :569/:586 h/v_offset, :716 get_camera_projection returning a full Projection) — nothing on the wired path calls them.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: add `near`/`far`/`keep_aspect`/`frustum_offset`/`h_offset`/`v_offset` to the camera state in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d.rs, populate them in `viewport_for_scene_camera` (viewport_3d_render.rs:2091) from the camera3d accessors, and use `gdscene::camera3d::get_camera_projection` to build the projection matrix instead of the local half-fov math at viewport_3d.rs:1330/:1568 and viewport_3d_render.rs:820 `project_view`, so near/far clipping and aspect handling are shared. Resolve a per-camera `environment` sub-resource in `editor_render_environment` (viewport_3d_render.rs:1992), falling back to the WorldEnvironment as Godot does.\n\nWIRING: .tscn Camera3D -> game_camera_for_play / viewport_for_scene_camera -> render_game_3d_frame / render_editor_3d_frame_gpu; the Play view must frame the scene exactly as Godot's game window would.

**Prove it:** A .tscn Camera3D with `near = 2.0` and `far = 10.0` clips a mesh at distance 1 and a mesh at distance 20 out of the Play frame while keeping one at distance 5; setting `keep_aspect = KEEP_WIDTH` on a non-square viewport changes the framing versus KEEP_HEIGHT; `h_offset` shifts the image. (test: `camera3d_near_far_keep_aspect_offsets_frame_play_view`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn Camera3D with `near = 2.0` and `far = 10.0` clips a mesh at distance 1 and a mesh at distance 20 out of the Play frame while keeping one at distance 5; setting `keep_aspect = KEEP_WIDTH` on a non-square viewport changes the framing versus KEEP_HEIGHT; `h_offset` shifts the image. (test: `camera3d_near_far_keep_aspect_offsets_frame_play_view`)

title: Nodes3D: add VisualInstance3D sorting + remaining GeometryInstance3D properties to the shared instance settings
description:

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp (layers, sorting_offset, sorting_use_aabb_center, get_aabb) and GeometryInstance3D (gi_mode, gi_lightmap_texel_scale, ignore_occlusion_culling, set_instance_shader_parameter, visibility_parent on Node3D)

**Patina today:**

Per-surface material overrides are flattened only for index 0 (gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:467, :724; gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs:807 maps only `surface_material_override/0`).

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: VisualInstance3D exposes `sorting_offset` and `sorting_use_aabb_center`, which bias transparent-object draw order (upstream/godot/scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp); GeometryInstance3D adds `gi_mode` (DISABLED/STATIC/DYNAMIC), `gi_lightmap_texel_scale`, `ignore_occlusion_culling` and per-instance shader parameters via `set_instance_shader_parameter`; Node3D adds `visibility_parent` for visibility-range hierarchies; and `surface_material_override/N` applies per surface for every N.\n\nPATINA: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:1826 `geometry_instance_settings` — the one function both the editor viewport and the (currently dead) runtime adapter share for GeometryInstance3D — reads cast_shadow, visibility_range_begin/end and both margins, visibility_range_fade_mode, custom_aabb, transparency, lod_bias and extra_cull_margin, and stops there. Repo-wide non-test greps: `sorting_offset` 0 hits, `sorting_use_aabb_center` 0 hits, `instance_shader_parameter` 0 hits, `visibility_parent` 0 hits; `ignore_occlusion_culling` and `gi_mode` appear only as ClassDB registrations (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3213, :13780). Per-surface overrides are flattened only for surface 0 at load (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:467 and :724) and on save (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs:807), so a two-material mesh loses its second material silently.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: extend `GeometryInstanceSettings` and `geometry_instance_settings` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs with sorting_offset, sorting_use_aabb_center, gi_mode, gi_lightmap_texel_scale and ignore_occlusion_culling, and have the renderer's transparent sort key use the sorting fields. title: Register the Shape2D resource subtree in ClassDB (WorldBoundaryShape2D and its 8 siblings)
description:

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/2d/world_boundary_shape_2d.h + the Shape2D subtree; doc/classes/WorldBoundaryShape2D.xml — inherits Shape2D, members `normal: Vector2` default Vector2(0,-1) and `distance: float` default 0.0. **Patina today:**
- [sweep-7] Behaviour exists, registration does not. Implementation: engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs:48 defines the infinite half-plane and gdphysics2d/src/world.rs:1060 raycasts it; engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:313-317 constructs it from a .tscn sub-resource by matching the literal "WorldBoundaryShape2D" and reading normal (default Vector2(0,-1)) and distance (default 0.0). Registration absence: `grep -x` against the 4186 literals extracted from engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs = 0 hits for EVERY 2D shape resource — Shape2D, CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SegmentShape2D, SeparationRayShape2D, ConvexPolygonShape2D, ConcavePolygonShape2D, WorldBoundaryShape2D — while the 3D twins ARE registered (Shape3D, BoxShape3D, SphereShape3D, CapsuleShape3D, CylinderShape3D, ConvexPolygonShape3D, ConcavePolygonShape3D, HeightMapShape3D, SeparationRayShape3D, WorldBoundaryShape3D). Consequences: `ClassDB.class_exists("WorldBoundaryShape2D")` false (interpreter.rs:14922); `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()` from GDScript errors because interpreter.rs falls through to `is_node_class_name` (interpreter.rs:21256, a hardcoded node-name list that contains no shape resources) and then raises; the ClassDB-driven editor create/inspector paths (gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs) cannot offer the resource. Scene loading itself still works because gdscene/src/physics_server.rs matches the resource class STRING rather than consulting ClassDB.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** Godot 4.6.1 registers the whole 2D shape resource subtree: Shape2D (abstract, Resource) -> CircleShape2D (radius 10.0), RectangleShape2D (size Vector2(20,20)), CapsuleShape2D (radius 10.0, height 40.0), SegmentShape2D (a Vector2(0,0), b Vector2(0,10)), SeparationRayShape2D (length 20.0, slide_on_slope false), ConvexPolygonShape2D (points), ConcavePolygonShape2D (segments), WorldBoundaryShape2D (normal Vector2(0,-1), distance 0.0). Defaults from upstream/godot/doc/classes/*.xml.

**Patina today:** the physics behaviour is implemented and consumed — gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs:48 (half-plane), gdphysics2d/src/world.rs:1060 (ray vs half-plane), gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:313-317 (constructs from a .tscn sub-resource by matching the class STRING and reading normal/distance) — but NOT ONE of the nine classes is in ClassDB (0 hits each against class_db.rs's string literals), while every 3D twin is registered. So `ClassDB.class_exists("CircleShape2D")` is false, `ClassDB.instantiate` on any of them fails, `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()` from GDScript errors (interpreter.rs falls through to the hardcoded node-name list at interpreter.rs:21256), and the ClassDB-driven editor create/inspector paths (gdeditor/src/create_dialog.rs) cannot offer a shape resource. This is rung (a) missing beneath working rungs (b)-(c).

**Implement:** register the subtree in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs's 2D block (`register_2d_classes()` at class_db.rs:5732), mirroring the existing 3D shape registrations: Shape2D `.abstract_class()` with parent Resource plus `custom_solver_bias`, then the eight concrete leaves with their doc-XML property defaults. Then make script construction work: extend the GDScript `.new()` path in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs so a registered Resource class name yields a Variant::Resource with the ClassDB defaults, instead of falling through `is_node_class_name` (interpreter.rs:21256) to an error.

**Wiring requirement:** a script in a loaded scene can build `var s = RectangleShape2D.new()`, set its size, assign it to a CollisionShape2D and have gdscene/src/physics_server.rs produce the same collider it produces from a .tscn sub-resource; ClassDB introspection reports the full subtree; the editor's resource-creation path lists the shapes.

**Prove it:** an app-level test that both loads a .tscn using a WorldBoundaryShape2D sub-resource AND builds one from script, asserting identical physics behaviour and full ClassDB introspection.

**Prove it:** ClassDB reports Shape2D as abstract with parent Resource and reports CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SegmentShape2D, SeparationRayShape2D, ConvexPolygonShape2D, ConcavePolygonShape2D and WorldBoundaryShape2D with parent Shape2D and their doc-XML property defaults (WorldBoundaryShape2D.normal == Vector2(0,-1), distance == 0.0); and a GDScript that does `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()`, sets normal/distance and assigns it to a CollisionShape2D produces the same collision result as the equivalent .tscn sub-resource (test: `shape2d_resource_classes_registered`)
acceptance_criteria: ClassDB reports Shape2D as abstract with parent Resource and reports CircleShape2D, RectangleShape2D, CapsuleShape2D, SegmentShape2D, SeparationRayShape2D, ConvexPolygonShape2D, ConcavePolygonShape2D and WorldBoundaryShape2D with parent Shape2D and their doc-XML property defaults (WorldBoundaryShape2D.normal == Vector2(0,-1), distance == 0.0); and a GDScript that does `WorldBoundaryShape2D.new()`, sets normal/distance and assigns it to a CollisionShape2D produces the same collision result as the equivalent .tscn sub-resource (test: `shape2d_resource_classes_registered`)

[audit-key: physics-3d/collision-polygon-3d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** `CollisionPolygon3D : Node3D` (extension_api.json) with `polygon` (PackedVector2Array, the outline in the node's local XY plane), `depth` (float, default 1.0 — extrusion along Z), `disabled` (bool), `margin` (float, default 0.04), `debug_color`, `debug_fill`. As a child of a CollisionObject3D it contributes a convex-decomposed extruded prism to the body. See `upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/collision_polygon_3d.cpp`.

**Patina today:** the geometry is already implemented — `engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape3d.rs:24` defines `Shape3D::CollisionPolygon3D { vertices, depth }` with AABB at `:52`, support mapping at `:95` and unit tests at `:251-285`. _ready parses to an EMPTY/TRUNCATED body: that alone fits all three observations at once — has_method('_ready') true, the call does NOT raise (ran.is_some() passes), and zero statements execute so stage keeps its initialiser. title: Area2D: route audio_bus_override to the mixer when a player enters the area
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-area-audio] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json Area2D properties include audio_bus_override and audio_bus_name; upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/area_2d.cpp reroutes AudioStreamPlayer2D voices whose node is inside the area to the named bus. | upstream/godot/scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:485-500 (area override + _calc_reverb_vol), upstream/godot/scene/3d/area_3d.cpp (audio_bus_override/audio_bus_name/reverb_bus_enabled/reverb_bus_name/reverb_bus_amount/reverb_bus_uniformity) | upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/area_2d.cpp; extension_api.json Area2D signals body_shape_entered/body_shape_exited/area_shape_entered/area_shape_exited (args: rid, node, node_shape_index, local_shape_index) and properties audio_bus_override/audio_bus_name | extension_api.json — Area2D signals: body_shape_entered(body_rid, body, body_shape_index, local_shape_index), body_shape_exited, area_shape_entered, area_shape_exited (plus the shapeless body_entered/area_entered pairs). RigidBody2D also declares body_shape_entered/body_shape_exited. Emitted from upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/area_2d.cpp _body_inout / _area_inout.

**Godot classes:** Area2D, AudioStreamPlayer2D, Area3D, AudioStreamPlayer3D, RigidBody2D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-2d] The audio server implements the reroute: `AudioServer::redirect_stream_bus` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:302, documented at server.rs:297-301 as being for "`Area3D`/`Area2D` audio-bus override". Nothing calls it from the scene layer: `grep -rn "area_bus_override|set_area_bus|audio_bus" engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/` → 0 hits. `grep -rn "Area2D" engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/` returns only that doc comment; the only test exercising the reroute is the Area3D one at server.rs:948. The properties are registered on Area2D in ClassDB (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1362-1366) and read by the editor inspector, so authoring works and the runtime ignores them.
- [audio] `AudioServer::redirect_stream_bus` exists with a unit test (crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:299-313, exercised at server.rs:948-957) and Area2D/Area3D register `audio_bus_override` + `audio_bus_name` in ClassDB (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1358-1370 and :8032-8044), but NOTHING in gdscene ever calls it: `grep -rn "redirect_stream_bus" crates/gdscene crates/patina-runner` → zero hits, and `AudioServerBridge::process` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:162-219) performs no area-overlap query at all. Area3D's reverb surface is not even registered: `grep -rn "reverb_bus" crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` → no hits (the only matches in the workspace are comments in crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:948-949).
- [nodes-2d] `rg -n 'body_shape_entered|area_shape_entered' crates/` returns ZERO hits anywhere in the repo — the signals are not declared in `crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs`, not emitted, and not connectable. Patina emits only the shape-less pair: `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2820-2826` ('Emit body_entered / body_exited signals on Area2D nodes' / 'Emit area_entered / area_exited signals between overlapping Area2D'). A Godot scene whose `[connection]` targets `body_shape_entered` therefore silently connects to nothing. For audio: `audio_bus_override` is declared in ClassDB (`crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1362, 8038`) and `crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:299,948` implements the reroute for Area3D, but no 2D path reads it — `grep -rn 'audio_bus_override' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdeditor/src` = 0 — so an AudioStreamPlayer2D inside an overriding Area2D keeps its own bus.
- [physics-2d] `grep -rn "body_shape_entered|area_shape_entered|body_shape_exited|area_shape_exited" engine-rs/crates/` returns nothing outside the editor inspector/UI schema — the runtime never emits them. The shapeless pairs ARE emitted: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2821 (`process_overlap_signals`), :2826 (`process_area_overlap_signals`), :2831 (`process_body_contact_signals`). The shape-index variants have no backing because bodies carry a single shape (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:51) — so this is blocked on the multi-shape work — but a script connecting `body_shape_entered` today receives nothing at all, silently.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/area2d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: an Area2D with `audio_bus_override = true` reroutes every AudioStreamPlayer2D whose node is inside it to `audio_bus_name` (a reverb/echo bus) until the node leaves (upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/area_2d.cpp). This is the standard 2D room-reverb technique.

PATINA: the mixer half exists — `AudioServer::redirect_stream_bus` (engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs:302), explicitly documented for `Area3D`/`Area2D` override at server.rs:297-301 — and nothing in the scene layer calls it: `grep -rn "audio_bus" engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/` → 0 hits. The only test is the Area3D one at server.rs:948. The properties are registered on Area2D (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1362-1366) and shown in the inspector, so they look supported.

APPROACH: read `audio_bus_override` (bool) and `audio_bus_name` (String) into `gdphysics2d::area2d::Area2D` in `register_bodies`/`sync_to_physics` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:998-1040, where the other Area2D properties are read). In the overlap pass that already runs each physics tick (`process_overlap_signals`, called from engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2821), for every AudioStreamPlayer2D node whose global position falls inside an override area, call `AudioServerBridge` → `AudioServer::redirect_stream_bus(playback_id, bus)`; on exit restore the player's own `bus`. Where several overlapping areas claim the same player, the highest `priority` wins (Area2D::priority is already read at physics_server.rs:1040). The bridge is engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, already held by MainLoop (main_loop.rs:2170).

WIRING: MainLoop physics tick → area overlap pass → AudioServerBridge → AudioServer::redirect_stream_bus → the mixed output for that voice comes from the override bus.

**Merged findings (4):** Area2D audio_bus_override / audio_bus_name; Area2D/Area3D audio bus override and Area3D reverb bus routing; Area2D shape-index overlap signals and audio bus override; Shape-index collision signals: body_shape_entered/exited, area_shape_entered/exited

**Prove it:** An AudioStreamPlayer2D playing on bus "Master" that moves inside an Area2D with `audio_bus_override = true, audio_bus_name = "Reverb"` has its live playback reported on the Reverb bus after the next physics tick, and returns to Master when it leaves; a non-override area does not change the bus. (test: `area2d_audio_bus_override_reroutes_player`)
acceptance_criteria: An AudioStreamPlayer2D playing on bus "Master" that moves inside an Area2D with `audio_bus_override = true, audio_bus_name = "Reverb"` has its live playback reported on the Reverb bus after the next physics tick, and returns to Master when it leaves; a non-override area does not change the bus. (test: `area2d_audio_bus_override_reroutes_player`)

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json PhysicsServer2D exposes ~110 methods across shape creation (8 types), space (create/active/param/get_direct_state), area (30+), body (50+: mode/shapes/layers/params/state/forces/impulses/exceptions/contacts/test_motion/direct_state), joint (15) and free_rid/get_process_info. | extension_api.json: PhysicsServer2D = 119 methods, PhysicsServer3D = 175 methods, both api_type=core singletons listed in `.singletons[]`; PhysicsServer2DManager = 2 methods (register_server/set_default_server). doc/classes/PhysicsServer2D.xml, PhysicsServer3D.xml.

**Godot classes:** PhysicsServer2D, PhysicsServer3D, PhysicsServer2DManager

**Patina today:**
- [physics-2d] `call_physics_server_2d_method` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:6611 has exactly 9 arms — circle_shape_create, rectangle_shape_create, shape_set_data, body_create, body_set_space, body_add_shape, body_set_state, body_get_state, body_test_motion — with everything else falling to `RuntimeError::UndefinedFunction("PhysicsServer2D.{method}")` at interpreter.rs:6757. Missing entirely: `space_get_direct_state`, all `area_*`, all `joint_*`, `body_apply_impulse/force/torque` (server form), `body_set_param`/`body_get_param`, `body_set_collision_layer/mask`, `body_add_collision_exception`, `body_set_max_contacts_reported`, `body_get_direct_state`, and 6 of the 8 shape constructors (capsule/segment/world_boundary/separation_ray/convex/concave). `body_get_state` is itself partial — it returns Nil for every state except TRANSFORM (interpreter.rs:6715-6721). `PhysicsServer2D` is dispatchable as a singleton (BUILTIN_SINGLETONS, interpreter.rs:14477) but is NOT registered in ClassDB, so `ClassDB.class_exists("PhysicsServer2D")` is false.
- [sweep-4] NOT REGISTERED: `rg -n 'ClassRegistration::new("PhysicsServer2D|PhysicsServer3D|PhysicsServer2DManager"' engine-rs apps` -> 0 hits, so `ClassDB.class_exists("PhysicsServer2D")` is false.
2D IS PARTIALLY SCRIPT-REACHABLE: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2880-2882 routes `PhysicsServer2D.x()`, :6599-6758 `call_physics_server_2d_method` implements exactly NINE of 119 methods (circle_shape_create, rectangle_shape_create, shape_set_data, body_create, body_set_space, body_add_shape, body_set_state, body_get_state, body_test_motion); "PhysicsServer2D" is in BUILTIN_SINGLETONS (interpreter.rs:14464-14483).
3D IS ZERO: `rg -c 'PhysicsServer3D' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0. The Rust server exists and IS ticked (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:426 `pub struct PhysicsServer3D`, :1252 `step`; owned + driven by gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:448/609/1987), but no script can address it.
SINGLETON TABLE GAP: of Godot's 39 `.singletons[]`, only 8 are registered in Patina's ClassDB (GDExtensionManager, WorkerThreadPool, ThemeDB, EditorInterface, JavaScriptBridge, CameraServer, XRServer, and none of these three); PhysicsServer2DManager/PhysicsServer3DManager are absent from BUILTIN_SINGLETONS too, so `Engine.get_singleton_list()` cannot match Godot.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: PhysicsServer2D exposes ~110 methods — the whole RID-level physics API (extension_api.json). Scripts and plugins use it for server-side bodies, area setup, joint creation and `space_get_direct_state`.

PATINA: `call_physics_server_2d_method` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:6611) implements 9 arms — circle_shape_create, rectangle_shape_create, shape_set_data, body_create, body_set_space, body_add_shape, body_set_state, body_get_state, body_test_motion — and everything else raises UndefinedFunction (interpreter.rs:6757). `body_get_state` returns Nil for every state except TRANSFORM (interpreter.rs:6715-6721). The singleton is dispatchable (interpreter.rs:14477) but unregistered in ClassDB.

APPROACH: stage the surface by usefulness. Tier 1: the remaining 6 shape constructors (capsule/segment/world_boundary/separation_ray/convex_polygon/concave_polygon) over `Shape2D` (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/shape.rs:20), `space_get_direct_state` returning the object built for the direct-space-state bead, `body_set_collision_layer/mask`, `body_set_param`/`body_get_param` (BODY_PARAM_BOUNCE/FRICTION/MASS/INERTIA/CENTER_OF_MASS/GRAVITY_SCALE/LINEAR_DAMP/ANGULAR_DAMP), `body_apply_central_impulse` / `body_apply_impulse` / `body_apply_torque_impulse` / `body_apply_central_force` / `body_apply_force` / `body_apply_torque` over the existing `PhysicsBody2D::apply_*` methods (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:321-360), and the full `body_get_state` set (TRANSFORM/LINEAR_VELOCITY/ANGULAR_VELOCITY/SLEEPING/CAN_SLEEP). Tier 2: `area_create`/`area_set_space`/`area_add_shape`/`area_set_transform`/`area_set_param`/`area_set_monitorable` over `AreaStore` (engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/area2d.rs), and `joint_make_pin`/`joint_make_groove`/`joint_make_damped_spring`/`joint_set_param` over engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/joint.rs. Each arm needs a matching SceneAccess method in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/bindings.rs (default impl returning failure) implemented in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs. Also register `PhysicsServer2D` in ClassDB.

WIRING: script call → interpreter singleton dispatch → SceneAccess → PhysicsServer's live PhysicsWorld2D/AreaStore, with results visible on the next MainLoop physics tick.

**Merged findings (2):** PhysicsServer2D script singleton covers 9 of ~110 methods; PhysicsServer2D / PhysicsServer3D / PhysicsServer2DManager singletons

**Prove it:** A script creates a body via `PhysicsServer2D.body_create()`, gives it a capsule shape, sets its collision layer and mass through `body_set_param`, applies a central impulse, and reads a non-zero `body_get_state(rid, PhysicsServer2D.BODY_STATE_LINEAR_VELOCITY)` after a tick; `PhysicsServer2D.area_create()` + `area_set_param` produces an area whose gravity override affects a body; `ClassDB.class_exists("PhysicsServer2D")` is true. (test: `physics_server_2d_singleton_area_and_joint_api`)

title: Joints3D: add Generic6DOF motors/springs, slider motion params and per-bone ragdoll joint types
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-joint-motors] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** doc/classes/Generic6DOFJoint3D.xml (linear_motor_x/y/z {enabled,target_velocity,force_limit}, angular_motor_*, linear_spring_* and angular_spring_* {enabled,stiffness,damping,equilibrium_point}, per-limit damping/restitution/softness/erp/force_limit); doc/classes/SliderJoint3D.xml (linear_motion/*, linear_ortho/*, angular_motion/*, angular_ortho/*); doc/classes/PhysicalBone3D.xml joint_type + joint_constraints/*

**Godot classes:** Generic6DOFJoint3D, SliderJoint3D, HingeJoint3D, PhysicalBone3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] crates/gdphysics3d/src/joint.rs:492-496 documents the gap in its own words: "Motors and springs are a later addition; this holds the limits and the per-axis limit-excess helper". `Generic6DofJoint3D` (:497-510) carries only `linear_limits: [AxisLimit;3]` / `angular_limits`, and `AxisLimit` (:374-381) is `{enabled, lower, upper}` — no damping/restitution/softness/erp/force_limit. The bridge matches: crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:975-1013 reads only `linear_limit_{axis}/enabled|lower_distance|upper_distance` and `angular_limit_{axis}/enabled|lower_angle|upper_angle`, so all 36 motor/spring properties and the per-limit softness/restitution/damping are dropped. SliderJoint3D reads limits but no `linear_motion/*` or `*_ortho/*` (:924-953). Ragdolls ignore joint_type entirely: crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:731-734 always builds `Joint3D::Pin(...)`, acknowledged at :661-664 ("only JOINT_TYPE_PIN is modelled faithfully. Cone/hinge/slider/6DOF bones still receive a pin"), even though ClassDB registers the full JointType enum (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1856-1863).

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/joint.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: Generic6DOFJoint3D exposes, per linear and angular axis, a motor (`enabled`, `target_velocity`, `force_limit`) and a spring (`enabled`, `stiffness`, `damping`, `equilibrium_point`) on top of the limit's `softness`/`restitution`/`damping`/`erp`/`force_limit` — 36 motor/spring properties in total (doc/classes/Generic6DOFJoint3D.xml). SliderJoint3D adds `linear_motion/*`, `linear_ortho/*`, `angular_motion/*`, `angular_ortho/*` softness-restitution-damping triples. PhysicalBone3D chooses its parent constraint via `joint_type` (PIN/CONE/HINGE/SLIDER/6DOF) with `joint_constraints/*` sub-properties, which is what makes an elbow bend one way and a shoulder swing in a cone.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdphysics3d/src/joint.rs:492-496 states plainly that motors and springs are absent; `AxisLimit` (:374-381) carries only enabled/lower/upper. The scene bridge reads only the three limit keys per axis (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:975-1013), so every authored motor/spring is silently dropped. SliderJoint3D's motion/ortho params are never read (:924-953). Ragdolls always build a pin regardless of joint_type — crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:731-734, acknowledged in the doc comment at :661-664 — although ClassDB already registers the JointType enum (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1856-1863).\n\nAPPROACH: (1) extend `AxisLimit` in crates/gdphysics3d/src/joint.rs with softness/restitution/damping and add `AxisMotor { enabled, target_velocity, force_limit }` and `AxisSpring { enabled, stiffness, damping, equilibrium_point }` arrays to `Generic6DofJoint3D`; solve them in the Gauss-Seidel sweep in crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs (the joint solver at :86-370, `solve_joints`) as velocity-level targets clamped by force_limit, and springs as position-error impulses toward the equilibrium point; (2) add the slider motion/ortho triples to `SliderJoint3D` and apply them in the same solver; (3) read every new key in `build_joint` (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:871-1027) using the existing `float_prop_3d`/`truthy_prop_3d` helpers; (4) in `start_ragdoll_simulation` (:671-740) switch on the PhysicalBone3D node's `joint_type` and build the matching Joint3D variant with its `joint_constraints/*` values instead of the unconditional pin at :731-734.\n\nWIRING: joints are already synced from .tscn nodes each tick (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:639 `sync_joints`) and solved inside `PhysicsWorld3D::step`, driven by crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2841 — the new parameters must ride that same path.

**Prove it:** Driven only by MainLoop::step on loaded .tscn scenes: (a) a Generic6DOFJoint3D authored with `angular_motor_y/enabled = true`, `target_velocity = 2.0`, `force_limit = 100` spins its body-B about Y to within 10% of 2.0 rad/s and holds it, while the same scene with the motor disabled stays still; (b) a `linear_spring_y` with stiffness 100 and equilibrium_point 0 pulls a displaced body back to within 0.05 of the anchor plane; (c) a PhysicalBoneSimulator3D whose bones declare `joint_type = 3` (HINGE) with a ±0.2 rad limit keeps each bone's relative rotation inside that range after 2 simulated seconds, unlike the pin fallback which does not constrain rotation at all. (test: `physics3d_joint_motors_and_springs`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_joint_motors_and_springs`.
acceptance_criteria: Driven only by MainLoop::step on loaded .tscn scenes: (a) a Generic6DOFJoint3D authored with `angular_motor_y/enabled = true`, `target_velocity = 2.0`, `force_limit = 100` spins its body-B about Y to within 10% of 2.0 rad/s and holds it, while the same scene with the motor disabled stays still; (b) a `linear_spring_y` with stiffness 100 and equilibrium_point 0 pulls a displaced body back to within 0.05 of the anchor plane; (c) a PhysicalBoneSimulator3D whose bones declare `joint_type = 3` (HINGE) with a ±0.2 rad limit keeps each bone's relative rotation inside that range after 2 simulated seconds, unlike the pin fallback which does not constrain rotation at all. (test: `physics3d_joint_motors_and_springs`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_joint_motors_and_springs`.

title: Physics3D: wire SoftBody3D nodes from .tscn mesh to solver to rendered vertices
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-softbody] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp; doc/classes/SoftBody3D.xml; extension_api.json class SoftBody3D (parent MeshInstance3D)

**Godot classes:** SoftBody3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] A working mass-spring solver lives at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/softbody3d.rs (598 lines) and the world owns and steps them: crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:380 `soft_bodies: Vec<SoftBody3D>`, :520 `add_soft_body`, :573-575 `for sb in &mut self.soft_bodies { sb.step(dt, gravity) }`. SoftBody3D is registered in ClassDB (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1701, parent MeshInstance3D) and in the inspector schema (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5089). But `grep -rn "SoftBody\|soft_body" --include='*.rs' crates/gdscene crates/patina-runner crates/gdrender3d` returns ZERO hits — no scene bridge ever calls `add_soft_body`, so a .tscn SoftBody3D is a plain MeshInstance3D. The crate's own test header states this: crates/gdphysics3d/tests/softbody3d_sag.rs:16-18 — "physics3d_softbody_node requires scene-level wiring — a .tscn SoftBody3D whose mesh drives the solver and whose rendered vertices follow it — which is not implemented."

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/softbody3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: SoftBody3D extends MeshInstance3D. On NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE it builds a soft-body from the assigned `mesh`'s vertices/edges, honours `simulation_precision`, `total_mass`, `linear_stiffness`, `pressure_coefficient`, `damping_coefficient`, `drag_coefficient`, `collision_layer`/`collision_mask`, and `parent_collision_ignore`; `set_point_pinned(idx, pinned, attachment_path)` anchors vertices; each physics frame the solved vertex positions are written back through PhysicsServer3DRenderingServerHandler so the rendered mesh deforms (upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp).\n\nPATINA: the solver is complete and already stepped by the world — crates/gdphysics3d/src/softbody3d.rs, crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:520 (`add_soft_body`) and :573-575 (stepped inside `PhysicsWorld3D::step`). The class is in ClassDB (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1701). Nothing connects the two: grep for `SoftBody`/`soft_body` under crates/gdscene, crates/patina-runner and crates/gdrender3d yields zero hits, and crates/gdphysics3d/tests/softbody3d_sag.rs:16 documents the missing wiring explicitly.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs add `sync_soft_bodies(&mut self, tree)` called from `sync_to_physics` (:635) that, for each SoftBody3D node, resolves the node's `mesh` (the same `__mesh__*`/SubResource flattening `shape_from_node_3d` uses at :296-316) into vertex positions + structural edges and calls `world.add_soft_body`, mapping node_id <-> SoftBodyId3D like `node_to_body`; (2) read `total_mass`, `linear_stiffness`, `damping_coefficient`, `pressure_coefficient`, `drag_coefficient`, `simulation_precision` off the node each tick; (3) apply pinned points from the node's `_pinned_points` array; (4) in `sync_from_physics` (:1442) publish the solved vertex array back onto the node as the deformed mesh the 3D render path reads (crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs mesh collection).\n\nWIRING: MainLoop's physics tick already calls sync_to_physics/step/sync_from_physics (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2840-2842); the new pass must ride that path so the deformation is visible in the runner without any manual call.

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn whose SoftBody3D carries a 5x5 plane mesh with the two top corner vertices pinned and stepping MainLoop for 1 simulated second: (a) the unpinned centre vertex published back onto the node has sagged at least 0.05 units below its authored Y while the two pinned vertices are unchanged; (b) the mesh the 3D render collection reads for that node reports the sagged positions, not the authored ones. (test: `physics3d_softbody_node`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_softbody_node`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn whose SoftBody3D carries a 5x5 plane mesh with the two top corner vertices pinned and stepping MainLoop for 1 simulated second: (a) the unpinned centre vertex published back onto the node has sagged at least 0.05 units below its authored Y while the two pinned vertices are unchanged; (b) the mesh the 3D render collection reads for that node reports the sagged positions, not the authored ones. (test: `physics3d_softbody_node`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_softbody_node`.

title: Physics3D: drive VehicleBody3D/VehicleWheel3D from the scene tree into the real 3D world
description:
[audit-key: physics-3d/phys3d-vehicle] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/vehicle_body_3d.cpp; doc/classes/VehicleBody3D.xml, VehicleWheel3D.xml; extension_api.json classes VehicleBody3D (parent RigidBody3D), VehicleWheel3D (parent Node3D)

**Godot classes:** VehicleBody3D, VehicleWheel3D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-3d] A complete raycast-vehicle solver exists at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs (VehicleBody3D::step applies gravity, suspension, drive, brake, steering; add_wheel at :136) and is exported at crates/gdphysics2d/src/lib.rs:77. Both classes are registered in ClassDB with full property surfaces (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1641 VehicleBody3D parent RigidBody3D, :1661 VehicleWheel3D) and the editor inspector lists them (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5194-5195), and crates/gdobject/tests/vehicle_wheel_3d_property_surface_test.rs passes green on the property defaults. But NOTHING outside the module constructs one: `grep -rn "vehicle3d\|VehicleBody3D\|VehicleWheel3D" --include='*.rs' crates/` returns only crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs, its own test crates/gdphysics2d/tests/vehicle3d_drive.rs, class_db.rs and inspector_schema_generated.rs. The scene bridge crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs::body_type_for_class_3d (:37) does not know the class, so a .tscn VehicleBody3D registers as a plain body (or not at all) and its wheels are inert. It also builds on a second, parallel 3D world (crates/gdphysics2d/src/world3d.rs, body3d.rs, shape3d.rs, collision3d.rs) that no runtime path uses, not on gdphysics3d::PhysicsWorld3D.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: VehicleBody3D is a RigidBody3D whose VehicleWheel3D children raycast down `wheel_rest_length + wheel_radius` each physics tick; the suspension spring (suspension_stiffness, suspension_travel, suspension_max_force, damping_compression, damping_relaxation) pushes the chassis up, `engine_force`/`brake` drive the contact patch, `steering` rotates the front wheels, and `wheel_friction_slip`/`wheel_roll_influence` shape the tire model (upstream/godot/scene/3d/physics/vehicle_body_3d.cpp `_update_suspension`/`_resolve_single_bilateral`/`_update_friction`). Wheels expose is_in_contact(), get_contact_body(), get_skidinfo(), get_rpm().\n\nPATINA: the solver already exists — crates/gdphysics2d/src/vehicle3d.rs (VehicleBody3D::new :115, add_wheel :136, step applies gravity/suspension/drive/brake) — and both classes are in ClassDB (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1641, :1661) with an inspector schema (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5194). Nothing constructs it at runtime: the class is absent from `body_type_for_class_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:37) and from every call site outside crates/gdphysics2d/tests/vehicle3d_drive.rs. It is also built on the orphan gdphysics2d::world3d/body3d/shape3d stack, not gdphysics3d::PhysicsWorld3D, so it cannot interact with the bodies a scene actually contains.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) move the vehicle model into crates/gdphysics3d/src/vehicle3d.rs and re-express the wheel raycast on gdphysics3d::query::PhysicsRayQuery3D against PhysicsWorld3D bodies, so wheels ride real StaticBody3D/trimesh ground; (2) in crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs add a `sync_vehicles` pass alongside `sync_areas`/`sync_joints` (called from `sync_to_physics`, :635-639) that registers each VehicleBody3D as a Rigid body and reads its VehicleWheel3D children's authored props (engine_force, brake, steering, wheel_radius, wheel_rest_length, suspension_*, damping_*, wheel_friction_slip, wheel_roll_influence, use_as_traction, use_as_steering); (3) apply the per-wheel suspension/traction impulses to the chassis body inside PhysicsWorld3D::step (crates/gdphysics3d/src/world.rs:569) before contact resolution; (4) publish `_wheel_*` results back onto each wheel node in `sync_from_physics` (:1442) so is_in_contact()/get_skidinfo() are script-readable.\n\nWIRING: MainLoop physics tick (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2840-2842 sync_to_physics -> step -> sync_from_physics) must drive it end to end, so a .tscn with a VehicleBody3D + 4 VehicleWheel3D children over a StaticBody3D floor drives forward when a script sets engine_force.

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn containing a VehicleBody3D with four VehicleWheel3D children above a StaticBody3D box floor and stepping MainLoop at 60 Hz: (a) the chassis settles at suspension rest height instead of sinking through the floor; (b) after a script sets `engine_force = 200` for 2 simulated seconds the chassis global position has advanced along its forward axis by > 1.0 m; (c) `$Wheel.is_in_contact()` reads true from GDScript while grounded. (test: `physics3d_vehicle_body_scene`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_vehicle_body_scene`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn containing a VehicleBody3D with four VehicleWheel3D children above a StaticBody3D box floor and stepping MainLoop at 60 Hz: (a) the chassis settles at suspension rest height instead of sinking through the floor; (b) after a script sets `engine_force = 200` for 2 simulated seconds the chassis global position has advanced along its forward axis by > 1.0 m; (c) `$Wheel.is_in_contact()` reads true from GDScript while grounded. (test: `physics3d_vehicle_body_scene`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test physics3d_vehicle_body_scene`.

title: Crypto: implement RSA/X509 (keys, self-signed certs, sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt), construct CryptoKey/X509Certificate/HMACContext, and back generate_random_bytes with a CSPRNG
description:
[audit-key: platform-os/platform-os-crypto] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json classes[Crypto,CryptoKey,X509Certificate,HMACContext]; upstream/godot/core/crypto/crypto.cpp + crypto_core.cpp (mbedTLS CTR_DRBG backs Crypto::generate_random_bytes) | doc/classes/AESContext.xml + upstream/godot/core/crypto/aes_context.cpp — update() requires a multiple of 16 bytes, adds NO padding, chains CBC IV state across calls, and get_iv_state() returns the current chained IV

**Godot classes:** Crypto, CryptoKey, X509Certificate, HMACContext, AESContext

**Patina today:**
- [platform-os] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17092-17094 stubs the entire asymmetric half: `"generate_rsa" | "generate_self_signed_certificate" => Ok(Variant::Nil)`, `"sign" | "encrypt" | "decrypt" => Ok(Variant::PackedByteArray(Vec::new()))`, `"verify" => Ok(Variant::Bool(false))`. CryptoKey, X509Certificate and HMACContext ARE registered in ClassDB (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10899 HMACContext, :10926 CryptoKey, :10937 X509Certificate) so `ClassDB.class_exists` reports true and the inspector schema lists them, but none is constructible: `grep -c 'class_name == "HMACContext"|class_name == "X509Certificate"|class_name == "CryptoKey"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` = 0, while Expression/Thread/Mutex/Semaphore/RegEx/HashingContext/AESContext/Crypto all have handle constructors at interpreter.rs:3113-3141. Separately `Crypto.generate_random_bytes` is not cryptographically secure: engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs:413-421 draws from `crate::rng::randi()`, a wall-clock-seeded xorshift (engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/rng.rs:128-131), and the doc comment at crypto.rs:405-412 admits it — Godot backs the same call with mbedTLS CTR_DRBG.
- [platform-os] engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs:260-268 documents the divergence in-tree: "Godot's `AESContext.update()` does *no* padding: it requires the input to be a multiple of 16 and returns the raw blocks. This pads with PKCS7 on encrypt and strips it on decrypt." The CBC path (crypto.rs:280-311) constructs a fresh `cbc::Encryptor` from `self.iv` on every call, so two successive `update()` calls both start from the original IV instead of chaining — different ciphertext from Godot for any multi-call stream. `finish()` (crypto.rs:367-372) is a no-op that leaves state usable. The script binding compounds it: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17050 returns `"get_iv_state" => Ok(Variant::PackedByteArray(Vec::new()))`, so a ported script that saves and restores the IV state gets nothing back. Ciphertext produced by a Godot project therefore will not decrypt here and vice versa.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/rng.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/config_file.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `Crypto.generate_rsa(bits)` returns a CryptoKey; `generate_self_signed_certificate(key, issuer_name, not_before, not_after)` returns an X509Certificate; `sign(hash_type, hash, key)` / `verify(hash_type, hash, signature, key)` / `encrypt(key, plaintext)` / `decrypt(key, ciphertext)` do RSA over that key. `CryptoKey.save/load/save_to_string/load_from_string/is_public_only` and `X509Certificate.save/load/save_to_string/load_from_string` handle PEM. `HMACContext.start/update/finish` is the streaming HMAC. `Crypto.generate_random_bytes` is a CSPRNG (mbedTLS CTR_DRBG, upstream/godot/core/crypto/crypto_core.cpp).\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17092-17094 returns Nil / empty PackedByteArray / false for the whole asymmetric family. HMACContext, CryptoKey and X509Certificate are registered in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (:10899, :10926, :10937) but have no handle constructor in the `.new()` dispatch at interpreter.rs:3113-3141, so a script that does `X509Certificate.new().load(path)` gets an object with no working methods — registration without construction. `gdcore::crypto::generate_random_bytes` (engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs:413) pulls from the xorshift in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/rng.rs:128-131 seeded from SystemTime, so keys/nonces/session ids generated by a ported project are predictable.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: (1) Swap `generate_random_bytes` in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/crypto.rs onto `getrandom` (native) / crypto.getRandomValues (wasm) — the doc comment at crypto.rs:405-412 states this is the whole fix and needs no call-site changes — and expose the same source as `OS.get_entropy`. (2) Add RSA (rsa/rustcrypto) + X509 (x509-cert / rcgen) behind `gdcore::crypto`, implementing key generation, PEM save/load and PKCS#1v15 sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt. (3) Add handle constructors and instance dispatch for CryptoKey, X509Certificate and HMACContext in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs alongside the existing HashingContext/AESContext handles, and have `Crypto.generate_rsa`/`generate_self_signed_certificate` hand back those handles. (4) Keep the existing ClassDB registrations in sync with the real method arities.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a script in a loaded scene must be able to run the full Godot idiom — `var c = Crypto.new(); var k = c.generate_rsa(2048); var cert = c.generate_self_signed_certificate(k, "CN=patina"); var sig = c.sign(HashingContext.HASH_SHA256, hash, k); c.verify(...)` — and `k.save_to_string()` / `CryptoKey.new().load_from_string(pem)` must round-trip.

**Merged findings (2):** Crypto: RSA/X509 half (generate_rsa, generate_self_signed_certificate, sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt), CryptoKey/X509Certificate/HMACContext construction, and CSPRNG-backed generate_random_bytes; AESContext: block semantics diverge from Godot (PKCS7 padding added, no IV chaining across update(), get_iv_state empty)

**Prove it:** A scene script generates a 2048-bit RSA key, signs a SHA-256 digest and verifies it (true), verifies a tampered digest (false), round-trips the key and a self-signed certificate through save_to_string/load_from_string, and drives HMACContext start/update/finish to the same digest as `Crypto.hmac_digest`; two consecutive `Crypto.generate_random_bytes(32)` calls differ and do not repeat across a process restarted with the same wall clock. (test: `crypto_rsa_x509_and_csprng_reachable_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene script generates a 2048-bit RSA key, signs a SHA-256 digest and verifies it (true), verifies a tampered digest (false), round-trips the key and a self-signed certificate through save_to_string/load_from_string, and drives HMACContext start/update/finish to the same digest as `Crypto.hmac_digest`; two consecutive `Crypto.generate_random_bytes(32)` calls differ and do not repeat across a process restarted with the same wall clock. (test: `crypto_rsa_x509_and_csprng_reachable_from_script`)

title: ImmediateMesh / MeshDataTool / MeshTexture / MeshConvexDecompositionSettings absent; SurfaceTool has no script surface
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-mesh-authoring-resources] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/immediate_mesh.cpp, scene/resources/mesh_data_tool.cpp, scene/resources/texture.cpp (MeshTexture), scene/resources/mesh.cpp (convex_decompose + MeshConvexDecompositionSettings); doc/classes/ImmediateMesh.xml (surface_begin/surface_set_color/surface_set_normal/surface_set_uv/surface_add_vertex/surface_end/clear_surfaces), MeshDataTool.xml, MeshTexture.xml, MeshConvexDecompositionSettings.xml

**Patina today:**
