**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Four Mesh-adjacent resource classes have no implementation of any kind in Patina — `rg '\bImmediateMesh\b|\bMeshDataTool\b|\bMeshTexture\b|\bMeshConvexDecompositionSettings\b' crates/` hits only gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs (the editor's generated parent table at :4603/:4670/:4671/:4675, which is a property-schema fallback consulted by inspector_schema.rs:191, not ClassDB), and none appears in class_db.rs.

ImmediateMesh is the important one: `surface_begin(PRIMITIVE_LINES); surface_add_vertex(a); surface_add_vertex(b); surface_end()` per frame is the standard way to draw debug geometry, gizmos, trajectory previews and dynamic ribbons in 3D. Patina's editor 3D viewport needs exactly this idiom for its own gizmos.

The adjacent builder already exists and is equally unreachable: gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:41-59 `pub struct SurfaceTool` ("Procedural mesh builder mirroring Godot's SurfaceTool") is re-exported at gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:55 but is not in ClassDB either — so today there is no script path to build a mesh at runtime at all.

MeshDataTool (read/modify ArrayMesh vertices, edges, faces), MeshTexture (a Texture2D that draws a mesh) and MeshConvexDecompositionSettings (parameters for Mesh convex decomposition, used by the editor's Create Multiple Convex Collision Siblings) are lower value but complete the family.

4. clear_surfaces() empties it and the next frame renders nothing.
5. Calling surface_add_vertex outside a begin/end pair errors rather than silently appending, matching Godot.
6. SurfaceTool is constructible from GDScript and its begin/add_vertex/commit path produces an ArrayMesh usable by MeshInstance3D (test: `immediate_mesh_built_from_script_renders`)

title: Finish the PrimitiveMesh family: PointMesh/QuadMesh/RibbonTrailMesh + fix the QuadMesh-is-PlaneMesh alias
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-primitive-mesh-family] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/3d/primitive_meshes.h; doc/classes/PointMesh.xml (inherits PrimitiveMesh, single point primitive), doc/classes/QuadMesh.xml (inherits PlaneMesh, `orientation` overrides to FACE_Z=2 and `size` to Vector2(1,1)), doc/classes/PlaneMesh.xml (`size` default Vector2(2,2), `orientation` FACE_Y=1, plus center_offset/subdivide_width/subdivide_depth), doc/classes/RibbonTrailMesh.xml (12 methods, 6 properties).

**Godot classes:** PointMesh, QuadMesh, RibbonTrailMesh

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-5] ClassDB registers PrimitiveMesh + BoxMesh/SphereMesh/CapsuleMesh/CylinderMesh/PlaneMesh/PrismMesh (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:4199-4225) and nothing else; `rg -c '"PointMesh"|"QuadMesh"|"RibbonTrailMesh"' class_db.rs` -> 0 for each. PointMesh geometry IS implemented but unreachable: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs:134-138 `pub struct PointMesh` with a `generate()` exercised only by its own unit test at :344 — it appears in no dispatcher (`rg -n 'PointMesh' engine-rs/crates/ | grep -v inspector_schema` hits only extra_meshes.rs). QuadMesh is aliased to PlaneMesh in all three renderers and is wrong in both directions: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:1095 `"PlaneMesh" | "QuadMesh" => PlaneMesh::default().generate()`, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:308-313 same, and gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs:261-286 shows PlaneMesh has only `size` (default [2.0, 2.0]) and generates an XZ quad with normal UP — i.e. a QuadMesh renders 2x2 on XZ when Godot says 1x1 on XY (FACE_Z). The 2D path has the mirror-image bug: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:699-706 gives BOTH `Some("QuadMesh") | Some("PlaneMesh")` a hardcoded 1x1 quad under the comment "Godot's QuadMesh defaults to 1x1", so PlaneMesh draws at half its real size there. RibbonTrailMesh exists only in a doc comment (extra_meshes.rs:17 lists it as remaining work) — `rg -n 'RibbonTrail' engine-rs/crates/` finds no type.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

ClassDB registers 6 of Godot's 12 PrimitiveMesh subclasses (class_db.rs:4199-4225: Box/Sphere/Capsule/Cylinder/Plane/Prism). PointMesh, QuadMesh and RibbonTrailMesh are unregistered, and the way QuadMesh is currently faked produces wrong geometry for two classes at once.

QuadMesh is aliased to PlaneMesh in every renderer — gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:1095 and gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:308 both do `"PlaneMesh" | "QuadMesh" => PlaneMesh::default().generate()`. But gdserver3d/src/primitive_mesh.rs:261-286 shows PlaneMesh models only `size` (default [2,2]) and always emits an XZ quad with normal UP. Godot's PlaneMesh has `orientation` (FACE_Y default), `center_offset`, `subdivide_width` and `subdivide_depth`; QuadMesh overrides `orientation` to FACE_Z and `size` to Vector2(1,1). So today a QuadMesh in a scene renders 2x2 in the wrong plane. The 2D editor path has the opposite bug: viewport_2d_render.rs:699-706 gives both class names a hardcoded 1x1 quad, so a MeshInstance2D with a PlaneMesh draws at half size.

PointMesh geometry already exists at gdserver3d/src/extra_meshes.rs:134-138 with a passing unit test, but nothing dispatches it — it is a dead module. RibbonTrailMesh does not exist at all (extra_meshes.rs:17 lists it as remaining work).

Scope: add `orientation` (with the PlaneMesh.Orientation enum FACE_X/FACE_Y/FACE_Z), `center_offset`, `subdivide_width`, `subdivide_depth` to PlaneMesh generation; register PlaneMesh's real defaults and QuadMesh as a PlaneMesh subclass whose registered defaults are size Vector2(1,1) / orientation FACE_Z; register PointMesh (parent PrimitiveMesh) and route it in the mesh dispatchers to the existing extra_meshes::PointMesh; implement and register RibbonTrailMesh (size, sections, section_length, section_segments, curve, shape). Fix the 2D path to stop conflating the two.

**Prove it:** A test asserts `class_exists` + correct parents for PointMesh (PrimitiveMesh), QuadMesh (PlaneMesh) and RibbonTrailMesh (PrimitiveMesh), and that ClassDB reports QuadMesh `size == Vector2(1,1)` / `orientation == 2` against PlaneMesh `size == Vector2(2,2)` / `orientation == 1`. A geometry test builds a .tscn MeshInstance3D with a QuadMesh sub_resource, runs it through gdscene::render_server_3d's mesh resolution, and asserts the four vertices span x,y in [-0.5, 0.5] with z == 0 and normals along +Z (today they span x,z in [-1,1] with normal UP), and that a PlaneMesh resolves to a 2x2 XZ quad. A third asserts a MeshInstance3D whose mesh is a PointMesh resolves to a single-vertex mesh rather than the default cube, and that a MeshInstance2D with a PlaneMesh draws at 2x2 not 1x1 (test: `primitive_mesh_family_quadmesh_orientation_and_pointmesh_routing`)
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts `class_exists` + correct parents for PointMesh (PrimitiveMesh), QuadMesh (PlaneMesh) and RibbonTrailMesh (PrimitiveMesh), and that ClassDB reports QuadMesh `size == Vector2(1,1)` / `orientation == 2` against PlaneMesh `size == Vector2(2,2)` / `orientation == 1`. A geometry test builds a .tscn MeshInstance3D with a QuadMesh sub_resource, runs it through gdscene::render_server_3d's mesh resolution, and asserts the four vertices span x,y in [-0.5, 0.5] with z == 0 and normals along +Z (today they span x,z in [-1,1] with normal UP), and that a PlaneMesh resolves to a 2x2 XZ quad. A third asserts a MeshInstance3D whose mesh is a PointMesh resolves to a single-vertex mesh rather than the default cube, and that a MeshInstance2D with a PlaneMesh draws at 2x2 not 1x1 (test: `primitive_mesh_family_quadmesh_orientation_and_pointmesh_routing`)

title: Import dock: persist import options to .import sidecars and run a real reimport
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/import-dock-persist] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/docks/import_dock.cpp (_update_options, _reimport_attempt/_reimport_and_cleanup) + editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp (reimport_files); options come from ResourceImporter::_get_import_options and persist into the asset's .import [params] section | upstream/godot/editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp (`_reimport_file`, `_save_filesystem_cache`, `.godot/imported/` naming = `<basename>-<md5(path)>.<save_extension>`), editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp (`_save_ctex`), core/io/resource_uid.cpp (uid_cache.bin / `.uid` sidecars)

**Godot classes:** EditorFileSystem, ResourceImporter, EditorImportPlugin, ResourceImporterTexture, ResourceUID

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19192-19197 — `api_set_import_settings` body is literally `let _ = parse_json_body(body); send_json(stream, r#"{\"ok\":true}"#)` with the comment "persisting to a `.import` sidecar is future work". engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19199-19226 — `api_reimport` validates the extension and echoes `{"ok":true,"reimported":"<path>"}`; no importer runs, no artifact is written, the TextureCache is never invalidated. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19050-19180 — `api_get_import_settings` returns a hardcoded option list per extension (compression="VRAM Compressed", mipmaps=true, …); it never opens the asset's `.import` file, so the dock can never show what an option is actually set to. engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:9996-10050 — the served JS renders the options and POSTs every change to the discarding endpoint; the Preset menu only relabels the button client-side. This is behind GREEN tests: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/tests/editor_suite_b/editor_import_hooks_test.rs:74-125 asserts `importable`, preset names and that reimport "reports the path" for `res://hero.png` — a file that is never created on disk.
- [asset-import-pipeline] Grep for any writer of a `.import` sidecar or a `.godot/imported/` artifact across `engine-rs/crates/*/src` — patterns `godot/imported`, `write.*\.import`, `generate_import`, `\[remap\]` — returns ONLY readers/tests: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:62-100 (`resolve_import_artifact` reads a sidecar), importers.rs:643-676 (accessors), and test fixtures. Nothing constructs one. The FileSystem dock never scans for importable sources: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs only mentions "import" as a file-icon category (filesystem.rs:314) and as a directory to skip (filesystem.rs:178). engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/fs_import_pipeline.rs is a status-bookkeeping model whose `reimport()` (lines 145-155) sets `imported_version` and increments a counter without touching the filesystem, and it has zero callers (`grep -rn fs_import_pipeline crates/ --include=*.rs` → only `lib.rs:68 pub mod fs_import_pipeline;`). Consequence: a project authored in Patina has no `.import`, no `.ctex`, no `uid://` — Godot cannot open it, and Patina's own remap resolution only ever works on projects a real Godot editor imported.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/import_settings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/filesystem.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/fs_import_pipeline.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/uid.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `ImportDock::_update_options` reads the selected asset's `.import` file, asks the matching `ResourceImporter` for its option list/defaults/visibility, and shows the CURRENT values; `_reimport_and_cleanup` writes the edited values back into the `.import` `[params]` section and calls `EditorFileSystem::reimport_files`, which re-runs the importer, rewrites `.godot/imported/<name>-<md5>.<ext>`, and reloads every in-memory reference (upstream/godot/editor/docks/import_dock.cpp, editor/file_system/editor_file_system.cpp).\n\nPatina current state: `api_get_import_settings` (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs:19050-19180) synthesises a hardcoded option list from the file extension and never opens the asset's `.import`; `api_set_import_settings` (editor_server.rs:19192-19197) drops the body on the floor with the comment "persisting to a `.import` sidecar is future work"; `api_reimport` (editor_server.rs:19199-19226) validates the extension and echoes the path. The served dock JS (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:9996-10050) is fully built and calls all three, so the UI looks live and changes nothing. `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/fs_import_pipeline.rs:145-155` `reimport()` only flips an `ImportStatus` enum.\n\nImplementation approach: add a typed import-option model in `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs` (extend `ImportFile` with a parsed `[params]` map keyed by importer, plus a writer that serialises an `ImportFile` back to Godot's INI form). In `engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs`: have `api_get_import_settings` load `<source>.import` through `gdresource::load_import_file` and overlay the stored `[params]` on the importer defaults; have `api_set_import_settings` write the edited key into `[params]` and mark the asset stale via `fs_import_pipeline::ImportPipeline::set_setting`; have `api_reimport` invoke the real importer (see the artifact-generation bead), rewrite the `.import` `[remap] path`/`uid`, drop the `state.texture_cache` entry for that path, and return the new artifact path.\n\nWiring requirement: EDITOR_HTML dock → POST /api/import_settings → `.import` file on disk → POST /api/reimport → importer runs → `.godot/imported/*` artifact rewritten → texture cache invalidated → next GET /api/import_settings reports the persisted value.

**Merged findings (2):** Editor Import dock: option persistence + real reimport (ImportDock/EditorFileSystem::reimport_files); Import artifact generation: `.import` sidecars, `.godot/imported/` outputs, `.uid` sidecars on filesystem scan

**Prove it:** Starting the assembled editor server on a temp project containing a real `hero.png`: (1) GET /api/import_settings?path=res://hero.png reports the values currently stored in `hero.png.import` (not hardcoded defaults); (2) POST /api/import_settings with `{"option":"mipmaps","value":false}` causes `hero.png.import` on disk to contain `mipmaps=false` under `[params]`; (3) POST /api/reimport regenerates the artifact named by `[remap] path` (file mtime/content changes) and a subsequent GET reports `mipmaps=false`. (test: `import_dock_persists_options_and_reimports`)
acceptance_criteria: Starting the assembled editor server on a temp project containing a real `hero.png`: (1) GET /api/import_settings?path=res://hero.png reports the values currently stored in `hero.png.import` (not hardcoded defaults); (2) POST /api/import_settings with `{"option":"mipmaps","value":false}` causes `hero.png.import` on disk to contain `mipmaps=false` under `[params]`; (3) POST /api/reimport regenerates the artifact named by `[remap] path` (file mtime/content changes) and a subsequent GET reports `mipmaps=false`. (test: `import_dock_persists_options_and_reimports`)

title: Navigation: NavigationAgent2D/3D method surface + stop moving the agent node
description:
[audit-key: navigation/nav-agent-runtime-contract] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/NavigationAgent2D.xml:7-10 ("The calculation can be used by the parent node to dynamically move it along the path"; "After setting target_position, get_next_path_position must be used once every physics frame"); NavigationAgent2D/3D inherit `Node` (extension_api.json .classes[].inherits) and therefore have NO transform; 20 methods on NavigationAgent2D.xml:16-141 | extension_api.json NavigationAgent2D/3D signals: path_changed, target_reached, waypoint_reached(details: Dictionary), link_reached(details: Dictionary), navigation_finished, velocity_computed; doc/classes/NavigationAgent2D.xml documents waypoint_reached/link_reached firing when path_metadata_flags include the relevant types

**Godot classes:** NavigationAgent2D, NavigationAgent3D

**Patina today:**
- [navigation] Patina registers NavigationAgent2D at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7544-7645 and NavigationAgent3D at :1529-1618 with PROPERTIES AND SIGNALS ONLY — zero `.method(...)` entries (verified: `awk 'NR>=7544&&NR<=7646' class_db.rs | grep 'method('` = 0 hits). No node-method arms exist either: `grep -rn "get_next_path_position|is_navigation_finished|distance_to_target|get_current_navigation_path|is_target_reached|is_target_reachable|get_final_position|set_velocity_forced" engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/ engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs` = 0 hits. The dispatcher therefore falls to engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11209-11218, which raises `UndefinedFunction("ObjectId.get_next_path_position")`. `NavigationAgent2D.new()` also fails — interpreter.rs:21256-21285 `is_node_class_name` lists 27 classes, none navigation. Instead of the Godot contract, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1742-1747 (2D) and :1780-1785 (3D) WRITE `node2d::set_position` / `node3d::set_position` onto the NavigationAgent node itself, and engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs:222 gives NavigationAgent2D a Node2D-style default set so it has a `position` at all. The parent CharacterBody is never moved. Additionally, `process_navigation` (main_loop.rs:1688-1741) reads ONLY `target_position` (:1643) off the node — `path_desired_distance`, `target_desired_distance`, `max_speed`, `radius`, `path_height_offset` are never synced from the scene (AvoidanceNodeParams::apply, main_loop.rs:224-256, runs only in the avoidance phase and only when `avoidance_enabled` is true), so a .tscn tuning those values is ignored by path following.
- [navigation] Patina computes these milestones but never emits them. engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs:1019-1031 defines `NavAgentSignal::{PathChanged, WaypointReached, TargetReached, NavigationFinished, VelocityComputed}`; they are pushed at :1149 (PathChanged), :1163 (WaypointReached), :1174-1176 and :1282 — and drained only by `NavigationAgent2D::drain_signals` (navigation.rs:1299). `grep -rn "drain_signals" engine-rs/crates/ | grep -i nav` returns 0 non-navigation.rs hits (the matches are AnimationPlayer at scene_tree.rs:2206 and the multiplayer peers). The runtime emits only three signals by hand: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1749-1750 (`target_reached`, `navigation_finished`), :1787-1788 (3D twin) and :1363-1364 (`velocity_computed`). `link_reached` has no producer anywhere (`grep -rn "link_reached" engine-rs/crates/` matches only the class_db signal declarations). All six signals ARE declared in ClassDB (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, NavigationAgent2D block at :7634-7639 and NavigationAgent3D at :1604-1609), so `connect("waypoint_reached", …)` succeeds and then never fires. NavigationAgent3D does not even maintain a pending-signal list (navigation.rs:1334-1395 has no `pending_signals` field).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/navigation.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/doc/classes/NavigationAgent2D.xml:7-10, NavigationAgent3D.xml): NavigationAgent2D/3D inherit `Node`, have no transform, and NEVER move anything. The canonical usage is `var next = agent.get_next_path_position(); velocity = (next - global_position).normalized() * SPEED; move_and_slide()` inside `_physics_process`. The agent exposes 20 methods (get_next_path_position, is_navigation_finished, is_target_reached, is_target_reachable, distance_to_target, get_current_navigation_path, get_current_navigation_path_index, get_current_navigation_result, get_final_position, get_path_length, get_rid, set_velocity, set_velocity_forced, get/set_navigation_map, get/set_navigation_layer_value, get/set_avoidance_layer_value, get/set_avoidance_mask_value).\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:7544-7645 (2D) and :1529-1618 (3D) register properties+signals and ZERO methods. No dispatch arm exists in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs (node method table, :1242-1916) or in gdscript-interop, so a script call lands on engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11209-11218 and throws `UndefinedFunction`. Meanwhile engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1742-1747 and :1780-1785 integrate the agent and write `position` back onto the NavigationAgent node itself (given a position only by engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/class_defaults.rs:222), so the character body a Godot project actually parents the agent to never moves. `process_navigation` also reads only `target_position` (main_loop.rs:1643) — `path_desired_distance`, `target_desired_distance`, `max_speed`, `path_height_offset` set in a .tscn are inert during path following.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) register the full method list on both classes in class_db.rs next to the existing property/signal builders; (2) add a `navigation_agents` dispatch module reachable from `SceneAccess::call_node_method` in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs that resolves the node's backing `NavigationAgent2D`/`3D` in `MainLoop::nav_agents_2d/3d` (main_loop.rs:507-511) and answers each method, including path recomputation on `get_next_path_position` when the target moved; (3) split `process_navigation` (main_loop.rs:1498) into a *path maintenance* pass (rebuild map, recompute path, advance waypoint index, publish `next_path_position`) and REMOVE the `set_position` writes at :1743 and :1781 so the agent stops teleporting itself; (4) sync `path_desired_distance`, `target_desired_distance`, `max_speed`, `path_height_offset`, `navigation_layers` from the node each tick the same way AvoidanceNodeParams does (main_loop.rs:186-256).\n\nWiring requirement: .tscn with NavigationRegion2D + CharacterBody2D whose child NavigationAgent2D has a script calling `get_next_path_position()` in `_physics_process` → MainLoop::step → interpreter dispatch → real Vector2 → `move_and_slide()` moves the BODY across the navmesh; the agent node's own transform must not change.

**Merged findings (2):** NavigationAgent2D/3D script API (get_next_path_position, is_navigation_finished, is_target_reached/reachable, distance_to_target, get_current_navigation_path[_index], get_final_position, get_path_length, set_velocity[_forced], get/set_navigation_map, get_rid, get/set_navigation_layer_value, get/set_avoidance_layer/mask_value, get_current_navigation_result) + the "agent does not move anything" contract; NavigationAgent2D/3D signals path_changed, waypoint_reached, link_reached (and per-frame ordering of target_reached vs navigation_finished)

**Prove it:** Loading a .tscn where a CharacterBody2D's child NavigationAgent2D is driven by a GDScript `_physics_process` that calls `get_next_path_position()` and `move_and_slide()` moves the CharacterBody2D from start to target across a NavigationRegion2D, while the NavigationAgent2D's own `position` stays at its authored value; `is_navigation_finished()` returns false mid-route and true on arrival; `distance_to_target()` decreases monotonically; the same script pattern works for CharacterBody3D/NavigationAgent3D. (test: `nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a .tscn where a CharacterBody2D's child NavigationAgent2D is driven by a GDScript `_physics_process` that calls `get_next_path_position()` and `move_and_slide()` moves the CharacterBody2D from start to target across a NavigationRegion2D, while the NavigationAgent2D's own `position` stays at its authored value; `is_navigation_finished()` returns false mid-route and true on arrival; `distance_to_target()` decreases monotonically; the same script pattern works for CharacterBody3D/NavigationAgent3D. (test: `nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test nav_agent_script_api_moves_parent_body`.

comments.text:
AmberForge handoff — I briefly held this bead, made ONE substantive fix, then it was reassigned
away mid-work. The change is already in the working tree (uncommitted). Do not redo it; do not be
surprised by it.

DONE (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, both the 2D and 3D agent update blocks):
  Stopped the NavigationAgent node teleporting itself.

  Before: each tick ran `agent.step(current, dt, &others)` - an internal simulation of the agent
  walking its own path - then wrote that simulated point onto the agent node via
  node2d::set_position / node3d::set_position, and derived `next_path_position` from the SIMULATED
  point.

  Two bugs from that one line:
   (a) the agent node teleported away from its authored position and away from its parent body;
   (b) `next_path_position` advanced on the simulation's schedule, not as the body actually moved.

  After: no self-simulation and no write to the agent's transform. `next` is now
  `agent.get_next_path_position(*current)` - the agent's REAL position. That function already
  contains the whole mechanism (it consumes waypoints against the position handed to it and pushes
  WaypointReached), so feeding it the real position makes progress follow the body, which is
  Godot's passive-agent behaviour. The blocks now publish `next_path_position` only.

  rustfmt clean; `agent.step` has no remaining callers on these paths.

NOT DONE (the rest of the bead):
 1. ClassDB method surface. NavigationAgent2D (class_db.rs:7918) and NavigationAgent3D (:1632) are
    registered with PROPERTIES AND SIGNALS ONLY - zero `.method(..)` entries (verified: 0 hits).
    SceneTree's script dispatch gates on class_has_method, so get_next_path_position(),
    is_navigation_finished(), distance_to_target() etc. are ALL unreachable from GDScript. This is
    the same shape as pat-s3rrv.23 slice 1, which I closed green - see that registration for the
    pattern.
 2. Node-method dispatch arms in gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs + gdscene/src/scripting.rs.
 3. NavAgentSignal milestones are computed but never emitted: navigation.rs:1019-1031 defines
    PathChanged/WaypointReached/TargetReached/NavigationFinished/VelocityComputed and they are
    pushed at :1149/:1163/etc, but nothing drains pending_signals into emit_signal.
 4. Sync path_desired_distance / target_desired_distance / max_speed / path_height_offset /
    navigation_layers from the node each tick (the bead suggests mirroring AvoidanceNodeParams).
 5. The acceptance test itself.

⚠️ The acceptance is runtime movement over frames (body crosses a NavigationRegion2D while the
agent's own position stays authored). Useful prior: a body sitting at EXACTLY its spawn position
means the update loop never ran for it, not that the movement maths is subtly wrong - check
registration/dispatch first.

title: Honor MeshInstance3D.skin: load the Skin resource's binds instead of always synthesizing a rest skin
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-skin-resource-binds] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/skin.cpp + scene/3d/skeleton_3d.cpp (register_skin/SkinReference); doc/classes/Skin.xml; extension_api.json Skin(Resource, 11 methods), SkinReference(RefCounted, 2 methods)

**Godot classes:** Skin, SkinReference

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] The skinning MATH is real and wired: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/skin.rs:60 `pub struct Skin` + `skin_matrices`/`skin_mesh`, consumed each frame by /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:565 `gdserver3d::skin::skin_mesh(base, &skin, &poses)`. But the Skin RESOURCE is never read: `resolve_skin` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:661-670 unconditionally rebuilds a default skin from the skeleton rest (`for (bone, rest) in skeleton3d::bone_rest_array(...) { skin.add_bind_from_rest(bone, rest) }`) — it never looks at the MeshInstance3D's `skin` property. `Skin` and `SkinReference` are absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, so `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` in a .tscn cannot resolve; `class_db.rs:1086` only declares a `skin` PropertyInfo of `Variant::Nil` on the node. Consequence: any imported rig whose Skin carries non-rest inverse-bind matrices or name-based bone remapping (the normal glTF/Blender case) deforms with the wrong bind poses, silently.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/skin.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `Skin : Resource` holds an ordered bind list — `add_bind(bone, pose)`, `add_named_bind(name, pose)`, `set_bind_pose`/`get_bind_pose`, `set_bind_bone`/`get_bind_bone`, `set_bind_name`/`get_bind_name`, `clear_binds` (11 methods). `MeshInstance3D.skin` selects it; when null the skeleton supplies `create_skin_from_rest_transforms()`. `Skeleton3D.register_skin(skin)` returns a `SkinReference` (RefCounted) holding the resolved bone indices and the live bind matrix array. Source: `upstream/godot/scene/resources/skin.cpp`, `scene/3d/skeleton_3d.cpp`.

**Patina today:** the math is present and driven every frame — `crates/gdserver3d/src/skin.rs:60 Skin` with `skin_matrices`/`skin_mesh`, called at `crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:565`. But the resource is ignored: `resolve_skin` (`render_server_3d.rs:661-670`) always rebuilds a default skin from `skeleton3d::bone_rest_array` and never reads the MeshInstance3D's `skin` property. `Skin` and `SkinReference` are not in ClassDB (absent from the 638 registrations; `class_db.rs:1086` only declares a `skin` PropertyInfo of `Variant::Nil`), so `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` in a .tscn cannot resolve at all. Any imported rig whose Skin carries non-rest inverse-bind matrices or name-based bone remapping — the normal glTF/Blender case — therefore deforms with wrong bind poses and does so silently, since the rest-derived fallback always renders *something*.

**Implement:** register `Skin` (Resource) and `SkinReference` (RefCounted) in `class_db.rs`. Teach `resolve_skin` to take the MeshInstance3D node id, read its `skin` property (SubResource copy or `Variant::Resource`), and build the `gdserver3d::skin::Skin` from the resource's `bind/N/bone`, `bind/N/name` and `bind/N/pose` entries — resolving named binds against `Skeleton3D` bone names — falling back to the rest-derived skin only when `skin` is null. Add a `SkinReference` handle so `Skeleton3D.register_skin` is script-callable.

**Wiring requirement:** the per-frame 3D sync path must build its skin from the MeshInstance3D's Skin resource, so a .tscn rig with explicit binds renders with those binds in the runner and the editor viewport.

**Prove it:** an app-level test loading a .tscn with a Skeleton3D, a skinned MeshInstance3D and a `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` whose bind poses are deliberately NOT the rest inverses (e.g. one bind offset by a known translation), ticking a frame, and asserting the deformed vertex positions match the explicit-bind expectation and differ from the rest-derived fallback — the assertion must fail if `resolve_skin` reverts to the rest path. Also assert a named bind resolves to the right bone index.

**Prove it:** A .tscn MeshInstance3D with an explicit `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` whose bind poses differ from the skeleton rest inverses deforms its mesh using those binds after one frame (vertex positions match the explicit-bind expectation and differ measurably from the rest-derived fallback), and a named bind resolves to the correct Skeleton3D bone index (test: `mesh_instance_skin_resource_binds_drive_deformation`)
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn MeshInstance3D with an explicit `[sub_resource type="Skin"]` whose bind poses differ from the skeleton rest inverses deforms its mesh using those binds after one frame (vertex positions match the explicit-bind expectation and differ measurably from the rest-derived fallback), and a named bind resolves to the correct Skeleton3D bone index (test: `mesh_instance_skin_resource_binds_drive_deformation`)

title: Make SurfaceTool script-callable and complete its 33-method surface
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-surface-tool] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/surface_tool.cpp; doc/classes/SurfaceTool.xml; extension_api.json SurfaceTool(RefCounted, 33 methods)

**Godot classes:** SurfaceTool

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] A `SurfaceTool` exists in Rust — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:41-130 (`begin`, `add_vertex`, `add_index`, `commit`), re-exported at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:55 — but nothing script-facing can reach it: `SurfaceTool` is absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, and `rg -n 'SurfaceTool' crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` returns zero hits, so `SurfaceTool.new()` and `ClassDB.instantiate("SurfaceTool")` both fail (the interpreter's only `instantiate` arm, interpreter.rs:10219, rejects everything except PackedScene). Coverage is 5 of Godot's 33 methods: no `set_normal`/`set_uv`/`set_uv2`/`set_color`/`set_tangent`/`set_bones`/`set_weights`/`set_custom`/`set_smooth_group`, no `add_triangle_fan`, no `generate_normals`/`generate_tangents`/`generate_lod`, no `index`/`deindex`/`optimize_indices_for_cache`, no `append_from`, no `create_from`/`create_from_arrays`/`create_from_blend_shape`, no `commit_to_arrays`, no `set_material`/`set_skin_weight_count`/`set_custom_format`.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `SurfaceTool : RefCounted` is the procedural mesh builder scripts use — `begin(primitive)`, per-vertex attribute setters applied before `add_vertex` (`set_normal`, `set_tangent`, `set_color`, `set_uv`, `set_uv2`, `set_bones`, `set_weights`, `set_custom`, `set_smooth_group`), `add_vertex`, `add_index`, `add_triangle_fan`, `index`/`deindex`, `generate_normals(flip)`, `generate_tangents`, `generate_lod`, `optimize_indices_for_cache`, `append_from(mesh, surface, transform)`, `create_from(mesh, surface)`, `create_from_arrays`, `create_from_blend_shape`, `set_material`, `set_custom_format`, `set_skin_weight_count`, `commit(existing, flags) -> ArrayMesh`, `commit_to_arrays`, `clear` (33 methods total). Source: `upstream/godot/scene/resources/surface_tool.cpp`.

**Patina today:** a Rust `SurfaceTool` exists at `crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:41-130` with 5 operations (`begin`, `add_vertex`, `add_index`, `commit`) and is re-exported at `gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:55` — but no script can reach it. `SurfaceTool` is not in ClassDB (absent from the 638 `ClassRegistration::new` names) and appears nowhere in the GDScript interpreter (`rg -n 'SurfaceTool' crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` = 0 hits); the interpreter's only `instantiate` arm (`interpreter.rs:10219`) rejects every class except PackedScene. So `SurfaceTool.new()` fails and procedural mesh generation from GDScript — a very common game pattern — is impossible.

**Implement:** register `SurfaceTool` (parent RefCounted) in `class_db.rs`. Extend the Rust struct in `mesh.rs` with the staged per-vertex attribute setters, index/deindex, `generate_normals`/`generate_tangents`, `append_from`/`create_from`, `set_material` and `commit_to_arrays`, producing an `ArrayMesh`-compatible surface. Add an interpreter object type (mirroring how another RefCounted handle is already exposed) so `SurfaceTool.new()` returns a live handle whose method calls mutate it and whose `commit()` returns a Mesh resource assignable to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a played scene must be able to build a mesh with SurfaceTool, assign `commit()` to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`, and have the 3D render pass draw it that frame.

**Prove it:** an app-level test whose script begins a TRIANGLES surface, sets normals/UVs/colors per vertex, adds a two-triangle quad, calls `generate_normals`, commits to a MeshInstance3D, ticks a frame, and asserts the render instance carries 6 vertices with the expected UVs, per-vertex colors and the generated face normal.

**Prove it:** A GDScript in a played scene calls `SurfaceTool.new()`, builds a two-triangle quad with per-vertex normals/UVs/colors, calls `generate_normals()` and assigns `commit()` to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`; after one frame the 3D render instance carries 6 vertices with the expected UVs, per-vertex colors and generated face normal (test: `surface_tool_builds_mesh_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript in a played scene calls `SurfaceTool.new()`, builds a two-triangle quad with per-vertex normals/UVs/colors, calls `generate_normals()` and assigns `commit()` to a MeshInstance3D's `mesh`; after one frame the 3D render instance carries 6 vertices with the expected UVs, per-vertex colors and generated face normal (test: `surface_tool_builds_mesh_from_script`)

title: Rendering2D: BackBufferCopy node + SCREEN_TEXTURE sampling in canvas_item shaders
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/backbuffer-screen-texture] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: STUB]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/back_buffer_copy.cpp; RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_copy_to_backbuffer; canvas_item shader `hint_screen_texture` / SCREEN_TEXTURE + SCREEN_UV

**Godot classes:** BackBufferCopy, Shader, ShaderMaterial

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-2d] `BackBufferCopy` is registered in ClassDB with `copy_mode`/`rect` and its CopyMode enum (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:6383 and the assertions in crates/gdobject/tests/misc_canvas_nodes_register_and_wire.rs:89,126-134), but no renderer ever copies a backbuffer: `grep -rn 'BackBufferCopy' crates/ --include='*.rs'` outside class_db/tests returns nothing, and neither `collect_canvas_items` nor `rasterize_render_list_with_quality` has a BackBufferCopy arm. The canvas shader translator explicitly rejects the feature: crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1119-1123 pushes "`SCREEN_TEXTURE` / screen-buffer sampling" onto `unsupported_features`. crates/gdserver2d/tests/screen_uv.rs:12-14 records that the acceptance test `shader_screen_texture_sampling` does not exist.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `BackBufferCopy` copies the framebuffer (whole screen or its `rect`, per `copy_mode`) into the back buffer at its position in the draw order, and canvas_item shaders sample it via `uniform sampler2D screen_tex : hint_screen_texture` / the legacy `SCREEN_TEXTURE` with `SCREEN_UV` (upstream/godot/scene/2d/back_buffer_copy.cpp; RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_copy_to_backbuffer). This is how 2D distortion, blur and glass effects are built.

PATINA NOW: the class is registered with its properties and CopyMode enum (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:6383; asserted by crates/gdobject/tests/misc_canvas_nodes_register_and_wire.rs:89,126-134) and does nothing — no arm in `collect_canvas_items` or `rasterize_render_list_with_quality` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs). The shader translator refuses the feature outright: crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:1119-1123 adds "`SCREEN_TEXTURE` / screen-buffer sampling" to `unsupported_features`, and crates/gdserver2d/tests/screen_uv.rs:12-14 records that the acceptance test does not exist.

APPROACH: in the rasterizer, add a `Render2DKind::BackBufferCopy { rect: Option<Rect2> }` produced for `BackBufferCopy` nodes (COPY_MODE_DISABLED=0 emits nothing, RECT=1 copies `rect`, VIEWPORT=2 copies the whole frame). During `rasterize_render_list_with_quality`, on encountering that item, snapshot the current `FrameBuffer` region into a back-buffer texture stored alongside the frame. Extend the canvas shader evaluator (crates/gdserver2d/src/shader.rs) to bind that texture for `hint_screen_texture`/`SCREEN_TEXTURE` uniforms and to supply `SCREEN_UV` as the fragment's framebuffer-normalised coordinate, and remove the corresponding `unsupported_features` entry. This depends on the per-item ShaderMaterial reaching the Play rasterizer (`play-raster-material-state`).

WIRING: a .tscn with a BackBufferCopy followed by a Sprite2D whose ShaderMaterial samples SCREEN_TEXTURE must produce the distorted pixels in the served Play frame.

**Prove it:** A scene of [ColorRect(red), BackBufferCopy(copy_mode=2), Sprite2D with a canvas_item shader `COLOR = texture(screen_tex, SCREEN_UV + vec2(0.05,0.0))`] renders sampled red pixels shifted by 5% of the frame width; setting `copy_mode = 0` makes the shader sample an empty back buffer instead. (test: `backbuffer_copy_screen_texture_pipeline`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene of [ColorRect(red), BackBufferCopy(copy_mode=2), Sprite2D with a canvas_item shader `COLOR = texture(screen_tex, SCREEN_UV + vec2(0.05,0.0))`] renders sampled red pixels shifted by 5% of the frame width; setting `copy_mode = 0` makes the shader sample an empty back buffer instead. (test: `backbuffer_copy_screen_texture_pipeline`)

title: Rendering2D: CanvasTexture class + normal/specular 2D lighting
description:
[audit-key: rendering-2d/canvas-texture-class] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json CanvasTexture (diffuse_texture, normal_texture, specular_texture, specular_color, specular_shininess, texture_filter, texture_repeat); RenderingServer.canvas_texture_create/set_channel/set_shading_parameters

**Godot classes:** CanvasTexture

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-2d] `CanvasTexture` is absent from Patina's registered class list (checked against the audit's patina_registered.txt: 638 classes, `grep -x CanvasTexture` → no match) and from all sources: `grep -rn 'CanvasTexture' crates/ --include='*.rs'` matches only property-hint exclusion strings and one inheritance-table row in crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4369. Correspondingly the 2D light pass has no normal/specular input: `gdrender2d::light2d::light_factor_at` computes distance falloff only, and PointLight2D/DirectionalLight2D `height` is never read (crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs:98-130).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `CanvasTexture` bundles a diffuse, normal and specular map with `specular_color`/`specular_shininess` and per-texture filter/repeat; when a CanvasItem's texture is a CanvasTexture, 2D lights shade it with normal mapping and specular highlights using the light's `height` (extension_api.json CanvasTexture; RenderingServer.canvas_texture_create / canvas_texture_set_channel / canvas_texture_set_shading_parameters).

PATINA NOW: the class does not exist — it is absent from the ClassDB registration tables (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs; the audit's registered-class list has no CanvasTexture entry) and appears in the codebase only as a property-hint exclusion string and one inheritance-table row (crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4369). The 2D light pass has nowhere to read a normal from: `gdrender2d::light2d::light_factor_at` is distance falloff only and PointLight2D/DirectionalLight2D `height` is never collected (crates/gdscene/src/light2d_scene.rs:98-130).

APPROACH: register `CanvasTexture` (parent `Texture2D`) with its seven properties in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs; teach crates/gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs to flatten a `texture = SubResource("CanvasTexture_x")` into `__canvas_texture__{diffuse,normal,specular,specular_color,specular_shininess,texture_filter,texture_repeat}` companions; extend the texture lookup used by the Play rasterizer to resolve the diffuse channel for drawing and expose the normal channel to `shade_runtime_canvas`. In crates/gdrender2d/src/light2d.rs add a normal-map-aware variant of `light_factor_at` that takes a per-pixel normal and the light's `height`, computing N·L plus a Blinn-Phong specular term from `specular_color`/`specular_shininess`; fall back to the current flat behaviour where no normal map is present.

WIRING: an authored .tscn Sprite2D with a CanvasTexture and a PointLight2D must shade with visible normal-mapped relief in the served Play frame through `shade_runtime_canvas`.

**Prove it:** `ClassDB.class_exists("CanvasTexture")` is true and its property list matches Godot's seven members; a Sprite2D whose texture is a CanvasTexture with a hemispherical normal map, lit by a PointLight2D at height 32 offset to the left, is brighter on its left-facing pixels than its right-facing ones (a flat texture under the same light is uniform). (test: `canvas_texture_normal_specular_2d`)
acceptance_criteria: `ClassDB.class_exists("CanvasTexture")` is true and its property list matches Godot's seven members; a Sprite2D whose texture is a CanvasTexture with a hemispherical normal map, lit by a PointLight2D at height 32 offset to the left, is brighter on its left-facing pixels than its right-facing ones (a flat texture under the same light is uniform). (test: `canvas_texture_normal_specular_2d`)

title: Decals3D: sample the decal albedo/normal/orm/emission textures during projection
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/decal-textures] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/decal.cpp — texture_albedo/normal/orm/emission are projected onto geometry with albedo_mix, normal_fade, emission_energy and modulate

**Godot classes:** Decal

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] gdserver3d/src/decal.rs:260 `sample_alpha` computes `vertical_fade * distance_fade * albedo_mix` from the projected point and returns a scalar — it never indexes any texture. The software decal pass (gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:1081 `apply_decal_pass`) blends `decal.modulate` by that alpha, so the four texture channels are decoded, transported and discarded. The GPU path drops decals entirely (see the wgpu trait-gap finding).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/decal.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a Decal projects `texture_albedo` (blended by albedo_mix and modulate), `texture_normal` (blended by normal_fade against the surface normal), `texture_orm` (AO/roughness/metallic override) and `texture_emission` (scaled by emission_energy) onto every surface inside its oriented box, with upper/lower fade and distance fade. See upstream/godot/scene/3d/decal.cpp and doc/classes/Decal.xml.

Patina current state: only the box test and the fades are implemented. engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/decal.rs:260 `sample_alpha` returns `vertical_fade * distance_fade * albedo_mix` — a scalar computed from geometry alone, with no texture lookup anywhere in the function. The software pass gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs:1081 `apply_decal_pass` then blends the decal's flat `modulate` colour by that alpha. So `texture_albedo` is parsed off the node, decoded, carried into the renderer, and never read. (The GPU path is worse — it drops decals entirely; that is tracked separately as the wgpu RenderingServer3D trait-gap bead, which this one depends on for the GPU half.)

Implementation approach: (1) change `Decal3D::sample_alpha` into `sample(world_point, camera_distance) -> Option<DecalSample>` returning the projected (u,v) plus the sampled albedo RGBA, normal, ORM and emission from the decal's `TextureImage` channels, still folded with the fades and `albedo_mix`; (2) in `apply_decal_pass` blend the sampled albedo (times modulate) over the fragment, perturb the shaded normal by the sampled normal map weighted by `normal_fade`, override roughness/metallic from ORM, and add emission * emission_energy; (3) mirror the same sampling in the GPU decal pass added by the trait-gap bead so both backends agree.

Wiring requirement: Decal node with texture_albedo in a .tscn -> decal snapshot -> decal pass -> the texture's pattern visible on the receiving surface.

**Prove it:** A .tscn Decal with a two-colour checker `texture_albedo` projected onto a white floor renders that checker pattern on the floor (two distinct colours inside the decal footprint), where today the footprint is a single flat colour. An emission texture brightens only its lit texels. (test: `decal_texture_projects_pixels`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders through the editor 3D render path, and asserts at least two distinct colours inside the decal footprint and one outside.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn Decal with a two-colour checker `texture_albedo` projected onto a white floor renders that checker pattern on the floor (two distinct colours inside the decal footprint), where today the footprint is a single flat colour. An emission texture brightens only its lit texels. (test: `decal_texture_projects_pixels`) — loads the scene from a .tscn string, renders through the editor 3D render path, and asserts at least two distinct colours inside the decal footprint and one outside.

title: LOD3D: select mesh LOD by screen-space error and implement visibility-range margins + fade modes
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/lod] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/mesh.cpp surface LOD arrays + Viewport.mesh_lod_threshold; scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp visibility_range_*_margin + visibility_range_fade_mode (Disabled/Self/Dependencies)

**Godot classes:** Mesh, GeometryInstance3D, Viewport

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lod.rs defines `LodRange` (:47), `LodEvaluator` (:146), `LodGroup` (:258) and `LodLevel` (:264); `grep -rn "LodEvaluator|LodGroup|LodRange|lod::" --include=*.rs engine-rs/crates` outside that file returns NOTHING — no renderer, no scene bridge, no editor. `mesh_lod_threshold` appears only in gdserver3d/src/reflection_probe.rs (as a probe field), gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs, gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs (parse) and class_db.rs — never as an LOD selection. Godot's automatic per-surface LOD arrays are absent from `Surface3D` (gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:29). Hard visibility-range culling does exist in the software renderer (`is_within_visibility_range`, renderer.rs:426/:673) but the fade modes and margins do not, and the GPU path has no visibility_range reference at all.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lod.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/instance.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: each ArrayMesh surface can carry LOD index arrays with distance thresholds; the renderer picks the level whose screen-space error is under `Viewport.mesh_lod_threshold` (in pixels), scaled by the instance's `lod_bias`. Independently, GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_begin/end plus their `_margin` values and `visibility_range_fade_mode` (Disabled/Self/Dependencies) hard-cull or cross-fade an instance by camera distance. See upstream/godot/scene/resources/mesh.cpp and scene/3d/visual_instance_3d.cpp.

Patina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/lod.rs is a complete, tested LOD module (`LodRange` :47, `LodEvaluator` :146, `LodGroup` :258, `LodLevel` :264) with ZERO consumers — `grep -rn "LodEvaluator|LodGroup|lod::"` outside the file matches nothing at all. `mesh_lod_threshold` is parsed in gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs and registered in ClassDB but never drives a selection. `Surface3D` (gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:29) has no LOD index arrays, so there is nothing to select between. Hard visibility-range culling does work in the software renderer (`is_within_visibility_range`, renderer.rs:426 and :673) but the margins and fade modes are absent, and the GPU pipeline never checks visibility range at all.

Implementation approach: (1) add `lods: Vec<(f32, Vec<u32>)>` (threshold, index buffer) to `Surface3D` and populate it from the mesh importer/ArrayMesh loader; (2) call `LodEvaluator` from the instance-submit step in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs and gdrender3d/src/wgpu_pipeline.rs, passing camera distance, projected screen size and the viewport's `mesh_lod_threshold` + the instance's `lod_bias`, and draw the selected index buffer; (3) extend `GeometryInstanceSettings` (gdserver3d/src/instance.rs) with the two range margins and the fade mode, and implement the fade as an alpha ramp (Self) or a dependency ramp (Dependencies) rather than a hard cut; (4) apply visibility range in the GPU path too, as part of the `set_geometry_instance_settings` implementation.

Wiring requirement: a multi-LOD mesh + camera distance -> LodEvaluator -> the index buffer actually rasterised.

**Prove it:** A .tscn mesh authored with two LOD levels renders the high-detail index buffer when the camera is close and the low-detail one when far (observable as a different triangle/edge count in the frame), switching at the distance implied by `mesh_lod_threshold`. An instance with `visibility_range_end = 10` and `visibility_range_end_margin = 5` fades out across 5..10 units instead of popping. (test: `mesh_lod_selects_by_distance`) — renders the same scene at two camera distances through the editor 3D render path and asserts the selected level and the fade alpha.

An instance with `visibility_range_end = 10` and `visibility_range_end_margin = 5` fades out across 5..10 units instead of popping. title: ReflectionProbe3D: capture a real cubemap, honour update modes and apply box projection
description:
[audit-key: rendering-3d/reflection-probe] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/reflection_probe.cpp + servers/rendering/renderer_rd/environment/… (probe capture, UPDATE_ONCE/UPDATE_ALWAYS, box_projection, interior, origin_offset, intensity/blend_distance/max_distance/mesh_lod_threshold)

**Godot classes:** ReflectionProbe

**Patina today:**
- [rendering-3d] gdserver3d/src/box_projection.rs is 185 lines and `grep -rn box_projection` finds only: the `pub mod` at gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:9, the boolean field on ReflectionProbe (reflection_probe.rs:47/:78), the .tscn parse at gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1713, a ClassDB default (class_db.rs:2846) and inspector schema — no call into the module's math. `ReflectionProbeUpdateMode` is parsed at gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1741-1742 and then never branched on. gdserver3d/src/reflection_probe.rs is 217 lines with no cubemap render target at all: the probe contributes a flat ambient term (`sample_reflection_probes` in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs), never a captured environment, so a probe cannot mirror the scene.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/reflection_probe.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/box_projection.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: a ReflectionProbe renders the surrounding scene into a cubemap (once, or every frame when update_mode = ALWAYS), stores it in the reflection atlas, and reflective surfaces inside its `size` box sample it — with `box_projection` re-projecting the sample ray onto the box so reflections track the room's walls, `origin_offset` moving the capture point, `interior` suppressing sky contribution, and `intensity`/`blend_distance`/`max_distance`/`mesh_lod_threshold` controlling strength and falloff. See upstream/godot/scene/3d/reflection_probe.cpp.

Patina current state: the probe contributes a flat ambient colour only. engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/reflection_probe.rs (217 lines) has no cubemap target; `sample_reflection_probes` in gdrender3d/src/renderer.rs adds an ambient term, so a probe can never mirror geometry. `ReflectionProbeUpdateMode` is parsed from the .tscn at gdeditor/src/viewport_3d_render.rs:1741-1742 and then never branched on. Worst of all, gdserver3d/src/box_projection.rs (185 lines of box-projection math, with tests) has ZERO callers — `grep -rn box_projection` finds only the `pub mod` declaration (gdserver3d/src/lib.rs:9), the bool field (reflection_probe.rs:47), the .tscn parse (viewport_3d_render.rs:1713), a ClassDB default and the inspector schema. Enabling box projection in Godot and loading the scene changes nothing.

Implementation approach: (1) give the render server a small reflection cubemap atlas and a `capture_reflection_probe` step that renders the scene six times from the probe origin (+ origin_offset) at low resolution, gated by update_mode (ONCE = capture on first frame / on invalidation; ALWAYS = every frame, with a frame budget); (2) sample that cubemap by the reflection vector in the specular term of gdrender3d/src/shader.rs and the WGSL fragment stage, replacing the flat ambient approximation and blending by `intensity`, `blend_distance` and probe overlap; (3) call gdserver3d/src/box_projection.rs to correct the sample ray when `box_projection` is set; (4) suppress the sky/ambient contribution when `interior` is set.

Wiring requirement: ReflectionProbe node in a .tscn -> render inputs -> probe capture pass -> specular sample in both pipelines.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a mirror-like (metallic 1.0, roughness 0.0) plane inside a ReflectionProbe box surrounded by a red wall renders red reflection pixels on the plane; moving the wall changes where those pixels land when `box_projection = true` and does not when it is false; `update_mode = ONCE` keeps the captured reflection after the wall moves while `ALWAYS` updates it. (test: `reflection_probe_capture_render`) — renders each case from .tscn strings through the editor 3D render path and asserts the reflected-colour region.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a mirror-like (metallic 1.0, roughness 0.0) plane inside a ReflectionProbe box surrounded by a red wall renders red reflection pixels on the plane; moving the wall changes where those pixels land when `box_projection = true` and does not when it is false; `update_mode = ONCE` keeps the captured reflection after the wall moves while `ALWAYS` updates it. (test: `reflection_probe_capture_render`) — renders each case from .tscn strings through the editor 3D render path and asserts the reflected-colour region.

title: MissingResource is an orphaned module: no loader produces one, so unknown resources lose their data on round-trip
description:
[audit-key: resources/resources-io-missing-resource] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/missing_resource.cpp, core/io/resource_format_binary.cpp / scene/resources/resource_format_text.cpp substitution path; doc/classes/MissingResource.xml (original_class, recording_properties)

**Godot classes:** MissingResource

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] A real implementation exists at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/missing.rs:110 `pub struct MissingResource` with new():119 and a recording_properties surface documented at :131. Its ONLY references repo-wide are the module itself, the re-export at gdresource/src/lib.rs:63 (`pub use missing::{MissingNode, MissingResource, PreservedProperties};`) and its own unit test at missing.rs:178 — `rg -n 'MissingResource' crates/gdresource/src/*.rs` returns nothing from loader.rs, res_loader.rs or any other loader. No load path ever constructs one. The class is also absent from class_db.rs's string literals, while its SIBLING MissingNode IS registered (class_db.rs:4014-4019) and instantiable (gdobject/tests/scene_main_classes.rs:186 `instantiate("MissingNode")`), and the editor's generated inspector table lists both (gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4677-4678) — so ClassDB and the editor disagree about whether MissingResource exists, the same defect gdobject/tests/oos_native_sockets.rs:9-13 was written to fix for the socket classes.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/missing.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot substitutes a MissingResource for any sub/ext-resource whose class it cannot construct, recording original_class and every property verbatim, so that saving the scene back writes the original data unchanged. That is what makes a project safe to open in an editor that lacks a plugin's custom Resource types — exactly Patina's situation.

Patina has the struct and no producer. gdresource/src/missing.rs:110 defines MissingResource with the right shape (original_class + recorded properties, missing.rs:131), but the only references anywhere are the module, the re-export at gdresource/src/lib.rs:63, and its own unit test at missing.rs:178. No loader in gdresource/src/{loader.rs, res_loader.rs} constructs one.

The asymmetry with MissingNode makes the gap concrete: MissingNode IS registered (class_db.rs:4014-4019), IS instantiable (gdobject/tests/scene_main_classes.rs:186), and is used for unknown NODE types. Unknown RESOURCE types get no such treatment. Also, gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:4678 already claims ("MissingResource","Resource") exists while ClassDB says it does not — the same editor/ClassDB disagreement that gdobject/tests/oos_native_sockets.rs:9-13 was written to eliminate.

The taxonomy is explicit that the .tscn/.tres path must have "NO silent skips of unparseable values". This is one.

Work: register MissingResource (parent Resource) in ClassDB with original_class and recording_properties; wire the .tscn/.tres sub-resource and ext-resource paths in gdresource to substitute one when the class cannot be constructed, recording every property; make the saver write the recorded properties back under the original class name.

**Prove it:** 1. ClassDB registers MissingResource with parent Resource and the original_class / recording_properties members; class_exists("MissingResource") is true.
2. Loading a .tscn containing `[sub_resource type="MyPluginResource" id="1"]` with two properties yields a MissingResource whose original_class is "MyPluginResource" and which carries both property values.
3. Saving that scene back writes `type="MyPluginResource"` with both properties byte-identical to the input — a load/save round-trip of the fixture diffs clean.
4. The same holds for an unknown ext_resource reference.
5. The load does not error or drop the node/property that referenced it (test: `unknown_resource_round_trips_through_missing_resource`)
acceptance_criteria:
1. ClassDB registers MissingResource with parent Resource and the original_class / recording_properties members; class_exists("MissingResource") is true.
2. Loading a .tscn containing `[sub_resource type="MyPluginResource" id="1"]` with two properties yields a MissingResource whose original_class is "MyPluginResource" and which carries both property values.
3. Saving that scene back writes `type="MyPluginResource"` with both properties byte-identical to the input — a load/save round-trip of the fixture diffs clean.
4. The same holds for an unknown ext_resource reference.
5. The load does not error or drop the node/property that referenced it (test: `unknown_resource_round_trips_through_missing_resource`)
