Implementation: engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs:254-586 implements the session state machine and signal queue, and it IS script-reachable via XRServer.find_interface (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2150-2152, handle dispatch at :2211-2313, tag/identity at :17339-17365). But the browser binding is absent: `rg -n 'navigator\.xr|requestSession|isSessionSupported'` outside upstream/ and target/ returns ONLY doc comments (gdplatform/src/xr.rs:50,74,90,161,236,238,258 and interpreter.rs:2284 "Patina test seam. There is no real navigator.xr here"); xr.rs:244-252 defines `WebXrStub { supported_modes, available_features, force_failure }` and xr.rs:294 `set_stub()` is the only thing that can answer a session request; xr.rs:257-263 states outright "driven by a WebXrStub standing in for navigator.xr. The browser bindings (wasm32) would drive the same state machine". engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs declares only `canvas`, `audio`, `web_audio` — there is no xr module and no wasm-bindgen WebXR code anywhere. In scope per the taxonomy scope anchor (WebXR named explicitly as in-scope for the browser port).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: WebXR ships in Godot's web export (upstream/godot/modules/webxr/config.py:1-2). `WebXRInterfaceJS` calls `navigator.xr.isSessionSupported(mode)` and `navigator.xr.requestSession(mode, {requiredFeatures, optionalFeatures})` through godot_webxr.h, then per frame `process()` (webxr_interface_js.cpp:602) reads the XRFrame: view transforms/projections (`get_transform_for_view` :457, `get_view_count` :280), the reference-space pose (`get_camera_transform` :439), and input-source connect/disconnect + selectstart/selectend/squeezestart/squeezeend events which it forwards as Godot signals and as XRControllerTracker updates on XRServer.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs:254-580 already models this state machine correctly (feature resolution, reference-space fallback, session_failed, input sources, refresh rates) and gdplatform is natively tested. But nothing drives it from a browser. Its only input is `WebXrStub` (xr.rs:243-252) set via `set_stub` (xr.rs:294), whose only non-test caller is the `_set_test_stub` seam at engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2280-2300 — explicitly documented there as not a Godot method. `rg 'navigator\.xr|requestSession' crates/ apps/` finds no browser code; `rg -l 'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")' crates/gdplatform/src/` lists only js_bridge.rs and os.rs. The browser-event entry points (set_input_source, on_input_event, set_visibility_state, notify_reference_space_reset, set_available_display_refresh_rates) have no non-test callers, so an actual headset session is impossible.\n\nImplementation: add a `#[cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")]` backend module beside engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs (mirroring the pattern in engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs) that (1) resolves `navigator.xr`, (2) fulfils `is_session_supported` from `isSessionSupported`, (3) issues `requestSession` and resolves it into `WebXrInterface::initialize`'s existing success/fail paths, (4) subscribes to session `end`, `visibilitychange`, reference-space `reset`, `inputsourceschange`, `selectstart`/`selectend`/`squeezestart`/`squeezeend` and calls the matching `WebXrInterface` methods, and (5) exposes a `poll()` that the web frame loop calls each tick. Keep `WebXrStub` as the non-wasm/test backend behind the same trait so the native tests still run. Then call `poll()` + `drain_xr_signals` from the runtime frame tick (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs frame step, reached by engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs) so signals reach scripts every frame instead of only synchronously inside a script's own `initialize()` call — today the drain happens only at interpreter.rs:2325.\n\nWiring requirement: with a session running, a browser `selectstart` must reach a script's connected Callable through the frame loop with no script-side method call in between.

**Merged findings (3):** WebXR has no browser binding — the session state machine is driven only by a non-Godot `_set_test_stub`, never by navigator.xr; WebXRInterface script surface: input-source, refresh-rate, reference-space and all XRInterface base methods missing (platform code exists, no binding); WebXRInterface: unregistered and backed by a test stub instead of navigator.xr

**Prove it:** With the stub backend installed as the platform backend (not via the `_set_test_stub` script method), a loaded scene whose script connects `session_started`, `selectstart` and `session_ended` on `XRServer.find_interface("WebXR")` receives all three callbacks purely by advancing the MainLoop frame tick — proving the drain runs from the frame loop, not from the script's own call. `_set_test_stub` is removed from the script-visible method table. On wasm32 the module compiles against web-sys/js-sys `navigator.xr`. (test: `webxr_browser_session_binding`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test webxr_browser_session_binding`.
acceptance_criteria: With the stub backend installed as the platform backend (not via the `_set_test_stub` script method), a loaded scene whose script connects `session_started`, `selectstart` and `session_ended` on `XRServer.find_interface("WebXR")` receives all three callbacks purely by advancing the MainLoop frame tick — proving the drain runs from the frame loop, not from the script's own call. `_set_test_stub` is removed from the script-visible method table. On wasm32 the module compiles against web-sys/js-sys `navigator.xr`. (test: `webxr_browser_session_binding`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test webxr_browser_session_binding`.

title: XR nodes: drive XRNode3D/XRController3D/XROrigin3D transforms from XRServer trackers each frame
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/xr-nodes] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp:246-260 (_bind_methods), :329 (set_show_when_tracked), :373-401 (_bind_tracker / pose_changed connect), :426 (_pose_changed applies the pose), :215-228 (XRCamera3D connects tracker_added/updated/removed on XRServer); extension_api.json XRNode3D/XRController3D/XRAnchor3D/XROrigin3D

**Godot classes:** XRNode3D, XROrigin3D, XRCamera3D, XRController3D, XRAnchor3D

**Patina today:**
- [xr-peripheral] Registration exists and is otherwise correct: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1484-1506 (XROrigin3D world_scale/current, XRNode3D tracker, XRController3D, XRAnchor3D, XRCamera3D). Behaviour is absent everywhere: `rg -n 'XR' crates/gdscene/src` -> only 3 comment lines at crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:405-408; `rg -n 'world_scale|world_origin|reference_frame' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdrender3d/src crates/gdserver3d/src crates/patina-runner/src` -> 0 hits, so XROrigin3D.world_scale is inert; `rg -n 'is_button_pressed|get_has_tracking_data|get_is_active|show_when_tracked|get_pose\b|trigger_haptic_pulse' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0 hits, so none of XRNode3D's 10 methods, XRController3D's 5 methods + 5 signals, or XRAnchor3D's get_size/get_plane are dispatchable. XRNode3D is missing the `pose` and `show_when_tracked` properties in ClassDB (only `tracker` is registered, class_db.rs:1502). No per-frame XR update exists in crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs (`rg 'XR' crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs` -> 0 hits). The only green XR node test, crates/gdscene/tests/xr_camera_active.rs, asserts registration + that XRCamera3D is picked by the 3D camera lookup — nothing about tracking.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/scene/3d/xr/xr_nodes.cpp): XRNode3D holds a `tracker` StringName + `pose` name + `show_when_tracked`. On entering the tree it binds the tracker from XRServer and connects `pose_changed` (:373-401); `_pose_changed` (:426) writes the pose's transform into the node's local transform, scaled by XRServer world_scale, and toggles visibility when `show_when_tracked` is set. It exposes get_is_active/get_has_tracking_data/get_pose/trigger_haptic_pulse and emits `tracking_changed`. XRController3D adds is_button_pressed/get_input/get_float/get_vector2/get_tracker_hand and the button_pressed/button_released/input_float_changed/input_vector2_changed/profile_changed signals, all fed from the bound XRPositionalTracker's input map. XROrigin3D's `world_scale` writes XRServer::set_world_scale and `current` selects the active origin. XRCamera3D connects XRServer tracker_added/updated/removed in its constructor (:215-228) and takes the head pose.\n\nPatina current state: the classes are registered (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1484-1506) and nothing else. `rg 'XR' crates/gdscene/src` returns only three comment lines in crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs:405-408. No method of any XR node is dispatchable (`rg 'is_button_pressed|get_has_tracking_data|show_when_tracked' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> 0 hits), XROrigin3D.world_scale reaches nothing (`rg 'world_scale' crates/gdscene/src crates/gdrender3d/src crates/gdserver3d/src crates/patina-runner/src` -> 0 hits), and crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs has no XR step. The existing green test crates/gdscene/tests/xr_camera_active.rs only checks registration and camera selection.\n\nImplementation: add engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/xr_nodes.rs providing `update_xr_nodes(tree, delta)`: walk nodes whose class inherits XRNode3D, resolve `tracker` against the XRServer tracker registry (today engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:17213 XR_TRACKER_REGISTRY — lift it into a shared store gdscene can read, or expose a gdplatform-level registry both crates use), read the named pose, and write `transform = world_scale * pose.transform` onto the node via the existing Node3D transform path (crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs); apply `show_when_tracked` visibility and emit `tracking_changed` on transitions. Call it from the frame tick in crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs immediately before the render publish, in the same place skeleton modifiers run (main_loop.rs:2982). Add the XRNode3D/XRController3D/XRAnchor3D/XROrigin3D method dispatch to the node method table used by GDScript, and add the missing `pose`/`show_when_tracked` properties to class_db.rs:1500.\n\nWiring requirement: loading a .tscn containing XROrigin3D > XRController3D(tracker="left_hand"), registering a tracker with a pose on XRServer, and stepping the MainLoop must move the controller node in the scene — no Rust helper call in between.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with XROrigin3D > XRCamera3D + XRController3D(tracker="left_hand", show_when_tracked=true) is loaded; a script registers an XRControllerTracker named "left_hand" with a pose at (0.3, 1.2, -0.4); after one MainLoop frame step the XRController3D's global transform origin equals (0.3, 1.2, -0.4), and with XROrigin3D.world_scale = 2.0 it equals (0.6, 2.4, -0.8). Before any pose exists the node is hidden (show_when_tracked) and `get_has_tracking_data()` is false; after the pose arrives `get_is_active()` is true and `tracking_changed` fired exactly once. `XRController3D.is_button_pressed("trigger")` reflects the tracker's input map. (test: `xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with XROrigin3D > XRCamera3D + XRController3D(tracker="left_hand", show_when_tracked=true) is loaded; a script registers an XRControllerTracker named "left_hand" with a pose at (0.3, 1.2, -0.4); after one MainLoop frame step the XRController3D's global transform origin equals (0.3, 1.2, -0.4), and with XROrigin3D.world_scale = 2.0 it equals (0.6, 2.4, -0.8). Before any pose exists the node is hidden (show_when_tracked) and `get_has_tracking_data()` is false; after the pose arrives `get_is_active()` is true and `tracking_changed` fired exactly once. `XRController3D.is_button_pressed("trigger")` reflects the tracker's input map. (test: `xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test xr_nodes_track_pose_from_server`.

title: Canvas2D: collapse the dead gdscene::scene_bridge onto the shipped viewport_2d_render path
description:
[audit-key: nodes-2d/scene-bridge-dead-path] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp — there is exactly one canvas draw path in Godot; a second divergent one is a parity hazard | upstream/godot/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp (NOTIFICATION_DRAW / `queue_redraw` → `_draw` → item command list); extension_api.json CanvasItem._draw + queue_redraw | upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_webgl2.js + servers/rendering canvas renderer running unchanged under the web export | extension_api.json CanvasItem methods — 32 `draw_*` entries; upstream/godot/doc/classes/CanvasItem.xml | upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_cull.cpp:110-181 (`_collect_ysort_children`/`_count_ysort_children` flatten the WHOLE subtree of a `sort_y` item) and :437-458; extension_api.json CanvasItem.top_level + ClipChildrenMode (CLIP_CHILDREN_DISABLED/ONLY/AND_DRAW); RenderingServer.canvas_item_set_canvas_group_mode | upstream/godot/editor/plugins/canvas_item_editor_plugin.cpp — the 2D editor renders the live canvas through the same RenderingServer viewport as the game, with editor overlays composited on top | upstream/godot/servers/rendering/renderer_canvas_render.cpp — a CanvasItem's material shader runs for every primitive the item emits (rects, textured rects at any transform, polygons, lines, circles, glyphs), not only axis-aligned textured rects

**Godot classes:** CanvasItem, Sprite2D, Node2D, Control, RenderingServer, Viewport, CanvasGroup, CanvasLayer, ShaderMaterial, ColorRect, Polygon2D, Line2D, Label

**Patina today:**
- [nodes-2d] `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` documents itself as THE scene->canvas bridge ('nothing connected a live SceneTree to a Viewport of CanvasItems', `:1-35`) and implements `build_canvas_viewport` / `render_scene_to_frame`. It has NO production caller: `rg --type rust -l -F 'scene_bridge::' crates examples` returns nothing outside `crates/gdscene/tests/*` (canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs, particle_2d_scene_renders_moving_particles.rs, gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels.rs, script_draw_and_gui_input_virtuals.rs, canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs). The real path is `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` (called from `crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:177` and `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`). The two have already diverged: `scene_bridge.rs:287-311 draw_commands_for` handles only Sprite2D/AnimatedSprite2D/ColorRect/TextureRect/GPUParticles2D/CPUParticles2D and its `sprite_commands` (`:317-341`) ignores `region_enabled`/`region_rect`/`hframes`/`vframes`/`frame`/`flip_h`/`flip_v`, all of which `viewport_2d_render::sprite_sheet_for_node` (`:83-117`) does support; it also has no Line2D/Polygon2D/TileMapLayer/Path2D/Label arms. Tests that 'prove' 2D features end-to-end through `scene_bridge` therefore prove nothing about the shipped renderer.
- [rendering-2d] GDScript `draw_rect/draw_line/...` land in `SceneTree::push_draw_command` (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1669-1875) and are stored in `SceneTree::custom_draw_commands` (crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:255,3070-3101), flushed each frame by `MainLoop` (crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:3117). The ONLY consumer in the whole workspace is `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:310` (`grep -rn 'custom_draw_commands' crates/ examples/` returns exactly that one non-definition hit). `scene_bridge::build_canvas_viewport` / `render_scene_to_frame` have ZERO production callers (`grep -rn 'build_canvas_viewport\|render_scene_to_frame'` → only crates/gdscene/tests/*). The served editor's Play loop is examples/editor.rs:290-345, which calls `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` → `collect_canvas_items` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:334-447); that walk never reads `custom_draw_commands`. Ironically the RenderingServer script items ARE merged there (viewport_2d_render.rs:403-441), so `RenderingServer.canvas_item_add_rect` draws but `_draw` does not. The green test `crates/gdscene/tests/gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels.rs:67` asserts pixels through the dead `build_canvas_viewport` path, so the gap is invisible to CI.
- [web-runtime] The wasm build has no 2D renderer. crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:41-45 pulls in gdrender3d (with the `webgl` feature) and nothing else render-side; gdrender2d and gdserver2d are absent. The only draw operation exposed to JS is a clear: crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs:145-148 `present_clear(&self, r, g, b) -> bool`, driven by the harness at crates/patina-web/web/index.html:128. gdrender2d is a CPU rasterizer that emits BMP frames over HTTP for the editor preview (crates/gdrender2d/src/frame_server.rs:1-5, 290-300), i.e. a server-side path with no browser-canvas consumer. `rg 'gdrender2d|gdserver2d' crates/patina-web/` → 0 hits.
- [rendering-2d] Patina's dispatch table (crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:1675-1875) implements 14 names: draw_rect, draw_line, draw_circle, draw_polyline(+_colors), draw_multiline(+_colors), draw_dashed_line, draw_arc, draw_polygon, draw_colored_polygon, draw_texture, draw_texture_rect, draw_string. Absent (grep for each literal across crates/ returns nothing outside class_db/inspector schema): draw_ellipse, draw_ellipse_arc, draw_texture_rect_region, draw_msdf_texture_rect_region, draw_lcd_texture_rect_region, draw_style_box, draw_primitive, draw_string_outline, draw_multiline_string, draw_multiline_string_outline, draw_char, draw_char_outline, draw_mesh, draw_multimesh, draw_set_transform, draw_set_transform_matrix, draw_animation_slice, draw_end_animation. Parameters are dropped even on implemented calls: `draw_rect` ignores `width` for unfilled rects (scripting.rs:1675-1685); `draw_circle` ignores `filled`, `width`, `antialiased` (1706-1716); `draw_polyline_colors`/`draw_multiline_colors` collapse to the first colour (1725-1755, and the DrawCommand has one colour: crates/gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs:67-86); `draw_polygon` drops `uvs`+`texture` and per-vertex colours (1801-1819, canvas.rs:125-130); `draw_texture_rect` drops `tile` and `transpose` (1838-1849); `draw_string` drops `font`, `alignment` and `width` by its own comment (1850-1875). `DrawCommand` has only 11 variants (canvas.rs:42-182) — no mesh, multimesh, primitive, stylebox or set-transform representation exists.
- [rendering-2d] Y-sort: `canvas_order::draw_ordered_children` (crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs:93-111) sorts only the DIRECT children of a `y_sort_enabled` parent; each child's own subtree still emits contiguously in `push_draw_order` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:522-534). Godot instead flattens every descendant reachable through non-y-sorted children into ONE list and sorts them by their composed ysort transform. top_level: `node2d::get_global_transform` (crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs:102-120) multiplies the whole ancestor chain with no `top_level` check — the flag is implemented for 3D only (crates/gdscene/src/node3d.rs:254-317); `grep -rn 'top_level' crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` returns nothing. clip_children: `clip_rect_for` (crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:543-556) treats any non-zero mode identically, requires the ancestor to have a `size` property (so a Sprite2D/Node2D clip parent yields None), and clips to an axis-aligned rect rather than the parent's drawn alpha; the rasterizer implements it by snapshot-and-restore (viewport_2d_render.rs:1639). CLIP_CHILDREN_ONLY (parent used as mask, not drawn) is not distinguished from CLIP_CHILDREN_AND_DRAW. `CanvasGroup` is registered with its properties (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:6374-6380) but has no compositing anywhere (`grep -rn 'CanvasGroup' crates/ --include='*.rs'` → class_db + tests + create-dialog catalog only). In the `scene_bridge` path `clip_rect` is never set at all (crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs:116-136).
- [rendering-2d] The edit-mode viewport is a third, independent renderer: `scene_renderer::render_scene_inner` (crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:222-330+) walks nodes, sorts them by `effective_z_index` only, and draws per-class glyphs/markers, positioning each node with `node2d::get_global_position(...) * zoom + offset` — a translation-and-uniform-scale, so a rotated or non-uniformly scaled node draws axis-aligned. `grep -n 'collect_canvas_items\|build_render_list\|Render2DItem' crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs` returns nothing, so the edit view shares no code with the Play render list. `draw_sprite2d_with_texture` (scene_renderer.rs:693-760) reads only the node's OWN `modulate` (line 720-723), not `canvas_order::effective_modulate`, and applies no rotation. CanvasLayer ordering, `show_behind_parent`, Y-sort, clip_children and the 2D light pass are all absent from this path (they exist only in viewport_2d_render.rs).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/examples/editor.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/frame_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver2d/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/canvas_order.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/node2d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/draw.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: there is exactly one canvas draw path — the scene tree feeds `RenderingServer` canvas items once per frame. Two divergent Rust implementations guarantee they drift and let green tests certify the wrong one.

PATINA: `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` presents itself as the scene->canvas bridge and is exercised by five integration tests (`crates/gdscene/tests/canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs`, `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs`, `particle_2d_scene_renders_moving_particles.rs`, `gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels.rs`, `script_draw_and_gui_input_virtuals.rs`), but nothing in `src/` or `examples/` calls it (`rg --type gust -l -F 'scene_bridge::' crates examples` -> only tests). The shipped path is `gdeditor::viewport_2d_render::build_runtime_render_list` + `rasterize_render_list`, invoked from `crates/gdeditor/src/scene_renderer.rs:177-201` and `engine-rs/examples/editor.rs`. They have already diverged: `scene_bridge.rs:287-311` handles six classes and its `sprite_commands` at `:317-341` ignores region/hframes/vframes/frame/flip entirely, while `viewport_2d_render.rs:83-117` handles all of them; `scene_bridge` has no Line2D/Polygon2D/TileMapLayer/Path2D/Label arms at all.

APPROACH: pick `viewport_2d_render` as the single canvas path. Move the features `scene_bridge` uniquely carries — the CanvasItemMaterial/ShaderMaterial resolution at `scene_bridge.rs:126-282` and the `custom_draw_commands` append at `:310` — into `viewport_2d_render::render_kind_for`/`rasterize_render_list` if they are not already there, then delete `crates/gdscene/src/scene_bridge.rs` and repoint the five test files at `build_runtime_render_list`/`rasterize_render_list`. If the crate layering forbids `gdscene` depending on `gdeditor`, move `viewport_2d_render`'s collection half down into `gdscene` (it only needs `gdscene` + `gdrender2d`) and have `gdeditor` re-export it, so there is one collection function and one rasterizer.

WIRING: after the change, every 2D pixel test drives the same `.tscn -> collect -> rasterize` path the Game view and the editor example use; no second bridge exists to drift.

## Lead from AmberForge (pat-s3rrv.28 owner) — the failure is NOT in the render list

I do not own this bead and have not edited anything. Flagging because .22 blocks .28's remaining scope and I had the files open.

### Failing assertion

The `"ColorRect"` arm of `render_kind` (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1078) is UNCONDITIONAL — it always returns `Render2DKind::ColorRect { size, color }`. The only unusual thing in that scene is an EMPTY sub-resource: `[sub_resource type="ShaderMaterial" id="Mat_1"]` with no body, referenced as `material = SubResource("Mat_1")`. gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs:507-508 says the ShaderMaterial pass 'deliberately filters `material` to `ShaderMaterial`', and :725 filters sub-resource ids by type == "ShaderMaterial". ⚠️ packed_scene.rs is itself part of this bead's uncommitted WIP, so check it in the WORKING TREE, not HEAD — the verifier builds the working tree.

### Cheapest next step
Assert on the TREE, not the render list: after `add_packed_scene_to_tree`, check the Rect node exists and its `size`/`color` survived. That splits 'the node was dropped at load' from 'the node exists but produced no item' in one run, instead of re-guessing at the render layer.

comments.text:
## ROOT CAUSE FOUND (AmberForge) — missing ClassDB registration in the new tests, NOT an engine bug

Follow-up to my earlier lead. I have now CONFIRMED the cause by reading, and corrected one claim I made before.

### The cause
`collect_canvas_items` (gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:346) filters EVERY node through:

    if !node.is_class("CanvasItem") { return None; }

`Node::is_class` (gdscene/src/node.rs:315) falls through to `gdobject::is_parent_class`, i.e. a **ClassDB lookup**. ClassDB is NOT auto-populated in tests. With it empty, `ColorRect` is not known to inherit `CanvasItem`, so every node is filtered and `build_runtime_render_list` returns EMPTY — which is exactly the failing assertion 'a materialled ColorRect must still produce a render item'.

### Proof by reference test
Green gdeditor tests that use `build_runtime_render_list` all register first:
- crates/gdeditor/tests/camera2d_drives_runtime_canvas_transform.rs:62 -> `gdobject::class_db::register_2d_classes();`
- crates/gdeditor/tests/camera2d_scroll_drives_runtime_canvas.rs:32 -> same, and its comment even says it mirrors 'the register_*_classes() calls that the editor/runner make at startup'.

The new crates/gdeditor/tests/single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs registers NOTHING (its `load()` helper is from_tscn + add_packed_scene_to_tree only).

### THE FIX
Add `gdobject::class_db::register_2d_classes();` to the test's `load()` helper (and to any test in that file that builds a tree directly). This is a HARNESS fix — the .22 implementation may be entirely correct and has never been fairly exercised.

### ⚠️ Two more files have the same latent fault
`canvas_item_material_blend_in_play.rs` and `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels.rs` were MOVED into crates/gdeditor/tests/ and now call `build_runtime_render_list` with **0** registration calls. On the old scene_bridge path they never hit the `is_class` filter; on the surviving path they do. Expect them to fail the same way — fix all three together.

### CORRECTION to my earlier note
I previously wrote that those two material tests were 'deleted'. **That was wrong** — `git status` reports them as `RM` (renamed) from crates/gdscene/tests/ to crates/gdeditor/tests/. They exist and are the right starting point; do not rewrite them from scratch.

### Hypotheses I ELIMINATED so nobody repeats them
1. 'The render list drops materialled items' — NO. The `\"ColorRect\"` arm of `render_kind` (viewport_2d_render.rs:1078) is unconditional: no material check, no size guard, no early-out.
2. 'The empty `[sub_resource type=\"ShaderMaterial\"]` swallows the following [node] lines' — NO. packed_scene.rs routes property lines to `current` (the node) BEFORE `current_sub`, so node properties land correctly.
3. 'Visibility filtering drops it' — NO. `node2d::is_visible(` defaults to TRUE when the property is absent/Nil (node2d.rs:201).

## Handoff (EmeraldIsland): 5 of 6 green, and the last red is a SECOND real product bug — flip_h displaces an uncentred sprite

The bead was parked after two verifies, but it advanced a long way in them. Latest run: **6 tests, 5 passed, 1 failed.** Do not restart from the top.

### DONE and confirmed working — do not redo
1. **ClassDB registration in all five canvas tests.** AmberForge's root cause was right and their five-file scope correction was right. `single_canvas_path…`, `gdscript_draw_api_renders_pixels` and `script_draw_and_gui_input_virtuals` now call `gdobject::class_db::register_2d_classes()` before every `SceneTree::new()` (2, 2 and 10 sites); `canvas_item_material_blend_in_play` and `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels` were fixed earlier under .28. PROOF: `script_draw_reaches_pixels_on_the_shipped_path` and `canvas_item_shader_material_still_reaches_pixels` both PASS now, where they previously saw an empty render list.
2. **`frame_coords` precedence bug — FIXED.** `packed_scene::node_with_class_defaults` seeds every ClassDB default before the scene values land, and Sprite2D registers `frame_coords` default `Vector2i(0,0)` (class_db.rs:6701). `sprite_sheet_for_node` treated mere PRESENCE as "authored", so the seeded default beat the authored `frame` and pinned every sheet to cell 0 in any real project (the editor and runner both register at startup). Now only a NON-ZERO cell wins. Three regression tests cover it, all green.

### THE REMAINING RED — a genuine defect, not a test bug
`single_canvas_path_renders_sprite_sheet_and_shader.rs:125` — the PIXEL half. Got `Color { r: 0, g: 0, b: 0 }`, i.e. the BACKGROUND. Note the assert message guesses "draws the red first cell instead" — that guess is wrong and will mislead you: nothing is drawn at that pixel at all.

**Cause: `flip_h` mirrors about the NODE ORIGIN instead of about the sprite rect.** In `rasterize_render_list_with_quality`'s Sprite arm the flip is `Transform2D::scaled((-1, 1))` composed as `xform * flip`. With `centered = false` the local rect is `(0,0)..(4,4)`, so the mirror maps it to `(-4,0)..(0,4)` and the quad lands at screen x in [12,16) — the test samples (18,10), which is now background.

Godot never moves the destination: `Sprite2D::_get_rects` flips the SOURCE/UV and leaves the dest rect in place. A CENTRED sprite hides this completely, because its rect is symmetric about the origin — which is why this has survived until an uncentred fixture existed.

**Suggested fix** (mirror in place; identical behaviour for centred sprites):

    let c = rect.position + rect.size / 2.0;   // rect centre, local space
    let flip = Transform2D::translated(c)
        * Transform2D::scaled(Vector2::new(if flip_h {-1.0} else {1.0},
                                           if flip_v {-1.0} else {1.0}))
        * Transform2D::translated(-c);

For a centred sprite `c` is the origin, so this reduces to the current transform and cannot move an existing pixel. Add an uncentred `flip_v` case too — it has the same bug on the Y axis and nothing covers it.

### Housekeeping on the bead itself
- **The Acceptance line's command is broken:** the suggested invocation omits `-p gdeditor`, so it dies at cargo target resolution (exit 101, nothing compiled, no information). Always pass `-p gdeditor`. Please fix the bead text; agents keep copying it.
- **The `rg 'scene_bridge' returns no hits` criterion cannot be met literally.** It returns 5 hits, ALL prose — doc comments explaining the collapse, plus this bead's own test header asserting "the bridge is gone (rg scene_bridge returns no hits)", which is itself a hit. There are ZERO code references (no `use`, no `mod`, no `::scene_bridge`) and the module file is a staged deletion. That is a wording fix, not a code change.
- Never run green: `canvas_item_material_blend_in_play` and `canvas_item_shader_scene_pixels`. Worth running each with `-p gdeditor --test <name>` once this closes.

All my file reservations are released.

A parallel test file records the same gap (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/vhash_parity.rs:22 lists exactly these types as not covered). Because Dictionary key lookup uses this notion of hashing, a Dictionary keyed by NodePath or Transform degenerates to a single bucket and `Array.hash()`/`Dictionary.hash()` are additionally not even exposed to GDScript (absent from the Array/Dictionary method tables at interpreter.rs:7800-8126 / 8537-8671).

PATINA CURRENT STATE: engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/hash.rs:186-378 handles 25 kinds and then falls back to `_ => 0` at line 379; the comment at 370-378 states outright that the remaining types are not covered, and engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/vhash_parity.rs:22 records the same list. NodePath, Transform2D, Transform3D, Basis, ObjectId, Resource, Callable and Signal therefore all hash to 0, which collapses any Dictionary keyed by those types into one bucket and makes cross-engine hash parity wrong. `Array.hash()` and `Dictionary.hash()` are also not callable from GDScript — neither name appears in the Array table (interpreter.rs:7800-8126) or the Dictionary table (interpreter.rs:8537-8671).

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: extend `recursive_hash` in gdvariant/src/hash.rs with the remaining arms, reading the exact murmur3 sequence from variant.cpp (the file already has `hash_murmur3_one_double`/`hash_murmur3_one_float`/`hash_fmix32` helpers and golden constants in its tests — add golden values for each new type computed from the C++). WIRING REQUIREMENT: a script in a scene keys a Dictionary by NodePath and by Transform2D and the lookups must resolve distinctly; `arr.hash()` must return Godot's value.

**Prove it:** A scene script builds `{^"A": 1, ^"B": 2}` and a Transform2D-keyed dictionary, reads both keys back distinctly, and `[1,2,3].hash()` / `{"a":1}.hash()` return the values Godot produces; `godot_hash` has no catch-all arm. (test: `variant_hash_full_type_coverage_from_scene`)

**Patina today:**
- [engine-virtual-method-table] XRInterfaceExtension, GLTFDocumentExtension and EditorVCSInterface exist in Patina's ClassDB as classes but with 0 of 32, 0 of 23 and 0 of 23 virtuals declared respectively; MovieWriter (6/6), RenderSceneBuffersExtension (5/5), RenderSceneDataExtension (6/6), RenderDataExtension (4/4) and EngineProfiler (3/3) are fully declared yet grepping their virtual names (`"_write_begin"`, `"_write_frame"`, `"_write_end"`, `"_toggle"`, `"_add_frame"`, `"_tick"`, `"_get_uniform_buffer"`, `"_get_cam_projection"`) over engine-rs/crates/ excluding tests hits class_db.rs only. **Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: several small extension surfaces let a script plug into engine subsystems. `extends Translation` with `_get_message(src, context)` / `_get_plural_message(...)` supplies a runtime-computed locale; `extends Logger` with `_log_message`/`_log_error` intercepts engine output; `extends VideoStream` + `_instantiate_playback` returning a `VideoStreamPlayback` (13 virtuals: `_play`, `_update`, `_get_texture`, `_get_playback_position`, …) implements a custom video decoder — the natural shape for a browser-native `<video>`-backed player. XRInterfaceExtension (32), GLTFDocumentExtension (23), EditorVCSInterface (23), MovieWriter (6), EngineProfiler (3), CompositorEffect (1) and CameraFeed (2) round out the tail.\n\nPATINA: Translation, Logger, VideoStream and VideoStreamPlayback are not registered at all (`rg -c '\"<Name>\"' engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/` = 0 for each). XRInterfaceExtension, GLTFDocumentExtension and EditorVCSInterface are registered as classes but declare 0 of their 32/23/23 virtuals. MovieWriter, RenderSceneBuffersExtension, RenderSceneDataExtension, RenderDataExtension and EngineProfiler are fully declared and never called — grepping `\"_write_begin\"`, `\"_write_frame\"`, `\"_toggle\"`, `\"_add_frame\"`, `\"_tick\"`, `\"_get_uniform_buffer\"` over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) hits class_db.rs only.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) Register the four missing classes plus the missing virtual rows on the three under-declared ones in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, arities from extension_api.json via jq. Godot's skeleton.glsl:144-148 is the contract: NORMALIZED (=0, the DEFAULT) is (1-Σw)*base + Σw*shape; RELATIVE (=1) is base + Σw*shape. apply_morph did the latter. Whoever wired it would have got Godot's non-default behaviour believing they had the default — a single shape at weight 1.0 should REPLACE the base and would instead DOUBLE it.
WHY SIX GREEN TESTS MISSED IT: all six assert on vertex 0 of a triangle whose vertex 0 is the ORIGIN, where (1-w)*0 == 0 and both modes agree for every weight. ⚠️ Σw COUNTS EVERY WEIGHT, including shapes whose delta array is short — Godot accumulates blend_total while walking the WEIGHTS, independent of how many vertices each shape touches. **Godot classes:** MultiplayerPeerExtension, MultiplayerAPIExtension, PacketPeerExtension, StreamPeerExtension, WebRTCPeerConnectionExtension, WebRTCDataChannelExtension

**Patina today:**
- [engine-virtual-method-table] Both are registered with full virtual sets in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (MultiplayerPeerExtension 23/23, MultiplayerAPIExtension 9/9) and the file's own comment at class_db.rs:11661-11670 says of them: "⚠️ Both are PURE VIRTUAL SURFACES — zero non-virtual methods between them. Every entry below is a hook the subclass provides, not an API the engine offers. That inverts the usual reading of a registration: nothing here is callable *on* the class; it is all callable *by* the engine." The engine never calls them: grepping `"_get_packet"`, `"_put_packet"`, `"_poll"`, `"_rpc"`, `"_get_peer_ids"`, `"_object_configuration_add"` across engine-rs/crates/ excluding tests hits class_db.rs only. PacketPeerExtension, StreamPeerExtension, WebRTCPeerConnectionExtension and WebRTCDataChannelExtension return 0 hits in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/ entirely.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/network.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: `extends MultiplayerPeerExtension` is how a project implements a custom transport — the engine calls `_poll()` each frame, `_put_packet(buffer)` / `_get_packet()` / `_get_available_packet_count()` to move data, `_set_target_peer`/`_get_transfer_mode`/`_get_packet_channel` for routing, and `_get_unique_id`/`_is_server`/`_get_connection_status`/`_close`/`_disconnect_peer` for lifecycle. `extends MultiplayerAPIExtension` replaces the whole multiplayer stack (`_poll`, `_rpc`, `_get_peer_ids`, `_object_configuration_add/_remove`). PacketPeerExtension / StreamPeerExtension / WebRTCPeerConnectionExtension / WebRTCDataChannelExtension are the same pattern one layer down.\n\nPATINA: MultiplayerPeerExtension (23/23) and MultiplayerAPIExtension (9/9) are fully registered in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, and the source comment at class_db.rs:11661-11670 states the situation exactly — \"nothing here is callable *on* the class; it is all callable *by* the engine\" — while the engine calls none of them. Grepping `\"_get_packet\"`, `\"_put_packet\"`, `\"_poll\"`, `\"_rpc\"`, `\"_get_peer_ids\"`, `\"_object_configuration_add\"` over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) hits class_db.rs only. PacketPeerExtension, StreamPeerExtension, WebRTCPeerConnectionExtension and WebRTCDataChannelExtension are absent from gdobject/src entirely.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) Register the four missing Extension classes in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs with their virtuals. (2) In engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/multiplayer.rs, add a script-backed MultiplayerPeer adapter: when `multiplayer_peer` is set to a script object, drive it from the SceneTree's per-frame multiplayer poll — call `_poll()`, drain via `_get_available_packet_count()`/`_get_packet()`, send via `_set_target_peer()`+`_put_packet()`, and read identity/status from `_get_unique_id`/`_is_server`/`_get_connection_status`. (3) Allow `SceneTree.set_multiplayer` to accept a script MultiplayerAPIExtension and route the frame poll and every `rpc()` through `_poll` and `_rpc(peer, object, method, args)` instead of the built-in stack, with `_object_configuration_add/_remove` called on Spawner/Synchronizer registration.\n\nWIRING: two SceneTrees in one process, each with a script MultiplayerPeerExtension backed by a shared in-memory queue -> per-frame poll -> an @rpc call on tree A arrives at tree B's node.

**Prove it:** Two SceneTrees whose `multiplayer_peer` is a GDScript `extends MultiplayerPeerExtension` sharing an in-memory queue deliver an `@rpc("any_peer") func ping(v)` call made on tree A to the matching node on tree B after stepping both loops, with `_poll` called once per frame per tree and `_put_packet`/`_get_packet` carrying the payload; a script MultiplayerAPIExtension installed via set_multiplayer has `_rpc` called instead of the built-in path. (test: `script_multiplayer_peer_extension_dispatch`)

title: Implement PacketPeerStream over the existing StreamPeer family
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-packet-peer-stream] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/PacketPeerStream.xml — `inherits="PacketPeer"`, is_instantiable=true, 3 properties (input_buffer_max_size, output_buffer_max_size, stream_peer) and 6 methods. Implements a length-prefixed packet protocol over any StreamPeer (upstream/godot/core/io/packet_peer.cpp).

**Godot classes:** PacketPeerStream

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-4] NOT REGISTERED: `rg -n 'ClassRegistration::new("PacketPeerStream"' engine-rs apps` -> 0 hits; `rg -n 'PacketPeerStream' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` -> 0 hits.
THE NEIGHBOURS ARE ALL PRESENT, WHICH ISOLATES THIS AS A GAP RATHER THAN A SCOPE DECISION: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11471-11473 registers the `PacketPeer` base, :11773-11780 PacketPeerUDP, :11792 StreamPeerBuffer, :11844 StreamPeerTCP, :11894 PacketPeerDTLS, and interpreter.rs:3100 + :16329-16484 give StreamPeerBuffer a live instance dispatch. PacketPeerStream is the one member of the family with neither a registration nor a dispatch, so `PacketPeerStream.new()` is an unknown class while its base and both its collaborators exist.
IN SCOPE: this class is pure in-process framing over an existing StreamPeer — it needs no socket of its own, so the web-limitations carve-out in .claude/skills/port-audit/references/taxonomy.md:10-19 does not apply to it (a PacketPeerStream over a StreamPeerBuffer works entirely in memory).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/stream_peer_buffer.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Every neighbour in this family is already registered — PacketPeer base (class_db.rs:11471), PacketPeerUDP (:11773), PacketPeerDTLS (:11894), StreamPeerBuffer (:11792, with live dispatch at interpreter.rs:16329-16484), StreamPeerTCP (:11844) — but PacketPeerStream has neither a ClassDB entry nor an interpreter arm, so `PacketPeerStream.new()` is an unknown class.

It is the cheapest member of the set: Godot's implementation (core/io/packet_peer.cpp) is a 32-bit-length-prefixed framing layer over any StreamPeer, with `input_buffer_max_size` / `output_buffer_max_size` ring buffers. Over a StreamPeerBuffer it works entirely in memory, so nothing about it is blocked by the web platform.

Register it under PacketPeer with its 3 properties and 6 methods, and dispatch put_packet/get_packet/get_available_packet_count/set_stream_peer/get_stream_peer over the existing gdplatform StreamPeerBuffer handle table.

Ground truth: upstream/godot/doc/classes/PacketPeerStream.xml; upstream/godot/core/io/packet_peer.cpp.

**Prove it:** 1. `ClassDB.class_exists("PacketPeerStream")` is true, it is instantiable, its parent is PacketPeer, and it registers input_buffer_max_size / output_buffer_max_size / stream_peer with Godot's defaults.
2. A GDScript wrapping a StreamPeerBuffer: `pps.stream_peer = spb; pps.put_packet(a); pps.put_packet(b)` then reading back yields `get_available_packet_count() == 2` and the two packets in order with byte-identical contents.
3. Packet boundaries survive fragmentation: writing the framed bytes into the stream peer a few bytes at a time still yields exactly the original packets, never a merged or split one.
4. Exceeding output_buffer_max_size returns ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (Godot's documented error) instead of panicking, and get_packet() with no pending packet returns an empty PackedByteArray with ERR_UNAVAILABLE (test: `packet_peer_stream_framing_over_stream_peer_buffer`)

3. Packet boundaries survive fragmentation: writing the framed bytes into the stream peer a few bytes at a time still yields exactly the original packets, never a merged or split one.
4. Exceeding output_buffer_max_size returns ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY (Godot's documented error) instead of panicking, and get_packet() with no pending packet returns an empty PackedByteArray with ERR_UNAVAILABLE (test: `packet_peer_stream_framing_over_stream_peer_buffer`)

title: Implement StreamPeerGZIP over the vendored miniz_oxide codec
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-streampeer-gzip] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_gzip.cpp; doc/classes/StreamPeerGZIP.xml; extension_api.json StreamPeerGZIP(inherits=StreamPeer, 4 methods: start_compression/start_decompression/finish/clear)

**Godot classes:** StreamPeerGZIP

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] Not registered and not implemented: `StreamPeerGZIP` is absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list (its siblings `StreamPeer`, `StreamPeerBuffer`, `StreamPeerSocket`, `StreamPeerTCP`, `StreamPeerUDS` ARE registered), and `rg -in 'StreamPeerGZIP'` over engine-rs finds only the generated inspector schema table. This one is squarely in scope for the browser target — it is pure in-memory gzip/deflate with no socket involved, so Godot's own web export supports it fully — and the dependency is already vendored: `miniz_oxide` is used at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/zip.rs:11-17 and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:195-197.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/zip.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `StreamPeerGZIP : StreamPeer` is a streaming gzip/deflate transform peer — `start_compression(use_deflate, buffer_size)`, `start_decompression(use_deflate, buffer_size)`, `finish()`, `clear()` — with the inherited StreamPeer put/get API pushing bytes in and pulling transformed bytes out (`upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_gzip.cpp`). It involves no socket, so Godot's own web export supports it unchanged.

**Patina today:** absent. `StreamPeerGZIP` is not among the 638 `ClassRegistration::new` names — its siblings `StreamPeer`, `StreamPeerBuffer`, `StreamPeerSocket`, `StreamPeerTCP` and `StreamPeerUDS` all are — and `rg -in 'StreamPeerGZIP'` over engine-rs finds only a row in the generated inspector schema table. No implementation exists.

**Implement:** register `StreamPeerGZIP` under `StreamPeer` in `class_db.rs` and implement the peer next to the existing StreamPeer family, backed by `miniz_oxide` — already a workspace dependency used at `crates/gdresource/src/zip.rs:11-17` (raw deflate) and `crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:195-197` (zlib). Support both the gzip container and raw deflate via `use_deflate`, honor `buffer_size`, and make `finish()` flush the trailing block. Expose it through the same script path the other StreamPeer classes use so `StreamPeerGZIP.new()` works from GDScript.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a played scene must be able to construct the peer, `put_data()` a payload, `finish()`, `get_data()` the compressed bytes, and round-trip them back through a decompression peer.

**Prove it:** an app-level test whose script compresses a ~64 KiB highly-compressible payload through `StreamPeerGZIP` in gzip mode, asserts the output is materially smaller and begins with the gzip magic `1f 8b`, feeds it into a decompression peer and asserts byte-exact recovery; repeats in `use_deflate` mode and asserts the raw-deflate output has no gzip header.

**Prove it:** A GDScript constructs `StreamPeerGZIP`, compresses a 64 KiB payload in gzip mode to a materially smaller buffer beginning with `1f 8b`, and a decompression peer recovers the original bytes exactly; the same round-trip in `use_deflate` mode produces a header-less raw deflate stream that also recovers exactly (test: `stream_peer_gzip_round_trips`)

title: Add the TLSOptions/StreamPeerTLS/StreamPeerExtension class surface with web-correct errors
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-tls-class-surface] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_tls.cpp + core/crypto/crypto.cpp (TLSOptions); doc/classes/{StreamPeerTLS,TLSOptions}.xml; extension_api.json StreamPeerTLS(StreamPeer,6 methods), TLSOptions(RefCounted,9 methods, not instantiable), StreamPeerExtension(StreamPeer,5)

**Godot classes:** StreamPeerTLS, TLSOptions, StreamPeerExtension

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] None of the three is registered: absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, and `rg -in 'tls|x509|CryptoKey' crates/gdcore/src crates/gdplatform/src` finds no implementation — only refusals: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs:32-34 `TlsUnsupported` returned for every `wss://` URL (:467-468), and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs:490-491 `request_sync_https_reports_tls_error`. `TLSOptions` is not itself a socket feature — it is the config object passed to `HTTPClient.connect_to_host`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` and `WebSocketPeer.connect_to_url`, all of which a browser satisfies natively via fetch/WebSocket, so a script calling `TLSOptions.client()` must not fail. `StreamPeerTLS`'s own transport (raw TCP + mbedtls) IS web-unavailable per `upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`, where every NetSocket op returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE — so its correct web behavior is a registered class returning ERR_UNAVAILABLE, matching Godot.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `TLSOptions : RefCounted` (not instantiable — built via the statics `client(trusted_chain, common_name_override)`, `client_unsafe(trusted_chain)`, `server(key, certificate)`) is the configuration object accepted by `HTTPClient.connect_to_host`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` and `WebSocketPeer.connect_to_url`. `StreamPeerTLS : StreamPeer` wraps a raw TCP peer in TLS (`accept_stream`, `connect_to_stream`, `disconnect_from_stream`, `get_status`, `poll`, `get_stream`). `StreamPeerExtension : StreamPeer` is the GDExtension virtual hook. Sources: `upstream/godot/core/io/stream_peer_tls.cpp`, `core/crypto/crypto.cpp`.

**Patina today:** none of the three is in ClassDB (absent from the 638 `ClassRegistration::new` names) and no TLS implementation exists — `rg -in 'tls|x509|CryptoKey'` over `crates/gdcore/src` and `crates/gdplatform/src` finds only refusals: `websocket_peer.rs:32-34,467-468` returns `TlsUnsupported` for every `wss://` URL, and `http_request.rs:490-491` pins that https reports a TLS error. So a script that merely constructs `TLSOptions.client()` to pass into an HTTP request fails at the class level.

**Scope note:** `StreamPeerTLS`'s transport (raw TCP + mbedtls) genuinely cannot work in a browser — Godot's own web platform stubs every socket operation to `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` (`upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`). So the target here is Godot-web parity: the classes exist and return the same errors Godot's web build returns. `TLSOptions` is different — it is pure configuration and must actually work, because fetch/WebSocket handle TLS natively.

**Implement:** register `StreamPeerTLS` (StreamPeer), `TLSOptions` (RefCounted, non-instantiable) and `StreamPeerExtension` (StreamPeer) in `class_db.rs`. Implement `TLSOptions` as a real value type carrying trusted chain / common-name override / server key+cert, expose the three static constructors to the interpreter, and thread it through `http_request.rs` and `websocket_peer.rs` so `set_tls_options` is accepted (and honored where a native backend exists, ignored where the browser owns the handshake). Give `StreamPeerTLS` methods that return `ERR_UNAVAILABLE`/`STATUS_ERROR` rather than being absent.

**Wiring requirement:** a GDScript in a played scene must be able to build a `TLSOptions` and pass it to an `HTTPRequest`, and calling `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(...)` must return Godot's web error code instead of raising an unknown-class error.

**Prove it:** an app-level test whose script constructs `TLSOptions.client()` and `TLSOptions.server(key, cert)`, asserts both are valid non-null objects reporting `is_class("TLSOptions")`, passes one to `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` and asserts it is accepted, then asserts `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(peer)` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` and `get_status()` reports the error status.

**Prove it:** A GDScript builds `TLSOptions.client()` and `TLSOptions.server(key, cert)` as valid objects reporting `is_class("TLSOptions")`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` accepts one without error, and `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(peer)` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` with `get_status()` reporting the error status rather than raising an unknown-class error (test: `tls_options_and_stream_peer_tls_surface`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript builds `TLSOptions.client()` and `TLSOptions.server(key, cert)` as valid objects reporting `is_class("TLSOptions")`, `HTTPRequest.set_tls_options` accepts one without error, and `StreamPeerTLS.new().connect_to_stream(peer)` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` with `get_status()` reporting the error status rather than raising an unknown-class error (test: `tls_options_and_stream_peer_tls_surface`)

title: Register UDSServer to complete the SocketServer/StreamPeerUDS family
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-uds-server-registration] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/doc/classes/UDSServer.xml (inherits SocketServer; `listen(path)`, `take_connection() -> StreamPeerUDS`); extension_api.json UDSServer(SocketServer, 2 methods)

**Godot classes:** UDSServer

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-6] `UDSServer` is absent from the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list, but its entire family IS registered: `SocketServer` (its parent), `StreamPeerUDS` (its return type), `TCPServer`, `StreamPeerSocket` and `StreamPeerTCP` all appear in that list. So Patina has already adopted the convention of shipping the native-socket class surface, and UDSServer is the single omission — `SocketServer` currently has a registered subclass (`TCPServer`) and a registered peer type (`StreamPeerUDS`) with no server to hand it out. Behaviorally it is native-only: Godot's own web platform stubs every NetSocket operation to ERR_UNAVAILABLE (`upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`), and UDSServer.xml notes Unix Domain Sockets are Unix-only.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

**Godot ground truth:** `UDSServer : SocketServer` listens on a filesystem socket path and hands out `StreamPeerUDS` connections — `listen(path) -> Error`, `take_connection() -> StreamPeerUDS`, plus the inherited `is_connection_available()`/`is_listening()`/`stop()` from `SocketServer` (`upstream/godot/doc/classes/UDSServer.xml`; the doc notes UDS is Unix-only).

**Patina today:** `UDSServer` is the single missing member of a family Patina has otherwise already adopted — `SocketServer` (its parent), `StreamPeerUDS` (its return type), `TCPServer`, `StreamPeerSocket` and `StreamPeerTCP` are all in the 638-name `ClassRegistration::new` list; `UDSServer` is not. The result is a registered peer type with no registered server that produces it, and a `SocketServer` base whose subclass set is incomplete, so `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` diverges from Godot.

**Scope note:** behavior is native-only. Godot's own web platform stubs every `NetSocket` operation to `ERR_UNAVAILABLE` (`upstream/godot/platform/web/net_socket_web.h:50-73`), so on the browser target the correct behavior is exactly what Godot's web build does: the class exists, `listen()` returns `ERR_UNAVAILABLE`, `take_connection()` returns null. This bead is the class surface plus those correct errors, matching how the sibling socket classes are already handled.

**Implement:** register `UDSServer` under `SocketServer` in `class_db.rs` and give it `listen`/`take_connection`/`is_connection_available`/`stop` returning the same values the existing registered `TCPServer` returns on this target, so the two servers behave consistently.

**Wiring requirement:** `ClassDB.class_exists("UDSServer")` and `ClassDB.get_parent_class("UDSServer") == "SocketServer"` must hold, and `UDSServer` must appear in `ClassDB.get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` alongside `TCPServer`.

**Prove it:** an app-level test asserting `UDSServer` instantiates through ClassDB with parent `SocketServer`, that `get_inheriters_from_class("SocketServer")` contains both `UDSServer` and `TCPServer`, and that `listen("/tmp/x.sock")` returns the same error code the already-registered `TCPServer.listen` returns on this target (so the two stay consistent).

PATINA: the PathFollow2D branch at `crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:1172-1200` reads `progress`, `progress_ratio`, `loop`, `rotates`, `h_offset`, `v_offset` and a Patina-invented `path_speed`, but never `cubic_interp` — `grep -rn cubic_interp crates/` is empty outside the generated inspector schema, so sampling is unconditionally linear. **Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/logger.h (Logger + the ErrorType enum), core/object/script_language_extension / OS.add_logger binding; doc/classes/Logger.xml "Custom logger to receive messages from the internal error/warning stream" (_log_error, _log_message virtuals; ERROR_TYPE_* constants), doc/classes/OS.xml add_logger / remove_logger

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot 4.4+ exposes Logger (core/io/logger.h) so a script or @tool plugin can subclass it, override _log_error / _log_message, and install it with OS.add_logger(logger) to receive every print, push_warning, push_error and engine error — with function/file/line and an ERROR_TYPE_* classification.

This matters more for Patina than for desktop Godot. The taxonomy's editor-ux stone calls for an Output panel with "rich errors w/ links" and console routing (print -> console.log, push_error -> console.error + editor capture). A Logger subclass is the sanctioned, script-visible way to do that capture, and it is also how a @tool plugin or an in-browser diagnostics overlay taps the stream without patching the engine.

Work: register Logger (parent RefCounted) with the _log_error / _log_message virtuals and the ERROR_TYPE_ERROR / _WARNING / _SCRIPT / _SHADER constants, add OS.add_logger / OS.remove_logger to the OS singleton, and route the engine's existing print/push_warning/push_error path through the installed logger list.

title: LightmapGIData / Lightmapper / LightmapperRD missing; LightmapGI is a registered stub with no data resource type
description:
[audit-key: rendering/rendering-3d-lightmap-bake-family] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/lightmap_gi.cpp (LightmapGIData), scene/3d/lightmapper.h (Lightmapper abstract base), modules/lightmapper_rd/lightmapper_rd.cpp (LightmapperRD); doc/classes/LightmapGIData.xml (lightmap_textures, light_texture, uses_spherical_harmonics, add_user, get_user_count, clear_users), Lightmapper.xml ("Abstract class extended by lightmappers, for use in LightmapGI"), LightmapperRD.xml

**Godot classes:** LightmapGIData, Lightmapper, LightmapperRD

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-2] All three return zero hits: `rg -n '\bLightmapGIData\b|\bLightmapper\b|\bLightmapperRD\b' -g '*.rs' crates/` finds nothing (only inspector_schema_generated.rs entries), and none is among class_db.rs's string literals. The parent node IS registered — class_db.rs:2984 `ClassRegistration::new("LightmapGI")` with defaults sourced from doc/classes/LightmapGI.xml (:2982) — but its backing implementation is self-declared inert: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs:1 "Global Illumination stub nodes: VoxelGI and LightmapGI", :5 "the configuration surface so that scenes using VoxelGI or LightmapGI can [load]", :278 "Stub for Godot's LightmapGI node", :283 `pub struct LightmapGI`. So LightmapGI accepts a `light_data` property it can neither type nor consume.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/gi.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

LightmapGI is registered (class_db.rs:2984, defaults taken from doc/classes/LightmapGI.xml per the comment at :2982) but its backing implementation announces itself as inert: gdserver3d/src/gi.rs:1 "Global Illumination stub nodes", :5 "the configuration surface so that scenes using VoxelGI or LightmapGI can [load]", :278 "Stub for Godot's LightmapGI node".

The three classes that make it mean anything are absent — `rg 'LightmapGIData|Lightmapper|LightmapperRD' crates/` returns nothing outside the editor's generated parent table. LightmapGIData is the Resource that a .tscn's `light_data = ExtResource(...)` points at: it carries the baked lightmap textures, the per-instance user list and the spherical-harmonics flag. Without it, a project that ships a PRE-BAKED lightmap (the common case — baking is an editor/offline step) loads a LightmapGI node whose light_data property references a type ClassDB cannot construct, so the baked lighting is silently dropped even though nothing needed to be baked at runtime.

Scope split worth respecting: CONSUMING a baked LightmapGIData is a runtime feature and the higher-value half. PRODUCING one (Lightmapper / LightmapperRD, which needs GPU compute raytracing) is an editor/offline feature and can follow later or be scoped out with a citation.

Work: register LightmapGIData (parent Resource) with lightmap_textures, light_texture, uses_spherical_harmonics and the user list API; load it from .tscn/.tres and feed its textures into the 3D renderer's ambient/indirect term for meshes with the matching bake flags. Register Lightmapper (abstract, parent RefCounted) and LightmapperRD (parent Lightmapper) as surface for now.

**Prove it:** 1. ClassDB registers LightmapGIData (parent Resource), Lightmapper (abstract, parent RefCounted) and LightmapperRD (parent Lightmapper); is_abstract("Lightmapper") is true and instantiate("Lightmapper") fails.
2. Loading a .tscn whose LightmapGI has `light_data = ExtResource("...")` pointing at a LightmapGIData .res yields a LightmapGI node whose light_data is a real LightmapGIData, not Nil — assert the lightmap_textures array is non-empty.
3. get_user_count()/get_user_path(i) round-trip through a save/load of that resource.
4. A MeshInstance3D registered as a lightmap user renders brighter with the baked data present than with light_data cleared (assert the sampled indirect term differs), proving the data reaches the renderer rather than sitting in a struct.
5. If runtime BAKING is deferred, LightmapGI.bake() returns a clear unsupported error rather than silently doing nothing, and the deferral is recorded with a scope citation (test: `prebaked_lightmap_gi_data_loads_and_reaches_the_renderer`)
acceptance_criteria:
1. ClassDB registers LightmapGIData (parent Resource), Lightmapper (abstract, parent RefCounted) and LightmapperRD (parent Lightmapper); is_abstract("Lightmapper") is true and instantiate("Lightmapper") fails.
2. Loading a .tscn whose LightmapGI has `light_data = ExtResource("...")` pointing at a LightmapGIData .res yields a LightmapGI node whose light_data is a real LightmapGIData, not Nil — assert the lightmap_textures array is non-empty.
3. get_user_count()/get_user_path(i) round-trip through a save/load of that resource.
4. A MeshInstance3D registered as a lightmap user renders brighter with the baked data present than with light_data cleared (assert the sampled indirect term differs), proving the data reaches the renderer rather than sitting in a struct.
5. If runtime BAKING is deferred, LightmapGI.bake() returns a clear unsupported error rather than silently doing nothing, and the deferral is recorded with a scope citation (test: `prebaked_lightmap_gi_data_loads_and_reaches_the_renderer`)

title: Physics2D: register/unregister bodies and areas as nodes enter and exit the tree
description:
[audit-key: physics-2d/physics2d-runtime-registration] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/collision_object_2d.cpp — CollisionObject2D::_notification NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE calls PhysicsServer2D::body_set_space / area_set_space, NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE clears it. Every node added to or removed from the tree at runtime joins/leaves the space immediately. | extension_api.json: CollisionObject2D._input_event(Viewport viewport, InputEvent event, int shape_idx) and CollisionObject3D._input_event(Camera3D camera, InputEvent event, Vector3 event_position, Vector3 normal, int shape_idx); upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp _process_picking; doc/classes/CollisionObject2D.xml | upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/collision_object_2d.cpp — shape_owner_* API; every CollisionShape2D/CollisionPolygon2D child is its own shape owner with its own Transform2D relative to the body (collision_shape_2d.cpp `_update_in_shape_owner` calls `shape_owner_set_transform(owner_id, get_transform())`). PhysicsServer2D exposes body_add_shape / body_set_shape_transform / body_set_shape_disabled / body_set_shape_as_one_way_collision per shape index. | extension_api.json CollisionObject2D._mouse_enter/_mouse_exit/_mouse_shape_enter(int)/_mouse_shape_exit(int), CollisionObject3D._mouse_enter/_mouse_exit; upstream/godot/scene/main/viewport.cpp picking hover transitions.

**Godot classes:** CollisionObject2D, RigidBody2D, Area2D, StaticBody2D, CharacterBody2D, CollisionObject3D, Area3D, CollisionShape2D, CollisionPolygon2D

**Patina today:**
- [physics-2d] `PhysicsServer::register_bodies` is the only path that creates 2D bodies (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:906). Its only non-test caller is `MainLoop::register_physics_bodies` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2183-2185), whose only non-test caller in the whole workspace is /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:369 — once, before the frame loop starts. `MainLoop::step`'s physics section (main_loop.rs:2807-2930) calls sync_to_physics/step_physics/sync_from_physics but never register_bodies. Grep: `grep -rn "register_physics_bodies" engine-rs/crates/` → only main_loop.rs:2183 + the runner + #[cfg(test)] uses. There is also no removal path for scene-node bodies: `self.world.remove_body` appears only at physics_server.rs:725 (the PhysicsServer2D RID free path) and physics_server.rs:1113 (tilemap regeneration). Contrast the 3D server, which re-scans the whole tree every tick and prunes stale bodies inside `sync_to_physics` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs:538-548 for adds, :628-631 for removals). Consequence: `add_child(preload("res://Bullet.tscn").instantiate())` produces a RigidBody2D that never falls, never collides, and emits no signals; `queue_free()` on a body leaves a permanent ghost collider.
- [engine-virtual-method-table] Patina calls the 2D virtual with ONE argument — `self.tree.call_script_method(nid, "_input_event", &[payload.clone()])` at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2306-2308 — and the 3D virtual with FOUR (camera, event, position, normal) at main_loop.rs:2437-2444, both omitting shape_idx (the in-source comment at main_loop.rs:2295-2304 and 2427-2434 admits it). The interpreter REJECTS an arity mismatch: `if args.len() < func.min_args() || args.len() > func.params.len() { return Err(RuntimeError::new(RuntimeErrorKind::TypeError(...` at engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:11773-11778, so a Godot-correct `func _input_event(viewport, event, shape_idx):` never runs — the failure is swallowed at scene_tree.rs:2861-2863 (`tracing::debug!`). This is masked by green tests: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/pick2d_signals.rs:113 and physics3d_picking.rs:141 assert only on SIGNAL connections to `_on_input_event`, and viewport_input_propagation_gui_stage.rs:181-192 asserts on a Rust `RecordingScript` mock that records the call name regardless of arity — no test ever compiles a GDScript with Godot's documented signature.
- [physics-2d] `PhysicsBody2D` holds exactly one shape: `pub shape: Shape2D` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs:51. The bridge takes the FIRST enabled collider child and discards the rest: `find_collision_shape` at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:345-356 returns on the first `Some(shape)`. The child's own transform is never applied — `register_bodies` (physics_server.rs:924-944) uses the BODY's global position/rotation and only passes the accumulated scale through `scale_shape` (physics_server.rs:413); there is no code anywhere that reads a CollisionShape2D's `position`/`rotation` into a shape offset. `PhysicsServer::server_body_add_shape` admits it in a comment at physics_server.rs:1121: "One shape per body here; Godot allows several." The `shape_owner_*` API has 0 hits in engine-rs/crates/. Consequences: (a) any CollisionShape2D authored with a non-zero `position` collides in the wrong place — silently; (b) an L-shaped or multi-collider body (two CollisionShape2D children) collides with only the first; (c) per-shape `one_way_collision` is lifted to the whole body (physics_server.rs:988).
- [engine-virtual-method-table] `rg -F '"_mouse_enter"' / '"_mouse_exit"' / '"_mouse_shape_enter"' / '"_mouse_shape_exit"' engine-rs/crates/` each return 0 hits tree-wide. Patina resolves the hover transitions correctly but emits only SIGNALS: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2282-2286 `self.tree.emit_signal(nid, "mouse_exited", &[])` / `emit_signal(nid, "mouse_entered", &[])`. Separately, gdscene DOES dispatch script methods literally named `_mouse_entered`/`_mouse_exited` (scene_tree.rs:3269, 3274) — those are Godot SIGNAL names with an underscore glued on, not Godot virtuals, so the names an author would write per the docs (`_mouse_enter`) are exactly the ones that do nothing.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server_3d.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/body.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdphysics2d/src/collision.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: CollisionObject2D joins the physics space on NOTIFICATION_ENTER_TREE and leaves it on NOTIFICATION_EXIT_TREE (upstream/godot/scene/2d/physics/collision_object_2d.cpp), so a body instanced mid-game simulates on the very next physics tick and a freed body stops colliding immediately.

PATINA: 2D bodies are built exactly once. `PhysicsServer::register_bodies` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs:906) is reached only through `MainLoop::register_physics_bodies` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2183), which the runner calls once at boot (engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:369). `MainLoop::step`'s physics loop (main_loop.rs:2807-2930) never re-registers. Nothing ever removes a scene-node body: `world.remove_body` is called only from the RID-free path (physics_server.rs:725) and tilemap regeneration (physics_server.rs:1113). A spawned RigidBody2D/Area2D/CharacterBody2D is completely inert; a freed one leaves a ghost collider.

APPROACH: mirror the 3D server. In engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/physics_server.rs, split `register_bodies` into an idempotent `sync_registrations(&SceneTree)` that (a) walks `tree.all_nodes_in_tree_order()`, registers any body/area/joint node not in `node_to_body`/`node_to_area`/`node_to_joint`, and (b) drops entries whose NodeId is no longer in the tree, calling `world.remove_body` / `area_store.remove_area` / `world.remove_joint` — exactly the shape of physics_server_3d.rs:538-548 and :628-631. Call it from `PhysicsServer::sync_to_physics` (physics_server.rs:1288) so it runs at the head of every physics tick, before `step_physics`. Keep `register_physics_bodies()` as a thin wrapper for the boot call so patina-runner is unchanged. Joints must be re-resolved after bodies (physics_server.rs:1162) so a joint spawned with its bodies binds.

WIRING: MainLoop::step → PhysicsServer::sync_to_physics → sync_registrations → world.add_body/remove_body, every physics tick, with no explicit call from game code.

**Merged findings (4):** Runtime body registration: physics bodies enter/leave the 2D world only once, at boot; CollisionObject2D/3D `_input_event` is dispatched with the wrong argument list; CollisionObject2D multi-shape bodies and per-shape local transforms; CollisionObject2D/3D `_mouse_enter`/`_mouse_exit`/`_mouse_shape_enter`/`_mouse_shape_exit`

**Prove it:** A scene whose script does `add_child(rigid_body)` in `_ready` (or on a later frame) produces a body that falls under gravity and lands on a StaticBody2D within a handful of ticks, and a body that is `queue_free()`d stops blocking a CharacterBody2D that walks through its former position. Body count in the world tracks the tree. (test: `physics2d_runtime_spawned_body_simulates`) — drives a real MainLoop with a scripted spawner, asserts the spawned node's `position.y` increases across ticks and that after freeing the platform the walker passes through.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script does `add_child(rigid_body)` in `_ready` (or on a later frame) produces a body that falls under gravity and lands on a StaticBody2D within a handful of ticks, and a body that is `queue_free()`d stops blocking a CharacterBody2D that walks through its former position. Body count in the world tracks the tree. (test: `physics2d_runtime_spawned_body_simulates`) — drives a real MainLoop with a scripted spawner, asserts the spawned node's `position.y` increases across ticks and that after freeing the platform the walker passes through.
