comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, slice-2 findings before implementing (sequencing matters here).

1. MISSING DEPENDENCY EDGE. The approach says to make gdserver2d/gdserver3d thin adapters over gdresource::shader_ast, but NEITHER server crate depends on gdresource today -- they are siblings, both on gdcore+gdvariant only. So item 3/4 starts with adding `gdresource = { path = "../gdresource" }` to gdserver2d/Cargo.toml and gdserver3d/Cargo.toml. I checked this is NOT a cycle: gdresource -> {gdcore, gdvariant, gdobject}, and none of those depend on either server crate. Safe, but it is an unstated prerequisite.

2. ORDERING HAZARD -- do the sampler plumbing BEFORE the routing. My instinct was to route parse_fragment_body/execute_fragment through the AST first and plumb textures after. That is backwards and would REGRESS visible output. execute_fragment receives only (instructions, ctx, uniforms) and FragmentContext carries no texture, so an AST-routed fragment() would evaluate texture(TEXTURE, UV) as transparent black (the no-sampler default I added in slice 1). For outline.gdshader that yields alpha 0 everywhere -- the sprite DISAPPEARS, which is worse than the current unshaded-sprite behaviour. Plumb the sampler through to execute_fragment first, then flip the routing.

3. SUGGESTED SHAPE for the routing, to keep the public signatures the bead requires: add a FragmentInstruction::Program(Arc<ShaderProgram>) variant so parse_fragment_body(source) -> Vec<FragmentInstruction> can carry the whole parsed program, and have execute_fragment match on it. That preserves both signatures so gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:875 keeps compiling, which is what the bead asks for.

4. SAMPLER PLUMBING OPTIONS. Adding `sampler: Option<gdresource::shader_ast::Sampler>` to FragmentContext is the natural home, but note there are ~16 FragmentContext literal sites and only 13 use ..Default::default() -- the other ~3 are full literals that would need editing. The lower-risk alternative is a new execute_fragment_with_sampler(instructions, ctx, uniforms, sampler) with execute_fragment delegating to it with None, leaving the struct and every construction site untouched.

Slice 1 (the Sampler hook in shader_ast) is already on disk and is the prerequisite for all of the above.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, follow-up: a flaw in the Sampler API I shipped in slice 1, found by reading the actual call site (gdrender2d/src/draw.rs:979).

LIFETIME PROBLEM. I typed Sampler as Arc<dyn Fn(&str,[f32;2])->[f32;4] + Send + Sync>, which implies + `static. The renderer call site has `texture: &Texture2D` -- a BORROW -- and everything it needs to sample is already in scope there (canvas_material::sample_texture(texture, u, v, tex_filter, tex_repeat) two lines above). A closure capturing that borrow is not `static, so `Sampler::new(...)` will not accept it as written.

Three ways out, in my order of preference:

(a) Clone the texture into the closure ONCE per draw call, before the pixel loop:
      let tex = texture.clone();
      let sampler = Sampler::new(move |_name, uv| { let c = canvas_material::sample_texture(&tex, uv[0], uv[1], tex_filter, tex_repeat); [c.r, c.g, c.b, c.a] });
    Texture2D is #[derive(Clone)] over a Vec<Color> (gdrender2d/src/texture.rs:10), so this copies the whole pixel buffer -- but once per draw call, not per pixel. Simplest, no API change.

(b) Give Sampler a lifetime parameter and hold a borrowed trait object. Cheapest at runtime, but the lifetime propagates into StageContext and would cost it the Debug/Clone/Default derives that other code relies on.

(c) Have the renderer hand ownership via Arc<Texture2D> instead. Cleanest long-term, but Texture2D is not currently stored behind an Arc anywhere, so it is the largest change.

I would take (a) unless profiling says otherwise -- it is contained to the call site and changes no public type.

ALSO NOTE: Texture2D lives in gdrender2d, NOT gdserver2d. So gdserver2d::execute_fragment can never name the texture type at all; the sampler MUST arrive as a caller-supplied closure from gdrender2d. That confirms the closure shape is right even though its lifetime bound is wrong.

comments.author: bone
comments.text: FuchsiaDeer, correcting my own wording in the previous comment: I called this "a flaw in the Sampler API", which overstates it. Option (a) needs NO API change -- an owning closure (move a cloned Texture2D in) satisfies Send + Sync + `static perfectly well. The constraint is on the CALLER (it must own, not borrow, its texture data), not a defect in the type. Options (b) and (c) are only worth considering if the per-draw-call clone shows up in profiling.

EmeraldIsland — measured this bead at HEAD. Its "Patina today" is largely STALE, the acceptance test
already exists, and the one clause nobody covers has a trap in it that I want recorded before someone
walks into it.

## STALE — the AST evaluator IS wired into both paths

`shader_ast` has 28 refs, not 2. Both renderers route through it: `gdrender2d/src/renderer.rs:440` and
`gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:2261` both call `parse_fragment_body`, which falls through to
`shader_ast::parse_shader` when the line matcher yields nothing (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:505-512).
The acceptance test EXISTS: `gdeditor/tests/shader_language_frontend_drives_scene_pixels.rs`, with 3
tests covering acceptance clauses 1 and 3.

## THE UNCOVERED CLAUSE IS 2 — "a syntax error yields a ShaderDiagnostic naming the line"

Two independent gaps, both confirmed:

1. `parse_fragment_body_checked` (gdserver2d/src/shader.rs:526) is the reporting variant, and it has
   **ZERO production callers** — its only callers are in `gdserver2d/tests/gdshader_parse_diagnostics.rs`.
   Both render paths use the lossy `parse_fragment_body`, so a broken shader renders unshaded and silent.
2. `validate_shader_source` (gdeditor/src/shader_editor.rs:492) **never runs the AST parse** —
   `grep -c shader_ast crates/gdeditor/src/shader_editor.rs` = **0**. It does a lex pass, a
   `shader_type` presence check, an undefined-function pass and an unused-uniform heuristic. So a
   shader that lexes cleanly, declares `shader_type`, and contains a genuine SYNTAX error validates as
   `ok: true`: the editor says the shader is fine while the renderer silently drops it.

## ⚠️ THE TRAP: DO NOT GATE VALIDATION ON `parse_shader` WITHOUT BOUNDING FALSE POSITIVES

The obvious fix — call `shader_ast::parse_shader` inside `validate_shader_source` and report its
`ShaderError` — is a REGRESSION RISK, because `parse_program` (shader_ast.rs:371) errors on any
top-level construct it does not model. That has already bitten once: the file's own comment at :391-400
records that `ShaderToken::Struct` had no arm, so **a shader declaring any struct failed to parse in its
entirety, taking its `fragment()` body with it**. `render_mode`/`group_uniforms`/`struct` are tolerated
today; anything else added to GDShader is not.

Gating the editor's validator on that parser would report a fabricated syntax error for every valid
shader using an unmodelled construct — turning a silent-failure bug into a false-alarm bug. Whoever
takes this should either (a) make `parse_program` tolerant-by-default for unknown top-level items, then
gate on it, or (b) gate the diagnostic on `parse_fragment_body` ALSO being empty (the
`parse_fragment_body_checked` semantics), which cannot false-positive on a shader that actually renders.
I did not attempt either blind: `semantic_pass_accepts_builtins_constructors_and_user_functions`
(shader_editor.rs:1260) is a live gate that a false positive would flip.

## ALSO: there is no 2D diagnostics channel to surface into

`gdserver2d::CompiledShader` (shader.rs:220) has **no diagnostics field**, unlike
`gdserver3d::CompiledShader3D` which carries `diagnostics: Vec<ShaderDiagnostic>`. And gdserver2d's
`ShaderCompiler` has zero production callers. So "surface a diagnostic from the 2D path" needs a channel
built first — that is the real cost of clause 2, not the parse call.

Note `ShaderDiagnostic` is TWO different types: gdserver3d's (`line`, `severity`, `message`, zero-based)
and gdeditor's (`line`, `col`, `message`, **1-based** — see the `shader_type` case using `line: 1`).
Do not cross them without converting.

## DELIVERED THIS PASS

`parse_shader` discarded the lexer's position: it mapped every `ShaderLexError` into
`ShaderError { line: 0, col: 0 }` even though all three lex variants carry `line`/`col` and their
`Display` prints them. Line 0 is out of range for a 1-based field, so no editor could highlight it.
Fixed with a wildcard-free or-pattern (mirroring `shader_lex_error_pos` in gdeditor), so a future lex
variant fails to compile here rather than silently regressing to 0. Two tests added asserting the real
line for an unexpected character and for an unterminated block comment (which correctly reports the line
it OPENED on, `start_line`, not the end-of-input line).

title: Theming: route Control draw through the real Theme chain (node theme, ancestors, project theme, ThemeDB)
description:
[audit-key: theming-text/theme-resource-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** scene/gui/control.cpp Control::_get_theme_item / get_theme_color; scene/theme/theme_owner.cpp (assigned → ancestors → project theme → ThemeDB default); scene/theme/theme_db.cpp:50-53 (gui/theme/default_theme_scale, gui/theme/custom, gui/theme/custom_font); doc/classes/Theme.xml | scene/theme/default_theme.cpp (fill_default_theme: 183 set_stylebox, 215 set_color, 170 set_constant, 164 set_icon, 62 set_font calls over 53 control types); scene/theme/icons/*.svg (97 icons); scene/theme/theme_db.cpp:50 gui/theme/default_theme_scale | upstream/godot/editor/scene/gui/theme_editor_plugin.cpp (ThemeEditorPreview with click-to-pick a control, per-type item management incl. Remove, type variations, 'Import Items' from another theme / editor theme / default theme)

**Godot classes:** Theme, ThemeDB, Control, StyleBox, StyleBoxFlat, CheckBox, OptionButton, Tree, TabBar

**Patina today:**
- [theming-text] The ONLY production call site that renders themed Controls hardcodes the built-in theme: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:992 `let theme = gdscene::theme::Theme::default_theme();` then :993 `control_draw_items(tree, root, &theme, size)`. A .tres Theme parser exists (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:887 `parse_theme_tres`, :1047 `Theme::from_tres`) — grep `parse_theme_tres|from_tres` over crates/ shows its only callers are engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/theme_tres_format_roundtrip.rs:47,117. Godot's full six-datatype lookup chain incl. the ancestor walk and theme_type_variation IS implemented at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:3158 `resolve_theme_item` — grep `resolve_theme_item` shows callers only in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/theme_chain.rs. The actual draw instead does a two-step ad-hoc lookup for a handful of hard-coded names, e.g. engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1161-1164 `color_prop(...,"theme_override_colors/font_color").or_else(|| theme.get_color("Label","font_color"))` — no ancestor walk, no variation, no stylebox/icon/font/constant override resolution. Project settings: grep `gui/theme` over crates/ hits only engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:730,732 (default_font_antialiasing, default_font_subpixel_positioning) — `gui/theme/custom`, `gui/theme/custom_font`, `gui/theme/default_theme_scale` are absent. ClassDB registers Theme/ThemeDB as bare names with zero properties and zero methods: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:8071,8074.
- [theming-text] engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:440-602 `Theme::default_theme()` contains 10 stylebox assignments, 6 set_color and 10 set_constant calls covering 31 type names, and ZERO `set_icon` / `set_font` calls (grep `set_icon|set_font\\(` inside the 440-602 range returns nothing). Godot's equivalent is 794 item assignments over 53 types. Patina's own comment at theme.rs:559-562 admits the palette is not Godot's derived base_color/accent_color scheme. Missing types include ColorPicker, FileDialog, FoldableContainer, GraphNode/GraphFrame, MenuBar, LinkButton, TooltipLabel, SplitContainer, all *Container separations, and every icon (checked/unchecked/radio/arrow_*/close/updown/grabber/tab_*). SVG rasterization already exists (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_svg.rs:40 `rasterize_svg_bytes`) so icons are reachable. `gui/theme/default_theme_scale` is absent from engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs.
- [editor-ux] The served theme panel (editor_ui.rs:2539-2552) renders a #theme-items list plus a two-control preview (#theme-preview-button, #theme-preview-label) whose values are updated in editor_ui.rs:12390-12415. POST /api/theme/item/remove exists in the editor_server.rs dispatch table but has 0 references in editor_ui.rs, so theme items can be added/changed but never removed. `grep -ci 'pick from\|pickFrom\|import from theme\|Type Variation\|variation' editor_ui.rs` = 0.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_svg.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/theme_editor.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: every themed value a Control paints resolves through Control::_get_theme_item (scene/gui/control.cpp) + ThemeOwner (scene/theme/theme_owner.cpp): (1) the node's own theme_override_<kind>/<name>, (2) the node's own `theme` Resource, (3) each ancestor Control/Window's theme nearest-first, (4) the project theme from ProjectSettings `gui/theme/custom` (scene/theme/theme_db.cpp:52), (5) ThemeDB's generated default. At every theme it tries `theme_type_variation` before the class name, and it does this for all six data types (color/constant/font/font_size/icon/stylebox).\n\nPATINA: the resolution logic already exists and is correct — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:3158 `resolve_theme_item` implements the whole chain incl. the ancestor walk and variation, and engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/theme.rs:887 `parse_theme_tres` loads a .tres Theme (colors, constants, font_sizes, styleboxes, `X/base_type` variations, default_font/default_font_size). Neither has a single production caller: grep `resolve_theme_item|parse_theme_tres|from_tres` over engine-rs/crates finds only tests (gdscene/tests/theme_chain.rs, gdscene/tests/theme_tres_format_roundtrip.rs). The one production render entry point hardcodes the built-in theme at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:992-993, and the draw code does ad-hoc per-property lookups (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:1136,1161-1164,1366,1403,1605) that skip ancestors, variations and every non-color data type. `gui/theme/custom` / `custom_font` / `default_theme_scale` are not in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (a) build a `ThemeContext` at the top of `control_draw_items` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs:174) holding the project theme (loaded once from `gui/theme/custom` via gdresource) + a `node_themes: HashMap<NodeId, Theme>` populated by resolving each Control's `theme` / `__extres__theme` property through the resource loader; (b) replace every ad-hoc `theme.get_*`/`color_prop` site in control_render.rs with a call to `control::resolve_theme_item` fed that context; (c) honor `theme_type_variation` on the node; (d) add `gui/theme/custom`, `gui/theme/custom_font`, `gui/theme/default_theme_scale` to engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs and consume the scale in Theme::default_theme(); (e) drop the hardcoded `Theme::default_theme()` in engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:992 in favour of the context.\n\nWIRING: .tscn with a Control carrying `theme = ExtResource("theme.tres")` → scene load → control_draw_items → ControlDrawItem colors/styleboxes that came from that .tres, in BOTH the editor viewport render and the Play render path.

**Merged findings (3):** Theme resource pipeline (Theme .tres load → Control.theme / theme_type_variation / ancestor theme chain / ThemeDB / gui/theme/custom) never reaches the draw path; Default theme parity: item count, per-control colors/constants/fonts, and the 97 built-in theme icons; Theme editor: pick-from-preview, type variations, import-from-theme, item removal

**Prove it:** Loading a scene whose root Panel has `theme = ExtResource(theme.tres)` (theme sets `Button/font_color` and a `Button/normal` StyleBoxFlat with a distinct bg color) and a Button child with no overrides produces draw items using the .tres values, not the built-in defaults; a Button carrying `theme_type_variation = &"FlatButton"` picks the theme's `FlatButton/normal` entry; a theme assigned on a grandparent still reaches the Button; `gui/theme/custom` in project.godot applies when no node theme exists; a local `theme_override_styles/normal` still beats all of them. (test: `theme_resource_reaches_control_draw`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test theme_resource_reaches_control_draw`.
acceptance_criteria: Loading a scene whose root Panel has `theme = ExtResource(theme.tres)` (theme sets `Button/font_color` and a `Button/normal` StyleBoxFlat with a distinct bg color) and a Button child with no overrides produces draw items using the .tres values, not the built-in defaults; a Button carrying `theme_type_variation = &"FlatButton"` picks the theme's `FlatButton/normal` entry; a theme assigned on a grandparent still reaches the Button; `gui/theme/custom` in project.godot applies when no node theme exists; a local `theme_override_styles/normal` still beats all of them. (test: `theme_resource_reaches_control_draw`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test theme_resource_reaches_control_draw`.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, opening survey. The chain already exists and is already tested — it just has no production caller.

`control::resolve_theme_item` (control.rs:3414) implements EXACTLY the precedence this bead asks for: local theme_override_* first, then the node theme, then each ancestor nearest-first, then the default (project/ThemeDB), trying `theme_type_variation` before `control_type` at every level. Its own doc records that its predecessor `resolve_theme_color` handled colours only, stopped before the ancestor walk, and had no production callers.

Counts, taken unpiped (I have gotten these wrong repeatedly on this epic by truncating greps, so these are `grep -c`):
  - resolve_theme_item references across engine-rs: 10 -> ONE definition + NINE in gdscene/tests/theme_chain.rs. Zero production callers.
  - control_render.rs flat `theme.get_*` lookups: 19 (5 get_color, 6 get_font_size, rest other kinds)
  - control_render.rs `stylebox_bg(` call sites: 15
  - control_draw_items( call sites across the workspace: 13 (1 production at gdeditor/src/viewport_2d_render.rs:1302, the rest tests)

So the bead is a WIRING job, not an implementation job. `control_draw_items` takes a single flat `&Theme` and every lookup goes straight to it, which is why a node `theme`, an ancestor theme, `theme_type_variation` and `gui/theme/custom` all change nothing on screen today.

LEVERAGE POINT: `stylebox_bg(theme, control_type, property, fallback)` at control_render.rs:637 is a single helper behind 15 of the call sites. Rewriting that ONE function to call resolve_theme_item converts 15 sites at once — but it needs (tree, node_id, variation, node_themes) which it does not currently receive, so its 15 call sites each need the extra arguments. Same pattern applies to the colour and font-size lookups.

ESTIMATED SHAPE (deliberately a shape, not a number I want anyone planning off): change control_draw_items to accept a node->Theme map alongside the default theme (13 call sites, mostly tests); rewrite stylebox_bg and add colour/font-size equivalents that delegate to resolve_theme_item (15 + 11 call sites gain arguments); then the acceptance test theme_resource_reaches_control_draw covering the five precedence cases the criteria name.

The existing gdscene/tests/theme_chain.rs is the reference test for the resolver itself — the new acceptance test should pin the same precedence but through control_draw_items, so a failure distinguishes "the chain is wrong" from "the chain is not reached".

description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/script-load-through-pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/resource_loader.cpp (`ResourceLoader::load` → `_path_remap` reads `.import` [remap] then dispatches a ResourceFormatLoader); modules/gdscript/gdscript_utility_functions.cpp `load`/`preload` | extension_api.json ResourceLoader: load_threaded_request, load_threaded_get_status, load_threaded_get, load, get_recognized_extensions_for_type, add/remove_resource_format_loader, set_abort_on_missing_resources, get_dependencies, has_cached, get_cached_ref, exists, get_resource_uid, list_directory (14). ResourceLoader exposes 14 methods (load_threaded_request/get_status/get, load, exists, get_dependencies, has_cached, get_cached_ref, get_resource_uid, list_directory, get_recognized_extensions_for_type, add/remove_resource_format_loader, set_abort_on_missing_resources); ResourceSaver exposes 6 (save, set_uid, get_recognized_extensions, add/remove_resource_format_saver, get_resource_id_for_path).

**Godot classes:** ResourceLoader, Texture2D, AudioStream, PackedScene, ResourceSaver, Resource

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4341-4398 — `"preload" | "load"` reads the file only for `.tres`/`.res` (`load_text_resource`, interpreter.rs:151-164) and for `.gdshader` (`code` property); for every other extension it string-matches the suffix (`.png`/`.jpg`/`.svg` → "Texture2D", `.wav`/`.ogg` → "AudioStream", `.ttf`/`.otf` → "Font") and returns `ResourceRef { path, class_name, properties: HashMap::new() }`. No `.import` remap is consulted and no pixel/sample data is produced, so `load("res://icon.png").get_width()` and `AudioStreamPlayer.stream = load("res://music.ogg")` see an empty object. The crate's own doc claims the opposite: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:816-828 says `UnifiedLoader` is "the engine-wide resource load entry point" and "Anything that needs a resource should come through here so all four consumers agree" — grep for `UnifiedLoader|ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults` under `crates/gdscript-interop/src` returns zero hits (the only real consumers are `gdeditor/src/texture_cache.rs:117` and two `gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs` sky call sites).
- [resources-io] Neither singleton is dispatchable from GDScript: `grep -n 'ResourceLoader\|ResourceSaver' gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` → 0 hits, and both are absent from `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14464-14483, which lists 18 names). `grep -rn "load_threaded" --include='*.rs'` over engine-rs/crates → 0 hits; `grep -rn "CacheMode\|take_over_path" ` → 0 hits. `gdresource/src/cache.rs:21 ResourceCache` is a plain path→Arc HashMap with only load/invalidate/clear (cache.rs:35-53) — no cache modes, no `has_cached`/`get_cached_ref`. The `load()`/`preload()` builtin (gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4341) only really loads `.tres`/`.res` (via `load_text_resource`, :151); for everything else it fabricates a placeholder `ResourceRef` with an inferred class name and an EMPTY property map (:4360-4394) — only `Shader` gets its `code` filled in. So `load("res://icon.png")` yields a `Texture2D` with no pixels and no methods (`get_width` is bound only on the Image handle, interpreter.rs:18904), and `load("res://s.ogg")` yields an inert `AudioStream`.
- [singleton-dispatch-table] ABSENCE: `rg -c '"ResourceLoader"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` -> 0; `rg -c '"ResourceSaver"' ...` -> 0; both names appear in the whole workspace only inside engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs (a generated class-name table, no dispatch). Neither is in `BUILTIN_SINGLETONS` (interpreter.rs:14464-14482) nor registered in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs (`grep -c '"ResourceLoader"' class_db.rs` -> 0). What scripts CAN do today is only the GDScript `load`/`preload` builtins (interpreter.rs:4341 and interpreter.rs:20757) — one path, no cache mode, no type hint, no threaded API, no existence/dependency queries, no saving at all. The engines exist and are unreachable: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs (7 pub fns), res_loader.rs (load_res_binary/parse_res_header), saver.rs:31 `save_to_string` / :96 `save_to_string_raw`, cache.rs, uid.rs. Enums absent: `grep -c '"CACHE_MODE_REUSE"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs` -> 0; same for THREAD_LOAD_LOADED and FLAG_COMPRESS; `global_enum_members()` (global_constants.rs:607-629) has no class-scoped enums at all.
- [sweep-5] Neither name appears in ClassDB: `rg -c '"ResourceLoader"' /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` -> 0, same for ResourceSaver. Neither is a script singleton: `rg -n 'ResourceLoader|ResourceSaver' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/*.rs` returns ZERO hits, and the interpreter's own singleton table at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14464-14483 (`BUILTIN_SINGLETONS`) lists 18 names — CameraServer, ClassDB, DisplayServer, Engine, EngineDebugger, GDExtensionManager, Input, InputMap, JavaScriptBridge, JSON, Marshalls, OS, PhysicsServer2D, ProjectSettings, RenderingServer, ResourceUID, Time, TranslationServer — with no ResourceLoader/ResourceSaver, so `Engine.has_singleton("ResourceLoader")` is false and `ResourceLoader.load(...)` is an undefined identifier. Only the bare `load`/`preload` builtins exist (interpreter.rs:4341, :20757). The Rust engines are present but are traits, not singletons: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs:20 `pub trait ResourceLoader`, saver.rs:15 `pub trait ResourceSaver`, pck.rs:637 `impl ResourceLoader for PckResourceLoader`.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/cache.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/unified.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/res_loader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/saver.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/cache.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/uid.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/saver.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `load()`/`preload()` call `ResourceLoader::load`, which first runs `_path_remap` (reading the asset's `.import` `[remap] path` so an imported project resolves `res://icon.png` to `res://.godot/imported/icon-<md5>.ctex`) and then dispatches to the registered `ResourceFormatLoader` for the resulting file, returning a fully-populated Resource (upstream/godot/core/io/resource_loader.cpp).\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4341-4398 guesses the class name from the file extension and returns `ResourceRef` with an EMPTY property map for everything except `.tres`/`.res` and `.gdshader`. So a script's `load(\"res://icon.png\")` yields a Texture2D with no `width`/`height`/`pixels`, and `load(\"res://sfx.wav\")` yields an AudioStream with no samples. Meanwhile `gdresource::importers::UnifiedLoader` (importers.rs:829-869) does exactly the right thing and its own doc comment (importers.rs:816-828) asserts that all consumers go through it — the interpreter does not.\n\nImplementation approach: give the interpreter a project-root-aware `UnifiedLoader` (it already knows the project root for `resource_fs_path`, interpreter.rs:151-152). In the `\"preload\" | \"load\"` arm, call `UnifiedLoader::load(path)`; on success convert the returned `gdresource::Resource` into `ResourceRef` (class_name + all properties, as `load_text_resource` already does); on failure keep the current extension-guess placeholder so unregistered types do not regress. Keep `.tscn`/`.scn` returning `PackedScene` on the existing path so scene instancing is unaffected.\n\nWiring requirement: a `.gd` script executed by the runner calling `load(\"res://icon.png\")` must get a Texture2D whose `pixels` array is populated, including when only `icon.png.import` + `.godot/imported/icon.ctex` exist and the source PNG has been deleted.

**Merged findings (4):** GDScript `load()`/`preload()` routing through the resource format loaders + `.import` remaps; ResourceLoader / ResourceSaver singletons + `load()` returning real resources; ResourceLoader / ResourceSaver script singletons (20 methods + ThreadLoadStatus/CacheMode/SaverFlags enums); ResourceLoader / ResourceSaver singletons

**Prove it:** In a temp project with `icon.png.import` pointing at a real `.godot/imported/icon.ctex` and the source PNG deleted, a GDScript snippet `var t = load("res://icon.png")` followed by reading `t.width`/`t.height` returns the artifact's true dimensions and a non-empty `pixels` array; a second snippet loading `res://sfx.wav` returns an AudioStreamWAV with a non-zero `length_seconds`. (test: `gdscript_load_returns_imported_resource_data`)
acceptance_criteria: In a temp project with `icon.png.import` pointing at a real `.godot/imported/icon.ctex` and the source PNG deleted, a GDScript snippet `var t = load("res://icon.png")` followed by reading `t.width`/`t.height` returns the artifact's true dimensions and a non-empty `pixels` array; a second snippet loading `res://sfx.wav` returns an AudioStreamWAV with a non-zero `length_seconds`. title: Web: drive MainLoop from requestAnimationFrame through FrameDriver in the wasm entry
description:
[audit-key: web-runtime/web-runtime-boot] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/js/engine/engine.js (rtenv main loop) + platform/web/os_web.cpp `OS_Web::main_loop_callback` via `emscripten_set_main_loop` | upstream/godot/platform/web/web_main.cpp (Main::setup → Main::start → OS_Web::run drives the full engine); platform/web/os_web.cpp | extension_api.json MainLoop._initialize(), _process(float)->bool, _physics_process(float)->bool, _finalize(); upstream/godot/core/os/main_loop.cpp; the ProjectSettings key `application/run/main_loop_type` selects the class (a script path works), and returning true from _process quits.

**Godot classes:** MainLoop, SceneTree, Engine, PackedScene, ResourceLoader, ProjectSettings

**Patina today:**
- [web-runtime] `FrameDriver` is a complete, documented rAF driver — delta from successive DOMHighResTimeStamps, pathological-delta clamp, max_fps coalescing with carry, hidden-tab throttling: engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs:36-130. Its own doc says "Created once by the wasm entry point and ticked from requestAnimationFrame" (frame_driver.rs:52-59). It has NO such caller. `rg 'frame_driver|FrameDriver' --type rust crates/` returns exactly three non-defining hits: crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:42 (`pub mod frame_driver;`) and crates/gdscene/tests/web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver.rs:20/58/78/112 — its own test. patina-web does not depend on gdscene at all (crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:16-26), and `rg 'requestAnimationFrame' crates/patina-web/` hits only web/index.html:136,138 (the demo clear loop, which calls `presentClear`, not any engine step). So a green module test masks a browser main loop that nothing drives.
- [web-runtime] `patina-web` is the only wasm32 compilation root (engine-rs/Cargo.toml:20) and it links ONLY gdcore, gdvariant, gdaudio (+ wasm-only gdrender3d): crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:16-51. gdscene, gdresource, gdobject, gdscript-interop and gdrender2d are NOT dependencies, so no SceneTree, no .tscn/.tres loader, no ClassDB, no GDScript VM and no 2D renderer exist on wasm32. The crate's own header admits it: crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs:9-10 ("Subsystems that still depend on native-only crates (gdscene -> std::fs) are cfg-gated and brought online by the remaining web beads"). The complete exported wasm surface is three entry points: `__patina_web_start` (src/lib.rs:79-83, sets a panic hook and nothing else), `startCanvasRenderer` (src/canvas.rs:155-167, returns a renderer whose only draw op is `presentClear`, canvas.rs:145-148) and `startWebAudio` (src/web_audio.rs:157-167). The shipped harness page proves the ceiling: crates/patina-web/web/index.html:124-138 animates a clear colour and plays a 440 Hz tone. Greps for absence: `rg 'gdscene|gdresource|gdscript-interop|gdrender2d' crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml` → 0 hits; `rg 'patina_web|patina-web' --type rust,toml` outside the crate → only engine-rs/Cargo.toml:20 and doc comments.
- [engine-virtual-method-table] MainLoop is registered WITH all four virtuals at engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:3957-3962, but nothing dispatches them: `rg -F '"_initialize"' / '"_finalize"' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**'` hits class_db.rs only (plus unrelated ScriptLanguageExtension/EditorVCSInterface rows). The setting is unread: `rg -F 'main_loop_type' engine-rs/crates/ -g '!**/tests/**'` returns 0 hits. patina-runner always constructs the built-in loop — `MainLoop::new(tree)` at engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:358, :490, :609 — with no branch on a project-configured class.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/tests/web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-web/web/index.html, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs, engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/project.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GROUND TRUTH — Godot's web build installs a browser main-loop callback (`emscripten_set_main_loop` from `OS_Web::run`, platform/web/os_web.cpp); each animation frame produces a delta that feeds `Main::iteration`, which runs process callbacks and the fixed-timestep physics accumulator. PATINA — the delta/clamp/max_fps/hidden-throttle logic is fully implemented in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/frame_driver.rs:36-130 and is documented as being ticked by "the wasm entry point" (frame_driver.rs:52-59), but no such caller exists: the only consumers workspace-wide are crates/gdscene/src/lib.rs:42 and crates/gdscene/tests/web_runtime_fixed_timestep_driver.rs. patina-web does not even depend on gdscene (crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:16-26), and the only rAF loop shipped calls `presentClear` (crates/patina-web/web/index.html:124-138). APPROACH — in the new `crates/patina-web/src/engine.rs` (sibling bead), own a `FrameDriver` + `MainLoop` pair; export `#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = tick)] pub fn tick(&mut self, now_ms: f64) -> u32` that calls `FrameDriver::tick(now_ms, &mut main_loop)` and returns the physics steps run; export `setMaxFps` and `setHidden` so the page can forward `Engine.max_fps` and `visibilitychange`. Replace the demo loop in crates/patina-web/web/index.html with `requestAnimationFrame(ts => engine.tick(ts))`. WIRING — the required call path is: browser rAF timestamp → `WebEngine::tick` → `FrameDriver::tick` → `MainLoop::step` → `_process`/`_physics_process` dispatch on scene nodes → renderer present.

**Merged findings (3):** Browser main loop: requestAnimationFrame driving process + fixed-timestep physics accumulation, visibility throttling, max_fps; wasm runtime links a real engine (scene tree + resources + scripts) — Godot's web export runs the SAME engine as native; Custom MainLoop from script — `_initialize`/`_process`/`_physics_process`/`_finalize` + `application/run/main_loop_type`

**Prove it:** Feeding one second of synthetic animation-frame timestamps to the wasm engine handle advances a scripted node's `_process` counter and its `_physics_process` counter to Godot's counts for that wall-clock span (60 physics ticks at the default 60 Hz), independently of whether the second arrives as 60 even callbacks or 5 uneven ones, and a hidden-tab span is throttled without losing time. **Patina today:**
- [web-runtime] No browser input binding exists anywhere in the wasm runtime. `rg 'addEventListener|KeyboardEvent|PointerEvent|getGamepads|requestPointerLock|WheelEvent|TouchEvent' crates/patina-web/` returns only web/index.html:93 (a `click` handler on the demo's "play tone" button). `rg 'web_sys::(Keyboard|Pointer|Mouse|Touch|Wheel)Event' --type rust crates/` → 0 hits; `rg 'requestPointerLock|pointerlockchange' --type rust crates/` → 0 hits. gdplatform has the *semantic* halves — browser standard-mapping gamepad normalization (crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:2041-2060), key-name/keycode tables (input.rs:189-272, 2563-2650), touch↔mouse emulation (input.rs:1838) — but gdplatform is not a dependency of patina-web (crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:16-26), so none of it is reachable from a browser build. - [resources-io] `gdcore/src/file_access.rs` is unconditional `std::fs`: `FileAccess::open` at :282 calls `OpenOptions::open`, and `grep -n 'wasm32\|target_arch' gdcore/src/file_access.rs` → 0 hits, so there is no browser code path at all. `resolve_path` (:190-208) just joins a `user_root()` PathBuf. On the platform side `gdplatform/src/web.rs:329-347` declares `enum WebStorageBackend { LocalStorage, IndexedDB, OPFS }` and its own module header at web.rs:11 calls it "File system access via IndexedDB/OPFS stubs"; the enum has no read/write/flush methods and is only stored as a field on `WebPlatformLayer` (web.rs:380). `gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:104` documents `force_fs_sync()` as flushing "the IDBFS write-back cache" but there is no IDBFS to flush. Result: on wasm32 any `user://` save/load — the mechanism every game uses for save files and settings — has no backing store.
- [web-runtime] `user://` resolves to a real filesystem path and every read/write goes through std::fs: crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs:198-202 (`strip_prefix("user://")` against a configured root, error when unset) with the whole module built on std::fs. On wasm32-unknown-unknown those calls fail, and there is no browser-storage backend: `rg 'indexedDB|IdbFactory|navigator.storage|showSaveFilePicker|OPFS|getDirectoryHandle' --type rust crates/` → 0 hits (the only `IndexedDB` tokens are the dead stub enum `WebStorageBackend::IndexedDB` at crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs:334-341 and a comment at crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs:330). `OS.is_userfs_persistent()` hardcodes false on web (os.rs:331-333). `JavaScriptBridge.force_fs_sync()` is a no-op default (crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:104-105) and the wasm backend does not override it with an IDBFS flush.
- [resources-io] The script-facing FileAccess handle binds exactly 6 methods: `gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14250 call_file_access_instance` handles only `get_as_text`, `get_buffer`, `store_string`, `store_buffer`, `close`, `get_error`, then falls through to `UndefinedFunction` at :14331. The static side (`call_file_access_static`, interpreter.rs:14196) binds only `open`, `file_exists`, `get_file_as_string`. `call_dir_access_instance` (interpreter.rs:14366) binds only open/dir_exists/list_dir_begin/get_next/current_is_dir/list_dir_end/make_dir/remove/rename. Meanwhile `gdcore/src/file_access.rs` HAS working `seek` (:543), `get_position` (:551), `get_length` (:556), `eof_reached` (:566), `get_8/16/32/64` (:489-533), `store_8/16/32/64/float/double` (:444-488), `set_big_endian` (:434) — none reachable from script. DirAccess likewise has `get_files` (:794), `get_directories` (:799), `copy` (:835), `make_dir_recursive` (:856), `change_dir` (:821), `get_current_dir` (:815) unbound. Genuinely absent from both layers: `grep -rn "open_compressed|open_encrypted|store_var|get_pascal_string|get_csv_line|store_csv_line" --include='*.rs'` over engine-rs/crates → 0 hits each; `grep -c "fn get_line|fn get_md5|fn get_sha256|fn get_half|fn get_real|fn create_temp" gdcore/src/file_access.rs` → 0 each. Two behavioral bugs in what IS bound: `get_error` returns a `Variant::String` (interpreter.rs:14322-14329) where Godot returns an int Error code, and `get_buffer` returns a `Variant::Array` of Ints (interpreter.rs:14276-14280) where Godot returns a `PackedByteArray` (a type Patina's Variant already has).
- [input] Absent from BOTH layers. Scripted check of `grep -c` in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs and `grep -c 'fn <name>'` in engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs returns 0/0 for: get_joy_name, get_joy_guid, get_joy_info, is_joy_known, add_joy_mapping, remove_joy_mapping, should_ignore_device, get_joy_vibration_strength, get_joy_vibration_duration, vibrate_handheld, set_joy_light, has_joy_light, joy_connection_changed. `GamepadButton` (input.rs:302-319) has 17 variants and omits JOY_BUTTON_MISC1/PADDLE1-4/TOUCHPAD (indices 15-20). Analog triggers never produce axis values: the client posts only `b.pressed` booleans (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs:10620-10625 `pad.buttons.map(function(b) { return !!b.pressed; })`), and `GamepadAxis::from_standard` returns None for indices 4/5 (input.rs:465-472), so `Input.get_joy_axis(0, JOY_AXIS_TRIGGER_LEFT)` is permanently 0.0.
- [resources-io] Binary resources: `gdresource/src/res_loader.rs:146-150` rejects the compressed variant outright — `if magic == RES_MAGIC_COMPRESSED { return Err(EngineError::Unsupported("compressed binary resource (RSCC) is not supported")) }`; big-endian is likewise rejected at :159-163. PCK: `gdresource/src/pck.rs:229-233` errors on `PACK_DIR_ENCRYPTED` and :293-298 errors on `PACK_FILE_ENCRYPTED` per entry. FileAccess: `grep -rn 'open_compressed|open_encrypted' --include='*.rs'` over engine-rs/crates → 0 hits in both source and tests, and `gdcore/src/file_access.rs` has no such constructors (its `pub fn` list at :282-574 stops at open/read/write/seek). The primitives to build these already exist in-tree: `miniz_oxide` is a gdresource dependency (Cargo.toml) and `gdcore::crypto` provides AES + SHA-256 (used by `gdresource/src/config_file.rs:122-147` for encrypted ConfigFile).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/patina-web/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdrender2d/src/frame_server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/file_access.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/os.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/web.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/res_loader.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GROUND TRUTH — Godot's web platform installs DOM listeners in `platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js` and `display_server_web.cpp`: pointerdown/up/move (with pointer lock and canvas-relative coordinates), keydown/keyup mapped through `dom_keys.inc` to physical keycode + key_label + unicode with echo detection, wheel with deltaMode normalization, touchstart/move/end as ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag, and `navigator.getGamepads()` polled per frame under the W3C standard mapping. It also applies a preventDefault policy so the game keeps space/F-keys while the browser keeps its own. PATINA — nothing binds any of this: `rg 'addEventListener|KeyboardEvent|PointerEvent|getGamepads|requestPointerLock' crates/patina-web/` finds only the demo tone button (web/index.html:93). The mapping logic already exists natively in engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs (standard-mapping gamepad poll at :2041, keycode tables at :2563-2650, touch/pointer emulation at :1838) but gdplatform is not a wasm dependency (crates/patina-web/Cargo.toml:16-26). APPROACH — add gdplatform to patina-web, make it wasm-safe, and add `crates/patina-web/src/input.rs` that installs `web_sys` listeners on the canvas/window, converts each DOM event to `gdplatform::input::InputEvent` (canvas-relative coordinates divided by the DPR scale from crates/patina-web/src/canvas.rs:64-83), pushes them into the engine handle's `InputState`, polls `navigator.getGamepads()` once per tick through the existing `apply_standard_gamepad_poll`, and exposes `requestPointerLock`/`exitPointerLock` for `Input.mouse_mode`. WIRING — required end-to-end path: DOM event → `patina_web::input` converter → `InputState` → `MainLoop` input dispatch → `_input`/`_unhandled_input` on a scripted node and `Input.is_action_pressed` in that script.

**Merged findings (10):** Browser input: pointer events + pointer lock, keyboard code/key mapping, wheel deltaMode normalization, touch, gamepads, preventDefault policy, IME; `user://` persistence on the web target (IndexedDB / OPFS + flush); user:// persistence on web (IndexedDB/OPFS backing + force_fs_sync flush); FileAccess / DirAccess script API surface; Joypad identity, SDL mappings, connection signal, handheld vibration, analog trigger axes; Compressed and encrypted containers: RSCC binary resources, encrypted PCK, FileAccess.open_compressed/open_encrypted; Input singleton method gaps: get_action_raw_strength, is_key_label_pressed, *_by_event, accumulated input, emulate_* toggles, get_last_mouse_screen_velocity, exact_match; Device sensors (accelerometer/gravity/gyroscope/magnetometer) implemented but unreachable from script and unfed by the browser; Bareword scoping of class-scoped constants (CURSOR_*, MOUSE_MODE_*, Object NOTIFICATION_*) in the @GlobalScope namespace; Input / InputMap ClassDB registration

**Prove it:** With a fixture scene whose script records every `_input` event and reads `Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right")`, feeding synthetic browser-shaped events (keydown code=ArrowRight, pointermove at a canvas point under a 2x device pixel ratio, wheel deltaMode=1, gamepad poll with axis 0 at 1.0) through the engine handle yields the Godot events with correct physical keycode, canvas-local position in project pixels, normalized wheel factor, and a pressed `ui_right` action. title: GDScript: resolve ClassDB integer/enum constants through Class.CONSTANT member access
description:
[audit-key: xr-peripheral/classdb-enum-static-access] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/servers/xr/xr_server.cpp:87-100 (BIND_ENUM_CONSTANT TRACKER_*/RESET_*); extension_api.json .classes[XRServer].enums = TrackerType/RotationMode; XRHandTracker.HandJoint (26 values) | upstream/godot/servers/xr/xr_server.cpp:60-100 (bindings), :299-312 (get_interfaces -> TypedArray<Dictionary> of {id,name}), :329-356 (add_tracker/remove_tracker emit tracker_added/tracker_updated/tracker_removed), :358+ (get_trackers filters by type mask); upstream/godot/doc/classes/XRServer.xml:72-77 | extension_api.json: XRServer 4 props / 22 methods / 6 signals (reference_frame_changed, interface_added/removed, tracker_added/updated/removed); XRController3D 5 signals (button_pressed/released, input_float_changed, input_vector2_changed, profile_changed); XRPositionalTracker 7 signals; XRNode3D tracking_changed; XRInterface play_area_changed; XRInterfaceExtension 37 methods

**Godot classes:** XRServer, XRHandTracker, XRBodyTracker, XRFaceTracker, XRPositionalTracker, XRInterface, XRCamera3D, XRController3D, XRAnchor3D, XRNode3D, XRInterfaceExtension

**Patina today:**
- [xr-peripheral] class_db.rs registers 183 XR enum constants — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5205-5460 (XRTracker/XRPositionalTracker/XRInterface/XRHandTracker/XRBodyTracker/XRFaceTracker constants). NONE are reachable via GDScript's `Class.CONSTANT` syntax: /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14111-14159 `try_static_member` matches ONLY "Vector2"|"Vector3"|"Color"|"Engine"|"FileAccess", then falls back to `variant_math::static_member` (crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs:427-448 — Transform2D/Transform3D/Basis/Quaternion/Plane only) and `global_constants::global_enum_member` (crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs:1170-1179, @GlobalScope enums only). With both None, interpreter.rs:3228 falls through to `eval_expr(Ident("XRServer"))`, which ends at interpreter.rs:2763 `UndefinedVariable`. Confirming greps: `rg 'class_get_integer_constant' crates/gdscript-interop/src` -> only the ClassDB.* method arm at interpreter.rs:14968-14994; `rg 'TRACKER_HAND\b|HAND_JOINT_WRIST' crates/` -> only class_db.rs and /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/xr_trackers.rs:87, which reads them via `ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant(...)` — i.e. the green test proves exactly the path a real script cannot use. Cross-cutting: the same hole hides Node.PROCESS_MODE_*, Tween.TRANS_*, etc.
- [xr-peripheral] /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:2121-2208 `call_xr_server_static` implements exactly 8 arms: get_hmd_transform, find_interface, get_interfaces, get_interface_count, add_tracker, remove_tracker, get_tracker, get_trackers; every other name errors 'XRServer has no method'. (a) interpreter.rs:2132-2136 constructs a FRESH `gdplatform::XrServer::new()` per call; `XrServer::default()` leaves `session_active=false` (crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs:11-15, :37-42), so `get_head_pose()` is always None and the method always returns identity basis + Vector3::ZERO — and the only test, crates/gdscript-interop/tests/xr_server.rs:29 `hmd_transform_is_reachable`, asserts only `matches!(.., Variant::Transform3D(_))`. (b) interpreter.rs:2157 returns `PackedStringArray(["WebXR"])`; Godot returns `Dictionary[]` with `id` and `name` keys (xr_server.cpp:299-309), so `XRServer.get_interfaces()[0]["name"]` breaks. (c) missing: get/set_world_scale, get/set_world_origin, get_reference_frame, clear_reference_frame, center_on_hmd, set/is_camera_locked_to_origin, add_interface, remove_interface, get_interface, get_primary_interface, set_primary_interface — grep `rg 'get_world_scale|center_on_hmd|get_primary_interface|camera_locked_to_origin' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdscene/src crates/gdobject/src` -> 0 hits. (d) add_tracker/remove_tracker (interpreter.rs:2165-2192) emit nothing, and `XRServer.connect(...)` is not an arm at all, so no script can observe tracker_added/tracker_updated/tracker_removed. (e) get_trackers (interpreter.rs:2193-2204) ignores its `tracker_types` mask argument. ClassDB registration is bare: class_db.rs:1493 `ClassRegistration::new("XRServer").parent("Object")` with no properties, no TrackerType/RotationMode enums.
- [registered-class-member-depth] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:1493 XRServer, :1500 XRNode3D, :1504 XRController3D, :1505 XRAnchor3D, :1506 XRCamera3D, :5215 XRPositionalTracker, :5225 XRInterface, :5601 XRInterfaceExtension register zero properties, methods and signals. A WebXR implementation does exist — engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs models the WebXRInterface session lifecycle — and its own doc comment at gdplatform/src/xr.rs:262 states "**Not yet wired to script.** `XRServer.find_interface(\"WebXR\")` and emitting …", confirming no script path. So the XR surface is registered names only, with neither ClassDB members nor script reachability.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/xr.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: every `BIND_ENUM_CONSTANT`/`BIND_CONSTANT` on an engine class is reachable from GDScript as `ClassName.CONSTANT` — `XRServer.TRACKER_HAND` (upstream/godot/servers/xr/xr_server.cpp:87-100), `XRHandTracker.HAND_JOINT_WRIST` (servers/xr/xr_hand_tracker.h), `XRInterface.XR_PLAY_AREA_ROOMSCALE` (servers/xr/xr_interface.cpp). GDScript's analyzer resolves the identifier to a ClassDB class and then reads its integer-constant table.\n\nPatina current state: the constants ARE registered — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:5205-5460 holds 183 XR enum constants alone, and `gdobject::class_get_integer_constant` (class_db.rs:535) reads them. But GDScript member access never consults ClassDB: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:14111-14159 `try_static_member` handles only Vector2/Vector3/Color/Engine/FileAccess, then defers to `variant_math::static_member` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/variant_math.rs:427-448) and `global_constants::global_enum_member` (engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/global_constants.rs:1170) which covers @GlobalScope enums only. When both miss, interpreter.rs:3228 evaluates `Ident("XRServer")` and errors `UndefinedVariable` at interpreter.rs:2763. The only working spelling is `ClassDB.class_get_integer_constant("XRHandTracker", "HAND_JOINT_WRIST")` — which is exactly what the green test engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/xr_trackers.rs:87 asserts, so the registration work looks done while no script can use it.\n\nImplementation: in `try_static_member` (interpreter.rs:14111), after the existing arms and before returning None, add a ClassDB fallback: if `gdobject::class_exists(type_name)`, return `gdobject::class_get_integer_constant(type_name, member).map(Variant::Int)`. Resolution order must stay Godot's: builtin math statics -> @GlobalScope enum member -> ClassDB class constant, so a @GlobalScope name never gets shadowed. Ensure the relevant `register_*_classes()` tables have been seeded before the lookup (register_3d_classes is what carries the XR constants — class_db.rs:955).\n\nWiring requirement: a .gd script loaded through the normal Interpreter path (no ClassDB.* helper call) must evaluate `XRServer.TRACKER_HAND` and `XRHandTracker.HAND_JOINT_WRIST` to the Godot integers, end to end.
