comments.author: bone
comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, CORRECTION to my partial (msg 77769). I said three of the six named methods "are not implemented" and called each "a new engine capability, not another dispatch arm". That is WRONG. All three have engine support already:

  * play_section — gdscene/src/animation.rs:836 `pub fn play_section(&mut self, name, start, end, custom_blend, custom_speed, from_end)`, alongside set_section/reset_section/has_section/get_section_start_time/get_section_end_time (:829-865).
  * root motion — :1298 `pub fn consume_root_motion(&self, prev_time, curr_time) -> RootMotionDelta`.
  * MANUAL mode — `AnimationCallbackMode` enum at :538 with the Godot integer mapping at :550.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG: I grepped the INTERPRETER for dispatch of each name, found 0, and concluded the engine side was absent too. I never grepped animation.rs for them. That is the same generalisation error as pat-s3rrv.41 (verifying one example and extrapolating) in a new costume: I verified one LAYER and extrapolated to another. The correct check was one `grep -c` per name against the engine module, which is what I did afterwards: section fields 9 hits, callback-mode 11, root-motion 4.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE REMAINING WORK: it is smaller and lower-risk than I reported. play_section is a dispatch arm over an existing 7-parameter method (note the extra custom_blend/custom_speed/from_end — a 3-arg script call must supply Godot defaults). Root motion needs the player to remember the previous frame`s time so `get_root_motion_position()` can call consume_root_motion(prev, curr) with no arguments; the computation itself exists. MANUAL mode needs a callback_mode field on AnimationPlayer — the struct has none (I checked, 0 hits) — plus MainLoop skipping auto-advance for it; the enum and its integer mapping are done.

Nobody should plan off the "new engine capability" framing in msg 77769. Treat the remaining scope as wiring plus one struct field.

Landed and unchanged: has_animation, get_animation_list, and the script-side speed_scale get/set.

title: Animation: add Bezier and Animation track types end-to-end (parse, sample, apply, save)
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-track-types] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json Animation.TrackType = TYPE_VALUE, TYPE_POSITION_3D, TYPE_ROTATION_3D, TYPE_SCALE_3D, TYPE_BLEND_SHAPE, TYPE_METHOD, TYPE_BEZIER, TYPE_AUDIO, TYPE_ANIMATION; methods bezier_track_insert_key / bezier_track_set_key_in_handle / bezier_track_set_key_out_handle / bezier_track_interpolate and animation_track_insert_key / animation_track_set_key_animation (upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp) | upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp (`track_set_interpolation_loop_wrap`, `_interpolate` wrap-around branch, `Animation::UPDATE_CAPTURE`, `add_marker`/`get_marker_names`/`get_marker_at_time`, `set_step`); doc/classes/Animation.xml

**Godot classes:** Animation, AnimationPlayer, AnimationMixer

**Patina today:**
- [animation] Patina's `TrackType` enum has 7 variants and neither Bezier nor Animation — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:85-104. `grep -rn 'TrackType::Bezier' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0 hits. The .tscn reader deliberately drops them: `tscn_track_type` returns `None` for anything not in {value, method, audio, position_3d, rotation_3d, scale_3d, blend_shape} — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs:171-182, and `track_from_props` returns `None` on that (animation_tscn.rs:112), with the doc comment at animation_tscn.rs:167-170 stating bezier/animation tracks are "not modeled by Patina's sampler". A clip authored in Godot's bezier curve editor therefore loads with that track silently absent.
- [animation] loop_wrap: `AnimationTrack::sample` clamps at the last keyframe and returns its value — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:341-345 — so a LOOP_LINEAR clip never interpolates last-key→first-key and pops at the wrap. `crates/gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs:372` *writes* `tracks/{i}/loop_wrap = true` but nothing parses it (grep `loop_wrap` → saver + two test fixtures only, 3 hits total). Per-key transition exponent: explicitly not read, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs:217-220. UPDATE_CAPTURE: parsed (animation_tscn.rs:227) but sampled as Continuous with the comment "capture blending is not yet modeled" — animation.rs:152-155 and the `TrackUpdateMode::Discrete`-only branch at animation.rs:320. Markers: `grep -rn 'marker_names' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0; `add_marker` hits only `gdeditor/src/profiler_panel.rs`. `Animation.step` unparsed (grep `\bstep\b` in animation.rs → only unrelated comments).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_saver.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `Animation::TYPE_BEZIER` stores per-key `{value, in_handle: Vector2, out_handle: Vector2}` and interpolates with `_bezier_interpolate` over the two handles (upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp, `bezier_track_interpolate`); it is what the editor's curve view produces and is the normal way a designer keys a single float with eased handles. `Animation::TYPE_ANIMATION` keys a StringName clip name on a *nested* AnimationPlayer, so a master timeline can trigger sub-clips (`animation_track_set_key_animation`). Their .tscn form is `tracks/N/type = "bezier"` with `keys = {"times": PackedFloat32Array, "points": PackedFloat32Array (5 floats per key: value, in.x, in.y, out.x, out.y), "handle_modes": PackedInt32Array}` and `tracks/N/type = "animation"` with `keys = {"times":…, "clips": [...]}`.

Patina current state: `TrackType` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:85-104) lacks both; `tscn_track_type` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tscn.rs:171-182) maps them to `None` and `track_from_props` (animation_tscn.rs:112) drops the whole track. The animation loads with fewer tracks than authored and nothing warns.

Implementation approach: add `TrackType::Bezier` and `TrackType::Animation` to animation.rs:85; give `KeyFrame` an optional `handles: Option<(Vector2, Vector2)>` (or a parallel bezier key vec on `AnimationTrack`) and implement `sample` for Bezier by solving the cubic in the time axis exactly as the existing `cubic_bezier_y` helper (animation.rs:1402) does, but with absolute handle offsets rather than the unit-square CSS form. Parse both forms in `fill_dictionary_track` (animation_tscn.rs:199) and add the inverse in `scene_saver.rs:570` so a round-trip is lossless. Apply Animation tracks in `SceneTree::process_animations_in_mode` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2173) next to the existing method/audio track dispatch (scene_tree.rs:2268-2310): resolve the track's node path to a child AnimationPlayer and call `play(clip)` when the key is crossed.

Wiring requirement: .tscn load → track present in the player → `MainLoop::step` idle/physics animation phase writes the bezier-interpolated property onto the node and starts the sub-clip on the nested player.

**Merged findings (2):** Animation track types TYPE_BEZIER and TYPE_ANIMATION; Track-level fidelity: interpolation loop_wrap across the loop point, per-key transition easing exponent, UPDATE_CAPTURE blending, Animation markers, Animation.step

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a bezier track keying `Sprite2D:position:x` with non-linear handles produces, after stepping the MainLoop to the segment midpoint, a value that differs from the linear midpoint by the handle-implied amount; a `tracks/N/type="animation"` key crossing starts the named clip on a child AnimationPlayer (its `current_animation` becomes that clip); re-saving the scene reproduces both track blocks. (test: `bezier_and_animation_tracks_from_tscn_drive_properties`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test bezier_and_animation_tracks_from_tscn_drive_properties`.
acceptance_criteria: A .tscn with a bezier track keying `Sprite2D:position:x` with non-linear handles produces, after stepping the MainLoop to the segment midpoint, a value that differs from the linear midpoint by the handle-implied amount; a `tracks/N/type="animation"` key crossing starts the named clip on a child AnimationPlayer (its `current_animation` becomes that clip); re-saving the scene reproduces both track blocks. (test: `bezier_and_animation_tracks_from_tscn_drive_properties`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test bezier_and_animation_tracks_from_tscn_drive_properties`.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, opening survey. Two findings that change how this bead should be approached.

1. A NAMING TRAP. `animation.rs` has `TransitionType::CubicBezier(f32,f32,f32,f32)` (:31) with EASE_IN/EASE_OUT/EASE_IN_OUT presets. That is NOT a Godot bezier TRACK — it is the easing curve between two keys on any track. A Godot bezier track is a value track whose every key carries its own `in_handle`/`out_handle` Vector2. Grepping for "bezier" finds 12 hits in animation.rs and none of them are this feature; `in_handle`/`out_handle` are 0 hits workspace-wide. Anyone starting here should not mistake the existing CubicBezier for partial support — it will look like the feature is half-done when none of it exists.

2. THE GAP IS DELIBERATE AND PINNED BY A TEST. `animation_tscn.rs:173-175` maps only value -> Property, method -> Method, audio -> Audio. There is an existing test at :644 `unsupported_track_type_is_skipped` asserting BOTH `tscn_track_type("bezier").is_none()` AND `tscn_track_type("animation").is_none()`, with the comment "A bezier track is not mis-read as a value track". So implementing this bead REQUIRES rewriting that test — it currently encodes the opposite of the acceptance. Landing the parser without touching it produces a red suite, and a reviewer seeing that test could reasonably think the change is wrong.

SCOPE, stated honestly rather than estimated: this is the largest bead I have surveyed in this run. It needs (a) two new `TrackType` variants — and an enum extension breaks every exhaustive match, which on pat-s3rrv.36 cost me two verify cycles across crates; (b) per-key in/out handle data on bezier keys, which no key struct currently carries; (c) cubic sampling through those handles; (d) an animation-track key STARTING a clip on a child AnimationPlayer, i.e. cross-node control from inside the sampler; (e) round-tripping both blocks through scene_saver; (f) rewriting the negative test above.

I am not starting the enum extension at the tail of a very long context. Half of (a) leaves the tree non-compiling for every other agent in gdscene, and I would rather hand over an accurate map than a broken working tree. The map above is the deliverable for this iteration.

RECOMMENDED ORDER for whoever takes it: rewrite the negative test FIRST so the suite states the intended contract, then (a)+(b) together in one commit since the variants and their payload are inseparable, then (c), then (d), then (e). Godot`s bezier handle semantics are in upstream/godot/scene/resources/animation.cpp — use it as the oracle for handle-relative-vs-absolute, which is exactly the kind of detail that is easy to assume and wrong.

comments.author: bone
comments.text:
FuchsiaDeer, correcting my own scope framing from msg 77806.

I wrote that adding TrackType variants "breaks every exhaustive match" and cited pat-s3rrv.36 costing two verify cycles, implying this is dangerous. I then declined to start on that basis. I had not measured it. Measuring now:

  * `TrackType::` appears 60 times across gdscene/src — but almost all are CONSTRUCTIONS or comparisons, not matches.
  * Exhaustive matches on a track type: **4**, in two files — animation.rs:1840, animation_tscn.rs:155, :187, :234.
  * Existing variants: Property, Method, Audio, Position3D, Rotation3D, Scale3D, BlendShape (7).

Four match sites is tractable, and the compiler names each one. My "breaks every exhaustive match" was true of pat-s3rrv.36`s FragmentInstruction (which had matches in two separate crates including WGSL translators) but I carried that fear across to a different enum without checking. Nobody should skip this bead because of my framing.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE from that report, and I still believe both:
  * TransitionType::CubicBezier is NOT bezier-track support — it is per-key easing. in_handle/out_handle are 0 hits workspace-wide.
  * animation_tscn.rs:644 `unsupported_track_type_is_skipped` asserts bezier and animation are unsupported, i.e. the opposite of this bead`s acceptance. It must be rewritten or the suite goes red.

REVISED SEQUENCING, now that the enum cost is known to be small: the variants + the 4 match arms + the parser mapping + the negative-test rewrite are ONE coherent commit and are not the hard part. The hard part is what makes a bezier track actually bezier — per-key in/out handle data on the key struct (nothing carries it today) and cubic sampling through it. Adding the variants WITHOUT that would parse a bezier track and then sample it linearly, which is silently wrong output rather than an honest unsupported-skip — strictly worse than today. So do not land the variants alone.

The animation-track half (a key starting a clip on a child AnimationPlayer) is independent of the bezier half and could ship separately.

title: Animation: barycentric blend spaces (triangles + auto_triangles) and the full blend-space parameter surface
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-tree-blending] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_blend_space_2d.cpp (`_blend_node` with Delaunay `triangles` + barycentric weights, `auto_triangles`, `blend_mode` INTERPOLATED/DISCRETE/CARRY, `min_space`, `max_space`, `snap`, `x_label`/`y_label`, `sync`), animation_blend_space_1d.cpp; doc/classes/AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D.xml | upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_blend_tree.cpp — AnimationNodeOneShot (mix_mode MIX_MODE_BLEND/ADD, fadein_time+fadein_curve, fadeout_time+fadeout_curve, autorestart, autorestart_delay, autorestart_random_delay, break_loop_at_end, OneShotRequest) and AnimationNodeAnimation (play_mode PLAY_MODE_FORWARD/BACKWARD, use_custom_timeline, timeline_length, stretch_time_scale, start_offset, loop_mode); doc/classes/AnimationNodeOneShot.xml, AnimationNodeAnimation.xml

**Godot classes:** AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D, AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D, AnimationNodeOneShot, AnimationNodeAnimation

**Patina today:**
- [animation] `sample_blend_space_2d` bilinearly blends ONLY when there are exactly four axis-aligned points, and otherwise snaps to the nearest point — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:1444-1460 (`if space.points.len() == 4 { bilinear_sample(...) } … nearest_point(space, library)`). `BlendSpace2D` carries only `points`, `blend_position`, `elapsed` (animation_tree.rs:142-149); `BlendSpace1D` the same (:117-124). `grep -rn 'auto_triangles' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0 hits; the `.tscn` builders read only `blend_point_N/node` and `blend_point_N/pos` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs:303-335) — `triangles`, `min_space`, `max_space`, `snap`, `blend_mode`, `sync` are all discarded (they appear only inside test fixture text at animation_tree_tscn.rs:719-720). A 9-point 8-directional locomotion blend space therefore snaps between clips instead of blending.
- [animation] Patina's `OneShot` carries base/shot/fade_in/fade_out/shot_length/trigger_param/elapsed only — /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:167-183 with `fire`/`abort`/`fade_out_now` at :368-388. `grep -rn 'autorestart|mix_mode|break_loop_at_end' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0 hits each, so the shot always blends (never adds), never auto-restarts, and its fades are linear (no Curve). `AnimationNode::Animation { name, position }` (animation_tree.rs:28) has no play_mode/timeline fields; `grep -rn 'use_custom_timeline|stretch_time_scale' --include=*.rs crates/` → 0 hits each.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/scene/animation/animation_blend_space_2d.cpp): a 2D blend space triangulates its points (explicitly via the serialized `triangles = PackedInt32Array(...)` or automatically when `auto_triangles` is on, using a Delaunay pass) and blends the three clips of the containing triangle by barycentric weights; `blend_mode` selects INTERPOLATED / DISCRETE (pick one) / CARRY (pick one, carry the playhead); `min_space`/`max_space`/`snap` define and quantise the coordinate space; `sync` keeps unselected inputs advancing. 1D spaces blend the two bracketing points with the same knobs.

Patina current state: `sample_blend_space_2d` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree.rs:1444-1460) handles exactly one shape — four points on an axis-aligned rectangle, bilinear — and falls back to `nearest_point` for everything else, so the common 9-point directional space snaps. `BlendSpace2D`/`BlendSpace1D` (animation_tree.rs:142-149, :117-124) carry only points/position/clock. The .tscn builders (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation_tree_tscn.rs:303-335) read only `blend_point_N/node` and `blend_point_N/pos`; `triangles`, `auto_triangles`, `min_space`, `max_space`, `snap`, `blend_mode`, `sync` are dropped.

Implementation approach: add the missing fields to `BlendSpace1D`/`BlendSpace2D` in animation_tree.rs and parse them in `build_blend_space_1d`/`build_blend_space_2d` (animation_tree_tscn.rs:303, :319), including the flat `triangles` int array (triples of point indices). Replace `sample_blend_space_2d` with: clamp/snap `blend_position` into [min_space, max_space]; locate the containing triangle (explicit list, else a Delaunay triangulation computed once and cached on the node); compute barycentric weights; blend the three clips with the existing N-way helper (extend `blend_value_lists`, animation_tree.rs, to a weighted list form); fall back to the nearest edge projection when the position is outside every triangle, as Godot does. Honor `blend_mode` DISCRETE/CARRY by short-circuiting to a single clip (CARRY preserving `elapsed`). Do the 1D analogue for min/max/snap/sync.

Wiring requirement: .tscn AnimationTree → `SceneTree::process_animation_trees` (scene_tree.rs:2511) driven from `MainLoop::step` (main_loop.rs:2968), with `parameters/<node>/blend_position` set from a script.

**Merged findings (2):** AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D/2D — triangulated barycentric blending, auto_triangles, min/max space, snap, blend_mode, sync; AnimationNodeOneShot full parameter surface (mix_mode, autorestart + delay + random delay, fadein/fadeout curves, request enum NONE/FIRE/ABORT/FADE_OUT, break_loop_at_end, active/internal_active params) and AnimationNodeAnimation options (play_mode, use_custom_timeline, timeline_length, stretch_time_scale, start_offset, loop_mode)

**Prove it:** A scene with a 2D blend space of 9 points (centre + 8 directions) and `blend_position = Vector2(0.3, 0.3)` set from a script produces a sampled property value that is a strict barycentric mix of the three enclosing clips — different from any single clip's value and matching the barycentric expectation within epsilon — where today it equals one clip exactly; `blend_mode = DISCRETE` reverts to the single nearest clip; positions outside the hull clamp to the hull edge, not to an arbitrary nearest point. (test: `blend_space_2d_barycentric_blend_from_scene`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test blend_space_2d_barycentric_blend_from_scene`.
acceptance_criteria: A scene with a 2D blend space of 9 points (centre + 8 directions) and `blend_position = Vector2(0.3, 0.3)` set from a script produces a sampled property value that is a strict barycentric mix of the three enclosing clips — different from any single clip's value and matching the barycentric expectation within epsilon — where today it equals one clip exactly; `blend_mode = DISCRETE` reverts to the single nearest clip; positions outside the hull clamp to the hull edge, not to an arbitrary nearest point. (test: `blend_space_2d_barycentric_blend_from_scene`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test blend_space_2d_barycentric_blend_from_scene`.

title: Animation: apply Tween process/pause modes and finish the Tween/Tweener script surface
description:
[audit-key: animation/anim-tween] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/animation/tween.cpp (`Tween::can_process`, TWEEN_PAUSE_BOUND/STOP/PROCESS, TWEEN_PROCESS_PHYSICS/IDLE, `set_ignore_time_scale`, `custom_step`, `interpolate_value`); doc/classes/Tween.xml, PropertyTweener.xml (from, from_current, as_relative, set_custom_interpolator)

**Godot classes:** Tween, PropertyTweener, MethodTweener, SubtweenTweener

**Patina today:**
- [animation] `Tween::can_process(tree_paused, bound_node_can_process)` is a faithful port at /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs:591-610 with ZERO production callers: `grep -rn 'can_process' --include=*.rs crates/` returns the tween.rs definition, an unrelated `SceneTree` node gate (scene_tree.rs:3204) and three integration tests. `SceneTree::process_tweens` (scene_tree.rs:2596-2650) advances every tween unconditionally, and `MainLoop::step` skips the entire animation/tween phase under pause (main_loop.rs:2954-2977, whose own comment admits per-node `process_mode` is not modelled), so a TWEEN_PAUSE_PROCESS tween freezes and a TWEEN_PROCESS_PHYSICS tween runs at render rate. Script dispatch `SceneAccess::tween_call` (gdscene/src/scripting.rs:2954-3098) implements 15 verbs; `tween_subtween`, `bind_node`, `custom_step`, `set_process_mode`, `set_pause_mode`, `set_ignore_time_scale`, `get_total_elapsed_time`, `interpolate_value`, `get_loops_left`, `from`, `from_current`, `as_relative` each appear exactly once in the workspace — as a ClassDB `MethodInfo` in gdobject/src/class_db.rs:2479-2560 — so ClassDB advertises them while a real call falls through to UndefinedFunction. `TweenStep::subtween` exists (tween.rs:470) but is unreachable. Signals `loop_finished`/`step_finished` are declared (class_db.rs:2502) and never emitted.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth (upstream/godot/scene/animation/tween.cpp): `Tween::can_process` decides each frame from `pause_mode` (BOUND — follow the bound node's process mode, STOP, PROCESS) and the tree's paused state; `process_mode` (IDLE / PHYSICS) picks the phase; `set_ignore_time_scale` bypasses `Engine.time_scale`; `bind_node` auto-kills the tween with the node. `PropertyTweener` adds `from(value)`, `from_current()`, `as_relative()`, `set_custom_interpolator(callable)`; `Tween` adds `tween_subtween`, `custom_step(delta)`, `interpolate_value(...)`, `get_total_elapsed_time`, `get_loops_left`, and the `step_finished(idx)` / `loop_finished(count)` signals.

Patina current state: `Tween::can_process` is ported at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/tween.rs:591-610 and has no production caller — `SceneTree::process_tweens` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:2596) steps every tween in the idle phase and `MainLoop::step` skips the whole phase under pause (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2954-2977). A pause-menu tween (TWEEN_PAUSE_PROCESS) therefore freezes with the game, and a physics-mode tween jitters. On the script side, `SceneAccess::tween_call` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scripting.rs:2954-3098) covers 15 verbs; the twelve listed above exist only as ClassDB `MethodInfo` entries (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:2479-2560), so `ClassDB.class_has_method("Tween", "tween_subtween")` is true while calling it errors — and `TweenStep::subtween` (tween.rs:470) is real but unreachable. `as_relative()`/`from()` are the two most-used PropertyTweener verbs and are absent entirely.

Implementation approach: (1) store `process_mode`, `pause_mode`, `ignore_time_scale`, `bound_node` on `Tween` (tween.rs:533) with setters; (2) in `SceneTree::process_tweens` (scene_tree.rs:2596) call `tween.can_process(self.is_paused(), bound_node_can_process)` per tween and skip when false, and split into `process_tweens_in_mode(delta, TweenProcessMode)` called from both the physics tick and the idle phase in `MainLoop::step` (main_loop.rs:2874 / :2977); move the tween call OUT of the blanket `if !paused` guard so PROCESS-mode tweens keep running; (3) add the missing arms to `tween_call` (scripting.rs:2954): `from`/`from_current`/`as_relative` mutate the last step's start value (`with_last_step`, scripting.rs:3018 pattern), `tween_subtween` wraps `TweenStep::subtween`, `custom_step`/`interpolate_value`/`get_total_elapsed_time`/`get_loops_left`/`bind_node`/`set_process_mode`/`set_pause_mode`/`set_ignore_time_scale` map to the new fields; (4) emit `step_finished` and `loop_finished` on the tween handle where `finished` is already emitted (scene_tree.rs:2665).

Wiring requirement: a script in a loaded .tscn creates the tween with `create_tween()` and its behavior differs correctly under `get_tree().paused = true`.

**Prove it:** With `get_tree().paused = true`, a tween created with `set_pause_mode(Tween.TWEEN_PAUSE_PROCESS)` keeps advancing its target property across MainLoop steps while a default (BOUND, owner not PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS) tween does not; a `set_process_mode(Tween.TWEEN_PROCESS_PHYSICS)` tween advances exactly once per physics tick; `tween_property(node,"position",Vector2(10,0),1.0).as_relative()` ends at start+10 rather than at 10; `tween_subtween` runs a nested tween to completion as one step; `loop_finished` fires per loop. (test: `tween_pause_process_modes_and_tweener_surface`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test tween_pause_process_modes_and_tweener_surface`.
acceptance_criteria: With `get_tree().paused = true`, a tween created with `set_pause_mode(Tween.TWEEN_PAUSE_PROCESS)` keeps advancing its target property across MainLoop steps while a default (BOUND, owner not PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS) tween does not; a `set_process_mode(Tween.TWEEN_PROCESS_PHYSICS)` tween advances exactly once per physics tick; `tween_property(node,"position",Vector2(10,0),1.0).as_relative()` ends at start+10 rather than at 10; `tween_subtween` runs a nested tween to completion as one step; `loop_finished` fires per loop. (test: `tween_pause_process_modes_and_tweener_surface`) runnable via `cargo nextest run --test tween_pause_process_modes_and_tweener_surface`.

title: Audio import: MP3 through the loader, .import remap in the audio bridge, WAV loop/trim options
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/audio-import-artifacts] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_wav.cpp (save extension `sample`, compress/mode = PCM/IMA-ADPCM/QOA, edit/loop_mode+begin+end, edit/trim, edit/normalize, force/{8_bit,mono,max_rate}), modules/vorbis/resource_importer_ogg_vorbis.cpp (`oggvorbisstr`), modules/minimp3/resource_importer_mp3.cpp (`mp3str`)

**Godot classes:** ResourceImporterWAV, ResourceImporterOggVorbis, ResourceImporterMP3, AudioStreamWAV, AudioStreamMP3, AudioStreamOggVorbis

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] MP3 is decodable but unreachable: `gdaudio::decode::decode_mp3` exists (engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs:276) with `is_mp3` (decode.rs:263), yet `decode_auto` (decode.rs:119-133) branches only on `RIFF` and `OggS`, and `AudioStreamLoader`'s `AudioFormat::from_extension` (engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs:55-62) accepts only "wav" and "ogg". The audio bridge ignores import remaps entirely: `AudioServerBridge::resolve_stream_path` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:148-154) does `base.join(path.strip_prefix("res://"))` with no `.import` lookup, so an imported project whose `music.ogg` was replaced by `.godot/imported/music-<md5>.oggvorbisstr` finds nothing. No artifact format is supported: `grep -rn 'oggvorbisstr|mp3str' crates/ --include=*.rs` → 0 hits. `import_wav` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:487-548) never reads the `smpl` chunk or the `[params]` loop/trim/normalize options, and there is no QOA support (`grep -rn 'qoa|QOA' crates/ --include=*.rs` → 0 hits) even though `engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/ima_adpcm.rs` exists.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `ResourceImporterWAV` writes a `.sample` artifact honoring compress/mode (PCM/IMA-ADPCM/QOA), edit/loop_mode+loop_begin+loop_end, edit/trim, edit/normalize and force/{8_bit,mono,max_rate}; `ResourceImporterOggVorbis` writes `.oggvorbisstr` and `ResourceImporterMP3` writes `.mp3str`, both carrying loop/loop_offset and bpm/beat metadata. At runtime an AudioStreamPlayer's `stream` resolves through the `.import` remap to the artifact, never to the loose source (upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_wav.cpp, modules/vorbis/, modules/minimp3/).\n\nPatina current state: MP3 decoding exists (`gdaudio::decode::decode_mp3`, engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/decode.rs:276) but is unreachable — `decode_auto` (decode.rs:119-133) sniffs only RIFF/OggS and `AudioFormat::from_extension` (engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/import.rs:55-62) accepts only wav/ogg, so no `.mp3` in any scene ever plays. `AudioServerBridge::resolve_stream_path` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:148-154) joins `res://` to the base dir with no `.import` remap. No `.sample`/`.oggvorbisstr`/`.mp3str` reader exists (grep → 0 hits). `import_wav` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:487-548) ignores the `smpl` loop chunk and every `[params]` edit option; there is no QOA support.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) add `Mp3` to `gdaudio::import::AudioFormat` and its `from_extension`, and add an MP3 branch to `decode_auto` guarded by `is_mp3`; (2) in `audio_server_bridge.rs`, route `resolve_stream_path` through a shared helper that checks for `<source>.import` and returns the `[remap] path` artifact when present; (3) add readers for `.oggvorbisstr`/`.mp3str` (a Godot Resource wrapper whose `data` is the raw ogg/mp3 byte payload) and `.sample` (AudioStreamWAV with `data` + `loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end`) in `gdresource`, and register the three extensions in `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults`; (4) parse the WAV `smpl` chunk in `import_wav` and set `loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end` on the resource so `gdaudio::stream` loops correctly.\n\nWiring requirement: an AudioStreamPlayer in a `.tscn` whose `stream` is `res://music.mp3` (and separately one whose `music.ogg` only exists as a `.oggvorbisstr` artifact behind a `.import` sidecar) must produce non-silent mixed output through the existing AudioServerBridge tick.

**Prove it:** A scene with an AudioStreamPlayer pointing at `res://tone.mp3` mixes non-zero samples through the AudioServerBridge; a second scene pointing at `res://tone.ogg`, where only `tone.ogg.import` + `.godot/imported/tone-<md5>.oggvorbisstr` exist on disk (source deleted), also mixes non-zero samples; a WAV fixture carrying a `smpl` loop chunk loads with `loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end` set and loops rather than stopping. (test: `audio_import_remap_and_mp3_stream_plays`)
acceptance_criteria: A scene with an AudioStreamPlayer pointing at `res://tone.mp3` mixes non-zero samples through the AudioServerBridge; a second scene pointing at `res://tone.ogg`, where only `tone.ogg.import` + `.godot/imported/tone-<md5>.oggvorbisstr` exist on disk (source deleted), also mixes non-zero samples; a WAV fixture carrying a `smpl` loop chunk loads with `loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end` set and loops rather than stopping. (test: `audio_import_remap_and_mp3_stream_plays`)

title: CompressedTexture2D: decode VRAM-compressed .ctex (BC1/BC3/ETC2) and the mip chain
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/ctex-vram-formats] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp (`CompressedTexture2D::_load_data` reads DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE with any Image::Format incl. the compressed range, plus the full mip chain) and editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp `_save_ctex` (compress/mode COMPRESS_VRAM_COMPRESSED is the DEFAULT for the "3D" preset and drives the S3TC/ETC2/ASTC dual-pack export policy) | upstream/godot/scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp (`CompressedTexture2D` DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE/PNG/WEBP/BASIS_UNIVERSAL, mip chain per level) and compressed_texture.cpp's layered/3D variants (`CompressedTexture2DArray`/`CompressedCubemap`/`CompressedTexture3D`, `.ctexarray`/`.ccube`/`.ctex3d`). Web export VRAM compression ships ETC2/ASTC (and S3TC for desktop-class WebGL), per Godot's 'Exporting for the Web' texture-format policy.

**Godot classes:** CompressedTexture2D, Image, ResourceImporterTexture, CompressedTexture2DArray, CompressedTexture3D, CompressedCubemap, PortableCompressedTexture2D

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs:163-176 — `CTEX_DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE` accepts only `IMG_FORMAT_L8/LA8/RGB8/RGBA8` (ctex.rs:67-70) and returns `EngineError::Unsupported` for every other `Image::Format`, i.e. every VRAM-compressed texture. ctex.rs:160-162 — `CTEX_DATA_FORMAT_BASIS_UNIVERSAL` returns Unsupported. Only mip level 0 is read (documented ctex.rs:41-44). Meanwhile `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/block_compression.rs` implements `decode_bc1` (line 156) and `decode_bc3` (line 164) and its own header (block_compression.rs:1-11) says these are "dependency-free block decoders that the `.ctex`/`.dds`/`.ktx` loaders can call" — `grep -rn block_compression crates/ --include=*.rs` outside the file returns only `lib.rs:24 pub mod block_compression;` and a comment at portable_compressed_texture.rs:54. There is no `.dds` or `.ktx` loader at all (`grep -rn 'dds|ktx' crates/*/src` → no image-format hits).
- [resources-io] `gdresource/src/block_compression.rs` implements exactly two decoders — `pub fn decode_bc1` (:156) and `pub fn decode_bc3` (:164). `grep -rn 'ETC2|ASTC|BPTC|BC7|RGTC' --include='*.rs'` over engine-rs/crates finds only enum-constant registrations and doc comments (gdobject/src/class_db.rs:8973-8975, gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:52/88 which states there is "no S3TC/ETC2/BPTC/Basis encoder in the engine yet") — no decoder or encoder. In `gdresource/src/ctex.rs`, `CTEX_DATA_FORMAT_BASIS_UNIVERSAL` returns `EngineError::Unsupported` (:160-162), the mip count is read and discarded (`let _mipmaps = c.u32()?; // extra mip levels; we read level 0 only`, :139), and the uncompressed `DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE` arm accepts only L8/LA8/RGB8/RGBA8 (:163-176). Layered/3D compressed textures have no loader: `grep -rn 'ctexarray|ctex3d|ccube' --include='*.rs'` over engine-rs/crates → 0 hits each.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/block_compression.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/block_compression.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `CompressedTexture2D::_load_data` (upstream/godot/scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp) reads `DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE` payloads in ANY `Image::Format`, including the block-compressed range (FORMAT_DXT1=17, DXT3, DXT5, RGTC_R/RG, BPTC_RGBA/RGBF/RGBFU, ETC, ETC2_*, ASTC_*), plus every mip level when `FORMAT_BIT_HAS_MIPMAPS` is set. `compress/mode = VRAM Compressed` is the default of the "3D" texture preset (editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp), so most 3D textures in a real project are stored this way.\n\nPatina current state: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs:163-176 supports only the four uncompressed 8-bit formats `L8/LA8/RGB8/RGBA8` (constants at ctex.rs:67-70) and errors on everything else; Basis Universal errors at ctex.rs:160-162; only mip level 0 is read (ctex.rs:41-44). A BC1/BC3 decoder already lives in the same crate — `block_compression::decode_bc1` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/block_compression.rs:156) and `decode_bc3` (line 164) — with ZERO consumers; its module header explicitly says the `.ctex` loader should call it.\n\nImplementation approach: in `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/ctex.rs`, extend the `Image::Format` match to map DXT1→`block_compression::decode_bc1`, DXT5→`decode_bc3`, and compute the correct block-stride byte count per level so the cursor advances properly. Add ETC2_RGBA8/ETC2_RGB8 decoders in `block_compression.rs` (Godot's Web export policy prefers ETC2/ASTC), and walk the full mip chain when the outer `df` FORMAT_BIT_HAS_MIPMAPS flag is set, exposing level-0 pixels as today plus a `mipmap_count` property. Keep the honest `Unsupported` error for Basis Universal and ASTC until decoders exist, but name the format in the message.\n\nWiring requirement: a `.ctex` written with `compress/mode=VRAM Compressed` must load through `UnifiedLoader::load(\"res://tex.png\")` (via its `.import` remap) and produce a populated `pixels` array the renderer can upload — not merely a direct `decode_bc1` unit call.

**Merged findings (2):** CompressedTexture2D `.ctex` VRAM-compressed payloads (S3TC/BPTC/ETC2/ASTC) + mip chain + Basis Universal; VRAM-compressed and layered texture formats: ETC2/ASTC/BPTC/RGTC decode, Basis Universal .ctex, .ctex mip levels, .ctexarray/.ctex3d/.ccube

**Prove it:** A `.ctex` fixture built with DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE + Image::Format DXT1 (and a second with DXT5 + 2 mip levels), referenced from a `tex.png.import` sidecar, loads through `UnifiedLoader::load("res://tex.png")` to a Texture2D whose `width`/`height` match the header and whose `pixels` array has exactly w*h entries matching the known block colors; the DXT5 fixture reports `mipmap_count == 2`. (test: `ctex_vram_compressed_decodes_to_pixels`)
acceptance_criteria: A `.ctex` fixture built with DATA_FORMAT_IMAGE + Image::Format DXT1 (and a second with DXT5 + 2 mip levels), referenced from a `tex.png.import` sidecar, loads through `UnifiedLoader::load("res://tex.png")` to a Texture2D whose `width`/`height` match the header and whose `pixels` array has exactly w*h entries matching the known block colors; the DXT5 fixture reports `mipmap_count == 2`. (test: `ctex_vram_compressed_decodes_to_pixels`)

title: GLTFDocument/GLTFState: dispatch append_from_* and generate_scene to the real parser
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/gltf-runtime-api] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp + gltf_state.cpp; extension_api.json: GLTFDocument 6 properties / 23 methods, GLTFState 31 properties / 71 methods, FBXDocument/FBXState inherit them — this is the runtime glTF load path scripts use (`GLTFDocument.new().append_from_file(path, state)` → `generate_scene(state)`) | upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp (`_parse_accessors` incl. sparse, `_parse_skins`/`_create_skeletons`/`_create_skins`, `_parse_meshes` morph targets + `KHR_mesh_quantization`, `_parse_images` bufferView + `data:` URI decode, `_parse_materials` KHR_materials_{emissive_strength,unlit,specular,ior,clearcoat,transmission,volume}, KHR_texture_transform)

**Godot classes:** GLTFDocument, GLTFState, FBXDocument, FBXState, GLTFDocumentExtension, GLTFAccessor, GLTFSkin, GLTFSkeleton, GLTFMesh, GLTFTexture

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11071-11122 registers `GLTFDocument` with six properties and 23 method NAMES (append_from_file/append_from_buffer/append_from_scene/generate_scene/generate_buffer/write_to_filesystem/…), class_db.rs:11331 registers `GLTFState`, class_db.rs:11433-11444 registers `FBXDocument`/`FBXState`. Nothing dispatches any of them: `grep -rn 'GLTFDocument|GLTFState|append_from_buffer|generate_scene' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdobject/src crates/gdscene/src --include=*.rs` excluding class_db.rs returns exactly ONE hit, a comment at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:1726. The registration's own test file admits the gap: engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/gltf_runtime_class_family_test.rs:1-8 — "The runtime API itself — constructing them from GDScript, routing `gdresource`'s `gltf_import.rs` parser through `GLTFDocument.append_from_buffer`, and `generate_scene` — is follow-up". So a registered, introspectable, method-listing class family that no script call can ever reach.
- [asset-import-pipeline] engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs:14-19 — the module's own "Unsupported (documented)" list: "Morph targets, sparse accessors, Draco/meshopt compression", "Skinned mesh skinning matrices / animation playback", "Image / texture sampling (albedo texture URI is recorded but not decoded)", "Multiple scenes (only default / first scene is imported)". gltf_import.rs:596-610 — `resolve_texture_uri` returns `None` for GLB `bufferView`-backed images, which is how virtually every real `.glb` stores its textures, so material texture maps silently vanish. gltf_import.rs:492-497 — the `unsupported_extensions` list only reports KHR_draco_mesh_compression, KHR_materials_transmission, KHR_materials_volume, KHR_animation_pointer; the other KHR material extensions are neither parsed nor reported. `parse_skins` (gltf_import.rs:1362) and `parse_animations` (gltf_import.rs:1410) exist, and JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 are read (gltf_import.rs:229-239), but no skin binding is produced for the renderer.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/render_server_3d.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: the runtime glTF path is `var doc = GLTFDocument.new(); var state = GLTFState.new(); doc.append_from_file(path, state); var node = doc.generate_scene(state)` — `append_from_buffer(bytes, base_path, state, flags)` and `generate_scene(state, bake_fps, trimming, remove_immutable_tracks)` (upstream/godot/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp). `GLTFState` then exposes the parsed document (31 properties, 71 methods: nodes, meshes, materials, animations, skins, buffers, json, …). `FBXDocument`/`FBXState` inherit this surface.\n\nPatina current state: the whole family is ClassDB-registered with correct names, parents, properties and method arities — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:11071-11122 (GLTFDocument), :11331 (GLTFState), :11433-11444 (FBXDocument/FBXState) — but nothing dispatches a single method. `grep -rn 'GLTFDocument|append_from_buffer|generate_scene' crates/gdscript-interop/src crates/gdobject/src crates/gdscene/src --include=*.rs` (excluding class_db.rs) yields one unrelated comment at engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/animation.rs:1726. The registration's own test file states the runtime API is "follow-up" (engine-rs/crates/gdobject/tests/gltf_runtime_class_family_test.rs:1-8). A real, working parser already exists at `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/gltf_import.rs`.\n\nImplementation approach: add a handle-backed `GLTFDocument`/`GLTFState` pair in `engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` following the existing ConfigFile handle pattern (interpreter.rs ~20750): `GLTFState` holds the `Arc<Resource>` produced by `gdresource::import_gltf_bytes` plus the source base path; `append_from_buffer(bytes, base_path, state, flags)` and `append_from_file(path, base_path, state, flags)` run the parser and store the result into the state handle; `generate_scene(state, bake_fps, trimming, remove_immutable_tracks)` converts the document into a live node tree via the scene-import path (shared with the glTF→PackedScene bead) and returns the root's ObjectId. Expose the GLTFState getters that the parser can actually answer (json, nodes, meshes, materials, animations, root_nodes, base_path, scene_name) and return an explicit unsupported error for the rest rather than silently returning defaults.\n\nWiring requirement: a `.gd` script executed by the runner must be able to load a `.glb` with GLTFDocument and add the generated node to the tree.

**Merged findings (2):** GLTFDocument / GLTFState runtime scripting API (append_from_file/buffer/scene, generate_scene, generate_buffer, GLTFState accessors); glTF import fidelity: skinning, morph targets, sparse accessors, embedded (bufferView) images, KHR material extensions

**Prove it:** A GDScript snippet that does `var d = GLTFDocument.new(); var s = GLTFState.new(); d.append_from_file("res://cube.glb", s, 0, ""); var n = d.generate_scene(s); add_child(n)` results in a node in the SceneTree whose name and child MeshInstance3D count match the GLB fixture's real contents, and `s.get_meshes().size()` equals the fixture's mesh count. (test: `gltf_document_append_and_generate_scene_from_script`)
acceptance_criteria: A GDScript snippet that does `var d = GLTFDocument.new(); var s = GLTFState.new(); d.append_from_file("res://cube.glb", s, 0, ""); var n = d.generate_scene(s); add_child(n)` results in a node in the SceneTree whose name and child MeshInstance3D count match the GLB fixture's real contents, and `s.get_meshes().size()` equals the fixture's mesh count. (test: `gltf_document_append_and_generate_scene_from_script`)

title: Audio: resolve res:// stream paths against the project root in the runner boot
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-runtime-wiring] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED/PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/resource_loader.cpp + ProjectSettings::globalize_path — `res://` always resolves against the project root, never the process CWD | upstream/godot/scene/audio/audio_stream_player_internal.cpp (set_stream stops+reloads; play() always starts a NEW playback and trims to max_polyphony); doc/classes/AudioStreamPlayer.xml (max_polyphony default 1) | extension_api.json AudioStreamPlayer (11 properties / 28 methods), AudioStreamPlayer2D (14/32), AudioStreamPlayer3D (23/44); doc/classes/AudioStreamPlayer*.xml

**Godot classes:** AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStreamPlayer2D, AudioStreamPlayer3D, AudioListener2D, AudioListener3D

**Patina today:**
- [audio] `AudioServerBridge::resolve_stream_path` (/Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:148-154) strips `res://` and joins `self.base_dir`, falling back to `PathBuf::from(stripped)` (CWD-relative) when `base_dir` is None. `set_base_dir` (same file line 123) is never called by the runner: `grep -rn "set_base_dir" crates/ --include="*.rs"` returns ONLY two call sites, both in a test (crates/gdscene/tests/audio_tscn_stream_resource_plays.rs:120,150). crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:580-638 (`init_running`) loads the bus layout and attaches the output sink but never sets the bridge's base dir, and patina-runner never chdirs (`grep -rn "set_current_dir" crates/patina-runner/src/` → no hits; main.rs:236-255 has its own separate `resolve_res_path` helper the bridge does not use).
- [audio] crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:405-411 reads the node's `stream` property ONLY as `Variant::String` (or the `__extres__stream` companion). But `load("res://sfx.wav")` in GDScript returns `Variant::Resource(ResourceRef{class_name:"AudioStream"})` — crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:4369-4394 — so `$Player.stream = load(...)` yields an empty path and silence. The stream is also imported only once: audio_server_bridge.rs:467 `if first_sight && !player.has_stream()`, so re-assigning `stream` mid-game (music track swap) never reloads. Finally, `play()` on an already-playing node is a no-op: the interpreter sets `playing = true` (interpreter.rs:9335-9377) and the bridge's branch chain (audio_server_bridge.rs:493-512) only starts a voice when `playing_prop && !voice_alive`, so a rapid-fire SFX retrigger is swallowed. `max_polyphony` appears nowhere: `grep -rn "max_polyphony" crates/ --include="*.rs"` → no hits.
- [audio] crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10113-10170 registers only stream/volume_db/pitch_scale/autoplay/bus/playing (+ max_distance/attenuation/panning_strength for 2D, + max_distance/unit_size/attenuation_model/max_db/panning_strength for 3D) and only three methods (play/stop/is_playing). Missing everywhere: `stream_paused` (which the bridge nonetheless reads at crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:427), `max_polyphony`, `mix_target`, `playback_type`, `volume_linear`, `area_mask`; missing on 3D: `emission_angle_enabled`, `emission_angle_degrees`, `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db`, `attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz`, `attenuation_filter_db`, `doppler_tracking`. Missing methods: `seek`, `get_playback_position`, `set_stream_paused`/`get_stream_paused`, `has_stream_playback`/`get_stream_playback`. Separately, `AudioListener2D/3D.make_current()/clear_current()` are registered in ClassDB (class_db.rs:1013-1020, :6441-6449) but the interpreter never dispatches them — `grep -n "make_current" crates/gdscript-interop/src/*.rs` returns no hits, so `$Listener.make_current()` raises UndefinedFunction.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/player.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT: every `res://` path resolves against the project directory (the folder holding project.godot), independent of the process working directory (core/io/resource_loader.cpp, ProjectSettings::globalize_path). Launching the game from any cwd loads the same assets.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:148-154 `resolve_stream_path` joins `self.base_dir` when set and otherwise returns a bare relative path, i.e. CWD-relative. `set_base_dir` (audio_server_bridge.rs:123) has ZERO production callers — `grep -rn "set_base_dir" crates/` matches only crates/gdscene/tests/audio_tscn_stream_resource_plays.rs:120 and :150. crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs:580-638 builds the MainLoop, loads the bus layout from `self.config.project_dir`, and attaches the audio sink, but never passes `project_dir` to the bridge. Result: a project launched from anywhere but its own directory silently loads no audio at all — the stream load fails and only logs `tracing::warn!` (audio_server_bridge.rs:474-478), which the runner does not surface.\n\nAPPROACH: in `EngineBootstrap::init_running` (crates/patina-runner/src/bootstrap.rs, right after `MainLoop::new(tree)` at line 586) call `main_loop.audio_bridge_mut().set_base_dir(self.config.project_dir.clone())`. Also make the bridge fall back to the same ancestor-walk `resolve_res_path` uses in crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:236-255 so loose-file layouts still work, and promote the stream-load failure from `warn!` to a runner-visible error line.\n\nWIRING: boot -> bridge.base_dir set -> `sync_player_node` first-sight import -> `AudioStreamLoader::load_buffer(project_dir/sfx/beep.wav)` -> non-silent mix on the first frame.

**Merged findings (3):** res:// audio stream path resolution in the runner; Runtime `stream` assignment, retrigger, and max_polyphony on AudioStreamPlayer*; ClassDB surface for AudioStreamPlayer*/AudioListener* (properties + methods)

**Prove it:** Booting a project whose scene has an autoplaying `AudioStreamPlayer` with `stream = "res://sfx/beep.wav"` from a working directory OUTSIDE the project directory produces a non-silent mix within the first few frames (bridge `last_mix()` has samples above the noise floor); the same boot with a missing file logs a visible error rather than silence. (test: `audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p patina-runner --test audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`.
acceptance_criteria: Booting a project whose scene has an autoplaying `AudioStreamPlayer` with `stream = "res://sfx/beep.wav"` from a working directory OUTSIDE the project directory produces a non-silent mix within the first few frames (bridge `last_mix()` has samples above the noise floor); the same boot with a missing file logs a visible error rather than silence. (test: `audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p patina-runner --test audio_res_path_resolves_from_project`.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_svg.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: each `ResourceImporter` declares its options in `_get_import_options` and the chosen values are persisted per-asset in the `.import` file's `[params]` section; the importer then applies them when producing the artifact (upstream/godot/editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp — 26 options; resource_importer_wav.cpp — 10; resource_importer_svg.cpp — 4). Project-wide defaults live in ProjectSettings under `importer_defaults/<importer_name>`.\n\nPatina current state: `.import` `[params]` IS parsed but immediately orphaned — `ImportFile::other_sections` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:641-649, populated at importers.rs:712-719) has zero readers outside its own module (verified by `grep -rn other_sections crates/ apps/ --include=*.rs`). The values are raw strings, so even a reader could not distinguish `true` from `\"true\"` from `1`. `import_svg` hardcodes `1.0` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_svg.rs:114-121); `import_wav` (importers.rs:487-548) ignores every loop/trim/normalize/force option; `import_image` (importers.rs:44-52) ignores size limit, mipmaps and alpha processing. `importer_defaults/*` does not exist anywhere.\n\nImplementation approach: in `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs`, add `ImportParams` that parses `[params]` values into `Variant` via the existing `gdresource::loader::parse_variant_value`, and expose `ImportFile::params()`. Give each importer entry point an `_with_params` variant: `import_image_with_params` (apply `process/size_limit` by downscaling, `mipmaps/generate`, `process/premult_alpha`, `process/fix_alpha_border`, `process/normal_map_invert_y`, `process/channel_remap/*`), `import_wav_with_params` (apply `force/mono`, `force/8_bit`, `force/max_rate_hz`, `edit/trim`, `edit/normalize`, and store `edit/loop_mode`/`loop_begin`/`loop_end` onto the AudioStreamWAV resource so `gdaudio::stream` honors them), `import_svg_with_params` (`svg/scale`, `base_scale`, `saturation`). Have `ResourceFormatLoader::load_resource` look for `<source>.import` and pass the parsed params through. Add `importer_defaults/<name>/<option>` lookup in `gdresource::project` as the fallback.\n\nWiring requirement: a loose source file plus a sibling `.import` with non-default `[params]` must load DIFFERENTLY through `UnifiedLoader::load` than the same file with default params — end-to-end, no direct call into the option struct.

**Prove it:** Loading `res://icon.svg` through `UnifiedLoader` with a sibling `icon.svg.import` containing `[params] svg/scale=2.0` yields a Texture2D with 4x the pixel count of the same file with `svg/scale=1.0`; loading `res://tone.wav` with `[params] force/mono=true` on a stereo source yields `channels=1`; loading `res://big.png` with `[params] process/size_limit=16` on a 64x64 source yields `width==16`. (test: `import_params_change_loaded_resource`)
acceptance_criteria: Loading `res://icon.svg` through `UnifiedLoader` with a sibling `icon.svg.import` containing `[params] svg/scale=2.0` yields a Texture2D with 4x the pixel count of the same file with `svg/scale=1.0`; loading `res://tone.wav` with `[params] force/mono=true` on a stereo source yields `channels=1`; loading `res://big.png` with `[params] process/size_limit=16` on a 64x64 source yields `width==16`. (test: `import_params_change_loaded_resource`)

title: Resource loaders: compile the orphaned import modules and register jpg/tga/bmp/hdr/ogg/obj/gltf
description:
[audit-key: asset-import-pipeline/loader-registry-extensions] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/io/image_loader.cpp + modules/{jpg,tga,bmp,hdr,svg,webp}/ register loaders for every source image format; editor/import/resource_importer_texture.cpp accepts bmp/dds/exr/hdr/jpg/jpeg/png/svg/tga/webp; modules/{minimp3,vorbis} for audio; modules/gltf/ for .gltf/.glb | extension_api.json ResourceFormatLoader (11: _get_recognized_extensions, _recognize_path, _handles_type, _get_resource_type, _get_resource_script_class, _get_resource_uid, _get_dependencies, _rename_dependencies, _exists, _get_classes_used, _load), ResourceFormatSaver (5), ImageFormatLoaderExtension (2); upstream/godot/core/io/resource_loader.cpp ResourceLoader::_load which walks the registered loaders.

**Godot classes:** ResourceFormatLoader, Image, ImageTexture, ResourceImporterTexture, ResourceImporterOBJ, ResourceFormatSaver, ImageFormatLoaderExtension, ResourceLoader, ResourceSaver

**Patina today:**
- [asset-import-pipeline] `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults` registers exactly 14 extensions — .png .webp .svg .ctex .wav .ttf .otf .tres .tscn .res .scn .vs .gdshader .gdshaderinc (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:755-771). Missing: .jpg/.jpeg/.tga/.bmp/.hdr/.exr/.ogg/.mp3/.gltf/.glb/.obj/.fbx/.csv/.glsl/.dds/.ktx. A unit test even pins the gap: `assert!(!rfl.can_load(".jpg"))` (importers.rs:1413). The decoders exist but are unreachable: (a) `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/texture_import.rs` (785 lines, hand-rolled PNG+JPEG decoder) and `engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs` (401 lines, WAV+OGG→Resource) are ORPHANED MODULES — neither appears in the `pub mod` list at engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs:23-50 and `grep -rn 'mod texture_import|mod audio_import' crates/` returns nothing, so rustc has never compiled them; this is independently documented at engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:237-242 ("25 KB never declared in lib.rs, so the compiler has never seen it"). (b) `image_tga_bmp::decode_bmp`/`decode_tga` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_tga_bmp.rs:33,83) and `radiance_hdr::decode_hdr` (radiance_hdr.rs:121) compile but have ZERO consumers. (c) `gdserver3d::mesh::Mesh3D::from_obj` (engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:713) has no callers outside its own module. The editor's own doc comment claims otherwise: engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/texture_cache.rs:107-114 says "This is what makes `.webp`, `.svg`, `.jpg` and `.ctex` render in the editor viewport".
- [engine-virtual-method-table] All 18 virtuals ARE declared — engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10707-10714 (ImageFormatLoaderExtension), :10731-10746 (ResourceFormatLoader), :10748-10758 (ResourceFormatSaver) — and the file's own comment at class_db.rs:10725-10730 states the gap outright: "⚠️ SCOPE: this registers the class surface so `extends ResourceFormatLoader` resolves. The runtime *dispatch* — `ResourceLoader.add_resource_format_loader` plus a `load()` that invokes a script subclass's `_load` — is a separate, larger gdscript-interop feature (no ResourceLoader singleton/registry exists in the interpreter yet) and is NOT wired here." Grepping `"_load"`, `"_save"`, `"_recognize_path"`, `"_get_recognized_extensions"` over engine-rs/crates/ (tests excluded) returns class_db.rs only.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/texture_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/audio_import.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/image_tga_bmp.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/radiance_hdr.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: every source asset extension Godot's importers accept (bmp, dds, exr, hdr, jpg, jpeg, png, svg, tga, webp for textures; wav, ogg, mp3 for audio; gltf, glb, obj, fbx for scenes) resolves through a registered loader, so `load()`/the editor/the renderer all agree (upstream/godot/core/io/image_loader.cpp, modules/{jpg,tga,bmp,hdr,minimp3,vorbis,gltf}).\n\nPatina current state: `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults` (engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/importers.rs:755-771) registers 14 extensions and none of jpg/jpeg/tga/bmp/hdr/exr/ogg/mp3/gltf/glb/obj; a test asserts the JPEG gap (importers.rs:1413). Real decoders sit unreachable: `texture_import.rs` (785 lines incl. a JPEG decoder) and `audio_import.rs` (401 lines) are NOT declared in engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs:23-50, so they are dead files rustc never compiles — confirmed in prose at engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/portable_compressed_texture.rs:237-242. `image_tga_bmp::decode_bmp`/`decode_tga` (image_tga_bmp.rs:33,83), `radiance_hdr::decode_hdr` (radiance_hdr.rs:121) and `gdserver3d::mesh::Mesh3D::from_obj` (engine-rs/crates/gdserver3d/src/mesh.rs:713) compile with zero consumers.\n\nImplementation approach: (1) add `pub mod texture_import;` and `pub mod audio_import;` to engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/lib.rs and fix whatever fallout compiling them produces (they were written against an older `Resource` API). (2) In `with_defaults`, register `.jpg`/`.jpeg` → the JPEG path, `.tga`/`.bmp` → thin wrappers over `image_tga_bmp::decode_tga/decode_bmp` producing the same pixel-bearing Texture2D shape as `import_image_bytes`, `.hdr` → `radiance_hdr::decode_hdr`, `.ogg`/`.mp3` → an `AudioStream*` Resource built from `gdaudio::decode`, `.gltf`/`.glb` → `gltf_import::import_gltf`, `.obj` → a wrapper over `Mesh3D::from_obj`. (3) Delete the `assert!(!rfl.can_load(\".jpg\"))` assertion and replace it with positive coverage. (4) Correct the stale doc at engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/texture_cache.rs:107-114.\n\nWiring requirement: every added extension must load through `UnifiedLoader::load(\"res://…\")` (the path the editor texture cache and — once its own bead lands — the interpreter take), not just through a direct module call.

**Merged findings (2):** ResourceFormatLoader extension coverage: .jpg/.jpeg/.tga/.bmp/.hdr/.exr/.ogg/.mp3/.gltf/.glb/.obj + orphaned decoder modules; ResourceFormatLoader / ResourceFormatSaver / ImageFormatLoaderExtension virtuals registered but never dispatched

**Prove it:** For a temp project containing real `a.jpg`, `b.tga`, `c.bmp`, `d.hdr`, `e.ogg` and `f.obj` fixtures, `UnifiedLoader::load` returns for each a Resource of the right class with real data (images: correct `width`/`height` and a `pixels` array of exactly w*h entries; ogg: non-zero `length_seconds`; obj: a Mesh with the fixture's real vertex count), and `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().can_load(".jpg")` is true. (test: `format_loader_covers_source_asset_extensions`)
acceptance_criteria: For a temp project containing real `a.jpg`, `b.tga`, `c.bmp`, `d.hdr`, `e.ogg` and `f.obj` fixtures, `UnifiedLoader::load` returns for each a Resource of the right class with real data (images: correct `width`/`height` and a `pixels` array of exactly w*h entries; ogg: non-zero `length_seconds`; obj: a Mesh with the fixture's real vertex count), and `ResourceFormatLoader::with_defaults().can_load(".jpg")` is true. (test: `format_loader_covers_source_asset_extensions`)

description:

title: Audio3D: match Godot's attenuation math and wire emission cone, distance lowpass, and doppler
description:
[audit-key: audio/audio-spatial-3d] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:232-259 (_get_attenuation_db) and :444-465 (max_distance rolloff, attenuation_filter highshelf, emission cone)

**Godot classes:** AudioStreamPlayer3D, AudioListener3D

**Patina today:**
- [audio] Formula mismatch: Godot's inverse-distance gain is `linear_to_db(1/((d/unit)+CMP_EPSILON))` and inverse-square is `1/((d/unit)^2+eps)`, logarithmic is `-20*ln(d/unit+eps)` (upstream audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:235-247). Patina uses entirely different curves: `unit/(unit+d)`, `u^2/(u^2+d^2)`, `1/(1+log2(1+d/unit))` (crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs:181-198). Godot additionally multiplies by `max(0, 1 - d/max_distance)` when max_distance>0 (upstream :445-447); Patina hard-cuts to 0 past max_distance (spatial.rs:176-179). The cone/filter/doppler fields are declared but dead: `emission_angle_degrees`, `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db`, `emission_angle_enabled`, `attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz`, `attenuation_filter_db`, `doppler_tracking` (crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs:79-97) are never read by `compute_spatial` (spatial.rs:204-231), and `grep -rn "doppler_pitch_scale\|emission_angle\|attenuation_filter" crates/ --include="*.rs" | grep -v spatial.rs` returns ZERO hits. The scene bridge's `read_spatial_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:319-346) mirrors only volume_db/unit_size/max_distance/max_db/panning_strength/attenuation_model.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT (scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp): `_get_attenuation_db(d)` returns `linear_to_db(1/((d/unit_size)+CMP_EPSILON))` for INVERSE_DISTANCE, `linear_to_db(1/((d/unit_size)^2+eps))` for INVERSE_SQUARE, `-20*ln(d/unit_size+eps)` for LOGARITHMIC, 0 for DISABLED; it then adds `volume_db` and clamps at `max_db`. `_update_panning` (:444-465) multiplies by `max(0, 1 - d/max_distance)` when max_distance>0, derives `db_att = (1-min(1,multiplier)) * attenuation_filter_db`, subtracts `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` when the listener is outside the emission cone, and feeds the result to `set_playback_highshelf_params(linear_attenuation, attenuation_filter_cutoff_hz)`. `doppler_tracking` shifts pitch from relative velocity.\n\nPATINA: crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs:181-198 implements three DIFFERENT curves (`unit/(unit+d)`, `u^2/(u^2+d^2)`, `1/(1+log2(1+d/unit))`) and hard-cuts at max_distance (:176-179) instead of the linear rolloff. `emission_angle_*`, `attenuation_filter_*`, `doppler_tracking` are struct fields (spatial.rs:79-97) that `compute_spatial` (:204-231) never reads, and `doppler_pitch_scale` (spatial.rs:339) has no callers anywhere. The bridge's `read_spatial_3d` (crates/gdscene/src/audio_server_bridge.rs:319-346) never mirrors them, and crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs:10148-10170 does not register them as properties.\n\nAPPROACH: (1) rewrite `compute_attenuation` in crates/gdaudio/src/spatial.rs to Godot's dB formulas, add the `max(0, 1 - d/max_distance)` factor, and clamp `att + volume_db` at `max_db`; (2) implement the emission-cone test against the source's -Z basis column and the high-shelf filter (reuse crates/gdaudio/src/biquad.rs) applied per-voice; (3) add a per-voice high-shelf slot on the server voice (crates/gdaudio/src/server.rs `stream_mut`) so `SpatialAudioResult` can carry `(highshelf_gain, cutoff_hz)`; (4) implement doppler by tracking the previous frame's source and listener global positions in the bridge and calling `doppler_pitch_scale`, gated on `doppler_tracking` (idle vs physics step); (5) extend `read_spatial_3d` to mirror all six properties and register them on `AudioStreamPlayer3D` in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs.\n\nWIRING: Node3D global transform each frame -> read_spatial_3d -> compute_spatial -> voice gain/pan/high-shelf/pitch -> mixed output.

**Prove it:** For a source at distance d with unit_size u, the mixed gain matches Godot's `db_to_linear(linear_to_db(1/(d/u)) )` within 1e-3 for all three attenuation models; a listener placed outside a 30-degree emission cone hears the source attenuated by `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` relative to on-axis; a source moving toward the listener with `doppler_tracking` enabled raises the mixed playback rate. (test: `audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`.
acceptance_criteria: For a source at distance d with unit_size u, the mixed gain matches Godot's `db_to_linear(linear_to_db(1/(d/u)) )` within 1e-3 for all three attenuation models; a listener placed outside a 30-degree emission cone hears the source attenuated by `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` relative to on-axis; a source moving toward the listener with `doppler_tracking` enabled raises the mixed playback rate. (test: `audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`) runnable via `cargo nextest run -p gdscene --test audio3d_attenuation_cone_doppler`.

BronzeLake: diagnosis after three verify rounds. The cone clause of the acceptance CANNOT pass as written. Read this before touching the test.

WHAT NOW PASSES (verifier log, run 3): all three attenuation models. Getting there took two fixes, both mine:
1. `peak(&mix)` is NOT the gain. Panning is equal-power (compute_spatial uses angle.cos()/angle.sin()), so a centred source puts gain/sqrt(2) in EACH channel. Use sqrt(L^2+R^2), valid at any pan since cos^2+sin^2==1. The tell was the ratio 0.176776/0.25 = 0.70711 exactly.
2. Godot's LOGARITHMIC attenuation is `-20 * Math::log(d/u)` and Math::log is the NATURAL log (scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:243). Not log10. At d/u=4 that is -27.7 dB, not -12.0 dB. Expected values now: 0.250000 / 0.062500 / 0.041087, the last matching the engine to six decimals.

WHAT STILL FAILS, and why it is not a test bug: `on 1.412538 vs off 1.412538`. Two facts.

(a) 1.412538 = 10^(3/20) exactly — both runs are pinned at max_db, whose Godot default is 3.0 dB. With unit_size 100 and distance 10 the raw gain is +20 dB, so the clamp flattens everything. Any cone fixture must keep the pre-clamp gain below max_db or set max_db high.

(b) THE REAL ISSUE: the cone is not a gain cut. compute_spatial does
      let highshelf_db = distance_filter_db + self.emission_cone_db(to_source);
    so emission_cone_db feeds the HIGH-SHELF, never volume_linear. That is CORRECT Godot behaviour - `emission_angle_filter_attenuation_db` is a filter attenuation, an HF rolloff, not a broadband cut. And apply_spatial (audio_server_bridge.rs) consumes only volume_linear and the pan pair, so highshelf_db is computed and then dropped on the floor.

    Net: the cone currently has ZERO audible effect, and no amplitude-based assertion can ever detect it. Worse, a DC or constant test signal has no high-frequency content, so even once the filter IS applied, a peak/energy comparison would barely move. A future test needs broadband content (noise or a high-frequency tone) to see an HF rolloff at all.

    The cone properties themselves ARE wired: read_spatial_3d reads emission_angle_enabled / _degrees / _filter_attenuation_db at audio_server_bridge.rs:513-523. So this is purely the missing filter application.

ALSO WRONG IN MY FIXTURE, fix it while you are there: the source's forward defaults to -Z, so a source at (0,0,-10) with the listener at the origin has the listener 180 degrees BEHIND it. My "on-axis" run was fully off-axis; both runs were outside the cone, which is the other reason they matched. Set the source's rotation/forward explicitly, or place the listener along the source's actual forward axis.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP, pick one: (i) apply highshelf_db to the voice - needs a per-voice filter slot on the playback stream, and then assert the cone with broadband content; or (ii) assert the cone where it is observable today, on SpatialAudioResult.highshelf_db (needs a small bridge accessor), and move "hears the source attenuated" to remaining scope until the filter lands. (i) is what the bead actually asks for.

NOT AT FAULT: the Doppler wiring in apply_spatial. It has never executed - fail-fast cancels after the attenuation/cone assertions, which run first - so its correctness is still unknown, not disproven. Consider running with --no-fail-fast once to get all the signal in one round.

The cone/filter/doppler properties are not registered on AudioStreamPlayer3D in gdobject/src/class_db.rs. read_spatial_3d reads them off the node so authored scenes work, but they are missing from reflection and the inspector. doppler_tracking should be registered as an enum-typed int with DISABLED 0 / IDLE_STEP 1 / PHYSICS_STEP 2.
DopplerTracking::PhysicsStep is not distinguished from IdleStep. Both enable tracking, but Godot samples velocity on a different step for each, so a physics-driven source reads its velocity one frame out of phase. The mapping is in place; the two-clock behaviour is not.
The 2D spatial path (compute_spatial_2d) has no filter or Doppler equivalent and has not been checked against audio_stream_player_2d.cpp.
PATTERN worth a sweep: this bead has now produced THREE registered-but-inert properties at different layers - the cone was computed and dropped by the mixer, doppler_tracking was never read from the node at all, and the filter fields before that were struct fields nothing wrote. When auditing a subsystem, grep each declared property for a WRITE from the scene side and a READ on the consumer side separately; either half missing makes the feature silently inert while looking fully wired.
