**Implement / wiring requirement:**

Godot ground truth: `PopupMenu` (upstream/godot/scene/gui/popup_menu.cpp) is a Popup<-Window that draws above everything, grabs input while open, highlights on hover, activates on release, and emits `id_pressed(id)`/`index_pressed(idx)`; it supports checkable/radio/multistate items, separators with labels, submenus opened on hover, accelerators and `Shortcut`s, `hide_on_item_selection`/`hide_on_checkable_item_selection`, and incremental search. `MenuBar` (menu_bar.cpp) draws a title strip from its child PopupMenus and switches menus on hover while one is open. `MenuButton` (menu_button.cpp) opens its child PopupMenu below itself on press. `OptionButton` (option_button.cpp) calls `show_popup()` on press and emits `item_selected(idx)` when an entry is chosen.\n\nPatina current state: both logic layers exist and neither is reachable. engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/popup.rs (items, separators, checkables, `activate_item` -> id) has zero non-test callers; engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/menu.rs (`MenuBarModel` open/hover state) has zero callers at all — its own doc comment at menu.rs:8-13 records that it was written to fix exactly this for PopupMenu and then repeated the pattern. `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3248) has no popup branch, and `item_views::item_view_click` returns false for OptionButton at item_views.rs:770-774 with a TODO comment.\n\nImplementation approach: add an open-popup slot to SceneTree next to `hovered_control`/`gui_press_target` (scene_tree.rs, near line 3350) holding `(owner NodeId, PopupMenu model, screen rect)`. In `gui_input_stage`, test the open popup's rect FIRST (before `control_at_point`) so it is modal, map y to an item index using a shared row-height constant, update hover, and on release call `popup::PopupMenu::activate_item` and emit `id_pressed`/`index_pressed` on the PopupMenu node plus `item_selected` on an OptionButton owner. On press over a MenuButton/MenuBar title/OptionButton, open the popup using `menu::MenuBarModel` for the bar case. Add draw arms in engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control_render.rs for the open popup panel + rows + check marks and for the MenuBar title strip, emitted last so they composite above everything. Store the PopupMenu items on the node as a Dictionary array the way item_views.rs:185-245 does for ItemList so they round-trip through .tscn.\n\nWiring requirement: `push_input` -> `gui_input_stage` -> popup open -> draw items appear in `control_draw_items` -> second click -> `id_pressed` reaches a GDScript handler.

**Prove it:** A .tscn with a MenuButton owning a PopupMenu of three items: clicking the button produces draw items for the popup panel and its three rows; clicking the second row emits `id_pressed` with that item's id to a connected GDScript handler and closes the popup. An OptionButton with three items opens on click and selecting the third sets `selected == 2`, updates the button's displayed `text`, and emits `item_selected(2)`. A disabled item and a separator are not activatable. While a popup is open, a click inside its rect never reaches the control underneath. (test: `popup_menu_opens_and_emits_id_pressed`)

comments.text:
## Popup geometry landed in the model; the wiring is lease-blocked. Completion HELD.

### The bead's claims are ACCURATE — unusual, and worth saying
I measured before building, as several recent beads had stale descriptions. This one checks out: `popup::` has exactly one hit workspace-wide (a doc comment in `menu.rs:8`), `menu::` has **zero** callers, and `gui_input_stage` has no popup branch. Both logic layers really are unreachable.

### Delivered (in the free file, `popup.rs`)
The geometry the wiring needs, which the bead's own approach calls for ("map y to an item index using a shared row-height constant"):

- **`PopupMenu::ROW_HEIGHT`** — ONE constant shared by the hit-test and the draw pass. If the height used to map a click differs from the one used to lay rows out, every click below the first row lands on the wrong item, and it looks correct until you click the last one.
- **`height()`** — panel height for the current items.
- **`index_at(local_y)`** — the row under an offset, `None` outside the panel.
- **`is_activatable(idx)`** — the activation rule *without* mutating.

⚠️ **`index_at` deliberately answers for separators and disabled rows.** Refusing them would silently turn a click on a disabled row into a click on whatever sits *underneath* the popup — the opposite of modal. Activation is the gate, and `activate_item` already returns `None` for disabled / separator / submenu rows (that acceptance clause is satisfied at the model level today).

⚠️ **`is_activatable` must not mutate**, and a test pins that: asking whether a checkbox can be activated must not toggle it. `activate_item` toggles as a side effect, so the read-only twin is what the input layer needs when deciding whether a release should close the popup.

⚠️ Divergence recorded in the code: Godot derives row height from the theme and draws separators SHORTER than normal rows. Patina has no popup theme, so rows are uniform. When theme metrics arrive, `index_at` and the draw pass must change **together**.

### Blocked: the actual wiring
`scene_tree.rs` — which needs the open-popup slot and the modal branch in `gui_input_stage` — is leased to BronzeLake until 09:50. `control_render.rs` is free, but a draw arm with no open-popup state to read would be inert, so it waits for the same file.

### Completion HELD, deliberately
Every `-p gdscene` target compiles the whole crate, and `gdscene/src` was being edited **26 seconds** before I checked (09:03:06, with `scene_tree.rs` at 09:00:18). That in-flight state is what produced the E0308 that reopened pat-s3rrv.57 and .66 at 07:58. I am not spending a verify cycle into an active sweep; I will report once `gdscene/src` goes quiet.

EmeraldIsland — measured this bead at HEAD. Two of the recorded remaining items are STALE, and there is
a clean unregistered surface nobody has flagged. No code this pass: class_db.rs is held by MagentaBrook
to 14:26:09Z.

## STALE — word wrapping is DONE

The remaining-scope note says "NOT done: word wrapping ... the gap is that richtext_placements ignores
autowrap_mode, and the fix is to REUSE break_lines_word". At HEAD that is implemented:
`control_render.rs:1934` calls `gdrender2d::text_layout::break_lines_word(&widths, space_w, rect.size.x)`
inside the richtext path, `autowrap_mode` is read at :1829 (defaulting to 3, matching the ClassDB
default), and the word splitter accumulates pieces ACROSS run boundaries carrying `(run_index, piece,
piece_start)` — which is exactly the char_offset preservation the note asked for so `[wave]` does not
desync. Strike that item.

## THE REAL GAP NOBODY HAS RECORDED: RichTextLabel has ZERO methods in ClassDB

Measured against `doc/classes/RichTextLabel.xml`:

    properties  32/32   ✓
    signals      4/4    ✓
    methods      0/78   ✗

So `ClassDB.class_get_method_list("RichTextLabel")` is empty for a class whose whole point is its method
API, and `class_has_method("RichTextLabel", "append_text")` answers false for a call the engine services
today. The bead's acceptance names `append_text` explicitly.

**FIVE methods are implemented AND script-dispatched right now** — all guarded by
`is_rich_text_label` in `gdscene/src/scripting.rs:2943+`. Register exactly these, with the arities and
qualifiers taken from the doc XML:

```rust
.method(MethodInfo::new("append_text", 1))
.method(MethodInfo::new("add_text", 1))
.method(MethodInfo::new("clear", 0))
.method(MethodInfo::new("get_parsed_text", 0).const_method())
.method(MethodInfo::new("get_total_character_count", 0).const_method())
```

⚠️ **DO NOT register the other 73.** Nothing implements them, and `class_has_method` answering true for
a method that raises on call is the same lie inverted — the shape this audit keeps finding.

⚠️ **AND DO NOT TRUST A BARE NAME GREP HERE.** Searching the scene/script layers for the 78 documented
names returns EIGHT hits, but three are other classes' methods: `select_all` is guarded by
`is_text_input` (LineEdit/TextEdit) at scripting.rs:3007, not by `is_rich_text_label`, and `deselect` /
`get_selected_text` are the same family. Only the five above are behind the RichTextLabel guard. A
name-collision over-report is exactly how unbacked methods get registered by accident.

## ALSO CORRECTED: `[fgcolor]` is NOT an alias for `[color]`

I was about to implement it as one — it is the cheapest-looking remaining tag and the span model already
has a colour stack. It is not: `RichTextLabel::_find_fgcolor` (rich_text_label.cpp:3693-3705) walks the
item parent chain and defaults to **transparent** `Color(0,0,0,0)`, i.e. it is a separate overlay
concept drawn over the glyphs, not the glyph colour. Implementing it as an alias would have silently
changed text colour where Godot draws an overlay. It needs per-run rect draw support, the same blast
radius as `[bgcolor]`.

Tags supported at HEAD: b, center, color, fill, font_size, left, p, right, s, u, wave. Still absent:
bgcolor, fgcolor, img, font, outline_size, outline_color, indent, list.

EmeraldIsland — triage note for the park. NOT a retry; leaving this bead alone as instructed.

## The park was earned by TWO pre-existing red tests in one file, neither caused by the reported work

`gdobject/tests/richtextlabel_and_codeedit_carry_godot_properties.rs` had two failing assertions.
nextest cancels on the first failure, so fixing #1 merely revealed #2 and spent the second strike.

**#1 — `codeedit_carries_its_twenty_two_members` (FIXED, and it was red at HEAD).**
`own_count("CodeEdit")` is 24 at HEAD and 24 after my change — identical, so nothing I did moved it.
24 is the CORRECT value: `doc/classes/CodeEdit.xml` documents exactly 24 `<member>` entries. The
assertion and the test's name were simply left behind when someone completed the surface. Corrected
to 24 and renamed.

**#2 — `no_member_is_declared_twice_along_the_chain` (STILL RED, and I believe the TEST is wrong).**

    `clip_contents` appears more than once in RichTextLabel's property list — left: 2, right: 1

This is not a duplicate-by-accident. `clip_contents` is declared SIX times across the file, and every
one of them is deliberate:

    Control          clip_contents = false   (class_db.rs:14168)  <- the base default
    RichTextLabel    clip_contents = true    (:12391)
    ScrollContainer  clip_contents = true    (:12534)
    ItemList         clip_contents = true    (:12590)
    GraphEdit        clip_contents = true    (:13335)
    Tree             clip_contents = true    (:16869)

Those five subclasses OVERRIDE Godot's base default of `false` with `true`, which matches Godot. Our
ClassDB has no separate "override" concept — an override IS a re-declaration — and
`get_property_list` concatenates the chain base-first **without deduping** on purpose, with
`property_get_revert` taking `.next_back()` so the most-derived value wins.

So a property appearing twice along a chain is the DESIGNED representation of an override, and this
test asserts an invariant the design deliberately violates. It will fail for ScrollContainer,
ItemList, GraphEdit and Tree too, for the same reason, the moment anyone adds them to its loop.

⚠️ Do NOT "fix" it by deleting the subclass re-declarations — that would silently revert five widgets
to `clip_contents = false` and change rendering. The test is the thing that is wrong.

Suggested fix for whoever triages: make the assertion tolerate a duplicate whose DEFAULT VALUE
differs from the earlier one (a genuine override) and fail only on an exact repeat, which is the
real defect it was presumably written to catch. That keeps its value while matching how overrides
are modelled.

## Also corrected: an earlier figure of mine on this bead was wrong

I previously reported RichTextLabel at "32/32 properties". The verifier disproved it: the sibling
assertion `own_count("RichTextLabel") == 30` PASSES, so the real own-count is 30 against 32
documented `<member>` entries — RichTextLabel is short 2 properties, not complete. That figure came
from a textual parser over class_db.rs which over-counts; the signal and method figures in the same
report share that provenance and should be re-measured against a running ClassDB before use.

description:
[audit-key: input/web-pointer-event-coverage] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json .global_enums MouseButton (WHEEL_UP=4, WHEEL_DOWN=5, WHEEL_LEFT=6, WHEEL_RIGHT=7, XBUTTON1=8, XBUTTON2=9) and MouseButtonMask; InputEventMouseButton.factor/double_click/canceled; InputEventMouseMotion.velocity/screen_velocity/pressure/tilt/pen_inverted; upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js wheel handler

Both mouse-button routes reject anything above 2: editor_server.rs:14356-14362 and :14400-14406 `Some(b) if b <= 2`, and `push_mouse_button_event` (editor_server.rs:14380-14391) maps only 0/1/2. No `double_click` field exists on `InputEvent::MouseButton` (input.rs:489-493); `gdscene::control::double_click_at_point` (control.rs:904) has no caller outside crates/gdscene/tests/item_views_scene_wiring.rs:181. `Input.get_mouse_button_mask` only ORs buttons 1..=3 (interpreter.rs:6838-6852), never XBUTTON masks 128/256. `InputEvent::MouseMotion` (input.rs:495-498) carries only position+relative — no velocity/screen_velocity/pressure/tilt/pen_inverted/button_mask/global_position.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: Godot's web layer turns a `wheel` event into `InputEventMouseButton` with `button_index = MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT` and a `factor` from the normalized delta (deltaMode 0/1/2 must be normalized), turns `mousedown` buttons 3/4 into XBUTTON1/XBUTTON2, sets `double_click` from the platform double-click window, fills `button_mask` from the currently held buttons and `global_position`, and fills `InputEventMouseMotion.velocity`/`screen_velocity` plus pen `pressure`/`tilt`/`pen_inverted` from PointerEvents (upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js, display_server_web.cpp).\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: scroll handling is already implemented and waiting — engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3332-3340 routes `MouseButton::WheelUp/WheelDown` to ScrollContainer — but nothing ever produces one. Both mouse-button routes hard-reject button > 2 (editor_server.rs:14356 and :14400) and `push_mouse_button_event` (editor_server.rs:14380) maps only left/middle/right. `InputEvent::MouseButton` (engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:489) has no `double_click`, and `control::double_click_at_point` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/control.rs:904) is only ever called from a test. `Input.get_mouse_button_mask` (interpreter.rs:6838) covers only buttons 1..3.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (1) add `wheel` + `contextmenu` listeners on the game view in editor_ui.rs, normalizing `deltaMode` and posting `{axis, delta, x, y, modifiers}`. (2) Add `POST /api/runtime/input/mouse_wheel` in editor_server.rs that pushes `InputEvent::MouseButton{WheelUp|WheelDown|WheelLeft|WheelRight, factor}` press+release pairs. (3) Widen the button routes to 0..=4 and add `MouseButton::WheelLeft/WheelRight/XButton1/XButton2` to input.rs:288. (4) Add `double_click`, `factor`, `button_mask`, `global_position` to `InputEvent::MouseButton` and `velocity`/`screen_velocity`/`pressure`/`tilt`/`pen_inverted` to `MouseMotion`, computing double_click in `InputState` the way `DOUBLE_TAP_FRAMES` (input.rs:1418) already does for touch. (5) Widen `get_mouse_button_mask` to the full MouseButtonMask set.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a browser wheel event must scroll a ScrollContainer in a played scene and reach a script's `_input` as an `InputEventMouseButton` with `button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN`.

**Prove it:** With a scene containing a ScrollContainer running under the editor server, POSTing a wheel-down event and stepping one frame advances the container's scroll offset AND a script's `_input` observes `button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_WHEEL_DOWN`; two mouse-down events inside the double-click window deliver a second event with `double_click == true`; the served EDITOR_HTML registers a `wheel` listener (assert on `pub const EDITOR_HTML`). comments.text:
MagentaBrook — correction to my own sizing in the block report (msg 79672), because it would send the next worker down a path that does not work.

I wrote that velocity/screen_velocity are 'derivable from the position delta and frame timing' inside push_input. The first half is right, the second is NOT: I checked, and `SceneTree::push_input(&mut self, event: &InputEvent)` takes no delta and SceneTree holds no wall-clock or per-frame time — every delta on SceneTree arrives as a parameter to a process_* method (process_timers, process_script_coroutines, process_video_players), none of which is on the input path. push_input only has trace_frame, a counter.

So velocity is NOT computable where double_click is computed. Godot builds it in the OS layer from event timestamps. Whoever takes this needs a transport decision, not a derivation:
  (a) stamp arrival time in the route (editor_server has a clock) and carry it, or
  (b) have InputState track it across MouseMotion events and expose a getter, then pass it into input_event_to_variant the way double_click is passed — note this needs MainLoop, which owns both InputState and the tree, since SceneTree deliberately cannot see InputState (scene_tree.rs:389).

Option (b) is the same shape as the emulate_mouse_from_touch work in pat-s3rrv.77: the decision is made in MainLoop because it is the only place that holds both halves.

button_mask IS derivable without timing — it is the set of currently-held buttons, which push_input can track the same way it tracks last_mouse_press_frame. That part of my note stands.

Unchanged and still the key warning: do NOT widen InputEvent::MouseMotion. 41 construction sites workspace-wide, and this bead family already chose the computed-flag route for double_click for exactly that reason (71 sites on MouseButton, per the comment at scene_tree.rs:4340).

title: Web input: touch pipeline (touchstart/move/end → ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag) + honor emulate_* project settings
description:
[audit-key: input/web-touch-pipeline] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** extension_api.json InputEventScreenTouch/InputEventScreenDrag; Input.set_emulate_mouse_from_touch/set_emulate_touch_from_mouse; ProjectSettings input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch|emulate_touch_from_mouse; upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js touch handlers

**Godot classes:** InputEventScreenTouch, InputEventScreenDrag, TouchScreenButton

**Patina today:**
- [input] IMPLEMENTED BUT UNREACHABLE. `InputEvent::ScreenTouch`/`ScreenDrag` with double_tap/canceled/pressure/tilt exist at engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:511-535; `InputState` tracks `touch_positions`, `touch_last_press_frame`, `mouse_from_touch_index`, `emulate_mouse_from_touch`, `emulate_touch_from_mouse` (input.rs:1381-1408) with `DOUBLE_TAP_FRAMES` (input.rs:1418). But `grep -rn 'touchstart|touchmove|touchend|TouchEvent' crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs crates/gdplatform/src/export.rs` returns 0 hits, and there is no touch route among editor_server.rs:2518-2537. `grep -rn --include='*.rs' 'touchstart|input/touch|ScreenTouch' crates/gdeditor/src/` finds only the inspector schema table entry (inspector_schema_generated.rs:4621). The project settings exist only as defaults — engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:738,742 declare `input_devices/pointing/emulate_touch_from_mouse` and `emulate_mouse_from_touch`, and grepping for consumers outside gdplatform/gdcore returns 0, so setting them in project.godot has no effect on `InputState`. Consequence: a phone or tablet cannot play a Patina game, and `TouchScreenButton` routing (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/main_loop.rs:2770) can only ever be driven by a real mouse.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: Godot's web platform registers `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend`/`touchcancel` on the canvas and emits `InputEventScreenTouch` (index, position, pressed, double_tap, canceled) and `InputEventScreenDrag` (index, position, relative, velocity, pressure, tilt) per finger (upstream/godot/platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_input.js). `ProjectSettings.input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch` (default true) makes the first finger drive `InputEventMouseButton`/`MouseMotion` so Controls and Buttons respond to touch; `emulate_touch_from_mouse` (default false) does the inverse for desktop testing.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: the whole engine-side model already exists and is tested — `InputEvent::ScreenTouch`/`ScreenDrag` at engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/input.rs:511-535, per-finger tracking, Godot's `mouse_from_touch_index` first-finger rule and double-tap window at input.rs:1381-1418 — but there is NO producer. The served EDITOR_HTML (engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_ui.rs) has zero touch listeners and engine-rs/crates/gdeditor/src/editor_server.rs has no touch route (routes end at editor_server.rs:2537). The two project settings are declared as defaults in engine-rs/crates/gdcore/src/project_settings.rs:738,742 and read by nobody, so `InputState::emulate_mouse_from_touch` keeps its hard-coded value regardless of project.godot.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (1) add passive-false `touchstart`/`touchmove`/`touchend`/`touchcancel` listeners on the game view in editor_ui.rs, posting the changed-touches array `[{identifier, x, y, force, tiltX, tiltY}]` with a `phase` field. (2) Add `POST /api/runtime/input/touch` in editor_server.rs that pushes `InputEvent::ScreenTouch`/`ScreenDrag` through `MainLoop::push_event`. (3) At boot in both engine-rs/crates/patina-runner/src/main.rs:366 and editor_server.rs:13011, read `input_devices/pointing/emulate_mouse_from_touch` / `emulate_touch_from_mouse` from the booted ProjectSettings and apply them to `InputState`. (4) Route ScreenTouch/ScreenDrag into `SceneTree::gui_input_stage` (engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs:3248) — today only MouseButton/MouseMotion/Key take a branch there.\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: a touchstart on the game view must press a Button in a played scene (via mouse emulation) AND reach a script's `_input` as an `InputEventScreenTouch`.

**Prove it:** With a scene containing a Button running under the editor server, POSTing a touchstart at the Button's rect and stepping one frame emits `pressed` on the Button and a script's `_input` observes an `InputEventScreenTouch` with `index == 0` and `pressed == true`; a project.godot setting `emulate_mouse_from_touch=false` suppresses the Button press while the ScreenTouch still arrives; the served EDITOR_HTML registers a `touchstart` listener. (test: `touch_events_reach_running_game`)
acceptance_criteria: With a scene containing a Button running under the editor server, POSTing a touchstart at the Button's rect and stepping one frame emits `pressed` on the Button and a script's `_input` observes an `InputEventScreenTouch` with `index == 0` and `pressed == true`; a project.godot setting `emulate_mouse_from_touch=false` suppresses the Button press while the ScreenTouch still arrives; the served EDITOR_HTML registers a `touchstart` listener. (test: `touch_events_reach_running_game`)

title: HTTP: wire HTTPRequest as a real scene node with a fetch/TLS backend and request_completed signal
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-http-fetch] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/platform/web/http_client_web.h:41-51 (godot_js_fetch_create/read_headers/read_chunk/state_get — Godot's web HTTPClient is fetch-based) + platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_fetch.js; extension_api.json HTTPRequest (request, request_raw, cancel_request, set_http_proxy, accept_gzip, body_size_limit, max_redirects, timeout, download_file, download_chunk_size, use_threads, signal request_completed) and HTTPClient (connect_to_host, request, poll, read_response_body_chunk, get_response_headers_as_dictionary, set_read_chunk_size, TLS options).

**Godot classes:** HTTPRequest, HTTPClient, TLSOptions

**Patina today:**
- [multiplayer] (1) SCRIPT-UNREACHABLE: `grep -rn 'HTTPRequest|HttpRequest|request_completed' crates/gdscene/src/ crates/gdscript-interop/src/ crates/patina-runner/src/` returns ZERO hits. `grep -rn -i 'http' crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` matches only two unrelated URL comments (lines 2970, 20241) and `grep -rn -i 'http' crates/gdscene/src/*.rs` matches one unrelated comment (scene_tree.rs:180). The 602-line `crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs` and 639-line `crates/gdplatform/src/http_client.rs` have no consumer in the scene tree, the interpreter, or the runner. HTTPRequest IS registered in ClassDB (crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, register block documented at :9983) so a `.tscn` node of that type instantiates and does nothing. (2) NO TLS AND NO FETCH BACKEND: crates/gdplatform/src/http_client.rs:15 `use std::net::{TcpStream, ToSocketAddrs}`; the module doc at line 9 states "Only plaintext http:// is wired here. https:// reports a TLS handshake" and line 451 returns TlsHandshakeError; crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs:490-496 has a test asserting https reports a TLS error. There is no wasm32 cfg in either file (grep of gdplatform for `target_arch = "wasm32"` hits only js_bridge.rs, os.rs, platform_targets.rs). Godot's own web build routes HTTPClient through `fetch()` and supports HTTPS.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_request.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/http_client.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscene/src/scene_tree.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `HTTPRequest` is a Node. A script does `var r = HTTPRequest.new(); add_child(r); r.request_completed.connect(_on_done); r.request(url)` and the node polls its client each frame, then emits `request_completed(result, response_code, headers, body)`. I was assigned this and started on remaining-scope item (3), specifically `cancel_request`, which
is the one item there that needs no new dependency: `gdplatform::http_request::HTTPRequest`
already has `cancel()` at http_request.rs:387. I got as far as reading the semantics before
reserving, and the reservation came back with BronzeLake holding BOTH
gdscene/src/http_request_node.rs and gdscene/src/scripting.rs exclusively to 12:14:19Z. Those two
files are exactly where cancel_request has to live, so there is no way to route around it. I have
released my claim rather than race a file someone is mid-edit in — that is what produced the
E0425 that sank an unrelated bead earlier today.

THE FINDING, which is not obvious and costs an upstream read to get right:

  A naive `cancel_request` that just delegates to the platform `cancel()` will fire a SPURIOUS
  `request_completed` with a failure result. Godot does not do that.

  - Godot's `HTTPRequest::cancel_request()` (scene/main/http_request.cpp:186-210) ends at
    `requesting = false;` and emits NOTHING. No `emit_signal("request_completed", ...)` anywhere
    in it.
  - Patina's platform `cancel()` (gdplatform/src/http_request.rs:387-396) deliberately does the
    opposite: it sets `in_progress = false`, `emitted = false`, and
    `response = Some(HttpResponse { result: RequestFailed, .. })` — its doc comment says
    "recording a failed result".
  - `poll()` (http_request.rs:319-341) returns early only on `in_progress || emitted`. After a
    cancel both are false and `response` is Some, so the very next poll builds a payload and runs
    the callbacks — which, in the scene node, pushes it onto the `completed` queue and emits it
    as a scene signal on the next frame.

  So the scene-side wrapper has to swallow it. What I was about to write:

      pub fn cancel(&self) {
          self.inner.cancel();
          // Flush the failure the transport just recorded, then drop it.
          // `poll` short-circuits on `emitted` afterwards, so nothing resurfaces.
          self.inner.poll();
          self.completed.lock().unwrap().clear();
      }

  Doing it in gdscene rather than changing gdplatform's `cancel()` keeps the shared API alone —
  that function has another caller (its own test at http_request.rs:483), and other consumers may
  want the recorded failure.

  Worth a test that asserts the ABSENCE: cancel an in-flight request, step the loop, and assert
  the script's handler was never called. An assertion that only checks `is_requesting() == false`
  passes against the spurious-callback version.

Also still open from your own list and not touched by me: accept_gzip, body_size_limit,
max_redirects, timeout, download_file as script-facing methods, and TLSOptions in ClassDB. Of
those, body_size_limit and download_file look honourable without a new dependency; accept_gzip,
max_redirects and timeout need transport support that does not exist yet, so registering them
alone would add the carried-but-inert surface this audit keeps flagging.

comments.text:
## Disposition of the REMAINING extension_api surface, one item at a time

The bead lists `set_http_proxy`, `download_chunk_size` and `use_threads` alongside the methods now
wired. They are NOT done, and — having group-labelled this bead's scope wrongly twice today — here
is a separate reason per item, each checked against the transport rather than inferred.

**`set_http_proxy` / `set_https_proxy` — must NOT be wired until the transport supports proxies.**
`grep -i proxy gdplatform/src/{http_client,http_request}.rs` returns NOTHING. A script sets a proxy
for routing or privacy reasons; storing the value while requests continue to go direct is not an
incomplete feature, it is a silent lie with a security dimension. This is the one item here where
wiring the setter would be actively worse than leaving it absent.

**`use_threads` — cannot be honoured, and `false` is the dangerous half.** The transport spawns a
background thread UNCONDITIONALLY (`http_request.rs:305`); there is no synchronous path. So
`set_use_threads(true)` would be accidentally correct while `set_use_threads(false)` — which in
Godot means "poll on the main thread" — would be silently ignored. A setter that is right for one
argument and wrong for the other is worse than none.

**`download_chunk_size` — there is nothing to configure.** The transport reads the whole body
(Content-Length, or to EOF, de-chunking `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` internally at
`http_client.rs:534`) and hands it over complete. Godot's value sizes the incremental read buffer,
which this design does not have. A getter/setter would round-trip a number that changes nothing.

⚠️ Note these three fail for three DIFFERENT reasons — missing subsystem, unrepresentable
semantics, and inapplicable design. That is exactly why they should not be carried as one
"remaining properties" bullet: the next reader would inherit a single label and, as happened twice
on this bead with `body_size_limit`/`download_file` and then `accept_gzip`, either skip work that
was doable or do work that should not be done.

For contrast, the items that ARE now wired and why they were never blocked: `body_size_limit` and
`download_file` are enforced by the NODE in `http_request.cpp`, not by HTTPClient; `accept_gzip`
needed a decoder that was already in the workspace and already in `Cargo.lock`.

comments.author: BronzeLake
comments.text:
DELIBERATELY DECLINED, not merely skipped (BronzeLake, 2026-08-19T22:13Z): set_http_proxy, use_threads, download_chunk_size as a GDScript property.

These three are named in this bead's Godot-ground-truth line but NOT in its implement instruction (b). I am recording the reasoning because 'named in the API list' reads like remaining parity work, and adding them would make this bead WORSE by its own stated standard.

This bead's own complaint about the starting state was: 'the class IS registered in ClassDB, so a .tscn type=HTTPRequest node loads as an inert Node - the worst failure mode, because it looks supported.' A setter that stores a value nothing reads is the same failure at method granularity.

- set_http_proxy: grep -c proxy crates/gdplatform/src/http_client.rs == 0. There is no proxy support anywhere in the transport, so the setter would be 100 percent inert. A script would set a proxy, get no error, and have its traffic go direct.
- use_threads: the native transport ALWAYS spawns a thread (http_request.rs request()), and the wasm arm cannot spawn one at all. Godot's flag selects between main-thread and threaded execution. Neither of our arms can honour either setting, so the flag would be unreadable in both directions.
- download_chunk_size: this one is HALF live and that is worse than either extreme. The plumbing now exists on the web side (WebTransfer::set_chunk_size, increment 10) but the native client does not stream - read_response() reads the whole body into a Vec and returns it, so there is no per-chunk granularity to control. Exposing the property would silently work on web and do nothing on native, which is the hardest kind of parity gap to diagnose later.

If someone does want these, the order is: implement the underlying capability FIRST (proxy support in http_client.rs; a streaming read path natively), then expose the setter. Not the reverse.

Related non-finding, so nobody re-checks it: http_client.rs:323 uses [0u8; 8192], which looks like the same defect as the 4096 download_chunk_size bug fixed in increment 10. It is NOT. That is a socket scratch buffer feeding a read-it-all loop; Godot's read_chunk_size governs the granularity of the streaming read_response_body_chunk API, which the native client does not implement. Changing 8192 to 65536 would be a no-op dressed as a parity fix.

comments.author: BronzeLake
comments.text:
TLS blocker (remaining_scope item 2) — reconnaissance, NOT an edit.

I have said three times that TLS "needs a new dependency" and left it there. That
was an unexamined claim, so I checked what is actually available. The blocker is
real but much smaller and better defined than I have been reporting.

## Re-verified: nothing TLS exists today (03:55Z)

Cargo.lock has no rustls / native-tls / openssl / ring / webpki, and nothing
pulls one transitively — no tungstenite, reqwest, ureq, hyper or curl either.
So http_client.rs:451 returning TlsHandshakeError is not a wiring gap; there is
genuinely no crypto in this workspace.

## But the whole rustls closure IS in the local registry cache

~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/ already contains:

    rustls-0.23.37        ring-0.17.14         rustls-pki-types-1.14.0
    rustls-webpki-0.103.10  subtle-2.6.1       zeroize-1.8.2
    untrusted-0.9.0       webpki-roots-0.26.11 and 1.0.6
    cc-1.2.57 (ring build-dep)

Eight new Cargo.lock entries would be needed: rustls, ring, rustls-pki-types,
rustls-webpki, subtle, zeroize, untrusted, webpki-roots. All eight are cached.
The rest of the closure is already locked at matching versions: log 0.4.29
(cached: log-0.4.29), once_cell, cfg-if, libc, getrandom, cc.

## THE TRAP — the naive line does not work

rustls 0.23 default features are:

    default = ["aws_lc_rs", "logging", "prefer-post-quantum", "std", "tls12"]

aws-lc-rs and aws-lc-sys are NOT in the cache. So a plain

    rustls = "0.23"

fails to resolve offline, and even with network drags in a large C/assembly
aws-lc-sys build. Anyone who tries the obvious line will conclude "TLS is not
feasible here" and back out — which may be exactly what happened before.

What resolves against what is cached:

    rustls = { version = "0.23", default-features = false, features = ["ring", "std", "tls12", "logging"] }
    webpki-roots = "1.0"

(`ring` = ["dep:ring", "webpki/ring"], `std` = ["webpki/std", "pki-types/std",
"once_cell/std"], `logging` = ["log"], and log is already locked at the cached
version.)

⚠️ Root store: rustls-native-certs is NOT cached. Use webpki-roots, which is.

⚠️ ring compiles C and assembly via its `cc` build-dep. Fine on this darwin box
with the Xcode CLT; whether CI images have a C toolchain is a separate question
someone should confirm before committing to ring over a pure-Rust provider.

## Why I still did not make the edit

Any Cargo.toml dependency addition forces a full lock re-resolution, and I cannot
run cargo to verify it. If I get the feature set or a version wrong, the whole
workspace stops building for every agent at once — the largest blast radius
available to me, and unverifiable from this lane. "Cached on this machine" also
is not "resolvable in CI".

So this stays blocked on a cargo-capable lane, but it is no longer blocked on an
unknown: the dependency set is decided, the trap is documented, and offline
resolvability is established.

crates/gdplatform/src/fetch_web.rs mtime: 2026-08-19 14:53. The artifacts are 23
days OLDER than the source, and target/wasm32-unknown-unknown has no
dep-lib-gdplatform at all. So increments 6-10 remain the largest never-compiled
pile in this bead.

## What I could do about it without a wasm build

Audited every js-sys / wasm-bindgen call in the cfg-gated module against the
VENDORED CRATE SOURCE, which is the exact resolved version:
~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/js-sys-0.3.91 and wasm-bindgen-0.2.114
(both match Cargo.lock). Seven API surfaces, all confirmed compatible:

- Reflect::get(&JsValue, &JsValue) -> Result<JsValue, JsValue>  (lib.rs:7316)
- Reflect::set(&JsValue, &JsValue, &JsValue) -> Result<bool, JsValue> (:7453)
- js_sys::global() -> Object  (:13061)
- Object::new(), Uint8Array::new(&JsValue) / ::from(&[u8]) (:13410) / .to_vec() (:13398)
- Promise::then2(...) -> Promise  (:13033)
- JsValue::from_str / NULL / UNDEFINED  (wasm-bindgen lib.rs:203/178/181)

## One thing that looked like a break and is not

then2 is declared

    resolve: &ScopedClosure<dyn FnMut(JsValue)>

and the code passes a `Closure`. That reads as a type error until you find
wasm-bindgen closure.rs:180:

    pub type Closure<T> = ScopedClosure<'static, T>;

Closure IS ScopedClosure. Compatible. Recording it because the next person to
read that signature will have the same scare.

## A real API-shape change worth knowing

js-sys 0.3.91 has made several types GENERIC with defaults:

    pub type Object<T = JsValue>;      (:6570)
    pub type Promise<T = JsValue>;     (:12733)
    pub type Function<T: JsFunction = ...>;  (:3573)

Our code uses the bare forms (`js_sys::Object`, `dyn_into::<js_sys::Promise>()`,
`dyn_into::<js_sys::Function>()`), which resolve through the defaults and are
exactly what still compiles. ⚠️ Note then2 specifically takes `&Promise` (i.e.
`Promise<JsValue>`) while its sibling `then` takes `&Promise<T>` — so a future
change that makes the promise generic would break then2 and not then.

⚠️ Also: there is a SECOND Reflect::set, generic over `&Object<T>`, gated behind
cfg(js_sys_unstable_apis). It is inactive by default. If anyone ever turns that
cfg on, our 3-arg &JsValue calls stop matching.

## What this audit does NOT establish

- I could not verify the `Deref<Target = JsValue>` coercion that three calls rely
  on for passing `&Object` where `&JsValue` is wanted (`&global`, `&init`,
  `&hdrs`). wasm-bindgen-backend is not in the local registry cache, so the
  codegen is unreadable from here. It is bedrock wasm-bindgen behaviour, but it
  is an assumption, not a check.
- Nothing here is a compile. A signature audit catches wrong-API errors; it does
  not catch borrow, lifetime, or inference errors.

Item (3) is unchanged in substance: it still needs someone with orchestrator
access to find out whether crate_breaker (verifier.rs:516/596) is skipping the
wasm target, or whether the gate was never wired up at all.

gdplatform/src/packet_peer_stream.rs:122-171 does it.

Verified inputs, so whoever takes this does not repeat the survey:

- TAG BYTE 0x48 is free (ASCII H, beside 0x57 W for WebSocket). Occupied bytes
  are 10 11 12 1A 4D 57 5B 5C 5D 5E 6D 6E 6F 70 77 78 A1 A2 A3 A4 A7 B9 CA CF

  underscore grouping) and 0xE9. Grep BOTH the value shape and the

  complete, and a collision makes is_*_handle answer true for another module's
  ids, surfacing as MethodNotFound naming the WRONG class.

poll-driven; our HttpClient is blocking. A faithful poll surface cannot sit on it
without lying about poll(). The honest mapping is eager work behind a poll-shaped

Chasing the "unverified" note from my previous comment. It is not a .78 problem —
it affects every RefCounted handle class in the engine.

## The claim

`c.read_chunk_size = 4096` does NOT route through the ClassDB accessor

works. In Godot both work; the property form is the documented one

1. `exec_assignment` (interpreter.rs:1685) handles a member target three ways:
   script-instance properties via `inst.class_def.setters` (:1734ish), scene_access
   node properties, and hard-coded special cases (`Engine.time_scale`,
   `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer`). There is NO branch that takes a
   `Variant::ObjectId` TARGET and looks up a ClassDB setter.

Every `.new()`-constructible handle class, not just HTTPClient: WebSocketPeer,

PCKPacker, XMLParser, ConfigFile, CameraFeed, the XR trackers, StreamPeer,

comments.text:
Type audit of the unverified interpreter hunk, plus one design property I should flag about my own code.

## Audit result (increment 15, interpreter.rs — still never compiled)

gdscript-interop has not been rebuilt since 21:09:42 local, before my 21:19-21:23
edits, so `call_http_client_instance` and the `HTTPClient.new()` arm have never
been type-checked. I re-audited every call against the real signatures:

- request(method: HttpMethod, url: &str, headers: &[String], body: &[u8]) -> i32
  call passes (HttpMethod, &String, &Vec<String>, &Vec<u8>) — three deref
  coercions, all valid at a call site.
- connect_to_host(host: &str, port: i32, use_tls: bool) -> i32
  call passes (&String, i32 via i32::try_from(...).unwrap_or(i32::MAX), bool).
- with_http_client<R>(id, f: impl FnOnce(&mut ScriptHttpClient) -> R) -> Option<R>
  closure is annotated -> Result<Variant, RuntimeError>; the outer
  unwrap_or_else handles the None (released handle) case.
- Vec<String> -> Variant::PackedStringArray, Vec<u8> -> Variant::PackedByteArray,
  i64 -> Variant::Int, i32 `as i64` at every error-code site.
- `matches!(args.get(2), None | Some(Variant::Nil))` on Option<&Variant> relies
  on match ergonomics; the identical shape already exists and compiles in
  gdscene/src/scripting.rs, so it is not a new risk.

No errors found. ⚠️ That is the same audit that missed two errors in my test file
last increment (wrong NodeId path, wrong find_child arity) — I only caught those
by checking the symbols against source, which is what I did here too. It is not a
substitute for a compile.

## ⚠️ Design property worth knowing: the lock is held across network I/O

`with_http_client` takes a process-wide Mutex on the handle table and my
dispatch calls `client.request(...)` INSIDE that closure. `ScriptHttpClient::request`
does a blocking connect/write/read. So an in-flight HTTPClient request holds the
global handle-table lock for the whole exchange, blocking every other HTTPClient
handle operation process-wide.

Not a bug today: the interpreter is single-threaded, HTTPRequest`s worker threads
use a different type and never touch this table, and the closure calls no script
code so it cannot re-enter the non-reentrant Mutex and deadlock. But it is a
latent deadlock/stall the moment any of those three facts changes, and it differs
from the exemplar I copied (packet_peer_stream) only because packet framing is
instant while a network round-trip is not.

If someone thinks that is too sharp an edge, the fix is to clone the needed state
out under the lock, drop the guard, do the I/O, then re-acquire to write results
back. I did not do that pre-emptively because it doubles the lock traffic for
every other method and the single-threaded assumption holds today — but I would
rather it be written down than discovered.

title: Multiplayer: add a wasm32 browser-WebSocket backend for WebSocketPeer/WebSocketMultiplayerPeer (incl. wss://)
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-web-websocket] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: MISSING]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/websocket/emws_peer.cpp + library_godot_websocket.js (Godot's web build binds the browser WebSocket API and supports wss://); modules/websocket/websocket_multiplayer_peer.cpp. Godot's web export explicitly supports WebSocket while raw sockets return ERR_UNAVAILABLE (platform/web/net_socket_web.h:51-60).

**Godot classes:** WebSocketPeer, WebSocketMultiplayerPeer

**Patina today:**
- [multiplayer] Patina's WebSocket stack is native-TCP-only and cannot run in a browser — the engine's only shipping target. `crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs:459-540` (`connect_to_url`) calls `(host, port).to_socket_addrs()` and `TcpStream::connect_timeout`, and line 468 returns `Err(WebSocketError::TlsUnsupported)` for any `wss://` URL — so even natively it cannot reach any TLS server, and any HTTPS-served game page cannot use ws:// (mixed content). `crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs:23` imports `std::net::{SocketAddr, TcpListener, TcpStream, ToSocketAddrs}`, and its own module doc at lines 17-19 states: "Only plaintext ws:// is wired: wss:// is rejected by WebSocketPeer::connect_to_url, and the browser (wasm) transport is not part of this module." There is no wasm variant: `grep -rn 'target_arch = "wasm32"' crates/gdplatform/src/*.rs` matches only js_bridge.rs (362/366/468/847), os.rs (50/353/426/432) and platform_targets.rs:56 — nothing in websocket_peer.rs, websocket_multiplayer.rs, tcp_multiplayer.rs, or enet_multiplayer.rs. Neither is `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` registered in ClassDB (`grep -c 'ClassRegistration::new("WebSocketMultiplayerPeer")' crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs` = 0).

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: Godot's web export implements WebSocketPeer over the browser's WebSocket object — upstream/godot/modules/websocket/emws_peer.cpp plus library_godot_websocket.js provide godot_js_websocket_create/send/close and the open/message/error/close callbacks. Subprotocols are passed to the constructor, binary frames arrive as ArrayBuffer, and `wss://` works because the browser terminates TLS. WebSocketMultiplayerPeer builds its client/server roles on top (server role is unavailable on web; the client role is the standard web multiplayer transport). Godot's web target returns ERR_UNAVAILABLE for every raw socket op (platform/web/net_socket_web.h:51-60) — WebSocket is the sanctioned replacement, not an optional extra.\n\nPATINA CURRENT STATE: there is exactly one backend and it is `std::net`. crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_peer.rs:459-540 resolves DNS with `to_socket_addrs()` and dials with `TcpStream::connect_timeout`; line 468 hard-rejects TLS with `WebSocketError::TlsUnsupported`. crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs:23 imports TcpListener/TcpStream, and its own module doc (lines 17-19) admits "the browser (wasm) transport is not part of this module". `grep -rn 'target_arch = \"wasm32\"' crates/gdplatform/src/*.rs` shows zero gating in either file. So on wasm32 the browser build has no working WebSocket at all, and on native it cannot reach any wss:// endpoint. WebSocketMultiplayerPeer is additionally unregistered in ClassDB.\n\nIMPLEMENTATION: (a) split websocket_peer.rs into a transport trait plus two backends: keep the existing RFC-6455 framing path (encode_frame/decode_frame/handshake helpers at websocket_peer.rs:175-360 — these stay, they are also used by the server role) behind `#[cfg(not(target_arch = \"wasm32\"))]`, and add `#[cfg(target_arch = \"wasm32\")]` backend that constructs a browser `WebSocket` through js-sys Reflect (the pattern already used in crates/gdplatform/src/js_bridge.rs:468+), sets `binaryType = \"arraybuffer\"`, registers onopen/onmessage/onerror/onclose closures pushing into the same packet queue the native path fills, and maps readyState 0..3 onto WebSocketState. Subprotocols go into the WebSocket constructor's second argument; extra handshake headers are not settable in the browser and must return ERR_UNAVAILABLE like Godot. (b) make `wss://` legal: on wasm it is free; on native add a TLS backend (or, at minimum, stop rejecting it and route through the same TLS choice made for HTTPClient). (c) give WebSocketMultiplayerPeer a wasm client role built on the same backend, with `create_server` returning ERR_UNAVAILABLE on wasm as Godot does. (d) register `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` in crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs next to WebSocketPeer (class_db.rs:11523).\n\nWIRING REQUIREMENT: the script-facing WebSocketPeer handle dispatch (crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:18283-18391) must reach the wasm backend unchanged, so the same GDScript works in the runner on both targets.

**Prove it:** `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p gdplatform` succeeds with the browser backend selected, and on native a GDScript scene doing `WebSocketPeer.new().connect_to_url("wss://<local TLS echo server>")` reaches READY_STATE_OPEN and echoes a text and a binary packet. `connect_to_url` no longer returns TlsUnsupported for any wss:// URL, and WebSocketMultiplayerPeer resolves through ClassDB. (test: `websocket_peer_wss_and_wasm_backend`)
acceptance_criteria: `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p gdplatform` succeeds with the browser backend selected, and on native a GDScript scene doing `WebSocketPeer.new().connect_to_url("wss://<local TLS echo server>")` reaches READY_STATE_OPEN and echoes a text and a binary packet. `connect_to_url` no longer returns TlsUnsupported for any wss:// URL, and WebSocketMultiplayerPeer resolves through ClassDB. (test: `websocket_peer_wss_and_wasm_backend`)

## Design note for the next increment: `heartbeat_interval` and `max_queued_packets` ARE implementable natively (MagentaBrook, 2026-08-19 13:26 UTC)

My last comment left the four unregistered properties as "nothing implements them". Two of them are implementable in this lane with primitives that already exist, and I read the semantics out of `wsl_peer.cpp` so the next pass does not have to. Recording it now rather than starting the edit, because my previous report is still awaiting verification and editing the same files underneath an in-flight build is how I broke gdserver3d for a peer earlier today.

### `heartbeat_interval` (default **0.0** = disabled) — it is a LIVENESS TIMEOUT, not a keepalive

⚠️ This is the part a reasonable implementation misses. Sending a ping every N seconds is only half of it. `wsl_peer.cpp:715-731`:

```
if (heartbeat_interval_msec != 0 && ticks - last_heartbeat > interval && ready_state == STATE_OPEN) {
    if (heartbeat_waiting) {          // the previous ping was never answered
        wslay_event_context_free(...);
        close(-1);                    // ABRUPT close, not a clean 1000
        return;
    }
    heartbeat_waiting = true;
    ...send PING...
    last_heartbeat = ticks;
}
```

and `:660` clears `heartbeat_waiting` when a **Pong** arrives. So a peer that stops answering is dropped at the *second* interval, with `close(-1)` rather than a normal closure. An implementation that only sends pings keeps a dead connection open forever and looks correct in every test that has a live server on the other end.

Primitives already present: `Opcode::Ping`/`Opcode::Pong` exist and both encode and decode (`websocket_peer.rs:115-141`), and `poll()` is the natural tick. What is missing is the `last_heartbeat` / `heartbeat_waiting` pair and the Pong handler clearing it.

⚠️ Also documented as having **no effect in Web exports** ("browser restrictions") — relevant to this bead's wasm half: the wasm backend must accept the setting and ignore it, not emulate it.

### `max_queued_packets` (default **4096**) — REFUSE the new packet, do not drop the oldest

⚠️ `wsl_peer.cpp:783`: `ERR_FAIL_COND_V(queued_msg_count >= max_queued_packets, ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY)`. Godot **rejects the send** and returns an error. Dropping the oldest queued packet is the intuitive choice for a bounded queue and is wrong here: it silently loses data a caller believed was sent, where the real behaviour hands back an error the caller can act on. The docs say the cap applies to "both inbound and outbound".

The inbound side has exactly one push site (`websocket_peer.rs:825`), so the cap is a one-line guard there plus the send-side check.

### `outbound_buffer_size` / `inbound_buffer_size` (default 65535 each)

`:784` refuses a send when `queued_bytes + this_packet > outbound_buffer_size`, also `ERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. ⚠️ But this engine's `send` writes straight to the socket and keeps **no outbound queue** at all — which is why `get_current_outbound_buffered_amount` is honestly 0 today. So `outbound_buffer_size` cannot be implemented meaningfully until an outbound queue exists, and implementing it before then would be carried-but-inert state. `inbound_buffer_size` sizes Godot's inbound ring (`:300`), which has no counterpart here either.

**So the split is: two implementable now (`heartbeat_interval`, `max_queued_packets`), two genuinely blocked on a buffering rewrite.** The test `the_unimplemented_properties_are_deliberately_absent` asserts all four absent and must be narrowed to the remaining two in whichever change implements the first two — that is what it is there for.

title: Variant: make Array and Dictionary reference types (shared storage) like Godot
description:
[audit-key: core-variant/core-variant-array-refsem] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: PARTIAL]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/core/variant/array.h + dictionary.h — Array/Dictionary hold a refcounted `ArrayPrivate*`/`DictionaryPrivate*`; `var b = a` shares storage, so `b.append(1)` is visible through `a`. doc/classes/Array.xml: "Arrays are always passed by reference." | extension_api.json Array: assign, is_typed, is_same_typed, get_typed_builtin, get_typed_class_name, get_typed_script, make_read_only, is_read_only, duplicate_deep, find_custom, rfind_custom, bsearch_custom; Dictionary adds the typed-key/typed-value variants (Godot 4.4 typed dictionaries) plus recursive_equal and sort. Upstream core/variant/array.cpp `Array::set_typed`/`_assign` enforces element type on every write. | upstream/godot/modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp parse_type (typed containers, 4.4 typed Dictionary); extension_api.json `.builtin_classes[] | select(.name=="Dictionary")` (is_typed/typed key+value); gdscript_analyzer.cpp type resolution

**Godot classes:** Array, Dictionary, @GDScript

**Patina today:**
- [core-variant] Patina models both as plain value types with derived Clone: engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs:253 `Array(Vec<Variant>)` and :255 `Dictionary(Dictionary)`; engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/dictionary.rs:1-45 stores `Vec` + `HashMap` with no Rc/Arc anywhere (grep `Rc<|Arc<` in dictionary.rs → no hits). The interpreter compensates with copy-then-write-back: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:7534-7547 `array_mutate` does `let mut items = arr.to_vec(); f(&mut items); self.write_place(object_expr, Variant::Array(items))`, and every Dictionary mutator does the same (interpreter.rs:8598-8612 `merge`, 8660-8666 `get_or_add`). Consequences: `var b = a; b.append(1)` leaves `a` empty; an Array passed to a function and appended to inside is not mutated for the caller (write_place targets the local param Ident, interpreter.rs:1582-1594 → exec_assignment); `arr.map(...)` results and node-property arrays diverge from Godot. No test in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/tests/ asserts aliasing (grep `alias` → only camera_feed.rs/encoded_object_as_id, unrelated).
- [core-variant] The type annotation is parsed then thrown away. .tscn side: engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs:667-680 parses `Array[Type]([...])` and returns a plain `Variant::Array` — the comment at :667-668 says "The element type annotation is accepted but not retained"; `parse_variant_value_typed` (loader.rs:285-291) exposes it only as an out-of-band string. GDScript side: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs:627-634 stores the hint as the string `"Array[int]"` and engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/type_checker.rs:450 explicitly treats `Array[int]` as an unknown type. Runtime introspection is absent: the Array method table (interpreter.rs:7800-8126) has no is_typed, get_typed_builtin, get_typed_class_name, get_typed_script, is_same_typed, assign, make_read_only, is_read_only, duplicate_deep, find_custom, rfind_custom, bsearch_custom, hash; the Dictionary table (interpreter.rs:8537-8671) is missing the same family plus sort, recursive_equal, and every typed-key/value query. There is no typed-Dictionary syntax anywhere (grep `Dictionary[` across engine-rs/crates → 0 hits).
- [gdscript] engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs:628-638 `parse_type_hint` reads a single identifier and special-cases exactly one shape — `Array[<ident>]`. Consequences: `var d: Dictionary[String, int] = {}` leaves the `[` unconsumed (the `Assign` check at parser.rs:657 fails), producing garbage statements; `var g: Array[Array[int]]` hits `eat_ident()` on the inner `Array` then expects `]` and errors; a qualified hint `var s: MyClass.State` truncates to `MyClass`. The hint is also only ever a String (`type_hint: Option<String>` at interpreter.rs:588, :646) and is never enforced at assignment — `grep -rn 'type_hint' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` shows it flowing only into ExportInfo and ClassDef, never into a runtime check.

**Files:** /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/dictionary.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdresource/src/loader.rs, /Users/bone/dev/games/patina/engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/parser.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

GODOT GROUND TRUTH: `core/variant/array.h`/`dictionary.h` — Array and Dictionary are handles to a refcounted private struct. `doc/classes/Array.xml` states "Arrays are always passed by reference"; the same holds for Dictionary. So `var b = a; b.append(1)` mutates the single shared array, and an Array passed into a function is mutated for the caller.

PATINA CURRENT STATE: both are value types. engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/variant.rs:253 is `Array(Vec<Variant>)`; engine-rs/crates/gdvariant/src/dictionary.rs stores `Vec<Entry>` + `HashMap` index with no Rc/Arc, and `Variant` derives `Clone` (variant.rs:208). The GDScript interpreter papers over this with copy-then-write-back: engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs:7534-7547 (`array_mutate`) copies the array, mutates the copy and assigns it back to the *place expression*; Dictionary mutators do the same (interpreter.rs:8598-8612, 8660-8666). That makes `a` and `b` independent after `var b = a`, and makes in-function mutation invisible to the caller because `write_place` resolves to the local parameter Ident (interpreter.rs:1582-1594).

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH: change `Variant::Array` to hold `Arc<RwLock<Vec<Variant>>>` (or `Rc<RefCell<…>>` if the interpreter is single-threaded — check `gdvariant` consumers first: gdscene, gdresource, gdeditor, gdserver2d/3d all import Variant) and `Variant::Dictionary` to hold `Arc<RwLock<Dictionary>>`. Keep `PartialEq` structural (deep compare) so `==` stays Godot-correct, keep `Dictionary`'s order-independent eq. Add `Array::duplicate(deep)` producing a NEW handle (Godot's copy op). Then delete `array_mutate`'s write-back and the equivalent Dictionary write-backs in interpreter.rs so mutators operate in place. Sweep every `Variant::Array(` / `Variant::Dictionary(` construction and pattern-match site across crates (gdvariant/src/{binary,serialize,hash,fuzz_variant}.rs, gdresource/src/{loader,saver,res_loader}.rs, gdscene/src/packed_scene.rs, gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs) — this is the bulk of the work.

WIRING REQUIREMENT: the end-to-end path is .tscn load → script attached to a node → `_ready()` builds an Array, stores it in a script var, passes it to a helper that appends → the caller's var must show the appended element, and the same array read back through the node property must show it too. The write-back hack must be gone, not merely bypassed.

**Merged findings (3):** Array/Dictionary reference (shared) semantics; Typed Array[T] / typed Dictionary[K,V] enforcement and read-only containers; Typed declarations: `Dictionary[K, V]`, nested `Array[Array[T]]`, qualified type names, runtime typed-container enforcement

**Prove it:** A scene whose script does `var a = []` / `var b = a` / `b.append(1)` prints `[1]` for `a`, and a script that passes an Array into a func which appends sees the append in the caller; the same for Dictionary key insertion; `a.duplicate()` still yields an independent copy. (test: `array_dictionary_reference_semantics_from_scene`) — loads a .tscn with an attached GDScript through the gdscene/patina-runner path, runs one frame, and asserts the aliasing observations above from script output/property reads, not from Rust-level Array APIs.
acceptance_criteria: A scene whose script does `var a = []` / `var b = a` / `b.append(1)` prints `[1]` for `a`, and a script that passes an Array into a func which appends sees the append in the caller; the same for Dictionary key insertion; `a.duplicate()` still yields an independent copy. (test: `array_dictionary_reference_semantics_from_scene`) — loads a .tscn with an attached GDScript through the gdscene/patina-runner path, runs one frame, and asserts the aliasing observations above from script output/property reads, not from Rust-level Array APIs.

### Why the remaining six cannot be delivered before the flip

The methods already implemented are **pure functions of the elements** — they need
nothing but the `Vec`. Each of the six still missing needs **per-container state**
(a type tag, a read-only flag, an identity) that a plain `Vec<Variant>` cannot
carry. They are therefore gated on the enum flip by construction, not merely
adjacent to it. That is why there is no safe partial left here for a worker that
cannot run cargo — not simply that the sweep is large.

`interpreter.rs:9558` — the `"duplicate"` arm comments *"Value semantics make
shallow and deep copies identical"* and returns `arr.clone()`. That comment
becomes false and the arm becomes a **bug** the moment Array is a handle: a
shallow duplicate must produce a NEW handle that shares nothing at the top level.
Grep for it during the gdscript-interop step.

738 sites / 115 files at 04:28 UTC -> 759 sites / 107 files at 11:23 UTC
(547 `Variant::Array(` + 212 `Variant::Dictionary(`). Every pass another worker

I am not re-deriving the analysis. **What nobody has measured is the growth rate, and it changes the scheduling argument.**

| when | sites | source |

| 2026-08-19 04:31 UTC | 738 | BronzeLake |

**+83 sites in the 3.0 hours since the last measurement — about 27 new call sites per hour, committed.**

⚠️ That number is measured at **HEAD**, not in the working tree, deliberately. A tree count conflates "the swarm committed more sites" with "someone is mid-edit right now", and only the first is real growth. The tree carries just +6 uncommitted on top of HEAD, so the growth is committed work by the swarm, not a measurement artifact.

Current spread (crates only): gdscript-interop 259, gdscene 185, gdobject 80, gdresource 94, gdvariant 77, gdeditor 68, gdplatform 4. 129 files. **16** crates now declare gdvariant as a dependency (BronzeBridge counted 14).

### Why this matters for scheduling

The existing comments ask for a build-lane session. This adds the reason it is urgent rather than merely correct: **the flip is a moving target that grows by roughly 650 sites a day while the swarm runs.** Every hour this sits in the worker lane, the eventual session gets bigger. It does not converge by waiting, and the six worker passes spent confirming that have themselves cost more sites than they saved.

The practical consequence: the session that lands this needs the swarm **quiesced**, or it will be sweeping against a tree that moves under it.

### Deliverable this pass

`tools/measure_variant_container_flip_scope.py` — re-runnable scope meter so the next assignee checks the state in one command instead of spending a pass re-deriving it, and so the build-lane session has a live count.

It fails closed: a zero count means the greps stopped matching (a rename, a moved tree), not that the scope is empty. It also asserts the *gate* — if `variant.rs` ever stops carrying both value-typed payloads, the script FAILS loudly with "the flip has started or landed, so re-read the bead", because at that moment the write-backs, the nine typed-container queries and the acceptance test all become deliverable. Same if the count ever falls, which would mean a sweep is underway and touching it would collide.

Verified from three working directories (`engine-rs/`, the repo root, and `/tmp`) because the verifier runs Rust commands from `engine-rs/`, not the repo root.

comments.text:
## PARKED 2026-08-19 12:13 UTC (MagentaBrook, 7th assignee) — the coordinator gate and the bead's own scope are mutually unsatisfiable

Setting status `blocked` with zero dependencies, which is this project's deliberate-park idiom. Recording exactly why, because the previous six workers each reported a block and each time the bead came straight back to the worker lane.

### The deadlock, stated once

1. The coordinator will not close this without `array_dictionary_reference_semantics_from_scene` passing. It said so verbatim at 12:11:36 UTC in response to my partial: *"acceptance test not run ... report the acceptance test."*
2. That test asserts `var b = a` then `b.append(1)` is visible through `a`. It is RED until the enum flip lands — 3 of its 4 clauses are, anyway; only the `duplicate()` independence clause passes today.
3. The flip is atomic across **825 call sites in 129 files**, and 16 crates depend on `gdvariant`. There is no green intermediate state, and a worker cannot run a compiler (AGENTS.md:88).

So the only report the gate accepts is one no worker can produce. It is not a reporting-format problem, and resending in a different shape will not fix it — I am deliberately **not** resending, because each report has produced another assign (8 in the six minutes before this park) and the escalation is what drives the flood.

### What would have been gaming the gate, and why I did not do it

The tempting escape is to land `array_dictionary_reference_semantics_from_scene` as `#[ignore]`, or carrying only the `duplicate()` clause. Either one makes `cargo nextest run -p ... --test array_dictionary_reference_semantics_from_scene` exit 0 — the first by running zero tests, the second by asserting the one thing that already works. Both would close this bead with the reference semantics still broken, which is the entire point of it. A test that passes because it tests nothing is worse than no test: it converts an open gap into a false green that nobody re-opens.

### Exit condition — how to un-park

Run `python3 tools/measure_variant_container_flip_scope.py`. It FAILS the moment `variant.rs` stops carrying both value-typed payloads, and its message says so. When that happens the flip has landed and everything else on this bead — the `array_mutate` write-back in interpreter.rs, the Dictionary write-backs, the nine typed-container queries, and the acceptance test — becomes deliverable in the ordinary way.

Until then this needs one build-lane session with a compiler, landing all sites before any verify, with the swarm quiesced so the tree does not move under the sweep. The target grew **+83 sites in the 3.0 hours** before this park (~27/hour, committed), so it does not converge by waiting.

## The rule: registerable-now == abstract BY DESIGN (all methods virtual, no members)

`StreamPeerExtension` and `PacketPeerExtension` were registerable because Godot declares them with
nothing but virtual methods and zero members — they exist so a GDExtension can implement a
StreamPeer/PacketPeer. Registering them IS the port; there is no behaviour to be missing because
Godot has none either. Both landed this pass with their parents already registered, so the chains
resolve to Object.

## I swept the other ten. NONE of them qualifies.

Measured from each class's doc XML (`<method ... qualifiers>` and `<member>` counts):

    StreamPeerTLS          methods= 6  virtual= 0  members=0
    TLSOptions             methods= 9  virtual= 0  members=0
    StreamPeerGZIP         methods= 4  virtual= 0  members=0
    ENetConnection         methods=18  virtual= 0  members=0
    ENetPacketPeer         methods=16  virtual= 0  members=0
    UPNP                   methods=11  virtual= 0  members=3
    UPNPDevice             methods= 4  virtual= 0  members=6
    JSONRPC                methods= 7  virtual= 0  members=0
    WebRTCPeerConnection   methods=12  virtual= 0  members=0
    WebRTCDataChannel      methods=12  virtual= 0  members=1

Every one has real concrete surface, and none of them is implemented anywhere in `gdplatform`
(checked: no implementing file for any). So registering any of them would advertise a class that
raises on use — the inverse lie this audit keeps finding, and the defect that already exists on
`WebRTCMultiplayerPeer`, whose registered `create_server`/`create_client`/`add_peer` do not exist on
the struct.

**Each of those ten should be registered in the same change that implements it, not before.**

## The two WebRTC *Extension* bases are a special case of the same rule

`WebRTCPeerConnectionExtension` and `WebRTCDataChannelExtension` ARE abstract-by-design (11 and 18
methods, all virtual, zero members) — so by the rule above they would be registerable. They are still
excluded, for a different reason: their parents `WebRTCPeerConnection` / `WebRTCDataChannel` are
unregistered, and an unregistered base silently severs the chain, so the child would answer
`class_exists` true while `inheritance_chain` stopped short of `Object`. They become free the moment
their parents land. A test in
`gdobject/tests/gdextension_peer_bases_registered.rs` pins that so a later sweep cannot add them
ahead of their bases.

## Worker-lane status

With PacketPeerStream (reachable end to end) and these two bases delivered, I believe this bead has
nothing further that can be done without a browser and a compiler. That is now a measured claim
rather than a judgement call.

title: Wire WebSocketMultiplayerPeer into ClassDB, GDScript and MultiplayerAPI so it is reachable from a game
description:
[audit-key: multiplayer/multiplayer-websocket-multiplayer-peer-unwired] [port-audit 2026-07-27] [status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** upstream/godot/modules/websocket/websocket_multiplayer_peer.cpp — WebSocketMultiplayerPeer inherits MultiplayerPeer with create_client(url, tls_options)/create_server(port, bind_address, tls_options)/get_peer(id)/get_peer_address/get_peer_port/disconnect_peer, plus handshake_headers, supported_protocols, handshake_timeout, inbound/outbound buffer sizes, max_queued_packets; doc/classes/WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.xml. It is the canonical browser-side multiplayer transport for a web export

**Godot classes:** WebSocketMultiplayerPeer

**Patina today:**
- [sweep-7] Real implementation with zero consumers. engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs:152 defines `pub struct WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` implementing `NetworkPeer` (websocket_multiplayer.rs:432) over RFC 6455. Consumer search: `rg -n 'websocket_multiplayer' engine-rs --glob '*.rs'` returns exactly TWO hits outside the module itself — gdplatform/src/lib.rs:37 (`pub mod websocket_multiplayer;`) and gdplatform/tests/websocket_multiplayer_e2e_test.rs:16 (its own test). Nothing in gdscene, patina-runner, the MultiplayerAPI or the interpreter constructs it. Script reachability: `rg -n '"WebSocketMultiplayerPeer"' engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs` = 0 hits (WebSocketPeer IS wired, interpreter.rs:3082 and :18283). ClassDB: `grep -x WebSocketMultiplayerPeer` against the 4186 literals extracted from engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs = 0 hits, while WebSocketPeer, WebRTCMultiplayerPeer (class_db.rs:11567) and ENetMultiplayerPeer (class_db.rs:11579) are registered. The only other mention is the inspector table row gdeditor/src/inspector_schema_generated.rs:5399 (that file has 0 register_class calls). This is exactly the systemic 'tested library code nothing calls' pattern named in the audit's Second Law.

**Files:** engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs, engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs

**Implement / wiring requirement:**

[status: UNWIRED]

**Godot ground truth:** WebSocketMultiplayerPeer (modules/websocket/websocket_multiplayer_peer.cpp) is a MultiplayerPeer subclass and the canonical multiplayer transport for a web export. Script surface: create_client(url, tls_options), create_server(port, bind_address, tls_options), get_peer(id) -> WebSocketPeer, get_peer_address(id), get_peer_port(id), disconnect_peer(id, code, reason), plus handshake_headers, supported_protocols, handshake_timeout, inbound_buffer_size, outbound_buffer_size, max_queued_packets. Assigned to `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer`, it drives peer_connected/peer_disconnected and RPC routing.

**Patina today:** the transport is implemented and e2e-tested but nothing in the engine ever constructs it. engine-rs/crates/gdplatform/src/websocket_multiplayer.rs:152 defines the struct and :432 implements NetworkPeer; `rg -n 'websocket_multiplayer' engine-rs --glob '*.rs'` finds only gdplatform/src/lib.rs:37 (the mod declaration) and its own test file. It is absent from ClassDB (0 hits against class_db.rs's literals, unlike WebSocketPeer / WebRTCMultiplayerPeer at class_db.rs:11567 / ENetMultiplayerPeer at class_db.rs:11579) and has no interpreter branch (0 hits for the literal in gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, where WebSocketPeer is wired at :3082 and :18283). A GDScript therefore cannot obtain one at all.

**Implement:** (1) register WebSocketMultiplayerPeer in engine-rs/crates/gdobject/src/class_db.rs next to WebRTCMultiplayerPeer (class_db.rs:11567) with parent MultiplayerPeer and the documented method/property surface. (2) add a `.new()` branch and instance dispatch in engine-rs/crates/gdscript-interop/src/interpreter.rs, following the WebSocketPeer handle pattern at interpreter.rs:3082 / :18283, delegating to gdplatform::websocket_multiplayer. (3) allow the handle to be assigned to `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer` and make the SceneTree tick call its poll() each frame so peer_connected/peer_disconnected and RPC traffic flow.

**Wiring requirement:** a script does `var p = WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new(); p.create_client(url); multiplayer.multiplayer_peer = p` and the frame loop polls it — peer_connected fires and an @rpc call routes over it. Module-level green tests in gdplatform prove nothing here.

**Prove it:** an app-level loopback test driving a server peer and a client peer through the SceneTree tick and asserting an @rpc arrives.

**Prove it:** `ClassDB.class_exists("WebSocketMultiplayerPeer")` is true with parent MultiplayerPeer; a GDScript in a loaded scene constructs one with `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new()`, calls create_server/create_client on a loopback pair, assigns each to `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer`, and — with polling driven only by the SceneTree frame loop — observes peer_connected on both sides and an @rpc call made on one peer executing on the other (test: `websocket_multiplayer_peer_script_reachable`)
acceptance_criteria: `ClassDB.class_exists("WebSocketMultiplayerPeer")` is true with parent MultiplayerPeer; a GDScript in a loaded scene constructs one with `WebSocketMultiplayerPeer.new()`, calls create_server/create_client on a loopback pair, assigns each to `multiplayer.multiplayer_peer`, and — with polling driven only by the SceneTree frame loop — observes peer_connected on both sides and an @rpc call made on one peer executing on the other (test: `websocket_multiplayer_peer_script_reachable`)
